t: Mao Zedong's initial blueprint for socialist agricultural and rural modernization and its historical lessons
zh: 毛泽东对社会主义农业农村现代化的初步擘画及历史启示
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the compilation of The Socialist Upsurge in China's Countryside (compiled late 1955, published early 1956), Xia Shaoguang asks what Mao Zedong's editorial notes to that volume reveal about his plan for modernizing agriculture and the countryside. The article argues that the notes set the fundamental direction of cooperativization, sketched a comprehensive blueprint, and offer lessons that remain relevant for building a strong agricultural country today.

The article first places the volume in the context of the 1950s: the two-step path Mao outlined at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee (1949), the general line for the transition period, and disputes within the Party over cooperatives. It then examines Mao's notes, which Xia summarises as "twelve unities", and the institutional advantages and Party working style the book displays. It closes with three historical lessons.

Xia's central claim is that Mao's notes treat modernization as a balanced whole. The "unities" include Party leadership with mass contact, productive forces with changes in relations of production, bold construction with thrift, economic work with ideological and political work, exploiting nature with ecological protection, and bold planning with continual revision. Others pair patient persuasion with firm struggle, economic with social development, and the interior with minority regions. Xia reads the book as showing the advantages of public ownership over smallholder farming, which was vulnerable to disaster and polarisation, and as embodying the mass line, fact-based investigation and a plain Marxist writing style. The author endorses the 1981 Party resolution's verdict that the socialist transformation was a great historic victory.

Xia draws three lessons. The achievements of Mao's leadership should be assessed in a long historical view, and the author opposes "historical nihilism" that exaggerates errors. Xia also claims four forms of progress for the Chinese path compared with traditional small-peasant production, capitalist modernization, Soviet agricultural stagnation and other agrarian countries' development. Finally, today's rural revitalization should follow Mao's balanced approach: keep the collective basis of agriculture, resist land privatization, loosen management systems, and uphold Party leadership in the countryside. Xia presents this as continuing Mao's blueprint. Read the original if you want a Party-line reappraisal of Mao's agricultural cooperativization, with close textual use of the volume's editorial notes.
quoteEn: The socialist transformation promoted the development of the productive forces and advanced modernization.
quoteZh: 社会主义改造促进了生产力发展，推动了现代化建设。

The Party's working method of gathering ideas from the masses, refining them and returning them as policy. It is described as the Party's fundamental working line.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.

t: On the new form of scientific socialism in the twenty-first century
zh: 论二十一世纪科学社会主义的新形态
paras: Wu Haijiang asks what historical position Chinese modernization occupies in the long development of scientific socialism, and what theoretical narrative should accompany it. The article argues that Chinese modernization has opened a new form of scientific socialism for the twenty-first century. In Wu's account this form rests on the achievements of developed socialism with Chinese characteristics, aims to surpass contemporary capitalism, and looks towards the next stage of socialism.

The article has three parts. The first treats Marxism as a "historical science" and traces scientific socialism through three forms: the classical conception built on developed Western capitalism and the Paris Commune, the twentieth-century practice in backward countries such as Russia and China, and the emerging twenty-first-century form. The second part explains how Chinese modernization creates this new form. The third part turns to building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system for scientific socialism, covering its context, methods and points of focus.

Wu's central argument is that Chinese modernization has solved three major problems of scientific socialism: how socialism should relate to capitalism, how to avoid the ills of capitalist modernization, and how to defend the socialist system against risks. It has also answered new questions of the era, namely the Chinese, world, people's and epoch questions, in the setting of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the great changes unseen in a century. The author lists new features in path, theory, institutions and culture, including the Two Integrations, the socialist market economy and whole-process people's democracy. For the knowledge system, Wu draws on narratology to describe scientific socialist narrative as both factual and normative. The article proposes methods that unite critique with construction, upholding fundamental principles with innovation, and a Chinese standpoint with openness.

Wu names three priorities for the new knowledge system: the new possibilities Chinese modernization opens for scientific socialism, the social effects of the technological revolution (digital productive forces and artificial intelligence), and new changes in contemporary capitalism such as financialization and populism. The conclusion presents the new form as a new version of modern human civilization and as a "Chinese sample" of scientific socialism for the twenty-first century. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how Chinese theorists place Chinese modernization within the genealogy of scientific socialism and frame an autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: Socialism exists not only as an ideal; it can also offer, in practice, a model of social development that has real superiority and faces the future.
quoteZh: 社会主义不仅作为一种理想而存在，更能够在实践层面提供一种具有现实优越性、面向未来的社会发展模式。

t: The Party and the Red Army's practice of close unity during the Long March, and its lessons
zh: 长征时期党和红军发扬紧密团结精神的实践探索和启示
source: Journal of the China Executive Leadership Academy Jinggangshan, 2026 no. 2
paras: Marking the 90th anniversary of the Long March, Li Zequan asks how the Party and the Red Army sustained close unity under near-annihilation, and what this offers today. Li argues that close unity was a major internal cause of the march's turn from strategic retreat to a victorious advance north against Japan. The article ties this to the Great Long March Spirit, which Xi Jinping summarised as including taking the overall situation into account, strict discipline and close unity.

The article has three parts. The first describes four manifestations of unity: the cohesion of the central leadership, co-ordination among the Red Army forces, solidarity within the ranks, and bonds with the civilians along the route. The second gives three causes: shared ideals and convictions, correct Party leadership, and strict discipline. The third draws four lessons. Li draws on episodes such as Xu Haidong's loan to the Central Committee and the "half a quilt" story, and on recollections by Li Xiannian, Peng Dehuai, Chen Yun and others.

Li's central claim is that unity was produced through principled, well-handled struggle rather than the absence of conflict. After the Zunyi Meeting, Mao Zedong and others rejected the "Left" military line but did not fully repudiate the "Left" political line or strip its leaders of other posts. Li presents this as necessary to keep figures such as Zhang Wentian and Wang Jiaxiang on side. Against Zhang Guotao's split, the Central Committee combined firmness with flexibility. It treated the dispute as an intra-Party contradiction and declined to expel him, and Li credits this with bringing the Fourth Front Army north. Li adds that leaders' own conduct (Zhou Enlai giving up the post of general political commissar, Zhu De, Ren Bishi and He Long resisting the split) and democratic centralism guaranteed the outcome.

Li lists the lessons as: set a correct strategic line, conduct correct inner-Party struggle, have leading cadres show Party spirit and model unity, and uphold democratic centralism. The article closes by saying that the Party is still "on the Long March", with new mountain passes and rivers to cross. It calls for carrying forward this spirit to consolidate unity among the Party, the army and the people in pursuit of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history account of the Zunyi Meeting and the Zhang Guotao split, and of how contemporary Chinese scholarship draws lessons from them.
quoteEn: Seek unity through struggle, and unity will survive.
quoteZh: 以斗争求团结则团结存

glossary.explanation: A Party-defined set of values drawn from the Red Army's Long March (1934–36). Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on the 80th anniversary listed its components, including taking the overall situation into account, strict discipline and close unity.
A Politburo enlarged meeting held in January 1935 in Guizhou. Party histories treat it as ending the dominance of the "Left" military line and establishing Mao Zedong's leading position.
The Communist Party's organisational principle combining discussion with binding decisions, in which the minority obeys the majority and lower levels obey higher ones.

t: The Long March spirit in Chen Yun's writings on the Long March and its contemporary value
zh: 陈云长征著作中蕴含的长征精神及其当代价值
source: Journal of Long March Studies, 2026 no. 3
paras: Chen Yun took part in the Long March and supported Mao Zedong at the Zunyi Meeting. He later wrote three accounts of it: Notes on Accompanying the Army to the West (Jianwen lu), the Outline for Conveying the Enlarged Politburo Meeting at Zunyi, and the Report on the Long March of the Red Army and the Zunyi Meeting. Zhao and Li note that existing scholarship treats these texts mainly as propaganda and historical sources. They argue that the Long March spirit embodied in them has been neglected, and that the texts remain valuable today for understanding and promoting that spirit. The article appeared in 2026.

The article has three main parts. The first reads Chen Yun's writings against the five components of the Long March spirit as set out by Xi Jinping. The second sets out the works' contemporary value. The third proposes practical ways to promote the spirit in the new era, and a short closing section places this within the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

In the first part, the authors pair each component with episodes Chen recorded. These include the crossing of the Dadu River and the Luding Bridge, the sacrifice of a division at the Xiang River, and the criticism of "dogmatism" for directing the army as if along a line drawn in pencil. They also cite the Zunyi Meeting's correction of errors, soldiers' discipline and equal treatment with officers, ethnic unity with the Miao and Yi, and Mao Zedong's gift of clothing to a destitute old woman. In the second part they argue that the works supply reliable historical evidence, preserve emotional memory through humane details, and serve as lively texts for communication. They stress that Chen's account reached Paris and Moscow in March 1936, before Edgar Snow's interviews, and was praised by the Comintern.

The authors call for collecting, protecting and digitising Long March documents, and for using the sources in education, including short videos and micro Party lessons. They also call for micro-level narratives and plain language in place of abstract preaching. In addition, they urge the Party to seize leadership of ideological work, to build the image of a great Party through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform, and to take control of international discourse so as to counter Western discursive hegemony. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based reading of Chen Yun's Long March texts and the official line on using them in education and external communication.
quoteEn: Chen Yun's Long March writings are both important historical sources for studying the Red Army's Long March and an effective vehicle for grasping the Long March spirit in depth.
quoteZh: 陈云长征著作既是研究红军长征的重要史料，也是深刻把握长征精神的有效载体。

t: The Long March Spirit in the process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context: logic, value and contemporary expression
zh: 马克思主义中国化进程中的长征精神：逻辑理路、价值意蕴与当代表达
source: Journal of Jinggangshan University (Social Sciences Edition), 2026 no. 2
paras: Zhu Hong and Li Xiaokang ask what role the Long March Spirit (1934–36) plays in the process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. They argue that the Long March moved the Party from a "dogmatic" Marxism towards a practice-based, nationalised one, and from passive imitation to active creation. In their account it launched the first historic leap in this process, and the spirit it produced is a concentrated form of the early intellectual achievements of that process.

The article has three parts. The first sets out five logics of the spirit: practical breakthrough and theoretical self-awareness, theoretical innovation, the formation of an ideological line, the mass line, and a cultural logic. The second discusses its value under three headings: a spiritual foundation (ideals and hard struggle), a methodological root (seeking truth from facts and independence), and organisational support (the mass standpoint and solidarity). The third examines its contemporary expression. A short conclusion follows.

The authors' central claim is that the Party's break with Soviet and Comintern models, marked by the Zunyi Conference (1935), produced the line of "seeking truth from facts" and independence. In their reading this line was later systematised in Mao Zedong's philosophical and strategic writings, the Yan'an rectification campaign and the 1945 Seventh Congress. They trace its continuation through reform and opening up and the Three Represents, then the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. For the present day they say the spirit informs poverty alleviation, rural revitalisation, the Belt and Road Initiative, red tourism, ideological and political education, technological self-reliance and the international presentation of China's experience.

Zhu and Li conclude that the Long March marked the logical starting point and methodological foundation of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. They treat Chinese modernization as a new "Long March", and call on the Party to strengthen theoretical self-awareness, cultural confidence and its people-centred stance. Revisiting the spirit is, in their words, a reconfirmation of the laws of theoretical innovation, not mere commemoration. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated journal links the Long March to successive stages of Sinicised Marxism, including its present-day uses in education, development policy and external communication.
quoteEn: Revisiting the Long March Spirit is not a commemoration of history but a reconfirmation of the laws of theoretical innovation and a renewed push for the process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 重温长征精神，不是对历史的缅怀，而是对理论创新规律的再确认，对马克思主义中国化时代化进程的再推动。

glossary.explanation: A Party-defined set of values attributed to the Red Army's Long March of 1934–36, such as firm ideals, hard struggle, independence and solidarity. It is regularly invoked in official political education.
A Politburo meeting in January 1935 during the Long March. Party history treats it as the point where Mao Zedong's leadership was established and Comintern-led dogmatism was criticised.

A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, made central to the Party's ideological line by Mao in the Yan'an period and by Deng Xiaoping later.
The official name for the Party's path of national development under Xi Jinping, presented as distinct from Western modernisation.

t: The historical contribution of the Long March to adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and its lessons for today
zh: 长征时期中国共产党推进马克思主义中国化时代化的历史贡献与当代启示
source: Journal of Sichuan Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2026 no. 5
paras: Marking the 90th anniversary of the Long March's victory, Li and Guo ask how the Chinese Communist Party advanced the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times during the Long March, even though the Party had not yet formally posed the question in those terms. They argue that the Long March's victory was in a real sense a victory for that adaptation and an important part of its first historic leap.

The article is organised around four contributions. It treats the break with dogmatism as the ideological foundation, the establishment of a strong leadership core as the organisational foundation, the mass line as the popular foundation, and the Long March spirit as a source of motivation. It draws on events from the Xiang River battle to the Zunyi Meeting, on recollections by Chen Yun, Geng Biao and others, and on statements by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

The authors argue that the "Left" dogmatism of the Party's provisional central leadership, under Bo Gu and Otto Braun (Li De), brought heavy losses. In their account, doubts grew through the Tongdao change of direction and the Liping and Houchang meetings, and Zunyi then ended that line's control and marked a turn in the ideological line toward seeking truth from facts. They attribute the earlier setbacks to an immature central leadership and to mechanical obedience to the Comintern, and cite Deng Xiaoping to the effect that no leadership before Zunyi was truly mature. The mass line is presented as both a value ("everything for the masses, everything relying on the masses") and a method ("from the masses, to the masses"). The authors illustrate it with the Red Army's discipline, its ethnic policy toward minority groups, and its use of local knowledge to cross the Wu River.

Drawing on Xi Jinping's 2016 account of the Long March spirit, the authors propose five lessons for adapting Marxism today. These are to uphold Party leadership as the guide to direction, to hold to ideals and convictions, to practise seeking truth from facts, to put the people first, and to keep a fighting spirit. They tie these to the Two Integrations, Chinese modernization and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-history article links Long March episodes to the current theory of adapting Marxism, or if you want its sources on Zunyi and the mass line.
quoteEn: The victory of the Long March was a victory for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and an important part of the great practice of its first historic leap.
quoteZh: 长征的胜利，就是马克思主义中国化时代化的胜利，是其第一次历史性飞跃伟大实践的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The Party's working method of gathering the views of the people, turning them into policy, and testing that policy among the people. It is described officially as the Party's lifeline.
An ideological line associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, stressing that policy should start from actual conditions and not from texts or dogma.

t: Mao Zedong's initial blueprint for socialist agricultural and rural modernization and its historical lessons
zh: 毛泽东对社会主义农业农村现代化的初步擘画及历史启示
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the compilation of The Socialist Upsurge in China's Countryside (1955–56), this article asks what Mao Zedong's editorial notes to the volume reveal about his plans for agricultural and rural modernization. Xia argues that in these notes Mao set the basic direction of cooperativization, sketched an initial blueprint, drew out the contradictions driving the process, and foresaw its prospects. The article holds that this legacy still guides rural work today.

The article first explains why agricultural cooperativization became the route to modernization, drawing on the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee (1949), the general line for the transition period, and early mutual-aid experience. It then recounts how Mao selected 176 of more than 200 reports and wrote notes for 104 of them. The central sections set out twelve unities in the notes, discuss the book as evidence of socialist institutional advantages and of the Party's style of work, and close with three historical lessons.

In Xia's reading, the twelve unities show Mao's approach of balanced planning (tongchou jiangu). Examples include Party leadership with close ties to the masses, developing productive forces with changing relations of production, bold construction with frugality, economic work with political and ideological work, and exploiting nature with protecting the environment. Others pair patient education with firm struggle, economic with social construction, the interior with ethnic minority regions, and the enthusiasm of all ages and classes. The author argues that the book embodies the mass line, seeking truth from facts through investigation, and a plain writing style. Xia cites the 1981 Resolution on Party history as endorsing cooperativization as a great historical victory.

Xia draws three lessons. Mao's achievements should be assessed in a long historical perspective, and Xia opposes what the article calls historical nihilism. Comparing social systems, the author finds four kinds of progress: over small-peasant production, over capitalist modernization's rural crises, over Soviet agricultural lag, and as a world-historical example for agrarian countries. Finally, rural revitalization today should keep collective ownership as its basis, resist land privatization, and uphold Party leadership in the countryside. Read the original if you want a Party-line reading of Mao's 1955–56 editorial notes and of how they are linked to current rural revitalization policy.
quoteEn: All cooperatives should take whether output has increased, and by how much, as the main criterion for testing whether they are sound.
quoteZh: 一切合作社，都要以是否增产和增产的程度，作为检验自己是否健全的主要的标准。

A principle of basing judgments on actual conditions; associated with Mao Zedong and treated as a core of the Party's ideological approach.

t: The core meaning, inner logic and practical path of building a culturally strong country in the new era
zh: 新时代文化强国的核心意蕴、内在逻辑与实践进路
paras: Taking its cue from the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), the article asks what it means to build a culturally strong country and how this should be done. Luo and Wu argue that the core of a cultural power is spiritual strength, which they break down into four capacities: ideological guidance, spiritual cohesion, value appeal and international influence. In their view these four, developed in step, are the key marker and lever of cultural-power building.

The article has three parts. The first places a culturally strong country within a modernized strong country and treats spiritual strength as the measure of national strength, drawing on Xi Jinping, R.S. Cline, Joseph Nye, and the historical views of Sun Yat-sen, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. The second sets out how the four capacities relate to one another. The third proposes four practical paths.

On the core argument, the authors say a country's cultural strength cannot be judged by the scale of the culture industry or the number of cultural products. It depends on whether a spiritual force pervades society and shapes people's inner world. They describe the four capacities as progressive. Ideological guidance, grounded in Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is the foundation. Spiritual cohesion, built on shared ideals and convictions, is the core. Value appeal, rooted in people-centred practice, is the focus. International influence is the outward expression. They add that rising international influence in turn strengthens the other three.

The practical path has four parts. The authors call for the Party's theoretical innovation through the Two Integrations, and for using advanced ideas to win over the masses through accessible language and digital media. They also call for sustained practice of socialist core values, and for multi-channel civilizational exchange and mutual learning that keeps the subjectivity of Chinese culture and aims at mutual understanding rather than cultural hegemony. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of the official framework of the "four forces" of cultural power, and of how Chinese scholars link Party theory, values and external communication.
quoteEn: The \"strength\" of a culturally strong country is in essence the strength of spiritual force.
quoteZh: 文化强国的“强”，本质上是精神力量的“强”

glossary.explanation: An official goal of building China into a country with strong cultural soft power and influence, set as part of the wider aim of a modern socialist strong country.
Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels.

t: On systems thinking in the five-year plans of the new era
zh: 论新时代五年规划的系统思维
paras: Written after the adoption of the 15th Five-Year Plan Outline in March 2026, the article asks what systems thinking contributes to China's five-year planning. Ha and Zhang argue that the plans' success as a mode of governance rests on systems thinking, which serves as their epistemological and methodological foundation. They contend that existing scholarship studies individual plans or the history of planning but neglects this feature, and they treat each plan as a layered, rigorously structured systems project.

The authors examine the plans along three dimensions: the overall arrangement of plan content, the linkage of the planning system, and the coordination of planning actors. Their examples come mainly from the 12th to the 15th Five-Year Plans, with illustrations from provincial and city plans, annual plans, special and regional plans, and the mid-term evaluation of the 14th plan.

On content, the authors identify four nested subsystems: guiding purpose, deployments, indicators and means. Each, they argue, balances a pair of tendencies: economic development with human development, overall advance with key breakthroughs, anticipated with binding indicators, and an effective market with a proactive government. On system linkage, they describe four kinds of connection: across time between successive plans, between short-term plans and long-term goals, vertically from national to provincial and county levels, and horizontally among development, spatial, special and regional plans. On actors, they describe a chain in which the Party proposes the Recommendations, the government drafts the Outline and the people's congresses approve it. The Party then exercises overall leadership in implementation, with government organising and congresses supervising. Evaluation by government, with Party approval and review by congress standing committees, feeds the next plan in a cycle of drafting, implementation, evaluation and redrafting. In the article's account this arrangement overcomes problems of Western capital-led development and of policy discontinuity in multiparty systems.

The authors conclude that content, system and actors depend on one another and together form the complete shape of the five-year plan as a systems project. They hold that grasping these features helps convert the institutional advantages of planning into national governance capacity and supports the modernization of the national governance system and capacity. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-theoretical account of how Chinese scholars present five-year planning as systems engineering, with concrete examples from recent plans.
quoteEn: In content, system and actors, the five-year plan displays relations of mutual dependence and coordinated action, which together build up its complete form as a systems project.
quoteZh: 五年规划在内容、体系和主体上具有相互依存、协同作用的关系，共同构筑起五年规划作为系统工程的完整形态。

glossary.explanation: China's medium-term national economic and social development plan, issued every five years since 1953 (called a 'plan' until the 11th, then a 'programme/plan'). The 15th covers 2026–2030.
A method stressing development, comprehensiveness, interconnection and the handling of major relationships, which Xi Jinping presents as part of the Party's dialectical method.

t: The dialectical unity of cultural diversity and the common values of all humanity
zh: 论文化多样性与全人类共同价值的辩证统一
paras: Zou and Han ask how cultural diversity and the common values of all humanity can be held together under economic globalization, which they say both enriches cultures and sharpens conflicts between them. Their thesis is that the two are dialectically united: diversity supplies the experiential soil from which shared values grow, while shared values give diversity a normative framework. They present this as grounded in Marxist historical materialism and in Xi Jinping's statements on civilizational exchange.

The article has three parts. The first treats cultural diversity as the basis of civilization, tracing its mixing through exchanges of peoples, species and ideas, and then lists modern challenges in the economic, political, cultural and ecological fields. The second sets out why a bottom-line consensus is needed and how the common values of all humanity (peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy, freedom) take shape over time and space. The third draws out the dialectic between diversity and unity and warns against two extreme attitudes.

Zou and Han argue that capital's standardizing logic, Western claims to political universality, algorithmic recommendation and fossil-fuelled climate change each erode diversity. Against this they ground common values in Marx's idea of the human species-essence formed through practice, and in shared existential threats such as ecological and security crises. The authors say these values are not fixed dogma but evolve, combining traditional wisdom with modern practice, as in the move from the idea of harmony between heaven and humanity to the slogan that clear waters and green mountains are invaluable assets. They hold that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers a model for going beyond Western 'universal values'.

The authors conclude that cultural relativism, which they say shields backward institutions, and cultural hegemonism, which packages one civilization's values as universal, must both be rejected. Common values should be sought in the 'commonality within difference' through economic interdependence, political trust and mutual learning among cultures. They call for cultural subjectivity and the creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture, in pursuit of the ideal of 'each beautiful in its own way, all beautiful together'. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Marxist scholars connect the discourse on common values to cultural diversity and a critique of Western universalism.
quoteEn: We acknowledge that difference is permanent, but are not confined by it; we pursue the universality of values, but avoid sinking into the mire of universalism.
quoteZh: 我们承认差异的永恒性，但又不囿于差异；追求价值的普遍性，但又避免陷入普遍主义泥淖。

glossary.en: the common values of all humanity
glossary.literal: shared values of the whole of humankind
glossary.explanation: A formula promoted by Xi Jinping from 2015 listing peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared across civilizations. It is presented in Chinese discourse as an alternative to Western 'universal values'.
The official name for China's path of modernization, described by the Party as distinct from Western models. It has been a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The inherent logic of the theoretical system of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化理论体系蕴含的内在逻辑
paras: Bao Xinjian asks what internal logic underlies the theoretical system of Chinese modernization, which the article presents as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author argues that this system contains a historical, theoretical, practical and contemporary logic, and that its essence lies in the Two Integrations: combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

The introduction traces the Party's exploration of modernization from the 'four modernizations' under Mao Zedong, through Deng Xiaoping's 'Chinese-style modernization' and the three-step strategy, to Xi Jinping's formulations. The body then sets out five 'adherences', each treated as one strand of the system's logic: national conditions, a people-centred orientation, civilizational foundations, reform as driving force, and problem orientation.

Bao contends that national conditions are the logical starting point. China is a socialist developing country of over 1.4 billion people still in the primary stage of socialism, so it must follow general laws of modernization without copying Western models. The author reads the five Chinese characteristics set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as showing the unity of the universal and the particular. The people-centred strand is grounded in the Marxist idea of the people as historical subject. Bao lists six elements of traditional culture (humanism, moral self-cultivation, family-state sentiment, renewal, harmony, holistic thinking) and five features of Chinese civilization (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness, peacefulness) as the cultural root of Chinese modernization. On reform, Bao stresses a 'competent market' and 'capable government', new quality productive forces and the modernization of institutions. The final strand names problems still to be solved, among them uneven development, institutional obstacles, outdated thinking, formalism and corruption.

Bao concludes that the theoretical system gives the Two Integrations richer content and shows the 'truth-power' of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times in building an autonomous body of knowledge. The author holds that Chinese modernization, led by the Communist Party, has broken the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers developing countries a Chinese approach. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party theorists organise the logic of the Chinese modernization theory.
quoteEn: The essence and quintessence of the theoretical system of Chinese modernization lie in adhering to the Two Integrations.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化理论体系的本质和精髓在于坚持“两个结合”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. Deng Xiaoping used a similar phrase in 1979, and it was elaborated by Xi Jinping, notably at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second was added in Xi Jinping's formulation of 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official judgment that China remains at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism, which Deng Xiaoping's reform-era theory used to justify market mechanisms and long-term development.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, linked to high-quality development.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the ongoing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the present era.

t: Mao Zedong's wisdom of struggle and its contemporary value
zh: 毛泽东的斗争智慧及其当代价值
paras: Chen Long asks what lay behind Mao Zedong's approach to struggle and what it offers the Party today. Starting from the 2021 Party resolution on history, which holds that all achievements came through continuous struggle, the article argues that Mao's "wisdom of struggle" is not personal calculation or mere stratagem. In Chen's account it is a multi-dimensional whole made up of an ideological foundation, value orientation, strategy and method, and fighting spirit.

The article first traces the objective and subjective conditions that shaped this wisdom: China's semi-colonial, semi-feudal condition, the lessons of two victories and two defeats in the revolution, the absence of precedent for building socialism, and Mao's early reading, Hunan culture and personal temperament. Four sections then take up the ideological foundation, the values, the strategic and tactical methods, and the spiritual will. A final section draws five lessons for the present, set within Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Chen contends that Mao's wisdom has a double theoretical root: struggle must be guided by scientific theory, and new theory must be created in struggle, as in On Practice, On Contradiction and On the Ten Major Relationships. Its values are a bright future for China, socialism and communism, and serving the people wholeheartedly, with policy set independently from investigation of actual conditions. On method, Chen stresses unities of strategic judgement and tactical decision, of principle and flexibility, and of unity and struggle, together with the formula "just, advantageous, restrained" and the pursuit of initiative. Chen presents the spirit of struggle as public-minded conduct, courage that does not fear ghosts, and confidence in victory grounded in a scientific view of contradictions.

For today, Chen calls for grasping the new historical characteristics of the great struggle and seizing initiative, and for consolidating the theoretical foundation through Xi Jinping's innovative theory. Chen also stresses keeping a socialist direction and upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee, citing the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and for training cadres through practice and reviving their fighting spirit. Chen concludes that learning from Mao's wisdom will help the Party win new victories in the new era. Read the original if you want to see how Party scholarship presents Mao's thought on struggle as a resource for current Party-building and ideological work.
quoteEn: An important mark distinguishing Mao Zedong's wisdom of struggle from vulgarised scheming and calculation is that it contains a lofty social ideal and has direction, standpoint and principle.
quoteZh: 毛泽东的斗争智慧区别于庸俗化的谋略算计的一个重要标志，就是内蕴崇高的社会理想，是有方向、有立场、有原则的。

glossary.explanation: The official Party framework for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022), presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated especially with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity.
A formulation from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party's requirement to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

t: The composite narrative of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的复合叙事
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2026 no. 1
paras: Zhao Yong and He Zhengtao ask what kind of story Chinese modernization tells, and how it differs from the narratives that have dominated accounts of modernization. Using narratology, they argue that Chinese modernization forms a new narrative paradigm, a "composite narrative" (fuhe xushi). In their account it is composite in four dimensions: narrator, narratee, story and discourse. The authors present it as going beyond the logic of capital and as promoting the coexistence of plural civilizations.

The article has four parts. It first analyses Western modernization narrative, both classical modernization theory and the postmodern narrative that arose in reaction to it, along the four narratological dimensions. It then sets out how the composite narrative takes shape in each dimension, in the form of a community of narration, a community of shared values, a social organism and a space-time continuum. A third part gives its philosophical grounding, and a fourth its significance for the world. Marx, Engels, Lenin, Hegel, Habermas, Žižek, Byung-Chul Han and Xi Jinping are among the sources drawn on.

Zhao and He argue that classical narrative has an abstract, elite narrator, a hidden narratee, a single storyline of capital accumulation and an omniscient viewpoint. Postmodern narrative, they say, dissolves narrator, narratee and chronology into fragments and ends in a "narrative vacuum". The Chinese composite narrative is said to respond with the people, led by the Communist Party, as the real narrators. It treats civilizations as both narrators and listeners, runs economic, political, cultural, social and ecological storylines in parallel ("parallel" rather than "serial" development), and joins past, present and future while remaining rooted in China and open to the world. The authors insist this is not eclecticism. They ground it in the concrete universal, the unity of subjective narrative and objective reality tested in practice, and a systems approach.

The authors conclude that the composite narrative breaks the discursive monopoly of "modernization equals Westernization" and moves beyond capital logic with "the people first" as its anchor. They also hold that it offers the Global South a model for pursuing modernization with autonomy, balancing growth and equity. They further claim that it anticipates a general trend toward a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese theorists apply narratology and Marxist philosophy to present Chinese modernization as a distinct discursive paradigm.
quoteEn: The composite narrative of Chinese modernization is a "global narrative grounded in the local": it avoids the spatial disorder of blindly aligning with the world and the spatial isolation of one-sidedly stressing localization, and achieves the continuous and organic unity of time and space in the narrative.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化复合叙事是一种“立足本土的全球叙事”，它避免因盲目接轨世界而导致的空间失序，也杜绝因片面强调本土化而变成空间孤岛，实现了叙事中时间和空间的连续贯通和有机统一。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state formulation of China's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for developing countries, whom China presents as partners in an alternative to Western-led modernization.

t: The discourse of the "salient hallmark" of the Communist Party of China in the new era: construction and effectiveness
zh: 新时代中国共产党“显著标志”话语建构及效能
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2026 no. 1
paras: How should the Communist Party of China be described and labelled? Lin and He take up this question through the phrase "salient hallmark" (xianzhu biaozhi), which Xi Jinping has repeatedly used since the 18th Party Congress (2012), usually prefaced by "distinguishing it from other political parties". The authors argue that this discourse is a comparative, value-laden, historical and forward-looking concept that expresses the Party's nature, purpose and mission. They present it as a resource for building an autonomous body of knowledge in Party history and Party building.

The article has four parts. It first sets out four types of "hallmark": courage in self-reform, standing firmly with the people, promoting the Party's glorious traditions and fine work style, and letting self-reform lead social revolution. It then analyses how the discourse is constructed, identifies three regularities in its construction, and ends with six functions or effects of the discourse. It cites Mao Zedong's 1945 report On Coalition Government and Xi's speeches, Party resolutions and the Party Constitution.

On construction, the authors argue that the discourse rests on the Party's nature, with its purpose (serving the people wholeheartedly) as its value core. It carries historical continuity, citing Mao's 1945 use of "salient mark" and the investigation-and-research campaigns of 1960–61 and 2023. It is also developmental, responding to new-era questions: self-reform answers how to govern the Party, and the people's standpoint answers whom the Party serves. The regularities are that the discourse serves full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, applies historical materialism, and stresses the initiative of individual Party members. Its effects, in the authors' account, are building ideological consensus, political mobilisation, consolidating long-term governance by winning popular support, distinguishing Party culture, raising Party soft power and shaping a better Party and government work style.

Lin and He conclude that the discourse has theoretical, methodological and practical value. In their view, studying such identifying concepts can supply a paradigm for an autonomous knowledge system in Party history and Party building, and the hallmark discourse can strengthen Party members' commitment, deepen Party–mass ties and support Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a close account of how Party theorists treat Xi's "hallmark" formulations as a discourse system and what functions they assign to it.
quoteEn: The "salient hallmark" is a comparative concept, and reflecting the Party's nature is the foundation of constructing the discourse.
quoteZh: “显著标志”是一个对比性概念，体现党的性质是话语建构的根本

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line since the 18th Party Congress (2012) stressing strict discipline, anti-corruption work and Party-building. It is treated as part of the Four-pronged Comprehensive Strategy.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continual cleansing and renewal of itself. Officially it is presented as the second answer to the question of escaping the 'historical cycle' of rise and decline.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership. It was given prominence at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for features said to distinguish the Communist Party of China from other parties, such as self-reform and the people's standpoint.

t: Paths to enhancing the Communist Party of China's international discourse power: reflections based on the new form of human civilization
zh: 论中国共产党国际话语权的提升路径——基于人类文明新形态的思考
paras: How can the Communist Party of China turn its achievements into greater influence over international opinion, rules and agendas? Wang Qiang argues that the new form of human civilization supplies both the value core and the strategic angle for this task. In Wang's account it lets the Party move from reactive rebuttal to initiative in the international ideological struggle.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how the new form of human civilization supports the Party's discourse power, through its theoretical roots and its claimed transcendence of capitalist modernization. The second analyses structural obstacles: Western discourse hegemony, the gap in cross-cultural understanding, and weaknesses in international communication. The third proposes a four-in-one path of value guidance, practical support, innovation in communication and a win-win pattern.

Wang grounds the new civilizational form in historical materialism, the Two Integrations and Chinese modernization. Wang lists its defining traits as putting the people first, peaceful development, win-win cooperation and a shared destiny, and contrasts each with a capitalist logic of capital, hegemony and zero-sum games. The proposals follow three shifts. The first is from 'geyi' (explaining Chinese ideas through Western categories) to 'reverse geyi', which means producing core concepts across languages and building an autonomous knowledge system. The second is from supplying public goods to leading a development paradigm, for example presenting the Belt and Road Initiative as a development philosophy set against the 'Washington Consensus' and seeking rule-setting power in areas such as AI governance. The third is from issue-based alliances to a 'community of consensus', through a Global South development community, layered dialogue, 'translator-type' scholars and institutional platforms.

Wang concludes that raising the Party's discourse power is no longer a technical matter of telling China's story in language the world understands. It has become a question of exchange between civilizations, which needs long-term strategic planning rather than piecemeal tactics. The article presents this as serving national rejuvenation and China's contribution to humanity's shared challenges. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links civilizational theory to concrete proposals on international communication and conceptual strategy.
quoteEn: Raising our international discourse power is no longer a technical question of 'telling China's story in language the world can understand'; it has been upgraded into a question of exchange between civilizations.
quoteZh: 我方国际话语权提升不再是“用世界听得懂的语言讲中国故事”的技术问题，而是升级为文明交往问题。

glossary.en: the new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation in Party discourse, used since the 2021 centenary of the Party, for the civilization said to be created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as going beyond Western capitalist modernization.
The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for China's path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
China's international infrastructure and connectivity initiative, launched in 2013.
A term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse often treats as partners and a constituency.

t: The narrative structure and contemporary value of the discourse of "standing on the side of human civilizational progress"
zh: “站在人类文明进步一边”话语的叙事结构与时代价值
paras: Against the background of accelerating global change, the article asks how the Chinese Party-state's political formula of "standing on the side of human civilizational progress" can be understood and conveyed as a coherent discourse. Lü argues that the formula, used by Xi Jinping and in the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, answers the question "where is human civilization heading?" and offers a Chinese approach to building a new order among civilizations.

The article has three parts. The first traces the discourse's origins in theory (Marxist world-history and civilizational-interaction theory), in history (lessons from socialism's development and the Soviet collapse) and in present needs (geopolitical conflict and the rise of the Global South). The second sets out its narrative structure as four linked layers: ontological, epistemological, axiological and practical. The third assesses its contemporary value for Marxist theory, for Chinese civilization and for global civilizational governance.

Lü's central move is the four-layer structure. Ontologically, civilization is a balanced whole of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilizations, within a single human community. Epistemologically, it rests on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and rejects linear history and the "clash of civilizations". Axiologically, it promotes "common values of all humanity" against what the author calls capitalist "universal values", an ideological tool of hegemony. Practically, it is carried out through the four global initiatives (security, development, civilization, governance) and the Belt and Road Initiative. Lü also holds that China's own path, built on Chinese modernization and the Two Integrations, disproves the "end of history" thesis and offers developing countries an alternative.

Lü concludes that the discourse extends Marxist world-history theory by stressing the conscious agency of civilizational actors and a "harmony and coexistence" model of interaction. It also guides the creative transformation of Chinese civilization and gives global governance an action framework built on consultation, fair rules and balanced development. The author presents it as a public good that China offers to humanity at a historical crossroads. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese theorists systematise Xi Jinping's civilizational rhetoric into ontology, epistemology, axiology and practice.
quoteEn: The discourse of "standing on the side of human civilizational progress" does not abandon China's own cultural subjectivity, but stresses rebuilding that subjectivity through integration into the world.
quoteZh: “站在人类文明进步一边”话语并非放弃自身文化主体性，而是强调在融入世界中重构主体性。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It is prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese official discourse to describe China's place among them.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation programme launched in 2013. The article presents it as an example of the Global Civilization Initiative in practice.
A formula Xi Jinping introduced in 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. It is offered as an alternative to Western "universal values".

glossary.zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议、全球治理倡议
glossary.pinyin: quánqiú fāzhǎn chàngyì, quánqiú ānquán chàngyì, quánqiú wénmíng chàngyì, quánqiú zhìlǐ chàngyì
glossary.explanation: Four proposals Xi Jinping advanced in 2021–2025 on development, security, civilization and governance. China presents them as public goods for international cooperation.

t: The theme, main thread, historical experience and contemporary features of the Communist Party of China's theoretical innovation
zh: 中国共产党推进理论创新的主题主线、历史经验和时代特点
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2026 no. 6
paras: This article asks what has driven and shaped the Communist Party of China's theoretical innovation over more than a century. Ai and Zhang answer that the Party's innovation has one theme, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and one main thread, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Its fundamental route is the Two Integrations. The authors say earlier scholarship, Chinese and foreign, lacked a broad historical view and neglected the theme, and they set out to supply it.

The article has three parts. The first traces the theme through four periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. For each it names the main task, the question to be answered and the resulting theory. The second part draws historical experience from the Party's resolutions on history. The third identifies features of theoretical innovation since the 18th Party Congress (2012), grouped in five pairs of principles.

In the authors' account, each period's thought answers a distinct problem. Mao Zedong's thought answers how to make revolution in a peasant-majority country, and his theory of contradictions answers how to build socialism. Deng Xiaoping's theory answers what socialism is, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era answers the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. The historical experience they list is: seeking truth from facts; the Two Integrations; testing truth in practice; grasping the trend of the times; the people's standpoint; and theoretical education within the Party. The five contemporary pairings are Party leadership with the people's principal role, self-confidence with openness, upholding fundamentals with innovation, mission with problem-orientation, and systematic thinking with precision.

The authors conclude that Xi Jinping Thought makes original contributions to developing Marxism, citing Chinese modernization, whole-process people's democracy and the Party's self-reform among others. They propose three tasks: systematising and theorising Xi Jinping Thought to build a Chinese independent knowledge system; pursuing the Second Integration to build a Marxist cultural system linking past and present; and combining "bringing in" with "going global" to broaden the international reach of Chinese Marxism. Read the original if you want a periodised, officially aligned account of how Party theory presents its own history and method, with Party documents and leaders' statements as its main sources.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's theoretical innovation revolves around one theme, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and runs along one main thread, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 中国共产党推进理论创新，围绕一个主题，这就是实现中华民族伟大复兴；贯穿一条主线，这就是推进马克思主义中国化时代化

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'. Xi Jinping has linked it to the Chinese Dream.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each era. The 'times' element was added to the older 'Sinification of Marxism', associated with Mao's 1938 formulation.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (first integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (second integration, added by Xi Jinping in 2023).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
Official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and as a basis for the national rejuvenation.
Xi-era concept of the Party's continuous self-purification and discipline, presented as the answer to how the Party can escape the 'historical cycle' of rise and decline.
Official description of China's democracy, introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019, stressing popular participation in every stage of governance rather than only in elections.

t: The value orientation of closely combining investment in things with investment in people
zh: 投资于物与投资于人紧密结合的价值旨归
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 8 June 2026, asks what value order should govern the relation between material capital accumulation and human development. Wang Wencheng argues that closely combining "investment in things" with "investment in people" is more than an economic policy line. In the author's account it is a fundamental value programme grounded in historical materialism, and it marks a transformation in China's philosophy of development.

The piece opens by contrasting Western modernization, which Wang says is driven by capital logic and prioritises material capital and wealth growth, with the shift to high-quality development in China. It defines investment in things as spending on material capital, infrastructure, industry, equipment and the environment. It defines investment in people as spending on education, health care, elderly care, employment, training, social security and cultural life. Two main sections follow, one on the historical-materialist meaning of the combination and one on its implications for social justice and state governance. The author draws on the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee and the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan.

Wang's core argument works on three levels. On the subject of development, people are the subject and material things the condition. On its driving force, Wang uses Marx's account of three forms of productive force, culminating in one led by general intellect, and links new quality productive forces to the combination of the two investments. On its purpose, human development is the end and material growth the means. Wang holds that the two forms of investment are dialectically unified. This rejects both utopianism that ignores the material base and the "thing-centred" worship of material capital, and it is said to answer liberalism's formalism and utilitarianism's focus on aggregates.

Wang concludes that the combination is the path to substantive justice and common prosperity, through equalised public services and broad investment in human capital. It also strengthens state governance by turning institutional advantages into governance effectiveness. In the author's view it offers a Chinese solution that moves beyond the alienation of capital logic by guiding and regulating capital so that it serves the people. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-aligned philosophers ground the current economic policy line in Marx's theory of alienation and productive forces.
quoteEn: Upholding the combination of the two means upholding the basic stance of historical materialism. It opposes both a utopianism that ignores the material base and a thing-centred doctrine that worships material capital, and it ultimately achieves an organic unity of the measure of things and the measure of people, and of conformity to laws and conformity to purpose.
quoteZh: 坚持二者结合，就是坚持历史唯物主义的基本立场，既反对忽视物质基础的空想主义，也反对崇拜物质资本的物本主义，最终实现物的尺度与人的尺度、合规律性与合目的性的有机统一。

glossary.zh: 投资于物与投资于人紧密结合
glossary.pinyin: tóuzī yú wù yǔ tóuzī yú rén jǐnmì jiéhé
glossary.en: closely combining investment in things with investment in people
glossary.literal: investing in things and investing in people closely combined
glossary.explanation: A policy formula in recent Party documents that pairs spending on physical capital and infrastructure with spending on education, health, social security and similar areas. The article treats it as a value principle as well as an economic policy.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, technology and high-quality factor combinations.
A stated socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which Party leaders have emphasised in recent years.
The official guiding concept for the economy since the late 2010s. It stresses quality, innovation and balance over speed of growth.

t: A brief analysis of the development of understanding of Mao Zedong Thought and its scientific connotations
zh: 关于毛泽东思想及其科学内涵的认识发展简析
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2025 no. 12
paras: Sun Jinbao asks how the Chinese Communist Party's understanding of the "scientific connotations" of Mao Zedong Thought (its name, concept, content and historical evaluation) has developed over time. The article argues that this understanding has deepened continuously through three stages and offers a model of Party theoretical innovation. It also presents the study as a basis for systematic, scholarly work on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article proceeds chronologically through Party documents and leaders' statements. It begins with the new-democratic revolution, from Li Dazhao and the 1938 proposal of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, through Zhang Ruxin, Wang Jiaxiang and Liu Shaoqi, to the 7th Party Congress (1945). It then covers the period after 1949 and the reform era around the 1981 Resolution on certain questions in the Party's history. Finally it takes up the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including Xi Jinping's speeches on Mao's anniversaries and the 2021 historical resolution.

Sun makes three central moves. First, the 1945 formula (the unity of Marxist-Leninist theory and Chinese revolutionary practice) was refined after 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. Mao Zedong Thought came to be defined as correct principles and experience \"proven by practice\" concerning revolution and construction, a product of collective wisdom, and as part of Marxism-Leninism rather than separate from it. Second, in Sun's reading the \"living soul\" (seeking truth from facts, the mass line, independence and self-reliance) carries the methodological value of the thought. Third, since 2012 Mao has been described as a great pioneer of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, and Mao Zedong Thought as the first historic leap. Sun says this wording stresses its creativity and its foundational status, and it rejects efforts to \"de-Maoify\" the Party's history as historical nihilism.

Sun concludes that the Party's understanding should be grasped as a whole, uniting history with reality, documents with practice, and upholding fundamental principles with innovation. The article holds that the logic and methods of theoretical innovation in Mao Zedong Thought remain applicable. It says they offer a reference point for studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a document-based account of how official formulations of Mao Zedong Thought changed from the 1940s to the 2021 resolution.
quoteEn: Not every sentence Mao Zedong said or every judgement he put forward belongs to Mao Zedong Thought, and conjectures not yet tested in practice cannot be counted as part of it.
quoteZh: 并非毛泽东说过的每句话、提出的每个论断都属于毛泽东思想，未经实践检验的设想不能归入毛泽东思想

glossary.explanation: The 1981 historical resolution's term for the standpoint, viewpoint and method running through Mao Zedong Thought. It is usually listed as seeking truth from facts, the mass line, and independence and self-reliance.

An official periodisation in which Mao Zedong Thought is the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to China, and later theoretical achievements are further leaps. The 2021 resolution speaks of a first leap and two 'new' leaps.

glossary.zh: 关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议
glossary.pinyin: Guānyú jiànguó yǐlái dǎng de ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
glossary.en: 1981 Resolution on certain questions in the Party's history
glossary.explanation: A resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1981. It assessed Mao Zedong and the post-1949 period and defined Mao Zedong Thought.
In official Party usage, a label for views that deny or distort the Party's revolutionary history and leaders such as Mao Zedong.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party Constitution in 2017.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: The inherent logic of the military and the economy: studying Mao Zedong's military-economic thought
zh: 军事与经济的内在逻辑——学习毛泽东军事经济思想
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2025 no. 12
paras: Qiao Yuting asks how Mao Zedong understood the relationship between war and the economy, and between national defence and economic construction. The article argues that this military-economic thought is a relatively complete and internally consistent system. It is presented as a component of Mao Zedong Thought that applies basic Marxist principles to Chinese conditions and is marked by scientific rigour, subjectivity (zhutixing) and practical orientation. Qiao maintains that it still offers guidance for handling major relationships in the new era.

The article first sets out the system's overall logic at three levels: a fundamental stance, a main line of argument and methodological principles. It then divides the thought chronologically. The first part is the wartime economic thought of the New Democratic Revolution, covering land revolution, base-area construction, army economic systems, wartime supply, mobilisation and the shift to peacetime. The second part is the national-defence economic thought after 1949. A final section draws lessons for the present.

In Qiao's account, the fundamental stance is the people's standpoint, drawn from the historical-materialist view that the masses make history, and it runs through people's war and the army's character. The main line is the dialectical unity of military and economy: the economic base determines politics and the military, and shifts in the principal contradiction set which of the two takes priority. Wartime economic work served the revolutionary war, while after 1949 economic construction came first so that defence could advance. The methodology rests on seeking truth from facts, independence and self-reliance, and overall planning ("playing the piano"). Qiao cites later policies such as the Third Front, "preparing for war and natural disasters, and doing everything for the people", the "two fists and one backside" formula, and civil-military integration.

Qiao concludes that the thought still has "lasting theoretical vitality" and draws four implications for Chinese modernization. These are to keep a bottom-line mindset and plan security in advance; to treat national-defence modernization as part of overall modernization; to build civil-military and peacetime-wartime integration, including new quality productive forces and new quality combat capability; and to pursue self-reliance in core technologies while opening up critically. Qiao also calls for data-property, distribution and security systems that spread the gains of the digital economy fairly, and for adapting people's war to new fields of competition. Read the original if you study Mao Zedong Thought or Chinese defence-economic thinking, or want to see how current security and technology policy is linked to Mao-era ideas.
quoteEn: The main logical line of Mao Zedong's military-economic thought lies in the theoretical elaboration and practical application of the dialectical unity of the military and the economy as a fundamental pair of contradictions.
quoteZh: 毛泽东军事经济思想的逻辑主线，在于对军事与经济这一基本矛盾范畴的辩证统一关系的理论阐释与实践运用。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and innovation.
A large programme from the mid-1960s to build industrial and defence facilities in China's interior, as a strategic rear area against the threat of war.
A policy of linking the defence and civilian sectors in technology, industry and resources. Xi Jinping elevated it to a national strategy.

glossary.en: preparing for war and natural disasters, and doing everything for the people
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the mid-1960s based on Mao Zedong's instruction and summarised by Zhou Enlai, guiding planning with attention to war readiness and disaster relief.

t: How Mao Zedong summed up the experience of revolutionary war: a reading of the telegrams he drafted for the Central Committee and Military Commission during the War of Liberation
zh: 毛泽东如何总结革命战争经验——解放战争时期代为中央（军委）起草电报解读
source: Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping Theory Studies, 2025 no. 12
paras: Chen Dong asks how Mao Zedong drew lessons from fighting during the War of Liberation (1946–49). The source base is the large body of telegrams he drafted on behalf of the Central Committee and the Central Military Commission. Chen argues that Mao built a mechanism of four linked stages: acquiring experience, summing up experience, reviewing experience and learning experience. In this account, summation stopped being a post-war retrospective and became a method of leadership that ran through the whole war.

The article begins with Mao's 1965 remark that he lived by 'summing up experience'. It then moves through the war's phases. It first treats how the Party was led to acquire experience for new tasks: siege warfare with explosives, the shift from dispersed guerrilla to concentrated mobile warfare, 'warfare without a rear', and the reporting system. Next come the strategic lessons Mao summed up, then the review of failures, and finally the channels through which lessons were passed on. It closes by linking this method to Xi Jinping's present-day remarks on experience.

Chen's central claim is that operational principles came out of concrete battles and were then turned into directives for the whole army. Examples include concentrating superior force to destroy the enemy one by one, drawn from the Longhai railway, Dingtao and northern Jiangsu engagements, and the 'mushroom' tactics of wearing the enemy down. They also include the 'ten major principles of operation'. Reviewing experience was handled from the top down through criticism of unprepared battles, failure to concentrate force and complacency, with the Jinmen defeat as the main warning. It was also built into routine practice, through reviews in the pauses between battles and a reporting system that demanded analytical reports. Learning ran through four channels: circulating successes, forwarding subordinates' reports, promoting model battles, and exchanging approaches between theatres. Chen says this let the centre guide the war without 'remote control' and sustained morale.

Chen concludes that Mao's treatment of wartime experience followed Marxist epistemology and let the Party correct its strategy and tactics continuously. The article presents this as a tradition the Party has inherited in the new era. It cites Xi Jinping on piloting reforms by 'crossing the river by feeling for the stones', and on treating failed experience as valuable. Read the original if you want a source-based account, built on Mao's telegrams, of how experience was turned into command doctrine in the Chinese civil war.
quoteEn: It was through this continuous reflection that several operational principles of overall significance were consolidated and deepened, and that wartime experience truly rose to strategic self-awareness.
quoteZh: 正是在这种持续反思中，若干具有全局意义的作战原则得到巩固和深化，也使战争经验真正上升为战略自觉。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese Communist Party's name for the final phase of the civil war with the Nationalists, from mid-1946 to 1949. The article also calls it the Third Revolutionary Civil War.

glossary.literal: system of requesting instructions and reporting
glossary.explanation: A Party discipline system, set out by Mao in 1948, under which subordinate bodies seek instructions beforehand and report afterwards to the centre.
Mao's colloquial term for wearing a strong enemy down through patience and manoeuvre before destroying it.
A summary of the People's Liberation Army's operational principles, which Mao drew up in late 1947 from a year of fighting.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling for the stones
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with reform-era policy making, meaning to experiment step by step and generalise what works. The article cites Xi Jinping using it.

t: The major significance of Mao Zedong's discourse system of "the people"
zh: 毛泽东人民话语体系的重大意义
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2025 no. 12
paras: Li Youxin and Lei Chengwen examine Mao Zedong's discourse system centred on "the people", which they describe as comprising discourses of the people as subject, people's democracy, serving the people and the mass line. The article argues that this system transformed Marxist class discourse into a people-centred political discourse suited to Chinese conditions. It further holds that the system is the ideological source and value foundation of the discourse system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article begins with the concept of "the people" within the whole discourse system, then contrasts it with classical Marxist class discourse. It traces how the content of "the people" shifted across the stages of the revolution (from the New Democratic revolution through the anti-Japanese and liberation wars) and into socialist construction. It then turns to what the discourse says about the Party's nature, stance and purpose, and ends with its legacy under Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping.

The authors argue that in the classical works of Marx, Engels and Lenin the peasantry was an ally but not an independent historical subject. Mao, analysing semi-colonial, semi-feudal China, where the proletariat was small and the peasantry the great majority, made peasants a main revolutionary force. He also defined "the people" through the "enemy, us, friends" distinction, so that the concept was historical and dynamic rather than tied to a single class. The authors describe four levels of the system: a historical view (the people as the driving force of history), a value orientation (serving the people wholeheartedly, written into the Party constitution at the Seventh Party Congress in 1945), an institutional design (people's democratic dictatorship) and a practical method (the mass line). On this basis they say the discourse defined the Party as a vanguard that represents the broadest people's interests, in contrast to what they portray as bourgeois parties serving particular interests.

The authors conclude that Mao's system gave the discourse of socialism with Chinese characteristics its people-centred ideological base, its core topics and its principles of plain, popular expression. They present later leaders' formulations, including Xi Jinping's "people first", as inheriting and deepening it. They add that, in a setting where China's international discourse power is described as relatively weak, it offers resources for building a discourse system with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a detailed account, from a Mao Zedong Thought research centre, of how the concept of "the people" is used to link Mao's revolutionary theory to today's Party discourse.
quoteEn: Building on the Marxist method of class analysis and starting from the concrete realities of the Chinese revolution, Mao Zedong raised the historical standing of the Chinese peasantry as a subject.
quoteZh: 毛泽东在继承马克思主义阶级分析法的基础上，立足中国革命具体实际，提升了中国农民的历史主体地位。

t: The theoretical content and global significance of the distinctive view of democracy embodied in Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化蕴含独特民主观的理论内涵与世界意义
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu Yanjiu), 2025 no. 11
