Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Culture was added to the earlier three in 2016.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second, added in 2021–23).
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping from 2023: a nation's self-awareness and initiative in cultural creation, treated as the basis of cultural confidence.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's exploration of "Chinese experience" and "Chinese theory" in the New Democratic Revolution period
zh: 新民主主义革命时期中国共产党对“中国经验”和“中国理论”的探索
paras: Zhou Jiabin asks how the Chinese Communist Party (CPC) came to summarise its revolutionary practice as "Chinese experience" and raise it to "Chinese theory" with a world-wide significance. Noting that existing scholarship mostly treats these concepts from a domestic ("China dimension") angle, the article takes the "world dimension" and looks back to the New Democratic Revolution period (1921–1949). Its thesis is that the current stress on "Chinese experience" and "Chinese theory" under Xi Jinping has deep historical roots and developed through five stages.

The article periodises the CPC's exploration into germination (1921–1922), initial stage (1922–1928), development (1928–1935), maturity (1935–1945) and deepening (1945–1949). It follows the Party's relations with the Comintern, with episodes such as Zhang Tailei's revision of the Comintern's classification of colonial and semi-colonial countries, the May Thirtieth Movement and proletarian leadership, armed separatist bases and the Soviet regime, the Zunyi Meeting, the Sinification of Marxism, Mao Zedong Thought, and Liu Shaoqi's 1949 "formula" of the revolutionary road. It also draws on evidence of how other communist parties received Chinese experience.

Zhou argues that the Party moved from individual to organisational summaries of experience, and from applying existing Marxist-Leninist positions to original innovation, notably armed separatism, which departed from the Russian model of armed uprising. After the Zunyi Meeting, in the author's account, a strong sense of the revolution's own subjectivity emerged, and Mao's formulation of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context turned scattered experience into systematic theory. The author reads the theory of New Democracy as one drawn from Chinese experience but meant to apply to colonial and semi-colonial revolutions generally. By 1949 the Party, Zhou says, treated propagating this experience abroad as a responsibility, citing Stalin's remarks on a division of labour and messages from parties such as Thailand's.

Zhou draws three lessons for the present. The formation of Chinese experience and theory was historically necessary, driven by practical needs of the communist movement and by Marxism's own demand for unity of the universal and the particular. It was a long process combining continuity and stages. And the two are related as source and stream, root and crown: experience is the basis of theory, and theory is its systematised result. The author calls on the Party to dig deeper into Chinese practice, refine theory from it and advance adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history account of the Comintern relationship and of how the Chinese revolution is presented as an internationally relevant source of theory.)
quoteEn: "Chinese experience" is the premise and basis for the formation of "Chinese theory", and "Chinese theory" is the basic direction and inevitable result of the development of "Chinese experience".
quoteZh: “中国经验”是“中国理论”形成的前提和基础，“中国理论”是“中国经验”发展的基本方向和必然结果。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for each era. The earlier term "Sinification of Marxism" was proposed by Mao Zedong in 1938.
In this article, the concrete, scattered ideas and practices that the CPC drew from the Chinese revolution, as opposed to the systematised "Chinese theory".
The systematic body of theory raised from Chinese experience. For the revolutionary period the author identifies it with Mao Zedong Thought.
Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution of 1919–1949: a bourgeois-democratic revolution in the colonial and semi-colonial context led by the proletariat and the Communist Party.

The strategy of building armed forces and rural base areas under CPC control, associated with Mao Zedong in the late 1920s and 1930s. The article contrasts it with the short-lived armed uprising of the October Revolution model.
The Party's guiding ideology, regarded officially as Marxism-Leninism adapted to China. It was written into the Party constitution at the Seventh Party Congress in 1945.

t: The Communist Party of China's development concepts and their development in the new era
zh: 中国共产党发展理念及其在新时代的发展
paras: Qiu Gengtian asks what the Communist Party of China's "development concepts" are, why they arose and how they have changed since 1949, especially in the new era. The author argues that these concepts form a coherent system of Marxist ideas about China's development. They have been continuous in basic orientation while changing with practice, and today they are centred on Chinese modernization and the new development philosophy. The article follows a method that unites logic and history.

The article first sets out four dimensions through which the Party leads development: practice, theory, discourse and emotion. It then describes the content of the concepts as four theoretical blocks: ontology, epistemology, axiology and methodology. It identifies five features (practical, people-oriented, dialectical, stage-specific, innovative) and four logics (practical, political, reform and world). It ends with the concepts' evolution from the revolutionary period through the reform era to the present.

Qiu holds that practice and theory are the two original sides of development, while discourse and emotion are derivative. Development ontology, the author argues, gives development supreme status as both end and means, a "fundamental law" for solving all problems, and Qiu cites the cost of earlier neglect of productive forces. Development epistemology is framed through information theory: knowledge removes blind spots and uncertainty and so makes development safer. Axiology asks "development for whom" and answers with the people-centred approach; methodology stresses overall planning and systems thinking. The political logic treats development as the "greatest politics" that must prove the superiority of socialism, and the world logic ties China's progress to its contribution to humanity.

Qiu concludes that, since the 20th Party Congress (2022), modernization has been the "main thread" and "underlying colour" of the Party's development concepts. The author therefore calls for those concepts to be built into a theoretical system of Chinese modernization, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On this view the new development philosophy is the main form of development thinking in the new era. Its five concepts (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) are matched to the dynamics, relationships, ecology, external environment and common prosperity of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Party theorists organise the philosophy of development from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: The Party's development concepts are, in essence, the theoretical ideas about China's socialist modernization drive.
quoteZh: 党的发展理念就是关于中国社会主义现代化建设的理论观念。

glossary.explanation: A set of five concepts (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 to guide economic and social development. Official texts treat it as the main form of the Party's development thinking in the new era.

The official name for China's path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as having distinctive Chinese features and as a way of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people. It is linked in Party discourse to the sharing concept and to Chinese modernization.

t: A historical-materialist interpretation of "the Party's self-reform focuses on governing power"
zh: “党的自我革命重在治权”的唯物史观阐释
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 10 February 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection that the Party's self-reform focuses on governing power, and that putting power into the cage of institutions is an important task of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Jin argues that this emphasis can be explained through historical materialism, and that it gives the Party a firm guarantee for achieving the goals of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
The article is organised in three parts: the historical grounding of the focus on governing power, the role of institutions in directing it, and the people as the value to which it belongs.

Jin first draws on Marx and Engels to argue that, in class society, power is coercive and tied to particular interests, so it risks deviating and must be supervised by society. The Party's answer, in this account, joins supervision by the people (the first answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall, given by Mao Zedong in the 1945 Yan'an cave dialogue) with self-reform (the second answer). Jin then holds that governing power depends on institutions: since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the eight-point rules and many Party regulations and laws have aimed to curb rent-seeking and the entwining of misconduct and corruption. Finally, Jin contends that, unlike Western bourgeois theories, Marxist supervision theory holds that power comes from the people and must be supervised by them, so supervision should target problems in education, healthcare, housing and rural areas.

Jin concludes that the Party should place popular supervision at the core of governing power, open channels and innovate methods of supervision, and keep power exercised openly. Doing so, Jin says, would let the Party keep answering the "Yan'an cave question" of the new era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame anti-corruption policy in historical-materialist terms.
quoteEn: The people are the source of state power, and all state power belongs to the people.
quoteZh: 人民是国家权力的源泉，国家一切权力属于人民。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work inside the Party.
Official term, prominent under Xi Jinping, for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself. It is presented as the Party's second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall.
The article's term for regulating and supervising the exercise of power, notably by binding it with institutions and popular oversight.

glossary.zh: 把权力关进制度的笼子
glossary.pinyin: bǎ quánlì guānjìn zhìdù de lóngzi
glossary.en: putting power into the cage of institutions
glossary.literal: lock power in the cage of institutions
glossary.explanation: A phrase associated with Xi Jinping, meaning that power should be constrained by rules and institutions.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials.

t: Grasping the dialectic of "investing in things" and "investing in people"
zh: 把握“投资于物”与“投资于人”的辩证法
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, takes up the policy formula of closely combining "investing in things" with "investing in people". Hou treats the pairing as a core question of Chinese modernization and argues that the two forms of investment form a dialectical unity of opposites. In Hou's account, things are the means and people the end, and the Party's emphasis on combining them reflects a deeper understanding of development.

The article opens by tracing the formula through Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks at the first meeting of the 20th Central Financial and Economic Commission, the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and its proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference, and Xi's January 2026 address. It then has three parts: definitions and the unity-of-opposites relationship, the understanding of development laws the formula reflects, and five practical orientations for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Hou defines investing in things as directing funds into production capacity, infrastructure, technology and reserves. Investing in people covers skills, health, culture and moral cultivation, aimed at overcoming one-sidedness and moving towards all-round development marked by "free individuality". The two compete for limited resources and differ in payback periods, yet depend on each other. Drawing on the historical-materialist idea of two yardsticks of social development, the productive forces and human development, Hou argues that relying on material inputs alone brings diminishing marginal returns. The formula, the author says, follows the shift to high-quality development and avoids the Western path centred on capital and expanding materialism.

For practice, Hou calls for five pairings: supply with demand creation, so that investment in education, healthcare and elder care raises incomes and consumption; talent with industry, through matched "talent maps" and "industry maps"; systematic planning with dynamic adjustment of investment structure; efficiency with fair distribution, through an effective market and a capable government; and domestic with international perspectives, to strengthen competitiveness. Hou presents this integrated deployment as a requirement for building a strong domestic market and a new development pattern. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how this slogan is justified theoretically and translated into policy priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Things are the means and people are the end; the ultimate value of combining the two is to make economic operations truly serve the "confirmation of human essential powers".
quoteZh: “物”是手段，“人”是目的，二者结合的最终价值归宿是使经济运行真正服务于“人的本质力量的确证”。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models and as combining material and cultural-ethical progress.
Policy term for investment in physical production capacity such as infrastructure, equipment and technology.
Policy term for spending on human capital and welfare: education, health, skills, culture and social security. It has been paired with investment in things in recent official documents.
Official term for a shift from rapid, extensive growth to growth driven by quality, efficiency and innovation.
Official strategy centred on the domestic economic cycle, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It was put forward in 2020.

t: The philosophical connotations of "investing in people"
zh: “投资于人”的哲学内涵
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily asks what philosophical content lies behind the economic phrase "investing in people". Zhang argues that the phrase expresses a deep philosophical conception and development philosophy rooted in Marxist theories of human liberation and all-round human development. The occasion is the call of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) to closely combine "investing in physical assets" with "investing in people".

The piece has two parts. The first sets out the theoretical foundations, drawing on Marx and Engels, on remarks by Xi Jinping, and on a contrast with Western capitalist modernization. The second analyses the "inner dimensions" of the idea through three lenses (value theory, practice theory and systems thinking) and then addresses how investing in people relates to investing in physical assets.

Zhang contends that investing in people does not reject the profit-seeking nature of investment but raises its direction and priorities, moving from "seeing only things" to "seeing people too". In value terms, the author says traditional investment treats people as instruments for meeting return targets and falls into "instrumental rationality". Investing in people instead makes human life, development and dignity the aim, and builds human capital as competition shifts from capital-intensive to talent-intensive. In practice terms, education, healthcare, pension and fertility-support policies are said to develop individual capacities and relieve livelihood worries, creating a virtuous circle between individual and social progress. In systems terms, such investment is described as covering the whole life cycle and expressing equal respect for development rights.

Zhang concludes that investing in people does not negate investing in physical assets. The two are dialectically unified: material investment supplies the base, while investment in people supplies the capacity to turn it into value. Each is said to fail without the other, and together they form the investment support for high-quality development. The author presents this as a scientific methodological guide for the new era and as a concrete expression of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars give a Marxist philosophical gloss to a current economic policy formula.
quoteEn: "Investing in physical assets" means putting resources into means of production and the material base; its core is to consolidate the material and technical conditions of economic and social development and to provide the necessary material guarantee for "investing in people".
quoteZh: “投资于物”是对生产资料、物质基础的投入，其核心是夯实经济社会发展的物质技术条件，为“投资于人”提供必要的物质保障；

glossary.explanation: A policy formula stressing spending on education, health, pensions, childcare and other human development, alongside investment in infrastructure and equipment. It was highlighted in Party documents of 2025.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, in place since about 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and better living standards.

t: A theoretical interpretation of the stepwise progression of socialist modernization
zh: 实现社会主义现代化阶梯式递进的学理阐释
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in January 2026, interprets a phrase from the Central Committee's Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan: that achieving socialist modernization is a historical process of "stepwise progression" requiring unremitting effort. Cao Ping argues that the formulation summarises past practice and scientifically captures the laws governing Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. It first unpacks the concept's meaning, then analyses the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) as a pivotal link in the process, and finally considers the concept's significance for the world.

Cao reads "steps" as the staged nature of development and "progression" as qualitative leaps built on quantitative accumulation, with each stage's material base, institutional results and experience forming the next stage's starting point. The plan period is presented as a connecting period between past achievements and the 2035 goal, a strategic window for high-quality development and new quality productive forces, and a period of consolidation in which high-level security protects development. Cao's security agenda includes political security, Marxism's guiding role in ideology, the Party's self-reform, and prevention of systemic risk.

Cao concludes that this path offers three lessons beyond China, as the author sees it: it challenges the equation of modernization with Westernization, it puts people's wellbeing above a capital-centred logic, and it rejects conflictual great-power rise in favour of peaceful development and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the Plan Recommendations in theoretical terms.
quoteEn: Stepwise progression embodies the necessary logic of development from lower to higher levels and from quantitative to qualitative change, and stresses that achieving socialist modernization must pass through a historical process of linked, gradually ascending stages.
quoteZh: 阶梯式递进体现了发展从较低级向高级、由量变到质变的必然逻辑，强调实现社会主义现代化必然经历前后衔接、逐步攀升的历史进程

glossary.explanation: A phrase in the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan describing modernization as a sequence of linked stages, each building on the last.
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation, especially in advanced industries and digital, green and intelligent technologies.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline itself and fight corruption, so that it keeps its character and governing capacity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations based on cooperation and shared interests, promoted since 2013.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Upholding the combination of an efficient market and a capable government
zh: 坚持有效市场和有为政府相结合
paras: This short commentary in the China Social Sciences Today (14 January 2026) takes up the principle, stressed by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), that economic and social development in the 15th Five-Year Plan period must combine an efficient market (有效市场) with a capable government (有为政府). Li Xiangxing argues that joining the market's "invisible hand" and the government's "visible hand" is the key to handling the government–market relationship correctly.

The article has three parts. It first explains why the market must decide resource allocation, then what a capable government must do and why its functions must change, and finally how the two should be combined.

Li gives four reasons for letting the market play the decisive role: it follows the general law of market economies, it allocates resources most efficiently as economic relations and needs grow complex, conditions in China are now mature after more than 40 years of reform and opening up, and it is required for deepening reform comprehensively. On government, Li holds that its role is indispensable, citing capitalist crises and China's experience, and warns against neoliberal calls for market absolutism and privatisation. Market and government have different boundaries: the market handles micro-level allocation, while government works at the macro level. Li says some government functions still carry traces of planning and calls for streamlining administration and delegating powers.

Li concludes that the two must be treated as equally important, must cooperate, and must complement each other's weaknesses. Government regulation is purposeful and forward-looking but slow, while market regulation is timely but spontaneous, blind and lagging. Combining them, Li says, uses the strengths of the market economy and of the socialist system. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official government–market formula is explained in Chinese academic commentary.
quoteEn: Macro-regulation by a capable government can make up for the shortcomings of regulation by an efficient market, while the market's regulatory mechanism can in turn make up for the weak points of government macro-regulation.
quoteZh: 有为政府的宏观调控可以弥补有效市场调节的不足，而有效市场的调节机制又可以弥补政府宏观调控的短板。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: The value implications of major-country diplomatic discourse with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 新时代中国特色大国外交话语的价值意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 12 January 2026, asks what distinguishes China's major-country diplomatic discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and what values it carries. Zhang Beiping defines diplomatic discourse as the official language of a sovereign state, marked by rigour, strategic stability and institutional constraint. The author argues that under the guidance of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought this discourse has become a complete system with a distinct style, serving to convey Chinese ideas, present China's image and take part in global governance.

The piece is organised around five features of that style: fusing ancient and modern in cultural inheritance; skilful use of metaphor; sincere emotional appeal through people-to-people exchange; a combination of firmness and flexibility; and leading global trends by supplying public goods. Each section gives examples drawn from Xi Jinping's speeches, such as classical quotations, proverbs, images like the 'ballast stone' for China–US relations, and the Belt and Road Initiative described as a painting in broad strokes and fine brushwork.

Zhang's central claim is that these devices turn abstract strategy into language that other peoples can grasp and feel. Storytelling, local-language greetings and proverbs, and the presentation of the leader as an 'old friend' are said to close cultural distance, while domestic livelihood goals such as poverty alleviation are framed as universal concerns. On the firmer side, the author says bottom-line statements on sovereignty answer Western discourse traps such as 'a strong country is bound to seek hegemony', and that the discourse transcends both the closed nationalist and the universalist liberal models. Zhang further contends that a community with a shared future for mankind works as a meta-narrative, and that the Global Development, Security, Civilization and Governance Initiatives make China a 'contributor of ideas' rather than a 'rule-taker'.

Zhang concludes that major-country diplomatic discourse is a key medium of strategic communication and value expression, and that it has formed a system with Chinese characteristics, style and manner. The author calls for further grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought and for innovating and spreading this discourse so that the world better understands China and a community with a shared future for mankind gains firmer discursive support. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics present the style and aims of official diplomatic language.
quoteEn: Only discourse that combines Chinese characteristics with world significance can more easily resonate widely with the international community.
quoteZh: 唯有兼具中国特色又具世界意义的话语表达，才能更容易引起国际社会的广泛共鸣。

glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on foreign affairs associated with Xi Jinping, presented since the 2010s as a component of Xi Jinping Thought and the guide for China's foreign policy.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13 describing a vision of interdependent global development and cooperation; it is a central slogan of Chinese foreign policy.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Understanding Chinese modernization through the "Two Integrations"
zh: 从“两个结合”看中国式现代化
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 8 January 2026
paras: Liu Yu asks why Chinese modernization differs in essence from Western modernization, and answers that the difference lies in cultural origins. In this newspaper commentary, Liu argues that Chinese modernization must be read on the long historical scale of Chinese civilization, whose "cultural pattern" guides the basic direction and inner logic of the nation's modernization.

The piece has three parts. It first defines a cultural pattern and shows how Western Christian civilization shaped Western modernization. It then describes the Chinese cultural pattern and its link to socialist modernization. Finally it presents the Two Integrations as the programme of action for Chinese modernization.

Liu contends that the Western pattern, an externally transcendent dualism of subject and object, produced a split between church and secular government. In Liu's account, this logic ran from the Renaissance through the Reformation, the Enlightenment and the industrial and bourgeois revolutions. The Chinese pattern is an ethical holism of "unity of heaven and humanity", rooted in a composite agrarian-steppe-maritime civilization and a "great unification" structure. Liu holds that China's choice of Marxism was guided by this pattern: the ideal of great harmony became the communist ideal, and the old integration of government and teaching became Party leadership and people's democracy. The "first integration" gives modernization its socialist character, while the "second" makes it modernization guided by Chinese civilization.

Liu concludes that Chinese modernization has broken the equation of modernization with Westernization and, in Liu's view, offers lessons to capitalist modernization in difficulty. Liu sees continuity between classical ideas and current Party concepts, including whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars use the idea of a civilizational "cultural pattern" to explain the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has not only broken the myth that modernization equals Westernization, but also opened a path of modernization in harmony with its own civilizational system.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化不仅打破了现代化等于西方化的迷思，开辟了与自身文明系统相协调的现代化道路

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It has been stressed in Xi Jinping-era ideology, especially since 2021–2023.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models. It was prominently formulated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019. It stresses popular participation across all stages of governance, not only voting.
Official goal of shared wealth for all people, promoted by the Party as a feature of socialism and given new emphasis under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign policy concept of global interdependence and cooperation, used since 2012–2013.

t: The scientific connotation and practical orientation of strengthening social resilience
zh: 增强社会韧性的科学内涵和实践指向
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 27 January 2026, takes up the call in the Proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), to "strengthen economic and social resilience". He and Sun define resilience as a social system's ability to keep its structure and functions under shocks and uncertainty and to emerge stronger through timely adjustment. They argue that strengthening social resilience matters for advancing Chinese modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, when strategic opportunities and risks coexist.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the resilience advantages of a "super-large-scale" country. The second explains what a resilience mindset requires of a social system. The third identifies priority areas for building resilience, and the authors tie each point to wording in the Proposals.

In the authors' account, China's advantages lie in the size of its economy and market, its complete industrial system, its extensive social security system, its governance experience, and its record of combining vitality with order. They cite figures including an economy that passed 140 trillion yuan, more than 400 million middle-income people, and 41 major industrial categories. Resilience thinking, they write, is not mere endurance but a paradigm that accepts uncertainty and stresses recovery, adjustment and active change. They break it into three capacities. Coping capacity rests on collaboration among government, social organisations, enterprises and citizens in a shared governance community. Adaptive capacity means learning from experience, shifting to prevention (including the "Fengqiao experience" and digital early-warning systems) and resolving risks before they appear. Transformative capacity means upgrading institutions towards fairness, notably through equalising basic public services.

For priority areas, the authors call for coordinating economic and social resilience, since economic strength underpins social order and welfare and governance must keep pace with growth. They also call for resilient infrastructure through "intrinsic safety" standards, life-cycle management and intelligent monitoring. A third priority is a new security pattern built on a holistic security outlook that covers physical, digital and social space, together with reform of risk governance and a higher-level "Peaceful China". Read the original if you want to see how Party-state scholars turn the resilience concept into policy priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: The best way of social governance is to dissolve contradictions before they arise and to defuse risks before they take shape.
quoteZh: 社会治理的最好办法，就是将矛盾消解于未然，将风险化解于无形。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

A local governance model from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, dating from the 1960s. It stresses resolving disputes at the grassroots by mobilising residents, so that conflicts are not passed up to higher levels. The Party has promoted it as a "new era" model.

An official phrase for a governance arrangement in which government, organisations, enterprises and citizens all take part. Its slogan is that everyone has responsibility, does their duty and shares in the benefits.
A policy goal of narrowing gaps in access to education, health care, social protection and similar services between regions, urban and rural areas, and social groups.
A concept from industrial safety engineering. It aims to build safety into the design and operation of facilities so they remain functional under shocks.
The Party's term, associated with Xi Jinping's holistic approach to national security, for treating security as covering many fields, from political and economic to cyber and social.

t: Grasping the rich connotations and practical requirements of combining rule of law with rule of virtue
zh: 深刻把握坚持依法治国和以德治国相结合的丰富内涵和实践要求
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in January 2026, explains what it means to combine governing the country by law (yifa zhiguo) with governing by virtue (yide zhiguo), and why and how this should be done. Zhou Youyong presents the principle as part of Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law and as a model of the Two Integrations, especially the integration of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. In Zhou's account, it extends the Party's understanding of how to govern and enriches Marxist legal theory.

The article has three parts. The first looks at traditional Chinese legal culture and its practice of joint rule by virtue and law. The second sets out the theoretical basis: the dialectical relationship between law and morality, and the stages by which the Party arrived at the principle from Deng Xiaoping to Hu Jintao and then after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to practical requirements for raising the rule of law to a higher level, a goal Zhou links to the Recommendations of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Zhou argues that historical experience supports the combination. Zhou reads Chinese dynastic history as showing that periods using both ritual and law, such as the Wen-Jing, Zhenguan and Kaiyuan reigns, were generally well governed, while reliance on one alone, as in the Qin, ended badly. On theory, Zhou follows Xi in treating law and morality as distinct but complementary: law is a rigid, externally enforced standard, and morality is a self-regulating inner one. Neither can replace the other, so the rule of law and the rule of virtue must work together.

For practice, Zhou proposes making socialist rule of law one of good laws and good governance, and building the core socialist values into legislation, enforcement and adjudication. Zhou also calls for legal requirements to be reflected in moral education and for legal means to be used against serious immoral conduct such as food and drug safety violations and counterfeiting. Leading cadres, as the "key minority", should model both obedience to law and moral conduct. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-state legal scholar presents the official case for joint rule by law and virtue, with its historical and theoretical justifications.
quoteEn: Law and morality differ in nature, and their functions also differ.
quoteZh: 法律和道德的属性不同、功能也有差别。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping's thought: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with its fine traditional culture (the second).

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on law and governance, which the Party made official guidance for legal work at the Central Conference on Law-based Governance in November 2020.
A set of 24 characters in 12 words, covering national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for leading cadres, whose conduct is said to set the example for the wider population.
An official formula for rule of law in which well-made laws are the basis for effective governance.

keywords: Xi Jinping thought on the rule of law

t: The rich connotations and original contributions of the anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色反贫困理论的丰富内涵和原创性贡献
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 23 January 2026, Wang Lin examines what the author calls the anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics, which Xi Jinping first named in February 2021 at the national poverty-alleviation commendation conference. Wang presents it as an original, signature concept of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article argues that the theory has rich content and original contributions, and that it should be upheld over the long term and developed further.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out six components of the theory: Party leadership, a people-centred stance and common prosperity, institutional advantages, development-oriented poverty alleviation, the initiative of poor people themselves, and a global outlook. The second describes original contributions in four dimensions: theory, method, values and practice. The third turns to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), the first five years after the transition period that followed the end of extreme poverty.

Wang argues that the theory applies Marxist anti-poverty ideas to China's conditions and to traditional Chinese culture. On the author's account, it goes beyond Western approaches that treat poverty as individual or marginal, and its method of targeted poverty alleviation moved from "flood irrigation" to "drip irrigation". This method rests on the "six precisions", the "five batches" and a full chain of identification, support, exit and monitoring. Wang also credits the poverty-alleviation spirit with providing a driving force, and presents China's experience as a reference for other developing countries.

Looking ahead, Wang calls for three shifts in the post-transition period. The first is from concentrated assault to routine consolidation, under the principle of "big stability, small adjustments". The second is from treating existing poverty to preventing a return to poverty, through a closed-loop mechanism of monitoring, verification, assistance, removal and follow-up. The third is from guaranteeing basic needs to promoting development, with support differentiated for low-income rural people who can and cannot work. Wang ties this to Chinese modernization and rural revitalisation. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Chinese commentators frame poverty alleviation as theory, and of the policy priorities set for 2026–2030.
quoteEn: Avoiding large-scale return to poverty is the bottom-line task of comprehensively advancing rural revitalisation; it requires moving the focus of poverty governance forward, as a way of active prevention.
quoteZh: 不发生规模性返贫致贫，是推进乡村全面振兴的底线任务，要求把贫困治理重心向前转移，是一种主动预防的方式。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has made a central policy aim, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than a few.
The official term for China's own path to modernisation, presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy approach launched around 2013 that identifies poor households individually and tailors support to each, replacing broad regional aid.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to modernise agriculture and the countryside; it follows the end of the poverty-alleviation campaign.

t: Why Marxism retains an even more vigorous vitality
zh: 为何马克思主义能保持更加旺盛的生命力
paras: Most schools of thought decline after their founders die, Yang Geng observes, yet Marxism has kept producing successors who answer new questions and absorb the best of human culture. The article, a newspaper essay in Guangming Daily, asks why Marxism still has such vitality. Yang's answer is that its value orientation (the free and all-round development of every person), its basis in laws of social development, its critical and scientific character, and its continual integration with Chinese conditions together explain its endurance.

The essay has three parts. The first sets out Marxism's value orientation and its grounds for argument. The second defends Marxism as a science rather than a book of revelation, and answers the charge that it is outdated. The third turns to China and the Two Integrations, which Yang presents as the way to open up new horizons for contemporary Chinese Marxism. Along the way Yang engages Lukács, Fromm, Popper, Heilbroner and Collingwood.

Yang rejects two readings. One holds that Marxism has an "empty space" where a theory of the human being should be. The other holds that it is mainly a moral protest or an ethics of sympathy for workers. In Yang's account, human emancipation is Marxism's theme, but its grounds are laws of social development and the laws governing the capitalist mode of production, and it works through three unified critiques: philosophical, political and critique of capital. Yang rebuts Popper's denial of historical laws and the claim that Marxism is outdated because it dates from the Victorian era. Truth is judged by whether a doctrine grasps the laws of its object, not by its date, and Marx derived general laws from the most developed cases of his time. Yang adds that Marxism offers a scientific method, not ready-made answers, and that treating the classics as a source of such answers turns it into a "revelation".

On China, Yang argues that integrating Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture must be organic fusion, not mechanical addition, term-swapping or a "Confucian Marxism" that would hollow Marxism out. It rests on real points of common ground and should be guided by the practice of Chinese modernization. Yang concludes that contemporary Chinese Marxism belongs to both Marxism and Chinese culture, and that it alone represents China's future direction. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a leading Chinese Marxist philosopher defends Marxism's scientific status and the cultural logic of the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Time is only a "filter" of truth and error, not a "test" of truth and error.
quoteZh: 时间只是真理与谬误的“过滤器”，而不是真理与谬误的“检验器”。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping-era Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The official term for the parts of China's cultural heritage that the Party regards as worth inheriting and developing.

t: Combining theory and practice to explain the power of ideas
st: A review of the fourth set of the Economic Daily series on Xi Jinping economic thought
zh: 理论和实践相结合诠释思想伟力
paras: This short commentary, published in Economic Daily in January 2026, reviews the fourth set of the Economic Daily's book series on studying and applying Xi Jinping economic thought. Xiao Xiao argues that the two volumes together show the strength of this body of thought by pairing theoretical exposition with practical cases. The set comprises the Collected Studies on Xi Jinping Economic Thought (2024) and the Collected Field Investigations on Putting Xi Jinping Economic Thought into Practice (2024), produced by the newspaper, which has run an essay competition on the subject for five years.

The review treats each volume in turn. The first, according to Xiao, gathers theoretical essays on strengthening Party leadership over economic work, people-centred development, the basic socialist economic system, deepening reform and developing new quality productive forces. The second collects the newspaper's own reporting in three sections: local, industry and enterprise investigations.

Xiao's central claim is that the thought answers questions that Marxist classics, earlier Chinese thinkers and Western economics did not resolve. Many of the theoretical essays, the author says, trace its inheritance and development of Marxist political economy and show its practical spirit and global outlook. The reporting volume is praised for combining solid data with ordinary people's accounts and for acknowledging difficulties. In Xiao's reading, this moves readers from impressions to an understanding of underlying regularities, and shows the advantages of the socialist system, the huge market, the complete industrial system and talent resources.

Xiao concludes that reading the series helps readers grasp the Two Establishes and align theory and practice with the blueprint for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, in order to keep strategic resolve and open up new prospects for high-quality development. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary presents official economic-theory publications and the theory-practice relationship.
quoteEn: Practice is the source of theory.
quoteZh: 实践是理论之源。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas and policy principles attributed to Xi Jinping since 2012, presented officially as a component of Xi Jinping Thought and as Marxist political economy adapted to contemporary China.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation in emerging and future industries.
An official guideline since 2017 that prioritises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the successor to the 14th Five-Year Plan.

t: The philosophical wisdom of "historical resolve"
zh: “历史定力”的哲学智慧
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2026, takes up "historical resolve" (lishi dingli), a category the authors describe as an original concept of Chinese communists in the new era. They define it as the steady, unshakeable strategic capacity and spiritual outlook of a historical subject that has grasped historical laws and the trend of the times. Xu and Xu argue that, seen through a "grand view of history", it unites conformity to law with purposiveness, long-term goals with stage-by-stage tasks, and national rejuvenation with human progress.

The article is organised around three formulations of Xi Jinping: "stand on the right side of history", "maintain historical patience" and "stand on the side of human progress". Each section treats one as a philosophical dimension of historical resolve: direction and orientation, time, and global horizon. The authors draw on Marx, Engels, the ancient thinker Xunzi and Immanuel Wallerstein, and refer to Party history from the New Democratic Revolution to the present.

In the first section, the authors argue that standing on the right side of history means uniting "conformity to law" (grounded in the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production) with "purposiveness" (the Party's fundamental aim of serving the people wholeheartedly). They read the stages of revolution, construction and reform, including the call for new relations of production suited to new quality productive forces, as applications of the first principle. In the second, historical patience is presented as the temporal form of resolve: a balance between agency and given conditions, and between continuity and stages. Xu and Xu cite Marx on the "natural historical process" and Xunzi on constancy and adaptation, and set the maxims "success need not be mine" and "success must include me" side by side. In the third, standing with human progress is described as a "critical construction" that rejects hegemonic systems and linear narratives of progress. The authors claim that a community with a shared future for mankind goes beyond realism, the "end of history" thesis and the "clash of civilizations" thesis, and they describe the Belt and Road Initiative as reshaping the logic of global spatial production.

The authors conclude that historical resolve, in its global form, is a "civilizational resolve" that "creates within tension", and that the Party stands on the side of "time" and "momentum". They present Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as a model of resolve guiding historical continuity through patience. Read the original if you want to see how Party-affiliated scholars give a Marxist philosophical grounding to a new official concept and tie it to Xi Jinping's formulations on history.
quoteEn: Historical resolve is manifested first in an accurate grasp of one's historical position and a fundamental choice of direction of advance, that is, always "standing on the right side of history".
quoteZh: 历史定力，首先体现为对历史方位的准确把握、对前进方向的根本抉择，即始终“站在历史正确的一边”。

glossary.explanation: A concept in recent Party discourse for steady strategic determination grounded in an understanding of historical laws and trends. The authors present it as an original category of new-era Party theory.
A phrase used by Xi Jinping for strategic composure over the long course of history. The authors treat it as the temporal expression of historical resolve.
A term in current Party discourse for assessing events across long time spans and broad contexts, often linked to Xi Jinping's remarks on studying Party history.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation. It is linked to calls for matching new relations of production.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy and global-governance concept, introduced around 2012–2013, which stresses shared interests and cooperation among states.
The official term for the Party's path of modernization with Chinese characteristics, central to the post-2022 narrative of national rejuvenation.
China's infrastructure and connectivity programme launched in 2013, linking Asia, Europe and Africa.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Continuously consolidating cultural subjectivity through the Two Integrations
zh: 在“两个结合”中不断巩固文化主体性
paras: Hou Yanshe asks how the Two Integrations help consolidate the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation, meaning the autonomy, initiative and creativity that a historical subject shows in cultural activity. The article, a newspaper commentary in Guangming Daily, argues that Xi Jinping's formulation of the Two Integrations contains a deep reflection on strengthening this subjectivity. In Hou's reading, it marks a new level of consciousness and self-direction in the Party's work on socialist culture with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has three sections. The first deals with the interaction of theoretical and practical innovation, the second with the mutual fusion of Marxism and traditional Chinese culture, and the third with cultural development and civilisational progress in the new era. It begins from the semi-colonial, semi-feudal period after the Opium War and ends with a list of principles for the present.

Hou's first move is historical. After the Opium War, Chinese cultural subjectivity was, in the author's account, seriously obscured. Marxism then gave the Party and the people a scientific theory and moved the Chinese people from passivity to initiative in spirit. Combining Marxism's universal truths with China's specific conditions produced a good interaction between theoretical and practical innovation. The second move concerns the Second Integration. Marxism is called the "soul" and traditional culture the "root". Hou says each activates the other: dialectical unity of humanity and nature revives the traditional idea of harmony between heaven and humanity, and the people's democracy idea revives the old notion of the people as the root of the state. In return, traditional culture gives Marxism a distinctly Chinese style. Hou concludes that Marxism becomes Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, while traditional culture becomes a modernised Chinese culture. Third, Hou treats the creation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the strongest expression of cultural subjectivity in the new era.

Hou calls for guidance by Xi Jinping Thought, especially Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, in advancing Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Five requirements follow: Party leadership in cultural work, the people's principal position, self-reliance that strengthens the Four-sphere Confidence, innovation on a firm foundation, and openness to the achievements of other civilisations. The last requirement is tied to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how current Party theory links the Two Integrations to cultural confidence and cultural subjectivity.
quoteEn: Through the mutual fusion and mutual fulfilment of Marxism as the soul and excellent traditional Chinese culture as the root, Marxism becomes Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and excellent traditional Chinese culture becomes a modernised Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 通过马克思主义这个魂脉和中华优秀传统文化这个根脉的相互融通、相互成就，马克思主义成为中国化时代化的马克思主义，中华优秀传统文化成为现代化的中华文化。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities (the First Integration) and with excellent traditional Chinese culture (the Second Integration).

A term Xi Jinping popularised in 2023 for the autonomy, initiative and creativity of a people in cultural activity. It is used to stress that China should develop its own culture rather than follow others.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
The official term for China's own path to modernisation, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, promoted in Chinese foreign policy.

t: The profound meaning of "ensuring decisive progress toward basically realizing socialist modernization"
zh: “确保基本实现社会主义现代化取得决定性进展”的深刻内涵
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily interprets a goal set by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025): that the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) must "ensure decisive progress toward basically realizing socialist modernization". Tao Wenzhao argues that the formula is more than a time-bound benchmark. In the author's reading, it expresses the Party's sense of mission and historical initiative, and its resolve to push Chinese modernization into greater depth.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the "spirit and essence" of the goal. The second places it in historical context, between the close of the 14th Five-Year Plan and the longer road to 2035 and beyond. The third names three key areas for breakthroughs: scientific and technological innovation, reform and opening up, and security-oriented development. The text quotes Xi Jinping on strategic patience and on pressing ahead with urgent tasks.

Tao argues that the goal rests on three foundations. These are a mission that anchors direction, continuity with earlier staged goals such as the step-by-step building of a moderately prosperous society, and an active stance that seizes the initiative. On the historical position, the author insists that "decisive progress" means a qualitative leap and systemic breakthroughs, not merely quantitative accumulation or isolated gains. It also requires seamless continuity with the 14th Five-Year Plan and early preparation for longer-term technologies, talent and governance.

For the key areas, Tao calls for a shift from "following and running alongside" to "running alongside and leading" in technology. The author names fields such as artificial intelligence, quantum information and integrated circuits, and calls for new quality productive forces and a new-type whole-nation system. Tao also calls for deeper reform toward a high-standard socialist market economy and a unified national market. The Two Unwaverings are to be upheld, and security is to be treated as the precondition of development, with food, energy, supply-chain and financial risks guarded against. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of how the 15th Five-Year Plan period is framed within the 2035 modernization goal.
quoteEn: It must be made clear that "decisive progress" is not simple quantitative accumulation but a fundamental qualitative improvement; not partial or single-item progress but overall, systemic breakthroughs.
quoteZh: 需要明确的是，“决定性进展”并非简单的量的积累，而是质的根本性提升；并非局部的、单项的进步，而是全局的、系统的突破。

glossary.explanation: China's national development plan for 2026–2030, whose recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in October 2025.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The policy formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.
A phrase in Party discourse for consciously grasping historical laws and acting proactively rather than adapting passively to events.

t: The planning wisdom of Chinese Communists: a long-termist outlook on economic and social development
zh: 中国共产党人的规划智慧：一种长期主义的经济社会发展观
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 27 October 2025, just after the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) adopted the Party's proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, this commentary asks what lies behind the Party's practice of drawing up and successively carrying out five-year plans. Qu Jing and An Weifu argue that the achievements of Chinese modernization are not a sudden "miracle" but the product of a distinctively Chinese long-termist outlook on economic and social development, which they call the planning wisdom of Chinese Communists.

The authors organise the piece around three questions: what planning is, why it is needed, and how plans are made and implemented. They draw on the history of the plans from the first (1953–57) to the 15th, citing Mao Zedong, Engels and Xi Jinping, official documents and examples from specific plans. The text is a short newspaper commentary rather than a detailed study.

On the first question, the authors say planning arose from China's conditions of scattered, small-scale production in 1949 and, after reform and opening up, became a remedy for the defects of spontaneous market adjustment. They define it along two dimensions, looking further in time and wider in space. On the second, they offer three reasons: planning is the necessary route for late-developing countries to "take off"; it addresses market failure and, in their view, forms an organic whole with the market; and it joins strategic goals to policies and concrete measures under a Party that coordinates the whole. On the third, they list three principles: a people-centred stance; research and consultation that combine top-down design with public input, citing over 3.113 million online suggestions for the 15th plan; and a clear implementation mechanism with defined responsibilities.

The authors conclude that this process keeps socialist construction going "generation after generation" with "one blueprint followed to the end", and that this is what makes the outlook long-termist. They present the plans as consistent in aiming at a modern socialist country while uniting long-term goals with stage-by-stage tasks. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese commentators justify five-year planning ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Planning aims to concentrate the strength of the whole of society on fundamental, institutional problems that market operation requires but cannot solve spontaneously, such as industrial foundations, industrial restructuring, economic reform, changing the growth model and common prosperity.
quoteZh: 规划旨在集中全社会的力量解决那些市场运行需要但又不能自发解决的工业基础建设、产业结构调整、经济体制改革、增长方式转变、共同富裕等基础性、制度性问题

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.
China's medium-term national development plan, issued every five years since 1953. Called a 'plan' (计划) until the 11th and a 'programme/plan' (规划) since then.

t: The Two Integrations as a powerful driving force for the development of Chinese philosophy
zh: “两个结合”激发中国哲学发展强大动力
paras: Han Donghui reviews Chinese philosophy during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–2025) in a commentary for the Chinese Social Sciences Today. The author argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Culture has given philosophy strong momentum, and that the Two Integrations have set its direction.

The piece surveys the field in broad strokes: the philosophical foundations of the Party's theoretical innovation, the cultural thought associated with Xi, the building of an autonomous knowledge system, and four relationships that Han says that effort has had to handle. It draws on work by Marxist philosophers, scholars of Chinese tradition and Chinese scholars of Western philosophy.

Han presents the Two Integrations, especially the second, as the basic guide and scientific method for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In this account they have extended historical materialism and the epistemology of practice, and have informed a methodology of seven modes of thinking. Han describes an autonomous knowledge system as neither simple "de-Westernization" nor a mere return to origins. It is meant to be rooted in Chinese practice and to engage in equal dialogue abroad. Examples include the concept of "Chinese Marxist philosophy", work on "all under heaven" and "great unification", and proposals for Chinese phenomenology and Sinophone philosophy. The four relationships are core research versus real-world concerns, reinterpreting the classics versus creative transformation, technology ethics, and self-confidence versus mutual learning among civilizations.

Han concludes that philosophers have strengthened cultural subjectivity and academic autonomy by linking past and present, tradition and modernity, and the local and the international. Looking to the next five years, Han expects a philosophy rooted in China yet global in outlook. Read the original if you want a brief official-academic overview of how Chinese philosophy presented its recent agenda under the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: An autonomous knowledge and thought system is neither simple "de-Westernization" nor a mere "return to origins". It must be rooted in Chinese practice, stand on Chinese soil and address Chinese problems, put forward subjective and original theoretical views, and be able to engage in equal dialogue and debate with the international academic community.
quoteZh: 自主知识体系和思想体系并非简单的“去西方化”，也不是单纯的“返本”，而是要植根中国实践、立足中国大地、关注中国问题，提出具有主体性、原创性的理论观点，同时能够与国际学术界平等对话、交流交锋。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the contemporary era.
A body of ideas on culture attributed to Xi Jinping and formally presented in 2023. It covers cultural leadership, Chinese cultural subjectivity and cultural development.
Official goal of building Chinese philosophy and social science with their own concepts and theories, rather than relying on Western frameworks.

t: Grasping the key points in a theoretical (xueli) elaboration of the Two Integrations
st: What "integration" means, and how the second integration can be carried out
zh: 把握“两个结合”学理化阐释的关键点
paras: Liu Jianjun, a professor at Renmin University of China, argues in this Guangming Daily article that any serious theoretical account of the Two Integrations must first settle a basic question: what exactly is "integration" (jiehe)? Liu holds that the term should be established as a philosophical category with a defined meaning and limits, rather than used loosely. Doing so, in Liu's view, gives later research a base and a direction.

The article moves in two steps. The first part defines the concept within materialist dialectics, locates it in the Party's innovation theory, and introduces a new notion, "mode of integration". The second part applies this to the two integrations in turn. It treats the first integration briefly and then sets out four ways of advancing the second: language, scholarship, theory and practice.

Liu defines integration as a state of mutual connection and unification between different things, based on real need and inner fit, that tends toward fusing into something new. On this reading it is both a category of universal connection and one of contradiction, reflecting the law of the unity of opposites. Liu says the second integration, between Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture, cannot reuse the pattern of the first, which joined theory and practice. It concerns the relation between the "soul" and the "root" of the Party's guiding ideology. Modelled on the "mode of production", the "mode of integration" is meant to show how integration happens. Liu separates mechanical, external combination from inner, organic integration, citing Xi Jinping's remark that integration is a "chemical reaction" rather than a "platter". The four ways proposed are Marxism speaking Chinese (translation, refined terminology, Chinese grammatical habits); joint scholarship by Marxist and traditional-culture researchers; the Party's theoretical innovation, culminating in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; and practice.

Liu concludes that theoretical innovation and practical innovation must advance together. The great practice of Chinese modernization is described as the source and driving force of the second integration, and Liu calls on theorists to take part in construction and reform. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese Marxist scholar tries to turn the Two Integrations into a defined concept with identifiable methods, and how the second integration is meant to proceed.
quoteEn: Only by grasping the "mode of integration" can one deeply grasp "integration" itself.
quoteZh: 只有把握了“结合方式”，才能深刻把握“结合”本身。

glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second integration). The second integration was added prominently in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 statements.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A concept the author proposes to describe the form and path by which integration takes place. It is modelled on the Marxist category of the mode of production.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times

t: Seek unity through struggle and unity survives
st: Revisiting Mao Zedong's "On Tactical Problems of the Present Anti-Japanese United Front"
zh: 以斗争求团结则团结存
zhSub: 重温毛泽东《目前抗日统一战线中的策略问题》
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 11 September 2025
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2025, rereads Mao Zedong's outline of a report given to senior Party cadres in Yan'an on 11 March 1940. Xiong argues that the text's maxim, that unity sought through struggle survives while unity sought through concession perishes, supplies a methodology of struggle for handling major risks and complex relationships.

The article sets the report in the crisis of late 1939, when Nationalist military and political pressure threatened the Communist–Nationalist alliance and the anti-Japanese national united front. It then presents two sets of principles drawn from the text: how to wage struggle that is justified, advantageous and restrained, and how to win the majority while opposing a minority. It closes by linking the text to present-day China–US relations.

On struggle, Xiong sets out three principles: self-defence, victory and truce. Self-defence means not attacking first, yet responding resolutely and actively to attack. Victory means keeping struggle local, preparing thoroughly and striking the most reactionary faction first. Truce means stopping after one round and seeking peace so the struggle stays temporary and controllable. On winning the majority, Xiong reports Mao's division of the Nationalists into diehards, middle and progressive groups. Mao also identified middle forces, such as the middle bourgeoisie, enlightened gentry and regional power-holders, who could be won if the Party was strong, respected their interests and showed progressive victories.

Xiong concludes that the Party's wartime practice of building up its own strength while struggling flexibly with the Nationalists preserved the united front. The author says the principles of unity and struggle remain a guide for new great struggles. Xiong then contends that concession and compromise earn no respect from the United States, which the author accuses of containment, tariff, trade and technology wars, and that firm resolve and skill in struggle are needed for stable relations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentators draw on Mao's wartime united-front writings to frame present-day foreign policy.
quoteEn: Faced with continual US provocation and bullying, concession and compromise cannot win respect; only by firming up the will to struggle and mastering the art of struggle can China–US relations genuinely be steered towards stability and long-term health.
quoteZh: 面对美国持续不断的挑衅与霸凌，退让和妥协换不来尊重，只有坚定斗争意志，掌握斗争艺术，才有可能真正推动中美关系行稳致远。

glossary.explanation: The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Nationalist Party, along with other forces, against Japanese invasion. It was formed in the late 1930s and was often strained.
Mao's term for the anti-Communist faction within the Nationalist camp that favoured attacking the Communists and resisting cooperation.
In Mao's analysis, groups such as the middle bourgeoisie, enlightened gentry and regional power-holders, standing between the Communists and the diehards and open to being won over.

t: Grasping theoretical and practical requirements: developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 把握理论和实践要求因地制宜发展新质生产力
paras: This short commentary from the Economic Daily takes up Xi Jinping's repeated instruction that new quality productive forces be developed "in light of local conditions" (yindi zhiyi). Chen Yunping argues that this is a scientific method which joins the Marxist theory of productive forces with the practice of Chinese modernization. In Chen's reading, it deepens understanding of how productive forces are driven and how they evolve.

The article first sets out why the approach matters, internationally and domestically. It then gives four theoretical foundations and three practical requirements, all in condensed form. The author closes by describing regional differences in factor endowments, industrial bases and functional positioning, with examples drawn from coastal and inland regions.

Chen makes two central moves. First, the approach is tied to the change in the principal contradiction of Chinese society and to deepening reform: uneven and inadequate development is partly regional, so letting each place pursue its own path should draw out local potential and gradually narrow gaps. Because productive forces determine relations of production, Chen adds, developing them requires adjusting those relations through further comprehensive deepening of reform. Second, the theoretical grounding is traced to dialectical materialism (the particularity of contradiction), to seeking truth from facts (no "one-size-fits-all" approach or campaign-style rushing), to comparative advantage theory (extended from labour, land and resources to new-quality factors) and to regional coordinated development theory.

In practice, Chen holds that resource-rich regions can start from resource-based industries and move towards deep processing and recycling. Labour-abundant regions can upgrade labour-intensive industries towards skill-intensive ones, and large industrial clusters are better placed for breakthroughs such as battery or autonomous-driving technology. Coastal regions are said to suit electronic information, biomedicine and new energy, and inland regions specialised manufacturing, resource processing or logistics. Chen concludes that tying development to functional positioning avoids homogeneous competition and resource misallocation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies regionally differentiated industrial policy in terms of Marxist theory and the Party's ideological vocabulary.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces must be closely combined with regional functional positioning; only then can homogeneous competition and resource misallocation be avoided, local conditions truly be respected, and a situation created in which each region plays to its strengths and complements the others.
quoteZh: 必须将发展新质生产力与区域功能定位深度结合，才能避免同质化竞争和资源错配，真正实现因地制宜，形成各扬其长、优势互补的良好局面。

glossary.explanation: A concept advanced by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading, rather than by traditional factor inputs.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, treated as the core of the Party's ideological line: policy should start from actual conditions.

t: Deepening the understanding of the laws governing the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 深化发展新质生产力的规律性认识
paras: Zhao Zhenhua, writing in Economic Daily in September 2025, asks how new quality productive forces should be understood and developed as the country enters the 15th Five-Year Plan period. The article argues that doing so requires a change in development thinking, respect for objective laws of development, and the guidance of dialectical and historical materialist method. It presents the concept as Xi Jinping's creative development of Marxist productive-forces theory and calls for developing these forces in ways suited to local conditions.

The piece has three parts. The first links leaps in productive forces to the liberation of thought and the renewal of development ideas, citing the 1978 debate on the criterion of truth, Deng Xiaoping's 1992 southern tour and the 14th Party Congress. The second sets out three laws of development: revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors, and deep industrial transformation and upgrading. The third lists four methodological principles.

Zhao first holds that new quality productive forces embody the new development philosophy and must break with extensive growth, so development should not put "old wine in new bottles", even under downward economic pressure.
