On the three laws, the author stresses basic research as the precondition for technological breakthroughs, combining free exploration with organised research on key technologies. Zhao adds that data, knowledge, technology and management now join labour, capital and land as production factors, and that a unified national market and the market's decisive role in allocating resources are needed to release them. For industry, Zhao calls for applying technology to traditional sectors, pursuing "AI Plus" initiatives and nurturing future industries with patient capital. The methodology section calls for seeing connections across the whole system, grasping principal contradictions (above all core technology bottlenecks), and building production relations suited to the new forces through deeper reform and opening up.

Zhao concludes that the "one key for one lock" principle should guide local practice: avoid rushing in and bubbles, avoid a single model, and base plans on thorough investigation of each place's resources, industrial base and research conditions. The author says this approach lets China seize the initiative in development and create new economic momentum. Read the original if you want a concise, Party School-style statement of how official discourse frames the laws, methods and local pathways of developing new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: The salient feature of developing new quality productive forces is innovation; innovation covers many kinds, of which scientific and technological innovation is the main one, and within it the main task is to solve major "chokepoint" technologies.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力的显著特点是创新，创新涉及各方面的创新，其中主要的方面是科技创新，在科技创新中主要的方面是解决重大“卡脖子”技术

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading, centred on higher total factor productivity.
Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, which guides Party economic policy.
A long-standing policy principle that methods should be tailored to the circumstances of each locality rather than applied uniformly.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose drafting was under way at the time of writing.

t: The dialectical logic of institution-building in the new era
zh: 新时代制度建设的辩证逻辑
paras: Xu Bin, writing in Guangming Daily in September 2025, asks how institution-building should proceed as the Party pursues further comprehensive deepening of reform. Taking Xi Jinping's instruction to make institution-building the main thread of reform, Xu argues that this guidance rests on materialist dialectics. Three paired relationships must be handled together: top-level design and grassroots exploration, establishing the new and abolishing the old, and systematic advance and local breakthrough.

The piece is a short commentary with three numbered sections, one for each pair. Each section follows the same pattern. It cites Xi Jinping's formulation, places the pair in the history of reform and opening up and in the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), then sets out what the pair requires in practice. Examples include Xiaogang village's household contract system, Shenzhen, free trade pilot zones and supervision and judicial reform pilots.

In the first pair, Xu reads the interaction of top-level design and grassroots exploration as a movement from the particular to the universal and back, an instance of the cycle of practice, knowledge and practice, and an application of the Party's mass line. Because reform has reached a "deep-water zone" and institutions are more mature, Xu says top-level design should now be strengthened. In the second pair, Xu cites Marx on dialectics and distinguishes "break first, then build", which suited the revolutionary period, from "build first, then break", which Xu calls the dominant method now that social structure is stable. Examples are revising laws, adjusting industrial structure and green transition. In the third pair, Xu says reform needs comprehensive coverage and a focus on the economic system, with the 20th Central Committee's Third Plenum (2024) stressing systems integration and priorities.

Xu concludes that only by combining these three pairs can institution-building meet the demands of the times and promote social development, laying an institutional foundation for Chinese modernization. Xu calls for scientific top-level planning under centralised Party leadership alongside encouragement of replicable local experiments. Xu also calls for decisive removal of entrenched institutional defects together with careful construction of new ones, and for coordinated reform that targets bottlenecks and points of public grievance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present reform strategy through dialectical categories and Xi Jinping's formulations.
quoteEn: Institution-building in the new era requires us to combine the dual wisdom of being \"bold in breaking with the old\" and \"skilled in establishing the new\".
quoteZh: 新时代制度建设要求我们融合“勇于破旧”和“善于立新”的双重智慧。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
A term for centralised, overall planning of reform objectives, paths and sequencing by the central leadership. It is commonly contrasted with local experimentation.

glossary.pinyin: pò lì bìngjǔ, xiān lì hòu pò
glossary.literal: break and build together; build before breaking
glossary.explanation: A formulation by Xi Jinping that new institutions or mechanisms should be established before old ones are dismantled. It is meant to ensure a smooth transition in reform.

A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering views from the people, concentrating them into policy, and returning to the people to test and implement them. The article cites it as "from the masses, to the masses".
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Upholding the "Two Integrations" to build a culturally strong nation
zh: 坚持“两个结合”建设文化强国
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 29 August 2025, asks how China should build a culturally strong nation. Liu Shuijing argues that the Two Integrations are the necessary path for developing socialism with Chinese characteristics on the foundation of more than five thousand years of Chinese civilization, and an important route for shouldering the cultural mission and building a culturally strong nation.

The piece draws on articles in volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, which stress that the key to Chinese characteristics lies in the Two Integrations. Liu briefly explains the concept, then reviews what has been achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and ends with two directions for future work.

Liu presents the Two Integrations, especially the "second integration", as the Party's summary of the experience of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and as a grasp of the laws of Chinese civilization's development. In Liu's account, since 2012 they have produced theoretical innovation, a fundamental turn in the ideological sphere, creative transformation of traditional culture, the Global Civilization Initiative, and a marked rise in cultural soft power.

Liu calls for two things. First, hold to the "soul" of Marxism, uphold its guiding position in ideology, and maintain the Party's cultural leadership, combining positive publicity with struggle over public opinion. Second, carry forward the roots of fine traditional culture, build cultural confidence and subjectivity, deepen cultural reform, and draw on foreign achievements to create new work. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links the Two Integrations to cultural policy.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership is the fundamental guarantee for following the path of developing socialist culture with Chinese characteristics while adhering to the Two Integrations.
quoteZh: 坚持党的文化领导权，是在坚持“两个结合”中走好中国特色社会主义文化发展道路的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second was emphasised by Xi Jinping from 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's project of adapting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to contemporary developments.
An official goal of building China's cultural strength and influence, set out in Party documents and linked to the 2035 targets.
The Party's official name for China's path and system since the reform era.
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2023 that stresses respect for the diversity of civilizations and exchanges and mutual learning among them.

t: Opening a new realm of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times through the Two Integrations
zh: 在“两个结合”中开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 26 August 2025
paras: This short commentary, a study note on Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is a major theoretical innovation produced by the Two Integrations. Tang Aijun contends that the Thought has opened a new realm of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece has two parts. The first presents the Two Integrations as the fundamental route for developing Marxism in China. The second treats the Thought as the model case of applying both integrations, drawing on passages from Volume V.

Tang says the first integration, with China's concrete realities, addresses theory and practice and aims to overcome dogmatism and subjectivism. The second, with excellent traditional Chinese culture, addresses the fusion of two cultures and aims to overcome cultural and historical nihilism. According to the author, the Thought answers the great questions of the new era, such as what socialism to uphold and how to build a modern socialist country. It also draws on traditional culture, and Tang gives the theory of exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations as an example. In this account, the theory combines Marxist views of civilizational exchange with the Chinese ideal of harmony without uniformity.

Tang concludes that the Two Integrations sum up the Party's historical experience and deepen its understanding of how theory is innovated. The author names a key task for studying Volume V: grasping the original contributions and principled theoretical results that the Thought has made to upholding and developing Marxism. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official Party-school reading of the Two Integrations and of Volume V's place in it.
quoteEn: The "second integration" mainly addresses the exchange, blending and innovative fusion of two different cultures, and focuses on eliminating cultural nihilism and historical nihilism.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”主要解决的是两种不同文化之间的交流交融、融合创新的问题，着重破除文化虚无主义、历史虚无主义。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was formally added in Xi Jinping's 2021 and 2022 statements.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each historical period. The "times" element was stressed in Party documents from 2021.
An official label for views that, in the Party's view, distort or negate the history of the Party and of socialism in China.

t: China's "people-centred" path of governing science and technology ethics
zh: “以人民为中心”的中国科技伦理治理之路
paras: Xiao Wei asks how science and technology ethics should be governed in an age of artificial intelligence and big data, when ethical challenges cut across disciplines and touch on safety, social fairness, public interest and human dignity. The article argues that China is following a "people-centred" path, in which ethics governance is oriented to the interests and participation of the people. It first appeared in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2025.

The piece has three parts. It first links the aim of "promoting human well-being" to the people-centred principle. It then explains why the people's principal position must be upheld in ethics governance. Finally it sets out how to build a governance system with broad public participation. Xiao draws on the 2022 Opinions on Strengthening Science and Technology Ethics Governance, with its five ethical principles, on Xi Jinping's April 2025 Qiushi article on building a strong science and technology nation, and on UNESCO, WHO and UN sustainable development frameworks.

Xiao contends that "promoting human well-being" is a shared international value, while the people-centred principle is the Communist Party's basic political stance. The two are said to coincide in treating the human being as the foundation, in focusing on dignity, rights and all-round development, and in stressing shared benefits. Because technology is double-edged, Xiao argues, governance cannot be left to experts, institutes or firms regulating themselves. The public should be participants, supervisors and beneficiaries, with rights to information, expression and participation. Drawing on a 2021 WHO framework, Xiao names participation, inclusiveness and responsiveness as key features. Inclusiveness is divided into inclusion of groups, of viewpoints and of rights protection.

Xiao proposes building the system at three levels. Institutionally, this means public hearings, social review and ethical impact assessment, with citizen forums before major biomedical applications. At the level of mechanisms, community organisations, media platforms and civil bodies would join a structure of government guidance, corporate responsibility, expert participation and shared governance by the people. Culturally, ethics education would be built into national education and public communication. Xiao concludes that public participation gives innovation social support and moral grounding, and also provides risk warning and social stability. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese official discourse links technology ethics governance to the people-centred principle and public participation.
quoteEn: Science and technology ethics is not the lofty talk of a few experts, but a public issue bearing on the basic rights and responsibilities of the people.
quoteZh: 科技伦理不是少数专家的高谈阔论，而是关乎人民群众基本权利与责任的公共议题。

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Party and government policy, closely associated with Xi Jinping, which holds that development should serve the people's interests and rely on them.
The first of the five science and technology ethics principles in the 2022 Opinions. The article presents it as a value shared with international ethics and development frameworks.
The management of ethical issues in research and technology through institutionalised norms, values and rules, a policy area stressed in China's 2022 official document.
A Party principle that the people are the main actors and ultimate beneficiaries of development and governance.

t: The international dissemination and influence of On Protracted War
zh: 《论持久战》的国际传播及影响
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks how Mao Zedong's On Protracted War (1938) travelled beyond China and what effect it had. Deng Shaogen argues that the Communist Party of China gave great weight to spreading the work abroad, and that through foreign journalists and international friends it had major international influence.

The article follows the text from its delivery as lectures in Yan'an (26 May–3 June 1938) through publication in the journal Jiefang and in separate editions. It then covers Soviet and Comintern endorsement, the English translations, Japanese translation and reading, and the reception among Western leaders and observers.

Deng stresses that the Comintern understood and supported the protracted-war line, citing Ren Bishi's September 1938 article in Pravda and Dimitrov's praise of the work as epoch-making. Citing the researcher Zhang Shengxiang, Deng records at least four English translation efforts, including a lost Wuhan manuscript and versions serialised in Shanghai. Deng also reports that Japanese media and military staff translated the text, and that the general Okamura Yasuji called it a highly valuable strategic document, with Japanese attitudes moving from disdain to despair.

Deng concludes that the work had a positive effect in the Western world and drew high praise internationally. As evidence, the article mentions reports that copies lay on the desks of Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill, Stilwell's description of it as a superb textbook, and Edgar Snow's phrase "prophecy in the cave dwelling". Read the original if you want a compact survey of the translation history and foreign reception of On Protracted War, as presented in Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's protracted-war strategy received the affirmation and support of the Soviet Union and the Comintern.
quoteZh: 中国共产党持久战方针得到苏联和共产国际的肯定支持。

t: The traditional cultural foundations of the "Three Musts"
zh: “三个务必”的传统文化底蕴
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2025, asks where the "Three Musts" announced by Xi Jinping draw on China's traditional culture. Yang Yunling's author, Yang Junling, argues that the Three Musts continue and develop Marxist theories of party and state building and also inherit and develop excellent traditional Chinese culture. Guided by the Two Integrations, Yang says, uncovering this cultural background helps to grasp the essence and practical demands of the formula.

The article takes the three "musts" in turn: never forgetting the original aspiration and keeping the mission in mind; remaining modest and prudent and working hard; and daring and being good at struggle. For each, Yang pairs classical sources, such as the Book of Documents, the Book of Changes, Laozi, Confucius, Mencius and Xunzi, with passages Xi Jinping has cited since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Yang argues that the first "must" combines the Marxist people's standpoint with the traditional idea that the people are the foundation of the state. The second joins the Marxist spirit of self-reform to traditional virtues of humility and vigorous striving. The third merges the Marxist spirit of struggle with an ancient wisdom of struggle, seen in myths such as Yu Gong moving the mountains and in Confucian and Daoist ethics. In each case Yang presents the Party's formula as a creative transformation and innovative development of tradition.

Yang concludes that on the new journey the Party should internalise the mission of the people's happiness and national rejuvenation, guard against officials turning from public servants into masters, and sharpen its methods of struggle. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-aligned scholarship ties current Party slogans to classical Chinese sources.
quoteEn: "Must never forget the original aspiration and keep the mission firmly in mind" inherits and develops the essence of traditional Chinese thought on the people as the foundation, and is a creative transformation and innovative development of excellent traditional Chinese culture that the Party has carried out in light of the new requirements of social progress in the new era.
quoteZh: “务必不忘初心、牢记使命”，是对中国传统民本思想精华的继承和发展，是我们党结合新时代社会发展进步的新要求对中华优秀传统文化进行的创造性转化和创新性发展。

glossary.explanation: A formula Xi Jinping presented at the 20th Party Congress (2022), urging the whole Party to keep its original aspiration and mission, stay modest and hardworking, and dare to struggle. It echoes Mao Zedong's 1949 "two musts".
The principle of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's excellent traditional culture (the second, stressed since 2023).
The Party's official term for its continuous internal self-correction and discipline, used in the Party's self-reform discourse under Xi Jinping.

t: Strengthening the ideological guiding force of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 增强新时代中国特色社会主义文化的思想引领力
paras: This newspaper commentary (Economic Daily, 14 August 2025) asks how culture can be made more prosperous and China made a cultural power. Xing Yunwen argues that the key is to strengthen the ideological guiding force of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, which the author treats as culture's core competitiveness. The piece takes its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks at a Politburo study session on developing a culture with strong ideological guiding force, spiritual cohesion, value appeal and international influence.

The article has three parts. The first explains why ideas form the core of culture. The second reads the Party's hundred-year history as a record of ideological leadership, from the New Culture Movement to the successive cultural goals set in each period. The third turns to present tasks: the Two Integrations, and arming society with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Xing contends that, on the historical-materialist view, the material basis of any culture is its mode of production while its inner core is a system of ideas; Marxism is said to be the core of socialist culture and the source of its advanced character. As cultural exchange and rivalry intensify, the author sees the contest for discursive power as a contest for ideological high ground, which requires continued theoretical innovation by the Party. The author holds that the "second integration", of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, is the premise of this innovation and that socialist culture is itself a product of the Two Integrations.

Xing concludes that cultural work must uphold Marxism's guiding position and the Party's cultural leadership, deepen study of Xi Jinping Thought, and foster two-way interaction between ideas and cultural vehicles. The aim is to strengthen the people's spiritual strength and the cultural foundations of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link cultural strategy to ideological leadership.
quoteEn: Thought is the soul of culture, and culture is the vehicle of thought.
quoteZh: 思想是文化的灵魂，文化是思想的载体。

glossary.explanation: Formula associating the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second, stressed by Xi Jinping from 2021–23).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–18.
Official goal of making China strong in culture, with global cultural influence and a prosperous domestic cultural life.

t: Economic globalization and developing new quality productive forces
zh: 经济全球化与发展新质生产力
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 5 August 2025 as a result of a National Committee of the CPPCC research project on new quality productive forces, asks how China should develop such forces under conditions of deepening economic globalization. The authors argue that no country can solve all innovation problems alone. In their view, open innovation and international scientific cooperation are therefore indispensable, and they present this as guidance from Xi Jinping's economic writings.

The article opens with Xi's statements on open innovation and then proceeds in three sections. The first treats globalization as a trend that must be grasped, looking at technological change (artificial intelligence, the digital economy, green technology) and at international competition. The second addresses new challenges to globalization. The third turns to the steady expansion of institutional opening up. Each section is anchored in quotations from Xi Jinping.

The core argument draws on historical materialism. The authors say the new challenges to globalization, such as the rise of anti-globalization sentiment, fragmented trade rules, protectionism and unilateralism, arise because relations of production lag behind the development of productive forces. They attribute these trends partly to some Western countries, whose hollowed-out manufacturing and domestic tensions between growth and distribution are, in the authors' account, wrongly blamed on globalization by some politicians. The answer they propose is to use innovation to adjust global relations of production: opposing unilateralism, improving the multilateral trading system, and pairing technological innovation with management innovation and industrial cooperation. Examples include digital core technologies, green and low-carbon industries, smart manufacturing and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation.

The authors conclude that China should steadily expand institutional opening up, moving from opening in flows of goods, capital and people to opening in rules, regulations, management and standards. They say this would help clarify property rights over innovation gains, improve the allocation of data and technology, and attract global factors of production. They call for alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules in areas such as intellectual property, subsidies, environmental standards, government procurement and finance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary links new quality productive forces, globalization and institutional opening up.
quoteEn: The new challenges facing economic globalization stem from a mismatch between the relations of production and the development of the productive forces.
quoteZh: 经济全球化面临的新挑战源于生产关系与生产力发展不适应。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 to describe growth driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional resource-intensive models. It is central to current official economic policy.
A policy of aligning domestic rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones, as distinct from opening up merely through flows of goods and capital.

t: Theoretical questions on the "Second Integration" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
st: Notes on studying and understanding the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture
zh: 学习理解马克思主义中国化“第二个结合”的若干理论问题探析
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 4
paras: Liu Shulin takes up several theoretical questions raised by the "Second Integration", the proposition that the basic principles of Marxism must be combined with fine traditional Chinese culture. The article argues that this proposition deepens the Party's understanding of how Marxism is adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It holds that it became possible because of new archaeological findings and a more mature theoretical understanding under Xi Jinping. It also holds that it requires a balance of critique and absorption, openness to other civilizations, and a view of tradition as a whole.

The article has five parts. It first traces the history of the Two Integrations from Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation to Xi Jinping's 2021 and 2023 statements. It then lists the new historical conditions for the Second Integration, drawing on the Chinese Civilization Exploration Project and research on the Xia dynasty. The remaining parts cover how the Party has treated tradition in different periods, how the Second Integration relates to learning from other civilizations, and why tradition should be approached as a composite whole.

Liu's central claim is that the Party's basic attitude to tradition has been consistent, with emphasis shifting to the main task of each period. In revolutionary periods critique of decadent elements dominated, while in peacetime construction absorption of the best elements does, and the other element is never dropped. On this basis Liu defends the May Fourth attack on Confucianism and Lu Xun's critique as historically necessary. Liu rejects any \"re-criticism\" of them today. On foreign cultures, the author urges mutual learning among civilizations while resisting \"Western-centrism\", \"universal values\" and \"Westernization\". Liu also warns against reviving any single school. Citing Chen Xianda, Ren Jiyu and Xi, Liu stresses that Chinese tradition is plural and mixed, with Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, Legalism and Buddhism interacting, and gives Xunzi's marginalisation as a warning against narrow orthodoxy.

Liu concludes that, under Marxist guidance, the progressive, people-oriented and useful elements of Chinese tradition should be developed through creative transformation and innovative development. The aim is to enrich contemporary Chinese Marxism and serve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Liu presents this as consistent with the Party's long-standing method rather than a break with it. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the Second Integration is justified historically, and of how it handles critique, foreign influence and the plurality of Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Our emphasis today on drawing on the intellectual wealth of fine traditional culture by no means implies that we may launch a "re-criticism" of the critique of decadent elements of tradition made in the revolutionary periods of history.
quoteZh: 我们今天强调吸取优秀传统文化的思想财富，决不意味着可以对历史上革命时期对传统文化腐朽部分的批判来一次“再批判”。

glossary.explanation: The combination of Marxism's basic principles with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping first stated it explicitly in 2021, as a complement to the First Integration with China's concrete realities.

The official formula that Marxism must be combined both with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping presented it in 2021 as a core principle of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A leading official goal of the Party, centred on restoring China's national strength and international standing. It is widely used in Party documents since the 2010s.

t: The key to socialism with Chinese characteristics lies in the "Two Integrations"
zh: 中国特色社会主义的关键在于“两个结合”
paras: Luo Wendong and Lü Handong take up Xi Jinping's claim, made at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, that what makes Chinese socialism distinctive is its Chinese characteristics, and that the key to those characteristics is the Two Integrations. The article, published in Shandong Social Sciences in 2025, argues that the Two Integrations are the necessary path, the greatest magic weapon and the continuing requirement for opening up and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article is organised in three parts. The first treats the Two Integrations as the necessary path, setting out how they provide the theoretical cornerstone, how the first integration (Marxism with China's concrete realities) gives the system its content in each era, and how the second (Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture) deepens its cultural roots. The second part tests the claim that the Two Integrations are the greatest magic weapon against four components: path, theoretical system, institutions and culture. The third part draws forward-looking requirements for the present.

The authors argue that socialism with Chinese characteristics is neither a copy of Marx's templates, of Soviet practice nor of Western modernization, but a creation produced by combining Marxism's basic tenets with Chinese conditions and culture. On the path, they cite Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping against copying foreign models. On theory, they present the Two Integrations as a weapon against dogmatism, empiricism, nihilism and restorationism. On institutions, they trace the people's congress system, political consultation and regional ethnic autonomy to traditional ideas such as people-centred governance and "great unity". They add that the integrations consolidate Chinese cultural subjectivity, which they describe as damaged in the modern semi-colonial period.

For the present, the authors call for self-confidence and self-reliance in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and for building an autonomous Chinese system of knowledge. They also call for openness in pursuing Chinese modernization, whose five features they link to traditional concepts such as "harmony between humanity and nature", and for creating a new form of human civilization. In their account, this requires both keeping to fundamental principles and innovating. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how current Party theory connects the Two Integrations to Chinese modernization, with the leadership quotations that support it.
quoteEn: The path of socialism with Chinese characteristics did not fall from the sky, nor is it innate in the Chinese mind a priori.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义道路不是从天上掉下来的，也不是中国人头脑中先验固有的

glossary.explanation: Party formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second integration was formally put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.
The official name for China's path, theory and system of socialism since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping.
The official term for China's path to modernization, defined in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) through five features, including common prosperity and peaceful development.
The consciousness and capacity of a nation to identify with, carry on and renew its own culture. Xi Jinping stressed it in his 2023 speech on cultural inheritance.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxism to China's realities and to each historical era.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A Party term, used by Xi Jinping in 2021, for the civilization it says Chinese modernization is creating, distinct from the Western model.

t: The theoretical innovation and practical power of the thesis that "humanity and nature are a community of life"
zh: “人与自然是生命共同体”重要论断的理论创新和实践伟力
paras: Yu Hai takes up the thesis, put forward by Xi Jinping in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), that humanity and nature form a community of life and that people must respect, adapt to and protect nature. The article argues that this thesis is a major theoretical innovation: it rests on Marxism, on traditional Chinese ecological culture and on long practical exploration, and it carries real weight in practice. Yu says it is central to grasping Chinese modernization and to advancing the building of a Beautiful China.

The commentary, a newspaper theory piece, looks at the thesis in historical, theoretical and practical terms. It first traces its three sources. It then sets out the basic requirements for implementing it, reviews the achievements recorded since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and ends with the international dimension of building a clean and beautiful world.

On the sources, Yu reads the thesis as continuing Marx's view that humans are products of nature, and as drawing on classical Chinese texts such as the Laozi, Mencius, Xunzi and the Book of Rites. Yu also traces it to Xi's local posts in Zhengding, Xiamen, Ningde, Sanming and Shanghai, where Xi stressed both preventing pollution and the economic value of green mountains and clear waters. The requirements are to plan development from the standpoint of harmony between humanity and nature, to treat respecting, adapting to and protecting nature as a dialectical unity, and to balance high-quality development with high-level protection. Yu argues that China, with over 1.4 billion people and limited environmental capacity, cannot follow the Western path. The article cites progress in air and water quality, green and low-carbon transition, ecosystem protection, the dual carbon goals and institutional reform. Examples include average PM2.5 falling from 72 to 29.3 micrograms per cubic metre between 2013 and 2024, and 90.4% of surface-water sections rated Class I–III in 2024.

Yu concludes that the thesis offers direction for international cooperation. The article calls for joint action on climate change under multilateralism and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, for biodiversity governance, and for cooperation on desertification, marine pollution and nuclear safety. It also calls for a green Belt and Road Initiative, which Yu presents as contributing Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to global ecological governance. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Chinese ecological civilization theory is framed and which achievements it cites.
quoteEn: High-level protection is an important support for high-quality development; ecology-first, green and low-carbon high-quality development can be achieved only by relying on high-level protection.
quoteZh: 高水平保护是高质量发展的重要支撑，生态优先、绿色低碳的高质量发展只有依靠高水平保护才能实现。

glossary.zh: 人与自然是生命共同体
glossary.pinyin: rén yǔ zìrán shì shēngmìng gòngtóngtǐ
glossary.literal: humanity and nature are a life community
glossary.explanation: A thesis stated in Xi Jinping's report to the 19th Party Congress (2017). It holds that humans and nature are interdependent and that people must respect, adapt to and protect nature.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. Official texts describe it as including harmony between humanity and nature.
The official term for the stage in which growth is meant to shift from speed to quality, with green and low-carbon development as a key element.
An official goal, in place since the 18th Party Congress (2012), of building a country with a healthy ecological environment.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation initiative, launched in 2013. The article presents its green dimension as part of global ecological governance.

t: The generative logic and practical principles of Chinese modernization
st: An examination based on Marx's theory of the social organism
zh: 中国式现代化的生成逻辑与实践遵循
zhSub: 基于马克思社会有机体理论的考察
source: Marxist Studies (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Liu Dong asks why Chinese modernization can offer other countries a new option for achieving modernization. The author's answer is that its generative logic can be explained through Marx's theory of the social organism, a component of historical materialism. Read this way, Chinese modernization is a creative application of that theory in China, and the theory in turn yields practical principles for advancing it.

The article, published in Marxist Studies in 2025, has three parts. The first sets out the theory: the holistic development of the organism's elements, its all-round production and reproduction, and its open, integrating tendency. The second maps five features of Chinese modernization onto the theory and traces each through the Party's history from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping. The third draws four lessons from the theory.

Liu's central move is to treat modernization as the outcome of the social organism's economic, political, cultural, social and ecological elements developing together, driven by the production of material goods, ideas, human life itself, social relations and the human–nature relationship. On this basis Liu links each feature to a part of the theory. A huge population corresponds to the reproduction of human beings. Common prosperity corresponds to the people as the subject of practice. Material and cultural-ethical advancement corresponds to resolving the principal contradiction. Harmony between humanity and nature corresponds to the reproduction of that relationship. Peaceful development corresponds to the ideal of a society without exploitation. The author contrasts this with Western modernization, which in the article's account is dominated by the logic of capital and has relied on pollution before clean-up, war, colonialism and plunder. The four lessons are that the organism's capacity for self-directed choice requires Party leadership. Its wholeness calls for a systems approach. Its changeability calls for reform and innovation. Its openness calls for expanding opening up.

Liu concludes that Marx's theory shows modernization to be neither a single path nor identical with Westernization. In the article's view, Chinese modernization is a form of conscious, Party-led remodelling of the social organism that both follows general laws and reflects China's own conditions. The author calls for upholding Party leadership in every field, coordinating development systematically, deepening reform, and widening opening up at a time of mounting risks. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese theorist grounds the official account of Chinese modernization in Marx's organism concept and in a Party-history narrative.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a creative application and development of Marx's theory of the social organism, and a practical manifestation of that theory in China.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是对马克思社会有机体理论的创造性运用和发展，是马克思社会有机体理论在中国的实践展现。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

A strand of historical materialism that treats society as an interrelated, evolving whole rather than a fixed structure. Marx's image of society as 'an organism capable of change' is the usual reference point.

A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping's leadership has made a central objective. The article treats it as the expression of the people's status as the main force.

The Party's official judgment of the central contradiction in society at a given stage. It was redefined in 2017 as one between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

t: Grasping the core meaning and practical requirements of developing new quality productive forces
zh: 深刻领悟发展新质生产力的核心要义和实践要求
paras: This article in Red Flag Manuscript sets out to explain what new quality productive forces are, why they matter and how to develop them, following Xi Jinping's speeches and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Zhong argues that Xi's discussion of the concept systematically answers these three questions and represents an innovation in, and development of, the Marxist theory of productive forces. The article is a Party-theory commentary.

The text has three parts. The first defines new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces consistent with the new development philosophy. The second presents their development as an intrinsic requirement of, and key lever for, high-quality development and Chinese modernization. The third gives practical requirements: innovation, industrial upgrading, local adaptation and reform of the relations of production.

In the first part, Zhong relies on Xi's definition: innovation-led, high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality, with a sharp rise in total factor productivity as the core marker. Zhong reads the "new quality" through the three elements of productive forces. These are new types of workers, new means of labour such as artificial intelligence and digital technologies, and new objects of labour such as new materials, new energy and data. Zhong holds that Chinese modernization and high-quality development need a solid material and technological base, which these forces supply. In the practical part, Zhong stresses original and disruptive innovation and says core technologies cannot be begged or bought. Technology must be turned into industry ("from 0 to 1" and "from 1 to infinity"), with strategic emerging and future industries as the main arena. Traditional industries should be upgraded rather than discarded: the article cites their share at about 80% of industrial value added above designated size. Zhong calls for adapting to local conditions, avoiding a rush into the same sectors and bubbles, and building the new before breaking the old.

Zhong concludes that production relations must be adjusted to suit new quality productive forces. The proposals include deepening economic and science-and-technology reforms, removing bottlenecks, building a high-standard market system, letting advanced factors of production flow smoothly, expanding high-level opening up and linking education, science and talent policy. Institutional innovation is presented as the way to remove obstacles and release innovative energy. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theorists link new quality productive forces to high-quality development, local policy and the reform agenda of the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces and traditional industries are not in opposition; the key is to use new technologies to transform and upgrade traditional industries and to actively promote their move towards the high end, intelligent and green.
quoteZh: 新质生产力与传统产业不是对立关系，关键是要用新技术改造提升传统产业，积极促进产业高端化、智能化、绿色化

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24 for an advanced form of productive forces driven by innovation, high technology and higher efficiency. It is presented as a development of the Marxist theory of productive forces.

The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and quality. Since the 20th Party Congress (2022) it has been called the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015 as guidance for economic policy.

t: Mao Zedong's exploration of and contribution to the path of modernization after the founding of the People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立后毛泽东对现代化道路的探索与贡献
paras: Zhang Guozuo and Yang Ruonan ask how Mao Zedong approached the modernization of a poor, populous country after 1949, and what that exploration left for later generations. Taking up Xi Jinping's description of Mao as the 'great founder' of China's socialist modernization, they argue that Mao's work gave Chinese modernization its ideological, material and institutional preconditions. They also contend that it anticipated the five features that Xi now attributes to Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around those five features, each treated as an area of Mao's post-1949 thought and practice. It covers the country's huge population, the orientation towards fairness, equality and common prosperity, the joint improvement of material and cultural life, and the pairing of economic growth with the protection of nature. It ends with the creation of a peaceful international environment. The authors draw on Mao's speeches, annotations and letters and on statistics from the Mao period, and close by linking Mao's exploration to Xi's formulations.

On population, the authors argue that Mao saw a large population as both a heavy responsibility and a source of strength. They credit his leadership with the patriotic health campaigns, rural barefoot doctors and cooperative medical care, which raised life expectancy, and with literacy drives, which cut illiteracy. On equality, they say Mao opposed both egalitarianism and excessive disparity, and pursued a staged, balanced route to common prosperity, set out in 'On the Ten Major Relationships'. On the environment and foreign policy, they cite Mao's calls to 'green the motherland' and to integrate farming, forestry and herding. They also cite his policy of fighting to stop war, advocating peaceful coexistence and 'never seeking hegemony'. The authors state that China under Mao launched no war of aggression for its own modernization.

The authors conclude that Mao's practice, in their words, gave a first answer, in theory and practice, to how a poor China could modernize. They present this as a process of repeated practice and understanding, in line with Mao's 'On Practice'. They add that Xi has inherited, enriched and systematized this legacy as Chinese modernization, with its essential requirements, strategic timetable to the middle of the century and guiding principles, and that studying Xi's statements reveals both continuity with Mao and further innovation. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars trace Xi-era Chinese modernization back to Mao-era policies and sources.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's view of modernizing a country with a huge population was dialectical: a huge population means many difficulties in providing food, clothing, housing and transport and a heavy responsibility for achieving modernization, but also great strength for achieving it.
quoteZh: 毛泽东对在人口规模巨大的国家进行现代化建设的看法是辩证的：人口规模巨大，解决衣食住行的困难多，实现现代化的责任大，但实现现代化的力量也大。

glossary.explanation: The official concept, elaborated by Xi Jinping especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a modernization led by the Communist Party and distinguished from Western models by features such as huge population scale and common prosperity.
A goal of prosperity shared by all the people, not only some groups or regions. It is associated with socialism in Party discourse and has been stressed under Xi Jinping.
Rural health workers with basic training who provided primary care in villages from the 1960s. They are commonly associated with the Mao-era rural cooperative medical system.

t: The "Two Integrations": historical context, theoretical logic, practical power and path of development
zh: “两个结合”：历史脉络、理论逻辑、实践伟力与发展进路
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (当代世界与社会主义), 2025 no. 1
paras: This article asks how the Party's principle of combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture, now formulated as the Two Integrations, arose and why it matters. Wang argues that the Two Integrations are the key to what distinguishes socialism with Chinese characteristics, and that they form the regular pattern by which Marxism is adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Wang presents the principle as a source of both theoretical innovation and national rejuvenation.

The article has four parts. The first traces the history of the "first integration" and the "second integration" from Mao Zedong through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to Xi Jinping, and links each to a historic leap in theory: Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second part sets out the theoretical logic. The third examines practical effects, and the fourth proposes directions for further development.

On theoretical logic, Wang gives four grounds. Marxism develops by being combined with each nation's conditions and by taking national form. China's revolution, construction and reform required a solution to the problem of how to apply Marxism, after dogmatism and copying Russian experience had caused setbacks. Marxism and fine traditional culture are held to be inherently compatible, illustrated by Guo Moruo's 1925 dialogue between Marx and Confucius and by Xi's list of shared values such as "the world belongs to all". Finally, Party members' cultural consciousness and confidence turned these needs into reality. Wang distinguishes the two integrations: the first joins theory with practice, while the second joins a body of thought with a national cultural form and supplies the cultural conditions for the first. On practical power, Wang says the principle carried the Party's central tasks in each period, opened and developed socialism with Chinese characteristics, and consolidated cultural subjectivity against cultural nihilism and "Westernization".

Wang concludes with three requirements. The Party must hold to Marxism as its "soul" and fine traditional culture as its "roots". It must fuse the essence of Marxism with the best of traditional culture, with Marxism remaining the guiding position and with opposition to both cultural nihilism and cultural restorationism. And it must draw fresh experience from the people's practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how the Two Integrations are traced historically and justified theoretically, with extensive citation of Mao and Xi.
quoteEn: The Two Integrations are closely linked and mutually dependent, and are unified in the process of advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: “两个结合”紧密联系，相互依赖，统一于推进马克思主义中国化时代化的进程之中。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2021 and the Party now treats it as a core method of theoretical innovation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions.
A concept stressed in recent Party discourse: a nation's capacity to maintain its own cultural identity and agency, especially in relation to Western influence.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Multidimensional reflections on constructing the theoretical system of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化理论体系构建的多维审思
paras: Wang Zengfu asks how the theoretical system of Chinese modernization, described as only preliminarily built since the 18th Party Congress (2012), can be systematically constructed and innovated. The article argues that this requires a combined view of history and reality, theory and practice, and China and the world. Wang presents the task as a requirement of summarising the Party's experience, a practical need for extending the path, and an academic mission for Chinese philosophy and social science in developing world modernization theory.

The article is organised in four parts. The first deals with the philosophical support and modes of thinking behind the system, beginning with a critique of Western modernization theory. The second traces the discourse and inner logic of the system, from earlier concepts such as the Four Modernizations to the formal concept of Chinese modernization. The third examines its cultural dimension and the claim that it creates a new form of human civilisation. The fourth considers its global outlook and world narrative, ending with a community with a shared future for mankind.

Wang first characterises Western modernization theory as a post-1945 ideological apparatus that rests on a tradition/modernity binary, a single-line model equating modernization with Westernisation, and an overemphasis on internal causes that ignores colonial expansion. Against this, the Chinese system rests on dialectical and historical materialism, critically absorbs virtue-based thought from traditional Chinese culture and the rationalism of Western philosophy, and replaces zero-sum, self-centred, one-sided and static thinking with symbiotic, perspective-switching, holistic and developmental thinking. Wang argues that its internal logic runs through the Two Integrations, historical materialism and a people-first orientation, in contrast with capital-first Western models. Wang also holds that cultural subjectivity lets the system escape imitation and dependence, while Chinese modernization turns the general idea of modernization into a Chinese proposition and, by adhering to and innovating on scientific socialism, adds to that body of theory.

Wang concludes that the system is both a product of Chinese practice and a contribution to world modernization. In Wang's account it supplies values and discursive resources for a community with a shared future for mankind, and it opens a different route for latecomer countries. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars frame the theoretical system of Chinese modernization against Western modernization theory.
quoteEn: The essence of Chinese modernization is to convert the universal proposition of modernization into a Chinese proposition, that is, to turn "building modernization in China" into "building China's modernization".
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的实质是把现代化的普遍命题转换为中国命题，即将“在中国建设现代化”转化为“建设中国的现代化”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, formally set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). Its stated features include a huge population, common prosperity, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
A formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for shared security, development and values among states. The article treats it as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization.
An official claim that Chinese modernization produces a civilisational form distinct from Western modernity, covering material, political, cultural, social and ecological dimensions.

t: Accelerating the formation of relations of production better suited to new quality productive forces
zh: 加快形成同新质生产力更相适应的生产关系
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), this article asks what institutional changes are needed to form relations of production that fit new quality productive forces more closely. Wang argues that better-adapted relations of production are the fundamental driving force of productive-force development. On that basis, the author holds that developing new quality productive forces requires further comprehensive deepening of reform, clearing institutional blockages, and so supplying strong momentum and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around four areas of reform. These are the new-type whole-nation system for science and technology, mechanisms for industrial transformation and upgrading, institutions supporting comprehensive innovation across education, science and talent, and the rules of factor markets. Each section follows a similar pattern: why the area matters, what has been achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012), what problems remain, and what measures should follow.

In the first two sections, Wang treats scientific and technological innovation as the core element of new quality productive forces. The author calls for a new-type whole-nation system under socialist market conditions, with centralised Party leadership of science and technology, a stronger role for enterprises as innovation actors, and a shift from "follower" to "leader". Industrial policy is to join technological and industrial innovation, upgrade traditional industries, and cultivate strategic emerging and future industries. The third and fourth sections argue that education, science and talent reforms must proceed together, including more autonomy for scientists and better conversion of research results. Wang also urges that factor markets, including data as a new factor, steer resources towards new quality productive forces. Proposals include patient capital, venture investment, a unified national market, anti-monopoly measures and curbs on "involution-style" competition.

Wang concludes that adapting relations of production to productive forces, the superstructure to the economic base, and national governance to social development is the task of deepening reform. The article sets out the policy mechanisms it considers necessary, while acknowledging problems such as weak original innovation, scattered research resources, shortages of top talent, local protectionism and market fragmentation. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how the policy agenda of the Third Plenum is linked to the theory of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that better-adapted relations of production are the fundamental driving force of productive-force development and can fully stimulate the vitality and enthusiasm of social production.
quoteZh: 实践证明，更相适应的生产关系是生产力发展的根本动力，能够充分激发社会生产的活力和积极性。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and better combinations of labour, means of labour and objects of labour.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: new-type system of mobilising the whole nation
glossary.explanation: An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs under market-economy conditions.

A Marxist category for the social relations, especially ownership and distribution, in which production takes place. Chinese official discourse stresses that they must be adjusted to the level of productive forces.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization.

t: Chinese modernization's answer to the "world history" problem and its world-historical significance
zh: 中国式现代化对“世界历史”难题的解答及其世界历史意义
paras: Against a backdrop of protectionism, unilateralism and a backlash against economic globalization, Liu Xingang asks how Marx's theory of "world history" can inform the present. The article argues that Marx identified a set of problems produced by Western-led modernization, and that Chinese modernization, by moving beyond that model, offers a scientific answer to them. In Liu's account, this answer is a Chinese contribution to the global problems of an era of great changes unseen in a century.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's critique of Western modernization's "world history" process, drawing on The Communist Manifesto, The German Ideology and Capital, and setting it against Ricardo, Adam Smith and Bastiat. The second sets out how Chinese modernization responds, citing Xi Jinping's speeches and initiatives such as the Belt and Road Initiative, the BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. The third assesses the world-historical significance of this response.

Liu says Marx found three problems. Formally equal exchange produced subordination, dependence and colonial relations; the world market widened development gaps and allowed the exploitation of poorer countries; and the transfer of capitalism's contradictions onto others bred trade friction, economic crisis and military conflict. Liu holds that the root error of Western modernization is to ignore differences of national conditions and culture, treating modernization as Westernization. Chinese modernization, which Liu says breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization, answers with a community with a shared future for mankind, equal and orderly multipolarity, inclusive economic globalization, genuine multilateralism and a people-centred stance. It also calls for reform of global governance that gives more weight to developing countries.

Liu concludes that Chinese modernization changes the way modernization is thought about. It affirms the diversity of national paths and gives developing countries confidence to look for their own. It also offers practical platforms for cooperation, and Liu presents these as "Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach" to unilateralism, protectionism and de-globalization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar links Marx's world-history theory to current Chinese foreign-policy concepts and global governance proposals.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization "breaks the myth that 'modernization equals Westernization'" and offers human society a new option for its modernization process.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化“打破了‘现代化=西方化’的迷思”，为人类社会的现代化进程提供了新的选择

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept for China's path of modernization, set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept advanced by Xi Jinping from 2013. It calls for cooperation, shared interests and a more equitable international order.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure, trade and policy links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse for the current shifts in the global balance of power, especially the rise of emerging economies and relative Western decline.
Chinese texts use this for the institutions and rules that manage international affairs. They often call for reforming it to give developing countries a larger voice.

t: Using scientific methods to further deepen reform comprehensively and advance Chinese modernization
zh: 以科学方法进一步全面深化改革、推进中国式现代化
paras: Lin Jianhua asks how the strategic plan to further deepen reform comprehensively can be turned into real momentum for Chinese modernization. The author's answer is that mastering and applying scientific method is an essential guarantee and a basic skill for Party members and cadres. Lin presents Xi Jinping's methodology of reform, developed since the 18th Party Congress (2012) from dialectical and historical materialism, as the guide for this task.

The article is a commentary on Xi Jinping's speech at the study session for provincial and ministerial leading cadres on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It opens with a short discussion of what "method" means philosophically. It then works through four relationships that Xi identifies, one section each: reform and the rule of law, breaking and establishing, reform and opening up, and deployment and implementation.

On the first two pairs, Lin argues that reform and law are like "two wings" and must move together. Reform should perfect the legal system, and major reforms should have a legal basis and proceed on legal tracks. Drawing on materialist dialectics and the Chinese tradition, Lin treats "breaking" and "establishing" as a dialectical unity: establish first, then break, and never break before establishing, so as to avoid an institutional vacuum. Lin cites past practice such as establishing the new development philosophy while breaking with GDP-centrism. On the third pair, Lin holds that deeper reform and high-level opening up reinforce each other, and calls for institutional opening up, meaning alignment with international rules and standards, while relying on self-reliance. On the fourth, Lin stresses that "one part deployment, nine parts implementation". The article calls for focus on key points, systematic integration, clear responsibilities, a correct view of performance and perseverance.

Lin concludes that these methods help cadres carry the Third Plenum's reforms through to practical results. The article insists that the Party's overall leadership, Marxism, socialism with Chinese characteristics and people's democratic dictatorship must never be shaken, whatever is reformed. It is a Party-line exposition of Xi Jinping's reform methodology rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how current Chinese leadership frames the "scientific methods" behind its reform agenda.
quoteEn: Breaking is the means; establishing is the aim.
quoteZh: 破是手段，立是目的。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's own path to modernization, elaborated by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.pinyin: pò lì bìngjǔ, xiān lì hòu pò
glossary.literal: break and establish together, establish before breaking
glossary.explanation: A principle Xi Jinping stresses for reform: new institutions or approaches should be built before old ones are discarded, to avoid disorder.
Opening up that goes beyond the flow of goods and capital to align domestic rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones.
The slogan of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which adopted a decision on deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization.

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: The Party's policy of governing through law under Party leadership, the theme of the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014).

t: Mao Zedong's thinking and practice on the "Second Integration" in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期毛泽东关于“第二个结合”的思考与实践
paras: Zhu Wei asks how Mao Zedong, in the Yan'an years (1936–1947), combined Marxism with Chinese history and culture, which today's Party theory calls the Second Integration. Zhu argues that Mao never formulated it as a separate concept, but that it was already embedded in his proposition of the sinification of Marxism. In Zhu's reading, it shows the theoretical awareness and practical initiative behind the "Second Integration" later set out under Xi Jinping.

The article has five parts. It traces how Mao raised the sinification proposition in 1938 and how his wording developed up to 1943. It then explains why Mao studied Chinese history and culture, and sets out his attitude, principles, methods and routes for treating the cultural heritage. It ends by showing how Mao drew on traditional culture to enrich Marxism. The evidence is Mao's speeches, letters and comments on the work of Fan Wenlan, Chen Boda and Ai Siqi, and on Peking-opera adaptations.

Zhu's central claim is that Mao read the heritage through historical materialism, not as simple inheritance. His attitude was to respect history and not sever it. His principles were "making the past serve the present" and "weeding through the old to bring forth the new". His method was critical sifting of "democratic essence" from "feudal dross", as in his support for a Marxist history of Confucian classics and for a general history of China. Zhu adds that Mao reworked old terms such as "seeking truth from facts", gave them Marxist content, and made them part of the Party's ideological line. In the other direction, Zhu says Mao drew on the national spirit (the Foolish Old Man story, hard struggle), on Sunzi's military thought, on cadre standards such as "appointing people on their merits", and on popular idioms and operas to give Marxism a national form. Zhu presents this as part of Mao's struggle against Wang Ming's dogmatism and of his response to the national crisis.

Zhu concludes that Mao treated integration with Chinese culture as subordinate to, and serving, integration with the concrete practice of the revolution, in order to make Marxism take root in China. Only after the 18th Party Congress (2012), Zhu says, did the Party need to separate out the Second Integration and give it explicit content. Zhu calls for continuing to link the essence of Marxism with the best of traditional culture and with the shared values of ordinary people. Read the original if you want a source-based account of the Yan'an roots of the Second Integration, with many of Mao's remarks on culture, history and philosophy.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's "sinification of Marxism" contains both the integration of the basic principles of Marxism with "the concrete practice of the Chinese revolution" and their "deep integration with Chinese history and Chinese culture".
quoteZh: 毛泽东提出的“马克思主义的中国化”，既包含马克思主义基本原理同“中国革命的具体实践相结合”，也包含同“中国历史、中国文化深相结合”。

glossary.explanation: The combination of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping presented it in 2023 as the counterpart to the First Integration, the combination of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The Party's term for adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions, history and culture. Mao Zedong first put it forward in 1938.
A phrase from the Han dynasty historian Ban Gu, which Mao reinterpreted in 1941. It became the core of the Party's ideological line.

glossary.en: making the past serve the present
glossary.explanation: A cultural-policy principle of using the heritage of the past for present needs. Mao stated it explicitly only after 1949.

glossary.en: weeding through the old to bring forth the new
glossary.literal: push out the old, bring forth the new
glossary.explanation: Mao's 1942 inscription for the Yan'an Peking Opera Research Institute. It later became a guiding principle of Party cultural policy.

t: The "Two Integrations" and the creation of a new cultural organism
zh: “两个结合”与新的文化生命体的造就
source: Marxist Studies (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Liu Jianwu takes up Xi Jinping's statement that integration is "not a platter" but a "chemical reaction" producing an organically unified new cultural organism. The article asks what this organism is, how it is formed, and what its outcomes and wider influence are. Liu's thesis is that the Two Integrations (of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture) are a process of mutual fit, fusion, interaction, respect and mutual fulfilment, and that this process has produced a new cultural form, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out five features of the formation mechanism. The second describes the product in three forms: a new theory, a new culture and a new civilisation. The third discusses the lasting effects of the concept. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches, with some reference to Mao Zedong and the Party's history from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On the mechanism, Liu argues that Marxism and traditional culture are compatible in four respects: ideals ("a world of great harmony" and communism), the people-centred standpoint, the spirit of striving, and the collectivist view of the person. Integration is achieved by solving China's concrete problems, not by moving from book to book. Marxism "activates" the genes of Chinese civilisation, while traditional culture "enriches" Marxism's cultural life. Liu rejects both "using Confucianism to transform Marxism" and the reverse, insisting on mutual respect. On outcomes, Liu holds that the new theory is Marxism adapted to China, which is the "soul" of the organism. The new culture is socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, joining the "soul vein" (Marxism) and the "root vein" (tradition). The new civilisation is Chinese modernization, which the article presents as surpassing Western modernization and breaking the equation of modernization with Westernization.

Liu concludes that the concept consolidates China's cultural subjectivity and spiritual independence, and helps resolve the "ancient–modern, Chinese–Western dispute". It also clarifies the Second Integration against the claims that one side must replace the other or that Marxism is simply foreign. In Liu's account, Marxism adapted to China is now Chinese culture that has grown from Chinese soil. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theoretical account of how the "new cultural organism" is conceptualised and what it is said to imply for culture, modernization and civilisation.
quoteEn: The process of "integration" is a process of mutual fulfilment, and the result of mutual fulfilment is the creation of a new cultural organism in which the basic tenets of Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture are organically unified.
quoteZh: “结合”的过程就是相互成就的过程，相互成就的结果就是造就了马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化有机统一的新的文化生命体

glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the First) and with its fine traditional culture (the Second, stressed by Xi Jinping since 2021–2023).
A phrase Xi Jinping used in 2023 for the product of the Second Integration, described as an organically unified whole of Marxism and traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.
The Party's term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Mao Zedong's threefold reshaping of the traditional Chinese doctrine of contradiction
zh: 毛泽东对我国传统矛盾学说的三维重塑
source: Journal of Social Sciences of Hunan Normal University, 2025 no. 2
paras: Wang Xiangqing and Yang Xue ask how Mao Zedong related to the doctrine of contradiction in traditional Chinese philosophy, which earlier thinkers expressed through the terms yin-yang, "two ends" and similar notions. They argue that Mao's engagement with it took three forms: sublation, innovative development and creative transformation. Because Mao treated the law of the unity of opposites as the fundamental law of materialist dialectics, the authors take his reading of this doctrine as the core of his encounter with traditional Chinese dialectics.

The article first traces the doctrine from the Book of Changes through Han Feizi, Liu Yuxi, Laozi, Dong Zhongshu, Ban Gu, Zhang Zai, Zhu Xi and Wang Fuzhi. It then sets Mao's On Contradiction (1937), his reading notes, his 1958 Chengdu talk and his leadership writings against this background. The three parts follow the three modes of reshaping, each illustrated with textual evidence.

On sublation, the authors say Mao kept the idea that opposites transform into each other but rejected the unconditional version found in Laozi and Wang Fuzhi, noting his marginal comment "under certain conditions" on Li Zhi's preface.
