Mao also reversed the tradition's tilt towards identity over struggle: in his account identity is relative and struggle absolute, and he added the category of antagonism. On innovative development, the authors credit Mao with first using the paired concepts of universality and particularity and of principal and non-principal aspects, with the latter prompted by his annotations to a Soviet dialectics textbook. He is also credited with holding that a thing's nature is fixed by the principal aspect of its principal contradiction, and that this aspect can change. On creative transformation, the authors show Mao turning contradiction into leadership methods. These pair a broad survey with close study, general calls with individual guidance, leaders with the masses, and the doctrine of two points with the doctrine of the key point, the last illustrated by the image of "playing the piano".

The authors conclude that Mao neither simply inherited nor simply discarded the traditional doctrine. He kept its rational elements, extended them with new concepts and arguments, and turned them into practical methods of work. The article presents this as a case of dialectical continuity between traditional Chinese thought and Marxist philosophy. Read the original if you study Mao Zedong Thought, the intellectual sources of On Contradiction, or the link between traditional Chinese philosophy and Party leadership methods.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's examination of the traditional doctrine of contradiction took the form of a threefold reshaping: its sublation, its innovative development and its creative transformation.
quoteZh: 毛泽东对传统矛盾学说的省察体现为三维重塑：即对传统矛盾学说的扬弃、创新性发展和创造性转化。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: keeping the rational elements of something while rejecting its negative ones and moving beyond it.
In Chinese discourse on tradition, extending and enriching inherited ideas with new content. It is usually paired with creative transformation.
Converting inherited cultural elements into forms suited to present needs. Here the authors use it for Mao turning the doctrine of contradiction into leadership methods.
A philosophical essay by Mao Zedong from 1937, based on lectures at Yan'an. It is treated in China as a major statement of Marxist dialectics in a Chinese setting.

t: Promoting the coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization
zh: 推动物质文明和精神文明协调发展
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how material and spiritual civilization should be related in Chinese modernization. Liu takes recent examples, including the DeepSeek AI model and the success of the animated film Ne Zha 2, as signs of vitality in both spheres. Citing Xi Jinping, Liu argues that the two must be handled through "two hands, both firm" so that they coordinate and reinforce each other.

The piece sets out three requirements for handling the relationship: a dialectical, a comprehensive and a balanced viewpoint. Each is explained briefly and tied to practical tasks such as building a high-standard socialist market economy and deepening cultural reform.

On the dialectical view, Liu holds that material civilization is the foundation, supplying conditions and practical experience, while spiritual civilization supplies spiritual impetus and intellectual support. Ethical guidance should help people handle competition and cooperation, efficiency and fairness, and reject profiteering. The comprehensive view treats the two as each other's condition and aim, and calls for the unity of abundant material goods and all-round human development, with the core socialist values leading. The balanced view warns against being firm on one side and soft on the other. It joins high-quality development and new quality productive forces on the economic side with cultural confidence and a stronger socialist ideology on the cultural side.

Liu concludes that socialism with Chinese characteristics is neither materially impoverished nor spiritually barren. Chinese modernization, in this account, is not one of accumulated wealth alongside lost belief and rampant materialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists frame the material–spiritual relationship in official cultural policy.
quoteEn: The socialism with Chinese characteristics that we uphold and develop is by no means a socialism of material poverty or spiritual impoverishment, but a socialism in which material and spiritual civilization develop in balance and promote each other.
quoteZh: 我们坚持和发展的中国特色社会主义，决不是物质贫困的社会主义或精神贫乏的社会主义，而是物质文明和精神文明均衡发展、相互促进的社会主义

glossary.explanation: A paired concept in Party discourse: material civilization covers economic and material progress, spiritual civilization covers ideology, ethics, education and culture. The Party has stressed developing both together since the 1980s.

glossary.pinyin: liǎng shǒu zhuā, liǎng shǒu yìng
glossary.literal: grasp with two hands, both hands hard
glossary.explanation: A slogan, associated with Deng Xiaoping, that calls for equal vigour in economic construction and in spiritual or cultural construction.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. Its stated features include common prosperity and the coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, centred on innovation-led, technology-intensive productive forces as a driver of high-quality development.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

t: Mao Zedong's historic contribution to the China-Africa community with a shared future
zh: 毛泽东对中非命运共同体的历史性贡献
paras: Xi Jinping first used the phrase "China-Africa community with a shared future" in 2013 and said that China and Africa had "always" been such a community. Zhu Bin asks what historical roots lie behind that claim and answers that Mao Zedong made a decisive contribution. In Zhu's account, Mao's support for African struggles against colonialism and imperialism laid an emotional foundation, shaped shared values and supplied basic guiding principles for the community.

The article is a historical-ideological study in four parts: three substantive sections, one for each contribution, and a conclusion. It draws on Mao's talks with African leaders and delegations, telegrams, Chinese aid records and statements by African figures such as Nyerere, Kaunda and Keita. The cases include South Africa's anti-apartheid struggle, Algeria, the Suez Canal crisis, Mali and the Tanzania–Zambia (Tazara) railway.

Zhu argues first that Mao built three kinds of feeling: political solidarity born of shared experience of Western aggression, friendly exchange through meetings with more than twenty African leaders, and selfless mutual help through arms, loans and training. Second, Mao promoted values of sincerity and equality, including criticism of "great-power chauvinism" among Chinese personnel in Africa. He also promoted a balance of righteousness and profit, with aid that carried no conditions or privileges, and a commitment to justice, as in his support for Egypt. Third, Mao's guiding principles were "Africa belongs to the Africans", the refusal to export revolution, service to shared strategic interests, and the improvement of ordinary people's welfare. Zhu uses the Tazara railway and well-drilling, textile and farming projects as illustrations. The article cites 2.476 billion US dollars in aid between 1956 and 1977 as 58 per cent of China's total foreign aid.

Zhu concludes that Mao never visited Africa yet shaped China–Africa relations from nothing to a firm partnership. The article draws three lessons for the present. China should keep its emotional foundation and the "correct view of righteousness and interests", keep the shared values in order to support modernization across the Global South, and follow the guiding principles so that China–Africa ties become a model for a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based Chinese account of how Mao-era Africa policy is being used to ground current China–Africa rhetoric.
quoteEn: Mao consistently held that Africa's affairs should be settled by Africans themselves, relying mainly on their own strength, with foreign aid only as a supplement.
quoteZh: 毛泽东始终坚持整个非洲事务由非洲人自己来解决，以依靠自己力量为主，争取外国援助为辅。

glossary.en: China-Africa community with a shared future
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first put forward in 2013 during a visit to Africa. It describes China and Africa as partners bound by common history and interests.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, in use since about 2013, for a cooperative world order. Chinese official texts present China–Africa ties as a model for it.
Term for developing countries, often used in Chinese official discourse to stress solidarity between China and Africa, Asia and Latin America.
A Maoist-era term for arrogant or condescending behaviour by a large country towards smaller ones. Mao used it to criticise Chinese personnel abroad.

glossary.en: correct view of righteousness and interests
glossary.explanation: A principle of Xi Jinping-era diplomacy that puts moral considerations alongside material gain, especially in dealings with developing countries.

t: How the young Mao Zedong understood and practised "seeking truth from facts"
zh: 毛泽东早年是怎样认识和践行“实事求是”的
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remark at the Yuelu Academy in September 2020 that Mao Zedong was 'nurtured here' and that seeking truth from facts 'originates from here', Liu Jianwu asks how the young Mao came to understand and practise the principle before he became a committed Marxist in the summer of 1920. Liu argues that the Party's ideological line of seeking truth from facts rests on this early formation. In Liu's account, the idea ran through Mao's thought and conduct as a continuous thread, even though no early text of Mao's is known to use the phrase itself.

The article follows Mao's path chronologically and by setting. It begins with his reading of Zheng Guanying's Words of Warning to a Prosperous Age in Shaoshan from 1907. It then covers his half-year at the Dongshan school, and his nine years in Changsha, at the Hunan First Normal School, under teachers such as Yang Changji and Xu Teli, and in the Yuelu Academy. It ends with Mao's own habits of reading, investigation and problem-posing, and a closing section on the character of the process.

Liu's central claim is that outside influences and Mao's own inquiry together explain the result. On the first, Liu reads Zheng as treating the phrase as practical, learning applied to use, and decisive for national strength, going beyond philological scholarship. Liu finds the same ethos in the Dongshan founding documents, in Zeng Guofan's fusion of seeking truth from facts with investigating things to reach principles, in the First Normal School's tradition of practical statecraft, and in the Yuelu plaque. On the second, Liu points to Mao's refusal to follow books uncritically, shown in his marginal comments on Paulsen's ethics text, and to his 'study tours' and factory and village investigations. Liu adds Mao's view that he should understand China before studying abroad, and his 1919 plan for a Problem Study Society listing 144 problems, together with his insistence on a guiding 'ism'.

Liu concludes that the young Mao's grasp of seeking truth from facts was continuous, multi-directional and concrete. It drew on late-Ming and early-Qing practical learning, reformist thought, Hunan statecraft culture and Western ideas. Liu holds that it prepared the ground for Mao's later Marxist transformation of the principle and for Xi's remarks at Yuelu. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account, written from within the Party's historiography, of the intellectual origins of Mao's seeking-truth-from-facts principle.
quoteEn: Starting from reality rather than from books, refusing superstition, blind obedience and bandwagoning, and thinking, analysing and judging independently: this was a distinct style of Mao Zedong's from his early years of reading, and it is precisely an inherent requirement and a vivid embodiment of seeking truth from facts.
quoteZh: 一切从实际出发而不是从书本出发，不迷信、不盲从、不跟风，独立思考、独立分析、独立判断，是毛泽东早年读书时就有的鲜明风格，而这种风格正是实事求是的内在要求和生动体现。

glossary.explanation: An old phrase from Han-dynasty scholarship, later reworked by Mao Zedong into the core of the Chinese Communist Party's ideological line. It stresses starting from actual conditions rather than from dogma or books.

glossary.literal: ordering the world and applying learning to use
glossary.explanation: A Chinese intellectual tradition, strong in Hunan, holding that scholarship should serve practical governance and social problems.

glossary.en: Words of Warning to a Prosperous Age
glossary.explanation: A reformist work by Zheng Guanying (1890s) urging Western-style institutional and educational reform. Mao read it as a teenager.

t: A historical study of the evolution of Mao Zedong's thought on spiritual initiative
zh: 毛泽东关于精神主动思想演进的历史考察
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2025 no. 1
paras: Wang Guanzhong and Deng Jiaojiao take up Mao Zedong's idea of "spiritual initiative" (jingshen zhudong): the active, forward-looking mental state that people bring to understanding and changing the world. They treat it as part of subjective initiative and as an indispensable subjective condition for reaching a goal in practice. The article argues that Mao's thinking on the subject developed in three stages: it emerged in his student years, matured during the New Democratic Revolution, and developed unevenly after 1949. The authors link the topic to Xi Jinping's call to stimulate the people's "historical initiative" in advancing Chinese modernization.

The article is organised chronologically. It begins with Mao's student decade (from 1910 to 1920), then covers the period from his conversion to Marxism in 1920 to the founding of the People's Republic in 1949. It closes with the years from 1949 to Mao's death in 1976. Evidence comes from Mao's early essays and reading notes, his letters, Party resolutions and his wartime and postwar writings. The authors also draw on his marginal comments on a Soviet political economy textbook.

In the first stage, the authors argue, the young Mao combined Wang Yangming's "philosophy of the mind" with Western ideas. He prized the "power of the mind", the tempering of will and a "life of upward striving", though still on idealist and dualist foundations. In the second stage, Mao criticised passivity and the "hired-hand" mentality within the Party, and tied initiative to seizing the initiative in practice. Wang and Deng reconstruct the sequence "spiritual initiative, practical initiative, attainment of the goal". They also set out four paths to spiritual initiative: mastering Marxism-Leninism, improving cadres' ability to mobilise the masses, mental preparation, and democratic centralism as an institutional guarantee. After 1949, the authors say, Mao tied initiative more firmly to seeking truth from facts, added economic development as a path, and stressed institutions. From 1957, however, leftist errors and an inflated view of subjective effort, most visibly in the Great Leap Forward, led him to leave "blind enthusiasm" uncorrected.

The authors conclude that the core of the idea is winning the initiative in practice through spiritual initiative, with respect for objective laws and seeking truth from facts as its basic constraint. They present it as a resource for overcoming pessimism, slackness and "lying flat" in the new era and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They call for building institutions, theoretical study and habits of thought that turn passivity into initiative. They also call for strict observance of democratic centralism, so as to avoid "exaggerating the role of subjective will and subjective effort". Read the original if you want a source-based chronology of how Mao's views on subjective initiative developed, including his early writings and his own errors after 1957.
quoteEn: Winning the initiative in practice through spiritual initiative is the essence of this thought, while respecting objective laws and upholding seeking truth from facts are its basic guidelines.
quoteZh: 以精神主动赢得实践主动权是这一思想的精华，尊重客观规律和坚持实事求是，是这一思想的基本遵循。

glossary.explanation: A positive, proactive mental state in practical activity, treated in Chinese Marxism as part of subjective initiative. It is linked to Xi Jinping's call for "historical initiative".
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A principle of basing policy on objective reality. It is associated with Mao Zedong and later with Deng Xiaoping, and is treated as the core of the Party's ideological line.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party: discussion and election from below combined with centralised, binding decisions.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution (c. 1919–1949) aimed at overthrowing imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism under proletarian leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".

t: Mao Zedong's exploration of and contribution to the path of modernization after the founding of the People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立后毛泽东对现代化道路的探索与贡献
paras: Zhang Guozuo and Yang Ruonan ask how Mao Zedong approached modernizing a poor, populous country after 1949. Taking Xi Jinping's description of Mao as the "great founder" of China's socialist modernization as their starting point, they argue that Mao's explorations laid ideological, material and institutional foundations for Chinese modernization. In their account, these explorations already showed five features that Xi later codified as distinctive of Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around those five features, each treated as a field of Mao-era practice. These are a huge population, the pursuit of fairness, equality and common prosperity, the joint improvement of material and cultural life, the parallel development of the economy and protection of nature, and the creation of a peaceful international environment. Evidence comes from Mao's speeches, comments and directives, together with statistics on health, literacy, schooling and forestry policy, and the 1971 UN vote on China's seat. A short conclusion links the Mao period to Xi's formulations.

The authors argue that Mao took a dialectical view of population: a large population meant heavy burdens but also great strength. They credit the new political order, patriotic health campaigns, barefoot doctors, rural cooperative medicine and literacy drives with raising life expectancy and educational levels. On values, they say Mao rejected both egalitarianism and excessive disparity, and pursued common prosperity step by step, citing the Ten Great Relationships and Mao's 1954 remarks on a phased path to a modern socialist country. They present his calls to afforest the country and balance farming, forestry and herding as early ecological thinking. In foreign policy they stress fighting to stop war, the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, and a pledge never to seek hegemony.

The authors conclude that Mao, working through repeated practice and reflection, gave a pioneering answer to how a poor and backward China could modernize. They argue that Xi Jinping creatively inherited and developed these explorations into the theory of Chinese modernization, with its stated features, essential requirements and strategic timetable to 2035 and mid-century. Studying Xi's discourse, they say, reveals both continuity with Mao and further innovation. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link Mao-era policy to the official genealogy of Chinese modernization, with the statistics and Mao quotations used to support it.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's view of modernizing a country with a huge population was dialectical: a huge population means many difficulties in providing food, clothing, housing and transport, and a heavy responsibility for achieving modernization, but also great strength for achieving it.
quoteZh: 毛泽东对在人口规模巨大的国家进行现代化建设的看法是辩证的：人口规模巨大，解决衣食住行的困难多，实现现代化的责任大，但实现现代化的力量也大。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, elaborated by Xi Jinping especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It lists features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development, and is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, invoked in Mao's time and later made a central objective under Xi Jinping. Official usage contrasts it with polarisation between rich and poor.

A 1956 speech by Mao Zedong on balancing relations such as those between industry and agriculture, coastal and inland regions, and the state and the individual. It is regarded in official accounts as an early attempt at a China-specific path of socialist construction.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
glossary.explanation: Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. China put them forward in the 1950s as the basis of relations between states.
Rural health workers with basic training who provided primary care in Chinese villages from the 1960s. Official narratives present them as a pillar of rural public health under Mao.

t: How digital industry clusters empower new quality productive forces: pathways and optimisation strategies
zh: 数字产业集群赋能新质生产力的作用路径和优化策略
paras: Wang Feng and Tian Maomin ask how digital industry clusters help form new quality productive forces, a concept Xi Jinping introduced and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) took up. They argue that existing studies of digital technology and the digital economy stay on the side of the productive forces and neglect relations of production. In their view the digital industry cluster is the organisational form that unites both, and so a key carrier for cultivating new quality productive forces.

After surveying the literature, which they group into schools on technological breakthroughs, factor allocation, labour quality, data, the digital economy, green production and the optimisation of production relations, the authors set out three reasons clusters matter. These are a transformative technology ecosystem, new production relations and a testing ground for practice. They cite Silicon Valley, Bangalore, Tsukuba and Zhongguancun, and give figures for 2023: a digital industry scale of 10.09 trillion yuan, 8.01 per cent of GDP. The article then examines five channels of empowerment and five strategies.

The core claim is that clusters work through five channels. They build multi-dimensional innovation networks and speed up the conversion of research into products. They change how production factors, especially data, are allocated. They gather and train skilled people, open green development paths, and offer new ways to integrate industries. Drawing on Marx on cooperation and division of labour and on Engels on planned distribution of productive forces, the authors say clusters create a networked division of labour and new economic relations among firms and institutions.

The strategies proposed are to put building before breaking, so that regions do not abandon traditional industries hastily. They also call for self-reliance in science and technology, a society-wide risk-prevention mechanism, and balanced development of traditional, emerging and future industries. The authors further want clusters to be used to incubate cross-regional digital industry belts. They give public ownership a leading role in governance and risk resistance, and conclude that internationally competitive clusters will help form production relations better suited to new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of industrial clusters that links Marxist productive-forces theory to current policy on the digital economy and regional development.
quoteEn: As a new mode of production organisation, digital industry clusters efficiently gather key production factors such as technology, data and talent, and are an important carrier for cultivating and promoting the vigorous growth of new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 数字产业集群作为新型生产组织模式，高效汇聚了技术、数据、人才等关键生产要素，是培育并促进新质生产力蓬勃发展的重要载体。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is now central to Chinese economic policy.

Spatial concentrations of interlinked firms, suppliers, research institutes, financial bodies and facilities engaged in digital products, services and technology. The article treats them as an organisational form of digital production.
A reform principle in the Third Plenum decision: new structures should be built up before old ones are dismantled. The authors use it to warn against abandoning traditional industries too hastily.

keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: The rich connotations of Chinese civilization and their significance for our times
zh: 中华文明的丰富内涵及其时代意蕴
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in March 2025, asks what Chinese civilization contains and why it matters today. Ji Mingming argues that it is the only great civilization that has continued unbroken to the present in the form of a state. In Ji's account, five outstanding features (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) shape its overall character, and a full grasp of them helps advance socialist cultural development and national cultural soft power.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the content of Chinese civilization: fine traditional culture, historical and cultural heritage, ethical values, and a record of exchange with other civilizations. The second takes the five features in turn, with examples from philosophy, technology and institutions. The third turns to the contemporary value of the civilization and what should be done with it. Ji leans throughout on statements by Xi Jinping and on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

On content, Ji lists values such as benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom and trustworthiness, harmony between humans and nature, and attention to human development beyond material wealth. Ji adds that the civilization has always drawn on outside sources, from Buddhism to Western learning, and that Marxism was chosen in the modern period while China's distinctive path and the independence of its civilization were kept. On the five features, Ji cites the classical canon and continuous historical records for continuity; the Hundred Schools of thought, Neo-Confucianism, the Four Great Inventions and the imperial examination system for innovation; a pluralistic and unified pattern, supported by shared political, cultural and psychological identification, for unity; and an openness to foreign cultures, religions and schools of thought, together with a long-standing preference for harmony, for inclusiveness and peacefulness.

Ji concludes that Chinese civilization has gathered strength in times of national crisis and led the way in times of national revival, and that its stress on harmony, balance and sustainability can offer ideas for global environmental, social and economic problems. Ji calls for inheriting the essence of tradition, absorbing contemporary achievements, and promoting exchange and mutual learning among civilizations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary currently presents the five features of Chinese civilization and their present-day relevance.
quoteEn: The peacefulness of Chinese civilization runs through its thought, institutions and cultural traditions; it is not only an important value of the civilization but also an important foundation for national stability, social harmony and individual well-being.
quoteZh: 中华文明的和平性贯穿于思想、制度和文化传统中，不仅是中华文明的重要价值观，也是推动国家稳定、社会和谐、个体幸福的重要基础。

glossary.explanation: An official term for the parts of China's inherited culture that the Party regards as worth preserving and developing. It is often paired with the call for its 'creative transformation and innovative development'.
The idea that a country's culture and values give it international influence. It has been a stated goal of Chinese cultural policy since the 2000s.
A formula, associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong, which holds that the Chinese nation is a single whole formed by many ethnic groups. It is used in official accounts of national unity.
The Communist Party of China's national congress held in October 2022. Its report is cited as an authoritative statement on culture and tradition.

t: "New quality productive forces": a signature concept of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: “新质生产力”：中国特色社会主义政治经济学的标识性概念
paras: Liu Mingsong and Wang Qian ask what the recently introduced term "new quality productive forces" means and why it can be called a signature concept (biaoshixing gainian) of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Their thesis is that the concept is semantically a specific kind of "productive forces", that it has three signature traits, and that its theory still has to be built up through practice, theoretical innovation and links to other concepts.

The article has three parts. The first analyses the concept's meaning from three angles: its prior context, its genus–species relation to "productive forces", and its word structure. The second sets out three signature traits: autonomy of creation, centrality of structural position, and strategic character in use. The third proposes three ways to keep constructing the theoretical system. The text appeared in Socialism Studies (Shehuizhuyi yanjiu), 2024, no. 6.

On meaning, the authors argue that the concept grew out of Chinese modernization, which gives it a value presupposition centred on people's development, harmony with nature and high-quality development. As a species of the genus "productive forces", it remains within Marx's framework of labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, but represents a systemic qualitative change in these elements and their combination, not a rupture. They read "new" as both temporal and evaluative, and "quality" as the leap that follows quantitative accumulation. They distinguish a science-and-technology-led aspect ("new modifying quality") from an innovation-driven one ("new promoting quality"). On signature traits, they cite Lenin's point that social relations reduce to production relations and these to the level of productive forces. In their reading, the concept gives the discipline a firmer basis in productive forces and ties together concepts such as the new development philosophy.

The authors conclude that, as a new concept, it needs further theoretical development. They call for analysing representative local practices, such as digital and intelligent transformation, and for generalising from them. They also call for letting concept-building and theory-building reinforce each other. They further propose a concept cluster including "future industries" and "disruptive technologies", linked to supply-side structural reform and the modern industrial system, and extended to green transition. Read the original if you want a conceptual-analytic account, in the Chinese academic debate, of how new quality productive forces is positioned within the discipline's concept system.
quoteEn: "New quality productive forces" is a subordinate species built on the superordinate genus concept "productive forces"; although "new quality" serves to elaborate, classify and emphasise, as a modifier it cannot change the nature of what it modifies.
quoteZh: “新质生产力”是基于“生产力”上位属概念而建构的下位种分支，“新质”虽有补充阐述、区分类别、强化重点之意，但它作为修饰词，并不能改变被修饰对象的性状。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, associated with high-quality development and emerging industries.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and as socialist in orientation.
Official term for a development model that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth, in use since about 2017.
Xi Jinping's framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015.
A term in Chinese academic discourse for a core concept that marks out a theoretical system and gives it a distinctive identity.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zhèngzhì jīngjìxué
glossary.en: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's body of economic theory, which builds on Marxist political economy and on China's reform-era experience.

keywords: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics

t: Mao Zedong on "genuine internationalism"
zh: 毛泽东论“真正的国际主义”
paras: Wu Bo asks what Mao Zedong meant by "genuine internationalism" and how it guided the Chinese Communists in linking China's own cause to the liberation of other peoples. Taking up Xi Jinping's description of Mao as a "great internationalist" (made at the symposium marking the 130th anniversary of Mao's birth), the article argues that Mao's statements correctly handled a series of paired relationships: patriotism and internationalism, self-reliance and foreign aid, struggle and its skilful conduct, independent development and mutual learning, national liberation and world progress.

The article is organised in five sections, each built around a quotation from Mao. It moves through the anti-Japanese war and the founding years of the People's Republic, with material from the 1950s and 1960s. It draws on Mao's talks, speeches and telegrams, and sets them against statements by Marx, Engels and Lenin on proletarian internationalism.

Wu's core argument is that, for Mao, patriotism is the foundation of internationalism rather than its rival. Wu cites the 1938 report \"On the New Stage\", in which Mao argued that patriotism is internationalism applied in a war of national liberation, and contrasts this with the mistaken priority given to internationalism by the Party leadership after 1931. Wu then sets out Mao's conditions for international solidarity: self-reliance as the main basis with foreign aid as a supplement, equality among nations and opposition to great-power chauvinism, and the united front as the practical form of cooperation. The article presents the \"intermediate zones\" and the \"three worlds\" as extensions of this approach.

Wu also stresses humility in learning from other countries and peoples, and Mao's call for aid to anti-colonial struggles and to newly independent states without political conditions. The examples cited include the Korean War, support for Vietnam, Algeria and Cuba, and assistance to Asia, Africa and Latin America. Wu concludes that Mao's thought offers guidance for taking a world perspective, bearing the responsibilities of a large Party and country, and offering new opportunities to the world through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a source-based overview of Mao's internationalism as the Party's historians present it today, with many dated quotations from his speeches.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong always understood and solved China's problems against the backdrop of the tide of world history and the trend of the international communist movement, closely linking China with the world, the domestic with the international, and organically combining internationalism with patriotism.
quoteZh: 毛泽东始终从世界历史发展大潮与国际共产主义运动大势的背景下理解和解决中国问题，把中国与世界紧密联系起来，把国内和国际紧密联系起来，把国际主义和爱国主义有机结合起来

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Here it appears as the means by which China is said to offer new opportunities to the world.
A long-standing Party principle of relying mainly on one's own strength, with outside assistance as a supplement. Mao used it in the anti-Japanese war and in the early People's Republic.

The Party's strategy of uniting varied social and political forces, domestic and foreign, against a main adversary. The article discusses both the anti-Japanese national united front and the international anti-fascist front.
Mao's 1960s formulation dividing the world into zones between the United States and the socialist camp: Asia, Africa and Latin America as the first, and Europe, Canada and Oceania as the second.
Mao's strategic division of the world, developed in the 1970s from the intermediate-zone idea, used to identify states with shared interests in opposing hegemonism.
The attitude of a large state or party that treats smaller ones as inferiors. Mao demanded that it be eliminated from China's international dealings.

t: Letting the building of a strong S&T nation lead the integrated development of education, science and technology, and talent
zh: 以科技强国建设牵引教育科技人才一体化发展
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in March 2025 under the heading of studying the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), asks how education, science and technology, and talent can be developed as one system. Shao and Lu argue that the building of a strong nation in science and technology should be the leading force that pulls the other two together.

The piece has three parts. It first explains why Chinese modernization depends on the modernization of science and technology. It then discusses the leading role of technological innovation among the three systems. Finally it sets out reform measures in evaluation, training, the innovation environment and enterprises.

The authors place the argument in a period of intensifying great-power rivalry and a new round of technological revolution, in which, they say, only high-level scientific and technological self-reliance lets China stand firm. They describe education and talent cultivation as "slow variables" with many goals and complex evaluation, and technological innovation as a "fast variable" with a narrower focus. In their account, major national S&T tasks should gather and train talent, and real scientific results should test how well education and talent work succeeds. Innovation-driven reform of institutions would then pull education and talent systems along.

Shao and Lu call for reform of how researchers and institutions are evaluated, including continued efforts to break the "four onlys", and for stronger self-reliant training of innovative talent, with emphasis on young people. They also propose a better environment for innovation, easier talent movement between universities, institutes and firms, and a leading role for enterprises backed by venture capital. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy logic linking science, education and talent reform in 2025.
quoteEn: Only by achieving high-level scientific and technological self-reliance can we \"withstand pressure\" and \"stand firm\".
quoteZh: 只有实现高水平科技自立自强，我们才能“顶得住”“站得稳”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of development under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as sharing features with other countries' modernization while having distinct Chinese characteristics.

glossary.literal: S&T standing on its own feet and strengthening itself
glossary.explanation: An official goal of reducing dependence on foreign technology, especially in critical core technologies. It has been stressed in Party documents since around 2020.
A reform campaign against evaluating researchers solely by papers, titles, diplomas and awards. It aims to judge research by quality and contribution instead.

t: On the "grand ecology" outlook of new quality productive forces
zh: 论新质生产力的大生态观
source: Journal of China University of Geosciences (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 1
paras: Since September 2023, Xi Jinping has repeatedly stated that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces. Lang Huihui takes up this claim and argues that existing scholarship has studied the ecological elements and structure of such forces but has neglected their external environment. The article proposes a "grand ecology outlook" (da shengtai guan), which it presents not as a narrow method of environmental protection but as a world-view and methodology that unites natural and social ecology.

The article follows a line from theoretical genesis to basic content to practical path. It first traces four sources of the outlook: Marx's ecological thought on productive forces, the Communist Party's historical exploration of ecological productive forces, the practical demands of the green and low-carbon transition, and systems thinking. It then sets out three sub-systems and closes with five practical measures and a short conclusion.

Lang's central move is to treat new quality productive forces as a complex system of three interacting sub-systems. The internal element system comprises ecologically aware workers, digital and green means of labour, and new objects of labour. The structural-carrier system covers the greening of the industrial structure chain, the industrial chain and the supporting chain. The external environment system covers policy and institutions, rule of law and ethics, the technological innovation ecosystem, and openness. Drawing on Marx's metabolism between humans and nature and on systems theory, Lang argues that these sub-systems must exchange information, energy and elements for the system to leap forward in ecological terms.

For practice, Lang identifies weak coordination among sub-systems and insufficient internal development. The article proposes five measures: coordinated action by government, enterprises and universities; stronger green technological innovation; integration of industrial clusters with green development; improved ecological standards and feedback; and a better external environment through top-level design and platforms. Lang concludes that the outlook develops Marxist theory of productive forces and offers a model for other countries facing the supposed trade-off between growth and ecology. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Chinese scholars link Xi Jinping's "green productive forces" thesis to Marx's ecological thought and to systems theory.
quoteEn: The grand ecology outlook of new quality productive forces is not a narrow methodology of environmental protection and governance, but a broad world-view methodology that proceeds from the internal laws and connections among ecosystems and stresses the organic unity of natural and social ecology.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的大生态观不是狭义的生态环境保护治理方法论，而是基于宽阔视野的大世界观方法论，从生态系统之间的内在规律和联系出发，强调自然生态与社会生态的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, as opposed to growth based on resource inputs. It is now a central theme of Chinese economic policy discourse.
The author's term for a holistic, systems-based view that joins natural and social ecology. It extends ecological analysis beyond environmental protection.

t: The place of New China's 75 years in modern world history
zh: 新中国的75年在世界现代史中的地位
paras: Zhu Jiamu asks what position the People's Republic's first 75 years occupy in modern world history. The answer is that China's size, long history and socialist system gave it an exceptional role. Zhu describes the PRC as a force for peace, justice, democracy and progress that has consistently stood on 'the right side of history'. In this account, the PRC's influence has grown through its economic success and its role in initiating and organising international bodies and initiatives.

Zhu says China's influence works through five channels: diplomacy, public appeals and global initiatives, aid, trade and economic cooperation, and demonstration through its own development. The article claims China has used force only to repel aggression and armed provocation. It then proceeds chronologically and thematically through three fields: opposing hegemonism and defending peace, opposing old and new colonialism and supporting the Global South, and resisting unilateralism and protectionism in trade, technology and ecology.

On peace, Zhu traces a line from the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, the Bandung spirit and the Korean War to Mao Zedong's 'three worlds' theory, which Zhu credits with enabling the thaw in US relations and China's return to the United Nations. Zhu then covers reform-era diplomacy and the new era's community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. On the Global South, Zhu presents Africa as the representative case, from the Tanzania–Zambia railway to the 2024 summit pledges. Zhu contrasts China's aid, described as unconditional, with US aid, which Zhu says carries conditions. China's poverty reduction and development experience are offered as models. On ecology, Zhu presents China as a country that, unlike capitalism, avoids the Western path of environmental plunder. The article lists environmental legislation, carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets, and renewable-energy figures.

Zhu concludes that at each historical crossroads China has sided with peace, developing countries and humanity's common interests. Zhu expects it to keep doing so and to contribute more to building a community with a shared future for mankind. The article ends with Mao's remark that China, as a large country, should make a greater contribution to humanity. Read the original if you want an official-leaning Chinese scholarly account of how the PRC's foreign policy, Global South ties and environmental record are framed as a contribution to world history.
quoteEn: At every stage, China has given positive answers and made constructive responses to the common problems of humanity.
quoteZh: 无论在哪个阶段，中国对于人类的共同问题都给出了积极答案，作出过正面回应

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for joint global governance, lasting peace and shared prosperity.
A term for developing and formerly colonised countries. Chinese official discourse uses it to stress solidarity with them.
An infrastructure and trade cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013. It links China with Eurasia, Africa and other regions.

glossary.literal: theory of the division into three worlds
glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's 1970s division of the world: the US and USSR as the first world, other developed countries as the second, and Asia, Africa and Latin America as the third. It underpinned China's identification with developing countries.
Principles for relations between states, including mutual respect for sovereignty and non-interference. China put them forward in the 1950s.

t: Foucault's resonant reception of Mao Zedong's thought on investigation and research
zh: 论福柯对毛泽东调查研究思想的共鸣式接受
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2025 no. 1
paras: Michel Foucault led the Prisons Information Group (GIP) in the early 1970s, and Western scholarship has noted its links to Maoism. Wang Yichen argues that this literature tells a vague, linear story in which Mao's investigation thought simply reached France and Foucault adopted it. The article proposes the concept of 'resonant reception': Foucault was moved by the slogan and spirit of investigation, but understood it within his own intellectual horizon, so his investigations differ fundamentally from Mao's.

The article has three parts. The first traces how Foucault met Mao's investigation thought, through the French Maoist organisations UJCM-L and the Gauche Prolétarienne, through his partner Daniel Defert, and through colleagues at the University of Paris VIII (Vincennes), including Badiou, Rancière and others. It also lists the Mao texts available in French. The second part reviews the GIP's prison inquiries: their object, purpose, method and outcomes, including the 'Intolérable' pamphlets and Discipline and Punish. The third part sets out the limits of Foucault's reception and criticises earlier scholarship.

Wang makes three main moves. First, the transmission was mediated and altered: Defert was trained as a sociologist, so Foucault received a hybrid of sociological and Maoist investigation. Second, Wang contrasts the two practices. Foucault investigated mostly ordinary prisoners, not revolutionary masses. He gave investigation an ideological role of awakening opinion and passing on information, but rejected direct intellectual intervention in struggle and never entered prisons himself. Mao treated investigation as a unity of understanding, mobilising and solving problems, grounded in 'On Practice' and 'On Contradiction'. Third, Wang finds a partial convergence on investigation as knowledge production, but holds that Foucault lacked Mao's Marxist character and rootedness in Chinese history. Wang rejects both the Nietzsche-only reading and over-attributing influence to 'Maoism', which is not the same as Mao's own thought.

Wang concludes that Foucault's silence about Mao reflects a free intellectual exchange of the kind he valued, and that the gap is one between the revolutionary's investigation and the scholar's. The article reads the 1968 generation's reception as a misunderstanding that took Mao's thought only as a theory of critique. In Wang's view, its constructive side, shown in On New Democracy, matters more and has been neglected by Western left-wing scholars, which Wang says should be addressed in telling China's story abroad. Read the original if you study the French reception of Maoism, Foucault's prison activism, or how Chinese scholars assess Western uses of Mao's thought.
quoteEn: The difference between Mao Zedong's thought on investigation and research and Foucault's view of investigation is, at root, the difference between 'investigation in the eyes of a revolutionary' and 'investigation in the eyes of a scholar': the former is a method and, more, a practice; the latter is merely a method.
quoteZh: 毛泽东调查研究思想与福柯调查观的差异，从根本上说，是“革命者眼中的调查”与“学者眼中的调查”之间的差异，前者是方法、更是实践；后者仅仅是一种方法。

glossary.explanation: The author's own concept for an influence that rests on historical links and emotional and selective affinity rather than on direct textual citation or systematic study.
Mao Zedong's 1940 text setting out the programme for a revolution of the 'new democratic' type in China. The article presents it as the constructive side of Mao's thought.

t: Mao Zedong's exploration of opposing neo-colonialism and its implications
zh: 毛泽东反对新殖民主义的探索与启示
paras: Xia Shaoguang asks how the People's Republic avoided the fate of many newly independent states, which escaped old colonialism only to meet neo-colonialism. The article argues that this owed much to Mao Zedong's foresight and to the struggle he led. Seen through opposition to neo-colonialism, Xia contends, China's socialist modernization breaks the myth that modernization equals Westernization and clarifies Mao's contribution to Chinese modernization.

The article opens with the shift from old to new colonialism. It draws on the 1960s polemic against the Soviet leadership and on Mao's 1949 editorials on the US White Paper on China. It then sets out six areas of Mao-era policy: defending sovereignty, clearing away colonial remnants, economic strategy, selective opening to the outside world, new principles of international relations, and theoretical and cultural critique. A comparative section follows, covering the whole history of the PRC, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, early US and German capitalist development, and the wider developing world. The conclusion draws three lessons.

Xia defines neo-colonialism as indirect control of formally independent states through economic, ideological and proxy means. In Xia's account, Mao's answer combined the Korean War, the policy of 'cleaning the house before inviting guests', socialist transformation, and building an independent and relatively complete industrial and national economic system. It also combined self-reliance, with foreign aid secondary, and aid to Asia, Africa and Latin America without political conditions. In the comparative section, Xia argues that Japan, South Korea and Taiwan modernized in dependence on the United States, and that Japan's long stagnation is a result of neo-colonialism. Xia also argues that the United States and Germany won autonomy through class oppression at home and later imperial expansion, whereas China, in Xia's telling, did neither and so shows the superiority of socialism.

Xia concludes that Mao's anti-neo-colonial exploration laid the foundation for the period of reform and opening up, and that the two periods form a continuous whole. Xia criticises tendencies that downplay or deny the pre-reform era, idealise the 'Four Little Dragons' or beautify colonialism, and calls for continued criticism of comprador culture. Xia also calls for drawing on this experience in the current 'great struggle' against US pressure and against Western claims of Chinese 'neo-colonialism'. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links Mao-era policy to Chinese modernization and to present-day debates on dependency and the Global South.
quoteEn: In leading the socialist modernization of New China, Mao Zedong neither practised capitalist brutal exploitation, racial oppression and class repression at home, nor waged wars abroad, imposed colonial oppression or carried out primitive accumulation.
quoteZh: 毛泽东在领导新中国进行社会主义现代化建设的进程中，既没有对内实行资本主义的残酷剥削、种族压迫、阶级镇压，也没有对外发动战争，实行殖民压迫，进行原始积累

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of development under Communist Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
Indirect control of formally independent states through economic, political and ideological means. Chinese Marxist writing, drawing on 1960s Party polemics, uses it mainly to describe US policy.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world economy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse often uses to frame China's international solidarity.
Originally local intermediaries for foreign firms in semi-colonial China. In Marxist usage it describes groups or ideas serving foreign interests.

t: The "Two Integrations": historical context, theoretical logic, practical power and path of development
zh: “两个结合”：历史脉络、理论逻辑、实践伟力与发展进路
paras: Wang Fei takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the Two Integrations are the Party's "greatest magic weapon" for success. These are the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The article argues that grasping their history, theory, practical force and future course deepens the Party's understanding of how to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It holds that theoretical innovation should keep resting on practical innovation.

The article has four parts. The first traces the history of the "first integration" and the "second integration" and the "historic leaps" each produced. The second sets out the theoretical logic. The third examines the practical power of the Two Integrations in achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The fourth sets out the path ahead. The author draws on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and above all Xi Jinping, together with Engels and Lenin.

Wang reads Party history as a continuous effort. It runs from Mao's 1938 call to "Sinify" Marxism and his 1956 idea of a "second integration" to Xi's formulation of the Two Integrations in 2021. The "second integration" is presented as the logical extension of the first. The first joins theory to practice, while the second joins a theoretical system to a national cultural form. The theoretical logic rests on four points: the law of Marxism's development, the needs of revolution, construction and reform, the inner compatibility of Marxism with fine traditional culture, and the Party's own subjective consciousness. Wang cites Guo Moruo's 1925 dialogue between Marx and Confucius as an image of that compatibility. The practical power is illustrated by the Party's central tasks in each period and by the opening of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author also links the Two Integrations to strengthening cultural subjectivity and to guarding against cultural nihilism and "Westernization".

Wang proposes three directions. The first is to hold both the "soul" (Marxism) and the "roots" (fine traditional culture), so that Marxism becomes "Chinese" and tradition becomes "modern". The second is to fuse the essence of each, with Marxism keeping its guiding role while opposing both cultural nihilism and cultural restorationism. The third is to draw fresh experience from the people's practice, so that theory gathers popular wisdom and benefits the people. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-orthodox account of how the Two Integrations are historically framed and justified in current Chinese theoretical writing.
quoteEn: The "Two Integrations" are precisely the integration of the "soul" and the "roots".
quoteZh: “两个结合”，就是“魂脉”和“根脉”相结合。

glossary.explanation: Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping first used the term in 2021 and the 20th Party Congress (2022) stressed it as the method of theoretical innovation.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing after the historical humiliations of the modern era. Xi Jinping has made it the central theme of Party objectives.

t: How the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind extends and elevates Marx's theory of world history
zh: 论人类命运共同体理念对马克思世界历史理论的拓展与升华
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2025 no. 2
paras: Fu and Yan start from what they call a period of great changes unseen in a century, in which the questions "What is wrong with the world?" and "Where is humanity heading?" press on policymakers. They argue that Xi Jinping's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind answers these questions. In their reading it is both a continuation and an extension of Marx's theory of world history, and in some respects a step beyond it.

The article has two main sections. The first, on "logical coupling", compares the two bodies of thought on three points: their philosophical foundation, their value orientation and their ideal destination. The second, on "practical path", sets out three innovations the authors attribute to the idea: of agent, of thinking and of practice. It closes by describing five features of the world the idea aims at.

On continuity, the authors say both rest on historical materialism, which Marx set against Hegel's "absolute spirit". Both aim at the free and all-round development of the human being, and both look to communism as the final goal. On innovation, they claim Marx's theory made the proletariat the agent of world history, whereas the shared-future idea widens the agent to the peoples of all countries. They also say Marx's theory pointed to class struggle against the bourgeoisie, while today's coexistence of capitalism and socialism calls for cooperation and win-win outcomes. In this account Marx criticised capitalist exploitation without denying capitalism's historical contribution, so the idea draws on the Chinese tradition of harmony to release capitalism's productive potential. It also favours dialogue over confrontation and partnership over alliance.

The authors conclude that the idea offers a practical route to a new international order based on mutual respect, fairness and justice, and win-win cooperation. They describe it as a world of lasting peace, universal security, common prosperity, openness and inclusiveness, and a clean and beautiful environment. They present this as Chinese wisdom for global problems and as a development of Marxism's own goal. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars justify the shared-future idea as a theoretical extension of Marx's world-history theory, especially its shift from class struggle to cooperation.
quoteEn: The idea of a community with a shared future for mankind has achieved an innovation of the agent in Marx's theory of world history.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体理念实现了对马克思世界历史理论的主体创新。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It stresses interdependence among states and calls for cooperation, mutual respect and shared development in international relations.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since about 2017 to describe a shifting global balance of power and rapid technological and geopolitical change.

The Marxist theory that material production and social relations drive historical development. The article treats it as the shared philosophical base of Marx's world-history theory and the shared-future idea.
Marx and Engels's account, developed in works such as The German Ideology, of how capitalism and global exchange turn local histories into one world history, creating conditions for communism.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Using sinicised Marxism to excavate and elucidate China's fine traditional culture
zh: 以中国化的马克思主义挖掘和阐发中华优秀传统文化
paras: Starting from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its call to carry forward fine traditional Chinese culture within Chinese modernization, Lin asks which theoretical tool is suited to "excavating and elucidating" that culture. The answer is that neither rationalised modern Western culture nor a conservative, self-enclosed Chinese tradition will do. Only adapted or sinicised Marxism (Marxism in its Chinese form) can serve.

The article is in four parts. It first examines Western readings of Chinese culture, mainly Hegel and Weber, with Russell as a contrast. It then assesses a purely tradition-internal approach, discussing Confucianism's "family-state isomorphism", the gap between official Confucianism and practical Legalism, and the role of rural society. The third part argues for sinicised Marxism, drawing on Marx, Engels and Mao Zedong. The last part sets out three methodological requirements.

Lin argues that Hegel and Weber judged China by Western political experience, notably the split between civil society and the political state, and by a faith in reason. In the author's view, this made them see Chinese culture as lacking subjectivity and a civil-society spirit, and it hid the Daoist and Buddhist longing for life outside politics. A purely internal approach, by contrast, understands the tradition but cannot lead it into modernity. Lin holds that Confucian ethics often functioned as an ideal or ideology in politics and took effect mainly in villages and families, which have since changed. Marxism, in Lin's account, disenchants Western rationalism and insists on concrete historical conditions. It must be adapted to China, treating Chinese culture as part of China's "actual conditions" and handling it dialectically, as Mao urged: discarding feudal dross and absorbing democratic essence.

Lin proposes three requirements. First, respect and understand the tradition and keep close to it. Second, treat excavation as nurturing a living organism rather than mining a resource, achieving creative transformation and innovative development. Third, enter into equal, subject-to-subject dialogue with tradition, avoiding any prophet-like posture (the Zhuangzi fable of Hundun is the warning). Lin adds that what counts as "fine" is historically conditioned, so present judgements need self-reflection and humility. Read the original if you want a philosophical account of how Party theory justifies using Marxism to engage China's cultural heritage, including its readings of Hegel, Weber and Confucianism.
quoteEn: Sinicised Marxism differs from Europeanised Marxism, is not Marxism copied from the Soviet Union, and is not dogmatised Marxism; it is Marxism rooted in China's realities, integrated into Chinese culture and reaching into every household.
quoteZh: 中国化的马克思主义既不同于欧洲化的马克思主义，也不是照搬苏联的马克思主义，不是教条化的马克思主义，而是扎根中国实际、融入中华文化、深入千家万户的马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernity, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as coordinating material and cultural-ethical progress.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula, repeated by Xi Jinping, for how traditional culture should be reworked to fit contemporary needs rather than simply preserved.

glossary.literal: Marxism that has been made Chinese
glossary.explanation: Marxism adapted to China's concrete conditions and culture, a theme traced to Mao Zedong. In recent Party language it appears as adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

glossary.literal: family and state share one structure
glossary.explanation: The idea that the traditional Chinese state is an enlarged family, so that family ethics, such as filial piety and loyalty, also govern politics.

t: Methodological guide and key directions for developing new quality productive forces through further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 以进一步全面深化改革发展新质生产力的方法指南和着力方向
paras: Xia Wenbin and Zhang Chuqiao ask how new quality productive forces can be developed on a sustainable basis. Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that this requires further comprehensively deepening reform and forming new relations of production suited to it, as well as the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), they argue that reform must target the institutional blockages that hold these forces back. Their thesis is that further comprehensive reform is both the necessary route and a source of method and direction.

The article, published in Shandong Social Sciences in 2025, has three parts. The first sets out the significance of the approach: for Marxist productive-force theory, for the practice of reform and opening up, and for world modernization. The second draws a methodological guide from the "three greater emphases" in the Third Plenum's Decision: systems integration, priority on key points, and practical results. The third names two main directions for effort: integrated reform of education, science and technology, and talent, and a higher-level system of opening up.

In the authors' account, new quality productive forces carry forward Marx's view of the dynamics of social development, which covers the internal structure of the productive forces, their contradiction with the relations of production, and the combined force of economic, political and cultural factors. They also see it as a continuation of reform-era thinking from Deng Xiaoping to Xi. Under systems integration, they list five relationships to handle: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, development and security. They argue that capitalism cannot institutionally unite efficiency and fairness, and that socialism can. Under key points, they stress innovation, inclusiveness of ownership forms, a unified national market, fair competition and resilient supply chains. Under results, they call for target-setting, local adaptation, coordinated factor inputs and scientific evaluation, including an index of new quality productive forces.

On the directions for effort, the authors call for strategic linkage of education, science and technology, and talent. They also call for stronger original, integrated and open innovation, and for joint training and operating mechanisms linking universities, firms and research bodies. They further propose institutional opening up, alignment with high international standards, and participation in reforming global economic governance. They present this as a way to bring about a different paradigm of world modernization built on common prosperity and cooperation. Read the original if you want a policy-oriented account of how Chinese scholars connect the Third Plenum's reform agenda to new quality productive forces, including concrete institutional recommendations.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces should start from reform of the economic system, with raising capacity for independent innovation as the top priority.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力要从经济体制改革入手，将提高自主创新能力作为重中之重

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and high-quality development, in place of growth based on resource-heavy models.
The policy course launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market mechanisms and opening China's economy to the outside world.
A Party goal of broadly shared prosperity for all, stressed under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

keywords: education, science and technology, and talent

t: The realisation path of the self-improvement of the socialist system
st: An analytical framework based on the "institutional process"
zh: 社会主义制度自我完善的实现路径
zhSub: 以“制度过程”为分析框架
paras: Zhao Lingyun starts from two claims by Deng Xiaoping: that reform is the "self-improvement of the socialist system", and that Chinese socialism may become "the best system in the world". The article asks how this self-improvement actually happens, and proposes the concept of the "institutional process" (zhidu guocheng) as a framework for answering. Zhao defines it as a closed cycle of five links: institutional design, institutional construction, institutional operation, conversion of institutional advantages, and institutional evaluation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the framework and grounds it in Marxist institutional theory, Deng Xiaoping's thinking on institutions, Xi Jinping's institutional discourse and the political-science literature on "process" approaches. The second applies it to three stages of the People's Republic: founding the socialist system (to 1978), establishing the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics (1978 to the 18th Party Congress, 2012), and improving and developing that system (2012 to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, 2024). The third draws out the framework's theoretical, historical and practical implications.

Zhao argues that each stage contains a complete cycle in which the evaluation stage opens the next round, so that the cycles form a spiral. On this reading, Xi Jinping's formulas of "two historical periods" and "two half-courses" describe one continuous history of building socialism. Zhao answers why the system can improve itself by pointing to its public-ownership basis and to its capacity to accommodate different economic arrangements, which Zhao contrasts with János Kornai's view that Soviet-type socialism could not be reformed. The "self" in self-improvement is identified as the system itself, with the Communist Party's leadership and the people it leads as the subject. Party leadership is therefore the internal driver of the process.

Looking ahead, Zhao calls for continuing the institutional process through repeated cycles, treating the second half-course as a long, step-by-step stage. Zhao further urges a focus on institutional integration, building and converting institutional advantages, and strengthening the Party's historical initiative. Self-improvement, in this view, is not automatic, and the Party's self-reform and the system's self-improvement are described as closely unified. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-theory account of how Chinese scholars periodise and conceptualise institution-building since 1949.
quoteEn: The internal driving force of the institutional process of China's socialist system lies in the leadership of the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 中国社会主义制度过程的内生动能在于中国共产党的领导

glossary.explanation: The author's proposed analytical concept: the practice of an institution seen as a closed five-link cycle from design to evaluation. It is offered as a new framework, not an established official term.

glossary.zh: 社会主义制度的自我完善
glossary.pinyin: shèhuì zhǔyì zhìdù de zìwǒ wánshàn
glossary.explanation: Deng Xiaoping's description of reform as the way socialism improves itself rather than being replaced. Later Party documents repeat it.
Xi Jinping's periodisation of socialist practice: a first half that built the basic system, and a second half that perfects and develops the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The Party's official name for its model of socialism since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's conditions.

t: The "Second Integration" in historical perspective
zh: 从历史维度看“第二个结合”
paras: Writing in Qiushi (2025, no. 5), Ouyang Junxi asks why the Communist Party of China has come to stress combining Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, and what the "Second Integration" adds to the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article argues that the Second Integration has deep historical roots, because Marxism and traditional Chinese culture are mutually compatible and the Party has inherited that culture since its founding. It opens with Guo Moruo's 1925 story "Marx Enters the Confucian Temple", in which Marx and Confucius find their ideals of society alike.

The article is organised in three historical and conceptual steps. It first examines the points of fit between Marxism and traditional culture. It then traces the Party's treatment of that culture through the Yan'an period, the early People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Finally it presents "the Two Integrations" as the Party's greatest asset for success.

Ouyang's first move is to explain Marxism's rapid spread in China partly by cultural affinity. The article finds proto-socialist elements in ideas such as "all under heaven is for the common good" and the Great Harmony, political values such as people-as-the-root and governing by virtue, and plain materialist and dialectical traditions. It cites Sun Yat-sen, Wu Yuzhang, Ai Siqi and Zhang Dainian in support. Its second move is to show continuity in Party leaders: Mao Zedong's 1938 call for Marxism to take a national form, his reuse of Chinese idioms and fables, and later formulations by Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. The article claims that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era draws on traditional concepts such as people-centredness, harmony between humanity and nature, and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Ouyang concludes that the Two Integrations are the fundamental route for adapting Marxism to China and the necessary path for developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. In this account, Chinese modernization continues an ancient civilisation rather than breaking with it. The Second Integration is described as a "chemical reaction" that produces an organic new cultural entity and strengthens cultural subjectivity, confidence and initiative. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party theorists trace the Second Integration back through Chinese Marxist history and quote the leadership's key formulations on it.
quoteEn: Integration is not a "platter" or a simple "physical reaction" but a profound "chemical reaction", producing a new, organically unified cultural entity; the result of the Second Integration is that Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture mutually fulfil each other.
quoteZh: “结合”不是“拼盘”，不是简单的“物理反应”，而是深刻的“化学反应”，造就了一个有机统一的新的文化生命体，“第二个结合”的结果是马克思主义与中华优秀传统文化互相成就。

glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second was formally stressed under Xi Jinping, notably in 2023.
The integration of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping elaborated it in June 2023 and described it as a further liberation of thought.

The official term for China's own path of modernization, which Party documents distinguish from Western models. It was developed after the 18th Party Congress (2012) and set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations built on common interests and cooperation, promoted since around 2012.
A term used in Xi-era discourse for a nation's cultural self-awareness and independence, in this case the Chinese nation's confidence in its own culture.

t: Did Mao Zedong really reject the "law of the negation of the negation"?
zh: 毛泽东真的否定“否定之否定规律”吗
paras: Some scholars hold that Mao Zedong rejected the law of the negation of the negation, citing his remark that he did not believe quantity–quality transformation and the negation of the negation stand parallel to the unity of opposites, since that would be "three-ism, not monism". Fu Zhiwei takes up this claim, noting that Slavoj Žižek and Wang Nanshi use the passage in this way and that Stalin and Althusser offer a precedent. Fu argues that Mao did not reject the law itself. What he denied was its foundational status alongside the law of the unity of opposites.

The article has four parts. It first traces the law to Hegel and sets out how Marx and Engels inverted and demystified it. It then clarifies the concept of "negation". Next it compares Mao's remarks, drawn mainly from his philosophical annotations and the Chronology of Mao Zedong, with Marx and Engels. Finally it answers three opposing positions: Stalin and Althusser, Žižek, and a more elaborate argument that the law cannot be separated from Hegelian idealism.

Fu defines dialectical negation as self-negation, a moment of development, a moment of connection and, in essence, sublation. It is neither the "either/or" of formal logic nor a subjective evaluative category. Fu finds that Mao's statements match each of these points: negation arises within the thing itself, it is continuous, and it preserves what is rational in the old. Mao's wish to treat the unity of opposites as the single core law explains his remarks, because the other categories are explained through it. Fu reads "there is no negation of the negation" as a point about theoretical economy, not a denial. Against Žižek, Fu cites Mao's endorsement of "analysis and synthesis".
