Against the idealism argument, Fu contends that Engels and Marx treated the law as necessary even when it describes a linear process, such as communism, and not a return to its starting point.

Fu concludes that Mao affirmed the law while denying it foundational status, and that this clarified the relation among the three laws of materialist dialectics. Fu presents this as consistent with Marxism and as a development of it. Fu leaves the final judgement to readers. Read the original if you want a close, text-based argument on Mao's dialectics, Hegel's logic and the Marx–Engels reworking of the negation of the negation, or if you want to see how this reading answers Žižek and Althusser.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's attitude toward the "law of the negation of the negation" was affirmative; while affirming it, he denied the law its foundational status.
quoteZh: 毛泽东对“否定之否定规律”的态度是肯定的，只是在肯定的同时，他否定了这一规律所具有的基础性地位。

glossary.en: law of the negation of the negation
glossary.explanation: One of the three basic laws of materialist dialectics as formulated by Engels in Dialectics of Nature, alongside quantity–quality transformation and the unity of opposites. It describes development as a spiral in which a thing negates itself and is then negated again.
The law that things contain contradictory aspects that are mutually dependent and in struggle. Mao treated it as the core of dialectics.
The Hegelian and Marxian idea (Aufhebung) of negating something while preserving its rational content in a higher form.

t: The Chinese narrative logic of the question of modernization and its world-historical significance
zh: 现代化之问的中国叙事逻辑和世界历史意义
paras: Wang Yonggui asks how Chinese modernization answers what the author calls the question of modernization, which he treats as the key to the larger question facing the world. The article argues that Chinese modernization shares features with other countries' modernizations but is not a 'special case' outside world trends. In Wang's account it is an original theoretical and practical achievement that points to a new form of human civilization and widens the range of paths to modernity.

The article is organised around five principles that Xi Jinping has set for modernization: putting the people first, independence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, helping others while pursuing one's own development, and an enterprising attitude. Each principle forms one section, presented as a 'new concept', 'new path', 'new chapter', 'new picture' and 'new realm' of modernization. Wang draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin on Eastern societies, and on Xi's speeches throughout.

Wang first contrasts a Western modernization driven by the 'logic of capital' with one in which the 'logic of the people' governs capital. Capital is treated as a production factor to be regulated, and Wang says public ownership turns the 'logic of capital' into a 'logic of labour'. He then argues that Chinese modernization dissolves the equation of 'modernization' with 'Westernization', escapes the 'centre–periphery' dependency trap and offers developing countries a model without exporting it. In the later sections, the author says a philosophy of 'unity of subject and object' and 'common values of all humanity' surpass hegemony and 'universal values'. The leadership of the Communist Party and its self-reform are credited with direction, stability and continuity.

Wang concludes that Chinese modernization enriches scientific socialism by making its goals concrete, developing its principles and offering a systematic practical programme. He holds that it reverses the post-Cold War low point of the socialist movement, supplies a model for building socialism in an 'Eastern society', and gives world history a socialist civilizational benchmark. He presents the community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative as expressions of this outlook. Read the original if you want a full, systematic statement of how Chinese academic writing in 2024 frames the world-historical significance of Chinese modernization against Western modernization theory.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization discards the Western modernization's single economic-driver theory and upholds a composite theory of driving forces in which endogenous forces play the main role.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化摒弃西方现代化单一的经济动力论，坚持以内生动力为主的综合动力论

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: guard what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for keeping to core principles, such as Marxism and Party leadership, while innovating in theory and practice.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted since 2012–13. It stresses shared interests, multilateralism and opposition to hegemony.
A formula announced by Xi Jinping in 2015 and later: peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Official texts present it as an alternative to Western 'universal values'.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: Reflections on the presuppositions of paradigm construction in Chinese Marxist philosophy
st: From the perspective of the "self-justification of philosophical paradigms"
zh: 中国马克思主义哲学范式建设的前提意识之思
zhSub: “哲学范式自我证成”的视角
paras: Cao Dianshun asks what presuppositions must be examined before a distinctive paradigm of Chinese Marxist philosophy can be built. Reading paradigm construction as a process of the paradigm's "self-justification", the author argues that four preliminary questions come first: its theoretical premises, its problem-consciousness, its theoretical grounds and its academic discourse. The thesis is that Chinese Marxist philosophy needs a paradigm that fuses "realistic practicality" with "scientific academic quality" and moves beyond a derivative "apprentice" stage.

The article, published in Theoretical Investigation (2024, no. 5), has four sections matching these four questions. The first treats "practicality" and "academic quality" as the twin theoretical premises and their inner unity. The second takes "concern for reality" and "genuine philosophy" as the problem-consciousness behind paradigm construction. The third reflects critically on the field's theoretical grounds, and the fourth defines the academic discourse of the new paradigm.

Cao's central move is a set of contrasts. Practicality is the guiding principle, logical starting point and test of any paradigm, while academic quality is its basic requirement. The author criticises "apprentice academic quality", Chinese scholarship that reads Marx through Hegel, Kant or Heidegger, copies Soviet textbooks (the author cites Ai Siqi's generation) or simply adopts Marxism outside China. In Cao's view this mimicry and dogmatism limits originality and delays the arrival of the paradigm-construction stage.

In the final section Cao separates "realistic practicality" from idealist "rational practicality" and from dogmatic "theoretical practicality", and "scientific academic quality" from "abstract rational" and "apprentice" scholarship. Cao holds that only a paradigm combining the first of each pair can guide Chinese modernization, by stressing the particular side of historical materialism while Marx already set out its general logic. The author concludes that this fusion is both a historical task set by social development and the academic discourse of paradigm construction. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese philosopher frames the shift from importing Western and Soviet theory to building an original, self-assertive Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Only by passing beyond the period of "apprentice academic quality" and entering that of "scientific academic quality" can a philosophical paradigm with Chinese academic characteristics be constructed.
quoteZh: 只有逾越“学徒学术性”时期而进入“科学学术性”时期,才能建构出具有中国学术特色的哲学范式。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's path of modernization, set out in Party documents especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article treats it as the practical task that Chinese Marxist philosophy should theorise and guide.

The author's term for a stage of research following studies of Marxist philosophical paradigms and of Chinese Marxist philosophical paradigms. It concerns building a distinctive paradigm of Chinese Marxist philosophy.
The author's label for scholarship that mainly imitates or applies foreign or Soviet theories without originality. The author treats it as a transitional stage.
The author's term for a practice-orientation grounded in real individuals and concrete social practice, as opposed to idealist or dogmatic versions of practicality.

t: The "comprehensive innovation" theory of culture and the "Second Integration"
zh: 文化“综合创新”论与“第二个结合”
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Can the twentieth-century philosopher brothers Zhang Shenfu and Zhang Dainian be compared with the Song-dynasty Cheng brothers? Taking up a suggestion by Fang Keli, Zhang Yunyi argues that they can: both pairs lived in epochs of cultural turning point, and the Cheng brothers' synthesis of Buddhism, Daoism and Confucianism finds its modern counterpart in the Zhangs' synthesis of Marxism, Chinese tradition and Western thought. The article's thesis is that a single thread, the "Second Integration" of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture, runs from the Zhangs' "comprehensive innovation" theory to Fang's later formula "Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western learning for application".

The article has four sections. The first traces the intellectual sources of "comprehensive innovation" over four centuries of Sino-Western encounter, from Xu Guangqi's "Chinese mould, Western material" through the debates on substance and function, on the origins of Chinese and Western learning, and on their relative merits. The second sets out the contributions of Zhang Shenfu (the 1930s "merging of three streams": Confucius, Russell, Lenin) and Zhang Dainian (the "synthesis of materialism, ideals and analysis"). The third examines Fang Keli's "Marxism as soul" formula and the criticisms it drew. The fourth presents the Second Integration as the unifying line of Fang's career.

Zhang Yunyi's central move is to distinguish synthesis from eclecticism. Drawing on the Zhangs, the author holds that a true synthesis needs a backbone, which for them was Marxist dialectical materialism, so that Marxism leads while Chinese and Western learning are absorbed. Fang's formula, in this account, adds a third term to the old two-term substance–function framework and answers the question of how Marxism, Chinese culture and Western culture relate. It is presented as a scholarly paradigm superior to wholesale Westernisation, Confucian revival, and the older formulas of Chinese substance with Western function or the reverse. Zhang cites Fang's replies to critics who call the three-part model a patchwork: each element has its own "function", with Marxism guiding, Chinese culture as the main subject, and Western learning as a "stone from another hill".

Zhang concludes that Fang, Zhang Dainian, Zhang Shenfu and Feng Qi belong to a "comprehensive innovation school" or "Second Integration school", which the author identifies with the Marxist school in Chinese philosophy. The article points out that Fang described the integration of Marxism with Chinese culture as his lifelong commitment, and that Xi Jinping's statements on the Two Integrations, on Marxism as the "soul" and traditional culture as the "root", echo elements of Fang's formula. Read the original if you want a detailed intellectual genealogy of the Second Integration in Chinese philosophy, with extensive quotation from the Zhangs and Fang Keli.
quoteEn: "Synthesis" is by no means an undifferentiated "mixture" with no primary and secondary, and "innovation" is not novelty for its own sake without anything to rely on.
quoteZh: “综合”绝非不分主次的“混合”，“创新”也不是无所凭依的标新立异。

glossary.explanation: Within the Two Integrations formula, the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping gave it prominence in 2023, though the article traces earlier uses by Fang Keli.
The official formula for adapting Marxism to China: integrating its basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.pinyin: Mǎ hún Zhōng tǐ Xī yòng
glossary.en: Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western learning for application
glossary.literal: Marxism the soul, Chinese the substance, Western the function
glossary.explanation: Fang Keli's formula, which adds Marxism as the guiding "soul" to the older "Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application" scheme. It is not an official Party term.
The cultural theory associated with Zhang Dainian: creating a new Chinese culture by synthesising Marxism, Chinese tradition and Western thought, with Marxism as the guiding axis.

A classical Chinese philosophical pair, "substance" (fundamental essence) and "function" (practical application). Late Qing reformers used it to frame the relation between Chinese and Western learning.
Zhang Shenfu's 1930s idea of uniting Confucius, Russell and Lenin, meaning Chinese philosophy, Western analytic philosophy and Marxism, into one new philosophy.

t: The trajectory and direction of the development of political economy with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学发展的脉络与方向
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 February 2025
paras: This short commentary in China Social Sciences Today asks how the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics has developed and where it should go next. Han Wenlong argues that this body of theory grew out of China's economic practice alongside reform and opening up, and that amid what the article calls changes unseen in a century it must keep widening its scope and depth. In Han's account, it should supply theoretical support for an autonomous Chinese system of economic knowledge and guidance for economic practice in the new development stage.

The article has two parts. The first divides the field's history into three periods: 1949–1978, 1978–2012, and 2012 to the present. The second sets out three directions for further development: stronger problem-oriented research, a more systematic and open theoretical system, and a wider international outlook.

On the historical side, Han describes the first period as one of exploration, producing theories of the basic contradictions of socialism, public ownership and comprehensive balance of the national economy, despite what the article calls a tortuous course. The second period, opened by the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and Deng Xiaoping's proposal at the 12th Party Congress (1982) to build socialism with Chinese characteristics, deepened work on ownership, distribution and the socialist market economy. For the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Han presents Xi Jinping's economic thought as the latest result, and lists ten research areas. These include the Party's overall leadership of economic work, high-quality development, common prosperity, new quality productive forces, the basic socialist economic system and the balance of development and security. For the future, Han calls for a 'problem–theory–practice' paradigm applied to issues such as local government debt, demographic change and artificial intelligence. Han also asks for clearer core concepts and foundations, given differing views on the starting category and main logical thread, together with new methods such as big data and causal inference and selective use of Western economics, and for explaining China's experience in accessible language.

Han concludes that the discipline is both a summary of past experience and a forward-looking project. Its tasks are to answer practical problems, build a rigorous and open system, and offer a Chinese approach to global economic governance. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic overview of how Chinese scholars periodise their political economy and what research agenda one economist proposes for it.
quoteEn: We need to adhere to the 'problem–theory–practice' research paradigm, taking the real problems of great economic practice as the guide and direction for theoretical research.
quoteZh: 需要坚持“问题—理论—实践”研究范式，把伟大经济实践中的现实问题作为理论研究的课题指南和路向。

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zhèngzhì jīngjìxué
glossary.en: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: A theoretical system, promoted in official discourse especially since the 2010s, that seeks to summarise China's reform-era economic experience in Marxist political-economic terms.
The part of Xi Jinping Thought dealing with the economy, presented officially as the latest development of Marxist political economy in China.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional factor inputs.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, presented as an essential requirement of socialism and stressed in policy since 2021.

t: Building Chinese economics under the guidance of Marxist political economy
zh: 以马克思主义政治经济学为指导建设中国经济学
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 27 February 2025, asks how China should build its own autonomous system of economic knowledge. He Zili argues that the system must be guided by Marxist political economy, which he treats as the only possible foundation for the country's political economy, rather than by any other body of economic theory. Its task, in his account, is to answer new questions arising from economic construction under socialism with Chinese characteristics and to reveal the laws governing its relations of production.

The piece is organised around four requirements for building this knowledge system. These concern the object of study, the value standpoint, the starting point of research, and the elaboration of Xi Jinping's economic thought. He draws contrasts with Adam Smith, Say, Robbins and Samuelson, and with what he calls Western economics, and ends with four practical tasks.

In the core argument, He contrasts Western definitions of economics, which centre on scarce resources, wealth production and distribution, with the Marxist definition. Marxist political economy takes the mode of production and its corresponding relations of production, distribution and exchange as its object, and He says Chinese economics should take the socialist mode of production with Chinese characteristics as its object. He holds that Western economics claims to be value-free but has itself become part of bourgeois ideology, whereas Marxist political economy openly states its class standpoint and its people-centred orientation. He also calls for starting from the "new historical juncture" of the new era, in which the principal contradiction is between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development, and for high-quality development to be the main task.

He concludes that the central task is now to raise the scholarly interpretation and systematic construction of Xi Jinping economic thought, which he lists as a series of original contributions, from Party leadership of economic work to new quality productive forces. He proposes four tasks: studying its formation and development, extracting its categories and logic, building textbooks around it, and strengthening the "three systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse). The aim is to end the practice of copying Western economics to tell China's story. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official line on how China's economics discipline should be constructed under Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: In building China's autonomous system of economic knowledge, we must uphold the guiding position of Marxist political economy.
quoteZh: 建构中国自主的经济学知识体系，必须坚持马克思主义政治经济学的指导地位

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, presented officially as a component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It covers topics such as high-quality development, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and upgraded industries. It is now a central slogan of economic policy.
The official goal, since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and balance in economic development.
A formula for building philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics through a disciplinary system, an academic system and a discourse system.

t: An outline of the theoretical themes of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 中国化时代化马克思主义理论主题论纲
source: Observation and Reflection (Guancha yu sikao), 2025 no. 2
paras: Zhang Ronghua and Liang Chao ask what central questions the Party's Marxist theory, adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, has set out to answer. They argue that this body of theory has a continuous "theoretical theme", which they call a "red thread" running through the stages the article labels saving the nation, building the country, enriching it and strengthening it. The authors note that few scholars have studied this theme directly, since most work treats the three major theoretical achievements separately. The article appeared in 2025, after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

The article first defines the theme, describes its structure and sets out why it is worth studying. It then takes in turn Mao Zedong Thought, the system of theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics (Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development), and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. For each, it lists how the theme was expressed: revolution, the building of socialism, and Party building, then development and national strengthening. A final section condenses these into one overall formula.

The core claim is that the theme has a "1+3" structure. The "1" is the question of what Marxism is and how to uphold and develop it. The "3" are the questions of what kind of socialism, what kind of socialist modern great country, and what kind of long-governing Marxist party to build, and how. The authors treat these three as extensions of the first. They say the three achievements share a common source (the Two Integrations and shifts in the principal contradiction), a common direction (national prosperity, rejuvenation and the people's happiness) and a common purpose (a mass-line view of history). They also distinguish the theoretical theme from the themes of the times, of practice and of Party congresses, and from major research questions, treating the theoretical theme as a distillation of the last.

The authors conclude that theoretical themes are layered and progressive, and that studying them clarifies the main line of the adaptation of Marxism and the content of twenty-first-century Marxism. They call for fully implementing Xi Jinping Thought and the spirit of the Third Plenum, so that this theory drives Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how Party theorists periodise the Party's theoretical innovation through a single set of recurring questions.
quoteEn: The theoretical theme of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has a \"1+3\" structure.
quoteZh: 中国化时代化马克思主义理论主题则是“1+3”的内容构成

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义理论体系
glossary.en: the system of theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official grouping of Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. The Party presents it as the second major achievement in adapting Marxism.
The authors' term for the central questions a body of theory sets out to answer. They distinguish it from the theme of the times, the theme of practice and the theme of a Party congress.
Jiang Zemin's formulation of the Party's role. It says the Party represents advanced productive forces, the orientation of advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept that stresses people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

t: An analysis of the subject dimensions of comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 全面深化改革的主体向度解析
paras: Li Gang and Cheng Xinlin take up a question raised by the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization: who is the 'subject' of reform when the Decision commits to 'putting the people first'? The authors argue that the people are the subject of comprehensive reform in four distinct senses, and that this reflects a new level of understanding of 'the people' in the Party's reform experience since 1978. The article was published in Theoretical Horizon in 2024.

The article is organised in four sections, each treating the people as one kind of subject: practical subject, value subject, interest subject and evaluation subject. Each section opens with a classical Marxist premise, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and then relates it to reform practice from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the present. Examples include the household contract responsibility system at Xiaogang village, market-oriented economic reform, and the Party's 2017 judgement on the principal contradiction in society.

In the authors' account, the people are the practical subject because history is made by the masses, but the masses can act effectively only if organised under Party leadership, which the authors treat as the guarantee of reform. As value subject, the people make reform a means of creating conditions for each person's free and all-round development, both by raising productive forces and by cultivating capable people. As interest subject, the people raise the problem of balancing individual and collective interests. The authors, following Marx and Engels, read these as dialectically united and cite whole-process people's democracy and the socialist market economy as ways of handling the relation. As evaluation subject, the people judge whether reform has delivered. The authors ground this in their practical experience, their value orientation and their direct interests.

On evaluation, the authors propose three measures: respect the people's capacity to judge and follow the mass line, build positive incentives by responding promptly to public feedback, and remove institutional obstacles to evaluation. For the last, they call for smoother channels, with more online and offline platforms and simpler procedures for passing opinions to the relevant departments. They conclude that, given the greater complexity and risks facing reform, reliance on the people's participation matters even more. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of the 'people as subject' principle in current Party reform theory, linked to Marxist classics and reform history.
quoteEn: The key question in treating the people as the evaluation subject of comprehensively deepening reform is how to improve the mechanisms through which the people evaluate, so as to promote reform, development and stability effectively.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革以人民作为评价主体的关键问题就在于，如何健全完善人民群众的评价机制，有效促进改革发展稳定。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official description of China's democratic system, stressing popular participation at every stage of political life rather than only in elections. Xi Jinping promoted the term from 2019.
The Party's working method, developed under Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of the masses, refining them and returning them as policy.

t: An analysis of the practical positioning of the new development stage
zh: 新发展阶段的实践定位探析
source: Guancha yu sikao (Observation and Thinking), 2025 no. 1
paras: Sun Yingshuai and Zhao Shiyu ask where the "new development stage", which China formally entered after the completion of a moderately prosperous society and the first centenary goal, sits in the Party's periodisation of Chinese society. They answer, following Xi Jinping's formulations, that it is a sub-stage within the primary stage of socialism, the stage of comprehensively building a modern socialist country and advancing towards the second centenary goal, and a great leap in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article appeared in Guancha yu sikao (Observation and Thinking), 2025, no. 1.

The article is organised in three parts that correspond to these three formulations. The first treats the relation between the new stage and the primary stage of socialism. The second discusses modernization, the new development philosophy, the new development pattern and high-quality development. The third covers national rejuvenation, common prosperity and a new form of civilisation suited to Chinese modernization. The authors draw on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi, together with economic data such as IMF figures and 2023 per-capita GDP.

In the first part the authors argue that scholars have studied what is "new" and "changed" in the stage more than what is unchanged. They list five points of continuity: time span, the basic contradiction, people's all-round development still resting on dependence on things, China's developing-country status, and the goals of modernization. They hold that the stage is a "leap stage" rather than a "transitional stage", belonging to the theory of social stages and not of social formations. It is, in their account, a partial qualitative change inside a continuing quantitative accumulation, and a preparation for a higher stage, for which they call for an evaluation system. Later sections link the new stage to new quality productive forces, common prosperity and a Marxism-based civilisational renewal.

The authors conclude that in the new stage the Party will lead the people towards a strong modern socialist country by applying the new development philosophy, building the new development pattern, pursuing high-quality development and common prosperity, and so achieving national rejuvenation. They stress the risks they identify, including great-power rivalry, containment by the United States, domestic imbalances and the demands of Party self-governance. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how current Party theory defines the new development stage and its relation to the primary stage of socialism.
quoteEn: The new development stage, as a sub-stage of the primary stage of socialism or a "leap stage" towards a higher stage, is not a phase of transition between different social formations but a stage of development within the socialist social formation.
quoteZh: 新发展阶段作为社会主义初级阶段的一个子阶段，或向更高阶段迈进的“跨越阶段”，不是不同社会形态之间的一个变迁阶段，而是社会主义社会形态之内的一个发展阶段

glossary.explanation: The Party's designation, since 2021, for the period after the completion of a moderately prosperous society, running to the middle of the 21st century. It is defined as a stage within the primary stage of socialism.
A thesis formalised at the 13th Party Congress (1987) holding that China is still in an underdeveloped phase of socialism lasting at least a century.
Xi Jinping's five-part guideline for development: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared.
An economic strategy centred on the domestic "great circulation", with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other.
A goal of shared affluence for all, presented by the Party as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, linked to high-quality development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, tied to the two centenary goals.

t: Deng Xiaoping's contribution to exploring the "Two Integrations" and its profound lessons
zh: 邓小平对“两个结合”探索的贡献及其深刻启示
source: Marxism Studies (马克思主义研究), 2024, no. 11
paras: Liu Zhiming asks how Deng Xiaoping contributed to what the Party now calls the Two Integrations, and what that record offers for the present. The article argues that after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), Deng led the Party in exploring both integrations around the building of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In Liu's account this produced a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is published in Marxism Studies (2024, no. 11). It has four parts: why socialist modernization requires the Two Integrations; how Deng developed them; the achievements that resulted; and the lessons for today. Liu concedes that Deng mostly spoke of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete reality and never explicitly proposed the integration with fine traditional Chinese culture. Liu nonetheless holds that the second integration is implicit in his work, because Chinese culture and history form part of China's "concrete reality".

Liu gives four reasons from Deng for the Two Integrations: the lessons of the revolution, the need to keep solving concrete problems, the novelty of modernization as an undertaking, and the failures of copying the Soviet model. Deng's exploration, Liu argues, rested on upholding Marxism's universal truth and basic principles, including seeking truth from facts, the Four Cardinal Principles and the principles of socialism. It also rested on grasping China's conditions: a weak economic base, a large population with little arable land, and the primary stage of socialism. On culture, Liu reports that Deng called for critical appraisal of tradition under Marxist guidance, while opposing both "Left" and Right errors and feudal and bourgeois influences. Liu lists five achievements: Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Party's basic line, a new path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a distinctive socialist system, and a renewed ethical-cultural life.

Liu draws three lessons. Marxism must be upheld fully and as a whole, including the successive theories of adaptation and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and Chinese modernization must be advanced. Policy must start from the primary stage of socialism, including the "new development stage" within it. China must keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, avoiding both ossification and abandoning socialism, while continuing to innovate. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of Deng Xiaoping's Marxism, and of how current official discourse links his thought to the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Deng Xiaoping's exploration of the "Two Integrations" and the great achievements it brought carry profound lessons in many respects for how we continue to advance the "Two Integrations" in the new era and new journey and write a new chapter of adapting Marxism to China and our times.
quoteZh: 邓小平对“两个结合”的探索及取得的伟大成就，对新时代新征程我们继续推进“两个结合”，续写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章，具有多方面的深刻启示。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was formally added in Xi Jinping-era discourse, around 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions and the demands of each era.

A judgement that China is in an underdeveloped stage of socialism that will last a long time. It was developed in the early 1980s and set out in the 1987 13th Party Congress report, and it underpins the Party's basic line.
The official name for China's socialist path since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping's 1982 formulation.
The official description of China's own path to modernization. Deng used the phrase in 1979, and it was elaborated as a major theme under Xi Jinping.
Deng's 1979 formulation: keep to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.

t: Working wholeheartedly in the interests of the people
st: Written for the 80th anniversary of "Serve the People"
zh: 彻底地为人民的利益工作
zhSub: 为《为人民服务》发表八十周年而作
paras: Marking eighty years since Mao Zedong's 1944 speech "Serve the People", Li Wei argues that the slogan is far more than propaganda. In Li's account, it is a theoretical and moral creation that turned Marxism into everyday practice and changed the moral outlook of the Chinese nation. Li laments that scholars have given it little dedicated study and calls for it to be treated as a permanent task for the Party and for Chinese thought.

The article opens with Li's personal route to the theme, from reading about Marx's choice of a profession and learning from Lei Feng in the 1960s to reflecting on the Soviet collapse. It then traces the idea's origins in Marx, Engels and Lenin, and its development in the Red Army's discipline and in Mao's work in the Jiangxi Soviet and at the Seventh Party Congress (1945). The later sections take up the meaning of "the people" and of "serve", and Mao's policies in education, health and Party conduct. Li ends with present-day corruption.

Li makes three main moves. First, the idea has Marxist roots, but Mao's distinctive step was to build a code of honour from the bottom up: the Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention first told soldiers what harm not to do, and only then asked for selfless service. Second, Li reads "the people" as a class and political concept, with workers and peasants as its main body. For this reason Mao said "serve the people" rather than "serve people", and Li accuses Gorbachev of using abstract talk of "the person" to disguise anti-people content. Third, the principle has to be specific: Mao attended to salt, rice, bridges and teachers' pay, and ran a frugal, clean government.

Li concludes that "Serve the People" is the Party's sole purpose, its lifeline and the bond between Party and people, and a landmark in the intellectual history of the Chinese nation. Citing cases of officials' corruption and press headlines on abuses against peasants, Li contends that the Party today often falls short of its own standard. Li therefore calls for a new chapter of "Serve the People" under reform and opening up and the socialist market economy. Read the original if you want a detailed, sympathetic Chinese reading of Mao's service ethic, and of how it is used to criticise present-day cadres' conduct.
quoteEn: "Serve the people" looks ordinary, yet within that ordinariness lie the direction of human social development and the most basic reason why a person becomes a social being.
quoteZh: “为人民服务”看似平凡，可就在它的平凡中包含着人类社会发展的方向，包含着人之所以成为社会的人的最基本的道理。

glossary.explanation: Title of Mao Zedong's September 1944 speech at a memorial meeting for the soldier Zhang Side in Yan'an. It became the best-known slogan of the Chinese Communist Party and is often called its fundamental purpose.

glossary.pinyin: sān dà jìlǜ bā xiàng zhùyì
glossary.en: Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention
glossary.explanation: Code of conduct for the Red Army and later the People's Liberation Army, developed from rules Mao set in 1927–28. It governs soldiers' behaviour towards civilians, for example taking nothing from them and paying for damage.

t: Chen Yun's method of thought on advancing reform
zh: 陈云关于推进改革的思想方法
paras: This short commentary, first published in Study Times in February 2025, asks how Chen Yun thought reform should be pursued. Xue argues that since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) Chen drew on long experience of economic leadership to set out a coherent approach, which played an important role in reform and opening up and socialist modernization.

The article is organised around five themes, each headed by a phrase of Chen's: the direction, principles, path, purpose and safeguard of reform. It draws on Chen's speeches and instructions from the late 1970s to 1988, and uses rural contracting and the Baoshan steelworks as examples.

Xue reports that Chen defined reform as the self-improvement and development of the socialist system and insisted that it stay socialist and keep faith in Marxism and communism. On method, Chen held that one must first establish the facts: he said most time should go to investigation and under ten per cent to deciding policy, a stance Xue links to his support for household contract responsibility and his decision that Baoshan be completed. Reform should proceed through pilots, in the manner of 'crossing the river by feeling the stones'.

Xue adds that for Chen reform must serve the people's welfare, balancing construction with livelihood ('first eat, then build'), and requires good Party conduct, with no 'loosening' of Party discipline and with senior cadres setting an example, including over their children's business activities. Xue presents these ideas as lasting guidance for economic and social development. Read the original if you want a brief, source-based overview of Chen Yun's reform thinking as presented in Party media.
quoteEn: Without good Party conduct, reform cannot be carried out well.
quoteZh: 没有好的党风，改革是搞不好的。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
glossary.explanation: A saying associated with reform-era China, meaning to advance step by step through experimentation rather than by a fixed blueprint.

t: People first: the core value orientation of Marxist social governance
zh: 人民至上：马克思主义社会治理的核心价值向度
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 13 February 2025
paras: This short commentary asks how the principle of putting the people first shapes social governance in China. Zhang and Liang argue that the 20th Party Congress (2022) formula of a social governance system of joint contribution, joint governance and shared benefits answers the questions of who governs, how, and who enjoys the results. In their reading, this formula expresses the people-first stance of Marxist social governance as developed under Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around the three elements of the formula: joint contribution (共建), joint governance (共治) and shared benefits (共享). Each section defines the element, links it to Marxist ideas and Xi Jinping's statements, and then sets out what the authors regard as required in practice today.

On joint contribution, the authors say the people are both the value subject and the builder of governance, so the government should address pressing livelihood concerns and strengthen citizens' sense of responsibility. On joint governance, they hold that it marks a move from social management to social governance, bringing Party, government, social organisations and individuals into one process, but only under the Party's overall leadership as the core. They cite the new-era Fengqiao experience as a model. On shared benefits, they argue that results should reach everyone and that sharing follows a process from uneven to balanced.

The authors conclude that sharing depends on supply-side measures: developing new quality productive forces, distribution with labour-based allocation as the mainstay, coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution, and laws guaranteeing equal rights to participate in and enjoy governance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese commentators link the joint contribution, joint governance and shared benefits formula to Marxist theory.
quoteEn: People each contribute their abilities in joint contribution and joint governance, and then each receive their due in sharing.
quoteZh: 人民在“共建”“共治”中各尽其能，而后在“共享”中各得其所

glossary.en: joint contribution, joint governance and shared benefits
glossary.explanation: A formula for social governance put forward in Party documents and in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It stresses that everyone takes part in governance and enjoys its results.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological innovation and upgraded industries.
A grassroots dispute-resolution model originating in Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s and later promoted by the Party as an example of local governance relying on the masses.
The official term that replaced "social management" (社会管理) in Party documents, stressing multiple participants rather than top-down administration.

keywords: joint contribution joint governance shared benefits

t: Creating a new form of human civilization through the coordinated development of the "five civilizations"
zh: 以“五大文明”协调发展创造人类文明新形态
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 7 February 2025
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that coordinated development of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization has created a new path of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization, this newspaper commentary asks what the "five civilizations" contribute. Wei argues that their harmonious advance gives Chinese modernization its comprehensive, coordinated, developmental and people-centred character. In the author's account, this marks a new height for Chinese civilization and enriches human civilizational progress.

The article is organised into five sections, one for each civilization, followed by a short closing statement. Each section defines the civilization concerned as a foundation for the others, then describes what the author sees as China's distinctive path in that field. The sections cover the material base, political institutions, culture and values, livelihoods and social governance, and ecology.

On material civilization, Wei points to Xi Jinping's economic thought and to new quality productive forces, which the author says reshape labour, the government–market relationship and capital allocation. On political civilization, the author contends that Chinese modernization surpasses the "endogenous difficulties" of the Western path, listing capital exploitation, alienated labour, polarization, environmental damage and expansionist plunder. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as going beyond Western "liberal democracy", which Wei says treats elections as the sole standard. On spiritual civilization, the author stresses the Two Integrations, which combine Marxism with traditional Chinese culture. On social and ecological civilization, Wei cites poverty alleviation, public services, grassroots governance, green development and participation in global environmental governance.

Wei concludes that Chinese modernization unites economic prosperity, political democracy, cultural flourishing, social fairness and good ecology. In the author's view, it has overcome the internal predicaments of conventional modernization and offers the world a distinctive route, contributing to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated scholars present Chinese modernization as a civilizational alternative to Western modernization.
quoteEn: The new path of Chinese modernization is a path of modernization marked by the coordinated development of the "five civilizations", one that unites economic prosperity, political democracy, cultural flourishing, social fairness and a sound ecology.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化新道路是“五大文明”协调发展的现代化道路，是经济富强、政治民主、文化繁荣、社会公平和生态良好相统一的现代化道路

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to productivity driven by advanced technology and innovation, such as artificial intelligence.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping. It stresses popular participation across decision-making, management and oversight, not only in elections.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was emphasised by Xi Jinping from 2021–2023.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations and global governance, presented as based on shared interests and cooperation.

t: Understanding common prosperity in step with the times
zh: 与时俱进地理解共同富裕
paras: This short commentary argues that common prosperity must be understood in both content and form in step with the times. Ma and Wang hold that, now that the building of a moderately prosperous society in all respects is complete, the concept differs qualitatively from what it meant three or four decades ago.

The article has three sections. They take up common prosperity as a response to the aspiration for a better life in the new era, its basis in the socialist market economy, and the need to broaden and raise the richness of what is shared.

The authors contend that once material scarcity has been overcome, the core issue is no longer opposition between rich and poor but differences in degrees of affluence. They cite per capita disposable income rising from 171 yuan in 1978 to 35,189 yuan in 2021, and Engel coefficients of 28.6 per cent (urban) and 32.7 per cent (rural). They argue that common prosperity rests on the socialist market economy and the Two Unwaverings, and that this economy is not simply "socialism plus a market economy". They also urge that shared public goods, such as transport, security, culture and ecological benefits, be counted alongside private wealth, and that digital sharing and less sensitivity to wealth gaps would help attract and develop talent.

Ma and Wang conclude that the goal is reached through high-quality development, with all positive forces united. They link this to the strategies of rejuvenating the country through science and education and of strengthening it through talent. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Party-aligned scholars recast common prosperity around public goods, market institutions and talent.
quoteEn: The socialist market economy is by no means "socialism plus a market economy"; it is the Communist Party of China's major, innovative answer to the "historical question" of what socialism is and how to build it.
quoteZh: 社会主义市场经济绝不是社会主义+市场经济，而是中国共产党对“什么是社会主义、如何建设社会主义”的这个“历史之问”的重大创新性回答。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping. It refers to prosperity shared by all, reached in stages.
The official line of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official guiding concept for the economy since 2017. It stresses quality, efficiency and balance over speed of growth.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s. It combines market mechanisms with public ownership as the main body and state macro-control.

t: Common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism
zh: 共同富裕是社会主义的本质要求
paras: Qi Yanhong, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, argues that common prosperity is the fundamental principle and essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a defining feature of Chinese modernization. The author proposes building on the idealist dimension of Marx's political philosophy while drawing on China's practice of socialist modernization, in order to develop a more realistic political philosophy.

The short commentary has three parts. It first sets out common prosperity as a goal of socialism, contrasting Marx and Engels's critique of capitalism with the Party's record from Mao Zedong to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It then traces the shift in China's basic social structure from an egalitarian orientation to one oriented to fairness. Finally, it considers how common prosperity should be advanced in the new stage.

Qi contends that capitalism, by its nature, produces polarisation between rich and poor, and that even Western welfare states serve to preserve the rule of capital. Socialist public ownership removes structural inequality and so provides the institutional precondition for common prosperity. Qi reads Deng Xiaoping's idea of letting some get rich first as grounding common prosperity in the development of productive forces. Marketisation has also brought social problems that, in Qi's account, now centre on how fairness and justice can promote common prosperity. For the new stage Qi proposes three measures: stronger state regulation of the market through taxation, social security and redistribution; stronger democracy and rule of law, including whole-process people's democracy; and socialist values of fairness, equality and community in place of Western individualism.

Qi concludes that common prosperity ultimately depends on the people acting as builders, governors and evaluators together, on sound institutional design and legal rules, and on a social ethos of fairness and solidarity. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese Marxist scholar links common prosperity to the contrast between socialist and capitalist modernization.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is not only an "economic issue" but also "a major political issue bearing on the Party's governing foundation".
quoteZh: 共同富裕不仅是“经济问题”，而且是“关系党的执政基础的重大政治问题”。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared affluence for all, which the Party presents as a principle of socialism. It has been given greater prominence since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western capitalist modernization.
The official description of China's democratic system, which the Party says involves popular participation in every stage of political and policy processes.
The official name for the Party's theory and system of socialism, developed since reform and opening up.

t: A political-philosophical interpretation of common prosperity
zh: 共同富裕的政治哲学诠释
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks what common prosperity means within Marxist political philosophy. Wang argues that common prosperity is a political project that goes beyond the difficulties of capitalist modernization. In the author's account it is a distinguishing mark of socialist political civilization, carrying the values of putting the people first and realising the people's longing for a better life.

The article sets Marx's view against the tradition of modern Western political philosophy, drawing on Locke, Hobbes and Charles Taylor. It is organised in three sections: common prosperity as the basic precondition for people's free and all-round development, as a value narrative of fair sharing, and as an ideal social vision that unfolds step by step.

Wang contends that Western political philosophy rests on an atomised individual driven by bodily wants, so that modernization becomes an arena of competing interests. Contractual procedural justice, built on the 'rational economic man', is said to weaken concern for concrete persons and the sense of community. Wang reads Marx's observation of paradoxical poverty amid growing wealth, and his statement that future production will aim at the prosperity of all, as the basis for common prosperity. On this reading it sublates procedural justice and capitalist poverty, and expresses a socialist justice of 'everyone participates, everyone benefits'.

Wang concludes that Marx's common prosperity is not mere material accumulation or levelling. It is directed against the 'absolute poverty of the human essence' under the logic of capital and fetishism, and values active individuals with individuality and independence. It will be realised through historical practice, ending in each person's free and all-round development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese philosopher grounds the policy of common prosperity in Marx's critique of liberal individualism.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is a positive sublation of Western procedural justice and of capitalism's paradoxical poverty, and it displays the value narrative of socialist fairness and justice in which 'everyone participates' and 'everyone enjoys'.
quoteZh: 共同富裕是对西方程序正义以及资本主义悖论性贫困的积极扬弃，彰显了“人人参与”“人人享有”的社会主义公平正义的价值叙事。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, stressed again under Xi Jinping since 2021. It means prosperity shared by all, in contrast to polarisation between rich and poor.

t: Deepening the Marxist Theoretical Research and Development Project in the new era
zh: 深入推进新时代马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
paras: Marking the 20th anniversary of the Marxist Theoretical Research and Development Project, Huang Zhaoquan takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction on the project's new-era direction. The commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, argues that universities should use their strengths to promote the project's high-quality development while adhering to fundamental principles and innovating.

Huang sets out three areas of work for universities: building the discipline, training teachers, and serving society. Universities are described as key sites of the project, with advantages in translating classic works, theoretical interpretation, textbook and discipline systems, and talent training.

On discipline building, Huang calls for upholding Marxism's guiding position, strengthening the first-level discipline of Marxist theory, and combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and traditional culture. Research should focus on major theoretical and practical questions around deepening reform and Chinese modernization, and on building an independent Chinese system of knowledge. On teachers, Huang calls for a corps that is politically strong, theoretically capable and morally sound, with faith in Marxism rooted in teachers before students. On social service, Huang proposes problem-oriented research, popularising the Party's innovative theory in plain language, and teacher participation in Party and government decision consultation.

Huang concludes that these measures would turn the discipline's strengths into practical contributions to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, backed by funding and evaluation reforms. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party leader translates Xi Jinping's instruction into institutional tasks for Marxist theory programmes.
quoteEn: Marxist theory arises and develops by continually facing, answering and solving problems, and answering and guiding the solution of problems is the fundamental task of theory.
quoteZh: 马克思主义理论是在不断面对问题、回答问题、解决问题中产生发展的，回答并指导解决问题是理论的根本任务。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: Marxist Theoretical Research and Development Project
glossary.literal: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
glossary.explanation: A national programme launched in 2004 to research, compile textbooks on and promote Marxist theory in China. It is organised by the Party and is carried out largely through universities and research institutes.
The official term for China's development path, set out by Xi Jinping's leadership, which presents it as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.

keywords: Marxist Theoretical Research and Development Project

t: Upholding the dialectical unity of breaking down and establishing in reform
zh: 在改革中坚持破和立的辩证统一
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Qin Long examines the reform methodology that Xi Jinping has summarised as upholding the dialectical unity of 'breaking down' (po) and 'establishing' (li). The formula calls for doing both together, establishing before breaking, and breaking what must go only once its replacement is in place. Qin argues that this approach is an important expression of Marxist materialist dialectics and a guide for deepening reform as part of Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first explains the po–li relation through three dialectical laws. The second traces the idea through Marx and Engels, Lenin, and the Chinese Communist Party's history from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi. The third turns to the present stage of 'further deepening reform comprehensively', which Qin describes as a tough phase of reform.

Qin argues that po and li are opposed, since strengthening one weakens the other, yet also unified: breaking without establishing is blind destruction, and establishing without breaking leaves no room for the new. In terms of quantitative and qualitative change, the new germinates inside the old, and old habits persist after the new appears, so the two alternate in cycles. Under the negation of the negation, breaking is sublation, discarding what is ossified while keeping what is useful. Qin reads the contradiction between productive forces and forms of intercourse in Marx and Engels as a po–li process. Lenin's insistence on smashing the old state machine, and his adoption of the New Economic Policy, are presented as the same logic applied in practice. The Party's history is read as a continuous application of this logic.

Qin concludes that reform today must be systemic and integrated rather than piecemeal. Its sequencing and timing should seek a balance between removing old ills and setting up new institutions, and the formula should be applied through the principle 'establish first, break later'. Establishing first means setting out the main direction and framework so as to stabilise expectations, growth and employment. Breaking later means screening out old systems and policies that no longer fit the aims of transforming the growth model and improving quality and efficiency. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how the Party presents this reform method as rooted in Marxist dialectics and in its own history.
quoteEn: Breaking is a means that serves establishing, and establishing is the purpose of breaking.
quoteZh: 破是为立服务的手段，立是破的目的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, promoted by the Communist Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The reform agenda set out at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), building on the comprehensive deepening of reform launched in 2013.

t: Strengthening the theoretical system of the Chinese nation as a community
zh: 加强中华民族共同体理论体系建设
paras: This newspaper commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Xi Jinping's call to build a theoretical system for the Chinese nation as a community (Zhonghua minzu gongtongti). Sun Beibei argues that forging a sense of community for the Chinese nation requires a scientific and complete theory. In the author's account, this is part of building an independent Chinese system of philosophy and social science knowledge and of shaking off the influence of Western theories of nationality and their discourse.
The piece has three parts. The first concerns method, the second the research agenda, and the third disciplinary development and personnel.

On method, Sun holds that the Two Integrations must run through the whole project: combining Marxist nationality theory with China's concrete realities, and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The first calls for study of the classical Marxist writers and of Xi Jinping's thinking on ethnic work. The second calls for deeper research on the history of the Chinese nation and on the 'four commons' view of history, in which territory, history, culture and spirit are all said to be jointly created by all ethnic groups. The aim is to secure the power to narrate history and set discourse. On content, Sun proposes three lines of research. These are a systematic study of Xi's thought on ethnic work, clarification of basic concepts and relationships (nation, commonality and difference, pluralistic unity), and major practical questions, including shared spiritual homeland, governance modernization and preventing risks in the ethnic sphere.

Sun calls for interdisciplinary cooperation among Marxist theory, ethnology, history, anthropology, archaeology and other fields. The author also proposes better research platforms, incentives, core expert teams, support for niche fields and training of young scholars. The aim is a Chinese-led body of sources, discourse and theory. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official research agenda for ethnic theory and its institutional implications.
quoteEn: In particular, efforts must be made to resolve the problem of Chinese ethnological research being swayed by Western theories of nationality and their discourse, and to speed up the formation of China's own systems of historical sources, discourse and theory on the Chinese nation as a community, so as to tell the story of the Chinese nation well.
quoteZh: 特别是要着力解决我国民族学研究中存在的被西方民族理论和话语体系所左右的问题，加快形成中国自主的中华民族共同体史料体系、话语体系、理论体系，讲好中华民族故事。

glossary.en: the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept presenting China's 56 recognised ethnic groups as one national community. The Party promotes it as the basis of its ethnic policy, including the drive to 'forge a sense of community'.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
An official formulation of the Chinese nation's history. It says that the territory, history, culture and spirit of China were jointly developed by all ethnic groups.

glossary.literal: pattern of pluralism and unity of the nation
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong. It describes the Chinese nation as one entity made up of many ethnic groups.

t: Understanding the holistic approach to national security through scientific thinking
zh: 以科学思维领悟总体国家安全观
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), posted 21 January 2025
paras: Marking the tenth anniversary in 2024 of Xi Jinping's holistic approach to national security, this newspaper commentary argues that the concept contains a rich set of scientific modes of thinking. Zhang contends that national security must be pursued by applying these methods, since security underpins the steady advance of Chinese modernization.

The article takes eight modes of thinking in turn, each paired with one feature of the approach: strategic (comprehensiveness of outlook), systems (totality), dialectical (integration), historical (continuity), innovative (development), rule-of-law (practicality), bottom-line (initiative) and extreme-case thinking (struggle). Each section is brief and draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In Zhang's account, the approach rests on strategic and systems thinking: it looks at the whole of national rejuvenation, links domestic and international situations, and treats security and development as mutually reinforcing. Dialectical thinking appears in the "five coordinations", for instance internal and external security, or traditional and non-traditional security. Zhang adds that historical thinking draws on the Party's century of experience while rejecting historical nihilism. Bottom-line and extreme-case thinking are presented as a pair: set thresholds that must not be crossed, and prepare for the worst and most extreme scenarios, using high-probability thinking to meet low-probability events.

Zhang concludes that applying the holistic approach requires combining these methods, linking theory with practice, and continually updating methods in science and technology, talent and international cooperation. Zhang also calls for security work to be placed on a rule-of-law footing. Read the original if you want a compact overview of how Chinese commentary maps Xi Jinping's thinking methods onto national security doctrine.
quoteEn: Extreme-case thinking requires us, in safeguarding national security, to take the initiative in considering the worst and most extreme situations, and how to respond to and handle unforeseeable risks and challenges once they appear.
quoteZh: 极限思维要求我们在维护国家安全的过程中，要主动考虑最坏、最极端的情况，考虑那些难以预料的风险挑战出现后如何应对和处置。

glossary.explanation: A national security doctrine put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014. It treats security as spanning many fields, including political, economic, cultural, technological and military, and links security with development.
The official Party formulation of China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
In Party usage, a label for views that deny or belittle the Party's and socialism's historical record.

t: Answering questions and guiding their resolution is the fundamental task of theory
zh: 回答并指导解决问题是理论的根本任务
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报)
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's instruction marking the twentieth anniversary of the Marxist Theory Research and Development Project, Yao asks how scholars should carry out their central task: studying and promoting Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today, argues that research should deepen the systematization and scholarly grounding of this body of thought, as a contribution to adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Yao first credits existing research with broad coverage of the thought's background, sources and content, then lists remaining weaknesses: fragmented study, theory lagging behind practice, inadequate attention to major real-world problems, and low-level repetition. Three sections then set out methods and tasks: upholding fundamental principles while innovating together with the Two Integrations, distilling signature concepts and original theories, and studying concrete Chinese problems.

On method, Yao calls for unity of critique and construction, of inheritance and development, and of Marxism (the "soul") and traditional culture (the "root"). Scholars should criticise erroneous ideological trends and identify what the thought adds to Marxism, not only what it inherits. Signature concepts such as Chinese modernization, whole-process people's democracy and a community with a shared future for mankind should be distilled, along with original theories such as Xi's diplomatic and cultural thought. Yao holds that this would turn institutional and cultural advantages into discursive ones and help build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system. On problems, scholars should sort concrete issues by priority, focus on the fundamental one (advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization), and criticise false problems.

Yao concludes that theory must be driven by real problems, and that identifying genuine questions and exposing false ones go hand in hand. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame research priorities for studying Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Problems are the voice of the times; answering them and guiding their resolution is the fundamental task of theory.
quoteZh: 问题是时代的声音，回答并指导解决问题是理论的根本任务。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the ongoing effort to combine Marxist principles with Chinese conditions and contemporary issues.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is a core formula of Xi-era theory.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019. It stresses participation at every stage of political life.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared global interests and cooperation.

keywords: Marxist Theory Research and Development Project

t: A new view of civilizations: opening a threefold transcendence in global civilizational development
zh: 新文明观：开启全球文明发展的三重超越
paras: This commentary, published in Beijing Daily in January 2025, draws on the newly issued Study Outline of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. Shao Sheng presents Xi Jinping's outlook on civilizations, built on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, as a "new view of civilizations". The author argues that it rests on three transcendences that reinforce one another.

The piece takes each transcendence in turn: exchange over estrangement, mutual learning over conflict, and inclusiveness over claims of superiority. It combines a historical account of Western expansion since the age of exploration with critiques of Samuel Huntington's "clash of civilizations" and of the idea of civilizational superiority.

Shao contends that Western colonial expansion built a West-centred world system, destroyed or remade other civilizations and made exchange coercive and one-way. In the author's account, this laid the seeds of racism, nationalism and terrorism, and today some Western leaders sustain estrangement through trade, technology and information wars. Huntington's thesis is described as a misreading of history that mistakes conflicts of interest for civilizational difference and serves hegemony. The author calls the doctrine of civilizational superiority a colonialist construct behind "universal values" and "the end of history", and argues that Western modernization itself depended on Mesopotamian, Chinese and Arab achievements.

Shao concludes that exchange, mutual learning and inclusiveness are the necessary path to prosperity and peace. The author calls for respecting each country's right to choose its own system and path, and for turning diversity into a source of development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholarship presents the official civilizational outlook and its critique of Western-centrism.
quoteEn: To change this situation, the first priority is to respect each country's right to choose its own social system and development path, dispel doubts and estrangement, and through equal civilizational exchange turn the world's diversity and national differences into vitality and momentum for development, opening new ground for the common progress of global civilization.
quoteZh: 要改变这一局面，首要之务是尊重各国自主选择社会制度和发展道路的权利，消除疑虑和隔阂，通过平等的文明交流，把世界多样性和各国差异性转化为发展活力和动力，进而为全球文明的共同进步开辟新天地。

glossary.explanation: A body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture and ideology, formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought. The Study Outline is an authoritative reader on it.
Samuel Huntington's 1990s thesis that post-Cold War conflict would run along civilizational lines. The article rejects it.
The idea that one civilization, usually the West, is inherently superior to others. The article treats it as a colonialist doctrine.
The claim that certain values, such as liberal democracy and human rights, apply to all societies. Official Chinese discourse often criticizes it as a vehicle of Western dominance.

t: Methodological consciousness in consolidating cultural subjectivity
zh: 巩固文化主体性的方法论自觉
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how cultural subjectivity (wenhua zhutixing) can be consolidated. Gu and Song take the concept from Xi Jinping's remarks that any culture must have its own subjectivity if it is to stand firm, travel far and have the power to lead, unite, shape and radiate. They argue that consolidating it is an original proposition of Xi Jinping's thought on culture and requires a high degree of methodological consciousness.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first deals with the methodological premises: the context in which the concept appeared, its essential determinations and its cognitive structure. The second sets out three methodological standpoints. The third presents three methodological principles. Each part is built around passages from Xi Jinping's speeches.

On the premises, the authors place the concept in three contexts. In the intellectual context it is a 'terminological revolution' within Marxist cultural thought. In the historical context it condenses the Party's experience of leading cultural development. In the contemporary context it answers the new cultural mission. They hold that its essence lies in practice, since it originates in the subjectivity of real people, and in an objective independence that distinguishes one culture from others. On standpoints, they require upholding the Party's overall leadership as the political guarantee and direction. They also require a people-centred value standpoint, in which the people are both the practical and the value subject. The third standpoint is resolving the 'dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western'. On principles, they name the Two Integrations, which they say consolidate cultural subjectivity. They also name upholding fundamental principles while innovating, which they cast as thesis and synthesis, and self-confidence and self-reliance. The last of these means avoiding a 'master copy', 'template', 'reprint' or 'replica' of other models.

The authors conclude that clarifying these premises, standpoints and principles gives consolidating cultural subjectivity its intellectual foundation and its practical direction.
