Zhao Zhenhua argues that they are a body of regularities distilled from the Party's economic work. In Zhao's account they apply dialectical and historical materialist method to current economic contradictions, serve as principles for economic work and as a method for high-quality development and Chinese modernization, and further enrich Xi Jinping's economic thought.

The article opens by defining "balancing" as taking the whole picture into account and coordinating policies, against a background of what Zhao calls great changes unseen in a century, pressure from the United States-led West, weak global recovery and insufficient domestic demand. It then takes the five pairs in turn: an efficient market and a capable government; aggregate supply and aggregate demand; nurturing new drivers of growth and renewing old ones; improving the increment and revitalising the stock; and raising quality and expanding total volume.

On the market and the state, Zhao holds that neither unregulated competitive capitalism nor a highly centralised planned economy has proved viable, and that the two should complement each other rather than stand as separate blocks. The cycle of "loosening leads to chaos, tightening leads to stagnation" is attributed to misplaced or absent government functions. On supply and demand, Zhao calls for deepening supply-side structural reform while expanding effective investment (housing, urban renewal, rural infrastructure) and consumption (income growth, social security, vouchers for low earners). On new and old drivers, Zhao says traditional industries are a base for new quality productive forces and should be upgraded with digital technology, with each region choosing its own path. Zhao treats increment and stock as mutually reinforcing, and defines quality through continuity, balance, sustainability, fairness and security.

Zhao concludes that quality should be raised within the expansion of total output and total output expanded through higher quality, since this lays the material foundation for Chinese modernization. Proposed measures include a unified, open and orderly market, breaking regional blockades and monopolies, integrating the real and digital economies, and higher-level opening up. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference's guiding principles and the policy measures attached to each.
quoteEn: The relationship between the market and the government is not one of opposition or substitution, but one of mutual complementarity, coordination and reinforcement.
quoteZh: 市场和政府之间不是对立的替代关系，而是相互补充、相互协调和相互促进的关系

glossary.explanation: Five pairs of relationships that the Central Economic Work Conference at the end of 2024 said must be handled in a coordinated way in economic work.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
The official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting the economy from speed of growth towards quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015 that seeks to improve the supply structure, for example by cutting overcapacity, to match changing demand.
The official name for the body of ideas on economic work associated with Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought.

t: Coordinating the relationship between an efficient market and a capable government
zh: 统筹好有效市场和有为政府的关系
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up a formulation from the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference: the need to coordinate an "efficient market" and a "capable government" so as to create an economic order that is both "lively" and "well managed". Hong Junjie, a university president and professor, argues that the formulation explains how government and market can be combined more effectively. In Hong's reading, it is a theoretical innovation that enriches Marxist political economy's account of the market economy and points the way to a high-standard socialist market economy.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the coordination matters, both for a high-standard socialist market economy, as stressed in the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), and for high-quality development. The second names three relationships to be handled: vitality and order, efficiency and fairness, and development and security. The third applies the market–government pairing to the four links of social reproduction: production, distribution, circulation and consumption.

Hong's central claim is that markets and governments are complementary. Markets allocate resources through price signals and competition and drive innovation. They also produce information asymmetries, under-supplied public goods and disorderly capital expansion, which government must correct through policy design, regulation and public services. Hong therefore says that to make the market more effective, government must be more capable. In production, Hong calls for supply-side structural reform and new quality productive forces, which are to be fostered jointly by government planning and market competition. In distribution, the market is said to dominate primary distribution, while government handles redistribution through taxes, social security and transfers, and both encourage a "third distribution" through charity. Hong grounds this in historical materialism: distribution relations are part of the relations of production and are determined by the state of the productive forces.

Hong concludes that the "visible hand" and the "invisible hand" should run through every link of the national economic cycle. In circulation, Hong urges a unified national market, institutional opening up and logistics infrastructure. In consumption, Hong urges a long-term mechanism for expanding demand: more jobs, higher pensions and medical insurance subsidies, the "two news" policies and new consumption areas such as the silver economy. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the 2024 economic policy line links market–government theory to concrete measures in each part of the economic cycle.
quoteEn: To make the market more effective, government needs to be more capable.
quoteZh: 让市场更有效，需要政府更有为。

glossary.en: efficient market and a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that accomplishes things
glossary.explanation: A formula in Chinese economic policy discourse for combining market mechanisms with active state guidance. The 2024 Central Economic Work Conference called for coordinating the two.

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A goal given prominence in the Third Plenum decision of 2024. It refers to a more developed version of the socialist market economy system that China established after reform and opening up.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation and emerging industries rather than by traditional resource-intensive inputs.
The official guideline for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth alone.

t: Accelerating the construction of a discourse system for the Chinese national community
zh: 加快构建中华民族共同体话语体系
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 20), Wang Yanzhong takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at a Politburo study session, to correct the tendency of Chinese ethnology to be swayed by Western theories of nationality and to build China's own systems of historical sources, discourse and theory on the Chinese national community. Wang argues that building this discourse system quickly is theoretically and practically important for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the task is urgent after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second presents cultural confidence as the basic precondition. The third sets out methods and concrete measures: historical research, a body of source materials, disciplinary development, training of researchers and fieldwork.

In Wang's account, a self-reliant discourse is needed to advance ethnic work with the aim of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation as its main line. It is also presented as a theoretical weapon against what the author describes as Western interference through ethnic, religious and human rights discourse. Wang holds that cultural confidence rests on more than 5,000 years of civilisation and on the nation's cultural subjectivity, and that only a holistic view of history, summed up in the "five commonalities", can ground an autonomous discourse. Wang then calls for research that follows the historical, theoretical and practical logics of the nation's formation, stresses the growing commonality among peoples, and compares China's path with other countries' handling of ethnic questions.

Wang calls for fuller use of historical and archaeological sources, multidisciplinary research led by the research bases for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, and support for young scholars. Wang also calls for more fieldwork, with theory drawn from the Party's practice of revolution, construction and reform and developed through the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale and the practical agenda for building the Chinese national community discourse in ethnic studies.
quoteEn: Without a high degree of cultural confidence, no autonomous theory and discourse system belonging to the Chinese nation can be formed, still less the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 没有高度的文化自信，就形成不了属于中华民族自主的理论和话语体系，就更没有中华民族伟大复兴。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Chinese nation as one community made up of all of China's ethnic groups. It underpins current Party ethnic policy, which stresses a shared national identity.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly forging the consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: Slogan adopted as the main line of the Party's ethnic work in the new era. It aims to consolidate national identity among all ethnic groups.
Official concept, promoted since the 2010s, of confidence in China's cultural traditions, socialist culture and revolutionary heritage. It is counted among the four forms of confidence.
Formula for combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Formula in official historiography stating that all ethnic groups jointly opened up the territory, built the unified state, wrote the history, created the culture and fostered the national spirit.

t: The "tianxia worldview" and the traditional legal-cultural origins of the sense of community for the Chinese nation
zh: “天下观”与中华民族共同体意识的传统法文化渊源
paras: Zhang Yan and Ke Lan ask where the sense of community for the Chinese nation (the Chinese term is zhonghua minzu gongtongti yishi) comes from in China's traditional legal culture. They argue that the ancient tianxia ("all under heaven") worldview is its cultural root. On their account, this worldview treated the order of the world as cultural and ethical rather than as a matter of blood, territory or a single dynasty. They also distinguish it from the Western concept of empire.

The article has four parts. It first traces the concept of tianxia and its links to "China" (zhongguo), the "five zones" (wufu) model and the unity of family, state and tianxia. It then looks at the "great unification" (dayitong) ideal and the fluid Hua–Yi distinction (Chinese versus "barbarian"). The third part follows the shift from "the Chinese nation" to the "community of the Chinese nation" and sets out the legal content of the sense of community. A short conclusion looks ahead.

The authors make three moves. First, they argue that in the Confucian tradition the Hua–Yi distinction rested on adherence to ritual (li) and not on descent. Outsiders who accepted ritual could become Hua, and Hua who abandoned it could become Yi. Together with dayitong, which turned the ideal into centralised, legal and administrative practice, this is said to have produced the idea of "Hua and Yi as one". Second, they say the defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 pushed China out of the tianxia order and into the nation-state order. Liang Qichao introduced "Zhonghua minzu" in 1902, and Fei Xiaotong's 1988 "pluriform and unitary" formulation completed the concept. Third, they describe the community as a political entity formed through national identity, identity with the Chinese nation and cultural identity. They support this with legal instruments: the 2018 constitutional amendment, the system of regional ethnic autonomy, the National Common Language Law of 2000, and the proposed law on promoting ethnic unity and progress.

The authors conclude that tianxia thinking carried the inclusive idea of "Hua and Yi as one family" and became a pillar of Chinese civilisation. It later developed into modern nation-state theory. They call for fuller implementation of the constitution's principle of ethnic unity, a more complete body of specialised laws, and faster legislation on ethnic unity and progress. They also call for stronger cultural and national identity, to lay the ideological and cultural foundations for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a legal-cultural account of how Chinese official discourse on ethnic policy traces its roots to classical sources such as tianxia, dayitong and the Hua–Yi distinction.
quoteEn: "Hua-Xia" and the "four Yi" are fully interchangeable; their identity is not static but in a state of dynamic flux.
quoteZh: “华夏”与“四夷”是完全可以转换的，他们的身份属性不是静态的，而是处于一种动态的流动变化中。

glossary.explanation: A principle first stated in the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, valuing political, cultural and legal unity under one rule. The authors treat it as the practical form of the tianxia ideal.
The traditional distinction between the civilised Huaxia and surrounding peoples. The authors argue it was defined by ritual and culture and not by descent.

glossary.en: sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A Party concept, written into the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), stressing that all ethnic groups form one organic whole. The usual official phrase is "forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation".

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term goal of national revival, widely used in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Four basic questions about adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化的四个基本问题
paras: Han Jianxin sets out a primer on a core concept of Party theory: what it means to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, why this is necessary, what it has produced, and how it should continue. The article argues that Marxism is a method rather than a dogma. In Han's account, it must be fused with China's concrete conditions and traditional culture, and each stage of this process has yielded a historic theoretical advance.

The text, which first appeared on the Xuanjiangjia website in November 2024, is organised into four numbered sections that follow the four questions of the title. It draws heavily on Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation of the "Sinification of Marxism", Engels's remarks on method, the 2021 Party history resolution, and speeches by Xi Jinping. The third section reviews a century of Party history from the October Revolution and the founding of the Party in 1921 to the present.

On the "why", Han argues that Marxism's own nature requires adaptation: citing Engels, Han holds that its worldview is a method and a starting point for research, and that its basic principles must be combined with each country's actual situation to solve real problems. On the "results", Han identifies three achievements: Mao Zedong Thought, the system of theories of socialism with Chinese characteristics (Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development), and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Each is presented as a "leap" that answered the main tasks of its period. Han adds that using plain Chinese idiom matters because truth only has force once the people grasp it.

For the future, Han calls for the Two Integrations and the "six musts" of the 20th Party Congress (2022) to guide theoretical innovation. Han also calls for innovation grounded in practice and in the creativity of the people through the mass line. Theory should be made systematic and academically rigorous, and the Marxist "soul" and Chinese cultural "roots" should not be abandoned. Han presents continuing this work as the historical responsibility of today's Communists. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how Party theorists periodise and justify the adaptation of Marxism in China.
quoteEn: Systematisation means bringing the experience we have formed in practice into a complete scientific system and logical structure.
quoteZh: 体系化是要把我们在实践中形成的经验纳入到完整的科学体系和逻辑结构中。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2021 formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

Principles set out in the 20th Party Congress report: put the people first, be confident and independent, uphold fundamental principles while innovating, be problem-oriented, adopt systems thinking, and have the world in view.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, which the Party presents as socialism adapted to Chinese conditions.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin-era doctrine holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

t: The high degree of fit between the moral outlook of fine traditional Chinese culture and the value propositions of scientific socialism
zh: 中华优秀传统文化中的道德观同科学社会主义价值观主张高度契合性研究
source: New Era New Thought Studies (新时代新思想研究), 12 November 2024
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which says that the moral outlook embodied in fine traditional Chinese culture is highly compatible with the value propositions of scientific socialism, Chen Hongjuan asks in what respects that fit holds. The article argues that, on the question of how individuals should relate to themselves, to others and to the group, traditional Chinese morality and Marxist scientific socialism converge at four levels: value concept, goal of individual moral development, principles of social morality, and the value logic of political morality.

The article is organised in four sections matching these levels. It pairs the Confucian-centred ideal of cultivating oneself to bring peace to others and taking the world as one's responsibility with Marx's "truly human morality". It then pairs the unity of knowing, feeling and willing with the all-round development of the human being, "delighting in the group and valuing harmony" with developing one's true nature in society, and "the world as one's own task" with liberating humankind. Throughout, Chen cites classical Chinese sources extensively alongside Marx, Engels and Xi Jinping, and contrasts both traditions with Western morality.

Chen's central move is a contrast. Traditional Chinese morality, Chen argues, starts from the distinction between humans and animals, treats morality as internally generated and self-disciplined, and is society-centred. Western traditional morality is described as starting from the human–god relation and as externally imposed, and as shifting after the Renaissance to individual-centred rationalism and utilitarianism. Scientific socialism, in Chen's account, criticises the individualism and hypocrisy of capitalist morality, grounds morality in autonomy and in humanity's "species-being", and subordinates private interest to common interest. Chen reads the traditional priority of righteousness over profit, the golden rule of reciprocity and the path from self-cultivation to governing the realm as parallel to this. A second move links the fit to economic base: Chen says traditional culture arose under what Marx called the Asiatic form of ownership, in which the individual is not independent of the community, which favoured collective morality. Chen also notes that early Chinese introducers of Marx stressed his perseverance in terms of the Confucian ideal person.

Chen concludes that both traditions refuse to see people as isolated individuals and look towards a return of values to the collective and society, citing Xi Jinping's remark to this effect. The article presents the fit as grounded in shared value logic rather than coincidence, and so as support for combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-by-source comparison of Confucian, Daoist and Neo-Confucian moral concepts with Marx's and Engels's writings on morality, as framed by official Party discourse.
quoteEn: Whether viewed in terms of value concepts, development goals, value principles or value logic, fine traditional Chinese culture and the value propositions of scientific socialism are highly compatible at the level of moral outlook.
quoteZh: 无论是从价值理念、发展目标、价值原则还是从价值逻辑来看，中华优秀传统文化同科学社会主义价值观主张在道德观层面都具有高度契合性。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the parts of China's historical culture that Party documents regard as worth inheriting and developing. It is central to the policy of combining Marxism with Chinese tradition.
The term used for the socialist theory of Marx and Engels, as opposed to what they called utopian socialism. In Chinese official usage it designates the theoretical basis of the Party's ideology.

glossary.en: cultivating oneself to bring peace to others
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the Analects (Confucius). It expresses the idea that personal moral self-cultivation leads to social peace and good governance.
A phrase from Engels's Anti-Dühring for a morality that transcends class antagonism, which he held possible only after class opposition had been abolished and forgotten.
The cognitive, emotional and volitional aspects of personality. Chinese moral philosophy uses the triad to describe a well-rounded ideal character.

glossary.en: the world as one's own task
glossary.literal: all under heaven is one's own responsibility
glossary.explanation: A Confucian-derived ideal that the individual should take responsibility for the welfare of all under heaven, linking self-cultivation to public duty.

t: On the necessity, possibility and innovative contribution of the "Second Integration"
zh: 论“第二个结合”的必要性可能性及其创新性贡献
paras: This article takes up the "Second Integration", the principle, announced by Xi Jinping in July 2021, of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Mei Rongzheng argues that it is necessary, possible and innovative, and that it is a "further ideological emancipation". The article is a response to the lively discussion that followed Xi's 2023 speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development. It singles out three questions that Mei thinks need deeper study.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the Second Integration is necessary, in three respects: understanding the socialist road, building a culturally strong country, and building a modern Chinese civilization. The second asks why Marxism and traditional culture can be combined, and gives four grounds. The third sets out the innovative contributions of the Second Integration. Mei draws on Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi, and cites passages by Marx and Engels on China.

On necessity, Mei argues that China's path cannot be understood without its five thousand years of civilization. He treats the "five outstanding characteristics" of Chinese civilization (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) as the basis of the Second Integration. On possibility, Mei argues that Marxism is the general and Chinese culture the particular. He adds that Marx and Engels wrote extensively on China, and that the Marxist classics therefore already contain elements abstracted from Chinese history. He also argues that the "First Integration" already included traditional culture, citing Mao's use of classical idioms.

On innovation, Mei contends that the Second Integration raises traditional culture from one element of "China's concrete reality" to an equal partner of Marxist principles, as one of the two sides of the "universal truth" Deng Xiaoping described. It also clarifies the route to the "new cultural mission", by promoting classical scholarship, strengthening Marxist guidance of cultural research and raising national cohesion. Mei casts this as a defence against Western ideological infiltration and historical nihilism. He concludes that it deepens the cultural roots of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theoretical defence of the Second Integration, including its use of Marx's and Engels's remarks on China.
quoteEn: This shows that the essence of China's fine traditional culture, after critique, transformation and processing, has been integrated directly into the principles of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 这表明，中华优秀传统文化中的精华，经过批判、改造和加工，被直接融入马克思主义中国化时代化原理之中。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2021, of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's fine traditional culture. It is paired with the First Integration, the combination of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official term for those parts of China's traditional culture that the Party regards as worth inheriting and developing.

glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài xīn de wénhuà shǐmìng
glossary.literal: new cultural mission of the new era
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2023 formulation: to promote cultural prosperity, build a culturally strong country and build a modern Chinese civilization.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that are said to deny or denigrate the Party's history and the socialist path.

glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's 2023 speech on culture. It denotes a modern civilization rooted in traditional culture and guided by Marxism.

t: A comprehensive understanding of the basic approach to constructing the subjectivity of Chinese culture
zh: 全面理解中华文化主体性建构的基本进路
source: Digest of Chinese Social Sciences (中国社会科学文摘), 2024 no. 6
paras: Han Sheng takes up the question of how Chinese cultural subjectivity (wenhua zhutixing) is built and why it matters for a country's modernization. The article argues that cultural subjectivity is an organic unity of "not forgetting one's origins", "absorbing the foreign" and "facing the future". In Han's account, China has since reform and opening up, and especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), developed a clear approach to this task, achieving spiritual independence and setting the goal of a strong cultural nation.

The article presents Xi Jinping's thought on culture as the fullest expression of this approach and as a guide to action for building a socialist cultural power with Chinese characteristics. It is organised around three themes, each introduced by a four-character slogan: the Second Integration as the inner thread, creative continuation of tradition as the basic proposition, and exchange and mutual learning among civilizations as the key arena.

First, Han argues that the combination of Marxism's basic principles with excellent traditional Chinese culture, the "Second Integration", has run through the Party's cultural work for over a century. Han calls it "another ideological emancipation" that moved China from absence to presence in the world's civilizational map, and that grounds Chinese modernization culturally. Second, drawing on historical materialism, Han holds that cultural subjectivity requires "upholding fundamental principles while innovating". Modernization should reactivate and renew tradition, not break with it, in the sense of Feng Youlan's "speaking on from" the past, while rejecting cultural conservatism and revivalism. Third, openness is said to be a precondition of a growing civilization. Han introduces the idea of the "meaningful other", whom a culture treats as a constitutive condition of its own growth, and urges a move from conflictual to constructive relational rationality.

Han concludes that this construction of cultural subjectivity gives Chinese modernization a deep cultural justification and breaks the myth that modernization equals Westernization. In the article's view it models a way to resist Western hegemonic thinking and the homogenising logic of colonialism in a new type of globalization. Understanding this approach is said to help Xi Jinping's thought on culture guide Chinese modernization towards national rejuvenation and the progress of world civilization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how current Chinese theory links the Second Integration, tradition and civilizational dialogue under the heading of cultural subjectivity.
quoteEn: In their \"mutual fit\" and \"mutual fulfilment\", the basic principles of Marxism and excellent traditional Chinese culture have built a cultural subjectivity with distinctive Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化在“彼此契合”和“相互成就”中建构了独具中国特色的文化主体性。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in recent Chinese official discourse, referring to a nation's capacity for cultural self-confirmation and independent cultural development. It was emphasised in Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on culture.

The formula, part of the Two Integrations, that joins the basic principles of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping put it forward in 2021–2023, after the first integration with China's concrete realities.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

A body of ideas on cultural work formally articulated at the national conference on propaganda and ideological work in October 2023. It is treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: The cultural theory of "comprehensive innovation" and the Second Integration
zh: 文化“综合创新”论与“第二个结合”
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Zhang Yunyi asks how the twentieth-century Chinese theory of cultural "comprehensive innovation" (zonghe chuangxin) relates to the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism's basic principles with China's fine traditional culture. The article argues that this combination is the guiding thread running from the "comprehensive innovation" theory of Zhang Shenfu and Zhang Dainian to Fang Keli's later formula "Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western culture as function". Zhang opens by comparing the two Zhang brothers with the Song Neo-Confucians Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi, as Fang Keli had suggested.

The article is built in four parts. It first traces the intellectual sources of comprehensive innovation over roughly four centuries of Sino-Western encounter, from Xu Guangqi's "Chinese mould, Western material" through the "substance and function" debates of the late Qing. It then examines the contributions of Zhang Shenfu and Zhang Dainian. Next it follows the move from comprehensive innovation to Fang Keli's formula, and finally it shows how Fang's career-long commitment links these ideas to the Second Integration.

Zhang Yunyi's central claim is that "synthesis" in the two Zhangs' thought is not eclecticism. Zhang Shenfu's 1932 "three streams into one" (Lenin, Russell, Confucius) and Zhang Dainian's later formulation both place Marxist dialectical materialism as the backbone, and the article defends them against orthodox critics who called them idealist compromise. Fang's formula, the article argues, adds a "soul" to the traditional substance–function pair. It defends the formula against charges of redundancy and replies to critics by distinguishing the different senses of "function" for each element. Zhang cites Fang's statements that Marxism-Chinese tradition integration was his lifelong commitment, dating a 1984 formulation of the "two integrations" to Fang.

Zhang concludes that scholars such as the two Zhangs, Feng Qi and Fang Keli form a Marxist school that could be called the "comprehensive innovation school" or the "Second Integration school". The article notes that Xi Jinping's statements on the Two Integrations, such as Marxism as the "soul" and fine traditional culture as the "root", contain elements of Fang's formula. Read the original if you are interested in the intellectual genealogy of the Second Integration within Chinese philosophy and in debates over how Marxism, Chinese tradition and Western thought should be related.
quoteEn: Both the "Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western culture as function" theory and the "comprehensive innovation" theory run through with the theme of combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, that is, the "Second Integration".
quoteZh: “马魂中体西用”论与“综合创新”论都贯穿着马克思主义基本原理同中国优秀传统文化相结合即“第二个结合”的思想主题

glossary.explanation: The combination of the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the formulation Xi Jinping stressed in 2023, the first being the combination of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official formula for adapting Marxism to China: combining its basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.

A cultural theory developed by Zhang Daiian and Zhang Shenfu and later promoted by Fang Keli. It holds that a new Chinese culture should synthesise Marxism, Chinese tradition and Western culture, with Marxism as the guiding element.

glossary.pinyin: Mǎ hún Zhōng tǐ Xī yòng
glossary.en: Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western culture as function
glossary.literal: Marxism the soul, Chinese the substance, Western the function
glossary.explanation: Fang Keli's formula for relating Marxism, Chinese culture and Western culture: Marxism guides, Chinese culture is the main body, and Western culture serves as a useful resource. It adapts the older "Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application" model.

A pair of categories in Chinese philosophy distinguishing the fundamental essence (ti) of something from its practical application (yong). It was central to late-Qing debates on Chinese and Western learning.
Zhang Shenfu's 1930s idea of uniting the best of Lenin (Marxism), Russell (Western analytic philosophy) and Confucius (Chinese tradition) into a new philosophy.

t: Digest of theoretical and academic viewpoints in 2024: Marxist philosophy
zh: 2024年理论学术观点要览——马克思主义哲学篇
paras: This short review, published in Beijing Daily on 6 January 2025, surveys Chinese scholarship in Marxist philosophy during 2024. Sun Shoutao, deputy dean of the School of Marxism at Nankai University, groups the year's work around three themes: Xi Jinping's thought on culture, the theoretical system of the Chinese nation as a community, and a Chinese Marxist ecology.

The first section covers studies of Xi Jinping's cultural thought, which the review calls the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second covers efforts to build a theoretical system of the Chinese nation as a community, presented as a showcase of China's independent knowledge system. The third covers attempts to define "Chinese Marxist ecology".

On culture, one scholar holds that the core theory is cultural subjectivity. This scholar says it resolves the relationship between the "soul" (Marxism) and the "root" (traditional culture) through the Two Integrations. Another scholar stresses that "integration" is universal, arduous and creative. On the national community, scholars propose frameworks built on background, change, content and traits, or on an "ontology–consciousness–practice" cycle. A third scholar locates community consciousness in complementary interests, shared memory and cultural cohesion. On ecology, one study treats "Chinese Marxist ecology" as a root concept with reflective, normative and constructive derived concepts, forming a three-part logical framework.

The review reports these positions without criticism and does not name further gaps. It presents the year's research as consolidating Xi's cultural thought, the independent knowledge system and a Marxist ecology with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a compact map of the main 2024 themes and framings in officially oriented Chinese Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's cultural thought contains both a "how to see" — profoundly explaining the theory of socialist cultural construction with Chinese characteristics — and a "how to act", setting out "golden keys" for propaganda, ideological and cultural work in the new era in response to practical problems.
quoteZh: 习近平文化思想既有“怎么看”——深刻阐明中国特色社会主义文化建设的学理，又有“怎么干”——针对实际问题明确提出新时代宣传思想文化工作的“金钥匙”。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Xi Jinping's cultural thought is presented as one part of it.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second was added in 2021–2023.

glossary.en: the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept for the unity of China's ethnic groups as one national community. Its "consciousness" is promoted as a core aim of ethnic affairs work.
A slogan calling for Chinese-originated concepts and theories in the social sciences, rather than reliance on Western frameworks.

t: Overview of theoretical and academic viewpoints in 2024: economics
zh: 2024年理论学术观点要览——经济学篇
paras: This short review, first published in Beijing Daily on 6 January 2025, surveys the main themes in Chinese economics in 2024. Fang Mingyue and Nie Huihua report that new quality productive forces drew the most attention, followed by supply-chain resilience and climate policy.

The review is organised around three clusters of research. The first covers new quality productive forces under four dimensions: theoretical meaning, basic features, paths of realisation and measurement indicators. The second covers supply-chain resilience, digital technology and institutional opening-up. The third covers climate policy, climate risk and ESG (environmental, social and governance).

On new quality productive forces, the authors report that scholars see them as a new, high-level modern productive force, consistent with the new development philosophy and high-quality development, and as an innovation in Marxist economics. Proposed paths stress innovation, the socialist market economy, a modern industrial system and the Two Unwaverings. Measurement studies mostly use the entropy method and find fast growth but large regional gaps. In the supply-chain work, scholars find that digitalisation, especially artificial intelligence and cloud computing, and deeper trade agreements such as RCEP and CPTPP strengthen resilience. In the climate work, scholars find that policy uncertainty suppresses firms' productivity and investment, and that customers' ESG strengths encourage upstream green innovation.

The review draws no overall conclusion beyond the reported findings. It notes that many scholars place new quality productive forces within Chinese modernization, as the key to building a modern industrial system during a shift between old and new growth drivers. Read the original if you want a brief guide to the main topics and empirical findings in Chinese economics in 2024.
quoteEn: In the post-pandemic era, supply-chain resilience has become a popular topic in economics and management studies.
quoteZh: 在后疫情时代，供应链韧性成为经济学和管理学关注的热门话题。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, as opposed to traditional growth models.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out as a central Party goal since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official economic goal, introduced in 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
The Party's guiding approach to development, put forward in 2015. It stresses innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

t: Giving full play to the guiding role of military theory modernization
zh: 充分发挥军事理论现代化的先导作用
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 5 January 2025, this commentary responds to Xi Jinping's recent instruction to an all-army conference on military theory work. Xi stressed that military theory modernization is an important part of national defence and military modernization and plays a leading role in strengthening the armed forces. Tang and Peng argue that the military must therefore accelerate theoretical innovation to build a modern military theory system with Chinese characteristics that supports the centenary goal of the armed forces in 2027 and the aim of a world-class military.

The article has three parts. The first explains why military theory should lead practice, citing technological change, the security environment and the military's own goals. The second sets out how theory secures a winning edge and strategic initiative, including the place of theory among the four modernizations of national defence and the armed forces. The third turns to the principles and methods for raising the quality and efficiency of theoretical innovation.

Tang and Peng contend that scientific military theory works as combat power, because it reveals the laws of war and of military building and thereby shapes force development and use. They point to networked information systems, intelligent warfare in the Russia–Ukraine and Israel–Palestine conflicts, and intensifying great-power rivalry as reasons why theory must move first. Theory, they say, should concentrate on war and operations, directing training and force building towards preparing for and fighting wars, and should lead the deepening of defence and military reform. The authors insist that innovation must keep the political character of war in view, uphold the Party's absolute leadership over the military and apply Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military. They also call for emancipating the mind, integrating disciplines and military-civilian cooperation, and attention to artificial intelligence, quantum information and unmanned systems.

The authors add that methods must be modernized as well: research should move from reviewing past wars to "designing wars", using big data, cloud computing, AI tools, combat laboratories, modern wargaming and net assessment, and borrowing models from leading firms and think tanks. They call for stronger organisation, policy support and research capacity. Read the original if you want an official-academic view from China's National Defence University of how military theory is being tied to Xi's directives, technology trends and reform goals.
quoteEn: Without the modernization of methods and means, there can be no true modernization of theory.
quoteZh: 没有方法手段的现代化，就没有真正的理论现代化。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on military building associated with Xi Jinping, stressing the Party's absolute leadership over the armed forces and combat readiness. It is presented as the guiding theory for national defence and military development.

glossary.en: centenary goal of the armed forces
glossary.literal: goal of striving for the 100th anniversary of the founding of the army
glossary.explanation: The official target to reach specified military-modernization objectives by 2027, the 100th anniversary of the People's Liberation Army.
The official programme of modernizing the armed forces, which the article describes as comprising four elements: military theory, organisational forms, military personnel and weaponry.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng duì jūnduì de juéduì lǐngdǎo
glossary.en: the Party's absolute leadership over the military
glossary.explanation: An official principle that the armed forces are under the direct command of the Communist Party of China, and not of the state or other bodies.

t: An ethical path to building a responsible AI governance system
zh: 构建负责任人工智能治理体系的伦理路径
paras: Liu Jing, an associate professor of philosophy, takes up the ethical challenges raised by rapidly advancing artificial intelligence, especially generative AI. The article argues that "developing responsible AI", the idea set out in the 2019 governance principles issued by China's national specialised committee on new-generation AI governance, offers a workable ethical path. In Liu's view, the key is that humans remain the responsible agents for the AI they create.

This is a short newspaper commentary in applied ethics. It first describes how AI blurs the boundary between humans and machines and extends ethical relations to a new pair, "human and AI". It then sets out a human-centred ethical stance with three principles, and ends with three requirements for building a responsible governance system: global cooperation, a shared responsibility mechanism, and the cultivation of AI literacy and a sense of responsibility.

Liu identifies three moral dilemmas in the human–AI relationship. The dilemma of good and evil arises because AI is no longer a simple tool and can bring benefit or harm. The dilemma of dignity arises because over-reliance on AI may weaken human subjectivity. The dilemma of responsibility arises because AI's partial autonomous behaviour leaves a "responsibility gap" in traditional ethics. Liu answers with a human-centred stance, citing Xi Jinping's idea of "people-centred, AI for good", and with three principles: intelligence for good, dignity, and responsibility. Liu stresses that responsible AI does not mean building moral machines. It means humans taking responsibility, and that this stance is not strong anthropocentrism but treats the human being as an end. Governance, Liu adds, needs a responsibility mechanism that spreads accountability across governments, firms, industry and users. Liu describes the responsible agent as a joint human–machine unit and says everyone should see themselves as a responsible agent.

Liu concludes that institutions and mechanisms are not enough and that moral cultivation of the "heart" is needed, since this is what AI cannot replace. The article presents China's Global AI Governance Initiative as a Chinese approach grounded in a community with a shared future for mankind, and urges narrowing the "intelligence divide" between countries. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese philosophy scholar links Party-endorsed AI governance language to ethical concepts such as dignity, responsibility and human-as-end.
quoteEn: \"Responsible AI\" points chiefly to humans being responsible: humans must shoulder responsibility for the AI they have created and develop it responsibly so that it serves humanity better.
quoteZh: “负责任的人工智能”主要指向的是人类要负责任，人类要肩负起对其所创造的人工智能的责任，负责任地发展人工智能使其更好地为人类服务。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It calls for shared responsibility among countries in global affairs. The article applies it to AI governance.

glossary.pinyin: yǐ rén wéi běn, zhìnéng xiàng shàn
glossary.explanation: A formula attributed to Xi Jinping on AI development and governance. It also appears in China's Global AI Governance Initiative.

glossary.zh: 全球人工智能治理倡议
glossary.explanation: A 2023 Chinese proposal on international AI governance. The article cites it as China's contribution to global governance in this field.
A concept in the ethics of technology. It refers to the difficulty of assigning moral responsibility when an autonomous system causes harm and no human clearly controlled the outcome.

t: The people's city concept and its humanist radiance
st: Speech by Researcher Xu Jinjiang at the "Sihai Forum"
zh: 人民城市理念彰显人文主义光辉
zhSub: 徐锦江研究员在“思海论坛”的演讲
paras: This is a speech by Xu Jinjiang, a researcher at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, delivered at the "Sihai Forum" and published in Jiefang Daily (reposted December 2024). Xu argues that the concept of the "people's city" expresses the essential character of Chinese cities and answers the question of for whom, by whom and to whom a city belongs. In Xu's reading, it also carries a humanist outlook that can offer lessons for urban development worldwide.

Xu begins with the "right to the city" as formulated by Western progressive scholars such as Lefebvre and Harvey, and with a personal anecdote about a "ruin" that Shanghai residents would call a "heritage site". The speech then sets out two competing urban ideas, "physicalism" (xingtizhuyi) and humanism, and lists problems in Chinese urban construction. It closes with seven paired urban types, three dimensions of the people's city in the Chinese context, and three coming transitions.

Xu's central distinction is between physicalism, which prizes order, geometry and the aerial view (Haussmann, Le Corbusier, Brasília, Moses), and humanism, which prizes the street-level view, historical continuity and everyday life (Jane Jacobs, Ebenezer Howard, Lewis Mumford, Sharon Zukin, Doug Saunders, Qian Xuesen's "shan-shui city"). Xu holds that early reform-era enthusiasm for physicalism was understandable and produced real achievements, but led to uniform cities, fake heritage, developer dominance and the neglect of residents' dignity and belonging. Xu proposes that humanism be the main concern now, as the flesh and blood within the physical frame, with the two ideas ultimately fused. The paired types include tourist city versus resident city, "luminous city" versus "arrival city", and internet-celebrity city versus ordinary city. Xu cites Shanghai's 2024 government work report on affordable rental housing as an example of progress.

In the Chinese context Xu gives the people's city three meanings: creatively drawing on Chinese civilisational resources, combining urban renewal with whole-process people's democracy through co-construction, co-governance and sharing, and building evaluation indicators around residents' sense of presence, security, happiness, gain and belonging rather than only benchmarking against global cities. Xu foresees three transitions: from capital-driven to people's cities, from physical to humanist cities, and from physical to digital cities. Read the original if you want a Shanghai scholar's account of how Western urban theory (Jacobs, Le Corbusier, Lefebvre) is used to interpret the official people's city concept.
quoteEn: If physicalism is seen as a frame and a structure, then humanism is the sinews and the flesh and blood within that frame.
quoteZh: 如果把形体主义看作是一种框架和结构，那么人文主义就是这一框架内的筋脉和血肉。

glossary.explanation: An urban-governance concept associated with Xi Jinping's 2019 remarks in Shanghai that cities are built by the people and for the people. It is used to frame urban planning around residents' interests.
An official term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019 to describe China's democratic model as covering every stage of decision-making, not only elections.
Xu's label for an urban planning approach that stresses controlled physical form, order and the aerial view. The English rendering here is a gloss, not an established term.

t: Spiritual construction, cultural power, philosophical thinking
zh: 精神建设—文化力量—哲学思维
paras: Writing at the turn of 2025, Han Qingxiang describes the present as an age of rapid change, "time-space compression" and spiritual anxiety. The commentary argues that reflection on such an age should start from each individual's inner spiritual world. Han holds that cultural power speaks directly to that inner world and that philosophical thinking helps people resolve doubts, so both are urgent.

The piece raises four questions in turn. These are the relation between Chinese modernization and the individual's spiritual world; the link between consolidating the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation and the individual's own subjectivity; the balance between "liberating people" and "restraining people"; and the relative distinction between culture and civilization.

First, Han proposes a rule of construction "from the outside in". China's response to Western modernization moved from material objects to institutions to culture, and reform and opening up first stressed material wealth. Han argues that the new era turns to the inner emotional and spiritual world, citing Xi Jinping's statement that modernization is at root the modernization of human beings. Second, Han presents Chinese modernization as a move beyond Western-centrism, in which the contest between China and the West is a "contest of subjectivity". Han also notes the tension between national strength and individual pressure, and calls for stronger inner drive. Third, on governance, Han calls for unifying drive, balance and governance, and for reforms that people can actually feel. Fourth, Han defines culture as the premise of civilization, which sublimates it. Culture stresses "humanizing" externally, while civilization stresses inner cultivation and virtue. Knowledge without virtue, Han warns, leads to refined egoism.

Han concludes that one aim of Xi Jinping's cultural thought is to move from culture to civilization. It would build a cultural form of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization, and produce people who combine inner drive and innovative vitality with rule-abiding virtue. Han says that uniting these qualities requires philosophical thinking. Read the original if you want a short example of how a Central Party School scholar links Xi Jinping's cultural thought to individual psychology and governance.
quoteEn: Culture is the premise of civilization; civilization originates in culture yet also transcends it, and is a sublimation of culture.
quoteZh: 文化是文明的前提，文明源于文化，同时又超越文化，文明是对文化的升华。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of national development, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
A term stressed in recent Party discourse for the Chinese nation's capacity to define and develop its own culture independently. Han extends it to the subjectivity of each individual.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, formally set out in October 2023, covering cultural confidence, cultural construction and civilization.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase for the civilizational form that Chinese modernization is said to create, set against the Western model.

t: Building China's autonomous system of pedagogical knowledge requires the "Two Integrations" as its methodology
zh: 构建中国自主的教育学知识体系要以“两个结合”为方法论
paras: Gu Mingyuan, writing in Guangming Daily on 31 December 2024, argues that an autonomous Chinese system of pedagogical knowledge is an important part of the modernization of Chinese education. Drawing on the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, Gu contends that this system must take the Two Integrations as its methodology: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture.

The short piece sketches the history of Chinese pedagogy, which Gu says was imported from the West via Japan about 120 years ago. It then discusses the Party's educational policy, traditional educational ideas, and a tentative framework for organising the resulting concepts.

Gu argues that education has both an individual, developmental side and a social side. Western pedagogy from Comenius and Herbart, in Gu's account, dealt mainly with the former. Marxist-inspired Chinese educators such as Yang Xianjiang stressed education's social character, and Party statements from Mao Zedong's 1957 formulation to Xi Jinping's 2018 addition of labour education kept this unity. Gu treats the Party's educational policy as the "big concept" of the Chinese system, from which ideas such as "fostering virtue through education" and quality-oriented education derive. Traditional ideas such as teaching according to aptitude and "education without discrimination" are described as universal principles that should be reinterpreted through dialectical and historical materialism.

Gu proposes a provisional structure headed by the Party's educational policy, divided into macro-level knowledge (education as a foundation of national prosperity, balanced development, urban–rural integration) and micro-level knowledge (the "five educations", home–school–community cooperation, student-centredness). Concepts would be classified by nature, type and level, then used to form propositions with Chinese cultural and social features. Gu calls the idea rough and offers it for discussion. Read the original if you want a brief statement by a leading Chinese educationist on how the Two Integrations apply to pedagogy.
quoteEn: The wording of the educational policy has been revised several times, but its basic meaning has not changed greatly, reflecting the unity of education's individual-developmental and social character.
quoteZh: 教育方针表述几经修改，其基本内涵没有大的变化，体现了教育的本体性和社会性的统一性。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was stressed under Xi Jinping.
A guiding principle of Chinese education policy that makes moral cultivation the fundamental task of schooling.
An education approach promoted since the 1990s that stresses all-round development rather than exam results alone.
The combined aim of moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education, set out as the Party's educational policy.

t: Grasping several questions about the "Second Integration" fully
zh: 完整把握“第二个结合”的几个问题
paras: This short commentary, published in Beijing Daily and written as study notes on the Outline for Studying Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, asks how the Party's formula of the Two Integrations should be understood, with emphasis on the "Second Integration": combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Tao Wenzhao argues that it must be grasped as a whole. This means keeping four points in balance: the relation between the two integrations, the primacy of Marxism, the criterion of "fine" culture, and the orientation towards adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article proceeds through four headed sections. It first sets out how the Second Integration relates to the First, then examines the grammatical "subject" of the formula, which is the basic tenets of Marxism. It then discusses what counts as "fine" traditional culture, and finally explains the purposes of the integration. Tao cites Xi Jinping's speeches of July 2021 and June 2023 and Mao Zedong's remarks on not severing history.

Tao argues that the Two Integrations have operated objectively since the Party's founding, but that the traditional-culture side was previously treated as subordinate to the First Integration. Singling it out is, in Tao's view, a deepening of understanding and practice. The First Integration remains the foundation, since "concrete Chinese realities" already include traditional culture. Tao stresses that Marxism is the "soul" and traditional culture the "roots": over-praising tradition while neglecting or belittling Marxism is wrong. The formula refers to basic tenets, meaning stance, viewpoint and method, not every individual claim, which guards against dogmatism. Only the "fine" part of tradition qualifies, to be judged by historical materialism through its political stance (democratic and progressive versus feudal) and its fitness for social development. Tao rejects cultural revivalism and the "Confucianisation" of theory.

Tao concludes that the Second Integration serves two ends. One is adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, so that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era carries the best of Chinese culture. The other is building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, with traditional culture creatively transformed to serve that practice. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of how the Second Integration is to be understood and what limits are placed on the use of tradition.
quoteEn: The object of the "Second Integration" is "fine" traditional culture, not traditional culture in a general, undifferentiated sense, still less the dross within it.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”的对象是“优秀”传统文化，而不是一般的笼统的传统文化，更不是传统文化中的糟粕。

glossary.explanation: Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was elevated as a distinct proposition under Xi Jinping, notably in 2021 and 2023.
The combination of Marxism's basic tenets with fine traditional Chinese culture, first put forward by Xi Jinping in July 2021.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the ongoing project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.
The Party's official term for China's own path of modernisation, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Core official goal of national revival, to be achieved by the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Rebuilding the system of Marxist philosophy through contemporary practice and scholarly proposals
st: A dialogue between Yang Geng and Zhang Liang on "rereading Marx" and the Collected Works of Yang Geng
zh: 以当代实践和学术主张，重建马克思主义哲学体系
source: China Reading Weekly (Zhonghua dushu bao), posted on marxism.cass.cn 27 December 2024
paras: This is a dialogue between Nanjing University philosopher Zhang Liang and Beijing Normal University professor Yang Geng, prompted by the publication of the ten-volume Collected Works of Yang Geng. Its subject is Yang's long-running programme of "rereading Marx" and what it implies for rebuilding a system of Marxist philosophy. Yang's answer is that rereading must be driven by contemporary practice, remain anchored in a single objective Marx, and lead to a system unified around practice.

The conversation moves through Yang's motives after the Soviet collapse, his method, the relation between "Marx's philosophy" and "Marxist philosophy", and his main works. These include In Defence of Marx, Reconstruction in Crisis, and The Rise of the East, on Chinese modernization. It ends with Yang's work on the system of Marxist philosophy, collected in Volume 6, and with Yang's own account of what the Collected Works contains.

Zhang summarises Yang's method as reading Marx within "three wholes": the full history of modern Western philosophy, the full history of Marxist philosophy, and the full theoretical framework of Marxism, including political economy. Yang rejects the idea that "a thousand readers have a thousand Marxes". In Yang's view, Marx was a real historical figure whose thought rests on objective historical laws, so interpretations have a limit, like readings of Hamlet. Yang defines Marx's philosophy as the thought of Marx himself, and Marxist philosophy as that thought as developed by successors. He treats it as political philosophy, tied to practical critique and to the question of human life. He says Marx shifted philosophy's theme from "how is the world possible" to "how is human emancipation possible", with practice as its ontological basis.

Yang says his aim is a Marxist philosophical system, grounded in practice, in which practical materialism, dialectical materialism and historical materialism are integrated. He presents it as a response to contemporary practice, science and philosophy. He treats Chinese modernization as the central reality for Chinese philosophers, describing it as modernization, marketization and socialist reform compressed into one time and space. He admits that his own understanding is limited by his pre-understanding, and does not claim to have recovered Marx's "original face". Read the original if you want a first-hand account, from a leading Chinese Marxist philosopher, of how he understands rereading Marx, the objectivity of interpretation and the reconstruction of the philosophical system.
quoteEn: For us there is only one Marx, the Marx who was the principal founder of Marxism; and only one Marxism, the one founded by Marx that already has objective meaning.
quoteZh: 对于我们而言，只有一个马克思，那就是作为马克思主义主要创始人的马克思；只有一种马克思主义，那就是由马克思所创立、已经具有客观意义的马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 2020s. Yang uses it for a process combining modernization, marketization and socialist reform.
Yang Geng's signature scholarly proposal from the 1990s. It calls for returning to Marx's texts and historical context while starting from present-day practice.
A reading of Marx's philosophy that makes practice its foundation and starting point. Yang proposes integrating it with dialectical and historical materialism.
Marx and Engels's theory of history and society, which explains social development through material production and its laws.

t: Deeply understanding "Upholding the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation"
zh: 深刻理解“高扬中华民族的文化主体性”
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), December 2024
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in December 2024, sets out how to understand the call to "uphold the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation". Hao defines cultural subjectivity as a culture's capacity, when it meets foreign cultures, to be both self-reflective and self-respecting, and on that basis to adapt and create. The author argues that this subjectivity is a precondition for national rejuvenation and for a new form of human civilisation, and that the Two Integrations supply the method for strengthening it.

The piece is organised in three sections. The first links the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation to cultural subjectivity. The second ties cultural subjectivity to the creation of a "new form of human civilisation" through Chinese modernization. The third reads the Two Integrations as both an expression of and a route to cultural subjectivity. Throughout, Hao draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements, including his remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, and on the 2021 Party resolution on history.

Hao's first move is to treat attitude toward cultural tradition as the main test of whether cultural subjectivity exists. In this reading, without it the basis on which the Chinese nation is itself a nation would disappear, and rejuvenation could not be discussed. Second, the author describes Chinese modernization as one that continues an ancient civilisation rather than destroying it, grows from Chinese soil rather than copying others, and is renewal rather than rupture. It is contrasted with a "universal" modern civilisation that abandons cultural subjectivity. Third, the Two Integrations are said to be Chinese-centred ("putting ourselves first and drawing on others for our own use"). Hao holds that subjectivity and the Two Integrations reinforce each other, and that paths of rigidity or of abandoning the banner fail because they suffocate or give up subjectivity.

Hao concludes that "keeping to fundamental principles" and "innovating" must go together, and that building China's own knowledge system is the practical form this takes. The author calls for scholars to work under contemporary Chinese Marxism, address the questions of China, the world, the people and the times, and promote the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture. Hao also says that explaining the new form of civilisation abroad requires stressing "harmony without uniformity". Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship links cultural subjectivity, Chinese modernization and the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a modernization that continues an ancient civilisation, not one that destroys it; it grows out of the soil of China, and does not copy other countries; it is the result of civilisational renewal, not the product of civilisational rupture.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是赓续古老文明的现代化，而不是消灭古老文明的现代化；是从中华大地长出来的现代化，不是照搬照抄其他国家的现代化；是文明更新的结果，不是文明断裂的产物。

glossary.explanation: The capacity of a culture to maintain its own standpoint, self-awareness and creativity when meeting other cultures. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2023 in connection with the Party's cultural work.
The formula of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is a central slogan in Xi Jinping-era Party theory.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party goal of restoring China's national strength and standing after the "century of humiliation" that began in 1840.
A Party formulation, used since 2021, describing the civilisation that Chinese modernization is said to create. It is presented as an alternative to Western modernity.
A call, associated with Xi Jinping in 2022–2024, to build humanities and social science theory based on Chinese experience rather than Western concepts.

t: Several relationships that research on Chinese economic history should handle well
zh: 中国经济史研究应把握好几个关系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in December 2024, Wang Jue asks how the study of Chinese economic history should be conducted so that it serves the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Starting from a 2021 instruction by Xi Jinping on historical research, Wang argues that the field must be guided by historical materialism and must handle four relationships correctly.

The commentary first credits the discipline with recent progress in its disciplinary, academic and discourse systems, including new sources, more quantitative work and a growing research community. It then points to deviations in a field that straddles economics and history, and sets out the four relationships in turn.

Wang says some work replaces historical logic with mathematical economic logic, substitutes theoretical assumptions for real social contexts, or generalises from isolated micro-level data. The four relationships are: economic theory and historical practice, where economic history should be the source of economics rather than its offshoot; national and world history, which Wang says explains why Chinese modernization is both universal and distinctive; the Chinese Communist Party and Chinese modernization; and scholarship and future development. On the third, Wang holds that research on modern and contemporary periods should show why only Marxism and the Party could lead China's rise, and that this is the main thread through the sources and data.

Wang concludes that the field should adopt the Two Integrations, a global historical perspective and a contemporary Chinese standpoint, so that it shows its present value and tells China's part of the story of human civilisation. It should also draw on long-run and comparative history to offer practical lessons on economic transition, industrial upgrading and environmental protection. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-aligned scholars set methodological priorities for economic history in 2024.
quoteEn: Economic history should be the source of economics rather than its tributary, and it bears the important mission of giving economics a deep historical foundation and theoretical root.
quoteZh: 经济史更应当成为经济学的源，而不是流，承担着为经济学提供深厚历史底蕴和理论根基的重要使命。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Xi Jinping's formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since 2012.
Marxist theory of history that explains social change through material production and class relations; presented here as the required guide for historical research.

t: Adhering to a people-centred approach and continuing to improve and develop the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚持以人民为中心 继续完善和发展中国特色社会主义制度
paras: Writing after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Wan Guangxia asks how the plenum's overall goal of reform should be pursued: continuing to improve and develop the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernising national governance. The author's answer is that this must rest on the principle of putting the people at the centre. Institution-building should be for the people, rely on the people and have its results shared by the people.

This is a theoretical commentary for a newspaper audience, organised in three sections. Each ties the people-centred principle to one aspect of institutional development: its starting point, its fundamental purpose and its source of dynamism. Wan draws throughout on Marx and Engels's conception of the "real individual" and the historical materialist view of the masses, and on statements by Xi Jinping.

First, Wan argues that meeting the people's needs for a better life is the basic starting point. Drawing on Marx and Engels, the author treats the needs of real individuals as the value origin of historical development. Institutions should therefore be universal, foundational and a safety net, and should be balanced, coordinated and inclusive. Second, the fundamental purpose is the all-round development of the human being and common prosperity for all the people. Wan holds that this requires fairness and justice in institutions, which the author illustrates with the market economy, urban–rural integration, income distribution, cultural provision and the rule of law. Third, respect for the people's principal position and creative spirit is the source of dynamism. Wan calls for institutions that heed popular opinion ("when the people call, reform responds"), draw on grassroots innovation and strengthen people's capacity to take part in governance through self-management, self-service, self-education and self-supervision.

Wan concludes that improving socialist institutions through further reform means converting institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. The author presents this as helping production relations fit the productive forces and as supplying momentum and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization. The piece restates the official framing without introducing new empirical material. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists link the Third Plenum's reform agenda to the people-centred principle and to classical Marxist concepts of the individual and the masses.
quoteEn: Achieving the all-round development of the human being and common prosperity for all the people is the value goal of continuing to improve and develop the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 实现人的全面发展和全体人民共同富裕是继续完善和发展中国特色社会主义制度的价值旨归。

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义制度
glossary.en: the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The set of fundamental, basic and important institutions that Party documents associate with China's socialist path. The Third Plenum (2024) set the aim of continuing to improve and develop it.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It holds that development and reform should serve the people's interests and rely on them.
A goal of shared affluence, which Party texts describe as an essential requirement of socialism. Official statements say it means neither the wealth of a few nor egalitarian levelling.
The official name for China's path to modernisation, presented since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A reform goal first put forward at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to improving both institutions and the ability to carry them out.

t: The value implications of whole-process people's democracy and the guarantees of its effectiveness
zh: 全过程人民民主的价值意蕴与效能保障
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in December 2024, asks what values whole-process people's democracy carries and what secures its effectiveness. Luo Feng argues that the concept inherits the core value of the Marxist view of democracy and that China's institutional system supplies several guarantees for it.
