In their account, a firm and correct political direction is the core and essence of the Yan'an spirit, and Mao Zedong's wartime statements on it remain significant for the Party today.

The article reviews Mao's talks and writings from 1937 to 1939. It starts from his 1938 remarks at the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University and Shaanbei Public School, where the phrase first appeared as an educational requirement. It then follows later speeches to graduates and to young model workers, and his reports to the 1937 Party conference and the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee (1938). It closes by linking these texts to the present.

The authors make three moves. First, they report Mao's view that political direction is 'like a person's head', setting the course for everything else and for the link between individual effort and national destiny. Second, they stress that choosing the right direction is easier than holding to it. They cite those who left the Party or yielded to temptation, and Mao's use of the characters of Journey to the West to illustrate firmness of direction, hardship and flexibility. Third, they argue that firmness requires uniting the Party's maximum programme (socialism and communism) with its minimum programme. Mao's 'two essays' formula, democratic revolution first and socialism second, and his statement that a Marxist bears 'both the practical tasks of the present and the lofty ideals of the future', are presented as the basis of this unity. For the authors, the concrete direction in Yan'an was anti-imperialist, anti-feudal revolution and national liberation in the War of Resistance and later the war of liberation.

The authors conclude that the direction to uphold today is the lofty ideal of communism and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, together with advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. They cite Xi Jinping's call on cadres not to stray in political direction. Cadres, they say, must tie all their efforts and sacrifices to this direction. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-historical account of how Mao's Yan'an formulations on political direction are now used in official discourse on Party discipline and ideals.
quoteEn: A firm and correct political direction means not only choosing the correct direction but, even more, holding to it unswervingly.
quoteZh: 坚定正确的政治方向，既要选择正确的政治方向，更要对这样的政治方向做到坚定不移。

glossary.explanation: A term for the values the Party attributes to its Yan'an years (1935–1948), such as self-reliance, hard struggle and devotion to the people. It is regularly invoked in Party education.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official name for the Party's current theory, system and path, associated with reform and opening up.
The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, usually phrased as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Systematising and theorising the Party's innovative theory, and building China's independent knowledge system
zh: 党的创新理论体系化学理化与中国自主知识体系的构建
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 14 September 2024
paras: Pang Lisheng and Sun Anmin ask how China's independent knowledge system (zhongguo zizhu zhishi tixi) can be built, and what part the Party's innovative theory plays in that task. They argue that the theory both guides the project and supplies its substance. Building the system therefore requires pushing the theory towards systematisation and theorisation, with special attention to its principle-level content (yuanli xing neirong). The article draws on Xi Jinping's 2016, 2022 and 2023 statements on philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

The article has three parts. The first defines the independent knowledge system and names its three features: subjectivity, originality and systematicity. It then shows how the Party's theoretical achievements, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, guide and fill out that system. The second part treats systematisation and theorisation as methods of thought, and the third turns to excavating the theory's foundational principles.

The authors say the Party's theory expresses Chinese practice and experience and applies Marxist standpoint and method. They list concepts such as whole-process people's democracy and a community with a shared future for mankind as original contributions that belong in the knowledge system. In their view systematisation and theorisation reinforce each other and require thoroughgoing theoretical thinking. They take Marx's Capital, with its ascent from abstract categories to the concrete, as the model, and ground the work in the questions raised by Chinese modernization. The Two Integrations and the "six musts" are named as the guiding methods. The authors call principle-level results the "foundation and base" of the theoretical edifice, and take the Two Integrations as their example of a principle needing fuller explanation.

The authors call for research that goes back to the leaders' original writings, such as Xi Jinping: The Governance of China and the Selected Readings, to extract the principles, show how they connect and avoid fragmentation. They also want these principles read in a contemporary light, raised to the philosophical level, and placed within a "grand historical view". The aim is to show the stronger persuasive force of contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-theory journal links knowledge-system construction to the systematisation of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: If a theoretical system is likened to a grand edifice, then the foundation and base of that edifice are its principle-level theoretical achievements.
quoteZh: 如果把理论体系比喻为一座理论大厦的话，那么这座大厦的根基和底座就是原理性理论成果。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping stressed in 2022 as the ultimate aim of building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. It refers to concepts, theories and discourse generated from Chinese practice rather than borrowed from Western frameworks.
The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from the Western model.
The official description of China's democratic system, said to cover every stage of political life and not only elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, built on shared interests and common development.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six methodological principles set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and a global vision.

t: Adhering to a systems approach as the scientific methodology for further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 坚持系统观念是进一步全面深化改革的科学方法论
paras: Xin Xiangyang takes up the call in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to 'adhere to a systems approach' (xitong guannian) in further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. The article argues that this approach is both a theoretical and a practical requirement of comprehensively deepening reform, and that the Decision not only applies it but also enriches and develops it.

The article has three parts. The first grounds the systems approach in Marxist dialectics and in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and in the experience of reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second places the Decision's 'five major relationships' in a line of earlier Party formulations, from Mao Zedong's ten relationships to the twelve of Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao's overall planning. The third turns to methods for hard problems: balanced coordination (tongchou jiangu) and consistency assessment of macro policy.

In Xin's reading, the systems approach means analysing problems developmentally, as a whole, in their connections, comprehensively and dialectically. In practice, it requires coordination of reform plans, implementation and results across fields. The core of the second part is the five relationships: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. For each, Xin sets out how the Decision's measures try to hold both sides together, citing market-oriented reform of natural monopolies, the 'two increases' in income distribution, opening up alongside the goal of stable expectations, and risk-prevention mechanisms. In the third part, Xin presents the Decision's requirement to include non-economic policies in macro-policy consistency assessment as a safeguard. It is meant to catch policies that decay over the medium and long term, and to prevent the 'fallacy of composition', in which individually sound departmental policies work against each other.

Xin concludes that the systems approach matters greatly for a cause that has no completed state, and that it is needed to build coherent, mutually reinforcing reform measures as new dilemmas multiply. The article is an official-line exposition of the Plenum Decision's methodology rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of how Party theorists link the Decision's five relationships to earlier leaders' formulations and to Xi Jinping's methodology.
quoteEn: Adhering to a systems approach means that every sub-goal must be developed and realised around the overall goal.
quoteZh: 坚持系统观念,就要使分目标都围绕总目标展开和实现。

glossary.explanation: A methodological principle in Xi Jinping Thought that stresses viewing problems as interconnected wholes rather than in isolation. It was written into the Party's guiding principles for reform in the Decision of the Third Plenum (2024).
The official name for the Party's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: overall planning and taking all sides into account
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party method of planning several interests or tasks together rather than one at a time. Mao Zedong used it in 1956, and it was revived in the early 2000s.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Grasping the multiple implications of the Two Integrations
zh: 深刻把握“两个结合”的多重意蕴
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: This article by Wu Manyi and Yang Rongsuo asks what the Two Integrations (combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture) mean and why they matter. The authors argue that the two integrations carry ontological, historical-subjective, logical and value implications, and that together they are the Party's most important means of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They open from the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and Xi Jinping's remarks on cultural inheritance.

The article has four parts. The first treats the "first integration" as ontological; the second treats the "second integration" as expressing historical subjectivity. The third sets out the inner logic linking the two. The fourth examines their value in three dimensions, history, reality and civilisation, which the authors tie to Xi Jinping's "grand view of history", "grand view of practice" and "grand view of civilisation". Throughout, the authors trace a line from Mao Zedong Thought through to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

In the authors' account, the first integration is ontological because Marxism's universal worldview and method fit China's particular conditions. They hold that the integration forms a continuous historical whole and is an independent act of creation, not mere application or "external reflection". The second integration, they argue, roots Marxism in the cultural psychology and everyday values of the people, so that Marxism "speaks Chinese" and traditional culture is modernised. The first is the premise and foundation of the second, and the second deepens the first. Together they are characterised by four features: a truth-bearing origin, a practical basis, a law-like direction and a purposive aim.

The authors conclude that the Two Integrations are the Party's greatest asset. They credit them with deepening understanding of the laws of Party governance, socialist construction and human social development. They present the Two Integrations as a mark of the historical and cultural subjectivity of Xi Jinping and the Party, and as the basis of Chinese modernization and a "new form of human civilisation". They call for studying Xi's statements on the Two Integrations to grasp the core of his Thought and advance high-quality development. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned philosophical reading of the Two Integrations as presented in a Chinese Marxist-theory teaching journal.
quoteEn: The "first integration" and the "second integration" are two dialectically linked aspects of the process of theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: “第一个结合”与“第二个结合”是理论创新进程中辩证关联着的两个方面。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added prominently in Xi Jinping's 2023 formulations and was written into the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's continuing effort to apply Marxism to Chinese conditions and to current circumstances, producing new theory.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and presented as an alternative to Western models.
A phrase associated with Xi Jinping, describing a way of reading events within long historical stages and broad world conditions.

t: Five points of fit between the new development philosophy and the holistic approach to national security
zh: 把握新发展理念与总体国家安全观的五个“契合点”
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 18 December 2024
paras: Xie Bo takes up the relationship between two components of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: the new development philosophy, presented as the guide for economic work, and the holistic approach to national security, presented as the guide for security work. Xie argues that the five elements of the first (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) correspond closely to the substance of the second. Grasping these points of fit, the author says, is necessary for advancing high-quality development and a high level of security together, so that a new security pattern safeguards the new development pattern.

The piece is a short theoretical commentary of five sections, one for each element of the new development philosophy. Each pairs the element with a security counterpart and a shared orientation: innovation with institutional change, coordination with scientific overall planning, green development with ecological security, openness with common security, and sharing with the people's security. Xie draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements, the 20th Party Congress report (2022), and the Party's decisions on security and development.

Xie's central move is to show that each pair rests on a common orientation. Innovation and security reform both seek "change for the new". Coordination ("balanced, whole-system thinking") and the "holistic" in the security approach share a systems logic. The author traces how the Party has moved from stressing security (the "stand up" stage), to development ("grow rich"), to coordinating both ("grow strong"). Green development and ecological security both aim at harmony between humanity and nature. Openness is set against what Xie calls Western "zero-sum" thinking in trade, technology and security, contrasted with common security and the Global Security Initiative. Sharing and the people's security both put the people at the centre, as a stance Xie says is fundamental to the Party's governance.

Xie concludes that security is the precondition of development and development the guarantee of security, and that this dialectic explains the points of fit. As the country moves toward building a modernized socialist country and the second centenary goal, the author expects the two to become more closely bound. Xie calls for mastering this dialectic, giving equal weight to development and security, and deepening their integration, in order to support Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link economic and security doctrines in official discourse.
quoteEn: Security is the precondition of development, and development is the guarantee of security.
quoteZh: 安全是发展的前提，发展是安全的保障。

glossary.explanation: A framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 that names five principles for development: innovation, coordination, green, openness and sharing. It is presented officially as the guide for economic work.

glossary.en: the holistic approach to national security
glossary.explanation: A security doctrine announced by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats security as covering many fields (political, economic, ecological, cultural and others), at home and abroad, and stresses the people's security as its aim.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth defined by efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The Party's official term for its own path of modernization, described as including common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature, and distinguished from Western models.

t: The contemporary meaning of upholding the organic unity of political security, the people's security and the supremacy of national interests
zh: 坚持政治安全、人民安全、国家利益至上有机统一的时代意涵
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), posted 2024-12-18
paras: Xie Bo examines a formula that recurs in the national security discourse of the new era: upholding the organic unity of political security, the people's security and the supremacy of national interests. The article argues that this triad is a core element of the holistic view of national security. Political security is its foundation, the people's security its purpose and the supremacy of national interests its standard. Xie holds that the three are distinct in meaning yet inseparable, and must be understood together in order to modernize the national security system and capacity.

The article is organised in four sections. The first three take each element in turn, tracing how Xi Jinping and Party documents have framed it: the 2014 first meeting of the Central National Security Commission, the 2018 and 2020 formulations, the 19th Party Congress report (2017), the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and laws such as the 2015 National Security Law. The fourth section turns to method, setting out how the three should be coordinated in practice.

Xie's central move concerns the two ways each element is described, and the reordering of the triad. Up to 2019 the formula placed the people's security before political security; from 2020 it puts political security first. Xie reads this as showing political security to be the basic condition of the state's survival, especially the security of political power and the political system, but not as lowering the people's security. The people's security is described as the central value, since national security ultimately protects the people's interests. The supremacy of national interests is presented as governing the other two, because in the author's account China's state system makes national interests the 'greatest common divisor' of the people's interests.

On method, Xie calls for coordination guided by the holistic view of national security, for each element's function to be fully used, and for the three to be integrated in the modernization of the national security system and capacity. For political security this means upholding Party leadership and the Two Upholds; for the people's security, relying on and mobilising the people; for national interests, firmly defending core interests. Read the original if you want a close textual account of how official phrasing on political security, the people's security and national interests has evolved, and how a Chinese security scholar justifies their ordering.
quoteEn: Political security undoubtedly constitutes the 'lifeline' of national security in the new era; it has a decisive influence on national security in other fields and bears directly on the country's long-term stability and the rise, fall and survival of the nation.
quoteZh: 政治安全无疑构成新时代国家安全的“生命线”，对其他领域国家安全具有决定性影响，直接关系着国家长治久安和民族兴衰存亡。

glossary.en: the holistic view of national security
glossary.explanation: A security doctrine Xi Jinping introduced in April 2014. It treats security as spanning many fields, from politics and the economy to culture and technology, and links internal and external security.
In official usage, the security of state power, the political system and ideology, treated as the foundation of national security.

A Party formula, stressed since 2018, of upholding Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and upholding the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 国家安全体系和能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā ānquán tǐxì hé nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization of the national security system and capacity
glossary.explanation: A general requirement set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022), covering institutions, capabilities, public security governance and social governance.

t: A theoretical exposition of the Marxist view of literature and art in the new era
zh: 新时代马克思主义文艺观的学理阐释
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 17 December 2024
paras: Liu Qirui and Luan Yongyu set out the main elements of the Marxist view of literature and art as it has developed in the new era. They argue that the Party's literary theory, from Marx and Engels through Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping, has been renewed by combining Marxism with China's creative practice and its fine traditional culture. In their account this forms the literature-and-art chapter of Xi Jinping's thought on culture and offers fundamental guidance for the Party's cultural work.

The short article is organised in five sections. They treat literature and art as part of Chinese modernization, the Party's overall leadership, the people-centred orientation, the demand for outstanding works in building a culture-strong country, and the Chinese national spirit as a source of subject matter. Each section is supported mainly by quotations from Party leaders and the Party constitution.

The authors argue that modernization must coordinate material and spiritual civilization, so that literature and art nourish people's spiritual lives and help build a modern Chinese civilization. They hold that Party leadership is the basic political guarantee because contemporary Chinese art is both Marxist and socialist, and so must resist what they call bourgeois liberalization and decadent values. On the question "for whom", they follow Mao and Xi in treating the people as the source and beneficiary of art. As examples of work that combines depth of ideas, artistic craft and fine production, they cite television dramas such as The Age of Awakening and In the World.

The authors conclude that works should carry the Chinese spirit, rooted in patriotism and reform, through creative transformation of traditional culture and by telling China's story abroad. They present this as practising core socialist values and building an inclusive Chinese cultural landscape. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how current Party discourse links cultural policy to Chinese modernization and Party leadership.
quoteEn: Only when literature and art flourish can the Chinese nation truly stand tall among the nations of the world in spirit.
quoteZh: 文艺繁荣才能使中华民族从精神上真正屹立于世界民族之林。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, developed prominently under Xi Jinping since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses coordination of material and spiritual civilization.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought, formally presented in 2023. It covers ideology, cultural development, and the role of traditional culture and the arts.
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since 2012.

t: Returning to fundamentals and breaking new ground while keeping to principle: understanding the regularities of cultural construction with Chinese characteristics
zh: 正本清源、守正创新——中国特色社会主义文化建设规律性认识
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Beijing Daily, asks how the Party's understanding of cultural construction under socialism with Chinese characteristics developed after 2012. Tao and Yang argue that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has worked through "returning to fundamentals and keeping to principle while innovating", and that this practice reached a new level of understanding and was summed up in Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The article follows three stages. The first covers the period around the 18th Party Congress, when the authors say ideological problems and online disorder required correction. The second runs from the 19th Party Congress (2017) and its goal of building a socialist cultural power. The third begins with the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the systematic formulation of Xi Jinping's thought on culture in 2023.

In the first stage, the authors describe a situation marked by money worship, hedonism, extreme individualism and historical nihilism, and by officials with unclear political positions. They present Xi's August 2013 speech on propaganda and ideological work as setting direction, and list four measures: cultural confidence, firm leadership over ideological work, the core socialist values, and flourishing socialist literature and art. In the second stage they cite the "nine upholds" of 2018, the institutional arrangements of the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), the 2035 goal of a cultural power set by the Fifth Plenum (2020), and the Two Integrations. In the third stage they point to the June 2023 symposium on cultural heritage and the October 2023 national work conference, which formally set out Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

Tao and Yang conclude that this thought sums up the Party's practical experience of leading cultural construction, enriches Marxist cultural theory and forms the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They describe it as an open system that will keep developing with practice and as a roadmap and guide to action for the new cultural mission. Read the original if you want a concise official-style chronology of how Party discourse on culture is presented as moving from 2012 to 2023.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's thought on culture is a continuously unfolding, open system of thought, and it will certainly be enriched and developed as practice deepens.
quoteZh: 习近平文化思想是一个不断展开的、开放式的思想体系，必将随着实践深入不断丰富发展。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing the combination of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping put it forward at the Party's centenary in 2021.
The Party's term for confidence in China's own culture, added to confidence in the path, theory and system to form the "four-sphere confidence" (Xi Jinping, 2016).
A set of twelve values, grouped at national, social and individual levels, formally put forward at the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
The body of Xi's statements on culture, formally presented at the national work conference on propaganda, ideology and culture in October 2023 as the cultural part of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

t: Forming a governance pattern of government, market and society: giving full play to the strengths of the socialist market economy
st: Approaches from multiple directions
zh: 从多个方面入手，形成政府、市场、社会共同参与的治理格局——充分发挥社会主义市场经济体制优势
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Beijing Daily, takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its demand that the government's role be better exercised. Huang Yanfen and Yang Yiyong argue that the strengths of the socialist market economy lie in the organic unity of an effective market and a capable government. They conclude that this requires a governance pattern in which government, market and society all take part.

The piece first explains the plenum's guidance on improving the macroeconomic regulation system, exercising government functions fully and correctly, and optimising government structure. It then sets out eight areas of action, each following a duty the plenum assigns to government: macroeconomic stability, public services, fair competition, market regulation, market order, sustainable development, common prosperity and remedying market failure.

In the authors' account, scientific macroeconomic regulation uses fiscal, monetary and industrial policy to secure growth, stable prices, full employment and balance of payments. Government should handle economic regulation, market supervision, social management and public services, neither over-intervening nor leaving the market disordered. The authors also call for slimmer, better-coordinated government bodies and for a pattern of government leadership, social participation and shared governance.

For each of the eight areas the authors list concrete measures. These include prudent monetary policy and supply-side structural reform, equalised public services, fair competition review, anti-monopoly enforcement, big-data supervision, consumer protection, clean energy, income distribution reform and a rural–urban social security system. Their closing point is that such multi-sided work can advance high-quality development and all-round social progress. Read the original if you want a short, official-line checklist of how Chinese economists translate the plenum's government-role guidance into policy tasks.
quoteEn: The strengths of the socialist market economy are concentrated in the organic unity of an effective market and a capable government.
quoteZh: 社会主义市场经济体制优势集中体现在有效市场与有为政府的有机统一上。

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The economic system officially adopted in China in the early 1990s, combining the socialist system with market mechanisms. Official texts present it as a new type of economic system.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation in growth rather than speed alone.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all, including narrowing income, regional and urban–rural gaps.
A policy line introduced around 2015 that seeks to improve the quality and efficiency of the supply system, for example by cutting overcapacity and filling gaps.

t: Upholding and implementing the "Two Unwaverings" to pool strong forces for development
zh: 坚持和落实“两个毫不动摇”汇聚强大发展合力
paras: This theory-page commentary in Economic Daily (6 December 2024) asks how the Party's long-standing line on ownership should be carried out in the current period of strategic opportunity and risk. Yang Ming argues that the Two Unwaverings must be upheld and put into practice: consolidating and developing the public sector while encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. In Yang's account, both are important foundations of the socialist market economy and of Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first presents the Two Unwaverings as a major Party and state policy, drawing on Xi Jinping's statements and on the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to build a high-standard socialist market economy. The second sets out how state-owned capital and enterprises should strengthen their core functions. The third turns to the private economy and proposes measures in law, reform and confidence-building.

Yang's central move is to reject the view, which the author says has circulated in society, that the public and non-public sectors are opposed. The two are described as an organic unity that should complement each other, with equal access to production factors, fair competition and equal legal protection. For state-owned enterprises, Yang lists three functions: leading industry by concentrating state capital in national security, public services and emerging strategic industries; driving original innovation under the new system for mobilizing national resources; and strategic investment through patient capital that supports new quality productive forces. For the private economy, Yang calls for a law promoting it, lower market-entry barriers, and support for capable private firms to lead major technology projects. Yang also urges easier financing, regulation of fees and payment arrears, and restraint in administrative inspections.

Yang concludes that deepening reform should let the two forms of ownership develop together and open up wider prospects for Chinese modernization. The author stresses that the Two Unwaverings must show up in concrete reform measures that private firms can perceive, so as to strengthen their expectations and confidence. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Party theorists frame the relationship between state-owned and private capital after the Third Plenum of 2024.
quoteEn: The public and non-public sectors should complement and reinforce each other, rather than exclude and cancel each other out.
quoteZh: 公有制经济、非公有制经济应该相辅相成、相得益彰，而不是相互排斥、相互抵消。

glossary.explanation: A formula that the Party will unwaveringly consolidate and develop the public sector and unwaveringly encourage, support and guide the non-public sector. It has been repeated in Party documents since the 1990s and under Xi Jinping.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A concept promoted since 2023 that stresses technology-driven, innovation-led growth in advanced industries.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership playing a leading role.

glossary.en: new system for mobilizing national resources
glossary.explanation: An official term for coordinated state-led mobilization of resources for major scientific and technological goals, combined with market mechanisms.

t: A deeper understanding of developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 深刻认识因地制宜发展新质生产力
paras: Fan Hengshan, writing in the theory pages of Economic Daily (6 December 2024), asks how regions should develop new quality productive forces. The article starts from Xi Jinping's instruction to hold to high-quality development as the primary task and to develop these forces "in line with local conditions". Fan argues that this principle reflects an inherent link between productive-force development and regional territorial space. In Fan's account, each locality should choose which new industries, models and growth drivers to promote according to its own resource endowments, industrial base and research capacity.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out the meaning and features of new quality productive forces. The second lists five pairs of relationships that localities must handle. The third proposes five practical principles for local implementation. It is a policy-oriented piece that gives general guidance and does not discuss particular regions or cases.

In the first part, Fan defines new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces led by innovation, with high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality features. Their core marker is a large rise in total factor productivity, and their main driver is scientific and technological innovation. Fan stresses that "new" is never settled for good, that traditional industries can become carriers of new quality productive forces once technology is applied to them, and that no single industry has an exclusive claim. From this Fan draws two regional conclusions. Every region has reason and capacity to pursue them, but localities must avoid herd behaviour, bubbles and a single model. The five relationships are new and old, taking and forgoing, inheriting and borrowing, point and area, and speed and stability. A sixth pairing, hard and soft conditions, covers infrastructure and talent alongside the business environment. The five principles are perseverance, building the new before breaking the old, seeking the lead through distinctive strengths, committed innovation, and integrated regional coordination.

Fan concludes that localities should pursue differentiated development. Each should concentrate on its own strengths, transform traditional industries instead of discarding them, and advance steadily without building "on sand". Regions should also cooperate through industrial parks, "enclave economies" and the flow of resources across the country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official economic commentary turns the concept of new quality productive forces into guidance for local governments.
quoteEn: There is no "new" that is settled once and for all, only a "new" that keeps pace with the times and brings forth the new through the old.
quoteZh: 没有一劳永逸的“新”，只有与时偕行、推陈出新的“新”。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023. It describes an advanced form of productive forces driven by innovation, technological breakthroughs and industrial upgrading rather than traditional growth paths.
An official economic goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A long-standing Chinese policy principle that measures should fit the circumstances of each place. Here it is applied to regional industrial strategy.

t: Understanding the basic connotation of new quality productive forces
zh: 深入理解把握新质生产力的基本内涵
paras: This short theory-page commentary, published in Economic Daily in December 2024, asks how to grasp the basic connotation of new quality productive forces. Huang Zhibin starts from Xi Jinping's formulation and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) decision. In that wording, the basic connotation is the leap in labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimised combination. Huang argues that developing these forces requires both upgrading each element and improving how the elements are combined.

The article has two parts. The first sets out the new, higher demands placed on labourers, means of labour and objects of labour. The second turns to the institutional guarantees and driving forces for optimal combination and renewal, ending with a note on developing the forces in line with local conditions.

Huang describes new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces, led by innovation and in line with the new development philosophy, and as inherently green. Labourers therefore need knowledge of intelligent and green technology, to be cultivated through education and talent-system reform. Means of labour, mainly tools, should be upgraded or redesigned with intelligent technology. Objects of labour call for ecological protection, resource conservation and big-data use. Huang adds that mismatches between elements, such as surplus or scarce labourers, idle tools or hoarded materials, waste resources and lower efficiency. Because ownership, labour and distribution relations act back on productive forces, the author links combination to institutional reform.

Huang calls for deeper economic reform and for improving the basic socialist economic system, with stronger state and private firms. The article also urges better cooperation in science and technology, a unified national market, a modern enterprise system with the Chinese characteristics the author names, and income distribution that rewards factors including data. Regions should develop new industries selectively according to their resources and industrial base. Read the original if you want a compact, official-style statement of how the three labour elements and reform measures are tied together in new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces requires accelerating the green transformation of the development model, and speeding up green scientific and technological innovation and the spread and application of advanced green technologies.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力必须加快发展方式绿色转型，加快绿色科技创新和先进绿色技术推广应用

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and it is now central to official economic policy discourse.
The official guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, set out in 2015.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The 2024 plenary meeting of the Party's Central Committee, which adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The official term for the system combining public ownership as the mainstay with multiple forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the main mode, and the socialist market economy.

t: Scientific answers to major economic questions of theory and practice in the new era
zh: 新时代重大经济理论实践问题的科学回答
paras: This theory-page commentary, published in Economic Daily on 5 December 2024, asks how Xi Jinping's economic thought answers the major questions of the new era: for whom development is pursued, what kind of development is pursued, and how. Liu Shouying argues that this body of thought, grounded in practice and problem-orientation, supplies scientific answers while advancing Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Liu also claims that it innovates on and goes beyond traditional development economics.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the fundamental guarantee and standpoint of economic development: the Party's overall leadership and a people-centred approach. It then treats high-quality development as the primary task, covering the new development philosophy, the new development pattern and new quality productive forces. A third part addresses strategic planning, and a final part compares Xi's economic thought with post-war development economics.

Liu's core argument is that China's main social contradiction has shifted, so growth must move from "having enough" to "being good". High-quality development, in this account, means quality-first and efficiency-first growth, driven by reforms in quality, efficiency and momentum. It requires applying the five elements of the new development philosophy together and building a pattern centred on domestic circulation. New quality productive forces are presented as the engine, defined by innovation and a marked rise in total factor productivity. On strategy, Liu points to further comprehensive deepening of reform after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), to rural revitalization, coordinated regional development and people-centred urbanization, to a modern industrial system, and to balancing development with security.

Liu concludes that, unlike traditional development economics, which drew its prescriptions mainly from the experience of successful countries, Xi's economic thought generalises from China's concrete practice. It is said to answer both how a country escapes poverty and how it then builds a modern, strong state. Liu presents it as Chinese wisdom for humanity's path to modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how Chinese scholars frame Xi Jinping's economic thought and its claimed break with development economics.
quoteEn: High-quality development means shifting from "whether there is enough" to "whether it is good"; it is development that can well satisfy the people's growing needs for a better life.
quoteZh: 高质量发展，就是从“有没有”转向“好不好”，是能够很好满足人民日益增长的美好生活需要的发展

glossary.explanation: The economic component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, covering Party leadership of the economy, high-quality development and related policy principles.
The official goal, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from rapid growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation.
Five principles put forward in 2015: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A strategy, put forward in 2020, of making domestic circulation the mainstay while domestic and international circulations reinforce each other.

t: Grasping the specific content and deep grounds of the "people's need for a better life"
zh: 把握“人民美好生活需要”的具体内涵和深刻依据
paras: Han Xiping and Du Du take up the shift in China's principal social contradiction in the new era. It has moved from one between growing material and cultural needs and backward production to one between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. The authors argue that understanding what this "need for a better life" contains is essential to tackling that imbalance, and that the concept rests on firm theoretical and practical grounds.

The short piece has two parts. The first sets out the concept's specific content, covering material needs and spiritual needs. The second gives the grounds for meeting these needs: Marxism's value aims, the essence of socialism, and the original aspiration of the Communist Party of China.

On content, the authors say material needs form the base and must be richer and of higher quality, fairer in distribution, and reasonable. By reasonable they mean guarded against the false and luxury needs Marx criticised, and against hedonism and consumerism. Spiritual needs, they add, lift the whole and follow from human nature as both material and social. On grounds, they hold that meeting these needs is the stage-specific form of Marxism's goal of human emancipation and all-round development. They link it to Deng Xiaoping's and Xi Jinping's accounts of socialism's essence and common prosperity. They also say the Party's history is one of meeting the people's needs, now moving from \"having or not\" to \"how good\".

The authors conclude that satisfying the people's need for a better life runs through the whole cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics and unites lawful development with purposeful aims. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists justify this reformulation of the principal contradiction.
quoteEn: It can be said that the goal of meeting the people's need for a better life runs through the entire cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics and is an inevitable requirement of its practical development.
quoteZh: 可以说，人民美好生活需要的满足这一奋斗目标贯穿于中国特色社会主义事业始终，是中国特色社会主义实践发展的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official judgement of the central contradiction in Chinese society, which guides its priorities. The 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined it as the one between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.
A goal of shared affluence for all, presented as an essential requirement of socialism and stressed in Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, which the Party says adapts socialism to Chinese conditions.

t: The philosophical meaning and contemporary demands of emancipating the mind
zh: 解放思想的哲学意蕴和时代要求
paras: Writing in December 2024, Gao Haitao asks what "emancipating the mind" (jiefang sixiang) means philosophically and what it requires in the present. Gao argues that it is an essential demand of Marxist epistemology and that it must be pursued consciously to advance Chinese modernization and further comprehensively deepen reform.

The commentary has three parts. It first grounds the concept in dialectical materialism, then reviews the direction and principles of emancipating the mind during reform and opening up, and finally turns to the tasks of the new journey.

Gao defines emancipating the mind as shaking off outdated ideas and thinking patterns so that thought matches reality, which in essence means theoretical innovation. Drawing on the cycle of practice, cognition, renewed practice and renewed cognition, Gao says ideas lag behind a changing reality and become fetters unless adjusted. The obstacles are of two kinds: empiricism and dogmatism produce rigidity, while voluntarism and intuitionism produce thought that ignores objective laws. Gao says emancipation also demands the courage for self-criticism and the Party's self-reform. For the reform era, Gao stresses two principles: keeping to the right direction, meaning the Four Cardinal Principles together with reform, and putting the people at the centre, since the masses are the subject of practice.

Gao calls for following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), breaking down ideological and institutional obstacles, and turning the Party's innovative theory into concrete practice at every level. Emancipating the mind, Gao concludes, serves to unify thought and action under that theory. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated writers link the Marxist concept of emancipating the mind to the current reform agenda.
quoteEn: The essence of emancipating the mind is to carry out innovation in thought and theory.
quoteZh: 解放思想的实质是进行思想和理论创新。

glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Deng Xiaoping and the late-1970s turn to reform. It calls for dropping outdated ideas that obstruct policy change.
The official term for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 2020s as distinct from Western models.
Deng Xiaoping's formulation of 1979: the socialist path, the people's democratic dictatorship, Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself. Here it is applied to the courage to abandon outdated thinking.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform.

t: A luminous text interpreting the fundamental purpose of the Communist Party of China: marking the 80th anniversary of "Serve the People"
zh: 诠释中国共产党根本宗旨的光辉文献——纪念《为人民服务》发表80周年
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of Mao Zedong's speech "Serve the People" (1944), Wang Chuanli and Tang Mengxin argue that this text of under 800 characters remains the fullest statement of the Communist Party of China's fundamental purpose. Published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2024, the commentary holds that the phrase "serve the people" has become the motto of Chinese communists and a guide to their work for the people's happiness and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has four parts. It first traces the Marxist foundations of the text, then sets out how the purpose of wholeheartedly serving the people is to be put into practice. It next surveys generations of Party members presented as exemplars, from the revolutionary war years through socialist construction to the reform era. It ends with the policies of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

The central argument is that the text embodies three Marxist positions: a view of history in which the masses create history, a conception of the Party as a vanguard with no interests of its own, and the idea of officials as public servants and "attendants" of the people, drawn from Marx and Engels on the Paris Commune. From this the authors derive three practical requirements: selfless sacrifice, including of life; readiness to correct mistakes when criticised, illustrated by the acceptance of proposals from non-Party figures Li Dingming and Huang Yanpei; and tireless work. Exemplars cited include Zhang Side, Lei Feng, Wang Jinxi, Jiao Yulu, Li Suli and Kong Fansen. For the present, the authors say the purpose appears in the people-centred approach, in "the people first, life first" during disasters and epidemics, in poverty reduction, and in sharing the fruits of reform through investment in education, health care, employment and social security.

The authors conclude that serving the people has "a starting point but no end point" and has become the Party's spiritual gene, which will continue to guide the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Their account is commemorative and presents the Party's record largely in positive terms. Read the original if you want to see how Party theorists link Mao's 1944 speech to Marxist theory, to model figures from each period and to current policy language on people-centred development.
quoteEn: Wholeheartedly serving the people has only a starting point and no end point.
quoteZh: 全心全意为人民服务，只有起点，没有终点。

glossary.explanation: Title of a speech Mao Zedong gave in September 1944 in memory of the soldier Zhang Side. The phrase became the Party's best-known slogan and was written into its constitution in 1945.
The Party's constitution describes wholehearted service to the people as its fundamental purpose. It is the basic standard against which Party work is meant to be judged.
A term used in Chinese translations of Marx and Engels on the Paris Commune and later by Mao for officials. It presents them as servants of the people rather than rulers.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A principle of governance emphasised since the 18th Party Congress. It states that development should aim at the people's wellbeing and rely on the people.

t: Basic dimensions of building China's autonomous philosophical knowledge system
zh: 建构中国自主的哲学知识体系的基本维度
paras: Cheng Biao takes up the task of building an autonomous Chinese philosophical knowledge system, which the author treats as both a major theoretical question for philosophy and a practical question bearing on China's social development and the future of Chinese civilization. The short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in December 2024, argues that the task can be understood only through three dimensions: theory, practice and civilization.

The piece takes each dimension in turn. The theoretical dimension concerns the course of Chinese philosophical research since reform and opening up. The practical dimension concerns the experience of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The civilizational dimension concerns the continuous development of Chinese civilization.

On theory, Cheng says Chinese philosophy broke free of dogmatism in Marxist philosophy research, put the concept of practice at the centre, and posed the question of integrating Chinese, Western and Marxist philosophy within the effort to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The author concludes that the conditions for a subjective and original system are now in place. On practice, Cheng holds that the "two miracles" and Chinese modernization supply an empirical basis, and that this experience must be raised into theory. On civilization, the author describes Chinese civilization as continuous, innovative, unified, inclusive and peaceful, contrasts it with Western modern civilization led by capitalism, and says the system's core task is to distil the "living soul" of a new form of human civilization.

Cheng concludes that only by grasping all three dimensions can a subjective and original contemporary Chinese philosophy be built, laying a theoretical foundation for national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese academic and official discourse frames the project of an autonomous philosophical knowledge system.
quoteEn: The core task of building China's autonomous philosophical knowledge system is to distil the "living soul" of the new form of human civilization and to present a fresh picture of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 建构中国自主的哲学知识体系的核心任务就是为人类文明新形态凝练其“活的灵魂”，展现出中国式现代化的崭新图景。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official name for China's system and path since the reform era, combining Party leadership, a socialist market economy and other features.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.
Official shorthand for China's rapid economic growth and long-term social stability under Party leadership.

t: Building China's autonomous knowledge system of regional economics
zh: 建构中国自主的区域经济学知识体系
paras: Wei Houkai asks how China can build an autonomous knowledge system of regional economics, and argues that this rests on the distinctive features of Chinese regional economics itself. In his view, Western regional economic theory is built on assumptions drawn from developed market economies and cannot fully explain China. The piece, first published in Guangming Daily in October 2024, calls for stronger originality, innovation that builds on inheritance, and critical borrowing from abroad.

The article has three parts. It first sets out what makes Chinese regional economics distinctive, then explains what an autonomous knowledge system requires, and finally proposes routes for building it. Wei points to features of China's regional economy that he says are rooted in national conditions: the Party's overall leadership, the leading role of governments at all levels, the weight given to regional strategies, plans and policies, competition and cooperation between regions, and the influence of administrative divisions and informal institutions such as cultural tradition.

Wei names three defining features: guidance by Marxism, including the classical writers' ideas on balanced distribution of productive forces and urban–rural integration; conformity with the requirements of the socialist market economy; and fit with China's basic national conditions, including the primary stage of socialism. He holds that autonomy means using Chinese theory to answer Chinese questions, explain Chinese phenomena and guide Chinese practice. He says China has many original regional economic ideas, but they remain fused with practice and insufficiently theorised, which explains why no systematic, widely recognised system exists. Research should therefore start from current regional problems, explain phenomena such as rapid urbanization, city clusters and the dual-residence status of migrant workers, and guide future practice.

Wei proposes a structure in which original knowledge forms the core, with inheritance-based innovation and critical borrowing as two wings. He lists concepts that he sees as originating in Chinese practice, such as targeted poverty alleviation, rural revitalization, paired-up assistance and main functional zones, and urges that they be theorised. He also urges mining ancient thought, citing the economic zoning in the Records of the Grand Historian, and adapting Western methods such as econometric techniques. Read the original if you want a short statement of how a leading Chinese rural and regional economist frames the 'autonomous knowledge system' agenda for this discipline.
quoteEn: Autonomy means using Chinese theory to answer China's questions, explain China's phenomena and guide China's practice.
quoteZh: 所谓自主，就是要用中国的理论回答中国的问题，解释中国的现象，指导中国的实践。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in recent Chinese official discourse for a body of concepts and theories that is said to originate in Chinese practice rather than rely on Western frameworks. It is meant to underpin the discipline, academic and discourse systems.
The official Party assessment, formalised in the 1980s, that China is still in an early, long period of socialist development with relatively underdeveloped productive forces.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining a dominant public sector and distribution according to work with market mechanisms.
A poverty-reduction policy launched around 2013 that identifies poor households individually and directs tailored assistance to them.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to promote rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A Chinese policy practice in which designated developed regions provide financial, personnel and technical support to less developed or disaster-hit regions.

t: On building a high-standard socialist market economy system
zh: 论构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Li Yiping, writing in Guangming Daily after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), asks what the plenum's call to build a "high-standard" socialist market economy system means. The commentary argues that the phrase can be grasped only by tracing how the socialist market economy developed and by understanding its essential features.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews the history: Deng Xiaoping's affirmation that socialism and a market economy can be combined, the 14th Party Congress's goal of letting the market play a basic role in allocating resources under state macro-control, and the 14th Central Committee's third plenum decision. It then links the new task to high-quality development, Chinese modernization and new quality productive forces. The second part defines the "high standard", and the third lists four priorities.

Li argues that a high-standard system allocates resources more effectively. This requires better price and competition mechanisms, so that prices reflect scarcity and competition, including the elimination of backward producers, drives innovation. It also requires a correct handling of the government–market relationship, in which the government's "visible hand" obeys market laws and the system is both "lively" and "well-managed". Li holds that an unruly market leads to market failure, so regulation must be scientific and standardised.

Li names four priorities: protecting market actors through the Two Unwaverings; building a unified national market; improving basic market institutions such as property rights, information disclosure, market access, bankruptcy and the social credit system; and forming a higher-level government–market relationship in which the market plays the decisive role. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line account of how the 2024 plenum's market-economy goals are framed for a general readership.
quoteEn: The more coordinated the relationship between government and market, the more it is possible to be both "free enough to be lively" and "managed enough to be under control".
quoteZh: 政府与市场的关系越协调，就越能实现既“放得活”又“管得住”。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula committing to unwaveringly consolidate and develop the public sector and unwaveringly encourage, support and guide the non-public sector.
The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological innovation and advanced industries.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, of shifting from high-speed growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation.

t: Mao Zedong's contribution to creating a new form of human civilization and its contemporary implications
zh: 毛泽东对创造人类文明新形态的贡献及其当代启示
paras: He Xinyuan and Zuo Yujie ask what Mao Zedong contributed to the "new form of human civilization" that the Party's 2021 historical resolution says the Communist Party created through Chinese modernization. They argue that Mao's leadership supplied the theoretical, practical and value foundations for this civilization. In their account, it differs from traditional Chinese civilization, from capitalist civilization and from the Soviet socialist experience.

The article has three parts. The first describes the historic shift of Chinese civilization from "dust-covered" to "dust-removed" civilization. The second examines the foundations laid under Mao in five fields: the economy, democratic politics, culture, society and ecology. The third draws four lessons for the present and closes by citing Xi Jinping's remark that the best way to commemorate Mao is to carry his cause forward.

The authors argue that the founding of the Party, the founding of the People's Republic and the establishment of the socialist system together reversed the decline of Chinese civilization. They say each of the five fields corresponds to one component of the present "five-fold" coordinated development (material, political, cultural, social and ecological civilization). For the economy they cite socialist industrialization and give growth figures for 1952–78. For politics they point to people's democracy and the people's congress system, which they contrast with bourgeois democracy. They also discuss the culture policy of serving the people, welfare and social governance, and Mao's thinking on nature, which they present as a source of Xi Jinping's ecological thought.

From this history the authors draw four lessons. First, Party leadership and the socialist road are the root cause of the new civilization. Second, its novelty lies in its people-centred character, which they set against feudal, capitalist and late Soviet civilizations. Third, the Two Integrations, which they trace back to Mao's Sinification of Marxism and his "second integration", are the basic method. Fourth, the civilization points towards communism and the free and all-round development of every person. They conclude that the new civilization will need continuing Party-led exploration. Read the original if you want to see how Mao's era is being recast in current Party theory as a foundation for the new form of human civilization.
quoteEn: The "newness" of the new form of human civilization lies fundamentally in its being a civilization that truly regards the people as a living, concrete and immensely powerful historical subject.
quoteZh: 人类文明新形态之“新”根本在于其是真正将人民视为鲜活的、具体的、力量非凡的历史主体的文明

glossary.explanation: A formulation in the Party's 2021 historical resolution and in Xi Jinping's speeches. It describes the civilization said to result from Chinese modernization under Party leadership.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party leadership since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second element was added in Xi-era formulations.

t: The innovative development of the Marxist theory of productive forces in contemporary China
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论在当代中国的创新发展
paras: Zhang Yu asks how the Marxist theory of productive forces has been developed in contemporary China and where Xi Jinping's concept of new quality productive forces fits within it. The author argues that Xi's discussions of productive forces, culminating in this concept, raise the Party's understanding of how productive forces develop to a new level. Zhang calls it an original and foundational result of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy and a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The piece first appeared in Guangming Daily in October 2024.

The article opens with Lenin's view that social relations reduce to relations of production and these to the level of productive forces. It then moves through nine themes, each pairing classical statements by Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping with Xi's remarks. The themes are the productive-forces standard, the purpose of production, the components of productive forces, technological revolutions, scientific and technological innovation, ecology, industrial innovation, reform of production relations, and the nature of new quality productive forces. Each section ends with a statement of what Xi is said to have deepened.

Zhang's core move is to read Xi's statements as creative extensions of historical materialism. Productive forces remain the basic yardstick of social progress, and in socialism their purpose is people's growing need for a better life. In Zhang's account, new quality productive forces are defined by a leap in labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimal combination. They are driven by the information revolution, digital technology and artificial intelligence, with scientific and technological innovation as the core element. Zhang also presents the slogan that protecting the environment is protecting productive forces as the systematic form of Marx's idea of regulating the metabolism between humans and nature. In this reading, the socialist system and market economy together, along with deeper reform, must produce production relations suited to the new productive forces.

Zhang concludes that new quality productive forces are essentially advanced productive forces. The author gives four features: they arise from the new round of technological and industrial change; they are the advanced productive forces of the information, digital and intelligent era; they rest on a leap in the combination of production factors; and they are the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization and high-quality development. In Zhang's view, the Party's vanguard character depends on representing advanced productive forces. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line overview of how Chinese theorists trace new quality productive forces back to Marx, Lenin, Mao and Deng.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are essentially advanced productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力本质是先进生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–2024 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded production factors. It is a central theme of recent Chinese economic policy and theory.
The official name for China's path to modernization, formalised at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal since about 2017 that stresses innovation, efficiency, sustainability and welfare over pure growth in output.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for the present. It is used to frame new Party theory as a continuation of Marxism.

t: The 75 years since the founding of the People's Republic as a glorious chapter in the history of socialism
zh: 新中国成立以来的75年是社会主义发展史上的光辉篇章
paras: Writing in 2024 for the 75th anniversary of the People's Republic, Zhu Jiamu asks why these seven and a half decades should be seen as the most brilliant chapter in the history of world socialism. The author answers that, whether in periods of correct policy or of deviation, the whole history has revolved around what socialism is and how to build it, and has produced major achievements and regularities of experience.

The article opens with a short account of socialism from Marx and Lenin to the post-war socialist states and the Soviet and East European collapse. It then reviews achievements and lessons in five fields: the economy, politics, culture, society and ecology. Each is traced through the pre-reform period, the era of reform and opening up, and the new era after the 18th Party Congress (2012), with frequent quotation from Xi Jinping and from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Zhu's central claims are that socialism with Chinese characteristics remains socialism and that errors were part of exploration. On ownership, Zhu holds that although private firms supply most tax revenue, output and jobs, public ownership remains dominant because it keeps control over the commanding heights of the economy. On the Cultural Revolution, Zhu follows the 1981 Resolution in calling it wholly wrong while insisting that the period's socialist character and construction work cannot be denied. In culture, Zhu endorses tight Party leadership of ideology and the primacy of social over economic benefit. In politics, Zhu contrasts a Party whose officials may not hold private capital with capitalist systems in which money openly shapes policy.

Zhu concludes that the record shows socialism's superiority over capitalism, citing industrial output, poverty reduction, health, education and environmental figures, and that the Party's direction has been consistently firm and serious. The author admits that tasks remain, including gaps in social security and in advanced technology, but expects the cause to withstand any test under Xi Jinping's leadership. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned overview of how a senior Party historian assesses the PRC's record across economy, politics, culture, society and ecology, including its handling of the Cultural Revolution.
quoteEn: To judge whether a form of ownership is dominant, one should mainly look at whether it holds absolute control over the economy.
quoteZh: 判断某种所有制是否占主体，主要应当看它对经济是否拥有绝对的控制力。

glossary.explanation: The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, introducing market-oriented reforms and engagement with the world economy.

t: Mao Zedong's practical exploration of China's rural land question (1924–1949)
zh: 毛泽东关于中国农村土地问题的实践探索（1924—1949）
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 5
paras: Zhang Yong asks how Mao Zedong worked out policies on the peasant land question during the democratic revolution, when neither the classics of Marxism nor Lenin's writings offered a ready answer for a semi-colonial, semi-feudal country. The article argues that Mao combined the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete conditions. In Zhang's account, this produced a coherent set of lines, policies and principles that carried the revolution to victory and opened a new chapter in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article follows Mao's work in four periods: the Great Revolution (1924–27), the Second Revolutionary Civil War, the War of Resistance against Japan, and the War of Liberation. It then draws four lessons from the whole record. For each period Zhang examines the key texts and legislation, including the Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan, the Jinggangshan and Xingguo land laws, rent and interest reduction, the May Fourth Directive (1946) and the Outline Land Law of China (1947).

Zhang presents the land policy as a series of adjustments to changing class relations. Mao first made the peasantry, and especially poor peasants, central to the revolution. He then moved from confiscating landlords' land to rent and interest reduction in order to build the anti-Japanese united front. After 1945 he returned to land distribution, and corrected leftist excesses by relying on poor peasants, uniting with middle peasants and treating rich peasants and landlords differently. Zhang also covers Mao's investigations of rural conditions, such as the Xunwu survey, and his criticism of ultra-leftist Party leaders who attacked his approach as a "rich-peasant line".

Zhang draws four lessons: independence and self-reliance, the mass line, land legislation, and seeking truth from facts through investigation. The author maintains that the policies enriched Marxist theory on the peasant question and laid the foundation for land reform after 1949. Zhang adds that the history still offers a reference for today's issues concerning agriculture, rural areas and farmers. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-historiography account of how Mao's land policy developed from 1924 to 1949 and how Chinese scholars now frame its lessons.
quoteEn: The main problem of the Chinese revolution is the peasant problem, and the peasants' foremost problem is the land problem.
quoteZh: 中国革命的主要问题是农民问题，农民的首要问题是土地问题。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and developing it further. The article places Mao's land policy at the start of this process.

The Party's method of leadership, developed under Mao, which holds that policy should come from the masses and return to them, and that the masses must act on their own behalf. The article treats it as the key to solving the land question.
The Party's land policy during the War of Resistance (from 1937). It capped rents and interest while still requiring peasants to pay them, and so replaced the confiscation of landlords' land.
A principle of basing policy on investigation of actual conditions, associated with Mao and later widely used in Party discourse.

t: Deng Xiaoping's thought on historical self-confidence: formative conditions, content and contemporary value
zh: 邓小平历史自信思想的形成条件、丰富内涵与时代价值
paras: Zhang Yanguo asks what Deng Xiaoping meant by "historical self-confidence" and why it still matters. The article defines the term as a conviction a nation forms about its own history, resting on trust in, belonging to and pride in that history.
