It argues that Deng developed a coherent body of thought on the subject over a long revolutionary career. In Zhang's account, this body of thought is a distinctive part of Deng Xiaoping Theory and an original contribution to historical materialism.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the sources of Deng's thinking: historical materialism and the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times; the 5,000-year history of Chinese civilisation and its traditional culture; and Deng's own experience, including his classical schooling and his lifelong reading of historical works. The second part sets out the content of the thought. The third discusses its value in the new era.

Zhang's central claim is that Deng answered four linked questions: why historical self-confidence is needed, what to be confident about, how to sustain it, and what it is for. It is needed because China must follow its own path and rely on its own strength, and Zhang quotes Deng as saying that copying foreign models never succeeds. It has five objects: love of Chinese history and patriotism; excellent traditional culture; openness to the achievements of other civilisations; the hard-won results of the revolution and the Party's history; and a historicist, \"seeking truth from facts\" attitude to historical figures and errors, including the 1981 Resolution on Party history and the distinction between Mao Zedong's late mistakes and Mao Zedong Thought. Zhang also presents Deng as opposing historical nihilism and as insisting that history be taught to young people. Zhang says the thought contributes to historical materialism on stages of development, paths of development, and the link between China and world history.

Zhang concludes that Deng's thought supplies empirical grounds for further adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It also supplies spiritual resources for Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Zhang's view, the Four-sphere Confidence rests on historical self-confidence, which is why Deng's thought remains a source of renewal in the new era. Read the original if you want a Party-theoretical account of how Deng's views on history are used to ground present-day confidence in the socialist path.
quoteEn: The deep roots of the "Four Confidences" come from historical self-confidence.
quoteZh: 四个自信”的深厚根基来自历史自信

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese Party discourse for confidence in one's own national and Party history and in the path that history has produced. It has been stressed in official texts of the Xi Jinping era and is here traced back to Deng Xiaoping.
Official formula for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was set out in the early 2010s and is often used to frame Party ideology.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official description of the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for the present. It is presented as the main line of the Party's theoretical development.
The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted especially since 2021. Zhang notes that Deng already used the phrase "modernization of the Chinese type".

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
In official usage, a label for views seen as wholly negating China's history, the Party's history or the socialist era. Zhang treats it as the main opposite of historical self-confidence.

t: The principles and direction of the "Two Integrations" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, seen through Mao Zedong's philosophy
zh: 从毛泽东哲学透视马克思主义中国化“两个结合”的原则与走向
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxist Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2023 no. 4
paras: Xue Guangzhou asks how the Two Integrations, the combination of Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture, should be understood, applied and developed. Drawing on Mao Zedong's philosophy, the article argues that the Two Integrations are practical principles, not slogans. It holds that the combination must be led by Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method, and that it points towards a new Chinese philosophy.

The article opens by tracing the history of the phrase "adapting Marxism to the Chinese context" from Mao's 1938 report. It then proceeds in three parts. The first interprets the two sides of the combination: "China's concrete realities" and "fine traditional Chinese culture". The second sets out principles for each integration, together with tendencies to avoid. The third outlines the developmental path of Marxist philosophy in China.

Xue defines China's concrete realities by the principal contradiction and the nature of Chinese society at a given stage, and criticises neoliberal economics for rejecting China's existing economic base. On culture, the author follows Mao's formula of discarding dross and absorbing essence. Xue distinguishes traditional culture's "quintessence" (jinsui, a factual judgement of its core spirit) from its "essence" (jinghua, a value judgement), and proposes "zhong" (the mean or centre) as the quintessence. Five principles are given: take the essence and discard the dross; critical inheritance; make the past serve the present; let a hundred flowers bloom and a hundred schools contend; and, above all, hold to Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method. Xue warns against treating the Second Integration as a fusion of equals, against reducing cultural rejuvenation to a Confucian revival, and against reading Xi Jinping's thought on culture only as inheritance of tradition or of a Confucian orthodoxy.

Xue sets out a three-stage path: from the Sinification of Marxist philosophy, to a Sinified Marxist philosophy, to a Chinese Marxist philosophy, and finally to a "new Chinese philosophy". Such a philosophy would absorb the best of traditional Chinese thought and of human intellectual achievement while keeping Marxism's core. Xue credits Mao's philosophical thought with a pioneering contribution and says Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has opened a new era for the process. Read the original if you want a Mao-centred, philosophical account of how the Two Integrations should be understood, including its warnings against cultural revivalism and neoliberalism.
quoteEn: In combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities, the "concrete realities" refers to the specific conditions determined by the principal contradiction currently present in Chinese society and by that society's nature.
quoteZh: 马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合，其中所说的“中国具体实际”，指的是中国社会当下所存在的主要矛盾及其社会性质所决定的社会具体状况。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021: combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities, and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the older formula in recent years.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.pinyin: qǔ qí jīnghuá, qù qí zāopò
glossary.en: take the essence and discard the dross
glossary.literal: take its essence, remove its dregs
glossary.explanation: A principle for treating cultural heritage, associated with Mao Zedong. It calls for keeping what is judged beneficial and rejecting what is judged feudal or backward.

t: The theoretical content and contemporary value of the "Speech at the Forum on Literature and Art"
zh: 《在文艺工作座谈会上的讲话》的理论内涵与时代价值
paras: Marking a decade since Xi Jinping delivered his speech at the Forum on Literature and Art on 15 October 2014, Hong Jun asks what the text contributes theoretically and how it has shaped practice. The article argues that the speech is a major Marxist document on literature and art, comparable in standing to Mao Zedong's 1942 Yan'an Talks. In Hong's reading it consolidated Marxism's guiding position in the field, steered the development of literature and art, set out their mission in national rejuvenation, and was an early, important component of Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The article is organised in four sections followed by a conclusion. It covers the speech's theoretical innovation within Marxist literary theory, its problem-oriented guidance of literary and artistic work, its account of the mission of literature and art in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and Chinese modernization, and its place in the formation of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. Hong draws on works of recent fiction and television, Party policy documents issued after 2014, and classical Chinese literary theory.

Hong makes three main moves. First, the speech is said to ground its call for realism, a people-centred orientation and a critical stance towards Western modernist and postmodernist theory in historical materialism, and to treat 'the people' as concrete individuals, not an abstraction, by combining Engels with the Chinese min-ben tradition. Second, it diagnoses a lack of masterpieces, a decline in artists' morality, and works promoting historical nihilism, and the author credits it with prompting a revival of realist writing and stricter industry regulation. Third, Hong traces continuities with Xi's later cultural thought: the speech's demand that art be combined with excellent traditional culture is described as logically consistent with the 'second integration', and its stress on telling China's stories anticipates later statements on international communication. Hong also links the speech's view of art's social function to the Confucian 'esteem for culture' (shang wen) tradition.

Hong concludes that the speech marks an epoch-making stage in adapting Marxist literary theory to the Chinese context, and that it supplied Chinese thought and approaches to new problems such as the effects of technological revolution on artistic creation and the role of art in exchanges between civilizations. The author adds that it strengthened scholars' confidence and theoretical agency in international dialogue. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese Marxist literary theory presents Xi's 2014 speech and its relation to the Yan'an Talks and to Xi Jinping Thought on Culture.
quoteEn: The Speech is not only an important component of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture but also an important milestone in its formation.
quoteZh: 《讲话》不仅是习近平文化思想的重要组成部分，而且是其形成过程中的一个重要节点。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022), combining material and cultural-ethical advancement.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's 'Chinese Dream'.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought, formally articulated at the national conference on propaganda, ideology and culture in October 2023.
The traditional Chinese idea of the people as the foundation of the state, associated especially with Confucian political thought.
A Confucian-derived notion that rule should be achieved through culture, ritual and education rather than coercion; Hong treats it as a distinctive trait of Chinese civilization.

t: An analysis of Deng Xiaoping's thought on exercising historical initiative
zh: 邓小平发挥历史主动思想探析
paras: Chen Dacai takes up the concept of "historical initiative" (fahui lishi zhudong), which the Party has stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022), and asks how Deng Xiaoping understood and practised it. Written ahead of the 120th anniversary of Deng's birth, the article argues that Deng developed a systematic body of thought on the subject. In Chen's account, this thought laid the groundwork for the Party's call to strengthen historical initiative in the new era.

The article opens by tracing the idea from Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao Zedong to Deng. It then arranges Deng's thought in three parts: the meaning of initiative, the qualities required of the historical agent, and the practical path of action. Chen draws on Deng's speeches and conversations from the revolutionary years through the reform period, including his 1978 speeches, the 1981 historical resolution and his talks with foreign visitors.

Chen first argues that Deng read initiative as subjective activity, as strategic initiative (the power to shape the situation), and as something that must be continually fought for. Second, the author holds that Deng's own conduct showed historical consciousness, historical thinking (holistic, process-based and objective) and historical resolve. The last is expressed in the Four Cardinal Principles. Third, Chen presents Deng's practical path as three steps: focusing on the central question of the age ("what is socialism and how to build it"), respecting historical laws, and opening new horizons. Chen links these to the primary stage of socialism, Chinese-style modernization, a moderately prosperous society, the "three-step" strategy, and the policies of reform and opening up.

Chen concludes that Deng combined a static account of initiative (subjective activity and initiative as power) with a dynamic one (striving for it in practice). In Chen's view this gave the Party an intellectual, subjective and experiential basis for the new era. Chen ends by citing Xi Jinping's remark that Deng succeeded because he grasped the trends of the age and the laws of China's development, and by urging the Party to keep drawing on that wisdom. Read the original if you study Deng Xiaoping Theory, or want to see how Party scholars now trace the concept of historical initiative back to Deng and the classical Marxist writers.
quoteEn: Exercising historical initiative is in essence a practical question; at each stage of historical practice (emergence, development, innovation) it faces different tasks of posing, solving and breaking through the problem.
quoteZh: 发挥历史主动本质上是一个实践课题，在历史实践历经的生成、发展、创新各阶段面临着开题、解题和破题的不同任务。

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the initiative in history
glossary.explanation: A concept in Party discourse for consciously using subjective activity, on the basis of grasping historical laws, to shape the course of history. It was emphasised in the 2021 Party history resolution and at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Deng Xiaoping's 1979 formulation: keep to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
The official thesis, set out at the 13th Party Congress (1987), that China is and will long remain in an underdeveloped stage of socialism.
Deng used the phrase in 1979 for China's own path to the Four Modernizations. In its current official form it is rendered "Chinese modernization".
A term from traditional Chinese thought that Deng adopted around 1979 as a mid-term goal of modernization. It became a lasting Party target.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.

t: New quality productive forces as an integration of practical and theoretical innovation in the new era
zh: 新质生产力是新时代实践和理论创新的集成
paras: Writing in Theory Guide (Lilun daobao) in 2024, Gu Hailiang asks how the concept of new quality productive forces relates to China's economic practice and to its economics since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Gu argues that the concept is an integration of that practice and of theoretical innovation, and that it achieves what Engels called a 'revolution in the terminology' of a science, here Chinese economics. For Gu it also marks the theoretical level reached by Xi Jinping's economic thought.

The article opens with Engels on scientific terminology and Lenin on reducing production relations to the level of the productive forces. It then has three main sections. The first traces the concept to Xi Jinping's formulations on productive forces after 2012. The second places it within the new development philosophy, the new development stage and the new development pattern. The third links it to the modern economic system, high-quality development and Chinese modernization.

Gu identifies two 'theoretical cornerstones' in Xi's statements of 2014: 'unleashing and stimulating to the greatest extent the enormous potential of science and technology as the primary productive force', and achieving an 'overall leap' in the level of China's social productive forces. In Gu's account, the first deepens the thesis that science and technology are the primary productive force, and the second expresses a shift from quantitative growth to qualitative change. Gu argues that the five elements of the new development philosophy (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) give the new productive forces their basic features. The new development stage and pattern, Gu says, describe a partial qualitative change under way within rapid quantitative growth. Gu holds that the modern economic system and high-quality development require qualitative improvement in the productive forces themselves, and that the new productive forces are their precondition and driving force. Gu adds that the 2035 goals set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) are tied to this development. In Gu's account, change is visible in the three elements of the labour process: labourers, means of labour and objects of labour. Examples include digitally skilled workers, artificial intelligence and automated equipment, new materials and energy, and data as a new production factor.

Gu concludes that the sequence of concepts since 2012 runs from the new normal in the economy and supply-side structural reform to the new development philosophy, pattern and stage, the modern economic system, high-quality development and Chinese modernization. In Gu's reading, this sequence both describes the practice of the new era and constitutes theoretical innovation in China's autonomous knowledge system of economics. The concept of new quality productive forces integrates the two and shows 'Chinese wisdom and Chinese strength'. Read the original if you want to see how a leading Party-line economist places the concept within the sequence of Xi-era economic concepts and Marxist classics.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are the concentrated embodiment of the leap in the level of advanced productive forces in the new era.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是新时代先进生产力水平跃升的集中体现。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries. It is now central to official economic policy discourse.
The official body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought and as guiding economic work since 2012.
The framework of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, announced in 2015 as guidance for development planning.
A strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth built on efficiency, innovation and better quality.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

t: Several issues in the study of China's fine traditional culture that call for deeper reflection
zh: 中华优秀传统文化研究中需再深化思考的若干问题
paras: Since the Two Integrations were put forward, Chinese scholars have produced a wave of work on China's fine traditional culture, and Mei Rongzheng notes that disagreements have accompanied it. This 2024 article offers the author's own views on three contested areas: how the concept is defined, how the good is to be separated from the bad in ancient culture, and how traditional culture can be given 'creative transformation and innovative development'. Mei argues that all three need sharper Marxist methodology.

The article has three parts. The first sets out five 'is and is not' propositions on the concept of fine traditional culture. The second addresses scholars who reject using ancient culture, arguing for scientific discrimination between dross and essence, and draws on the experience of the Communist Party and Mao Zedong's method of analysis. The third turns to creative transformation and innovative development (the 'two creations') and proposes a method for achieving them.

On the concept, Mei holds that fine traditional culture is narrower than 'ancient Chinese culture'. It is the part with scientific, democratic, revolutionary and popular qualities, and it is a vast, integrative and historical concept. Mei rejects both historical nihilism and reactionary restorationism, such as the idea of 'Confucianising' China or the Party. On discrimination, Mei says the Party has used the people's standpoint and the practical standard of the new cultural mission, together with Mao's distinctions between slave-era, feudal-era and feudalist culture and between thinkers and the later accretions attached to them. On the 'two creations', Mei says they apply to fine traditional culture as much as to ancient culture generally, because grafting a non-Marxist heritage onto Marxism would produce eclecticism. Mei proposes Marx's method of scientific abstraction, which moves from the sensuous concrete to rational abstraction and back to the rational concrete. In this reading, Confucian concepts are stripped of their feudal social basis and then filled with the content of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

Mei concludes that scientific abstraction is the effective route to the 'two creations', and that it should be combined with other methods, including the logical-historical method, critical inheritance and class analysis. Mei adds that applying it to traditional culture is a new task needing careful study and not simplification. Read the original if you want a detailed Marxist-methodological account, from a Wuhan University Marxist theorist, of how Chinese scholars debate the Second Integration of Marxism with traditional culture.
quoteEn: Simply grafting non-Marxism onto Marxism can only produce eclecticism, not Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 非马克思主义和马克思主义的简单嫁接只能出折中主义，不能出中国化时代化的马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: The official term for the parts of China's ancient cultural heritage judged valuable for the present. Mei defines it as the portion with scientific, democratic, revolutionary and popular qualities.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second).
A slogan calling for traditional culture to be creatively transformed and innovatively developed so that it fits contemporary needs. The article abbreviates it as the 'two creations'.

In official Chinese discourse, a label for views that are said to deny or denigrate the historical record of China, its revolution or its traditions. Mei applies it to those who would discard the whole feudal-era cultural legacy.

t: Integrating the "Two Establishes" into the soul and turning them into action
zh: 把“两个确立”融入灵魂化为行动
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo jijian jiancha bao), 10 October 2024
paras: This piece, published in the discipline-inspection newspaper in October 2024, is a review and study guide for a training textbook, Deeply Grasping the Decisive Significance of the "Two Establishes". The book is one of the sixth batch of national cadre training textbooks. Qu Qingshan argues that it explains systematically how to understand the Two Establishes and helps Party members and cadres turn this political consensus into practical action in support of the Two Upholds.

Qu first summarises the book's account of the Two Establishes through three logics: theoretical, historical and practical. He then lists four features of the book: political character, intellectual depth, practical guidance and readability. The last part draws on the book's fourth chapter and conclusion to set out what cadres should do in practice.

Qu reports that the book treats the Two Establishes as a basic political principle of Marxist parties, drawing on historical materialism and Marxist party-building doctrine. It presents them as the distilled core of the Party's century of experience, in which the Party's cause advanced when the authority of the Central Committee and a guiding theory were upheld, and suffered when they weakened. It also presents them as the most important political outcome of the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Qu praises the book for tying these claims to the Party's current tasks and for using plain language, illustrations and QR-code links to reach cadres.

Qu concludes that, amid what he calls great changes unseen in a century, cadres should study the book in order to take their practical lessons. He calls for reinforcing ideals and convictions through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and for improving political capacity so that the Two Upholds are carried out. He also calls for a stronger fighting spirit, broad unity, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, including sustained anti-corruption work. Read the original if you want to see how a senior Party historian presents the Two Establishes in official cadre-education literature, and how the textbook is promoted to its audience.
quoteEn: The "Two Establishes" are the most important political achievement the Party has made in the new era.
quoteZh: “两个确立”是党在新时代取得的最重大政治成果。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution: establishing Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and establishing the guiding position of Xi Jinping Thought. Official texts describe it as decisive for the Party and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership. Official texts call it the Party's highest political principle.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the programme of strict Party discipline, organisational building and anti-corruption work promoted since 2012.

t: Grasping the "Second Integration" by systematising and theorising Xi Jinping's thought on culture
zh: 以体系化学理化为着力点深刻把握“第二个结合”
paras: Wang Weiguang, writing in the People's Daily in October 2024, asks how students of Xi Jinping's thought on culture can best grasp its central innovation, the "Second Integration": combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Wang argues that this should be done by treating the thought as a systematic, logically tight theoretical system and by handling three relationships correctly: upholding fundamental principles and innovating, the "soul-line" and the "root-line", and "substance" and "application".

The commentary opens by presenting the Second Integration as the necessary path for upholding and developing socialist culture with Chinese characteristics. It then has three main sections, each taking one of the three relationships. A short closing passage returns to the practical side of the thought, in which Wang says theory and implementation are linked.

In the first section Wang claims that the Second Integration enriches Marxist cultural theory, meets a requirement of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and is internally required for cultural flourishing. The core argument concerns the three relationships. Upholding fundamental principles is the premise and innovation the driving force. Wang holds that the Party's cultural leadership and the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity must be kept, while Marxism is used to revitalise living elements of tradition and give them new meaning. Marxism is the "soul-line" and traditional culture the "root-line", and neither may be abandoned. Marxism is the standard for separating the essence of tradition from its dross, and Wang presents this as the way to resolve the old dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western, and so consolidate cultural subjectivity. Finally, Wang says the thought joins "substance" (epistemology, what the Second Integration is) with "application" (methodology, how to carry it out), which Wang describes as a clear blueprint for building a country strong in socialist culture.

Wang concludes that deepening the Second Integration on the new journey requires being guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture and combining learning with thinking, application and action. The aim, in Wang's account, is a better fit between Marxism's basic principles and traditional culture and a new phase in propaganda, ideological and cultural work. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official line presents the Second Integration and the logic linking it to cultural subjectivity, in the words of a senior scholar writing in the Party's main newspaper.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles is the premise; innovation is the driving force.
quoteZh: 守正是前提，创新是动力。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. It is paired with the first integration, of Marxism with China's concrete realities, and was stressed from 2023.
The body of Xi's statements on culture, ideology and propaganda work, formally presented as a distinct theoretical system in October 2023.
Xi's term for Marxism as the spiritual lifeline of the Party's theory, which he says must never be abandoned.
Xi's term for China's fine traditional culture as the nation's cultural roots, paired with the soul-line.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's long-running project of fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to each era.
A concept in Xi's cultural thought: a nation's firm cultural self-identity, which the Party presents as the base of cultural confidence and of exchange with other civilisations.

t: Methods for interpreting the further comprehensively deepening of reform
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的阐释方法
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 9
paras: Chen Jinlong asks how the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) narrates and explains the task of further comprehensively deepening reform, and which interpretive methods its Decision uses. The article argues that the Decision builds its account on four bases: the achievements and experience of reform, a problem-oriented stance, the theme of Chinese modernization, and dialectical and historical materialism. Together, Chen says, these give the reform agenda historical, practical and philosophical support and strengthen its explanatory and persuasive force.

The article has four main sections, one for each method. It first traces reform from partial reform to comprehensive deepening and reads the Decision against that history. It then links the Decision's fourteen task areas to the "three confrontations": a complex international and domestic situation, a new round of technological and industrial revolution, and the people's new expectations. A third section follows the idea of modernization from the Four Modernizations of the 1950s and 1960s to the present. The last section examines the philosophical content of the document.

Chen holds that the "six adherences" distilled from reform experience (the Party's overall leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, institution-building as the main thread, law-based governance, and systems thinking) are both principles and methods. In Chen's reading, the Decision's specific institutional proposals, from data property rights to AI safety supervision, put these principles into practice. The article presents the relation between reform and Chinese modernization as reciprocal: reform supplies momentum and institutional guarantees, while modernization determines reform's content. It finds dialectics in the handling of paired relations such as government and market or efficiency and fairness, and in the formula of "establishing before breaking". It also finds historical materialism in the stress on economic reform as the lead, on the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, and on the people as the main force of history.

Chen concludes that the Plenum's method of interpretation has wider methodological value. Explaining a present problem should start from history and experience, keep a clear problem orientation, state its goals, and rest on dialectical and historical materialism. The article is a supportive reading of an official document, not a critical assessment. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how the Third Plenum's Decision is framed and justified, and of how its official narrative logic is explained.
quoteEn: The Third Plenum's systematic plan for further comprehensively deepening reform is organised around the theme of Chinese modernization, and is a concrete application of thematic thinking.
quoteZh: 党的二十届三中全会对进一步全面深化改革的系统部署，是围绕中国式现代化这一主题展开的，是主题思维的具体运用。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist modernization with Chinese characteristics, distinct from the Western model.

The reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024. It builds on the "comprehensively deepening reform" launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013).

The six lessons of reform experience listed in the 2024 Decision: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, institution-building, law-based governance and systems thinking. They also serve as the principles of further reform.

t: Deng Xiaoping: a model of seeking truth from facts
zh: 邓小平：实事求是的典范
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2024 no. 4
paras: Written for the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, this article argues that seeking truth from facts (shishi qiushi) is the thread running through Deng's two great historical contributions. Yang Chungui identifies these as leading the Party's assessment of its history and of Mao Zedong's place and Mao Zedong Thought, and creating Deng Xiaoping Theory and opening the path of building socialism with Chinese characteristics through reform and opening up. Yang holds that revisiting Deng's scientific attitude, creative spirit and courage is of major practical relevance for the new journey.

The article is organised in six parts. It covers Deng's role in re-establishing the ideological line after 1976, his guidance of the 1981 Resolution on Party history, and his grounding of socialism with Chinese characteristics in national conditions. It then treats his stress on practice and the masses in reform and opening up, his insistence on dialectics and on "grasping with both hands", and his preference for practical results over formalism. Yang draws throughout on Deng's speeches from 1977 to the 1992 southern tour.

Yang first presents Deng as the first leading figure to oppose the "Two Whatevers" before his return to work, and as a supporter of the discussion on practice as the sole criterion of truth. The same principle, Yang argues, shaped the Resolution's verdict that Mao's merits were primary and his errors secondary, and its rejection of both wholesale repudiation and dogmatic worship. Yang then argues that Deng rejected a fixed Soviet-style model and derived policy from the primary stage of socialism. On reform, Deng is shown relying on practice and popular initiative: the "three benefits" test replaced abstract arguments over whether something was capitalist or socialist, and rural reforms are credited to peasants and grassroots innovation.

Yang adds that Deng's method combined "two-point" dialectical thinking with practical, anti-formalist habits, citing his criticism of excessive meetings and long speeches in 1992. Yang concludes that Deng regarded seeking truth from facts as the basis of Marxism and the key to past and future success. The article calls on readers to study this quality and to uphold emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, keeping pace with the times and being pragmatic in advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Party-school account of how Deng's key sayings and speeches are used to frame his legacy and the 1981 Resolution.
quoteEn: the ideological line of seeking truth from facts
quoteZh: 实事求是的思想路线

glossary.explanation: A phrase taken from classical Chinese and adopted by Mao Zedong as a core principle of the Party's ideological line. After 1978 it became the slogan for Deng Xiaoping's pragmatic approach.
A 1977 formula holding that whatever policy decisions Mao made and whatever instructions he gave must be upheld. Deng and reformers criticised it as an obstacle to correcting past errors.
The official judgement that China is in an underdeveloped initial phase of socialism, which is meant to determine policy for a long historical period.
Deng's 1992 criteria for judging reforms: whether they promote productive forces, raise national strength and improve living standards.
The official term for China's path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Firm cultural confidence and the new mission of social science workers in the new era
zh: 坚定文化自信与社会科学工作者的时代新命
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), posted 28 November 2024
paras: Gao Dongxin, writing in China Social Sciences Today, takes up Xi Jinping's 2016 statement that confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics ultimately rests on cultural confidence. The commentary argues that eight years of practice show this judgment has enriched the theory of socialist culture, laid a scholarly foundation for Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and given momentum to Chinese modernization. Its answer to what social scientists should now do is that they must take on the task of strengthening cultural confidence.

The piece is organised in four parts. It first explains why firm cultural confidence matters in historical, practical and material terms. It then sets out what cultural confidence means, along horizontal and vertical dimensions. The third part builds its theoretical foundation on the "five outstanding characteristics" of Chinese civilisation and on traditional humanistic values. The last part lists five duties for social science workers.

Gao argues that cultural confidence helps the nation recover from the cultural inferiority of the modern period and break with "Western-centrism". In Gao's account it is also an inner force for renewing tradition, and a defence against the "erosion" of Western culture and values. At its core is confidence in core values. Gao draws on Xi's formulation of the five characteristics: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. Gao holds that Chinese culture has repeatedly absorbed foreign influences without losing its roots, and that ideas such as harmony between humanity and nature, benevolence, and valuing righteousness over profit can help address global problems.

For social scientists, Gao proposes five tasks: hold to a firm political direction guided by Marxism; strengthen theoretical consciousness and problem orientation; lead with innovation, following the Two Integrations; adopt a people-centred stance; and tell China's story well as interpreters and communicators of excellent traditional culture. Gao presents these as obligations flowing from Xi's directives. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a local Party-affiliated academy head restates official cultural-confidence discourse and the duties it assigns to social scientists.
quoteEn: The core of culture is values, and the essence of cultural confidence is confidence in values.
quoteZh: 文化的核心是价值观，文化自信的本质就是价值观自信。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping from 2016, referring to confidence in China's own cultural heritage, socialist culture and values. It is presented as the deepest basis of confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally highlighted by the Party in 2023. It covers the role of culture in governance, traditional culture and ideology.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
The principle of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's excellent traditional culture. It is a formula associated with Xi Jinping.

t: Building an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences through adhering to the Two Integrations
zh: 在坚持“两个结合”中构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in October 2024, Zhang Zhengwen takes up the call in the Third Plenum Decision of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to build an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences. Zhang argues that adhering to the Two Integrations (combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture) provides the methodological guidance and the fundamental route for this task.

The commentary has three parts. The first explains why the Two Integrations are the fundamental route, the second identifies where to apply effort, and the third lists the supports needed. It draws throughout on statements by Xi Jinping and on the Party's century-long record of theoretical innovation.

Zhang reads the two integrations as two anchors. Integration with concrete realities supplies the logical starting point: knowledge should be drawn from the practice of reform and development and answer China's problems. Integration with traditional culture is described as keeping the "soul" and the "root". Marxism, above all Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is the soul; the scholarly traditions from pre-Qin philosophers to Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism are the root. The author then names three practical levers: the discipline system (including support for fields such as oracle-bone studies and Dunhuang studies), the academic system, and the discourse system. On discourse, Zhang calls for popularising academic language, internationalising Chinese discourse and shedding reliance on Western discourse.

Zhang concludes that the knowledge system must unite the three systems and be consolidated in textbook development, which is to be treated as a matter of state authority and political direction. It is described as a systemic project requiring stronger Party leadership, ideological platforms, integration of Marxist, traditional and useful foreign resources, and cultivation of talent and cross-disciplinary work. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official line links the Two Integrations to disciplinary, academic and discourse construction and to textbook policy.
quoteEn: In building an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences, we must never abandon Marxism, the soul of the system; we must uphold and consolidate Marxism's guiding position, and above all the guiding position of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
quoteZh: 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系，决不能抛弃马克思主义这个魂脉，必须坚持和巩固马克思主义指导地位，最重要的是坚持和巩固习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想指导地位。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added prominently in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 statements.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
Xi Jinping's term (2022) for a body of concepts and theories originating in China rather than derived from Western frameworks.

t: The evolutionary logic, value implications and basic principles of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era
zh: 新时代全面深化改革的演进逻辑、价值意蕴及基本原则
paras: Written in the wake of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), this article asks why comprehensively deepening reform should be given greater prominence and how it should be pursued around Chinese modernization. Chen Mingfan and Xiao Yao argue that reform in the new era is a continuation of the reform agenda set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and a new chapter in advancing Chinese modernization. They present reform as a "key move" and an important instrument for that project.

The article has three parts. The first traces the evolutionary logic of reform through theoretical inheritance (Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Xi Jinping), historical change from the modern period to reform and opening up, and shifting tasks. The second sets out four value implications. The third lists six basic principles for further deepening reform.

On evolutionary logic, the authors claim that theoretical, historical and practical logic are unified. They stress the shift in the principal contradiction of Chinese society, the theme of Chinese modernization, and the overall goal of improving socialist institutions and modernizing the system and capacity of national governance. On value, they argue that reform has deepened the Party's reform record, hardened its resilience (citing growth figures and China's contribution to the world economy), extended the range of socialist reform for countries such as Vietnam, Laos, Cuba and the DPRK, and raised the effectiveness of reform for human civilization. In this last point they say reform undermines the pattern of the East's subordination to the West and encourages late-developing countries to choose their own paths.

The six principles are: upholding the Party's overall leadership; putting the people first; staying true to fundamental principles while innovating; making institution-building the main thread; ruling the country by law in all respects; and applying systems thinking. The authors conclude that reform must be planned as a whole and advanced with a strong sense of historical initiative. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-scholar exposition of how the Third Plenum's reform agenda is justified historically, theoretically and internationally.”
quoteEn: Comprehensively deepening reform is a great undertaking with no precedent to follow.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革是一项没有任何成例可援的伟大事业。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The reform programme launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), covering economic, political, cultural, social and Party-building fields.

t: Understanding the contributions of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era at the level of principle
zh: 深刻理解习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的原理性贡献
paras: Li Haiqing asks in what sense Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era can be said to have made "principle-level" (yuanlixing) contributions to Marxism. The article's answer is that the Thought has enriched Marxism's basic principles at the more specific levels of its hierarchy of principles. It does so by deepening knowledge of three laws: those governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development.

The article has three parts. The first sets out what counts as a basic principle of Marxism and argues that principles are layered, using historical materialism and its sub-principles as the example. The second defines what a principle-level contribution is, separates it from policy or method innovation and from mere originality, and gives three criteria. The third identifies eight areas of contribution.

Li argues that principle-level contributions concern understanding the world, not policies and methods for changing it. Such contributions take three forms: extending principles Marxism has already developed, filling gaps the classics left, and making breakthroughs where a classical principle clashes with Chinese reality. The three criteria are a deeper account of the laws, broad guiding significance beyond China, and a key place within the Thought itself. Applying them, Li lists the following contributions. They are new quality productive forces and ecological productive forces; the socialist market economy as a basic economic system; whole-process people's democracy; the modernization of state governance; treating security as intrinsic to development; a community with a shared future for mankind; the Party's self-reform; and the claim that Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For Li, the market-economy case is a "subversive" innovation relative to the classical expectation of a product economy. Li presents the governance, security and self-reform theories as pioneering ones that fill gaps the classical authors left.

Li concludes that the Thought, shaped by new historical conditions and practical demands, has made specific and profound principle-level innovations. In this account these are pioneering, comprehensive and historic contributions to Marxism in contemporary China and the twenty-first century, opening a new realm of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want to see how a Party School scholar defines and classifies the theoretical contributions of Xi Jinping Thought and what criteria the author proposes for judging them.
quoteEn: The principle-level contributions of Xi Jinping Thought lie in principles for understanding the world, not in policies and methods for changing the world and transforming reality.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的原理性贡献集中体现在认识世界的原理方面而非改造世界、变革现实的政策与方法方面。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. Official texts describe it as the latest result of adapting Marxism to China.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, digitalisation and high-quality development.
The official term, used since 2019, for China's democratic model. It stresses popular participation across the whole cycle of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international order, based on cooperation, shared interests and shared responsibilities among countries with different systems.
An official theme since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself through internal discipline and anti-corruption work.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing project of combining Marxist theory with Chinese conditions and with contemporary developments.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: An important meeting for further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的重要会议
paras: This commentary interprets the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, held on 15–18 July 2024. Li Zhenghua argues that the meeting was a very important gathering held at a critical period for advancing national strength and rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. In Li's account, the plenum scientifically summarised experience since reform and opening up, continued the practice begun at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), and opened a new chapter of further comprehensively deepening reform.

The article has three sections. The first presents the plenum as a summary of reform-era experience, citing the ten third plenums held in 46 years and economic figures such as average growth of 9.9% in 1979–2012 and GDP rising from 53.9 trillion yuan in 2012 to 126.1 trillion in 2023. The second treats it as the practical sequel to the 2013 plenum, and the third sets out the new content of the plenum's Decision, including its targets, priorities and 300-plus reform measures.

Li's central claim is that reform has to be planned around the Party's central task, and that the Decision does this by linking reform to Chinese modernization and the goal of basically realising socialist modernization by 2035. Li lists six principles drawn from experience: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, institution-building as the main thread, law-based governance and a systems approach. Li also stresses continuity: the general goal of improving socialist institutions and modernising national governance repeats that of 2013, now with a deadline of 2029 and a stress on a high-standard socialist market economy and the Two Unwaverings. The plenum's "seven focuses" and three "greater emphases" (systemic integration, key priorities, practical results) are presented as the method for this stage.

Li concludes that the plenum further clarified the general goal of comprehensively deepening reform and tied reform and opening up to the nation's future, the course of Chinese modernization and individual destinies. Li ranks it as another milestone in the history of reform and opening up, after the Third Plenums of the 11th and 18th Central Committees. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's official-line reading of how the 2024 plenum is positioned within the sequence of reform-era plenums.
quoteEn: In further comprehensively deepening reform, the key lies in "deepening" and the emphasis lies in "comprehensive".
quoteZh: 进一步全面深化改革，关键在于“深化”，重点在于“全面”。

glossary.explanation: The official concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a distinct Chinese path to modernity, presented as the Party's central task for national rejuvenation.

The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It was set out in the 2013 plenum decision and restated in 2024.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal formulated at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) as the overall aim of deepening reform, together with improving socialist institutions.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, shifting the Party's focus to economic construction and engagement with the world economy.

t: Freedom and democracy: a preliminary theoretical construction of the common values of all humanity beyond Western "universal values"
zh: 自由与民主：超越西方“普世价值”的全人类共同价值理论建构初探
paras: Lin Xiuneng takes up a problem raised by the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls on all countries to uphold the common values of all humanity, including democracy and freedom. Lin observes that the right to interpret these two values has long been held by a few Western states, which bind them together as the core of their "universal values" discourse and use them to attack China's system. The article argues that freedom and democracy must be rebuilt as common values of all humanity that go beyond Western "universal values" in both content and form.

The article has two main parts. The first traces how freedom, democracy and finally "liberal democracy" became Western "universal values", drawing on Constant, Berlin, Schumpeter, Hayek and Fukuyama, and then critiques that discourse. The second builds the alternative: freedom reconstructed around relations, especially relations of production, and democracy reconstructed around the people as its basis. A short conclusion draws these together.

Lin contends that Western liberalism creates "universal values" by first emptying concepts of any limits on their application and then filling them with a liberal, individualist and capital-serving content. In Lin's reading, this equates modernization with Westernization and serves capital's global expansion, producing economic dependence and political disorder in countries that copy it. Against this, Lin argues that common values must address problems shared by humanity while respecting different countries' paths, so that they unite the universal and the particular. Freedom is then understood, following Engels, as understanding and consciously ordering relations between people and nature, between people, and within the self. Its limits are set by the framework of relations at each stage of development and can be widened only by collective action that changes those relations. Democracy is understood as a balance between individual and state in which the people, not an aggregate of individuals, are the subject. Lin calls for "solidarity democracy" in place of "adversarial democracy".

Lin concludes that freedom and democracy belong to no single civilization or doctrine and that their meaning develops over time. They should not let the individual override the collective but should coordinate the two, and they require respect for the diversity of civilizations and paths to modernization. Lin presents this as a way for China to contest Western discursive dominance. Read the original if you want a Marxist-informed, China-based critique of liberal universalism and an attempt to rework freedom and democracy in terms of production relations and people-centred democracy.
quoteEn: Freedom and democracy are not the business of one person but of a group of people, and only the collective has the capacity to transform society, pursue freedom and realize democracy.
quoteZh: 自由与民主不是一个人的事，是一群人的事，也只有集体才拥有变革社会、追求自由、实现民主的能力

glossary.literal: common values of the whole of humankind
glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted by Xi Jinping since 2015 that names peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared across nations. Chinese writers present it as an alternative to Western "universal values".

The idea that certain values, such as liberal freedom and multiparty democracy, hold for all peoples. Chinese official and academic discourse often treats it as a Western construct and puts the term in quotation marks.

t: "Attach importance to solving water security problems"
st: Studying Xi Jinping's important statements on water management
zh: “重视解决好水安全问题”
zhSub: 学习习近平关于治水工作的重要论述
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2024 no. 1
paras: Liu Zhihui sets out to systematise Xi Jinping's statements on water management since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article asks why water work matters in the new era and how it should be done. Liu's answer is that Xi treats water security as a strategic question for the lasting development of the Chinese nation, requiring a change in thinking, large-scale ecological and engineering measures, and a stronger system of flood and drought control.

The article is a study of Xi's speeches and instructions, organised in five parts. It begins with the current water-security situation, then covers the policy line on water management and the national "river strategy" for the Yangtze, the Yellow River and major lakes and wetlands. It goes on to the national water network and the South-to-North Water Diversion project, and ends with flood and drought prevention. Liu supports the account with figures on rainfall, shortages, pollution and engineering capacity.

Liu's first move is to divide water-security problems into old and new. The old ones are uneven distribution of water in time and space and the resulting disasters. The new ones are water shortage, ecological damage and pollution. Second, Liu presents Xi's approach of "prioritising water conservation, balancing spatial distribution, systematic governance, and applying both the government and market hands". In this reading, population and economic scale must be fitted to water carrying capacity, and water must be managed together with mountains, forests, fields, lakes, grassland and desert. The government sets strict management and taxes, while the market handles water-rights trading. Third, Liu reports Xi's guidance on rivers and engineering. For the Yangtze this is "joint protection, no large-scale development", and for the Yellow River "protection and coordinated governance". The national water network is to be built on lessons from earlier diversion projects. Flood control is to combine structural works with non-structural measures such as responsibility systems, early warning and joint reservoir operation, always putting people's lives first.

Liu concludes that Xi's statements capture the regularities of water management and provide fundamental guidance for the new era. The author calls for water resources, ecology, environment and disasters to be handled together, and for the Party to raise its capacity in saving water, allocating it, protecting rivers and lakes, and defending against floods and droughts. Liu presents this as securing water for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history-institute account of how Xi's water policy is framed, with the figures and Xi's own formulations organised by theme.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's important statements on water management contain a profound revelation and scientific grasp of the laws of water work, pointing the way forward and providing the fundamental guidance for water work in the new era.
quoteZh: 习近平关于治水工作的重要论述，蕴含着对治水工作规律的深刻揭示与科学把握，为新时代治水工作指明了前进方向、提供了根本遵循。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses a large population, common prosperity, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China to national strength and prosperity by the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.en: applying both the government and market hands
glossary.explanation: One of the four elements of Xi's 2014 water-management approach. Water governance should combine the decisive role of the market in allocating resources with a stronger role for government.

A planned integrated system of natural rivers and lakes, water-diversion channels, storage works and smart controls. It is meant to allocate water, control floods and protect water ecosystems across basins.

t: The distinctive value of the Chronicle of the Communist Party of China (New-Democratic Revolution period)
zh: 《中国共产党编年史》（新民主主义革命时期）的独特价值
paras: Marking the 75th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic, this commentary introduces the newly published Chronicle of the Communist Party of China (New-Democratic Revolution period), compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and issued by the CPC History Publishing House. Qu Qingshan, who heads the Institute, argues that the work is highly significant. In Qu's account it answers new demands on Party history work, enlarges the body of core Party histories, fills a gap in research and serves as an authoritative textbook.

The piece is organised around four claims about the Chronicle's value. Qu first recounts its origins: a 2010 Central Committee document called for a chronicle to be compiled, and work was restarted in February 2023 after the Chinese and English editions of The Communist Party of China's Hundred Years were finished. The text then covers the work's structure, the question of historical genres, and the guidance Xi Jinping has given on how to treat Party history.

Qu's central argument is that existing core Party histories are all general histories, concise and limited in scale, so they give only the trunk and outline of a great tree and not its branches and leaves. The Chronicle runs to 29 volumes, one per year from 1921 to 1949, with more than nine million characters. According to Qu, it is the richest and largest chronological core history so far, and it covers politics, military affairs, economy, culture, society, foreign relations and Party building. Qu says the compilers broke with the habits of general-history writing. They organised the work by year, month and day, supplemented it with event-based narration, and so created a new method of Party history research. Qu also stresses the word 'zheng' (correct, orthodox) in Xi's remarks on history. The compilers say they applied Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, opposed historical nihilism and relied on the Party's three historical resolutions, so as to produce an orthodox and reliable history.

Qu concludes that the Chronicle is an authoritative textbook and basic reader. It is meant to help make Party history study and education a regular, long-term practice, and to help the whole Party and society learn and use Party history. Read the original if you want an official account, from the Institute's head, of why this multi-volume chronicle was compiled and how its compilers describe its method and political guidance.
quoteEn: Taking the chronicle form as the main approach, supplemented by the event-based form, with time as the warp and events as the weft: this way of writing is itself innovative in genre and also effectively makes the content more readable and vivid.
quoteZh: 以编年体为主、辅之以纪事本末体，以时间为经、以事件为纬，这样的写法，不仅本身就具有体裁上的创新性，而且也有效增加了内容的可读性和生动性。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official periodisation for 1919–1949, from the May Fourth Movement to the founding of the People's Republic. The Chronicle covers 1921–1949.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Party publications cite it as the guide for work in many fields, including history.

An official term for views that, in the Party's reading, deny or distort the Party's history and the achievements of the revolution and socialism. Party leaders have repeatedly called for opposing it.
A campaign launched across the Party in 2021, the centenary year, and then made a regular practice. In February 2024 the Central Committee issued regulations on it.

keywords: Chronicle of the Communist Party of China

t: Key relationships to grasp in strengthening Party discipline in the new era and on the new journey
zh: 新时代新征程加强党的纪律建设需要把握的若干关系
paras: How should the Chinese Communist Party strengthen its discipline in the new era? Lü Huidong and Ding Junping argue that discipline building is the fundamental, root-cause measure of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and that it works only if five relationships are handled correctly. Drawing on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), they present discipline as a safeguard for the Party's self-reform and for solving the problems unique to a large party.

The article is a policy-theoretical essay in five numbered sections, each taking one relationship: Party leadership and discipline building; discipline and the Party's other forms of building; strict discipline and officials' personal freedom; strict discipline and care for Party members and officials; and Party discipline and state law. It relies heavily on Xi Jinping's statements and on Party documents, with a short citation of Mao Zedong on conscious discipline, and it gives a brief historical account of discipline building over more than a century.

The authors argue first that Party leadership determines the direction, tasks and methods of discipline building, so discipline must be built under unified central leadership and led by political building, with political discipline as the most important kind. Discipline is tied to ideological, organizational, conduct and institutional building and to the anti-corruption struggle. Second, they hold that members' personal freedom is relative while Party discipline is absolute. They add, citing Mao, that discipline must be conscious, tied to the masses and guided by a correct political line, and that it must not become a tool for retaliation. Third, they treat strictness and care as compatible, citing the 'Four Forms' of supervision and discipline enforcement, the 'three distinctions' and mechanisms that tolerate and correct errors. Fourth, they defend the principle that discipline is stricter than law and comes before it, with discipline and law kept separate. In their account, this ends an older confusion that lowered the standard for members.

The authors conclude that the Party, now pushing forward a new great project of Party building, places discipline building in a more prominent position and runs it through the whole of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. They present this as the disciplinary guarantee for a stronger, long-governing Marxist party and for the Party's role as the core of leadership. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party scholars frame discipline, internal regulations and the relationship between Party rules and state law in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Party leadership determines the direction, tasks, content, principles and methods of Party discipline building, and plays a fundamental guiding and safeguarding role.
quoteZh: 党的领导决定了党的纪律建设的方向、任务、内容、原则、方法，具有根本的引领和保障作用。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan and programme promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption, internal regulations and ideological education for Party members.
An official concept stressing that the Party must correct its own problems and purify itself without outside pressure. It is closely linked to Xi Jinping's discourse on Party building.

glossary.literal: four forms of supervision and discipline enforcement
glossary.explanation: A graded approach to handling violations: most cases get criticism or light sanctions, fewer get heavy sanctions, and very few are referred for criminal investigation.

glossary.pinyin: jì yán yú fǎ, jì zài fǎ qián
glossary.en: discipline is stricter than law and comes before it
glossary.literal: discipline stricter than law, discipline ahead of law
glossary.explanation: A principle promoted under Xi Jinping that Party discipline sets a higher standard for members than state law and applies earlier, so that minor breaches are dealt with before they become crimes.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Paying more attention to systematic integration to further deepen reform comprehensively
zh: 更加注重系统集成 进一步全面深化改革
paras: Wang Aiyun examines why the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), in deploying further comprehensive deepening of reform to advance Chinese modernization, calls for "paying more attention to systematic integration". The article argues that the requirement rests on a systems approach developed since 2012 and now acquires richer content through five major relationships that reform must handle.

The piece has three parts. It first describes comprehensive deepening of reform as a complex systems project. It then traces how Xi Jinping's statements built up the systems concept as a basic way of thinking and working. Finally it takes up the five relationships named in the Plenum's Decision. Wang draws mainly on Xi's speeches and Party documents from 2012 to 2024, with illustrations from urbanisation, state-owned enterprise reform, ecological governance, and science and technology reform.

Wang argues that post-2012 reform differs from earlier reform in being comprehensive. In breadth, it spans every field and both the economic base and the superstructure, so that each measure depends on the others. In depth, it has reached the "deep waters", where interests are intertwined. The author traces the progression from calls for systematic, holistic and coordinated reform (2012–13) to "systematic integration", and notes that Xi in 2020 for the first time called the systems concept a "basic" way of thinking and working. The Decision's sixth principle, upholding the systems concept, names five relationships to be handled: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. For each, Wang holds that the two sides are mutually conditioning, and that neither should be pursued one-sidedly.

Wang concludes that handling these five relationships will strengthen the systematic, holistic and coordinated character of reform over the next five years. In this account, it will give Chinese modernization strong momentum and institutional guarantees. The article is an official-line exposition, citing the leadership's statements closely and offering no critical assessment. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-by-source account of how the Party's "systems concept" and the "five relationships" were assembled into the reform guidance of the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The most fundamental difference between comprehensively deepening reform and the reforms of the past thirty-plus years is that it is conceived from the overall perspective of the national governance system and governance capacity, with the emphasis on being \"comprehensive\".
quoteZh: 全面深化改革与中国过去30多年改革最根本的区别在于全面深化改革是从国家治理体系和治理能力的总体角度考虑的，突出的是“全面”。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is characterised by a huge population, common prosperity, and material and cultural-ethical advancement, among other features.

A methodological principle in Xi Jinping's thought that stresses planning and advancing reform and development as an interconnected whole. In 2020 it was described as a basic way of thinking and working.
A reform requirement that measures across fields be designed to fit together and reinforce one another. The 2024 Plenum made it a keynote of further reform.

t: The threefold logic of the development of the supervision system of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义监督制度发展演进的三重逻辑
paras: Supervision of power, and especially self-supervision by a ruling party, is described by Xiao Ruining and Hong Xianghua as a worldwide problem and the 'Goldbach conjecture' of state governance. The article asks how the supervision system of socialism with Chinese characteristics emerged and what marks it out in the new era. Its thesis is that the system, which began in the New Democratic revolution and matured after the 18th Party Congress (2012), can be understood through three dimensions: theory, history and practice.

The article has three main sections. The first traces the theory, from Marx and Engels on the Paris Commune and 'public servants', and Lenin on workers' control and the Control Commission and Workers' and Peasants' Inspectorate, through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to Xi Jinping. The second follows the institutions through four stages: germination (1921–49), foundation-laying after 1949, basic formation in the reform era, and maturation since 2012. The third sets out the system's present-day characteristics.

The authors argue that the system is an institutional arrangement uniting the 'two answers' to the problem of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. The first answer, attributed to Mao in his exchange with Huang Yanpei, is letting the people supervise the government. The second, put forward by Xi, is the Party's self-reform. In the authors' account the system is led by intra-Party supervision, with four forms (discipline, supervisory commission, dispatched-agency and inspection supervision) coordinated with nine others in a '1+9' pattern. It also serves the Party's overall leadership, the people's principal position, and the unity of rule by Party regulations and rule of law.

The authors add that the system draws on traditional Chinese supervisory culture, such as imperial inspection and impeachment, and offers what they call a 'Chinese solution' to problems they attribute to Western separation-of-powers models. They conclude that supervision must be guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, aimed at modernizing national governance, and rooted in domestic conditions, since copying foreign systems will not work. They also call for better coordination among the different forms of supervision. Read the original if you want a Party-school account of how official discourse periodises Chinese supervision institutions, from the 1925 Guangdong supervisory committee to the 2018 supervisory commissions.
quoteEn: The supervision system of socialism with Chinese characteristics is an institutional arrangement that unites the "two answers".
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义监督制度就是“两个答案”相统一的制度安排。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation, presented as the 'second answer' to the historical cycle problem: the Party must continually purify and correct itself.

glossary.en: the historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea, raised by Huang Yanpei in 1945, that regimes rise and then decay. Mao's reply and Xi's later 'second answer' are presented as Party solutions.
