t: Further study of the Marxist thought on power and the supervision of power
zh: 进一步深入研究马克思主义权力和权力监督思想
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2024 no. 7
paras: Yan Shuhan starts from Xi Jinping's remark that self-supervision is a worldwide problem and "the Goldbach conjecture of state governance". Yan argues that a ruling party can only tackle this problem by returning to the theoretical origins of Marxism and studying the classical writers' thought on power and its supervision. The article claims that this thought is a neglected resource, and that it explains both why supervision is so difficult and how the Chinese Communist Party should now approach it.

The article moves from Marx and Engels to Lenin and then to the present. It first sets out two basic points in Marx and Engels: power as a general product of the state, and corruption as a product of private ownership and exploitation. It then turns to the Paris Commune and Engels's 1891 introduction to The Civil War in France. Next it covers Lenin's development of the theme: democratic centralism, party and state supervisory bodies, and the purges and anti-corruption struggle of the early Soviet years. The final section applies these ideas to the Party today.

Yan's central move is to read the Commune's two measures, election with recall and workers' wages for officials, as "democratic election" and "equal wages". The aim of both is to stop officials turning from "servants" into "masters". Yan warns against taking them literally. Engels himself, Yan notes, blamed the Commune's fall partly on a lack of centralisation and authority, so recall "at any time" should not be over-stressed. Equal wages, in turn, express equality between leaders and masses as a historical-materialist category, not identical pay. Yan presents Lenin as turning this into democratic centralism, independent control commissions with authority parallel to the Central Committee, and purges that removed large parts of the membership.

Yan concludes that supervision of power is a problem unique to a large party, and lists the six "how to always" problems Xi Jinping named. Yan reports reluctance to supervise, fear of supervising superiors, and weak intra-Party supervision. Confidence in solving them rests, in Yan's account, on three things: Marxist Party-building theory, the "second answer" of self-reform to the question of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall, and a Party and state supervision system. Yan stresses that giving the second answer does not mean the task is finished. Read the original if you want a Party-school scholar's account of how classical Marxist texts are used to ground current Party discipline and anti-corruption policy.
quoteEn: It can thus be seen that, on the supervision of power in socialist society, the classical Marxist writers' focus was to prevent state power and public officials from degenerating from "servants" into "masters".
quoteZh: 可见，关于社会主义社会的权力监督问题，马克思主义经典作家着眼点就是防止国家政权和公务人员由“公仆”蜕变为“主人”。

glossary.explanation: The Leninist organisational principle: the minority obeys the majority, lower bodies obey higher ones, and leaders are elected and accountable to congresses.

glossary.en: escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.literal: jumping out of the historical cycle
glossary.explanation: Refers to a 1945 exchange between Huang Yanpei and Mao Zedong in Yan'an about how a regime could avoid the rapid rise and collapse seen in past dynasties.

t: Development and innovation in the party diplomacy of socialist countries: experience and lessons
zh: 社会主义国家政党外交的发展创新及其经验启示
paras: Yang Xiuwen and Chen Haiyan ask how the external activity of ruling parties in socialist states, which they call party diplomacy, has developed over more than a century, and what lessons it offers today. They define it as the external affairs that ruling Marxist parties conduct around their own development and the realisation of their values. They argue that it has moved from a narrow, bloc-bound practice to a plural, institutionalised one, and that this record guides efforts to revive the world socialist movement and build a community with a shared future for mankind.

The article opens by building a three-level concept of party diplomacy, from the general, to socialist parties not yet in power, to the specific case of ruling socialist parties. It then follows the history in three phases: the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks) and the Comintern; the Cold War period, including the Yugoslav split, the Sino-Soviet dispute and setbacks for the Chinese party in the 1960s and 1970s; and the period since the Soviet collapse. The post-1991 section draws mainly on China, Vietnam, Laos, the DPRK and Cuba, and also covers the São Paulo Forum and the international meetings of communist and workers' parties.

In the authors' account, Cold War party diplomacy was narrow and often subordinated to Soviet leadership. Reflection on the resulting conflicts produced the principle of independence and autonomy, which they treat as a basic norm. Since the 1990s, they argue, ruling parties have served central national tasks, built multilevel networks and, in China's case, developed new forms of exchange with other parties. From this history they draw five lessons: keep innovating theory; align "a new type of party relations" with new international relations on the basis of seeking common ground while respecting differences and mutual learning; make methods coordinated, scientific and effective; diversify institutional platforms through specialised bodies and trained personnel; and treat the building of a community with a shared future for mankind as the value orientation.

The authors conclude that socialist-state party diplomacy serves both the interests of its own peoples and world peace, development and the progress of civilisations. They present it as rooted in the First International and the October Revolution, and as likely to widen the international space for ruling socialist parties. Read the original if you study the history of communist party relations, the Chinese Communist Party's external work, or how Chinese scholars frame party diplomacy conceptually.
quoteEn: Party diplomacy of socialist countries looks not only to realising the interests of the peoples of socialist countries, but also carries the mission and responsibility of safeguarding world peace and development and advancing human civilisation.
quoteZh: 社会主义国家政党外交不仅着眼于实现社会主义国家人民的利益，更肩负着维护世界和平与发展、促进人类文明进步的使命与担当。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese scholarship for the international exchanges and cooperation conducted by ruling and other legitimate parties alongside state diplomacy. It came into use in China from the 1970s and drew academic attention in the early 1990s.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping, presented officially as a vision of shared security, prosperity and openness among nations.

glossary.en: a new type of party relations
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2017 formulation for inter-party relations based on seeking common ground while respecting differences, mutual respect and mutual learning. It builds on the Chinese party's four principles of independence, complete equality, mutual respect and non-interference.

glossary.en: seeking common ground while respecting differences
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Chinese diplomatic formula for cooperating on shared interests while setting aside disagreements.
The international movement of socialist and communist parties and states, which Chinese scholars treat as a single historical process from the First International onwards.

t: Capitalist civilisation in decline and the new form of human civilisation: an ecological perspective
zh: 从生态视角看资本主义文明没落与人类文明新形态构建
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 4
paras: Zhang Jian asks what the ecological crisis reveals about the condition of Western capitalist civilisation, and what is replacing it. The article argues that, from the standpoint of an antagonism between the logic of capital and the logic of life, Western capitalist civilisation has reached its end. In Zhang's account it will be superseded by the new form of human civilisation, represented by China and created through Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first treats neoliberalism's loss of legitimacy through its anti-ecological character, covering the commodification of nature, "green capitalism" and the export of polluting industry. The second turns to the crises of the twenty-first century and to Marx's analysis of capital's self-imposed limits. The third surveys China's ecological civilisation achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), set against Western experience. Zhang draws on Marx, on Xi Jinping's statements, and on Carlos Martinez and John Molyneux.

Zhang holds that capital must break through every boundary, while the biosphere and the worker's vitality are finite. Capital is therefore self-devouring, and the article reads Marx's remark that the limit of capital is capital itself as having ecological implications. Zhang rejects blaming consumerism or treating workers as automatic bearers of species interest. In this account the underlying conflict is between capital and life, and solving the climate crisis requires a revolution in ownership of the means of production, led by a Marxist party. Zhang credits China's public ownership, Party leadership and planning with the progress made. The author lists four ways Chinese modernization goes beyond capitalism: balancing equity and efficiency, coordinated development, simultaneous growth and ecological repair, and the Belt and Road Initiative. The article cites figures on forest cover, clean energy and international cooperation.

Zhang concludes that capitalism's anti-ecological character is one expression of its sharpening basic contradiction. Economic, social, political and ecological crises are deepening under accelerating technological change. In the article's view, Western capitalist civilisation is at its end while the new form of human civilisation is rising. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links ecological Marxism, critique of neoliberalism and the official narrative of ecological civilisation.
quoteEn: Between capital, which pursues the infinite, and finite life there is an insurmountable contradiction.
quoteZh: 追求无限的资本与有限的生命之间就有着不可克服的矛盾。

glossary.en: the new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A formulation in Party discourse, notably since Xi Jinping's 2021 speech, for the civilisation said to be created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as going beyond capitalist modernity.
The official name for China's path of modernization, described by the Party as distinct from Western models.
A Chinese policy goal, written into Party documents since the 17th Party Congress (2007) and elevated at the 18th, aimed at integrating environmental protection into economic and social development.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: Upholding the principal position of the people in cultural development
zh: 坚持文化建设中的人民主体地位
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 15 October 2024, p. 1
paras: Taking its cue from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization, this newspaper commentary asks how the people's principal position should be upheld in cultural development. Jiang argues that reform of the cultural system should be guided by the principle of putting the people first, so that it supports the building of a culturally strong country and Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised under three headings: guaranteeing cultural rights as part of building a culturally strong country; stimulating the people's sense of agency as the central link; and promoting well-rounded human development as the core task. It draws on examples such as dragon-boat races, the village football league, book fairs, square dancing, short video, drone shows and rural art projects.

Jiang contends that China has already built up practice in protecting cultural rights, with the state providing conditions and the public taking part actively. Further institutional reform is needed, for instance for disabled and elderly people in a digital setting. Citing Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, the author holds that popular creativity and the initiative of cultural workers drive innovation, and that science and technology should lead cultural change, including the cultivation of new quality productive forces in culture. Drawing on Marx's remarks on free time and on 'environment shapes people', Jiang adds that public cultural activity and cultural volunteer mechanisms should foster well-rounded development.

Jiang concludes that upholding the people's principal position means protecting cultural rights, respecting popular initiative and awakening agency. It also means raising social civility and cultivating 'modern new people' alongside common prosperity, giving spiritual support to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-aligned scholars link cultural policy to the Third Plenum's reform agenda.
quoteEn: Respecting the people's creative agency means encouraging them to create better space for development and innovation; in cultural development in particular, technological innovation should lead cultural change.
quoteZh: 尊重人民的主体创造，就是要鼓励人民创造更优的发展空间和创新空间，在文化建设领域尤其要以科技创新去引领文化变革。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation and advanced industries.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed by the Party under Xi Jinping.
An official aim of building China's cultural strength and influence, set out in Party documents.

t: Xi Jinping's thought on culture and its original contribution to the Marxist theory of culture
zh: 习近平文化思想对马克思主义文化理论的原创性贡献
paras: Gao Ren asks how Xi Jinping's thought on culture has added to the Marxist theory of culture. The article argues that this body of thought, presented as a theoretical summary of the Party's cultural work in the new era, makes an original Chinese contribution. In Gao's account it forms the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and opens a new stage in Marxist cultural theory.

This is a short commentary first published in the Guangming Daily in June 2024. It is organised in three parts. Each part names one dimension of the contribution: the Party's cultural leadership, a strong sense of cultural subjectivity, and a sense of cultural mission. Each is tied to a deeper understanding of, respectively, the principles of Marxist cultural theory, the laws of socialist cultural development, and the paths to building a modern Chinese civilization.

In the first part, Gao argues that a rising class must hold cultural leadership to establish its position, so the Party must keep full leadership over propaganda, ideology and the media. Marxism must remain the guiding ideology, and a people-centred orientation must govern creative and research work. The second part credits Xi with proposing cultural confidence as one of the Four-sphere Confidence, with building the core socialist values into the basic policy of upholding socialism, and with the Two Integrations of Marxism with China's realities and with its fine traditional culture. Gao presents these as safeguarding both the "soul" of Marxism and the "roots" of Chinese culture. The third part says that building a modern Chinese civilization requires cultural confidence and an independent path, openness to the achievements of other civilizations, and a balance of upholding fundamental principles with innovation.

Gao concludes that Xi's cultural thought is an open, evolving system that will keep developing with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Gao's view it helps create a new culture for the era and promotes the free and all-round development of the human being. Gao adds that building a modern Chinese civilization also contributes to human civilization more broadly. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists present Xi's cultural thought as an advance in Marxist theory.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's thought on culture is a continually unfolding, open system of thought, and it will certainly be enriched and developed as the building of a strong country and the great cause of national rejuvenation advance.
quoteZh: 习近平文化思想是一个不断展开的、开放式的思想体系，必将随着强国建设、民族复兴伟业的深入推进而不断丰富发展

glossary.explanation: A formula for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Cultural confidence was added as the fourth, under Xi Jinping.
The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2023.
The Party's authority over ideology, culture and the media. The term echoes the Gramscian notion of hegemony.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017. Xi's thought on culture, formally articulated in 2023, is presented as one of its components.

t: Deepening reform to inject vitality into building a cultural powerhouse
zh: 深化改革为文化强国建设注入活力
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in September 2024, reads the cultural section of the Decision of the Central Committee on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization (the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, 2024). Xiao Guiqing argues that the Decision sets out major reforms of cultural institutions and mechanisms for building a socialist cultural powerhouse. In Xiao's account, these reforms provide ideological guarantees, spiritual strength and favourable cultural conditions for national rejuvenation.

The commentary is organised under four headings: improving the responsibility system for ideological work; optimising the supply of cultural services and products; strengthening the comprehensive governance of cyberspace; and building a more effective international communication system. Each section paraphrases the Decision's measures and adds the author's explanation of why they are needed.

On ideology, Xiao describes ideological work as extremely important to the Party and says that, although the situation has changed fundamentally since the 18th Party Congress (2012), struggle in this field remains sharp. The author calls for the Party to keep firm leadership, management and discourse power, to maintain Marxism's guiding position, to arm Party members with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and to cultivate core socialist values. On culture and the internet, Xiao stresses equal access to public cultural services, putting social benefits first in cultural production, protecting historical heritage, and regarding the internet as the main ideological battleground. This requires the principle of Party management of the internet, law-based governance and a multi-actor governance pattern. On external communication, the author identifies gaps between China's real image and Western perceptions, and between soft and hard power, and calls for Chinese discourse and narrative systems alongside civilizational exchange and mutual learning.

Xiao concludes that deepening cultural reform will strengthen the Party's ideological leadership, spiritual prosperity for all the people and China's international voice, presenting a trustworthy, lovable and respectable image of China. The piece is a policy explanation rather than an academic analysis. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the Third Plenum's cultural-reform agenda, including its approach to ideology, internet governance and international communication.
quoteEn: The internet is increasingly the main position, main battlefield and front line of ideological struggle; to firmly hold the leadership of ideological work, the key is to occupy online positions and win online dominance.
quoteZh: 互联网日益成为意识形态斗争的主阵地、主战场、最前沿，牢牢掌握意识形态工作领导权，关键要占领网上阵地、赢得网上主导权。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Party mechanism, formalised in 2015, that makes Party committees and leading cadres accountable for ideological and propaganda work in their areas.
A twelve-word official formulation of values (such as prosperity, democracy, harmony, patriotism and integrity) promoted since the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models and as coordinating material and spiritual civilization.
An official goal of building China into a country with strong cultural influence, productivity and soft power, set out in Party documents and targeted for 2035.

t: Whole-process people's democracy: opening a new realm of human political civilization
zh: 全过程人民民主：开辟人类政治文明新境界
paras: Bao Xinjian asks what kind of political civilization the world needs and argues that China's whole-process people's democracy answers the question. In the article's account, Xi Jinping's statements on the subject have raised socialist political civilization to a new level, opened a new realm of human political civilization and created a new form of it. Bao presents this as a response to problems that Western political models have left unresolved.

The article is organised in four parts, each describing one orientation of whole-process people's democracy and what it adds to human political civilization. These are: the people as the main body of democracy; institutional guarantees and institutional reform; governance as a mission; and a commitment to the common values of all humanity. Bao draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin on democracy, the state and the Paris Commune. Bao also cites Xi Jinping, the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and recent plenums, and contrasts the approach with American-style democracy.

Bao's central claim is that the decisive question in democracy is who its main body is. In Bao's reading, party and interest-group manipulation has turned American democracy into a tool of privileged minorities, causing political polarisation and social division. By contrast, the Communist Party of China is said to represent no special interest, so the people remain the main body. Bao describes a full 'chain' of democratic institutions: electoral democracy through the people's congresses, consultative democracy through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and grassroots self-government. Bao says these link election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. Bao argues that this design joins democracy to governance, turning institutional strengths into governance effectiveness through broad consultation ('matters for everyone are discussed by everyone') and the building of consensus. Bao also traces the idea to the Party's century of struggle for people's democracy and to the inclusiveness of Chinese civilization.

Bao concludes that whole-process people's democracy, as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, is not democracy for a minority or a formality but the most extensive, genuine and effective kind. Bao holds that it offers a Chinese approach to the shared problem of how popular democratic power can drive state governance. It also fits the view of civilizations as diverse, equal and inclusive, set against the 'clash of civilizations' and Western-centrism. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how whole-process people's democracy is framed as a contribution to world political civilization.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy is all-round democracy: it has not only a complete institutional chain but also broad participatory practice.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主是全方位民主，不仅有完整的制度链条，而且有广泛的参与实践

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and promoted since the 19th Party Congress period as the defining feature of Chinese socialist democracy. It stresses that democratic participation runs through election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not just voting.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.
The official term for institutionalised consultation among the Party, state organs, the CPPCC, social groups and communities. It is presented as a distinctive feature of China's political system.

A national advisory and consultative body that brings together the Communist Party, other parties, mass organisations and representatives of different sectors. It is officially described as a special consultative institution.

t: Broadening the development path of the rural collective economy
st: Improving the system of rural collective economic organisations
zh: 农村集体经济发展路径的拓展
zhSub: 完善农村集体经济组织体系
paras: Zheng Youguiv asks how China can consolidate and improve its basic rural operation system and strengthen the rural collective economy. The article draws on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and the Law on Rural Collective Economic Organisations, passed in June 2024. Its thesis is that the collective economy has lagged behind household contract farming, and that the remedy lies in a fuller system of collective organisations built on a systems approach.

The article has three parts. The first argues that the dual-layer system, with household contracting as its base and a combination of unified and separate operation, requires the collective and household levels to develop together. The second reviews the long evolution of collective organisation, from agricultural producers' cooperatives through the people's communes to household contracting and shareholding reform, to draw out directions and principles. The third sets out concrete measures for improving the organisational system.

Zheng holds that the constant is collective ownership of rural land, while the forms of collective economy change with the stage of development. Weakened collective economies, in Zheng's reading, stem from historical conditions such as tax-and-fee reform and the loss of managerial talent, not from household contracting itself. Reforms such as the separation of the three land rights and the "three changes" (resources into shares, funds into stock, farmers into shareholders) show that collective ownership can be innovative. For the organisational system, Zheng proposes making township, village and group levels substantive, with special attention to the neglected group level, and protecting original collectives' assets when administrative units merge. Zheng also urges collectives to move from "boarding someone else's boat" (joining companies or cooperatives) to "building their own boat", and to form leading organisations, as shareholding cooperatives, that work across townships.

Zheng concludes that the new law gives collective economies stronger policy and legal support, but that development must follow economic laws and avoid crude administrative pressure. Party leadership should integrate resources through shareholding cooperation, not by command. Read the original if you want a policy-oriented account of how Chinese scholars link the 2024 collective economy law to the history of rural cooperation and to practical organisational design.
quoteEn: In short, the weakening of the collective economy caused by historical conditions should not be blamed on the reform of household contract operation, nor should confidence in the development of the collective economy be lost because of it.
quoteZh: 简言之，不能将历史条件所致的集体经济弱化归于实行家庭承经营这一改革，也不能因此对集体经济的发展失去信心。

glossary.explanation: Region-based economic bodies that exercise ownership of collectively owned rural land on behalf of their members. The 2024 law recognises them at township, village and group levels.
The basic rural operation system written into China's Constitution: household contract farming as the base, combined with unified collective services and operation.

glossary.en: separation of the three land rights
glossary.explanation: A reform dividing rural land rights into collective ownership, household contract rights and operation rights, so that operation rights can be transferred to others.

keywords: Law on Rural Collective Economic Organisations

t: Another milestone meeting in the history of China's reform and opening up
zh: 我国改革开放史上又一次里程碑式重要会议
paras: Writing in Qiyi (Banner) in 2024, Jin Minqing asks where the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) stands in the history of reform and opening up. Jin argues that it is a landmark meeting comparable to two earlier plenums, and that it produced a major leap in the history of reform and opening up. The commentary presents the 2024 meeting as the third in a series of historic turning points, each responding to the demands of its own period.

The article is organised around the three Third Plenums. It first treats the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), then the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), and then the 2024 meeting. For each, Jin describes the historical situation, the decisions taken and the opening of a new stage. The last section sets out the "leaps" that Jin finds in the 2024 Decision on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization.

Jin contends that the Party has consistently made major reform decisions suited to each critical period. In 1978, it corrected "Left" errors, shifted the focus to economic construction and launched reform and opening up. In 2013, facing a stage of difficult reforms and entrenched interests, it moved reform from local exploration to systematic integration. For 2024, Jin identifies leaps in several areas. These are content (the "seven focuses"), principles (the "six adherences"), the planning of reform around Chinese modernization, and the main task, which Jin says shifts from liberating productive forces to developing new quality productive forces.

Jin concludes that the 2024 plenum, led by Xi Jinping, expresses the Party's resolve to carry reform through to the end. Jin also says it reaffirms the banner to be held and the path to be followed in the new era. The text mainly summarises and interprets the Decision and offers little independent analysis. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how Party scholars place the 2024 plenum alongside the 1978 and 2013 plenums.
quoteEn: The Third Plenum of the 20th Party Central Committee was a milestone meeting held in precisely this new critical period.
quoteZh: 党的二十届三中全会就是在这个新的关键时期召开的一次具有里程碑意义的重要会议。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization models.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It stresses technology-driven, innovation-led productive forces as the basis of high-quality development.
The official programme launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It covers economic, political, cultural, social, ecological and Party-building reforms.

The seven areas highlighted in the 2024 Decision. They include the socialist market economy, whole-process people's democracy and cultural strength, as well as living standards, ecology, security and Party leadership.

t: Taking institution-building as the main thread in further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 以制度建设为主线挈领进一步全面深化改革
source: Chinese Political Science Research (政治学研究), 2024 no. 4
paras: Wang Puqu takes up a principle in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization: that institution-building should be the main thread (主线) of reform. The article argues that this principle sums up the experience of reform in the new era and guides the next stage. Its aim is to set out the basic theory of institution-building and the regularities it follows in deepening reform.

The article has three parts. The first explains what institution-building means for reform. The second sets out its guiding functions. The third proposes practical paths for implementation. Wang draws on historical materialism, on statements by Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, on the Plenum decision, and on economic, political, sociological and cultural accounts of what institutions do.

In the first part, Wang defines institution-building as the process by which a state regulates behaviour through rules, thereby building its governance system and capacity. Wang presents it as driven by the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, as an adjustment of interests and of the relations between power and rights, and as supply-side structural reform of institutions. It combines top-level design with grassroots experience, and Wang describes it as a dynamic, long-term process. The second part credits institution-building with a series of functions: realising the Two Integrations, freeing productive forces, adjusting interests, resolving the paradox of reforming institutions through legal procedure, carrying core socialist values, and guarding against major risks. The third part sets out implementation: strengthening Party leadership, putting the people at the centre, keeping to the central task of Chinese modernization, and taking economic reform as the lead. It adds rule-of-law methods, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, 'establishing before breaking', and a problem-oriented approach that integrates systems and evaluates results.

Wang concludes that the sequence runs from institution-building to deeper reform, then to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and that this is the Party's roadmap for the new journey. Institutions should be judged by whether they suit national conditions, work effectively and win popular support, and by their conversion into governance effectiveness. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese political scientists frame institution-building as the logic of the 2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: Institution-building is supply-side structural reform of institutions in the process of building a modern state.
quoteZh: 制度建设是现代国家建设进程中的制度供给侧结构性改革。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and based on China's national conditions.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.pinyin: pò lì bìngjǔ, xiān lì hòu pò
glossary.literal: breaking and establishing together; establish first, break afterwards
glossary.explanation: A reform principle stressed by Xi Jinping: build new institutions or arrangements before dismantling old ones, to keep change stable.

t: Improving the institutions and mechanisms for integrated urban–rural development: forming a new pattern
zh: 完善城乡融合发展体制机制：形成城乡融合发展新格局
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in October 2024, takes up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to improve the institutions and mechanisms for integrated urban–rural development. Shangguan argues that handling urban–rural relations well is a necessary requirement of Chinese modernization and that a new pattern of integration should be formed to narrow urban–rural differences.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's and Marx's remarks on urban–rural relations, then reviews the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It next explains why improvement is needed, and ends with practical measures.

Shangguan reports that the urban–rural income ratio fell from 2.81:1 in 2013 to 2.39:1 in 2023, after poverty alleviation and rural revitalization. The author nonetheless stresses that agriculture's foundation is still unstable and that gaps persist, which the article treats as a concentrated expression of the principal contradiction in society. Improvement is justified on three grounds: it fills agriculture's weak points and builds a strong agricultural country; it releases the demand of a huge market and supports high-quality development; and it meets the people's aspirations and promotes common prosperity.

For practice, Shangguan proposes integrated provision of public services at county level and registering household residence where people live so that migrants share local social insurance, housing and schooling rights. The author also proposes strengthening county-level industries that enrich residents and encouraging talent, land, capital, industry and information to flow into the countryside. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of the policy rationale and measures for urban–rural integration after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Improving the institutions and mechanisms for integrated urban–rural development is the necessary choice for filling the weak points of agriculture and rural areas and building a strong agricultural country.
quoteZh: 完善城乡融合发展体制机制，是补上农业农村短板、建设农业强国的必然选择

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's own path to modernization, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official economic goal emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A stated goal of socialism in which prosperity is shared by all, with reduced gaps between regions, urban and rural areas, and income groups.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop agriculture, villages and farmers' incomes.

t: The system of people's congresses as a great creation in the history of China's political development
zh: 人民代表大会制度是中国政治发展史上的伟大创造
paras: Zhang Yuan, an associate professor at the Central Party School, argues that the system of people's congresses is not only a great creation in China's political history but also in the history of human political institutions. Written after Xi Jinping's speech marking the 70th anniversary of the National People's Congress (NPC), the article presents the system as China's fundamental political system and as the main institutional vehicle of whole-process people's democracy. Its claim is that the system suits Chinese conditions, secures popular sovereignty and offers an alternative to Western democratic models.

The article has four sections. The first traces the system's growth from the workers' and peasants' bodies of the 1920s through the Jinggangshan congresses, the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia border-region councils and the liberated-area representative conferences, to the 1953 elections and the 1954 Constitution. The second turns to popular sovereignty, elections and grassroots participation. The third examines governance capacity. The fourth considers the system's wider significance for democratic politics.

Zhang's core argument is that the system integrates Party leadership, the people being masters of the country and law-based governance. Because administrative, supervisory, judicial and procuratorial organs are all created by, and answerable to, the people's congresses, and because democratic centralism governs state power, the author says the state acts coherently and avoids the mutual obstruction attributed to the separation of powers in some Western countries. The article credits the system with electoral safeguards (state-funded elections, said to prevent 'money politics'), with 45 grassroots legislative liaison points set up by the NPC Standing Committee, and with coordinating policies such as drug-price reform. Zhang also contrasts whole-process people's democracy, which spans decisions before, during and after, with Western 'electoral democracy', which the author describes as granting formal rights and little real power.

Zhang concludes that democracy must be concrete and rooted in national history, and that the system offers a reference for other countries seeking models suited to their own conditions. It is judged, in the author's words, by objective national conditions, practical results and the people's own sense of it. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's official-line account of the people's congress system's origins, claimed advantages and its comparison with Western democracy.
quoteEn: Democracy is not abstract but concrete, embodied in the different political practices of countries around the world; it is not singular or fixed but diverse, growing from each country's culture and real conditions and reflecting the wisdom and creativity of its people.
quoteZh: 民主不是抽象的而是具体的，体现在世界各国不同的政治实践中；民主不是单一的、固化的，而是丰富多彩的，成长于世界各国的文化和现实土壤之中，体现各国人民的智慧与创造。

glossary.explanation: China's fundamental political system, in which congresses from township to national level are elected and hold state power, with the National People's Congress at the top. It was established by the 1954 Constitution.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019 holding that democracy covers all stages of governance (election, consultation, decision-making, management, supervision), not only voting.
A Leninist organising principle of the Communist Party and the state, combining discussion and election from below with unified decision-making and discipline from above.

glossary.literal: to take charge of the household and make decisions
glossary.explanation: A standard phrase in Party discourse meaning that the people hold ultimate power in the state.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground: the core logic and practical guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture
zh: 守正创新：习近平文化思想的核心逻辑与实践遵循
paras: Writing in Jiangsu Social Sciences (2024, no. 5), Cao Jinsong examines Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and argues that its core logic and practical guide is "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" (shouzheng chuangxin). In Cao's account, this method expresses the inner logic that cultural and ideological work must follow. It is also the foundation for building a modern Chinese civilization and creating a new form of human civilization through Chinese modernization.

The article has four main sections. The first unpacks the meaning of the concept from three angles: individual consciousness, creative practice, and the dialectic of historical development. The second argues that the guiding value of "upholding principles" should keep enriching theoretical innovation, through truth, practice, the people and core values. The third turns to culture-centred development, grouped under four formulas: using culture to educate people, benefit the people, nourish cities and boost industry. The fourth sets out four "lineages" to strengthen: the soul, the roots, scholarship and the cultural thread.

Cao's central move is to read the formula through Xi Jinping's statement that upholding principles means safeguarding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, the Two Integrations, and the Party's cultural leadership and the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity. Innovation means new ideas, discourse, mechanisms and forms. Cao holds that the two are internally unified: upholding principles serves better innovation, and innovation serves firmer adherence. Cao then reads the thought as uniting truth with value, so that Marxist principles are joined with the value of excellent traditional culture.

Cao's practical proposals include arming minds with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, protecting cultural heritage, building a philosophy and social science system with Chinese characteristics, and pursuing the national cultural digitalization strategy. The conclusion calls for more scholarly interpretation of the thought's system, closer study of its internal logic, and summing up its practical experience. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-theory exposition of how Xi Jinping Thought on Culture frames its method and its links to cities, public services, the humanistic economy and digital culture.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground is the core logic and practical guide of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture; its meaning is rich, and it reveals the inner logic that ideological and cultural construction must follow.
quoteZh: 守正创新是习近平文化思想的核心逻辑与实践遵循，内涵十分丰富，揭示了思想文化建设必须遵循的内在逻辑。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
glossary.literal: guarding what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: A method stressed in Xi Jinping's discourse, combining adherence to core Marxist and Party principles with innovation in theory and practice.
A body of ideas on cultural work, formally put forward in 2023 and presented as an important part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in 2021–23.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
The idea that Chinese culture should keep its own independent character and self-awareness, stressed in Xi's 2023 remarks on culture.

glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi in 2023, referring to a civilization that continues Chinese tradition while being built through Chinese modernization.

t: A pioneer of contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy
st: A study of Chen Xianda's philosophical thought
zh: 当代中国马克思主义哲学研究的开拓者
zhSub: 陈先达哲学思想研究
paras: Written shortly after the death of the Marxist philosopher and educator Chen Xianda (1930–2024) on 10 October 2024, this commemorative appraisal presents Chen as a pioneer and leading figure of contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy. Hao Lixin argues that Chen's work combined philosophical depth with practical concern, and that he carried on Marxism's practical character and critical spirit under the maxim that "philosophers are not onlookers of society".

The article opens with a biographical summary of Chen's posts, honours, textbooks and collected works, then proceeds through four thematic sections. These cover Chen's insistence on practice and engagement with reality, his research on the history of Marxist thought, his problem-oriented approach to Marxism and Chinese traditional culture, and his philosophical essays written for general readers.

Hao's central claims are as follows. On the history of Marxist philosophy, Hao credits Chen with pioneering systematic studies, including The History of Marx and Engels's Thought, Studies on Marx's Early Thought and Towards the Depths of History. Chen's method, in Hao's account, joins history with logic, treats Marxism as an integrated whole, and rejects attempts to set the "young Marx" against mature Marxism, so as to avoid dogmatism. On culture, Hao reports that Chen saw adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and modernising traditional culture as two sides of one process. Chen used the phrase "an old country with a new mission" to argue that Marxism and traditional culture must not be treated as opposites, and he grounded cultural confidence in traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture alike. Hao also stresses Chen's opposition to historical nihilism and to cultural conservatism.

Hao concludes that Chen was a model for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and for popularising it. Chen did this through essay collections such as Strolling and Musing, in which he explained abstract principles in everyday language, and through a conviction that Marxist teaching is both a profession and a belief. Hao ends with the line that the philosopher has died but his thought endures. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-academic assessment of Chen Xianda's career and of the methodological principles that shaped a generation of Chinese Marxist philosophy, historical materialism and the debate on Marxism and traditional culture.)
quoteEn: Adapting Marxism to China means, in the final analysis, taking Chinese reality as the foundation and the solution of China's problems as the guide.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化，说到底就是立足中国现实，以解决中国问题为指针。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary problems. It is a standard framing in Party theory.
A concept stressed in Party discourse since the 2010s. It holds that China should be confident in its traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture.
A label used in Chinese official and academic writing for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's and the nation's history.

glossary.en: an old country with a new mission
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the Classic of Poetry. Chen used it to describe socialist China as the contemporary form of an ancient country.
Marx's materialist conception of history, which explains social development through material production and social relations.

t: Studying Deng Xiaoping's educational theory to open a new phase in building a leading education country
zh: 学习邓小平教育理论开拓教育强国建设新局面
source: Journal of CPC History Studies, 5 September 2024
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, Huai Jinpeng asks what Deng's educational theory offers for building a leading education country (jiaoyu qiangguo) today. Huai argues that the theory, formed from Deng's 1977 decision to restore the college entrance examination and his wider handling of education within socialism with Chinese characteristics, is a new development of Marxist educational theory. The task now, Huai says, is to study, inherit and carry it forward.

The short commentary takes five themes from Deng's thinking. They are Party leadership and the socialist orientation of schooling, the strategic priority of education, the "Three Orientations", the central role of teachers, and the present-day tasks that follow. Each theme pairs Deng's statements with Xi Jinping's more recent formulations.

Huai's central claim is that Deng's positions underpin current policy. Deng held that schools must put a firm political direction first, that all-round moral, intellectual and physical development is the standard for training talent, and that education must "face modernization, the world and the future". Huai presents this last principle as the essence of the theory. Huai links these ideas to Xi's view that who to train, how to train them and for whom is the fundamental question, and to the goal of a leading education country by 2035. Huai also stresses integrated planning of education, science and technology, and talent, and says teachers are the key to training qualified people.

Huai concludes that the guiding principle must be Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, together with a firm grasp of the Two Establishes. Huai calls for education to support Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and for a corps of high-calibre, professional teachers. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state education officials link Deng Xiaoping's legacy to current education policy.
quoteEn: The \"Three Orientations\" are the essence of Deng Xiaoping's educational theory.
quoteZh: “三个面向”是邓小平教育理论的精髓。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of making China a world leader in education, with a target of 2035. It has been promoted in Xi Jinping-era Party documents.
Deng Xiaoping's 1983 inscription that education should face modernization, the world and the future.
A formulation from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, as set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in Party discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream and a modern, strong China by mid-century.

t: The principles and direction of the "Two Integrations" in adapting Marxism to China, seen through Mao Zedong's philosophy
zh: 从毛泽东哲学透视马克思主义中国化“两个结合”的原则与走向
source: Public account of the School of Marxism, Peking University, 5 September 2024
paras: Xue Guangzhou asks how the "Two Integrations" (combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture) should be understood, applied and developed, and answers from the standpoint of Mao Zedong's philosophy. The article argues that both integrations must rest on seeking truth from facts, on the Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method, and on a critical, selective treatment of tradition. It also maintains that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context points towards a "new Chinese philosophy".

The article has three parts. The first clarifies the terms: what counts as "China's concrete realities" and as "fine traditional culture". The second sets out basic principles for each of the two integrations and warns against several tendencies. The third traces the future path of the adaptation of Marxist philosophy. Xue draws on Mao's formulations, Marx and Engels's 1872 preface to the Communist Manifesto, and Xi Jinping's statements on culture.

Xue holds that "concrete realities" means above all the principal contradiction of Chinese society at each stage, and that neoliberal economics is detached from them. Xue distinguishes the "quintessence" (jingsui) of traditional culture, a factual judgement about its core, from its "essence" or best elements (jinghua), a value judgement made from the present. Xue proposes "zhong" (the mean, or centrality) as the quintessence, carrying harmony, unity, rectitude and greatness. Following Mao, Xue sets out five principles: take the best and discard the dross, critical inheritance, serving the present, a hundred schools contending, and holding to the Marxist standpoint. Xue warns against treating Marxism and Chinese culture as equal partners in a cultural fusion, against equating revival with a Confucian restoration, and against reading Xi Jinping's thought on culture as merely continuing tradition or an orthodox lineage (daotong).

Xue sees a logical sequence: the adaptation of Marxist philosophy, then adapted Marxist philosophy, then Chinese Marxist philosophy, then a new Chinese philosophy. The last would absorb the best of traditional Chinese philosophy and of human thought, while keeping the Marxist soul. Xue credits Mao with pioneering work and says Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opens a new stage, tied to building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system. Read the original if you want a Marxist-philosophical, Mao-centred account of how the Two Integrations should be applied and what they are said to lead to.
quoteEn: In the integration of the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities, "China's concrete realities" means the specific conditions of society determined by the principal contradiction that exists in Chinese society today and by its social character.
quoteZh: 马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合，其中所说的“中国具体实际”，指的是中国社会当下所存在的主要矛盾及其社会性质所决定的社会具体状况。

glossary.explanation: Formula that Xi Jinping stated in 2021 and later expanded: combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It is now a core principle of Party theory on adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for those parts of China's historical culture that the Party regards as worth inheriting and developing, as distinct from material it treats as feudal dross.

A body of ideas on cultural work, first named at the national conference on propaganda and ideological work in October 2023, and presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.pinyin: qǔ qí jīnghuá, qù qí zāopò
glossary.en: take the best and discard the dross
glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Mao Zedong for treating inherited culture: absorb its useful elements and reject the feudal or backward ones.

glossary.literal: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend
glossary.explanation: A policy Mao Zedong announced in 1956 to encourage diversity and debate in the arts and sciences.

t: Keeping the tree of theory evergreen
zh: 让理论之树常青
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 10 September 2024, responds to Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth. Huang argues that Deng Xiaoping Theory is an important milestone in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The author also holds that it must be studied and applied creatively rather than dogmatically, so that "the tree of theory" stays evergreen.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why Deng Xiaoping Theory is a milestone. The second explains how to study and use it today. The third links it to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and to the continuing task of theoretical innovation. Throughout, Huang relies heavily on quotations from Xi, Deng and Mao Zedong.

On the first point, Huang says the theory emerged while socialism with Chinese characteristics was being opened up after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). It laid the foundation for the Party's system of theory. It addressed the question of what socialism is and how to build it, and it located the essence of socialism in liberating and developing the productive forces, eliminating exploitation and polarization, and reaching common prosperity. On the second point, Huang calls for a complete and accurate grasp of the theory as an interconnected whole, read in its historical context. Huang insists that what guides practice over the long term is its basic principles and the Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method, not particular phrases. Emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts are called its essence. Creative application means upholding Deng's major conclusions while adjusting to changing circumstances.

Huang presents Xi Jinping Thought as a new leap in adapting Marxism, calling it contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. It builds on Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. The author names the Two Integrations as the fundamental path of adaptation and the "six musts" as its method. The commentary calls on Party members to take Chinese modernization as the soil for further innovation and to answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames Deng Xiaoping Theory's place in the Party's theoretical lineage.
quoteEn: Taking Marxism as a guide means using its scientific worldview and methodology to solve China's problems, not reciting and repeating its specific conclusions and phrases, still less treating Marxism as an unchanging dogma.
quoteZh: 坚持以马克思主义为指导，是要运用其科学的世界观和方法论解决中国的问题，而不是要背诵和重复其具体结论和词句，更不能把马克思主义当成一成不变的教条。

glossary.explanation: The body of ideas associated with Deng Xiaoping on reform, opening up and building socialism with Chinese characteristics. The 15th Party Congress (1997) wrote it into the Party's guiding ideology.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. It is used to present successive leaders' theories as innovations within Marxism.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is promoted as the fundamental path of adapting Marxism in China.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path to a modern socialist country, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The goal of prosperity shared by all, which Deng Xiaoping listed as the end point of socialism and which has been emphasised again in recent years.

t: Deng Xiaoping and strengthening the Party's leadership over propaganda, ideological and cultural work
zh: 邓小平与加强党对宣传思想文化工作的领导
paras: Song Yuehong asks how Deng Xiaoping guided the Party's propaganda, ideological and cultural work during reform and opening up, and why this mattered for the Party's fate. The article argues that Deng set the correct direction for this work by re-establishing the Marxist ideological line, holding to the Four Cardinal Principles, and drawing lessons from the Party's history, thereby upholding and strengthening Party leadership over the ideological field.

The article is a historical-political study built on Deng's speeches and talks from 1975 to 1992. It has three main sections: the debate on the criterion of truth and the restoration of the ideological line; the Four Cardinal Principles as the precondition for the four modernizations; and the 1981 Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party since the Founding of the People's Republic of China. A short closing section links these to socialism with Chinese characteristics and to material and spiritual civilization.

Song first presents Deng as opposing the "Two Whatevers" from 1977 on, supporting the 1978 discussion that "practice is the sole criterion of truth" and treating it as a question of whether to liberate thought. In Song's account, this restored "emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts" as the Party's line and prepared the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). Song then reports Deng's 1979 insistence that the four modernizations required adherence to the socialist road, the dictatorship of the proletariat, Party leadership and Marxism-Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought. Deng is shown calling Party leadership the core of the four, criticising bourgeois liberalization, and urging stronger propaganda and education on these principles. Finally, Song describes Deng drafting the Resolution, assessing Mao Zedong's merits as primary and his errors as secondary, and defending Mao Zedong Thought as the guiding ideology.

Song concludes that, under Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Party combined the Four Cardinal Principles with economic construction as the central task and with reform and opening up. In this account, that produced the basic line of the primary stage of socialism and the three-step development strategy, and opened the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Song adds that Deng called for paying equal attention to material and spiritual civilization and for firm action against "spiritual pollution". Read the original if you want a source-rich account, in Deng's own words, of how the official Party narrative links the truth-criterion debate, the Four Cardinal Principles and the 1981 Resolution to ideological leadership.
quoteEn: Upholding the Four Cardinal Principles in ideology and politics is the fundamental precondition for realizing the four modernizations and is the foundation of the state.
quoteZh: 在思想政治上坚持四项基本原则是实现四个现代化的根本前提，是立国之本。

glossary.explanation: Deng Xiaoping's 1979 formulation: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship (dictatorship of the proletariat), Communist Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought. The Party treats them as the political foundation of the state.
A 1977 formula holding that whatever decisions Mao Zedong made and whatever instructions he gave must be upheld. Deng and other reformers opposed it as dogmatic.

glossary.zh: 关于真理标准问题的讨论
glossary.pinyin: guānyú zhēnlǐ biāozhǔn wèntí de tǎolùn
glossary.en: the debate on the criterion of truth
glossary.explanation: A 1978 nationwide discussion launched by an article arguing that practice is the sole criterion of truth. It is regarded in Party history as intellectual preparation for the reform turn.
A Party term for tendencies to adopt Western-style liberal political ideas and to question Party leadership and the socialist system. Deng used it in campaigns of the late 1970s and 1980s.

glossary.zh: 关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议
glossary.pinyin: guānyú jiànguó yǐlái dǎng de ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
glossary.en: Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party since the Founding of the People's Republic of China
glossary.explanation: A 1981 Party document adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 11th Central Committee. It assesses the Cultural Revolution and Mao Zedong's role, and Deng oversaw its drafting.
The official judgement that China is at an early stage of socialism, which is expected to last a long time. It underpins the Party's basic line of one central task and two basic points.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, associated with Deng's call to build socialism suited to Chinese conditions.

t: The profound significance of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building
zh: 深刻领悟习近平总书记关于党的建设的重要思想的重大意义
paras: Gong Yun takes up the significance of what the article calls General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building, which it describes as formed since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article argues that this body of thought answers the question of what kind of long-ruling Marxist party to build and how to build it, and that it has historical, theoretical and practical significance of a major and lasting kind.

The article is organised in three parts that correspond to these three kinds of significance. The first treats the thinking as a response to the times: a world undergoing great changes, the task of national rejuvenation, and the need to solve problems in Party governance. The second sets it within the history of Marxist party-building theory, from the Soviet experience through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. The third turns to its effects in practice.

In its first part, Gong contends that the thinking keeps the Party at the forefront of the times and enables it to deal with problems that had arisen earlier, including weakened Party leadership, formalism, bureaucracy, privilege and corruption. In the second, Gong argues that it answers a question open since the October Revolution, noting that the Soviet party explored it for 74 years before the party and state collapsed. Gong presents the thinking as the 'Party building chapter' of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, organised as 'thirteen adherences' and offered as a Chinese approach for party governance worldwide. In the third, Gong holds that it has reversed the weakening of Party leadership, strengthened the Party through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and secured what the article calls an overwhelming victory in the anti-corruption struggle.

Gong concludes that this thinking provides the fundamental guide for advancing the 'new great project' of Party building and a firm political guarantee for Chinese modernization. The article stresses the decisive role of Party leadership and the Party's self-reform in the course of national rejuvenation and calls for continued, unwavering full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Party theorists frame the importance of Xi's Party-building thought for domestic governance, Marxist party theory and the Party's international claims.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building, through its 'thirteen adherences', forms a complete, logically rigorous and organically unified scientific system, greatly deepens understanding of the laws governing the building of a Marxist ruling party, and is a milestone in the history of Marxist party building.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记关于党的建设的重要思想，以“十三个坚持”构成一个系统完备、逻辑严密、有机统一的科学体系，大大深化了对马克思主义执政党建设规律的认识，在马克思主义政党建设史上具有里程碑意义。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building slogan prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption, ideological work and institutional rules for Party members and organisations.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official concept that the Party must continually correct its own problems through internal discipline and rectification, presented as a source of its long-term governance capacity.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Striving to write a new chapter in building a strong education nation in the new era and on the new journey
zh: 奋力书写新时代新征程教育强国建设崭新篇章
authors: Party Leadership Group of the Ministry of Education
paras: This commentary, issued by the Party Leadership Group of the Ministry of Education and carried in the People's Daily on 16 October 2024, responds to Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference. The authors present the speech as a systematic plan and a call to the whole Party and society to build a strong education nation (教育强国). They state that the education system will carry it out firmly, and they treat the task as a new mission for strengthening education.

The text has three parts. The first explains why the education system should raise its ideological and practical awareness of the task. The second sets out the strategic picture, described as the "four pillars and eight beams" of the project. The third lists priority tasks to be carried out in a spirit of reform and innovation, and a short closing stresses implementation.

In the first part, the authors argue that education's status, the system's responsibilities and the grounds for confidence are all "unprecedented". They cite the 20th Party Congress (2022) goal of a strong education nation by 2035 and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) decision on integrated reform of education, science and technology, and talent. They name challenges: a falling birth rate, an ageing population, and imbalances between people's wish for better education and its uneven development. The second part says construction must follow education's political, popular and strategic attributes and aim at six capacities: ideological and political guidance, talent competitiveness, scientific and technological support, livelihood security, social coordination and international influence. It also calls for a high-quality education system that links basic, higher, vocational and lifelong education. The third part covers fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in textbooks and classrooms. It also covers supporting science, technology and talent, improving public education services, building a high-level teaching force, and making China an education centre with global influence.

The authors conclude that the blueprint must become concrete work plans and responsibilities, carried out with a "nail-driving spirit" and a long-term view. They present this as turning the speech into support for Chinese modernization. The text is an official statement of the ministry's priorities and agenda, with little independent argument. Read the original if you want the education authorities' own account of the goals, vocabulary and policy priorities that followed the 2024 National Education Conference.
quoteEn: The political, popular and strategic attributes of education profoundly reveal the advanced essence, distinctive features and unique strengths of China's socialist education.
quoteZh: 教育的政治属性、人民属性、战略属性，深刻揭示我国社会主义教育的先进本质、鲜明特色、独有优势。

glossary.explanation: A goal set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) of building China into a leading country in education by 2035. It is presented as foundational to national strength and rejuvenation.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and said to differ from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is taught throughout the education system.
The official "fundamental task" of education. It stresses moral and ideological formation alongside knowledge and skills.

t: The milestone significance and innovative achievements of further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的里程碑意义和创新性成果
paras: Writing in the Study Times in September 2024, Jiang Hui interprets the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024) and its decision on further comprehensively deepening reform. The article argues that the plenum is a landmark in the history of reform and opening up and of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In Jiang's account, it opened a new stage in which further comprehensive reform is used to advance Chinese modernization, and it produced practical, theoretical and institutional results.

The commentary is organised under three headings: a new stage of reform and its milestone significance; a new reform layout and its pioneering practical meaning; and new ideological development and its innovative theoretical meaning. It places the plenum alongside the Third Plenums of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the 18th Central Committee (2013). A closing section briefly describes how Chongqing is implementing the plenum's spirit.

Jiang's central move is to present reform as continuous yet staged. The line from "reform" to "comprehensively deepening reform" to "further comprehensively deepening reform" is described as a response to changed conditions, with direction, theme and overall goal unchanged. Jiang contends that the 2024 plenum "upgraded" objectives, development tasks and reform deployment around the central task of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The plenum is said to address high-quality development, new quality productive forces and structural obstacles, led by economic reform and grounded in social fairness and people's wellbeing.

On theory, Jiang holds that the plenum's decision condenses over forty years of experience. It also systematises Xi Jinping's new ideas on comprehensively deepening reform, which Jiang calls the "reform chapter" of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Jiang lists its main principles. They include Party leadership, a people-centred approach, problem orientation, systems thinking, institution-building as the main thread, the rule of law, and opening up. Jiang concludes that this enriches Marxist reform theory and guides the new journey. Read the original if you want an official Party-school account of how the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee is framed historically and theoretically, including a local Party leader's application in Chongqing.
quoteEn: Reform and opening up has only a present continuous tense, never a completed one.
quoteZh: 改革开放只有进行时、没有完成时

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The reform programme launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It covers economic, political, legal, cultural, social and ecological fields and Party building.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
The official term for the development goal that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth alone.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal. It is tied to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The historical roots, value foundations and practical basis of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 中华民族现代文明的历史根源、价值根柢与实践根基
paras: Xiang Jiuyu takes up the concept of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation (中华民族现代文明), a term in current Party theory. The article asks where this new civilizational form comes from, what values underlie it and what practice sustains it. Xiang's thesis is that it is the product of civilizational renewal rather than rupture, distinct from Western modern civilization, and that it answers the long-standing doubt over whether China could create its own modern civilization and pursue modernization independently.

The article is organised in three parts: historical roots, value foundations and practical basis. The roots are examined on three levels: culture, Chinese civilization as a living organism, and world history. The value part discusses national rejuvenation and civilizational flourishing, people-centredness, and the vision of a world of great harmony. The practical part names four supports: Party leadership, coordinated material and spiritual development, innovation, and building a community with a shared future for mankind.
