The sections on inclusiveness and peacefulness are shorter. Shao presents Mao as favouring a critical, selective absorption of Chinese and foreign culture, including Western science and management methods, and as supporting the Common Program, the policy of letting a hundred flowers bloom and academic debate. Mao's repeated calls for peace and peaceful coexistence, alongside firm resistance to aggression, are read as expressions of the "dialectics of war". Shao concludes that we should uphold fundamental principles while innovating, continue the historical lineage and write a contemporary chapter. Read the original if you want a dense, dated collection of Mao's statements on history and culture, organised to fit the official framework of five civilizational characteristics.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong opposed cutting history apart, and held that in cultural inheritance one should take the essence and discard the dross.
quoteZh: 毛泽东反对割裂历史，主张在文化传承上要取其精华，去其糟粕。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 2020s. It is presented as rooted in Chinese conditions and civilization rather than modelled on the West.

glossary.zh: 中华文明五大突出特性
glossary.pinyin: Zhōnghuá wénmíng wǔ dà tūchū tèxìng
glossary.en: five salient characteristics of Chinese civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation attributed to Xi Jinping (2023) describing Chinese civilization as marked by continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness.
The official thesis that China remains at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism, which would last a long time. It became a basic premise of Party policy from the 1980s.

glossary.pinyin: gǔ wéi jīn yòng, yáng wéi Zhōng yòng
glossary.en: making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China
glossary.literal: let the ancient serve the present, let the foreign serve China
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Mao Zedong from the 1950s, calling for critical use of both the Chinese heritage and foreign culture in building a new socialist culture.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi huā qí fàng, bǎi jiā zhēng míng
glossary.en: letting a hundred flowers bloom and academic debate
glossary.literal: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools contend
glossary.explanation: A policy announced in 1956 encouraging diversity in the arts and open debate in scholarship, within limits set by the Party.

t: Deng Xiaoping's major contribution to the methodology of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 邓小平对马克思主义中国化方法论的重大贡献
paras: Tian Keqin asks what Deng Xiaoping added to the methods by which Marxism has been adapted to China. The article argues that Deng upheld, developed and creatively applied this methodology with a high degree of methodological self-awareness. In Tian's account, Deng's constant method was to proceed from reality, from world trends and from national conditions, relying on seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence and self-reliance. Tian presents this as a historic contribution to the methodology of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three parts. The first covers the years from Deng's return to office (1977) to the 12th Party Congress (1982). It deals with the restoration of the Party's ideological line and the assessment of Mao Zedong Thought. The second part examines the theme of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the founding of Deng Xiaoping Theory. The third part sets out how Deng applied the methodology to Chinese modernization, through four methods: seeking truth from facts, the mass line, independence and self-reliance, and dialectical thinking.

Tian argues that Deng first restored the authority of practice as the test of truth, against the "two whatevers". Deng then protected Mao Zedong Thought as a coherent system and identified its "living soul" in seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence. Tian then reads Deng's key concepts as methodological applications. The primary stage of socialism is presented as the basis grounded in seeking truth from facts. Common prosperity and reliance on the people are traced to the mass line. Deng's "Chinese-style modernization", framed in terms of xiaokang (a moderately well-off household), is linked to independence and self-reliance. The "one central task, two basic points" layout and the "two-handed" approach are credited to dialectical thinking. Tian also stresses Deng's view that the Four Cardinal Principles are the political precondition of modernization.

Tian concludes that Deng combined Marxist fundamentals with China's conditions and the features of the era, and so gave the Party's later theory its methodological foundation. The article calls on the Party today to build on this methodology. It names the "six musts" of the new era as the Party's shared language, and calls for advancing the theory of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times together with Chinese modernization in practice. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Deng's thought is placed within the sequence from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping's new era.
quoteEn: Deng Xiaoping firmly grasped the ideological line as the fundamental question of ideological method.
quoteZh: 邓小平紧紧抓住了思想路线这个根本性思想方法问题

glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping that policy should start from actual conditions, not from dogma. Party theory treats it as the core of the Party's ideological line.
The Party's method of leadership 'from the masses, to the masses': gathering popular views, refining them into policy, and returning them to the people. It was developed under Mao Zedong.
A 1977 formula holding that whatever policy decisions Mao made, and whatever instructions he gave, must be upheld. Deng and reformers opposed it during the debate on the criterion of truth.
The official judgement that China is in an underdeveloped, long-lasting early phase of socialism. Party policy is meant to be based on this.
The official name for China's path to modernization, distinguished from Western models. Deng used the phrase in 1979, and it has been central to Party discourse in the Xi Jinping era.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all, rather than polarisation. Deng linked it to letting some people and regions get rich first.

glossary.pinyin: yí gè zhōngxīn, liǎng gè jīběndiǎn
glossary.en: one central task, two basic points
glossary.explanation: The Party's basic line for the primary stage of socialism, formalised at the 13th Party Congress (1987). The central task is economic development; the two basic points are the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up.

t: On the value outlook of Mao Zedong's thought of "serving the people"
zh: 论毛泽东“为人民服务”思想的价值观
source: Zhonghua Hun (China Soul) WeChat account, 8 September 2024
paras: Niu Baoliang asks why Mao Zedong's thought of "serving the people" could become the political purpose of the whole Chinese Communist Party. The article's answer is that it rests on a Marxist view of class, of life and of practice, and that the three are unified in one value outlook. Niu limits the discussion to the period of the New Democratic Revolution.

The article is organised in three numbered sections. The first links the value outlook to the class outlook, the second to the outlook on life, and the third to the outlook on practice. Niu draws on Mao's texts from 1925 to 1945, including "Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society", the 1944 speech "Serve the People", "On Coalition Government" and the 1945 Party Constitution. The article also cites Lenin, the Communist Manifesto and early Party programmes.

Niu argues first that a party's character follows the class it represents. As a Marxist party recognising the people as creators of history, the Party represents the fundamental interests of the proletariat and the broad masses. Mao's class analysis separated enemies from the people, and Niu presents this as the basis for the claim that the Party and its armies serve the people. Second, Niu reads Mao's speech at Zhang Side's memorial, with its image of a death "heavier than Mount Tai", as defining the life value of Communists. Mao's call for "wholehearted" service was written into the 1945 Party Constitution, which demanded close ties with the masses and warned against tailism, commandism, bureaucratism and warlordism. Third, the article sets out how value became practice, from the 1921 programme and the minimum and maximum programmes of 1922 to the united fronts and the land revolution. Niu explains the alliance with the national bourgeoisie by China's small working class and weak capitalism.

Niu concludes that the thought is the Party's unified value outlook and, logically and objectively, its outlook on class, life and practice, in line with historical materialism. For Niu, the divide between Communists and bourgeois parties lies in a people-centred view of history as against a view centred on heroes. Niu also warns against tailism, meaning doing whatever the masses demand, which would deny the leader's role and weaken the Party's core and its correct leadership. Read the original if you want a Party-school account of how the New Democratic Revolution-era texts on serving the people are tied to Marxist class theory.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's thought of "serving the people" is not only the Party's unified value outlook; logically and objectively it is also the whole Party's outlook on class, on life and on practice.
quoteZh: 毛泽东“为人民服务”的思想不仅是全党统一的价值观，其在逻辑上和客观上还是全党的阶级观、人生观和实践观。

glossary.explanation: A slogan from Mao Zedong's 1944 speech at the memorial for the soldier Zhang Side. It later became the declared political purpose of the Communist Party.

Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution, roughly 1919–1949, aimed at overthrowing imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism under proletarian leadership. It was seen as a transition towards socialism.
A term in Party language for trailing behind the masses' spontaneous demands instead of leading them. It is criticised as abandoning the Party's leadership role.
The Party's strategy of allying with other classes and parties against a main enemy while keeping its own leadership and independence.

t: Mao Zedong's leadership of the "Second Integration" during the War of Liberation: a great achievement
zh: 毛泽东领导解放战争时期开创“第二个结合”的伟大成就
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2024 no. 1
paras: Liu Shulin asks how Mao Zedong, between June 1946 and September 1949, combined Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, and argues that this period opened a new chapter in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. In Liu's account, the Chinese Communists faced a civil war launched by the Kuomintang with US backing. Mao responded by repeatedly drawing on, and transforming, China's cultural heritage, which Liu presents as the practice of what is now called the Second Integration.

The article is organised in six thematic sections, each pairing a traditional idea with Mao's reworking of it. These are the "Great Harmony" ideal and the pursuit of communism; the old "people as the root" tradition and the scientific concept of "the people"; popular dignity and backbone against imperialism; the classical phrase "self-reliance" and its modern political meaning; the military history of Nanyang, invoked in a 1948 news dispatch; and Sunzi's maxim against pursuing a cornered enemy. Liu draws on Mao's speeches, telegrams, poems and editorial writing from 1946 to 1949.

Liu's central claim is that Mao did not simply revive tradition but changed its class content. The ancient Great Harmony ideal, Liu says, was a recollection of primitive communism, and only Marxism and the Party could turn it into a real path. Likewise, ancient min-ben ("people-rooted") thought did not mean "the people" in the modern sense. Liu traces how Mao defined the people as a united front of workers, peasants, urban petty bourgeoisie and national bourgeoisie under working-class leadership, culminating in "people's democratic dictatorship" in 1949. Liu also reads Mao's rewriting of "do not pursue a cornered enemy" as "pursue the enemy with our remaining courage" as a shift from tactics to grand strategy and social transformation. Liu adds that Mao used the story of Wen Yiduo and Zhu Ziqing to turn traditional moral backbone into anti-imperialist resolve, and presented self-reliance as the basis for securing peace.

Liu concludes that these cases show Mao fusing Marxism-Leninism with fine traditional culture, and links them to later ideas such as "putting the people at the centre" and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Liu's view, the establishment of the new China turned the Great Harmony ideal from utopia into practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-heavy account of how Mao's wartime texts used classical Chinese references, and how Chinese scholars now frame them as an early form of the Second Integration.
quoteEn: "Pursue the enemy with our remaining courage, and do not seek empty fame like the Hegemon-King" means insisting on carrying the revolution through to the end.
quoteZh: “宜将剩勇追穷寇，不可沽名学霸王”就意味着坚持将革命进行到底。

glossary.explanation: The Party's formulation, stressed by Xi Jinping from 2021–2023, of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the first being Marxism with China's concrete realities.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".
Mao's 1949 formula for the state of the new China: democracy within the "people" and dictatorship over those classed as reactionaries. It remains a constitutional description of China's state system.

glossary.literal: relying on one's own strength to be reborn
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan, used from the Anti-Japanese War period, of depending mainly on one's own efforts rather than outside help. It later became a basic principle of policy in the People's Republic.

glossary.en: putting the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A principle of Xi Jinping-era Party theory that development and governance should centre on the people's interests; the article treats it as a descendant of the Party's earlier concept of "the people".

t: Developing new quality productive forces urgently requires winning five innovation campaigns
zh: 发展新质生产力亟待打好五大创新战役
paras: Fan Jida, a professor and vice-dean at the Central Party School's graduate school, asks how China should put innovation at the centre of developing new quality productive forces. Writing in a Party journal after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the author argues that innovation must be pursued through five "campaigns". These are a battle over key core technologies, a protracted war in basic research, a contest for innovative talent, a breakthrough battle for enterprises, and a positional battle in regional innovation.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's description of new quality productive forces as an inherent requirement of high-quality development. It then takes each campaign in turn and ties it to the Plenum's reform decisions. Fan draws on national figures, such as R&D spending, the share of basic research and manufacturing R&D intensity. Historical examples include Britain's lead in the first industrial revolution and Germany's in the second.

In the author's account, key core technologies are still often controlled by others, so China needs a new whole-nation system. Fan stresses that this system is not a return to the planned economy and does not replace private-enterprise innovation. It would work under unified Party leadership, with market, government and society acting together. Basic research is called the root of many "bottleneck" problems. The author notes that it received only 6.65% of the 2023 R&D budget of 3,327.8 billion yuan, and calls for stable funding, fewer non-research burdens for scientists and new evaluation standards. On talent, Fan proposes prioritising education, nurturing young scientists and engineers, attracting overseas experts, possibly through a high-skilled immigration system, and judging people by contribution. Enterprises are described as hindered by an inability, unwillingness or reluctance to innovate. Fan proposes wider roles for firms in setting national research agendas, R&D reserve funds, "patient capital" and stronger intellectual property protection. Regionally, the author proposes a networked pattern led by Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. It would use technology to upgrade traditional industries and develop future ones, and stay open to international cooperation.

Fan concludes that new quality productive forces need matching production relations. That means reforming the science and technology system, improving incentives, and building a stronger environment for talent and enterprises. The article is a policy-oriented interpretation of Party decisions, not a theoretical study. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how a Central Party School scholar translates the Third Plenum's innovation agenda into concrete priorities, with statistics on R&D, basic research and talent.
quoteEn: This \"whole-nation system\" is by no means the government taking charge of everything, nor a substitute for private-enterprise innovation, and still less a return to the management system of the planned-economy period.
quoteZh: 这一“举国体制”绝不是政府包揽一切，不是对民营企业创新的替代，更不是回到计划经济时期的管理体制

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It denotes an advanced form of productive forces driven by innovation and high technology, moving away from traditional growth models.
The official aim for China's economy since around 2017. It stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
A model for mobilising state, market and social resources behind strategic technology goals under Party leadership. The article distinguishes it from the planned economy.
Colloquial term for technologies on which China is dependent on foreign suppliers and which can be used to constrain it.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024)
glossary.explanation: A Central Committee meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform. The article cites its innovation-related provisions.

t: Studying Deng Xiaoping's educational theory to open a new phase in building a leading country in education
zh: 学习邓小平教育理论开拓教育强国建设新局面
source: Studies on CPC History (中共党史研究), 2024 no. 4
paras: This is a speech by Huai Jinpeng, Minister of Education, given at the opening of the national academic symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth (published in 2024). Huai argues that Deng's educational theory, a new development of Marxist educational theory with distinct Chinese features, should guide efforts to build a leading country in education.

Huai begins with Deng's 1977 decision to restore the national college entrance examination, which he describes as a breakthrough in setting right the errors of the previous period. The speech then takes five themes in turn: Party leadership and the socialist orientation of schooling, the priority of education, the "Three Orientations", the role of teachers, and the tasks for today. Each theme pairs Deng's statements with remarks by Xi Jinping.

In Huai's account, Deng held that schools must put a firm and correct political direction first, and that "cultivating new socialist people is itself politics". Deng also placed education in a position of strategic priority and called for respect for knowledge and talent. His call for education to face modernization, the world and the future is called the essence of the theory. Huai links each point to current policy: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, moral education, the integrated advancement of education, science and technology, and talent, and the goal of a leading education country by 2035. He calls teachers the key to producing qualified talent.

Huai concludes that studying Deng's theory means above all following Xi Jinping Thought, applying Xi's discourse on education and grasping the decisive significance of the Two Establishes. He calls for planning ahead, meeting change and opening new ground, so that education supports the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a short, official example of how the Education Ministry ties Deng-era theory to current education policy.
quoteEn: Comrade Deng Xiaoping explicitly proposed that education should face modernization, the world and the future. The \"Three Orientations\" are the essence of Deng Xiaoping's educational theory.
quoteZh: 邓小平同志明确提出教育要面向现代化，面向世界，面向未来。“三个面向”是邓小平教育理论的精髓。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the "core" of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since it was written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, usually dated to the 2012 Party Congress. It is tied to building a modern socialist country by mid-century.
Deng Xiaoping's 1983 inscription that education should face modernization, the world and the future.
A goal set by the Party in 2023–24 to make China a world-leading education system by 2035.

t: Mao Zedong's work method of having a firm grasp of the "numbers"
zh: 毛泽东胸中有“数”的工作方法
paras: Lü Zhen examines the work method that Mao Zedong summarised in 1949 as having a firm grasp of the "numbers" (胸中有“数”). The article argues that Mao creatively applied the materialist-dialectical law of the mutual transformation of quantity and quality to leading the Chinese revolution and construction. In Lü's reading, the quotation marks around "numbers" mark the word's literal sense of figures and quantities, not the everyday sense of "having a good idea" of a situation.

The article is organised in five parts: the demand for scientific and meticulous work; how this grasp comes from investigation and study; the need to "see the big picture, reckon the big accounts and plan the big numbers"; attention to "degree" (度); and the move from having the "numbers" to effective action. Lü draws on Mao's 1949 speech at the Second Plenary Session of the 7th Central Committee, his notes on philosophical works, the 1930 Xunwu investigation, "On Protracted War", and military and land-reform documents from 1947–48.

Lü's central claim is that quantitative analysis serves, and does not replace, judgement about essentials. Investigation must be done properly, as in the Xunwu report with its detailed class percentages and trade figures, which the author says supplied the basis for policy on rich peasants and land distribution. Numbers must also be selected from the standpoint of the whole situation: Lü reads Mao's reckoning in "On Protracted War" and his stress on uniting the great majority as examples of reckoning big accounts, citing Lenin against picking isolated facts. Finally, "degree", the quantitative limit that determines quality, let Mao periodise the civil war and set policy lines. Lü cites his troop-strength calculations in 1947–48 and his differentiated land-reform tactics for old and newer liberated areas.

Lü concludes that Mao both proposed and exemplified this method, which has long helped Party cadres improve their leadership. The article presents it as relevant to the new tasks of advancing national strengthening and national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, where precision is said to be both a work requirement and an expression of Marxist epistemology. Lü ties this to seeking truth from facts and the dialectical unity of quality and quantity. Read the original if you want a detailed, document-based account of how Mao's quantitative and investigative methods are presented in Party-history scholarship, and how they are linked to present-day cadre training.
quoteEn: The work method of having a firm grasp of the "numbers" is a valuable experience Mao Zedong drew from the practice of the Chinese revolution and construction, a creative development of the laws of Marxist philosophy in a Chinese form, and it has rich ideological content.
quoteZh: 胸中有“数”的工作方法，是毛泽东从中国革命和建设实践中总结得出的宝贵经验，是对马克思主义哲学规律的中国化的创造性发展，具有丰富的思想内涵。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctive path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article invokes it as the setting for present-day cadre work.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, stressing that policy should start from actual conditions. It is treated as the core of the Party's ideological line.

glossary.en: the law of the mutual transformation of quantity and quality
glossary.explanation: One of the basic laws of materialist dialectics: gradual quantitative change reaches a limit and produces qualitative change, and vice versa.
The official goal of the "rejuvenation of the Chinese nation", a central theme of Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A Maoist method of gathering first-hand facts on the ground before making policy, summed up in his slogan "no investigation, no right to speak".

t: Mao Zedong's historical contribution to the "Two Integrations" and its lessons
zh: 毛泽东对“两个结合”的历史贡献及其经验启示
source: Research on Marxist Theory in Higher Education (Gaoxiao Makesizhuyi lilun yanjiu), 2024 no. 2
paras: Xi Jinping's formulation of the Two Integrations (2021) joins the basic tenets of Marxism to China's concrete realities and to its fine traditional culture. Ding and Chen argue that this is not a new problem. In their account, Mao Zedong, as pioneer and founder of the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, made foundational contributions to both integrations, and these offer lessons for the present.

The article has three parts. It first asks why Mao was able to advance the Two Integrations, citing objective needs (China's historic tasks, the failure of earlier ideologies, and the tension between a Western-born theory and Chinese conditions) and subjective conditions (his classical learning, his study of Marxist texts, and independent practical exploration). It then sets out his contributions to each integration. Finally it draws lessons for the new era.

On the first integration, the authors credit Mao with proposing, in 1938, the proposition of the "sinification of Marxism". They read it as having two sides: Marxism taking Chinese form, and Chinese practice being raised into Marxist theory. They cite his methods of investigation, contradiction analysis and the mass line, and treat Mao Zedong Thought as the first historic leap. On the second integration, they argue that Mao transformed traditional culture through Marxism (for example reinterpreting "seeking truth from facts"). He also set principles for treating heritage, namely keeping the essence and discarding the dross, critical inheritance, and "letting a hundred flowers bloom". In addition, he expressed Marxism in national forms and a new literary style, helping to create a new national culture.

The authors draw three lessons. The Party should arm itself with its innovative theory and keep a practice-based style of study. It should ground itself in China's national conditions amid the "changes unseen in a century". It should pursue the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, so that Marxism becomes "Chinese". They present Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as continuing Mao's project. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of Mao as precursor of the Two Integrations, or the genealogy behind current official discourse on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong was the principal creator of the new culture of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 毛泽东是中华民族新文化的主要缔造者。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping's July 2021 speech for the Party's centenary: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to the older idea of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's circumstances. "Times" was added to the older "sinification" in recent Party documents.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The Party's official term for the Chinese form of Marxism developed under Mao. It was made the guiding ideology at the Seventh Party Congress in 1945.
The policy slogan "let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend", announced in 1956 to encourage open debate in the arts and sciences.
A Party method of leadership associated with Mao. Opinions are gathered from the masses, concentrated into policy, and then tested again in practice with them.

t: Four relationships to grasp in building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明要把握好的几个关系
paras: Liu Cang takes up what building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation requires, calling it a systemic project that spans the economy and society, domestic affairs, foreign affairs and defence. The article, a commentary in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts, argues that the task depends on handling four dialectical relationships correctly. Liu presents these as reflecting the development laws of subject and object, past and future, content and form, source and stream.

The text is organised in four sections: tradition and modernity; culture and civilization; unity and plurality; and Chinese civilization and world civilization. Each section ends by claiming that getting the relationship right lets the modern civilization stand at a particular 'commanding height': historical, ideological and cultural, that of national righteousness, and that of human civilization.

On tradition and modernity, Liu holds that modern China continues and develops historical China, and that modern civilization is an innovative sublimation of ancient civilization. Without the ancient, the modern becomes 'water without a source'; without the modern, the ancient becomes 'a river that runs dry'. The author calls for protection and transmission, and for creative transformation and innovative development of fine traditional culture. On culture and civilization, Liu treats civilization as the overall state of a social formation, with socialism with Chinese characteristics as its social basis. The cultural form of Chinese modernization is described as its discursive expression. Liu links this to the cultural mission of the new era, to the Four-sphere Confidence, the Two Integrations and Xi Jinping's cultural thought.

On unity and plurality, Liu argues that Chinese civilization was created jointly by all ethnic groups and that the modern civilization is a 'plural yet unified' picture. Liu cites the Party's work on forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation as its foundation. On China and the world, Liu says Chinese modernization, as a new form of human civilization, offers solutions to global problems and supports a community with a shared future for mankind. This rests on exchange and mutual learning among civilizations rather than one replacing another. Liu concludes by calling for China's concepts of development, civilization, security, human rights and global governance to be explained abroad, so that the world understands China. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party-journal author sets out the conceptual structure of the 'modern civilization of the Chinese nation' under Xi Jinping's cultural thought.
quoteEn: Without ancient civilization, modern civilization would become water without a source; without modern civilization, ancient civilization would become a river that has run dry.
quoteZh: 离开古代文明，现代文明将成为无源之水；没有现代文明，古代文明也将成为断流之河。

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 to describe a civilization built on the basis of Chinese civilization's continuity and socialism. It is presented as the cultural counterpart of Chinese modernization.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy and global-governance concept, promoted since 2012–13, calling for shared security, development and exchange among nations.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding line for ethnic affairs since the 2010s, stressing shared national identity among all ethnic groups.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: The value implications, logical path and development principles of the "Second Integration"
zh: “第二个结合”的价值意蕴、逻辑理路和发展原则
source: Journal of Hohai University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2024 no. 4
paras: Zhang Haifang asks what the "Second Integration", the combination of the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, means, how it works and what principles should guide it. The article argues that the two traditions share many affinities, that Marxism has gradually become the dominant ideology in China through this combination, and that the process is a two-way "mutual transformation" in which each side is changed and each fulfils the other.

The article is organised in three parts. The first examines value implications: the Communist Party as the driving agent, Marxism "transforming" traditional culture, and traditional culture "transforming" Marxism. The second sets out a logical path in three registers: theoretical, historical and value logic. The third derives development principles from the "six musts" that the article presents as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Zhang's core move is to treat the integration as a dialectical process with stages. Theoretically, it moves from mutual fit (for example, ideas of "all under heaven for the public" and the Great Harmony set beside Marxist ideas of human emancipation and communism), through mutual selection, to mutual fulfilment. Historically, it moves from formal analogy in concepts and language around the May Fourth period (Guo Moruo's "Marx Enters the Confucian Temple"), to creative development of content (Mao Zedong's reading of "seeking truth from facts", On Practice and On Contradiction), to a higher level that joins the "soul" (Marxism) with the "root" (traditional culture). The author adds that this higher level does not negate the earlier ones. In terms of value, the integration is said to reveal a general law of how Marxism takes national forms and to offer a lesson on treating tradition in modernization.

The article concludes that the Second Integration should be guided by six principles: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systemic thinking, and a global outlook. Zhang says these require resisting dogmatism, historical nihilism, cultural revivalism and "Western-centrism", and that they would allow Marxism's adaptation to the Chinese context and the needs of our times to advance further. Read the original if you want a systematic statement, in current Party-theory language, of how Chinese scholars justify and structure the Second Integration.
quoteEn: Without upholding fundamental principles, innovation will go astray; without innovation, upholding them cannot be sustained.
quoteZh: 没有守正，创新就会走向邪路；没有创新，守正也难以为继。

glossary.explanation: Shorthand for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023 as a companion to the first combination, with China's concrete realities.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), associated with General Secretary Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keeping to what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for balancing fidelity to core principles with innovation. It is one of the "six musts" in official theory.

t: "Act in accordance with dialectics": Deng Xiaoping's far-sighted strategic thinking
zh: “照辩证法办事”：邓小平同志高瞻远瞩的战略思维
paras: Marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, Li Qinggang takes up one of the qualities Xi Jinping singled out in Deng: far-sighted strategic thinking. Li argues that its philosophical foundation is the phrase Deng himself used and Mao Zedong endorsed, "act in accordance with dialectics". In Li's reading, many of Deng's major ideas and judgements are shot through with materialist dialectics and show a global outlook and strategic vision.

The article is a short commentary published in the Party Central Committee's theoretical journal. It is organised in five parts, each pairing a Deng formula with a dialectical principle and illustrating it from the War of Resistance against Japan, the civil war, the early People's Republic, the 1975 rectification and the reform era. Li draws on Deng's wartime reports, his remarks on reform and his 1992 southern tour talks.

Li's core argument runs through five pairs. First, Deng held fast to the principal contradiction: expanding the Sino-Japanese contradiction in wartime, and economic construction as the centre once the principal contradiction was defined as that between growing material and cultural needs and backward production. Second, the "emphasis on the key point" is joined to the "two-sided approach", as in Deng's insistence on "grasping with both hands, both firmly" for material and spiritual civilization, or for reform and the fight against corruption. Third, the part must serve the whole, illustrated by the Huai-Hai Campaign and by Deng's view that coastal development should first lead and later be repaid by support for the interior. Fourth, opportunities must be seized and decisions made in good time, with "crossing the river by feeling the stones" as a method of pilot testing. Fifth, "be bold, but steady" unites subjective initiative with respect for objective laws.

Li concludes that the founding of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the achievements of reform and opening up are inseparable from Deng's strategic thinking and Deng Xiaoping Theory. Party members and officials are urged to study the theory completely and accurately, and not one-sidedly, and to learn Deng's world outlook and his habit of grasping the key link. They are also urged to place the cause of the Party and people in a historical and global perspective. Read the original if you want to see how a Central Party School historian presents Deng's method as dialectics, with the key quotations from Deng arranged by theme.
quoteEn: "Be bold, but steady": the combination of the two embodies the unity of exercising subjective initiative with respecting objective laws, and the unity of daring to try and break new ground with advancing steadily and solidly.
quoteZh: “胆子要大，步子要稳”，二者的结合体现了发挥主观能动性和尊重客观规律的统一、敢试敢闯和稳扎稳打的统一。

glossary.explanation: The body of ideas associated with Deng Xiaoping on reform, opening up and socialist modernization. It was written into the Party constitution in 1997 as a guiding ideology.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official name for the Party's path of socialism since the reform era, presented as adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
glossary.explanation: A saying associated with Deng and reform-era policy, describing gradual, experimental reform through pilot projects before wider rollout.

glossary.pinyin: liǎng shǒu zhuā, liǎng shǒu dōu yào yìng
glossary.en: grasping with both hands, both firmly
glossary.literal: grasp with two hands, both hands must be firm
glossary.explanation: A Deng-era formula calling for equal attention to material and spiritual civilization, or to development and legal order.

t: On the momentum of modernization in a super-large-scale country
zh: 论超大规模国家现代化发展之势
paras: Luo Yuting and Liu Hongchang ask what is distinctive about Chinese modernization as the modernization of a country with over 1.4 billion people, a population the 20th Party Congress (2022) report said exceeds that of all existing developed countries combined. They argue that this scale produces a characteristic "momentum" (shi), in which potential and kinetic energy are converted into a trend and an overall tendency of development. The article identifies five forms of this momentum: catching up, release of latent potential, scale effects, graded advance and inertial development.

The article takes each form in turn. The catching-up section traces China's path from a backward agrarian state in 1949 through the Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping periods to the present, and compares it with the United States. The potential section examines institutional, human and spiritual potential. The scale section covers market size, economic resilience and room for manoeuvre. The last two sections deal with the staged, regionally sequenced character of China's modernization and with its inertia, including how that inertia should be steered.

In the authors' account, China learned from the experience of earlier developers and avoided what they call the "maladies of modernity" of Western capitalist modernization, such as ecological damage, alienation, polarization, war and colonial expansion. They contend that Party leadership and the socialist system, combined with the socialist market economy, allow resources to be concentrated on major tasks. The article cites figures on manufacturing, GDP, consumption and education to support the claim that China is narrowing the gap with the United States. The authors also argue that a very large country cannot advance evenly, so reform must be staged and paced to what society can bear. Once set in motion, they say, such a country builds up great inertia, so its strategic direction should not be changed lightly.

The authors conclude that modernization should proceed in graded steps while urban–rural and regional gaps are narrowed and rural revitalization pursued. They call for steering inertial momentum through economic restructuring, innovation-driven development, new quality productive forces and the pursuit of common prosperity. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how scale is used to explain the dynamics and advantages of Chinese modernization, with the supporting statistics and historical periodization.
quoteEn: The potential energy of inertial development in the modernization of a super-large-scale country cannot easily be altered.
quoteZh: 超大规模国家现代化惯性发展的势能无法轻易变更。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and high-tech industries.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed in Party policy, especially since 2021, in connection with narrowing income and regional gaps.

t: Several questions in the study of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times in the new era
zh: 新时代马克思主义中国化时代化研究的几个问题
paras: How has the meaning of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times developed, what is new about the "new leap" of the new era, and what links the Party's successive theoretical achievements? Xiao Guiqing takes up these three questions. The author argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era marks a new leap, and that Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and Xi's thought form one developing whole.

The article has three parts. The first traces the concept from Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation through the Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao periods to the Two Integrations after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second examines three respects in which the new era is said to bring a leap. The third sets out the internal logic that unites the theoretical achievements, under historical, theoretical and value headings.

In Xiao's account, earlier theory stressed combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with the features of the age. Xi adds a combination with fine traditional Chinese culture, which Xiao calls a new theoretical proposition. Xiao holds that traditional culture was the cultural soil, not the theoretical basis, of Mao Zedong Thought and the earlier theoretical system. The leap also lies in a new theoretical system, set out in the 19th and 20th Party Congresses and the sixth plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), and in answers to major questions of the era: the direction of socialism with Chinese characteristics, Chinese modernization, and building a long-governing Marxist party. Xiao presents the Party's self-reform as a second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. On unity, Xiao argues that all the achievements serve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, rest on Marxism and seeking truth from facts, and put the people first.

Xiao concludes that the three achievements are successive and logically connected, forming one continuously innovating theoretical system. The text is written to support further theoretical innovation as the Party pursues its second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a mainstream Party-theory account of how the concept of adapting Marxism to China has been periodised and how the Two Integrations are presented as the basis of a new leap.
quoteEn: Although the theoretical achievements of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times arose in different historical periods and with their own concerns, all of them are major results that grasp the central theme and thread of Chinese history, and all revolve around the historical theme of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化时代化理论成果虽然产生于不同历史时期、拥有各自的时代关切，但都是深刻把握中国历史主题主线的重大成果，都紧紧围绕着实现中华民族伟大复兴这一历史主题

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for applying Marxist principles to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. Mao Zedong first used the Sinification idea in 1938; the 'needs of our times' element was added more recently.
The formula that Marxism must be integrated with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is presented as the fundamental path of adapting Marxism in China.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central historical goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, described as moving from 'standing up' to 'becoming prosperous' to 'becoming strong'.
The official name for the Party's path and system since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping.
Xi-era term for the Party's own efforts to purify and renew itself, presented as a second answer to the historical cycle of dynastic rise and fall.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The "Fengqiao experience": Mao Zedong's governance philosophy and wisdom and its contemporary development
zh: “枫桥经验”：毛泽东治国理政的理念与智慧及其当代发展
paras: Zhou Zhongzhi asks what the "Fengqiao experience", endorsed by Mao Zedong in 1963–64, reveals about Mao's approach to governing China and why it still matters. The article argues that the experience embodies Mao's governance ideas and wisdom, and that its continued development under Xi Jinping has theoretical and practical value for realising Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first traces Mao's thinking from "On the Ten Major Relationships" (1956) and "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People" (1957) to the Fengqiao case in Zhejiang, where cadres and villagers reformed "four-category elements" locally. The second links the experience to traditional Chinese culture, namely joint rule by virtue and law and the people-as-foundation tradition. The third follows its development from Mao to Xi Jinping, including its adoption in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

Zhou's central claim is that Mao joined a "grand pattern" of top-level design with a "downward shift of the centre of gravity" to grassroots governance. The slogan "contradictions are not passed upward but resolved on the spot" rests on three elements: dialectical analysis of contradictions and their transformation, a historical-materialist mass line, and roots in Chinese tradition, including village rules and mediation. Zhou also treats governance culture as an "implicit institution" that supports formal rules. For the present, the author sees growing domestic and international risks as making grassroots governance urgent, and says the new-era experience has grown into a system combining self-governance, rule of law and rule of virtue.

Zhou concludes that the experience should be upheld and developed by combining human effort with technology. Digital tools bring efficiency and fine-grained management, which Zhou links to Xi's image of governing "like embroidery". Zhou warns that they cannot replace face-to-face work with the masses, since reliance on online contact could breed bureaucratism and formalism. The author also says Chinese governance must rest on Chinese culture and cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a Party-theoretical account of how the Fengqiao experience is tied to Mao's texts, traditional culture and Xi-era grassroots governance.
quoteEn: "Contradictions are not passed upward but resolved on the spot" is the core content of what Mao Zedong affirmed and promoted in the Fengqiao experience.
quoteZh: “矛盾不上交，就地解决”是毛泽东肯定和倡导“枫桥经验”的核心内容。

glossary.explanation: A model of grassroots conflict resolution originating in Fengqiao, Zhuji, Zhejiang, in 1963, summed up as resolving disputes locally by mobilising residents. Mao endorsed it in 1963–64, and later leaders, including Xi Jinping, have promoted a "new-era" version.

A Party working method, associated with Mao, of drawing ideas from the masses, turning them into policy and returning to the masses to implement them. It is described as the Party's fundamental line of work.
The official term for China's own path of modernisation under Party leadership, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Mao's 1957 category for non-antagonistic contradictions within society, to be handled by democratic methods and distinguished from antagonistic contradictions between the people and their enemies.

glossary.en: self-governance, rule of law and rule of virtue
glossary.explanation: An official formula for grassroots governance that combines residents' self-governance, legal regulation and moral guidance.

t: Deng Xiaoping's major contribution to the methodology of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 邓小平对马克思主义中国化方法论的重大贡献
paras: Tian Keqin asks what Deng Xiaoping contributed to the methodology by which Marxism is adapted to Chinese conditions. The article argues that Deng held a strong methodological self-awareness. In Tian's account, he upheld and developed Mao Zedong's method, and he applied the methodology of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context in new ways. This opened up socialism with Chinese characteristics and moved Marxism's Chinese development into a new stage. Tian takes as his starting point Xi Jinping's remark that seeking truth from facts was Deng's most important intellectual trait.

The article, published in 2024 in Marxist Studies, has three parts. The first covers the period from Deng's return to office (1977) to the 12th Party Congress (1982). It deals with his restoration of the Party's ideological line and his assessment of Mao Zedong Thought. The second part examines how he set the theme of socialism with Chinese characteristics and founded Deng Xiaoping Theory. The third part examines his creative use of four methods: seeking truth from facts, the mass line, independence and self-reliance, and dialectical thinking.

Tian's central claim is that Deng tied the universal principles of Marxism to the concrete practice of modernization and to the features of the era. Tian presents the formula of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the result of that tie. Deng Xiaoping Theory, Tian argues, rests on three linked emphases: practice, productive forces and the creativity of the masses. In the third part, each method is matched to a problem. Seeking truth from facts grounds the primary stage of socialism as the basis of policy. The mass line explains the driving force of modernization, including common prosperity. Independence and self-reliance mark out a distinct path, with Deng's 'Chinese-style modernization' defined as 'xiaokang' (a moderately comfortable standard). Dialectical thinking underlies the 'one centre, two basic points' layout and the 'grasp with both hands' policies.

Tian concludes that Deng combined Chinese conditions with a world outlook, and that his methods guide later development. The article calls on the Party in the new era to carry forward and apply this methodology, linking it to the 'six musts' and to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Deng's thought is placed in the lineage of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, and of how it is tied to current official discourse.
quoteEn: Deng Xiaoping did not stop at grasping the general meaning and status of seeking truth from facts, but linked seeking truth from facts with emancipating the mind.
quoteZh: 邓小平没有停留在对实事求是的一般性含义与地位的把握上，而是将实事求是与解放思想相衔接

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete conditions and culture. It is traditionally traced to Mao Zedong and is presented as continuing through later leaders.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions rather than doctrine. The Party treats it as the core of its ideological line, and Deng Xiaoping stressed it after 1978.
The Party's method of leadership: 'from the masses, to the masses'. It means gathering the people's views and returning them as policy.
The body of ideas associated with Deng's reform-era leadership. It was written into the Party constitution at the 15th Party Congress (1997) as part of the Party's guiding ideology.
The official judgement that China is in a long, underdeveloped first phase of socialism. It is used to justify reform-era policies.
A phrase Deng used around 1979 for China's own path to modernization. It is now an official slogan, usually rendered 'Chinese modernization'.
The goal of prosperity shared by all, which official discourse treats as an essential feature of socialism.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Deng Xiaoping's thought on reform and its value for our times
zh: 邓小平改革思想及其时代价值
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's speech marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, Qu Qingshan asks what Deng's thought on reform contained and why it still matters. Qu argues that it forms a complete system within Deng Xiaoping Theory and that the Party's current drive for further comprehensively deepening reform continues it. In Qu's account, the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) upheld, enriched and developed it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the historical conditions in which Deng's reform thinking arose, which Qu summarises as four "bases": the future of the Party and country at the end of the Cultural Revolution, lessons from socialist revolution and construction, the trends of the age, and the aspirations of the people. The second sets out eight themes in the thought itself and the results of reform. The third draws lessons for today from the "six adherences" of the 2024 plenum.

Qu presents Deng's thought as answering the question of what socialist reform is and how to carry it out. The themes are Party leadership, reliance on the masses, reform as the self-improvement of the socialist system, reform as liberating the productive forces, comprehensive reform, and "bold but steady" method. They also include the "three favourables" as criteria for judging reform, and opening up as part of reform. Qu then links each of the plenum's six principles to Deng: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, institution-building, law-based governance and a systematic outlook. Qu holds that the shift from a highly centralised planned economy to a socialist market economy, and the rise of the economy to second in the world, vindicate Deng's decision.

Qu concludes that reform and opening up has "no completion, only a present tense", and that the continuity of its historical, theoretical and practical logic links Deng's era with the new era. Qu calls for unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and for implementation of the 2024 reform decisions. Qu describes Chinese modernization as drawing its momentum from reform and its vitality from opening up. Read the original if you want an official Party-history account of how Deng's reform thinking is being tied to the 2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: Reform and opening up has only a present tense, never a completed one.
quoteZh: 改革开放只有进行时，没有完成时。

glossary.explanation: The policy course launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It introduced market-oriented economic reform and opening to the outside world.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.
The body of ideas associated with Deng Xiaoping, written into the Party constitution in 1997. It is treated as the foundation of the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Deng's criteria from his 1992 southern tour for judging reform: whether it promotes the productive forces, increases overall national strength and raises living standards.

t: Comprehensively deepening reform provides institutional guarantees for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 全面深化改革为因地制宜发展新质生产力提供体制保障
paras: Writing after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Zhou Wen asks what institutional mechanisms are needed to develop new quality productive forces in line with local conditions. The article takes the Plenum's Decision on further deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization as its starting point, in particular its call for a mechanism that adapts new quality productive forces to each locality. Zhou argues that three sets of reforms supply the necessary guarantees: a high-standard socialist market economy, a system supporting comprehensive innovation, and high-level opening up.

The article is organised in three parts, each opening with a passage from the Decision and then setting out specific measures. The first deals with the market economy system, covering basic market institutions and a unified national market. The second deals with the coordination of education, science and technology, and talent. The third deals with regional opening-up patterns, investment and trade mechanisms, and institutional opening-up.

In the first part, Zhou holds that localities, especially less developed ones, need outside resources to unlock their own. This requires protecting property and intellectual property rights, improving market access, safeguarding fair competition and building a social credit system, together with a unified national market in which factors of production flow freely. The second part argues that education, science and technology, and talent must be planned together. Zhou proposes discipline-building and evaluation reforms, science and technology planning that combines national direction with local initiative, and leading technology firms that draw in small and medium-sized enterprises. Talent policy covers training, recruitment, use and orderly mobility, including movement towards poorer regions that take on national projects. The third part assigns different roles to the eastern, central, western and northeastern regions, and calls for investment and trade liberalisation. It also calls for alignment with high-standard international trade rules and support for the multilateral trading system centred on the World Trade Organization.

Zhou concludes that these reforms together would channel advanced production factors towards new quality productive forces, raise total factor productivity and create production relations better suited to them. The measures are presented as concrete tasks for implementing the Plenum's decisions. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented account of how the Third Plenum's reform agenda is linked to regional development of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: A high-level socialist market economy system is an important institutional guarantee for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions.
quoteZh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制是因地制宜发展新质生产力的重要体制保障。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and innovative factor allocation. It has since become a central theme in Chinese economic policy.
The official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, which the Party leadership presents as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system since the 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.

A long-standing principle of tailoring policy to the circumstances of each region. Here it means that each locality develops new quality productive forces according to its own resources and strengths.
Opening up that goes beyond trade and investment flows to align domestic rules, regulations and standards with international ones.

t: Mao Zedong's philosophy and practice of struggle: "neither believing in evil nor fearing ghosts"
zh: 毛泽东“不信邪、不怕鬼”的斗争哲学和实践
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 4
paras: Xin Ping and Zou Wulong take up the injunction to be "unbelieving in evil and unafraid of ghosts", which the Party's third historical resolution (adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, 2021) wrote into a historical resolution for the first time. They argue that Mao Zedong was its chief proponent and practitioner, and that guided by historical materialism he gradually built a systematic philosophy of struggle that is now a fine tradition and valuable experience of the Communist Party of China.

The article has three parts. It first sets out the philosophical foundations of the idea, then traces three stages in its practical development from the 1910s to the socialist construction period, and finally identifies three features of the philosophy. The evidence is drawn from Mao's speeches and writings, the New Youth debate on spiritualism, the revolutionary war years and the compilation of the 1961 book Stories of Not Fearing Ghosts.

On the foundations, the authors hold that "ghosts and evil" stand for superstition and illusion, and that Marxist views of truth, the analysis of contradiction and the mass line supply the philosophical basis. Mao, they say, extended the term to everything that must be fought: imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism before 1949, then reactionary forces worldwide, natural disasters, setbacks in construction, and even timidity among Party members. On the practical stages, the idea first appeared in Mao's 1919 call "do not fear ghosts" after the New Youth attack on the Shanghai Spiritualist Society. It developed through armed struggle, the Jinggangshan base, opposition to "Left" lines and the War of Resistance, and was refined after 1949, when Mao urged contempt for the enemy strategically and seriousness tactically. The three features are: starting from the principal contradiction and the main task of each period; daring to struggle; and protecting national security and social stability.

The authors conclude that the philosophy proved successful and is a spiritual asset that changed the fate of the Chinese nation and contributed to the liberation of oppressed peoples. They call for studying and carrying it forward amid what they term "changes unseen in a century", so as to be "daring and good at struggle" in advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese historian's account links Mao's revolutionary-era language and texts to current Party discourse on struggle.
quoteEn: The more one fears ghosts, the more ghosts there are; if one does not fear ghosts, there are no ghosts.
quoteZh: 越怕鬼就越有鬼,不怕鬼就没有鬼了

t: Mao Zedong and the construction of the New Democratic system
zh: 毛泽东与新民主主义制度的建构
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2024 no. 4
paras: Zhang Jianzhou asks how Mao Zedong built the New Democratic system, which the author calls the "preface" and "first part" of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article argues that Mao was its chief architect: he set its historical preconditions, designed its "four beams and eight pillars" in politics, economy and culture, and charted its transformation into a socialist system. Zhang presents this as a solution to the institutional crisis of semi-colonial, semi-feudal China, with lessons for other formerly colonised countries.

The article has three parts. The first covers the preconditions: the adaptation of Marxist state theory to Chinese conditions and the lessons of political-power building under the Soviet, anti-Japanese and liberation-war periods. The second sets out the political, economic and cultural institutions. The third examines the "timetable" and "road map" for the shift to socialism after 1949. A short conclusion places the New Democratic system within Marxist theory and in today's institutional development.

Zhang's central argument is that Mao departed from a dogmatic reading of the classics and from the "one-revolution" and "two-revolution" theories. Politically, the system combined a joint dictatorship of several revolutionary classes with democratic centralism, under the Communist Party's unified leadership. Economically, it combined a state-led "one dominant, several coexisting" ownership structure with both planning and market mechanisms. Culturally, it sought a national, scientific and mass culture while seeking a "greatest common divisor" among classes' ideologies. Zhang explains Mao's 1952 decision to begin the transition at once by two factors: recovery data showing a material base, and the system's limits in financing industrialisation and checking capitalist tendencies. The transition then ran through ownership change, a political shift to a people's democratic dictatorship that is in essence proletarian dictatorship, and a longer cultural transformation.

Zhang concludes that the New Democratic system was an inevitable choice and a creative answer to how socialism could be built in a backward semi-colonial country. In this reading it supplied what Marx's account of the "transition period" left unspecified. Although it became a historical concept once socialist transformation was complete, the author urges today's China to draw on Mao's legacy in improving its system of fundamental, basic and important institutions and in pursuing the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of Mao's institutional design, with the economic data and Mao quotations used to justify the 1952 shift to the transition to socialism.
quoteEn: The New Democratic system was the inevitable choice after China's descent into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society and the failure of many institutional experiments, and it was a great creation of the Chinese Communists represented by Mao Zedong.
quoteZh: 新民主主义制度是近代中国沦为半殖民地半封建社会，多种制度尝试无果后的必然选择，是以毛泽东为代表的中国共产党人的伟大创造。

glossary.explanation: The set of political, economic and cultural institutions Mao Zedong designed for the stage between the Chinese revolution's democratic phase and socialism. It rested on a joint dictatorship of revolutionary classes under Communist leadership, and was in place from about 1949 until the mid-1950s.

Mao's formulation of the state system, in which the working class leads an alliance of workers and peasants. The article argues that it became in essence proletarian dictatorship after the 1956 completion of transformation.
An architectural metaphor for the main structural framework of a system. Here it refers to the core institutional pillars of the New Democratic system.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, denoting the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Comrade Deng Xiaoping and the pioneering of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 邓小平同志与中国特色社会主义的开创
source: Studies on the History of the Communist Party of China, 2024 no. 4
paras: This short commemorative commentary asks what Deng Xiaoping contributed to opening up socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xie Chuntao presents Deng as a figure of the century and as chief architect of reform and opening up and modernization. Xie also calls him the founder of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics and principal creator of Deng Xiaoping Theory.

The piece is organised around three contributions: a new path, a new theory and a new historical period. It ends by linking Deng's legacy to the work of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping.

On the path, Xie says that when Deng returned to work in the late 1970s he started from correcting the ideological line and pushed the Party to rethink what socialism is. Deng drew on Mao Zedong's explorations, the Party's own setbacks and world socialist experience, and combined socialism with Chinese characteristics. On theory, Xie credits Deng with the first fairly systematic answers on building socialism in a economically and culturally backward country. Xie cites the essence of socialism, the primary stage of socialism, the socialist market economy and the Party's basic line of "one central task, two basic points". Xie holds that these made an original contribution to scientific socialism and marked a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. On the period, Xie points to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee, rural contracting, special economic zones, and Deng's 1992 southern tour.

Xie concludes that Deng's work is best honoured by carrying forward the cause he began, as Xi Jinping has said. Xie calls for closer unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and for deepening reform and opening up in pursuit of Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Central Party School leader presents Deng's legacy in official Party history.
quoteEn: With great theoretical courage, Deng Xiaoping gave the first fairly systematic, preliminary answers to a series of basic questions on how to build, consolidate and develop socialism in a country as economically and culturally backward as China, creating Deng Xiaoping Theory and achieving a new leap in the adaptation of Marxism to China.
quoteZh: 邓小平同志以巨大的理论勇气，第一次比较系统地初步回答了在中国这样经济文化比较落后的国家如何建设社会主义、如何巩固和发展社会主义的一系列基本问题，创立了邓小平理论，实现了马克思主义中国化新的飞跃。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, associated with Deng Xiaoping's call from 1982 to build socialism suited to China's conditions.
The body of ideas credited to Deng Xiaoping on reform, the market and the nature of socialism, written into the Party Constitution in 1997.
The official judgement that China is at an early, long-lasting stage of socialism, used as the basis for Party policy.
The policy begun at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, introducing economic reform and opening to the outside world.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and producing new theory, treated as a series of historic leaps.
The official term, prominent since 2021, for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership.

t: Deng Xiaoping's acceptance of Marxism as a young man: historical conditions and intellectual trajectory, seen through sources on his years in Europe
zh: 从留欧史料透视青年邓小平接受马克思主义的历史条件与思想脉络
paras: Why did the young Deng Xiaoping, who went to France on a work-study programme at 16 and later studied in the Soviet Union, come to adopt Marxism? Liu argues that existing studies divide his time abroad into separate periods and rarely set it against modern China's wider history or treat the French and Soviet years as one whole. The article contends that his turn to Marxism was historically necessary, shaped by the political climate, by earlier Chinese communists in Europe and by his own experience.

The article has two main parts. The first examines four historical conditions: the May Fourth Movement of 1919, the Chinese work-study movement in France, the founding of Chinese Communist Party and Youth League organisations in Europe, and the movement to study in the Soviet Union. The second traces four stages in Deng's thinking. The evidence includes his own later recollections, his 1985 talks with foreign visitors, French police reports, Soviet-period questionnaires and self-assessments, and his articles in the Europe-based Party and Youth League periodicals.

Liu argues that Deng began with a patriotic, reformist ideal of "saving the nation through industry". Hard factory labour in France then showed him the nature of capitalist society, and he abandoned that ideal. Comrades such as Zhou Enlai, Cai Hesen and Zhao Shiyan introduced him to socialist literature, and Deng later described the combination of study, persuasion and personal suffering as leading him to seek a revolutionary organisation. Liu reads his articles in the periodical Chiguang, which attack the nationalist "statist" Youth Party and denounce imperialism through an analogy with the Dawes Plan, as his first Marxist theoretical work. In Moscow, at Sun Yat-sen University, Liu says he studied a systematic curriculum, including political economy centred on Capital, and received Party discipline training, which gave him "a considerable understanding of communism".

Liu concludes that Deng's early development reflected the historical setting, his hardships abroad, his exposure to capitalism and European Marxism, and the influence of a cohort of early Chinese communists who studied abroad. Liu proposes further individual, comparative and overall studies of that cohort and its contribution to the Party's founding. Read the original if you want a source-based account of Deng Xiaoping's ideological formation in France and the USSR, or of the early Chinese communists' European networks, as Chinese Party historians present them.
quoteEn: The idea of \"saving the nation through industry\", which Deng Xiaoping developed during the May Fourth Movement under the influence of those around him, was in essence a reformist idea, advocating the transformation of an economically and technologically backward China with a dark political system by learning advanced ideas and technology from abroad.
quoteZh: 邓小平在五四运动中受周围人影响萌发的“工业救国”思想实质上是一种改良主义思想，主张通过向国外学习先进理念和技术来改造经济科技落后、制度黑暗的中国。

glossary.explanation: A movement from 1912 onwards that sent Chinese students to France to combine manual work with study. It peaked in 1919–1920, and many later communist leaders took part.

A patriotic and anti-imperialist protest movement that began in Beijing on 4 May 1919 and grew into a wider intellectual and cultural upheaval. Chinese historiography treats it as a key background to the spread of Marxism in China.

A reformist idea popular in early twentieth-century China that national salvation lay in industrial development and learning foreign technology. The article presents it as Deng's first form of patriotism.

t: On the construction and consolidation of the subjectivity of Chinese culture
zh: 论中华文化主体性的建构与巩固
paras: Zhao Jianying takes up a concept that Xi Jinping put forward in 2023: the "subjectivity" (zhutixing) of Chinese culture, which Zhao presents as a hallmark concept of Xi Jinping's thought on culture. The article asks what the concept means, why it must be consolidated, and how. Its thesis is that building and strengthening cultural subjectivity is necessary for cultural prosperity, for a strong cultural nation and for the modern Chinese civilization that the Party seeks to build. Zhao also presents it as an advance in the Party's cultural self-awareness and in Marxist cultural theory.

The article has three parts. The first traces "subjectivity" from Protagoras, Socrates and Aristotle through Descartes, Kant and neo-Kantianism to Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, then derives cultural subjectivity from it. The second sets out four reasons why consolidation is required.
