The third proposes six routes: guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Party's cultural leadership, the Two Integrations, an autonomous Chinese knowledge system, openness to other civilizations, and cultural subjectivity in cyberspace.

Zhao defines cultural subjectivity through four capacities named by Xi: guiding, cohesive, shaping and radiating power. In Zhao's account, Chinese cultural subjectivity has four features: originality, a leading culture within a plural whole, autonomy in exchange with other civilizations, and a conscious tradition of cultivating people through culture. Zhao says the article concerns the subjectivity of contemporary socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, guided by Marxism. The article links this subjectivity to cultural confidence, to the Party's capacity to lead its era and to national cohesion, and to cultural security. It describes Western ideological infiltration and a "Western strong, China weak" pattern in international opinion. The Two Integrations, especially integration with traditional culture, are called a "chemical reaction" in which Marxism supplies the "soul" and traditional culture the "roots". Zhao argues that Chinese theory and the social sciences need originality and must not follow foreign models.

Zhao concludes that Chinese civilization has endured because of its cultural subjectivity. The article says this subjectivity was shaken after 1840 and rebuilt after Marxism arrived and the Party was founded. Zhao credits the Party leadership since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with reversing the marginalisation of Marxism in ideology. The proposals include stronger Party leadership over cultural work, management of online content, and the promotion of distinctive Chinese concepts abroad. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how Chinese Marxist scholars ground Xi Jinping's cultural thought in the history of philosophy and in the cultural security and ideological agenda of the Party-state.
quoteEn: Cultural subjectivity is the set of characteristics that appear in the process of cultivating people through culture, shown above all in the \"guiding, cohesive, shaping and radiating power\" that General Secretary Xi Jinping summarised.
quoteZh: 文化主体性即以文“化人”过程中所呈现的特性，突出表现为习近平总书记所概括的“引领力、凝聚力、塑造力、辐射力”。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration, with traditional culture, was stressed from 2021 onward.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023, meaning a culture's capacity to stand on its own, with its own guiding, cohesive, shaping and radiating power. It is the central concept of the article.
The confidence in a nation's own culture and its vitality. The Party treats it as the foundation of confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The Party's authority over cultural and ideological work. It is related to the Gramscian idea of hegemony but is used here in an official sense.
A slogan from Xi Jinping's 2022 and 2023 speeches calling for philosophy and social sciences that rest on Chinese experience and concepts rather than Western models.

t: Mutual learning among civilizations and the building of a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 文明互鉴与中华民族现代文明建设
source: Social Sciences in China (中国社会科学), 2024 no. 7
paras: Qian Chengdan, a historian at Peking University, asks how mutual learning among civilizations bears on the building of a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. He argues that modernization is a profound civilizational transformation and, for China, another great fusion of civilizations, larger and deeper than earlier ones. Through it, Qian says, Chinese civilization has both absorbed the world and entered it.

The article is organised around three questions: the two carriers of a civilization and the "inner core" of Chinese civilization; the fusing nature of that civilization, or its capacity for "outward integration"; and the construction of a modern civilization during modernization. Qian compares China with ancient Greece, Rome, medieval Western Europe, South Asia and West Asia–North Africa. He then reviews three great fusions in Chinese history and the crisis that began in the mid-nineteenth century.

Qian's central claim is that every civilization has a spiritual carrier (a religion or non-religious doctrine, its ideology) and a political carrier (state power, its institutional guarantee). Civilizations last when the two support each other. Chinese civilization, in his account, joined Confucian doctrine to a unified state more than two thousand years ago, and this pairing formed an unchanging core. The other cases, he argues, lacked such a match: Greece had no unified state, Rome had no unified ideology until it was declining, medieval Europe had faith without a state, India had ideology without a strong state, and West Asia achieved both only with Islam in the seventh century. Alongside this core, Qian presents fusion as a constant trait: the Wei-Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties period, the Song-Liao-Jin-Yuan era, and the Qing each enlarged Chinese civilization while preserving its core. He rejects as a Western fabrication the "Inner Asia" thesis about the Qing, and links Chinese openness to an early shift from a single-god cosmology to rationalism.

On the modern period, Qian describes the mid-nineteenth-century crisis, in which industrial power broke open China, as a civilizational crisis as well as a political one. He concludes that China answered by pursuing modernization. It holds to its core, its core values and the cooperation of spiritual and state power, and it learns with great openness from the West and humility from non-Western experience. Chinese modernization is thus, in his words, another great civilizational fusion, at once inheritance and innovation. Read the original if you want a historian's civilizational framework, built on the "two carriers" and "core plus fusion", for the official idea of a modern Chinese civilization.
quoteEn: Every growth of Chinese civilization has been achieved through fusion, with the "inner core" and "outward integration" working at the same time.
quoteZh: 中华文明的每一次壮大都是在融合中完成的，“内核”和“外融”同时起作用。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
A phrase in official Chinese diplomacy and theory, associated with Xi Jinping's Global Civilization Initiative. It stresses exchange and learning between civilizations rather than clash or hierarchy.
Qian's term for the enduring structure of Chinese civilization: the pairing of Confucian doctrine as spiritual carrier with a unified state as political carrier.
Qian's term for the capacity of Chinese civilization to absorb and merge with outside cultures while keeping its core.

t: Deepening cultural system and institutional reform to build a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 深化文化体制机制改革 建设中华民族现代文明
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today shortly after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Liu Lyuhong and Yue Heng ask how deepening reform of the cultural system and its mechanisms can advance the Party's cultural mission of building a "modern civilization of the Chinese nation". They argue that such reform is both the means and the guarantee of that project, and that it drives the modern transformation of Chinese civilization.

The article is organised in three parts. It first sets out the logic of the link between cultural reform and civilization-building, with a historical survey running from Deng Xiaoping's era through successive Party congresses and plenums to the present. It then explains the internal pathway by which reform supplies momentum, institutional guarantees and spiritual strength. Finally it outlines the tasks of the new era, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The authors present cultural reform as a "magic weapon", a basic principle and an unavoidable road. Historically, they trace the "two serves" and "double hundred" policies, the concept of spiritual civilization, the inclusion of the cultural industry in the national economy and the 2011 decision on cultural reform, up to the Second Integration. They argue that the modern civilization is a product of the Two Integrations and that reform must balance national character, modernity and global reach, so that Chinese culture neither reverts to the past nor becomes a Western appendage. Reform supplies momentum by activating traditional and revolutionary culture, guarantees by upholding Marxism's guiding role in ideology, core socialist values and a people-centred orientation, and spiritual strength by building cultural self-reliance, confidence and strength.

For action, the authors call for guidance from Xi Jinping's thought on culture, stressing cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and keeping to fundamental principles while innovating. They urge joining the "root" of traditional culture with the "soul" of Marxism, and building a more effective international communication system, with discourse, narrative and knowledge systems based on Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link cultural system reform to the civilizational goals set after the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Both deepening reform of the cultural system and mechanisms and building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation are about liberating and developing cultural productive forces.
quoteZh: 深化文化体制机制改革和建设中华民族现代文明都是解放和发展文化生产力。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the First Integration) and with China's fine traditional culture (the Second Integration, stressed since 2021-23).
The official name for China's own path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, used as a guiding idea in Chinese foreign policy and communication.
The body of Xi's ideas on culture and ideology, formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
The official call for confidence in the value and vitality of Chinese culture, including traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture.

glossary.en: keeping to fundamental principles while innovating
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan about adhering to core principles and the Party's leadership while pursuing new approaches.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: On the practical principles of Deng Xiaoping's theory of building socialist ideology
st: In commemoration of the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth
zh: 论邓小平社会主义意识形态建设理论的实践原则
zhSub: 纪念邓小平诞辰120周年
paras: Jiang Yingchun asks how Deng Xiaoping's thinking on building socialist ideology can guide ideological work today, when the coordinated development of material and cultural-ethical civilization is, in the article's words, an important feature of Chinese modernization. Jiang argues that this coordination is a process of contradiction, marked by clashes between the advanced and the backward, so that ideological struggle remains necessary. The article's thesis is that Deng's theory rests on three practical principles: grasping the fundamentals, staying vigilant in times of peace, and holding firm to conviction.

Written to mark the 120th anniversary of Deng's birth, the article is organised in three sections, one for each principle. It draws mainly on Deng's speeches and interviews from the early reform period, set alongside statements by Xi Jinping, the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014) and the resolution of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It also refers to the collapse of the Soviet Union and the upheavals in Eastern Europe as a negative lesson.

On the first principle, Jiang reads Deng's Four Cardinal Principles as the political foundation of reform and modernization, a "complete set of equipment" that must not be split up. They are presented as the basis for correcting both "Left" and Right errors, since without them correcting the Left would become "correcting" Marxism-Leninism. On the second, Jiang argues that a small minority can damage the cause, that attacks on Party leadership, multi-party systems and Western-style "constitutionalism" aim at socialism itself, and that ideological collapse brought down the Soviet Communist Party. Jiang endorses Deng's call for ideological workers to carry out criticism and self-criticism with confidence, rather than avoid struggle. On the third, Jiang holds that shared ideals unite the people and are the Party's "real advantage". Developing the productive forces is described as the material basis for showing socialism's superiority, consolidating the system and eventually reaching communism. Conviction, Jiang adds, must survive a long historical process, mistakes in work and major setbacks.

Jiang concludes that these three principles remain practically important for building a socialist ideology with strong guiding and unifying power and for coordinating the two civilizations. The article presents the shift in ideological work under Xi Jinping's leadership as a result of this continuing struggle. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Deng's ideological writings are mobilised in current debates on Party leadership, "Western" political ideas and the lessons of the Soviet collapse.
quoteEn: Deng Xiaoping always viewed the preconditional, foundational and safeguarding role of upholding the Four Cardinal Principles from the standpoint of the success or failure of the cause.
quoteZh: 邓小平总是从事业成败的高度看待坚持四项基本原则的前提性、基础性和保障性作用

glossary.explanation: Formulated by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought. They are treated in official discourse as the political bedrock of reform and opening up.

The "two civilizations" paired in official discourse since Deng's era: economic and material progress on one side, and cultural, ideological and moral progress on the other. Their coordinated development is a recurring policy aim.
The official term for China's path of modernization, stressed in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which presents it as distinct from Western models.

t: The principles and direction of the "Two Integrations" in adapting Marxism to China, seen through Mao Zedong's philosophy
zh: 从毛泽东哲学透视马克思主义中国化“两个结合”的原则与走向
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxism Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2023 no. 4
paras: Xue Guangzhou asks how the Two Integrations (combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture) should be understood and carried out, and where the adaptation of Marxism to China is heading. Reading the question through Mao Zedong's philosophy, the author argues that the Two Integrations are not slogans. They need clear principles. Marxism must remain the standard by which tradition is judged, and the process should end in a new Chinese philosophy.

The article has three parts. The first clarifies the two objects of integration, "China's concrete realities" and "excellent traditional Chinese culture". The second sets out the principles for each integration and warns against several tendencies. The third traces the path from the sinicisation of Marxist philosophy to Marxist philosophy in sinicised form, then to a Chinese Marxist philosophy, and finally to a Chinese "new philosophy". Mao's discussions of practice, contradiction and cultural inheritance, together with Xi Jinping's statements, supply the reference points.

Xue defines China's concrete realities by the principal contradiction and the social character of each stage. The author criticises neoliberal economics for rejecting China's existing economic base, and criticises online claims that equality of starting point is enough. On tradition, Xue separates its "essence" (jīngsuǐ, a factual judgement about its basic spirit) from its "best elements" (jīnghuá, a value judgement made from the present). Xue proposes the concept of "zhōng" (the mean, rendered as harmony, unity, rectitude and greatness) as the essence of Chinese philosophy. For the integration, the author lists Mao-derived principles: take the essence and discard the dross, inherit critically, make the past serve the present, let a hundred flowers bloom, and above all keep Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method. Xue rejects treating Marxism and Chinese tradition as equal partners, and rejects reading cultural revival as a revival of Confucianism. Xue also rejects reading Xi Jinping's thought on culture only as inheritance of tradition or as a lineage of orthodoxy (dàotǒng).

Xue concludes that Marxism and Chinese philosophy will eventually converge in a Chinese new philosophy. That philosophy would absorb the best of Chinese tradition and of humanity's intellectual achievements, and would be accepted by most Chinese people. The author credits Mao's thought with a pioneering contribution and says Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opens a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, linked to building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system. Read the original if you want a Mao-centred, philosophically oriented account of how Chinese scholars debate the limits of the "Second Integration" with tradition.
quoteEn: Combining the basic tenets of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture means applying those basic tenets to tell the best elements from the dross, and to critique and transform traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合，就是要运用马克思主义的基本原理，鉴别精华或糟粕、批判与改造中国传统文化

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping, notably his speech at the Party's centenary in 2021. It calls for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing task of fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the present era. The earlier term "sinicisation of Marxism" was used by Mao Zedong in 1938.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A Neo-Confucian notion of an authoritative line of transmission of the true Way from the sage kings onward. The author warns against tying Xi's cultural thought to it.

t: Advancing the building of a modern civilization of the Chinese nation through the continuity of Chinese civilization
zh: 以中华文明的连续性推进中华民族现代文明建设
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remark at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development that Chinese civilization has a "outstanding continuity", Li Zheng asks how that continuity can be used to build a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. The article argues that continuity gives the country cultural subjectivity and a model of "keeping to fundamental principles while innovating". Li presents it as the spiritual and methodological resource for a new form of human civilization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out what continuity means: the deep origins of Chinese civilization, its uninterrupted transmission, and its habit of innovating within tradition. Li draws on archaeology, from early hominid finds through Neolithic cultures to the sequence of early states, kingdoms and empires, and on classical texts. The second part gives the "internal logic" linking past and present, and the third draws practical lessons.

Li's core argument is that three features of the historical record explain why continuity can drive modern civilization-building. These are a stable and distinctive geographical environment, the value of "zhonghe" (balance and harmony), and a pattern of unity in diversity among peoples. The author reads the geography as offering strategic depth and room for development in the west, the deserts and the south, and links it to the Belt and Road Initiative. Zhonghe is read as the basis for moderate development, peaceful cooperation and a community with a shared future for mankind. Unity in diversity is traced through Xi's "four commonalities" and the Sui–Tang period. From this Li derives four relationships to manage: harmony between humans and nature, coordination of material and spiritual civilization, unity of tradition and modern wisdom, and mutual learning with other civilizations.

Li concludes that building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation is a new cultural mission of the new era. The author says it must proceed along the path of Chinese modernization, through the creative transformation and innovative development of fine traditional culture. Li presents this as enriching the "new form of human civilization", which is said to go beyond Western capital logic. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese academic links archaeology, classical philosophy and official cultural-policy language into a continuity-based account of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The continuity of Chinese civilization both embraces tradition and connects with the modern; it is a unity of traditional and innovative elements.
quoteZh: 中华文明的连续性既涵纳了传统，又连接了现代，是传统因素与创新因素的统一。

glossary.explanation: The official Party description of China's path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2013. It stresses cooperation, mutual benefit and opposition to hegemony.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A concept from the Confucian classic Zhongyong, meaning moderation and harmony that tolerates difference. The author treats it as the core value behind China's civilizational continuity.
An official formula describing the civilization created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as an alternative to Western-led modernity.

t: The "Second Integration" and the rebuilding of cultural subjectivity
zh: “第二个结合”与文化主体性重建
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2024 no. 7
paras: Li Wentang takes up the question of cultural subjectivity, which the author says has run through more than a century of Chinese debates over the relation between ancient and modern, China and the West. Li reads Xi Jinping's remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development as an answer to this question, framed through the Two Integrations and especially the "Second Integration" of Marxism with traditional Chinese culture. The thesis is that this integration has revitalised Chinese civilisation and is rebuilding its cultural subjectivity.

The article defines cultural subjectivity as a self-aware, creative and transcendent cultural life-consciousness, marked by historicity, creativity and transcendence. It surveys Chinese cultural history, from the Yin-Zhou transition and Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism to the late Qing, the May Fourth movement and Yan'an. It ends by assessing current scholarship.

Li argues that rebuilding means renewal rather than starting over. "Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application" and wholesale Westernisation both failed, in Li's account, because they ignored how cultural life develops. Marxism succeeded for three reasons: it critiques Western modernity and cultural colonialism, it points the direction by affirming science and democracy, and it is a new humanism. Li holds that this humanism fits Chinese ideals of moral self-cultivation and the unity of heaven and humanity better than liberalism does, which explains why early communists fused political and moral idealism.

Li concludes that the Second Integration is another act of intellectual emancipation by the Party, to be pursued under three principles: cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and upholding fundamental principles while innovating. Li also says that scholars who command both Chinese and Western learning are in short supply and that an autonomous knowledge system is still far off. Read the original if you want a concise statement, in the Central Party School's idiom, of how the Second Integration is justified through Chinese cultural history.
quoteEn: Cultural subjectivity is a cultural life-consciousness that has awareness of its cultural lineage, engages in autonomous creation and reaches a dimension of transcendence.
quoteZh: 文化主体性是一种具有文脉自觉、进行自主创造、达到超越维度的文化生命意识。

glossary.explanation: The formula that Marxism must be integrated with China's concrete realities (the first) and with its fine traditional culture (the second, added in 2021–23).
The integration of the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2023 as a key to cultural development.
The idea that a culture has its own distinct identity and capacity for autonomous creation. Xi Jinping discussed it in 2023 in connection with Chinese civilisation.

glossary.en: debates over the relation between ancient and modern, China and the West
glossary.explanation: A long-running set of Chinese debates since the late Qing about how to relate tradition to modernity and Chinese culture to Western culture.

glossary.en: Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application
glossary.explanation: A late-Qing reformist formula that kept Chinese values as the core while adopting Western technology and methods.

t: Building a modern Chinese civilization: profound connotations, guiding thought and practical orientation
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明：深刻内涵、思想遵循与实践旨趣
paras: Liu Lina takes up the proposition of 'building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation', first put forward by Xi Jinping in October 2022 and restated in June 2023 as part of the Party's new cultural mission. The article asks what this civilization is and how it should be built. Liu's answer is that it is the cultural form of Chinese modernization and, in substance, a new form of human civilization. It must be understood through the relations among culture, civilization and modernization.

After a brief review of existing scholarship, the article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the 'profound connotations' of the concept, in historical and contemporary terms. The second treats Xi Jinping's thought on culture as the 'guiding thought'. The third turns to the 'practical orientation', which Liu divides into four requirements for construction.

In the first part, Liu argues that a civilizational view of modernization differs from the older, Western-derived account in three ways. It balances the universal and the particular, drawing on the late Marx's view that different civilizations cannot simply follow the Western European path. It stresses culture as an endogenous driving force. It also attends to people's conditions of existence, where it contrasts Marx's critique of bourgeois civilization with an approach that treats industrialization and urbanization as the main indicators. The second part draws on Xi Jinping Thought on culture. It names three sources of strength: consolidating the subjectivity of Chinese culture, the unity of 'substance and function' as an expression of the Second Integration, and a cultural mission that answers the value crisis Liu attributes to capitalist modernity. Liu presents capital's logic as the root of that crisis.

Liu concludes that construction requires firm cultural confidence grounded in the Two Integrations, rootedness in Chinese modernization, and a proper relation between the Party's historical mission and its cultural mission. It also requires deeper exchange and mutual learning among civilizations, in opposition to theories of civilizational clash or superiority. The author links this to a community with a shared future for mankind. Liu holds that people-centredness replaces the logic of capital accumulation. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how current Party discourse connects culture, civilization and Chinese modernization, or an example of how Xi Jinping's cultural thought is expounded in Chinese academic writing.
quoteEn: The modern civilization of the Chinese nation is the cultural form of Chinese modernization, and in essence a new form of human civilization.
quoteZh: 中华民族现代文明就是中国式现代化的文化形态，实质是人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from the Western model.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the First Integration) and with its fine traditional culture (the Second Integration).
The task Xi Jinping set out in June 2023: to promote cultural prosperity, build China into a cultural power and build the modern civilization of the Chinese nation.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture and ideology, presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests, cooperation and mutual respect among states.
A pair of categories in Chinese philosophy, contrasting the fundamental nature of a thing with its practical working. Liu applies it to the unity of understanding principles and applying them.

t: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership and the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation
zh: 坚守党的文化领导权和中华民族的文化主体性
paras: Song Yuehong's commentary expounds Xi Jinping's statement at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development that "keeping to the fundamental principles" in cultural work means upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, the requirements of the Two Integrations, and the Communist Party's cultural leadership and the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation. Song presents this as a major innovative point drawn from the Party's historical experience, and argues that holding to it provides political assurance and spiritual strength for building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece has three parts. The first argues that upholding the Party's cultural leadership bears on the fate of the Party and country. The second sets out how to maintain the Party's overall leadership over propaganda, ideological and cultural work. The third turns to concrete steps for carrying out the new cultural mission.

In the first part, Song traces the Party's attention to cultural leadership from Marx and Engels through the first Party congress resolution, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. The author says this leadership is a political strength of the Party and a requirement for safeguarding Marxism as the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture as the "root". It is also described as a guarantee for the new cultural mission of building a strong cultural country and a modern Chinese civilization. The second part calls for confidence in culture, the cultivation of core socialist values through law and policy, the principle that the Party manages propaganda and ideology, and firm control of media positions, including the internet, with media placed under Party leadership and run by people loyal to it.

Song concludes with proposals. These include fully implementing the ideological work responsibility system, building an independent Chinese knowledge system, strengthening international communication, and training a capable propaganda workforce. They also include reforming media and cultural institutions and perfecting the institutions through which the Party leads cultural development, such as a "big propaganda" pattern, integrated management of old and new media, and public cultural services. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-line understanding of cultural leadership and its institutional and media-management implications under Xi Jinping Thought on Culture.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership is a major political strength through which our Party continues to develop and grow stronger.
quoteZh: 坚持党的文化领导权，是我们党不断发展壮大的一大政治优势。

glossary.explanation: Formula associating the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture; emphasised by Xi Jinping, especially since 2021–23.
The Party's leading authority over ideology, culture and propaganda work, a concept related to hegemony in the Gramscian tradition but used here in an official Party sense.
The idea that the Chinese nation has its own independent cultural identity and agency, built on Marxism, fine traditional culture and revolutionary culture; emphasised by Xi Jinping in 2023.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values at national, social and individual levels, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, central to Party discourse under Xi Jinping.

t: Green development empowers the leap of new quality productive forces
zh: 绿色发展赋能新质生产力跃升
paras: Taking as its starting point Xi Jinping's statement that green development is the foundation of high-quality development and that new quality productive forces are by nature green productive forces, this Red Flag Manuscripts article asks how green development and new quality productive forces are linked. Jin argues that green development is a basic requirement of new quality productive forces, and that it has to be realised through a green transition in both the mode of development and the way of life.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why green development is required of new quality productive forces, drawing on Marx and Engels on natural conditions and on the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second turns to the green transition of the mode of development, covering the production system, the energy system and institutions. The third deals with green lifestyles and consumption, which Jin treats as the demand-side force behind new quality productive forces.

Jin reasons from Marx's view that natural conditions, as objects and means of labour, are a source of use-values. On this basis, protecting the ecological environment is said to protect productive forces, and improving it to raise natural productive capacity, so that green mountains become mountains of gold and silver. The author cites figures: average annual energy consumption growth of 3% alongside economic growth above 6%, and world-leading capacity in hydro, wind, solar and biomass power. Jin nonetheless judges the overall level of green development to be still low, with growing resource and environmental pressure. The proposed remedies are digital and intelligent green production, a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient energy system built on smart grids, and an institutional order combining an effective market with a proactive government. That order would include property rights in natural resources, ecological compensation and market trading of carbon, energy-use, water and emission rights. Jin also argues that green production technologies such as 3D printing, repair economies and sharing platforms make low-carbon consumption possible. Platform data collection that stimulates unnecessary consumption is flagged as a problem, to be met through ecological education and greener public services.

Jin concludes that new quality productive forces must be green productive forces, and that development must stay within the carrying capacity of resources and the environment. The article calls for deeper integration of digitalisation and greening, a new energy system supporting the carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals, and thrifty, low-carbon habits in daily and public life. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school commentary connects Marx's account of natural conditions with the policy agenda of new quality productive forces and the green transition.
quoteEn: Protecting the ecological environment means protecting natural conditions, and thus protecting the potential and staying power of economic and social development, so that green mountains and clear waters keep yielding ecological, economic and social benefits.
quoteZh: 保护生态环境就是保护自然条件，就是保护经济社会发展潜力和后劲，使绿水青山持续发挥生态效益和经济社会效益。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 to describe advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, as a basis for high-quality development.
The official goal of shifting China's economy from rapid quantitative growth to growth emphasising quality, innovation and sustainability.
China's declared goals of peaking carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.pinyin: lǜshuǐ qīngshān jiù shì jīnshān yínshān
glossary.en: green mountains become mountains of gold and silver
glossary.literal: clear waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping (2005) holding that ecological protection and economic prosperity are mutually reinforcing.

t: Mao Zedong's contribution to building the Chinese nation as a community, and its lessons, from the perspective of the "grand historical outlook"
zh: 历史观视域下毛泽东对推进中华民族共同体建设的贡献与启示
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2024 no. 4
paras: Yang Xiaojun and Li Yinyan ask how Mao Zedong's work on ethnic affairs should be assessed when seen through the "grand historical outlook" (大历史观) that Xi Jinping has stressed. They argue that earlier studies examined Mao's ethnic policy in narrow, specific dimensions and lacked a long-term, holistic view. Their thesis is that Mao made foundational and pioneering contributions to building the Chinese nation as a community (中华民族共同体建设), and that these contributions offer lessons for today.

The article has three parts. The first defines the grand historical outlook: a long time span, wide spatial vision and holistic treatment of history, which the authors contrast with Huang Renyu's and Braudel's long-duration history. The second sets out Mao's three contributions. The third draws three present-day lessons. The authors also place the Party's current ethnic work in a line of continuity from the Mao era through reform and opening up to the new era.

On the authors' account, Mao first led the peoples of all ethnic groups to found the new China, creating the basic political precondition for community-building. He reinterpreted "Chinese nation" to include the Han and dozens of minorities, and used the image of a "big family". Second, he led the establishment of the system of regional ethnic autonomy, which the authors present as moving from early ideas of self-determination and federalism to autonomy within national unity; they stress the training of minority cadres. Third, he set the principles of ethnic equality, unity and common development. The authors present reform-era and later policies such as targeted poverty alleviation as inheriting these principles, and they defend the autonomy system against calls to abolish it.

The three lessons are to combine upholding and innovating Marxist ethnic theory, to unite Party leadership with a people-centred approach, and to match the nation's historical position to the goals of community-building. The authors treat the Cultural Revolution's damage to ethnic relations as a deviation in Mao's late years that should not erase his wider record. They argue that studying Mao in this way serves the Party's current ethnic work and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link Mao-era ethnic policy to the current official line on forging a shared national community, or to follow the argument against historical nihilism in ethnic affairs.
quoteEn: The grand historical outlook is the methodological basis for understanding the Party's century of ethnic work.
quoteZh: 大历史观才是理解中共百年民族工作的方法论依据。

glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping has stressed in the new era. It calls for viewing history over long time spans, across wide space and as a whole, and is used against what the Party calls historical nihilism.

glossary.en: building the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.literal: construction of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A core concept of Party ethnic work, first stated in Party documents at the Central Ethnic Affairs Work Conference in August 2021. It stresses the shared identity and common interests of all ethnic groups in China.

The basic political system under which areas where minorities are concentrated have self-governing organs within the unitary state. It was written into the 1949 Common Program and the 1954 Constitution.
A Party term for views that, in its account, deny or distort the Party's history and achievements, including the standing of its leaders.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal in Party discourse, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream and with Chinese modernization.

t: Online ideological risks in the new era: forms, sources and governance
zh: 新时代网络意识形态风险：样态、来源、治理
paras: Writing in 2024, Wang Yonghua takes up the question of how China should identify, explain and govern ideological risks in cyberspace. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that the internet is now the front line of ideological struggle, Wang argues that online ideological security must be addressed through scientific prediction, precise positioning of risk sources and modernised governance. The article presents these as a necessary part of preventing and defusing risk and keeping cyberspace "clean and clear".

The article is built in three parts: the forms that online ideological risk takes, where such risks come from, and how they should be governed. Wang identifies three forms of risk and four sources, then sets out governance measures under four headings: principles, content, methods and technology. Wang draws on Xi Jinping's speeches throughout, and cites Cass Sunstein on group polarisation and Neil Postman on entertainment culture.

Wang names three risks. The first is "Westernisation" through the penetration of Western currents such as universal values, which the author says hostile forces use to promote colour revolution. The second is "group polarisation", where poorly guided online media amplify extreme views and trigger real-world incidents. The third is "pan-entertainmentisation", in which non-mainstream ideologies such as fan-circle culture dissolve the seriousness of mainstream ideology and encourage historical nihilism. Wang traces these to an imbalance in the distribution of social interests, weak risk awareness among officials, ordinary users and service providers, mainstream propaganda that does not suit fragmented online habits, and weak regulation. On regulation, Wang cites technological dependence, outdated laws and overlapping agencies.

Wang proposes that governance combine Party leadership of the internet with rule by law, including dedicated laws on extreme speech and rumours. Positive propaganda should be diverse and close to ordinary life, with "one guiding many", interactive rather than top-down, and should draw in online opinion leaders and social organisations. Wang also calls for linking online and offline work. On technology, Wang urges self-reliant innovation in encryption, AI public-opinion monitoring and VR red culture, together with crawler technology, real-name registration ("voluntary front end, real name back end") and talent training. Read the original if you want a Party-line account of how Chinese scholars classify online ideological risks and what governance measures they recommend.
quoteEn: Governing online ideological risk is a systematic project that requires multiple measures in cyberspace and the joint participation of all relevant social actors, strengthening the autonomy and coordination of socialised online governance and forming an all-round pattern of online governance.
quoteZh: 网络意识形态风险治理是一项系统工程，需要网络空间多管齐下，社会各相关主体共同参与，增强网络治理社会化的自主性和协同性，形成全方位网络治理格局。

glossary.explanation: A security concept in Chinese Party discourse, referring to protecting the dominance of mainstream (Marxist, Party-led) ideology in cyberspace. Xi Jinping has linked it to state sovereignty and political power.
Official term for popular uprisings, such as those in post-Soviet states, which Chinese discourse presents as foreign-backed efforts at regime change.
A term describing the spread of entertainment content into every area of public life, which critics say dilutes serious public and political discussion.
In official usage, a label for views that deny or belittle the Party's history and revolutionary figures, regarded as an ideological threat.

t: Understanding the four dimensions of promoting a community with a shared future for mankind
st: Values, development, security and civilization
zh: 深刻理解和把握推动构建人类命运共同体的四重向度
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 7
paras: Qin Long and Zhang Guangquan take up the question of what supports the effort to build a community with a shared future for mankind, which they describe as a core part of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought and the Chinese Communist Party's answer to the question of what kind of world to build and how. Their thesis is that four initiatives together provide its value basis and main support: the common values of all mankind, the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative and the Global Civilization Initiative.

The article is organised into four sections, one per "dimension": value, development, security and civilization. Each section follows the same pattern. It explains why the initiative was proposed, sets out its main content, and then assesses its significance for the community with a shared future for mankind. The authors rely largely on Xi Jinping's speeches, from the 2015 UN General Assembly address to the 2023 dialogue between the Party and world political parties.

In the authors' account, each initiative answers a crisis they attribute to the West. They present the "universal values" of the West as an exclusive bourgeois ideology, the Western development outlook as governed by the logic of capital and a "law of the jungle", and the Western security outlook as zero-sum hegemonism. They also describe the Western civilizational outlook as expansionist, and argue that Western modernization has produced wealth gaps, ecological pollution and disorder of values. Against these, the authors say, the common values of all mankind rest on Marx's theory of world history and on traditional Chinese ideals such as "great harmony". The Global Development Initiative offers six principles, including putting development first and putting people at the centre. The Global Security Initiative likewise offers six, including a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security outlook. The Global Civilization Initiative has four, including respect for civilizational diversity. The authors claim that each initiative gives the community a foundation and guides practice, citing bodies such as the Group of Friends of the Global Development Initiative, mediation of international disputes, the Belt and Road Initiative and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

The authors conclude that the four initiatives form a coherent framework for rallying consensus and building a community with a shared future for mankind. They say this community means neither replacing one system or civilization with another nor reaching the goal quickly, but is a long historical process. They tie it to Marx's vision of a "community of free individuals". Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned exposition of how Chinese scholars present the relationship between these initiatives and Xi Jinping's foreign-policy thought.
quoteEn: The Global Development Initiative transcends the Western traditional view of development, which puts interests above all, exposes the self-contradictory development predicament of Western capitalist countries mired in the logic of capital, and puts forward a new view of development stressing pluralistic unity and a shared destiny.
quoteZh: 全球发展倡议超越了坚持利益至上的西方传统发展观，揭示了西方资本主义国家深陷资本逻辑自我悖谬的发展困境，提出了一种强调多元一体和命运与共的新型发展观。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since about 2012–2013, presented as China's vision for international relations based on shared interests, cooperation and mutual respect.

glossary.literal: common values of the whole of humanity
glossary.explanation: A formulation introduced by Xi Jinping in 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Chinese official discourse sets it against the Western notion of "universal values".
Proposed by Xi Jinping at the UN General Assembly in September 2021. It stresses development first, people-centredness and support for the UN 2030 Agenda.
Proposed by Xi Jinping at the Boao Forum in April 2022. It promotes a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security outlook and settling disputes through dialogue.
Proposed by Xi Jinping in March 2023. It calls for respect for civilizational diversity, common values, cultural inheritance and innovation, and people-to-people exchanges.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Methodological analysis of building a discourse system for socialist ethics with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义伦理学话语体系建设的方法论探析
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory, 2024 no. 3
paras: Xiao Xiang asks how a discourse system for socialist ethics with Chinese characteristics can be built and renewed. Xiao argues that the task cannot be reduced to linguistic framing or conceptual wording. It requires methodological self-awareness, so that ethical discourse can better explain, influence and guide Chinese practice. The article treats this ethics as a new form of Marxist ethics adapted to the new stage of socialist construction, and as distinct from the Soviet-model version.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the epistemological basis: Marxism's active, revolutionary theory of reflection, with dialectical and historical materialism, practice and the interplay of knowledge, emotion and will. The second describes a three-level methodology: philosophical methodology, general scientific methodology, and the methods of specific disciplines such as linguistics, communication studies, psychology, sociology and logic. The third turns to practical innovation, through discourse practice, the resolution of current difficulties, and the shaping of discourse power.

Xiao holds that ethical discourse must come from, and be tested in, social practice, not abstract logical construction or a 'language game'. The author rejects both empiricism and rationalism, and also rejects pure speculation and supposed value-neutrality. Two present difficulties are named. One is inheriting traditional Chinese ethical discourse while facing the deconstructive pull of Western discourse, including the linguistic turn and postmodernism. The other is raising the value-critical and guiding force of ethical discourse against value relativism, liberalism and nihilism. Xiao proposes that discourse be built along historical, contemporary and Chinese dimensions. Drawing on MacIntyre and Wittgenstein, the author argues for retrieving tradition and for engaging the issues of the age.

Xiao concludes that ethical discourse influence has three layers: communicative power, recognition and leadership. Leadership is the final aim. The article cites the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind as a successful example of ethical discourse practice. It urges China to escape the predicament of being 'large in size but weak in voice', to learn from others on the principle of mutual learning, and to contribute to a system of global shared values. Read the original if you are interested in how Chinese Marxist ethicists connect epistemology, discourse theory and the project of international discourse power.
quoteEn: The discourse system of socialist ethics with Chinese characteristics does not passively reflect ethical facts or describe ethical phenomena, but actively reveals, constructs and creates reality.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义伦理学话语体系不是被动地反映伦理事实和描述伦理现象，而是主动地揭示现实、建构现实和创造现实。

glossary.explanation: The set of concepts, categories and modes of expression through which a discipline presents itself. In Chinese policy language it is one of three strategic tasks, alongside the disciplinary system and the academic system, for building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.
The capacity to set agendas, define terms and be heard and accepted in public or international debate. Chinese official and academic writing often calls for strengthening it internationally.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s for China's vision of international relations and global governance. The article treats it as an example of successful ethical discourse practice.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The logic of the "Two Integrations" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化“两个结合”的逻辑理路
source: Research on the Marxist Theory Discipline, 2024 no. 7
paras: Wang Gang asks how the Two Integrations (combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture) relate to Mao Zedong's earlier call for the "sinification of Marxism". The article argues that the Two Integrations are not a mere addition of words but an upgrade and extension of the Party's "theory of integration", and an original theoretical contribution. In Wang's account, understanding their internal logic helps in opening up a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three sections. The first treats the "single integration" (Marxism with Chinese realities) as the consistent requirement of the Party's history, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Li Dazhao and Mao. The second traces how culture entered the picture through the "three deep integrations" proposed in 1943, asking why this was necessary, possible and achievable. The third presents the Two Integrations as the "greatest magic weapon" of socialism with Chinese characteristics and sets out three practical dimensions: Marxist guidance, creative transformation of traditional culture, and Chinese modernization.

Wang's central move is to deny that the Two Integrations simply move "from one integration to two". The article reads Mao's 1938 demand that Marxism take "national form" as already implying integration with Chinese history and culture, so the second integration was latent in the first. On this reading culture entered the field of integration because the Party came to adopt a stance of "critical acceptance" of tradition. Wang finds Marxism and fine traditional culture compatible, citing ideas such as datong (the "great harmony") and people-as-the-root, and says their union resolves the old dispute over ancient versus modern and Chinese versus Western. The result is described as mutual fulfilment: Marxism gains Chinese roots, and traditional culture becomes modern.

Wang concludes that the Two Integrations flow necessarily from the single integration, which rooted Marxism in China, while the second makes that rooting firm by strengthening its historical and popular base. The article calls for maintaining Marxism's guiding position, drawing on traditional governance wisdom, and using the Two Integrations as the method for Chinese modernization, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a people-centred approach. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese account of how Party theorists trace the second integration back to Mao's wartime formulations and present it as a continuous line of thought.
quoteEn: The proposition of the "single integration" already contains the implication of the "second integration".
quoteZh: “一个结合”命题包含了“第二个结合”的意蕴。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressed by Xi Jinping since 2021: integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It extends Mao Zedong's earlier call for the sinification of Marxism.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the current era. The term "sinification of Marxism" goes back to Mao in 1938.

A 1943 formulation by Mao that Marxism should be deeply combined with China's revolutionary practice, history and culture. The article treats it as the point at which culture entered the idea of integration.
Official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China
st: The distinctive view of history embedded in Chinese modernization
zh: 中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化
zhSub: 中国式现代化蕴含的独特历史观
source: People's Forum · Academic Frontiers (人民论坛·学术前沿), 2023 no. 8
paras: Xia Chuntao takes up the formula from the 20th Party Congress report (2022) that Chinese modernization is "socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China". The article asks who leads China's modernization and which road it takes, and answers from history. Xia argues that Party leadership and the socialist road are inseparable, and that holding to both reflects a correct view of history.

The article is organised in three parts: modernization led by the Party, modernization as socialist modernization, and the unity of the two. It runs from the Opium War of 1840 through the failed reform efforts of the late Qing and early Republic. It then follows the Party's record across the New Democratic Revolution, the Mao-era building of socialism, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It ends with a section on historical nihilism.

Xia's first move is that every earlier attempt to modernize China failed: the Taiping, the Self-Strengthening Movement, the 1898 reforms and the 1911 Revolution. In Xia's account only the Party completed the anti-imperialist and anti-feudal tasks and then led national construction. The second move is that capitalism was neither viable nor desirable for China. Xia cites Sun Yat-sen's doubts about the West, the chaos of early Republican parliamentary politics, and imperialist aggression. Xia also says the post-1949 socialist transformation settled the question of path at the institutional level. Xia presents China's "five features" of modernization, including common prosperity and peaceful development, as meeting the essential requirements of socialism, and contrasts them with Western modernization, which Xia associates with polarisation, colonial plunder and hegemonism. Xia adds that the Party's leadership was "history's conclusion and the people's choice", not self-appointed.

Xia concludes that Party leadership is the greatest advantage of Chinese modernization and determines its fundamental character. Xia warns that historical nihilism, which Xia says is spreading through new online forms such as entertainment-style "retellings" and fragmented "newly declassified" material, denies the Party's leadership and the socialist road, and calls for firm defences against it. The article closes by urging the Party to follow the historical trend, strengthen historical initiative and hold firm historical confidence. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's account of how the leadership-plus-socialism formula is justified historically, and of how historical nihilism is characterised.
quoteEn: The Party's leadership is the greatest advantage of Chinese modernization and determines its fundamental nature.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国式现代化的最大优势，决定中国式现代化的根本性质。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation, developed especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to modernization. It is said to share common features with other countries' modernization while having distinct Chinese characteristics.
In Party usage, a label for views that are said to deny or distort the Party's history and the socialist path. Official texts treat it as an ideological danger.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978. It shifted the Party's focus to economic development and brought market reforms and engagement with the world economy.

t: Mao Zedong and the five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization
zh: 毛泽东与中华文明突出特性
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2024 no. 3
paras: Shao Yong's article starts from the claim that Chinese modernization continues Chinese civilization and is directly linked to the five outstanding characteristics of that civilization identified by Xi Jinping. Shao argues that Mao Zedong, drawing on wide historical knowledge and a deep grounding in traditional culture, made many incisive remarks on each of these characteristics, which are worth revisiting. The author calls for upholding fundamental principles while innovating, so as to continue the historical cultural lineage.

The article is organised into five sections, one for each characteristic: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. Each section is built from a chronological string of Mao's speeches, letters, poems, marginal annotations on historical works and conversations with foreign visitors, from the 1930s to the 1970s. Shao uses these to show Mao's reading of Chinese history, from the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors to Sun Yat-sen.

On continuity, Shao stresses Mao's 1938 statement that as Marxist historicists the Communists should not cut off history, and his 1941 criticism of Party members who neglected the study of their own past. Shao also points to the lesson Mao drew from Li Zicheng's defeat. On unity, Shao shows Mao repeatedly praising Qin Shihuang, Cao Cao and Xie An for their roles in unifying the country, and treating unity as the basic guarantee of the cause. On innovation and inclusiveness, Shao cites Mao's formulas of making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China, and his view that socialism might pass through an undeveloped and a more developed stage. Shao presents this as an intellectual basis for the later theory of the primary stage of socialism. Shao adds that inclusiveness has principles: one selects what is good and rejects the rest.

On peacefulness, Shao cites Mao's calls for ending civil war in 1936, the 1945 Chongqing negotiations, and the principle of peaceful coexistence among states with different social systems. Shao also cites Mao's view that the war against Japan was fought to win lasting peace, and his statement that China does not want war but would firmly repel aggression. Shao concludes that Mao's remarks show a deep connection between Mao's thought and Chinese civilization's distinctive traits. Read the original if you want a dense, source-based compilation of Mao's statements on Chinese history and culture, arranged by the five characteristics, as used in current Party scholarship.
quoteEn: In Mao Zedong's view, innovation means, under the guidance of Marxism, truly making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China, bringing forth the new from the old and establishing a distinctive school of one's own.
quoteZh: 在毛泽东看来，创新就是在马克思主义指导下真正做到古为今用、洋为中用、推陈出新、独树一帜。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models and rooted in Chinese conditions and traditions.
The official thesis, developed in the 1980s, that China is in a long initial period of socialism marked by underdeveloped productive forces.

glossary.pinyin: gǔ wéi jīn yòng, yáng wéi Zhōng yòng
glossary.en: making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China
glossary.literal: let the ancient serve the present, let the foreign serve China
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Mao Zedong on cultural policy: critically drawing on both China's heritage and foreign cultures for present socialist needs.

t: Promoting cultural development with the people at the centre
zh: 以人民为中心推动文化建设
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2024, asks why and how cultural development should be people-centred. Sun Daiyao argues that a people-centred orientation has been the Party's consistent position on culture throughout its century-plus history. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the author says, it has been expressed as culture developed for the people, by the people and with its fruits shared by the people.

The piece is organised in three parts: the theoretical and practical grounds for a people-centred approach; the fundamental question of "for whom, relying on whom, and who am I"; and the practical orientation of cultural work. It draws on Marx and Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and above all Xi Jinping's remarks on literature and art. Examples include Lenin's exchange with Gorky, Mao's praise of Lu Xun and Fadeyev's The Rout, and the Epic of Gilgamesh.

Sun's central claim is that culture originates in the people's practice, belongs to them, and stays vital only if it voices their concerns. Cultural workers are therefore called on to serve the people and socialism, to enrich people's spiritual world, to respect the people's principal role and to treat the people as judges of quality. Sun connects this to Chinese modernization, described as the coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, and to the free and all-round development of the individual. The article also presents it as a requirement for telling China's story abroad.

Sun proposes three practical steps: strengthening cultural confidence and recording the people's creative achievements; standardising and equalising basic public cultural services across regions and between town and countryside, so as to achieve common prosperity in spiritual life; and supplying high-quality cultural products. On the last point, the author holds that the main problem is no longer shortage but quality, and that social benefit must come first in the cultural industries. Read the original if you want a concise Party-theoretical statement of how people-centred cultural policy is framed, with its standard classical and Xi Jinping citations.
quoteEn: Culture originates in the people's practice and belongs to the people.
quoteZh: 文化源于人民实践，文化属于人民。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, articulated prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, among other features.
A socialist goal of shared wealth and narrowing of inequality, emphasised by Deng Xiaoping and given renewed prominence under Xi Jinping. Here it is extended to spiritual and cultural life.
A concept promoted under Xi Jinping referring to confidence in the value and vitality of Chinese culture, including revolutionary culture and traditional culture.
The Communist Party congress of 2012 at which Xi Jinping became General Secretary; official texts use it to mark the start of the "new era".

t: The worldview and methodology contained in Xi Jinping's thought on culture
zh: 习近平文化思想蕴含的世界观和方法论
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2024 no. 5
paras: Mei and Chen take up Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, first put forward at the national conference on propaganda, ideological and cultural work in October 2023. They treat it as the cultural chapter of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article argues that it applies that thought's worldview and methodology through the "six musts": putting the people first, being self-confident and independent, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, being problem-oriented, adopting a systems approach, and taking the whole world into account.

The article is organised in six sections, one for each "must". Each section ties the principle to a Marxist basis, such as the mass view of history, dialectics, historical and dialectical materialism, or the theory of world history. Each then shows how the principle appears in Xi's statements and in Party policy on culture. The authors add historical narrative covering the late Qing, the May Fourth period, the early People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the post-2012 period. They also add policy examples on rural cultural revitalisation, cultural digitisation, ideological security and international communication.

Three moves carry the argument. First, the people-first principle is said to answer the basic questions of whom culture is for, whom it relies on, and who cultural workers are. Cultural self-confidence is traced to cultural subjectivity, which the authors say Marxism restored after the loss caused by the "wholesale Westernisation" position, and which the Two Integrations then deepened. Second, the authors read "upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground" as the core of the thought. It draws on the Chinese tradition of renewal and rests on the Two Integrations, which they say are building a modern Chinese civilisation distinct from Western modernity. Third, they present the problem-oriented, systems and global-minded principles as methods. These address the contradiction between people's cultural needs and uneven development, ideological risk, coordination of culture with the economy, politics and ecology, and exchange and mutual learning among civilisations.

The authors conclude that the six musts run through all of the Party's cultural work in the new era and serve as an ideological weapon and guide to action for building a leading socialist cultural country. They call for continued study, interpretation and application of this worldview and methodology in cultural practice, in support of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars link Xi's cultural thought to Marxist philosophy and to the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles without clinging to the old, and respecting antiquity without restoring it, contains the rich dialectical thinking of Chinese culture. It embodies the dialectic between change and constancy and between inheritance and innovation in cultural construction, and the principle of advancing through upholding fundamentals and innovating through respect for antiquity.
quoteZh: 守正不守旧、尊古不复古包含了中华文化丰富的辩证法思想，体现了文化建设变与不变、传承与创新的辩证关系，体现了在守正中前行、在尊古中创新的原则。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on cultural work first formally announced at the national propaganda, ideological and cultural work conference in October 2023. Official discourse presents it as the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six methodological principles in official discourse on Xi Jinping Thought: put the people first, be self-confident and independent, uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground, be problem-oriented, adopt a systems approach, and take the whole world into account.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was emphasised by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.

glossary.literal: modern civilisation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept from Xi's 2023 cultural speeches. It describes a modern civilisation said to form through the Two Integrations and Chinese modernization, distinct from Western modern civilisation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: New quality productive forces and a new horizon in adapting Marxist productive-forces theory to China
zh: 新质生产力与马克思主义生产力理论中国化新境界
source: Studies of the Marxist Theory Discipline (Marxism Theory Discipline Research), 2024 no. 4
paras: Tang Zhengdong asks what Xi Jinping's discourse on new quality productive forces adds to the Marxist theory of productive forces. The article argues that Marx and Engels concentrated on how capitalist relations of production fetter the productive forces. New quality productive forces, in Tang's reading, give an original account of how productive forces develop within a given set of production relations, here the socialist market economy. Tang presents this as a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three parts. It first reviews how Marx and Engels treated productive forces, drawing on The German Ideology, the Communist Manifesto, Capital, the 1857–58 manuscripts and the 1859 Preface. It then sets out the conditions of China's new development stage and Xi's definition of the concept. Finally it lists three ways the concept develops Marxist theory.

Tang's central move is to separate two dimensions of the theory. One is the fettering of productive forces by existing relations of production. The other is the room that a given relation can still accommodate before it is exhausted. Tang finds the second dimension only in embryo in Marx, in the Preface's claim that no social formation perishes before all the productive forces it can contain have developed, and in the 1857–58 description of future productive forces as free and unobstructed. Tang argues that Xi links the Two Inevitables and the Two Never-Wills and so develops both dimensions.

Tang then argues that new quality productive forces, driven by innovation, define advanced productive forces by the new development philosophy and clarify the laws of socialist productive-force development. These laws combine liberating and developing productive forces, now through deepened reform and original technological innovation. Tang concludes that the socialist market economy has wide room for productive forces, and that the task is to resolve the gap between that system and the forces it has not yet released. Read the original if you want a philosophical, textual account of how Party theorists place this concept within historical materialism, with close reference to Marx's own passages.
quoteEn: The systematic application and creative development of the two dimensions of the historical-materialist theory of the contradictory movement of productive forces and relations of production by new quality productive forces opens up a new horizon in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 新质生产力对历史唯物主义生产力与生产关系矛盾运动理论中两个维度的系统运用和创造性发展，开辟了马克思主义中国化时代化发展的新境界

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It describes innovation-led, high-tech and high-efficiency productive forces that break with traditional growth paths.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era.
The five principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015 at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee.

A shorthand for Marx's 1859 Preface claim that no social order perishes before its productive forces are fully developed, and no new relations appear before their material conditions mature. It is paired with the 'Two Inevitables' of capitalism's fall and the proletariat's victory.

t: Where historical initiative comes from
st: The methodological orientation of Mao Zedong's On Protracted War
zh: 历史主动何自来
zhSub: 毛泽东《论持久战》中的方法论指向
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Yang Dong asks how Communists seize historical initiative, a concept much discussed in recent Chinese theory, and answers by rereading Mao Zedong's On Protracted War (1938). Although the text sets out strategy against Japan, Yang argues that it is a classic methodological guide to grasping and exercising historical initiative, and that it matters for developing a stronger sense of initiative in the new era.

The article is organised in five parts. The first four draw out, in turn, the correct reading of the situation, the subjective consciousness and political responsibility of the agent, conscious initiative, and scientific foresight. The fifth part turns to what the present can draw from the classic. Yang works mainly through close reading of Mao's text, together with his 1936 talk with Edgar Snow, his 1937 report to Party activists and his dispute with Wang Ming over who should lead the united front.

Yang's central claim is that initiative is not rash action but depends on a one-sided or comprehensive view of reality. Mao's rejection of both the theory of national subjugation and the theory of quick victory is read as a rejection of subjective and one-sided judgement, which leads to blind action. Yang argues that initiative requires grasping the particular features of each side's contradictions, and that the Party and the awakened masses are its twin bearers. Conscious dynamism means turning inferiority into superiority through flexibility and knowledge of laws, while avoiding gambles on decisive battles.
