Finally it lists achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in eight areas: the economy, democracy and law, culture, livelihoods, ecology, Party building, the military and foreign affairs.

The core claim is that reform since 2012 has been pursued with unprecedented resolve and has made the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics more mature and fixed. The commentary asserts that no other country or party has shown comparable political courage or carried out reform on such a scale and so quickly. It presents these results as proof of the importance of the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds and of the leadership role of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.

The commentary concludes that reform and opening up has no end point and calls on readers to study Xi's statements on reform, build consensus and keep pushing reform forward. Under the Party's leadership, it says, reform will supply strong impetus and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party press framed the Third Plenum at the time of its opening.
quoteEn: Reform and opening up has only a continuous tense, never a completed one.
quoteZh: 改革开放只有进行时,没有完成时。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's own path of modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal, often tied to building a strong, modernized China by mid-century.

t: The theoretical contribution, connotation and development path of new quality productive forces
zh: 新质生产力的理论贡献、内涵特征和发展路径
authors: Research Group on New Quality Productive Forces, Economic Committee of the CPPCC National Committee
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 17 July 2024 and written by a research group of the CPPCC National Committee's Economic Committee, explains what new quality productive forces are and how to develop them. It presents the concept as one that Xi Jinping put forward by combining the basic principles of Marxist political economy with economic practice in the new era. The group argues that the concept has three theoretical contributions, a definite set of defining features, and a clear path of development.

The article follows Xi's remarks during inspection tours from July 2023 and his systematic exposition at the 11th collective study session of the 20th Politburo (January 2024). It has three sections. The first covers the concept's theoretical contribution, the second its connotation and features, and the third six lines of work for promoting it.

On theory, the group places the concept in a lineage running from Mao Zedong's emphasis on liberating and protecting productive forces through Deng Xiaoping's "science and technology are the primary productive force", Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao's Scientific Outlook on Development. It describes the concept as an innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and as a development of Marx's three-element account of productive forces (labourers, means of labour, objects of labour) that adds digital technologies and data. It also treats the concept as a deepening of Xi Jinping's economic thought. On features, the group lists revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors, deep transformation of development methods (intelligent, green and integrated), and a marked rise in total factor productivity as the core indicator.

On the path forward, the group proposes high-level scientific and technological self-reliance, supported by basic research and a new whole-nation system; a modern industrial system; green and low-carbon transition; new relations of production suited to the new forces, including factor-market reform, data valuation and wider opening up; promotion of entrepreneurship; and new mechanisms for training and attracting talent. It argues that these measures would raise productivity, build material wealth and improve people's wellbeing. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how the concept is framed theoretically and what policy steps are linked to it as of mid-2024.
quoteEn: The salient feature of new quality productive forces is innovation, including innovation in technology and business models as well as in management and institutions.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的显著特点是创新，既包括技术和业态模式层面的创新，也包括管理和制度层面的创新。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading. It is presented as the basis for high-quality development.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's continuing effort to apply Marxism to Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
Hu Jintao's guiding concept, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
An official term for mobilising state, market and institutional resources nationally to achieve major scientific and technological goals.

t: Adhering to reform and innovation to advance new quality productive forces
zh: 坚持改革创新推动新质生产力发展
paras: Ding Jinqing, writing in the Economic Daily in July 2024, takes up the question of how new quality productive forces can be developed through reform. Citing Xi Jinping's statement that developing them requires further comprehensively deepening reform and forming new types of relations of production, Ding argues that the task is both a development question and a reform question. The article is a newspaper commentary rather than a research paper.

It is organised in three parts. The first deals with deepening reform to release innovative vitality, mainly in science and technology institutions. The second concerns accelerating a modernised industrial system through intelligent, green and integrated industry. The third is about shaping new relations of production through reform of the economic system and of education, science and technology, and talent systems.

Ding's central claim is that innovation, both technological and institutional, is the defining feature of new quality productive forces, so institutional barriers must be removed. On science and technology, Ding calls for perfecting the new whole-nation system, strengthening the Party Central Committee's centralised leadership of scientific work, using the socialist system's ability to concentrate resources on major tasks, and expanding international scientific cooperation, including through the Belt and Road Initiative. On industry, Ding urges supply-side structural reform to make industry more intelligent (artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, new growth engines such as commercial space and the low-altitude economy), greener (carbon trading, green certificates, ecological compensation) and more integrated across sectors and regions. On relations of production, Ding invokes the Marxist principle that productive forces determine relations of production, and argues for a high-standard socialist market economy, a unified national market, support for private firms under the Two Unwaverings, and joined-up reform of education, science and talent so that innovative personnel can be trained and rewarded.

Ding concludes that deepening reform and opening up at a higher starting point will clear the obstacles that hold back new quality productive forces and provide continuing momentum for high-quality development. The piece is a policy-oriented exposition that restates official lines on reform, industry and talent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official commentary in 2024 linked new quality productive forces to institutional reform, industrial upgrading and talent policy.
quoteEn: Accelerating the development of new quality productive forces is both a question of development and a question of reform.
quoteZh: 加快发展新质生产力，既是发展命题，也是改革命题。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industry, characterised as high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality.
An official economic goal, prominent since 2017, that emphasises innovation, efficiency, green growth and balance over the speed of growth alone.
An official term for mobilising state, market and research resources nationwide under Party leadership to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs.
The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A policy line introduced in 2015 aimed at improving the quality and structure of supply, such as cutting overcapacity and upgrading industry.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Making socialism with Chinese characteristics "the best system in the world"
st: Deng Xiaoping's thought on institution-building and the further deepening of reform
zh: 让中国特色社会主义“成为世界上最好的制度”
paras: Writing in 2024, the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth and the opening year of the "further comprehensively deepening reform" agenda, Zhao Lingyun asks what Deng's thinking on institution-building was and how it guided reform. Zhao argues that its core is Deng's 1980 aspiration that the socialist system would "become the best system in the world", and that reform and opening up is best read as a process of institution-building.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Deng's thought around four questions: what counts as the best system, why socialism with Chinese characteristics can become it, when, and how. The second traces institution-building in three phases: rectification and restoration (1975, 1977–78), reform and innovation from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the 18th Party Congress (2012), and institutional integration and operation since then. The third looks ahead to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Zhao argues that Deng offered evaluation criteria (political stability, popular unity and living standards, sustained growth of the productive forces) and tied the goal to the mid-twenty-first century, which Zhao links to the "Two Centenary Goals". Zhao claims the post-2012 reforms moved from building a basic framework (2014–16), through key reforms (2017–19), to system integration (2020–23), while also converting institutional strengths into governance effectiveness, citing the response to Covid-19. The "new development stage" is presented as the key step toward the "best system", a stage of quantitative accumulation approaching a qualitative leap.

For further deepening of reform, Zhao proposes focusing on a complete, standardised and effective institutional system, supplying the institutions Chinese modernization needs (a common prosperity system, institutions supporting new quality productive forces), and expanding institutional openness. The last point rests on Deng's "two bold absorptions", with a clearer distinction between capitalism's fundamental and specific institutions. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-theory account of how Deng's institutional thinking is used to frame four decades of reform and the agenda of 2024.
quoteEn: "Becoming the best system in the world" is Deng Xiaoping's long-term strategic conception for developing and perfecting the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and also a major strategic design for reform and opening up and institution-building.
quoteZh: “成为世界上最好的制度”是邓小平关于发展和完善中国特色社会主义制度的长远战略构想，也是关于改革开放与制度建设的重大战略设计。

glossary.explanation: The reform agenda set for the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024, presented as continuing the comprehensive deepening of reform launched in 2013.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).
The official term, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to modernization.
A concept promoted from 2023–24 by Xi Jinping, stressing technology-driven, innovation-led productive forces as the basis of high-quality development.
A long-standing socialist goal that the Party has stressed again since the 2020s, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than polarisation.
The term, used in the article for the post-2012 approach of coordinating reforms into a coherent, complete and effective system.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization requires adherence to independence, self-reliance and self-strengthening
zh: 推进中国式现代化必须坚持独立自主自立自强
authors: Party Leadership Group of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
paras: This article, issued collectively by the Party leadership group of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and carried in Qiushi in 2024, sets out why Chinese modernization must rest on independence, self-reliance and self-strengthening. It argues that this principle is a historical conclusion of the Party's century of struggle, a necessity in the present international environment, and something to be upheld through strategic resolve, theoretical innovation, balanced opening up and determined struggle. It frames the principle with Xi Jinping's statements and the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

The text has three parts. The first traces independence and self-reliance through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution under Mao Zedong, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up under Deng Xiaoping, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi. The second explains why the principle is needed now and what supports it. The third sets out four practical requirements.

In the second part the authors make three main moves. They argue that universal laws of social development coexist with diverse national paths, citing Marx and Lenin, so that no country can be strong by following others, and China cannot copy Western modernization given its size and its more than 1.4 billion people. They describe a harsher external environment, with containment and suppression by the United States and other Western states, and weak original innovation and dependence on foreign core technologies, so that high-level scientific self-reliance becomes a priority. They also list the foundations they see for self-reliance: Party leadership, the socialist system's capacity to concentrate resources, economic and scientific indicators such as 2023 GDP above 126 trillion yuan, and cultural confidence.

The conclusion lists the requirements: keep strategic resolve and avoid both a closed, rigid old path and an erroneous path of abandoning socialism; pursue the Two Integrations to advance theoretical innovation; treat self-reliance and opening up dialectically, building the new development pattern with domestic circulation as the mainstay while staying open; and meet risks with determined struggle. The authors hold that, on this basis, China can become a modern socialist great power. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of the official case for self-reliance as a principle of Chinese modernization, and the sources it draws on.
quoteEn: In human history, no nation or country has become strong and revitalised by relying on external forces or following others step by step.
quoteZh: 人类历史上，没有一个民族、没有一个国家可以通过依赖外部力量、跟在他人后面亦步亦趋实现强大和振兴。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as having five features, including a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.

The formula of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is a core principle of the Party's theoretical innovation under Xi Jinping.

glossary.literal: independence and autonomy, self-reliance and self-strengthening
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party principle that China decides its own path and depends mainly on its own strength. Under Xi it is applied in particular to science and technology.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
An economic strategy announced in 2020 that makes domestic circulation the mainstay while linking it with international circulation.

t: Mao Zedong and the outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization
zh: 毛泽东与中华文明突出特性
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2024 no. 3
paras: Shao Yong takes up the five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization that Xi Jinping has summarised and asks what Mao Zedong said about each of them. The article argues that Chinese modernization continues Chinese civilization, and that Mao, drawing on wide historical knowledge and classical learning, offered incisive remarks on all five that are worth revisiting. Shao ends by urging adherence to the principle of upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, so as to carry the historical cultural lineage forward.

The article is organised in five sections, one for each characteristic: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. Each section assembles Mao's speeches, letters, poems, marginal notes on the dynastic histories and conversations with foreign visitors from the 1930s to the 1970s. Shao presents these sources largely in chronological order, with brief commentary. Examples include the 1938 report on the Party's place in the national war, the 1939 essay 'The Chinese Revolution and the Chinese Communist Party', the 1937 sacrificial text for the Yellow Emperor's tomb and Mao's remarks on Qin Shihuang and Cao Cao.

On continuity, Shao stresses Mao's formula that Marxist historicists must not cut off history, and shows him using Chinese history as a guide for the Party. Examples are the circulation of Guo Moruo's essay on Li Zicheng to guard against complacency after victory, and the call for research on the past century's history. On innovation, Shao reads Mao's idea of making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China as a creative method. Shao also treats Mao's 1959–60 view that socialism has an underdeveloped and a more developed stage as a basis for the later theory of the primary stage of socialism. On unity, Shao cites Mao's repeated praise of Qin Shihuang, Cao Cao and Xie An as unifiers, and his rejection of a 1949 proposal to divide China along the Yangtze.

Shao shows Mao's inclusiveness in his support for letting a hundred flowers bloom and a hundred schools contend, and in his call to learn from every nation's strengths while adopting them selectively. His peacefulness appears in his calls for ending civil war in the 1930s, the Chongqing negotiations, and his statements on peaceful coexistence and resistance only to aggression. Shao concludes that Mao's thinking links closely to the five characteristics and that inclusiveness has principles, accepting what is good and rejecting what is not. Read the original if you want a dense, chronologically arranged collection of Mao's statements on Chinese history and tradition, organised around Xi Jinping's formulation of civilizational characteristics.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's theoretical innovation that socialist society may pass through stages provided an intellectual basis for the 'primary stage of socialism' thesis, the basic theoretical premise of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 毛泽东关于社会主义社会可能分阶段的理论创新，为中国特色社会主义的基本理论前提——“社会主义初级阶段”论，提供了思想基础。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as rooted in Chinese civilization and socialism.

glossary.zh: 中华文明五大突出特性
glossary.pinyin: Zhōnghuá wénmíng wǔ dà tūchū tèxìng
glossary.en: five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization
glossary.literal: five prominent features of Chinese civilization
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2023 summary of Chinese civilization as marked by continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. It is used in official discourse on cultural heritage.
The Party's official assessment, formalised in 1987, that China remains in a long initial period of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces. It underlies current policy.

t: Mao Zedong's theoretical reflections and strategic planning on national political security
zh: 毛泽东关于国家政治安全的理论思考与战略谋划
source: Journal of China Jinggangshan Cadre Academy, 2024 no. 1
paras: Political security, the authors write, is the foundation of national security, covering sovereignty, state power, the system and ideology. The article asks what Mao Zedong understood by national political security and how he planned to achieve it. Ye and Zheng argue that Mao applied the basic principles of the Marxist view of national security to Chinese conditions, and so laid the groundwork for a national security path with Chinese characteristics.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Mao's concept of political security: its four meanings (complete sovereignty, a stable state power, institutional security and ideological security) and its source and purpose in the people. The second sets out four strategic measures. The third draws lessons for the present, tied to the holistic national security outlook and to the new era.

On the authors' account, Mao held that people are the decisive factor, more so than institutions, and that political security is both achieved through the people and meant to serve them. The strategic plan has four elements. The first is keeping the Party from degenerating, with the Soviet collapse offered as a warning. The second is a people's army backed by a modern defence industry. The third is struggle, which covers military action, diplomacy by means of the Five Principles, and internal struggle against corruption and in the ideological sphere. The fourth is training successors to the proletarian cause, as a defence against the "peaceful evolution" strategy associated with John Foster Dulles. The authors present Mao's emphasis on Marxist education and on remoulding workers as part of this effort.

For the present, Ye and Zheng propose three tasks. The first is to strengthen the Party's leadership of political security, including its strategic thinking, its ability to mobilise the masses and its leadership in ideological struggle, with online ideological struggle singled out. The second is to use the people's role in safeguarding security, through identification with the system, wider outreach, and reporting and reward mechanisms. The third is to build a material base through Chinese modernization and common prosperity, with attention to distribution, to coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution, and to tax and social security tools. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Party scholars link Mao-era security thinking to current national security policy.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong held that external causes are the condition of change and internal causes its basis, with external causes working through internal ones.
quoteZh: 毛泽东认为：“外因是变化的条件，内因是变化的根据，外因通过内因而起作用。”

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path of modernization. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A goal of shared wealth for all, associated with socialism and emphasised in recent Party policy. Mao used the term in 1955 when discussing agricultural cooperation.
Xi Jinping's framework, introduced in 2014, which treats security as spanning many fields and takes political security as its foundation.
A term in Chinese Party discourse for a supposed Western strategy of changing socialist states from within, by ideological and cultural means, without war.

t: Overseas scholars' perceptions and assessments of Chinese-style agricultural and rural modernization
zh: 海外学者关于中国式农业农村现代化的认知与评价
paras: This literature review, published in 2024 in Contemporary China History Studies, surveys how scholars and institutions outside China have understood and evaluated Chinese-style agricultural and rural modernization since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Chen Yitao notes that Chinese scholarship has tracked overseas rural studies mainly by looking at researchers, theories and methods. The article instead samples English-language work from roughly the past decade, to offer an "other's perspective" and help "tell the story" of rural revitalization.

The sources include journals such as The China Quarterly, think tanks such as the International Institute for Environment and Development, and bodies such as the Asian Development Bank and the OECD. Chen organises the material under four headings: achievements (agriculture, farmer incomes, rural public services, grassroots governance); driving forces; distinctive features; and global significance. A closing section describes the characteristics, contributions and limits of the overseas literature.

In Chen's account, overseas writers see four mutually supporting drivers: Party leadership as the leading force, farmers as the main agents (including returning youth, the "new farmers"), institutional flexibility, and technological diffusion. They identify three distinctive features: combining top-level design with local pilot projects, urban–rural integration alongside green development, and a value orientation centred on farmers' welfare. They also credit China with contributing to global food security, to cooperation opportunities, and to rural governance and poverty-reduction models for developing countries. Chen largely presents these views as consistent with China's actual conditions.

Chen concludes that overseas research is diverse in its authors, scope and methods, and is often driven by pragmatic policy concerns. It supplements domestic scholarship, though a minority of authors are said to remain bound by "Western-centrism" or to exaggerate rural problems. Chen calls for tracking foreign research, rebutting what the article regards as misrepresentation, and building a discourse system that is Chinese in character but intelligible abroad, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a catalogue of the overseas scholars, think tanks and reports that Chinese academics cite on rural modernization, and a sense of how they are being read.
quoteEn: Overseas scholars hold that Chinese-style agricultural and rural modernization is a modernization that always places the interests of the peasantry at its core, and that continually meeting farmers' needs for a better life and promoting rural social fairness and justice are its value orientation and inner driving force.
quoteZh: 海外学者认为，中国式农业农村现代化是始终把农民群众利益置于核心地位的现代化，不断满足农民群众对美好生活的需要、促进农村社会公平正义是农业农村现代化的价值导向和内在动力。

glossary.zh: 中国式农业农村现代化
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's own path to modernizing agriculture, villages and farmers' livelihoods under Party leadership. It is the rural component of the wider Chinese modernization agenda.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop rural industries, ecology, governance and living standards. It followed the campaign against poverty.

t: The idea of inter-subjectivity in traditional Chinese culture and its contemporary significance
zh: 中国传统文化中的互主体思想及其现实意义
paras: Cheng Long takes up a question raised by Xi Jinping's call to advance the Second Integration: what is the basic character of traditional Chinese culture? Some scholars locate it in 'subjectivity'. Cheng disputes this, since Western thought from Descartes through Kant and Hegel also champions human subjectivity. The article argues that the distinguishing trait is 'inter-subjectivity' (互主体性). Western culture proceeds from the 'self' and a subject–object split, and so is in essence single-subject. Chinese culture proceeds from the unity of self and other, and so favours pluralistic coexistence.

The article has three parts. The first reads Confucian, Daoist, Mohist and some Legalist texts, plus modern figures such as Hong Xiuquan, Kang Youwei and Sun Yat-sen, for five kinds of relation between subjects: harmony and integration, mutual respect and love, equality, tolerance, and good faith. The second asks why the idea arose so early, drawing on a historical-materialist comparison with ancient Greece. The third sets out its present-day significance.

Cheng gives three reasons for the contrast, each tied to China's formative period. First, humanism emerged early: belief in ghosts and spirits gave way, from the Yin–Zhou transition, to concern with people, whereas Greek thought looked outward to nature and was constrained by religion. Second, the rich river-valley geography made the 'person–person' relation the main problem, while Greece's poor, fragmented land pushed trade, expansion and a 'philosophy of struggle'. Third, clan kinship survived in China as a 'family–state unity', whereas in Greece it dissolved into contractual political relations, which in Cheng's account led to others being treated as objects.

Cheng concludes that inter-subjectivity offers a window onto the distinctive value of traditional culture. It helps end the modern 'ancient–modern, East–West' dispute. It also supplements Marxism, which in Cheng's view says little concrete about how subjects cultivate themselves under socialism. Finally, it forms the cultural basis of a community with a shared future for mankind, set against what the author calls Western zero-sum hegemonic logic. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-by-text case for a China–West contrast built on inter-subjectivity, and its link to current Party discourse on the Second Integration.
quoteEn: Committing to the construction of inter-subjective relations is the consistent value pursuit of traditional Chinese culture; it embodies the essence of that culture and is the fundamental trait distinguishing Chinese from Western civilization.
quoteZh: 致力互主体关系的建构，这是中国传统文化一以贯之的价值追求，体现了中国传统文化的精髓，更是中华文明不同于西方文明的根本特质所在。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2023, for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's excellent traditional culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the first being with China's concrete realities.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted since about 2012–2013. It stresses interdependence and shared development among states.
The author's key concept for a relation in which each party is treated as a subject rather than an object. The author contrasts it with a 'single-subject' Western mode of thought.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: A historical-political interpretation of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
st: Centred on how the Zhou–Qin transition shaped China's model of state governance
zh: 中华民族现代文明的历史政治学阐释
zhSub: 以周秦之变对中国国家治理模式的塑造为中心
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Huang Tao asks how the modern civilization of the Chinese nation should be understood in relation to China's ancient state. The article argues that this civilization is a politics-centred civilization that grew out of traditional Chinese civilization, so that its formation must be read with respect for historical continuity and close attention to major changes in the model of state governance. Using a historical-political approach, Huang takes the Zhou–Qin transition as the key moment for tracing that continuity.

The article defines the Zhou–Qin transition as a comprehensive transformation of Chinese civilization, led by changes in governance and state form. It runs from the founding of the Zhou dynasty (1046 BCE) to the death of Emperor Wu of Han (87 BCE), more than 900 years. Huang then reviews what Zhou and Qin institutions bequeathed and where they fell short. The article goes on to the late-Qing crisis, the revolutions led by the Communist Party, and the two great transformations seen together.

Huang's central claim is that the Zhou–Qin transition produced the core structure of Chinese civilization: six basic paradigms of state. These are the centralised state, the multi-ethnic state of diversity in unity, the all-under-heaven (tianxia) state, the unified state, the super-large-scale state and the secular state. From them derive features such as the county system, bureaucracy, a strong state, popular-basis (minben) thought and meritocracy. Huang argues that these formed the political and social setting for the modern revolutions, and that without these roots modern civilization would lose its foundation. The article also lists the limits of Zhou rule (weak centralisation, fragmentation, rigid hierarchy) and of Qin rule (excessive monarchical power, harsh law, a weak society). Huang holds that these limits were largely those of traditional civilization. It argues that the Party, guided by Marxism-Leninism and the Two Integrations, inherited the six paradigms. It also added socialism, republican democracy, the rule of law, the people's congress system and regional ethnic autonomy, reorganising them in a revolutionary way.

Huang concludes that continuity and major change are dialectically united in Chinese civilization: the two great transformations form a relay across more than two thousand years, and neither is a break or a simple inheritance. Both began with changes in governance and state form, which for Huang confirms that Chinese civilization is politics-centred. The author holds that modern China is on a path combining Chinese subjectivity, historical continuity and human universality, a result of civilizational renewal rather than rupture, and that a universal political science cannot exclude China. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese scholars use ancient state history to ground claims about the continuity of Chinese modernity.
quoteEn: Modern China is walking a correct path marked by Chinese subjectivity, historical continuity and human universality; this path is the result of civilizational renewal, not the product of civilizational rupture.
quoteZh: 现代中国恰恰走在一条具有中国主体性、历史连续性和人类普遍性的正确大道上，这条道路是文明更新的结果，不是文明断裂的产物。

glossary.literal: the change from Zhou to Qin
glossary.explanation: A term for the shift from the Zhou enfeoffment system to the unified, centralised bureaucratic monarchy of Qin and Han. Huang extends it from 1046 BCE to 87 BCE.
A formula in Party theory: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A state model based on the idea of a universal order 'under heaven' rather than a bounded nation-state. Huang counts it among China's six basic paradigms.
A Confucian-derived idea that the people are the foundation of the state, so that rulers should govern for their welfare.
A traditional ideal of political, territorial and cultural unity under one central authority, associated with Qin and Han.

t: Building China's independent knowledge system requires strengthening theoretical thinking
zh: 建构中国自主的知识体系必须强化理论思维
paras: Sun Laibin takes up Xi Jinping's call, made in 2022, to build China's independent knowledge system, and asks what role theoretical thinking should play in it. The article argues that philosophers and social scientists must deliberately strengthen theoretical thinking, using theoretical insight, abstraction and creativity to summarise Chinese experience in terms of "Chinese principles" and raise it to the level of Chinese theory.

The article has three parts. The first defines theoretical thinking, contrasts it with empirical thinking, and says why scholars in the new era should develop it. The second explains why building an independent knowledge system cannot do without it. The third sets out how the three capacities named above can each advance the project. Sun draws throughout on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Hegel and Einstein, and on Xi Jinping's speeches.

Sun distinguishes empirical thinking, based on experience and common sense, from theoretical thinking, which uses scientific abstraction to reach essence and laws. Moving from the first to the second needs abundant, accurate empirical material and the power of abstraction. The author holds that theoretical thinking helps turn "external" problems (conflicts between existing theory and new practice) into "internal" ones, and so serves the three priorities of subjectivity, originality and systematicity in Chinese-style philosophy and social science. In practice, theoretical insight is meant to grasp China's real conditions and identify genuine problems. Abstraction distils identifying concepts, with "a community with a shared future for mankind" given as a model. Creativity then organises concepts into a systematic whole, in the manner of Marx's method in Capital, fusing Marxism, traditional Chinese culture and foreign scholarship.

Sun concludes that scholars should use the Chinese worldview and methodology, in theoretical form, to explain Chinese modernization and turn its experience into theory. Sun lists high-quality development, new quality productive forces and similar concepts as new-era achievements that await further study. Read the original if you want to see how a Peking University Marxism scholar links the official project of an independent knowledge system to classical Marxist accounts of abstraction and theory-building.
quoteEn: Theoretical thinking is a mode of thinking that uses theory to grasp reality and guide practice.
quoteZh: 理论思维是用理论把握现实、引领实践的思维方式

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping used in April 2022 at Renmin University, describing the ultimate aim of building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. It is usually understood as comprising disciplinary, academic and discourse systems.
The official name for China's path of modernisation, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy thought, promoted since about 2012, about cooperative international relations and shared global interests.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological innovation and high-quality development.
An official economic goal since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

glossary.literal: China's reasoning / Chinese way of reasoning
glossary.explanation: Used in the article for the systematised, theorised principles and worldview that explain Chinese practice, rooted in Marxism and traditional Chinese culture.

t: Deng Xiaoping and Chinese modernization
zh: 邓小平与中国式现代化
source: Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping Theory Studies (Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping lilun yanjiu), 2024 no. 5
paras: Shi Zhongquan asks what role Deng Xiaoping played in Chinese modernization. The article's thesis is that, if Mao Zedong laid the foundations of the thinking behind Chinese modernization, Deng was the first to put forward the idea of a "Chinese-style modernization" and the great pioneer of the path that realises it.

The article has three parts. It first places Deng within the first generation of Party leaders and their exploration of socialist modernization, then examines the historical background and initial meaning of the idea in 1979. It next traces how Deng opened the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, through theoretical preparation, major reform policies and the 13th Party Congress (1987). Finally it treats Deng's 1992 southern tour talks as lifting this thinking to a new level.

Shi argues that Deng first used the phrase in March 1979 to describe a deliberately modest goal: a "xiaokang" (moderately well-off) standard, with per-capita GNP of around US$1,000 by the end of the century. Shi suggests Deng then preferred "the path of building socialism with Chinese characteristics" for four reasons: it was the more normative wording, the 1979 meaning did not reach beyond 2000, Deng was already planning for the 21st century, and the two concepts are related but not identical. Shi lists five theoretical "weapons" and three major policies behind the path, including letting some get rich first, the household contract responsibility system and the special economic zones. The 13th Party Congress added the primary stage of socialism, the basic line of "one centre, two basic points" and a three-step development strategy. The southern tour talks, Shi says, defended that basic line, set out the essence of socialism and the case for a socialist market economy, and served as Deng's "political testament".

Shi concludes that Deng's talks were the direct source of the theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, later named Deng Xiaoping Theory and treated as the origin of the system of theories of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Shi reads Deng's 1989 and 1992 speeches as a unity, and presents Deng's three-step strategy as the roadmap to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's account of how Deng's 1979 formulation relates to later official terminology and to his policies and theory.
quoteEn: "Chinese-style modernization" is a popular, figurative expression, whereas "building socialism with Chinese characteristics" is normative language that fixes a position.
quoteZh: “中国式的现代化”是通俗的形象说法，“建设有中国特色的社会主义”是定位性的规范语言。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Shi traces the phrase back to Deng Xiaoping's 1979 usage.

glossary.zh: 建设有中国特色的社会主义
glossary.pinyin: jiànshè yǒu Zhōngguó tèsè de shèhuìzhǔyì
glossary.explanation: The formula Deng Xiaoping announced at the 12th Party Congress (1982) for the Party's line of building socialism suited to Chinese conditions. It remains the Party's central label for its path.

The Party's assessment that China is at an early, long-lasting stage of socialism, in which it must develop its productive forces and a market economy. It was systematically set out at the 13th Party Congress (1987).
A placeholder; see xiaokang entry.

glossary.pinyin: yí gè zhōngxīn, liǎng gè jīběndiǎn
glossary.explanation: The Party's basic line from the 13th Party Congress (1987): economic development as the centre, with adherence to the Four Cardinal Principles and to reform and opening up as the two basic points.

t: Grasping the laws of Chinese modernization politically
zh: 从政治上把握中国式现代化建设规律
source: Study Times (Xuexi Shibao), 10 July 2024, p. A1
paras: This commentary in the Party School newspaper Study Times takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Central Economic Work Conference that advancing Chinese modernization must be treated as "the greatest politics". Bao Xinjian argues that this formulation is a fundamental guide for understanding the laws governing modernization from a political vantage point. In Bao's account, it matters for strengthening the Party's overall leadership, keeping modernization on the right course and releasing its driving force.

The article first sets out a Marxist view of politics: politics reflects fundamental interests and objective laws of economic and social development, is the operation and governance of the state, and concentrates the interests of the majority. It then identifies three sources of the political significance of Chinese modernization: the goal of national rejuvenation, the task of modernizing state governance, and the subjectivity and needs of the people.

On rejuvenation, Bao traces the path from the Opium War through failed reform and revolutionary attempts to the founding of the Communist Party, and then from Mao Zedong's "four modernizations" through Deng Xiaoping's "Chinese-style modernization" to Xi Jinping's theoretical innovation. The author presents modernization as the only correct road to national rejuvenation, one that does not copy Western models. On governance, Bao holds that institutions play a fundamental, overall, stable and long-term role. The article links this to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). In this reading, institutional reform turns institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. On the people, Bao says modernization is fundamentally the modernization of people, and that it avoids the polarisation, extreme individualism and loss of human subjectivity the author attributes to Western modernization driven by the "logic of capital". Meeting people's growing needs for a better life through high-quality development is described as its core political value.

Bao concludes that because Chinese modernization is the greatest politics, leaders must strengthen the Party's overall leadership from a political standpoint, hold to the people-centred orientation, and raise officials' political judgement, political understanding and political execution. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2024 justify the claim that modernization is "the greatest politics" through national rejuvenation, institutional reform and the people's role.
quoteEn: The people's aspirations are the greatest politics; it is precisely in continually meeting the people's growing needs for a better life, this core political value, that Chinese modernization becomes the greatest politics shaping every aspect of contemporary China.
quoteZh: 民心所向是最大的政治，正是在不断满足人民日益增长的美好生活需要这一核心政治价值上，中国式现代化成为影响当代中国一切方面的最大的政治。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official name for China's path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models and defined by features such as large population size and common prosperity.
An official economic priority since 2017, emphasising innovation, coordination, greener growth and sharing over speed of expansion alone.

t: A political-economy interpretation of new quality productive forces
zh: 新质生产力的政治经济学阐释
paras: Han Wenlong takes up Xi Jinping's 2023–2024 formulation of new quality productive forces and asks how it can be understood as a category of Marxist political economy. The author argues that the concept is a new political-economy category which enriches Marxist productive-force theory, and that it can be explained by materialist dialectics, by identifying its drivers and by pairing it with a partial change in relations of production.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the concept's meaning, covering the "new" and the "quality" in the term, the dialectic of quantitative and qualitative change, advancement of structure and content, and two unities that mark advanced productive forces. It then examines the motive force and sources of development, turns to the relations of production, and ends with practical paths. Han draws on Marx's remarks on means of labour, the productivity of labour, complex labour and distribution relations.

Han holds that the "new" lies in new elements (workers with new skills, intelligent equipment, digital and deep-sea or deep-space objects of labour) and in new technologies, industries, business forms and fields. The "quality" has four aspects: a new essence, high-quality development, high-quality living and a "quality" advantage in international competition. Demand change is presented as the trigger, the organic combination of production-force elements led by complex labour as the internal driver, and contradictions among those elements as the source. Han then argues that relations of production must be partly restructured. The proposals include a mixed ownership system for data elements with a "three-rights separation" of property rights, a collaborative innovation system led by a new national system, distribution tilted towards data, technological and complex labour, a high-standard market system, and consumption relations that integrate natural and social dimensions.

Han concludes that developing new quality productive forces is central to Chinese modernization and to building new competitive advantages. The practical agenda comprises high-level scientific and technological self-reliance, advanced manufacturing with strategic emerging and future industries, institutional reform of property rights, evaluation and incentives, and accumulation of high-quality human resources through complex labour. Read the original if you want a systematic Marxist-theoretical framing of the concept, including its treatment of data ownership, distribution and the labour theory, as well as its policy proposals.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are a new category of political economy, and understanding their profound meaning requires adherence to materialist dialectics.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是一个政治经济学的新范畴，认识和理解其深刻内涵需要坚持唯物辩证法

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and high-quality factors, as opposed to input-driven growth.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, presented in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
A model that mobilises state, market and social resources behind major scientific and technological goals, as in the projects the author cites.
Data treated as a production factor alongside land, labour and capital, subject to rules on property rights, trading and income distribution.

t: The multi-tense cultural form of Chinese modernization
zh: 多时态的中国式现代化文化形态
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in July 2024, takes up Xi Jinping's formulation that the "Second Integration" produces a new culture that becomes "the cultural form of Chinese modernization". An Deming argues that this cultural form is not static. It develops alongside Chinese modernization and enriches its theory and practice, and it has a dynamic, multi-stage character that can be read in three tenses: completed, ongoing and future.

The article is organised around these three tenses. The completed tense covers the cultural achievements of the Party-led revolution and socialist construction. The ongoing tense corresponds to cultural construction in the new era. The future tense concerns the goals and significance of that construction, both for China and for the wider world.

In An's account, the completed form rests on the organic combination of two core elements: excellent traditional Chinese culture and the basic principles of Marxism. Marxism acts as a "catalyst" that activates the cultural genes of the tradition, and An links the inclusiveness of Chinese civilisation to Marxist internationalism. For the ongoing tense, An cites Xi's point that the Two Integrations is a "chemical reaction", not a "platter" of parts. An therefore warns against treating tradition in a homogenised, mechanical way and calls for historical materialism, dialectics and a sublating attitude. Three practical paths follow: raising the cultural literacy of workers and the public, attending to living popular cultural practice (including intangible cultural heritage), and contributing Chinese approaches to international cultural exchange. The future tense is said to face both inward, towards confidence in Chinese culture, and outward, towards offering solutions to global problems.

An concludes that the multi-tense cultural form is both a result of Chinese modernization and a constituent part of its process. It shows, in An's view, that Chinese modernization is comprehensive, covering cultural and spiritual as well as scientific, technological and material dimensions. Emphasising this cultural form, An says, enriches the meaning of modernization and adds depth to the Chinese path. Read the original if you want a short, official-line account of how the Two Integrations is being framed as a cultural theory of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: This multi-tense cultural form of Chinese modernization is both a result of Chinese modernization and an organic component of its process.
quoteZh: 这种多时态的中国式现代化的文化形态，既属于中国式现代化的成果，又是中国式现代化进程的有机组成要素。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a modernization path with Chinese characteristics, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2023, for combining the basic principles of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, after the first, combining Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The Hegelian-Marxist notion of Aufhebung: simultaneously negating, preserving and transcending. Here it describes a critical, selective attitude towards tradition.

t: The fourfold transcendence of Chinese modernization as the modernization of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature
zh: 人与自然和谐共生的中国式现代化的四重超越
paras: Taking up the 20th Party Congress (2022) statement that Chinese modernization is a modernization of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature, Yan Xiaofeng and Zhang Yanhong ask how it differs from the Western path. They argue that it surpasses Western modernization on four levels: the view of nature, value stance, global governance and practical model. In their reading, it amounts to socialist modernization transcending capitalist modernization and offers a theoretical form and practical template for resolving what they call the institutional ecological crisis of the West.

The article is organised into four sections, one for each level, and each ends with a summary contrast with the West. It draws on Descartes, the Enlightenment, Marx's theory of metabolism between humans and nature, Lenin on raw materials and colonies, and classical Chinese thinkers such as Mencius, Zhuangzi and Xunzi. It also reviews Western "deep green" and "light green" currents, ecological modernization, and Chinese policy examples such as the Belt and Road Initiative and carbon targets.

The authors' central move is to trace Western ecological failure to capital's logic of accumulation. On the view of nature, they say Western dualism and anthropocentrism treat nature as capital's "tap" and "raw-material store", and that both green currents stay within this dualism. Chinese modernization instead rests on the "life community" idea, which they present as joining Marxist ecological thought with the traditional view of the unity of heaven and humanity. On values, they hold that capital exploits both nature and workers, while Chinese modernization is people-centred. On global governance, they describe Western "eco-imperialism", which shifts pollution and resource extraction onto developing countries, and contrast it with a community with a shared future for mankind and common but differentiated responsibilities. On practice, they say Western ecological governance never challenges capitalist institutions, whereas socialist ecological civilization integrates green development into economic, political, cultural and social construction.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization overcomes dualism, capital-centredness, hegemony and one-sidedness. They call it an original Chinese contribution to world modernization and civilization, and a path for developing countries towards green, low-carbon and sustainable development. They say it shows the institutional superiority of socialism in ecological civilization. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of the official Chinese case that Chinese modernization is ecologically distinct from, and superior to, Western modernization.
quoteEn: Western modernization is a modernization based on private ownership of the means of production and centred on the valorization of capital; the limits of this value stance mean that it is inherently "anti-ecological" and "anti-worker".
quoteZh: 西方现代化是以生产资料私有制为基础、以资本增殖为价值轴心的现代化，这种价值立场的局限性决定了其天然具有“反生态”“反工人”的本性。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official formula for China's path of development, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature
glossary.literal: harmonious symbiosis of humans and nature
glossary.explanation: One of the stated features of Chinese modernization in official discourse. It underpins the policy of building an ecological civilization.

A concept associated with Xi Jinping, notably in the phrase that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form a life community. It treats ecosystems as interdependent wholes.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance, stressing cooperation and shared interests.

glossary.literal: heaven and humans united as one
glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese philosophical idea that humans and the natural order form a single whole. Official discourse invokes it as a source for Chinese ecological thought.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013. A green version is promoted as embedding ecological standards.
An official Chinese policy concept for a form of development that integrates environmental protection with economic, political, cultural and social construction.

t: Creating the cultural form of Chinese modernization
zh: 创造中国式现代化的文化形态
paras: Yang Geng asks what cultural form Chinese modernization should take and how it is to be created. Writing in the Party-school newspaper Study Times (8 July 2024), Yang argues that the new culture produced by the Second Integration, joining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, is that cultural form. In this account the Second Integration makes Marxism Chinese and makes traditional culture modern, and the cultural form unites the spirit of the times with the spirit of the nation.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first sets out the theoretical basis and the guiding standard for combining Marxism with traditional culture. The second deals with absorbing new research results from Marxism outside China. The third addresses how this cultural form should embody the common values of all humanity. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on passages from Marx.

Yang's central reasoning is that the combination is possible because the two traditions share points of convergence, which Xi Jinping calls a high degree of mutual compatibility. Yang adds that traditional ethics concern human relations, which are social relations, and that the further the feudal order recedes, the weaker the ideological character of traditional culture becomes. Because tradition has a dual character, the combination also requires separating its essence from its dross. What to inherit and what to transform, Yang says, depends on the practice of Chinese modernization, not on Marxism or tradition alone. On foreign Marxism, Yang holds that Western Marxist cultural critique, covering cultural hegemony, the culture industry and postcolonial theory, helps in understanding capitalist modernity and its culture. Yang says it should be studied critically, neither rejected wholesale nor copied, and then localised.

Yang concludes that the new cultural form must reflect China's core values and the essential features of socialism, and also the common values of humanity: peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Yang presents this as consistent with building a community with a shared future for mankind and as a way to create a new form of human civilization. The author calls for a new cultural mission in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists connect the Second Integration, foreign Marxism and universal values in discussing Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture is not founded on an abstract "must"; the possibility of such a combination genuinely exists.
quoteZh: 把马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合不是建立在抽象的“必须”上，而是确实存在着这种结合的可能性

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist and distinct from Western capitalist modernization.
Xi Jinping's formulation of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. It complements the First Integration, which combines Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official term for those elements of traditional Chinese culture deemed worth inheriting, as distinct from elements regarded as outdated or dross.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy and civilizational concept, put forward from 2012–13, which calls for shared global governance and common interests among countries.
Xi Jinping's formulation (peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom), presented as an alternative to the notion of Western 'universal values'.

t: The value implications of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 中华民族现代文明的价值意蕴
paras: This newspaper commentary asks what is at stake in building a "modern civilization of the Chinese nation", a task the author links to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Chinese modernization and the creation of a "new form of human civilization". He Zhonghua argues that this is an ongoing, open-ended process with deep historical roots, and that its value lies in showing that a civilization grounded in national particularity can modernise without copying the West.

The article is organised in three parts. The first presents the Chinese nation's modern civilization as opening new possibilities for a new form of human civilization. The second treats it as the objective marker of national rejuvenation. The third holds that Chinese modernization is the only path by which it can be built. He draws throughout on Marx, Engels and Hegel, and on classical Chinese sources.

In the first part, He recounts, through Marx and Engels, the achievements and costs of capitalist civilization, namely ecological crisis and conflict among people. He contends that shifting from industrial to ecological civilization is needed for a new form of civilization, and that the Chinese case offers a route that is not the Western one. In the second part, he argues that the West modernised by returning to its classical heritage, so that China's modernization is likewise a renewal of its own tradition. Drawing on Marx's remarks on the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, he concludes that, in a world-historical setting, the decisive criterion of rejuvenation is the successful construction of this civilization. In the third part, He diagnoses the "dialectic of enlightenment" in the West, where reason produces both the discovery and the loss of the human being. He sets against it Chinese ideas such as "Dao follows nature" and an introspective way of understanding the person, which he says guard against reification. Chinese modernization is also socialist, owing to the adapting of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

He concludes that Chinese modernization can largely avoid the "terrible vicissitudes" of Western capitalist modernization. It must still draw critically on all human achievements, including science and technology, while keeping tension between history and morality, reason and value, and lawfulness and purposiveness. Read the original if you want a short example of how a Chinese philosopher uses classical Marxist texts and Chinese tradition to justify the idea of a distinctive Chinese modern civilization.
quoteEn: Only by taking a world-historical perspective can one see clearly the historical meaning and substance behind China's revolution, construction and reform.
quoteZh: 唯有着眼于世界历史视野，才有可能看清中国革命、建设、改革背后的历史含义及其实质

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept in official discourse, prominent after Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on cultural work, for a civilization that joins Chinese tradition with modern, socialist content. It is presented as the cultural counterpart of Chinese modernization.
An official phrase, used in Party documents since 2021, for the claim that Chinese modernization offers a model of civilization different from the Western capitalist one.
The official name for China's path of development, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as socialist and as combining universal features with Chinese conditions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse since Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream formulation. It refers to restoring China's historical standing and strength after the 'century of humiliation'.

t: Strengthening the reach and influence of Chinese civilization
zh: 增强中华文明传播力影响力
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts, takes up the requirement in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to strengthen the reach and influence of Chinese civilization, together with Xi Jinping's October 2023 instruction on propaganda, ideological and cultural work. Liu Xiaoxin argues that this task is central to cultural confidence, to China's international discourse power and to building a community with a shared future for mankind. Telling China's story well, in Liu's account, is the way to achieve it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the task matters. The second says what stories should be told: those of traditional culture, of Chinese modernization and of the Communist Party. The third turns to practical capacity-building in international communication, covering the discourse system, communication platforms, think tanks and professional education.

Liu argues that stronger international communication supports cultural confidence, gives China a voice commensurate with its overall national strength, and promotes dialogue among civilizations. Liu presents the community with a shared future for mankind as respecting civilizational diversity rather than imposing one civilization on others. On content, Liu says traditional culture should show China as a peace-loving, responsible power. Chinese modernization is described as a new form of human civilization that differs from the Western model and widens the options open to developing countries. Liu also wants the Party's history and character explained abroad in order to correct what the article calls overseas prejudice.

On capacity, Liu calls for a strategic communication system with distinctive Chinese features. It would include leading new-type mainstream media, differentiated messaging for regional and specific audiences, and a role for overseas Chinese, Chinese enterprises and foreign friends. Liu also calls for 5G-enabled platforms and short-video and mobile formats, as well as regionally distributed think tanks and a dedicated academic discipline for international communication. Liu stresses speaking to audiences on equal and candid terms and finding common ground with them. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party-line writing links cultural confidence, discourse power and media strategy in China's international communication agenda.
quoteEn: Strengthening the reach and influence of Chinese civilization means telling China's story well, and also conveying the ideas and spirit behind it, so as to create a favourable external climate of opinion for China's reform, development and stability.
quoteZh: 增强中华文明传播力影响力，就是把中国故事讲好，同时把中国故事背后蕴含的思想和精神讲出来，为我国改革发展稳定营造有利外部舆论环境。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, led by the Communist Party and presented as distinct from Western models. It has been elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and civilizational concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012. It calls for shared responsibility and mutual respect among states with differing systems.
An official term for confidence in China's cultural traditions, revolutionary culture and socialist culture. It is closely tied to the Four-sphere Confidence promoted under Xi Jinping.
A slogan from Xi Jinping's guidance on external propaganda. It calls for presenting China's experience, values and image to international audiences in persuasive, accessible ways.
The capacity of a country to shape international agendas, concepts and narratives. Chinese official writing treats it as something that should match a country's overall national strength.

t: The "Fengqiao experience": Mao Zedong's governance philosophy and wisdom and its contemporary development
zh: “枫桥经验”：毛泽东治国理政的理念与智慧及其当代发展
paras: Zhou Zhongzhi asks what the "Fengqiao experience" reveals about Mao Zedong's approach to governing China, and why it still matters. Zhou argues that Mao's endorsement of this grassroots model (resolving conflicts locally and not passing them upward) expressed a coherent governance outlook. In Zhou's account, that outlook remains productive in the twenty-first century and has theoretical and practical value for Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first places the Fengqiao experience in Mao's writings of 1956–57, "On the Ten Major Relationships" and "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People", and recounts how Mao praised the 1963 practice in Fengqiao, Zhuji, Zhejiang, and ordered it promoted nationally. The second reads the experience against traditional Chinese culture, in particular the joint rule of virtue and law and the people-as-foundation idea. The third follows it from Mao to Xi Jinping and sets out its current form.

Zhou's central claim is that Mao's governance joined a "big picture" of top-level design with a "centre of gravity downward" in grassroots work. Three supports are named: dialectical analysis in which contradictions of different kinds can be transformed, so that negative factors become positive ones; the mass line, "from the masses, to the masses"; and continuity with the Chinese tradition. Zhou reads the village rules and mediation work in Fengqiao as modern forms of virtue-and-law governance, and the grassroots emphasis as an update of the people-as-foundation idea. For the present, Zhou cites the Party's 19th Central Committee Fourth Plenum and the 20th Party Congress (2022), and says the experience now rests on combining self-governance, rule of law and rule by virtue, and on uniting human effort with technology.

Zhou concludes that, given external pressure and domestic risks, the Fengqiao experience is more urgent than before as a way to resolve risks at source and strengthen the base of state governance. Digital tools bring efficiency and fine-grained management, but Zhou warns that they cannot replace face-to-face work with the masses, because online-only contact breeds bureaucratism and formalism. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese account of how Party scholarship links Mao-era grassroots governance to Xi Jinping-era social governance and to claims about traditional culture.
quoteEn: To uphold and develop the "Fengqiao experience" well is to uphold and carry out the Party's mass line well.
quoteZh: 把“枫桥经验”坚持好、发展好，就是要把党的群众路线坚持好、贯彻好。

glossary.explanation: A model of grassroots conflict resolution that began in Fengqiao, Zhuji, Zhejiang, in 1963. Its slogan is to resolve contradictions locally and not pass them to higher levels, relying on the masses. It was endorsed by Mao and later promoted by Xi Jinping.

The Party's working method of drawing ideas from the people, turning them into policy and returning to the people to carry it out and test it. It is described in Party theory as the Party's basic work line.
Mao's 1957 category for non-antagonistic conflicts within society, set against antagonistic conflicts between the people and their enemies. He held that they should be resolved by democratic methods.
The official term for the Party's path of national development, under Xi Jinping, as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: joint rule of virtue and law
glossary.explanation: The idea, drawn from traditional Chinese political thought, that moral education and legal norms should work together in governing society.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization requires continually consolidating cultural subjectivity
zh: 推进中国式现代化要不断巩固文化主体性
paras: Tong Ping and Lei Bingjie take up the claim that "the Integrations have consolidated cultural subjectivity", which they present as a major thesis about the deep roots needed to build a modern Chinese civilisation. Their answer is that Chinese modernization depends on continually strengthening cultural subjectivity, which they treat as the source of cultural confidence and a basis for building ideological and cultural strength. This is a Party-school commentary for a Party journal.

The article has three parts. The first argues that consolidating cultural subjectivity is a requirement of the new journey. The second sets out the scientific meaning of the concept, using its foundation, core and underlying tone. The third lists the fundamental requirements for consolidating it. These are Party leadership and the guiding role of Marxism, the core socialist values, deeper reform of the cultural system, and a philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics.

The authors argue that cultural subjectivity deepens the cultural base of Chinese modernization and builds a socialist ideology with strong cohesion. In their account it also protects cultural security, since they hold that losing cultural autonomy and confidence is the greatest cultural-security problem. They define its foundation as conscious awareness of and deep identification with one's own culture. Its core is the autonomous capacity to carry forward, develop and transform that culture, which they say is neither closed nor arrogant. Its underlying tone is ideological: they hold that every cultural system's character is set by its ideological attributes. They state that claims of value neutrality carry political purposes, and they warn that neglecting this leads to the loss of cultural leadership and discourse power under Western discursive hegemony. A culture that disarms itself, they say, would become a dependent "follower".

The authors conclude that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Two Integrations and the Party's cultural leadership must guide the cultural work of the new era. They add that the core socialist values should draw on the creativity of the people, and that cultural reform should put social benefits first. Philosophy and social science should build Chinese discourse and contribute Chinese wisdom on shared human problems. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school writers present cultural subjectivity, ideology and cultural security as parts of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The underlying tone of cultural subjectivity is its ideological attribute, and ideology has a distinct political standpoint and value orientation.
quoteZh: 文化主体性的底色是意识形态属性，而意识形态具有鲜明的政治立场和价值指向。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's path of modernization. It is presented as distinct from Western models, and it stresses common prosperity and the coordination of material and spiritual civilisation.
A concept Xi Jinping stressed in 2023. It refers to a nation's clear awareness of its own culture and its capacity to keep and develop that culture while engaging with others.

The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping said in 2023 that the second integration consolidated cultural subjectivity.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It is written into the Party and state constitutions.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They are set at national, social and individual levels.
Confidence in China's own culture. Since the 18th Party Congress it has been added to confidence in the path, theory and system.

t: In Chinese modernization, people's livelihood comes first
zh: 中国式现代化民生为大
paras: Taking as its starting point Xi Jinping's remark during an April 2024 inspection in Chongqing that "in Chinese modernization, people's livelihood comes first", this commentary asks why livelihood (minsheng) is central to Chinese modernization and what that requires in practice. Zhang Yuanxin argues that the principle fixes the value orientation and goal of Chinese modernization and marks it off from Western modernization. The article presents this as having both theoretical and practical significance for pursuing Chinese modernization through high-quality development.

The article has three parts. The first explains why Chinese modernization must put livelihood first, drawing on the nature of the Party and of the socialist system. The second sets out the livelihood content of the goal, stated at the 20th Party Congress (2022), of building a modern socialist country by the middle of the century. The third turns to practical requirements for the new era.

In the first part, Zhang reasons that the Party's founding purpose, original aspiration, ideals and mass line all commit a modernization it leads to serve the people. Socialism with Chinese characteristics, through its guiding ideology, political leadership, basic institutions, emphasis on developing the productive forces and commitment to fairness, is said to supply the guarantees for improving livelihood. Zhang contrasts this with Western modernization, which the author describes as capital-centred and as producing wide wealth gaps and polarisation. In the second part, five goals are tied to livelihood: common prosperity, the people being masters of the country, coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress, social harmony and stability, and harmony between humanity and nature. The third part recommends meeting people's aspirations for a better life, addressing urgent concerns in education, employment, income distribution, social security and health, and holding the bottom line while prioritising key groups and regions.
