paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in December 2023, asks what contribution China can make to humanity, recalling Mao Zedong's remark that China should make a larger contribution. Wang Xingsheng argues that Chinese modernization answers this by creating a new form of human civilization, which the author describes as a light the Chinese nation offers to the world.

The piece has three parts. The first places modernization within the long history of human civilization and the Western origins of the modernizing process, then sets out how China came to its own path. The second, the longest, examines four sets of relations: between people, between people and things, between people and nature, and between China and other countries. The third turns to the global and historical significance of the path.

Wang's central claim is that the novelty of this civilization lies in overcoming the congenital defects that Western modernization inherited from the capitalist mode of production. In the author's account, capitalism produces polarisation, inverts the relation between people and things through commodity fetishism, damages the environment and rests on colonial plunder. Chinese modernization is presented as the opposite on each count: it pursues common prosperity, unites material abundance with human development, places ecological civilization within the overall plan, and follows peaceful development and a community with a shared future for mankind. The author cites the elimination of absolute poverty since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the Occupy Wall Street movement as contrasting evidence.

Wang concludes that the path's significance is world-historical. It is said to confirm the scientific truth of Marxism and to advance scientific socialism in the twenty-first century, to make the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation irreversible, and to break the myth that modernization equals Westernization, offering developing countries another option. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary presents Chinese modernization as a new form of civilization in contrast with Western capitalist modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization", offering developing countries a new choice and a new way of thinking about reaching modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，为广大发展中国家走向现代化提供了新的选择、新的思路。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from the Western model.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation used in Party discourse for the civilization that Chinese modernization is said to create, set against Western capitalist modernity.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, described in Party documents as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept put forward by Xi Jinping since 2012, calling for joint development, peace and cooperation among countries.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal of restoring China to a leading position, linked to the Chinese Dream.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: From "mutual fit" to "mutual fulfilment": the Second Integration of Marxism and traditional Chinese culture
zh: 由“彼此契合”到“互相成就”
paras: Why should the basic tenets of Marxism be combined with China's fine traditional culture, and how can this "Second Integration" be achieved? Shang Zhixiao takes up these questions in a study framed by Xi Jinping's remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development (2 June). The article argues that Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture are highly compatible. In Shang's account, that compatibility leads through organic combination to "mutual fulfilment", and the result is a cultural form of Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the compatibility of the two, historically and in terms of ideas. The second explains how each "fulfils" the other. The third clarifies what "integration" means and what it should produce. The historical section moves from Marx's writings on China during the Second Opium War, through the October Revolution and the May Fourth Movement, to the founding of the Communist Party in 1921.

Shang's core argument rests on three moves. First, the author finds parallels in content: communist ideals and the ancient ideal of "a world of great harmony"; the people-centred outlook of historical materialism and the tradition of "the people as the foundation of the state"; and revolutionary spirit and the ethos of constant self-renewal. Second, mutual fulfilment runs both ways. Marxism gives traditional culture a scientific worldview and method, enabling its "creative transformation and innovative development", while traditional culture gives Marxism Chinese style and cultural vitality. Third, integration is described as a "chemical reaction", not a physical mixture or a "platter". It does not merge the two into one: it aims to make Marxism Chinese and traditional culture modern.

Shang concludes that the new cultural life-form created this way is the cultural form of Chinese modernization. It draws on traditional culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, and on the achievements of other civilizations. In the author's view, it deepens the historical roots of socialism with Chinese characteristics and shows a higher level of the Party's historical and cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how the Second Integration is justified and what theoretical outcome it is meant to produce.
quoteEn: "Integration" is not a "platter" and not a simple "physical reaction", but a profound "chemical reaction".
quoteZh: “结合”不是“拼盘”，不是简单的“物理反应”，而是深刻的“化学反应”。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation, part of the Two Integrations, of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It was emphasised from 2021–2023 as a complement to combining Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for handling traditional culture. It means reworking inherited cultural elements so that they fit contemporary society.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since reform and opening up. It describes socialism adapted to Chinese conditions.

t: Grasping the meaning of high-quality economic development
zh: 深刻把握经济高质量发展的内涵要义
paras: Lin Jiang's commentary, first published in Economic Daily in September 2023, sets out what high-quality development means and why it is the first task of building a modern socialist country in all respects. The author argues that the judgement that China's economy has shifted from a stage of rapid growth to one of high-quality development rests on Xi Jinping's economic thinking and reflects the Party's deepening grasp of economic laws.

The piece begins by tracing Xi Jinping's statements on the topic from the 19th Party Congress (2017) to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It then reads high-quality development from five angles: the new development stage, the new development philosophy, the change in the principal contradiction in society, the laws of economic development, and the strategic timetable to the middle of the century. A second section links the judgement to basic Marxist principles, and a third names the new development pattern as the key to carrying it out.

Lin distinguishes economic growth, a quantitative increase, from economic development, the unity of quantity and quality. Quality for the author means structure and efficiency, and quantity means scale and speed. In Lin's account, extensive, factor-input growth has reached its limits: resource constraints, a shrinking working-age population and weaker comparative advantages call for innovation-driven growth. Drawing on empirical research, the author describes a move from "structural acceleration" to "structural deceleration" and the "new normal". The author also maintains that the judgement embodies the dialectical relation of matter and consciousness, the law of quantitative into qualitative change, universal connection and the doctrine of contradiction. The new development pattern, with domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other, is presented as the strategic base. Lin presents it as a response to weakened traditional international circulation and as an open, not closed, pattern.

Lin calls for balancing expanded domestic demand with supply-side structural reform, speeding up technological self-reliance, closing gaps in industrial and supply chains, building a modern industrial system, promoting rural revitalisation and regional coordination, and deepening opening up. The aim is to provide a solid material and technological base for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Party economists justify the shift to high-quality development in Marxist and policy terms.
quoteEn: Economic development is a spiralling process of ascent, and the ascent is not linear; once quantitative accumulation reaches a certain stage, it must turn to qualitative improvement, and China's economic development must follow this law too.
quoteZh: 经济发展是一个螺旋式上升的过程，上升不是线性的，量积累到一定阶段，必须转向质的提升，我国经济发展也要遵循这一规律。

glossary.explanation: Official slogan, adopted at the 19th Party Congress in 2017, for a shift from speed and scale of growth to quality, efficiency and structure. It is now the stated main theme of China's economic work.
Five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 as guidance for development.
Strategy announced in 2020 that treats domestic circulation as the mainstay while domestic and international circulations reinforce each other.
A Marxist-Maoist concept. The 19th Party Congress redefined it as the contradiction between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
Term used by Xi Jinping from 2014 for the shift to medium-high growth, structural optimisation and innovation-driven growth.
The Party's official designation of China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on the economy, presented officially as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: Stimulating the spiritual strength to advance Chinese modernization
zh: 激发推进中国式现代化的精神力量
paras: This short commentary, originally published in the People's Daily on 26 September 2023, asks how the Party's moral and ideological resources can drive Chinese modernization. Hao Wenbin argues that the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists, whose source is the great founding spirit of the Party, supplies lasting strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Party members and officials should therefore carry it forward in order to innovate and make new breakthroughs.

Taking up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), the piece is organised around four qualities drawn from that lineage: firm ideals and convictions, a sincere commitment to the people, a fighting spirit, and the character of self-reform. Each section opens with a statement by Xi Jinping and ends with practical demands on cadres.

On ideals, Hao holds that conviction has carried the Party through hardship and must rest on the scientific truth of Marxism. This requires study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On the people, Hao lists spirits such as the Yan'an spirit, the Lei Feng spirit and the spirit of the fight against poverty and the pandemic as expressions of devotion to the people. Hao links this to common prosperity, investigation and research, and the Party's mass line. On struggle and self-reform, Hao calls for vigilance against "black swan" and "grey rhino" events, and for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, with the Party's self-reform keeping it from losing its character.

Hao concludes that drawing on this spiritual lineage will sustain officials' drive and diligence on the new journey. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary presents the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists as a resource for modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a great and arduous undertaking; only by actively taking responsibility and daring and knowing how to struggle can this historic cause be advanced to victory.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是一项伟大而艰巨的事业，唯有积极担当作为，敢于善于斗争，才能胜利推进这一历史伟业。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, elaborated by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as involving a huge population, common prosperity and material and cultural-ethical advancement.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.en: the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists
glossary.explanation: An official term for the series of named 'spirits' formed in the Party's history, such as the Yan'an spirit and the Lei Feng spirit. It is said to begin with the great founding spirit of the Party.
An official goal of socialism in China, meaning prosperity shared by all the people. It has been stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, supervision and internal Party life.
A term used in Xi Jinping-era discourse for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purify itself. It is presented as its most distinctive quality.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of ordinary people and serving them. It is restated here as the mass line for the new era.

t: Advancing cultural self-reliance, confidence and strength under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture
zh: 在习近平文化思想指引下推进文化自立自信自强
paras: This commentary by Wang Menghui, Party secretary of Hubei Province, was published in the People's Daily in January 2024. It asks how Party members and officials should understand and apply Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. Wang's answer is that the thought rests on three linked commitments: cultural self-reliance, cultural confidence and cultural strength. Wang presents it as the theoretical summary of the Party's cultural work in the new era and as a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece has an opening statement of the cultural mission, followed by three sections, one for each commitment, and a short regional close. It draws on the history from the Opium War onwards, on Mao Zedong's New Democracy writings, and on Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It ends by applying the framework to Hubei and the Jingchu cultural heritage.

On self-reliance, Wang argues that national independence includes spiritual independence, and that this requires a firm cultural subjectivity. In Wang's account this means arming the Party and people with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, following the path of socialist cultural development, and upholding the Party's leadership over ideology and the media. On confidence, Wang treats cultural confidence as the most fundamental of the Four-sphere Confidence and as an original contribution to Marxist cultural theory. It calls for telling China's story well, building Chinese-style philosophy and social science, and strengthening international communication. On strength, Wang links national rejuvenation to cultural flourishing and names the Two Integrations as the key to Chinese modernization.

Wang concludes that cultural strength is needed for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. He proposes promoting core socialist values and the spirit of Party members, encouraging virtues such as diligence and dedication, and building "complete communities" through Party-led grassroots governance. For Hubei, Wang calls for creative transformation of Jingchu culture and for building a province strong in culture. Read the original if you want a compact, official provincial-level statement of how Xi Jinping Thought on Culture is organised and put into practice.
quoteEn: Upholding cultural self-reliance requires constantly consolidating cultural subjectivity.
quoteZh: 坚持文化自立必须不断巩固文化主体性。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on culture and ideology formally put forward in October 2023. Official texts present it as the cultural part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Culture was added as the fourth item under Xi Jinping.
The official term for China's path of development, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as Party-led, socialist, and based on China's national conditions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse under Xi Jinping. It refers to restoring China to national strength and prestige by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Handling well the relationship between upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
zh: 处理好守正与创新的关系
paras: This commentary in Red Flag Manuscripts takes up how Chinese modernization, which it calls a pioneering undertaking without precedent, should balance "upholding fundamental principles" (shouzheng) with innovation (chuangxin). Yue argues that the two are dialectically unified and complementary. The author presents this as a key method of thought for the Party's governance in the new era.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping on the dialectic of continuity and change. It then traces the approach to Chinese cultural tradition and to the Party's commitment to emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts. Two main sections follow, one on upholding principles and one on innovation.

On the first, Yue says that Chinese modernization must keep its "root and soul": leadership by the Communist Party of China, socialism, and the Party's basic theory, line and strategy. The author contends that its eventual success will show capitalism is not the only route to modernization. On the second, Yue says that Chinese modernization is exploratory and faces unknown territory, so innovation must be placed at the centre of national development. The author calls for implementing the new development philosophy, pursuing high-quality development, liberating thinking, innovating in theory, and reforming institutions and mechanisms. Leading cadres should change outdated ideas and become leaders of innovation.

Yue concludes that principle without innovation leads to rigidity, and innovation without principle leads to loss of direction. Both are needed to steer Chinese modernization through a period of great global change. Read the original if you want a short, authoritative example of how Party-aligned writing frames continuity and innovation in Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles does not mean clinging to convention and never changing, and innovation is not a tree without roots or a river without a source.
quoteZh: 守正不是墨守成规、一成不变，创新不是无本之木、无源之水。

glossary.literal: keeping to the correct path and innovating
glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse that pairs fidelity to core political principles with innovation in theory and practice. In the article it is the basis of a method of governance.

The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as having both features common to all countries and specifically Chinese ones.
The official framework, set out in 2015, that stresses innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
The official goal of the current stage of the economy. It emphasises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth alone.

t: A theoretical reading of "the people's need for a better life"
zh: “人民美好生活需要”的学理性解读
paras: Han Xiping and Du Du take up the concept of "the people's need for a better life", introduced at the 19th Party Congress (2017) when the principal contradiction in Chinese society was redefined. They argue that the concept must be read historically and dialectically: it is a stage-specific need, rooted in material conditions, that expands as society develops. Grasping it correctly, in the authors' view, is necessary for tackling unbalanced and inadequate development.

The article has four parts. It first traces the concept's evolution, then sets out its specific content, then gives its theoretical and practical grounds, and finally identifies the basic guarantees for meeting it. It draws on Marx and Engels (the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The German Ideology, Capital, the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy), Engels's Dialectics of Nature, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

The authors treat human needs and the productive forces as mutually driving each other. On this basis they trace a historical line in China from the need for independence, to subsistence, to prosperity, and now to a "better" life. They divide the concept's content into material needs, which are primary and must be richer, fairer and kept reasonable so as to avoid consumerism, and spiritual or social needs, which Marx treats as essentially human. They ground the concept in the Marxist value aim of free and all-round human development, in the essence of socialism as Deng and Xi state it (ending polarisation and achieving common prosperity), and in the Party's founding mission. Finally they argue that satisfying it requires mature, rational and green material production, and a sound ecological environment drawing on Xi's "two mountains" thesis.

The authors conclude that the need for a better life is neither rigid nor quantitative but a changing, open and historical category. Meeting it requires the unity of the historical stage and the long term, of the material and the spiritual, and of production and ecology. They add that it cannot be achieved at one stroke but through continued development that resolves the principal contradiction. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the 19th Congress formulation is linked to Marx's theory of needs and to Xi Jinping's statements on ecology and common prosperity.
quoteEn: From seeking independence to seeking subsistence, and from seeking prosperity to seeking a better life, is the logical main thread in the development of the Chinese people's needs over the past 200 years.
quoteZh: 由求独立到求温饱，由到求富裕到求美好，是近200年以来中国人民的需要问题发展演变的逻辑主线。

glossary.explanation: In Party theory, the most prominent contradiction in society at a given stage, which shapes policy priorities. The 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined it as the contradiction between unbalanced and inadequate development and the people's ever-growing needs for a better life.

glossary.en: the people's need for a better life
glossary.explanation: A formulation introduced by Xi Jinping at the 19th Party Congress (2017). It replaced the earlier reference to "material and cultural needs" and covers areas such as democracy, rule of law, fairness, security and the environment.

A goal of socialism in Party discourse, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by a few. Deng Xiaoping included it in his definition of the essence of socialism, and Xi Jinping has given it new emphasis.
Xi Jinping's saying that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets". It holds that ecological protection and economic development should reinforce each other.

t: Upholding institutions as the guarantee for developing whole-process people's democracy
zh: 坚持以制度为保障发展全过程人民民主
paras: Bao Xinjian takes up the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls whole-process people's democracy the essential attribute of socialist democracy and an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. The article asks how this democracy is secured in practice. Bao's answer is that institutions are the guarantee: a complete 'chain' of democratic institutions is what makes it, in the official formula, the most broadly based, genuine and effective form of democracy.

The commentary is built in three parts, drawing heavily on Xi Jinping's speeches and Party Congress reports. The first part reviews the institutional system: the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation and political consultation under Party leadership, and grassroots self-governance. The second part concerns the 'true meaning' of democracy and its link to state governance. The third part treats popular support, equality and inclusiveness.

Bao's core argument has two moves. First, whole-process people's democracy is a 'full-chain' institutionalised democracy. The fundamental, basic and important political institutions cover political and social life, and each has a specific function: the people's congresses for elections, legislation and oversight, consultative channels for building consensus, and grassroots autonomy for direct democracy. Second, Bao contends that this democracy joins democratic institutions to state governance, a problem the author says Western democratic models have never solved because procedure and efficiency seem to conflict. In Bao's account, Western democracies drift from the people's needs and become tools of politicians, whereas the Communist Party's 'people-centred' stance turns institutional strengths into governance capacity. Bao ties this to the principle that matters of common concern are discussed by everyone concerned, with consultation scaled to national, local, group and grassroots issues.

Bao concludes that Chinese modernization requires the democratic institutions to be strengthened further and made more institutionalised, standardised and procedural. Broad, multilevel, institutionalised consultation is said to reach the largest common denominator of public opinion, to balance unity and diversity, and to consolidate the patriotic united front. Bao presents this as a creative development of the Marxist view of democracy, with continuing political value. Read the original if you want a representative, source-heavy statement of the official 2023 case for whole-process people's democracy as an institutional and governance system.
quoteEn: The fundamental reason our democracy is whole-process people's democracy is that it is a full-chain, institutionalised democracy.
quoteZh: 我国民主之所以是一种全过程人民民主，根本依据就在于，这是一种全链条式的制度化民主

glossary.explanation: A concept presented by Xi Jinping in 2019 and promoted in official discourse as the defining feature of Chinese socialist democracy. It stresses popular participation in every stage of the political process, not only in elections.
The official name for China's development path, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.

China's fundamental political institution, a hierarchy of congresses from local level to the National People's Congress. Officially it is the organ through which state power is exercised by the people.
The Party-led alliance of non-Party groups, parties, ethnic and religious groups and overseas Chinese. Official discourse describes it as a means of building broad support.

The system of self-management through urban and rural community bodies such as villagers' and residents' committees. Officially it is described as the main form of direct democracy, under Party leadership.

t: Progress and practical testing in adapting Marxist ownership theory to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 马克思主义所有制理论中国化时代化的进展和实践检验
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxist Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2023 no. 2
paras: Hong Yinxing takes up how Marx's theory of ownership, which Hong calls the core of Marxist economics, has been adapted to China's reform practice. The article argues that reform and opening up used ownership as its breakthrough point and produced a framework of ownership theory for the twenty-first century. Hong holds that this framework is faithful to Marx's method rather than a departure from it, and that practice has confirmed it.

The article is organised in five parts. It covers the ownership structure of the primary stage of socialism, the capital attributes of state-owned assets, mixed ownership, property-rights institutions, and household property rights and factor incomes. Hong draws on Capital, the Communist Manifesto and the preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, and on Party documents from 1993 to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Hong also briefly contrasts Western property-rights theory and cites Piketty on inequality.

Hong's first move is that the form of ownership depends on the level of the productive forces, so private ownership cannot be abolished until the non-public sector has exhausted its capacity. This is said to justify public ownership as the mainstay alongside other forms, and the shift from the Two Unwaverings to the 'two inviolables' of public and non-public property rights. The second move is that state capital, though lacking the capital-labour relation, shares capital's other traits: profit-seeking, motion and accumulation. On this basis Hong defends the exit of state capital from uncompetitive sectors, mixed ownership through joint-stock firms, and the shift from managing assets to managing capital. The third move extends ownership from means of production to all factors, including data, so that distribution by factor contribution is explained as the economic realisation of factor ownership. Hong proposes narrowing income gaps by increasing the non-labour factors workers hold, not by denying factor incomes.

Hong sums up the path as moving from abolishing private ownership to using it under public-sector dominance, from denying to affirming state assets' capital attributes, from ownership to property-rights systems, and from means of production to factor ownership with household property income. In Hong's view, this twenty-first-century ownership theory keeps pace with the times and has raised overall efficiency across forms of ownership. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese economist's account of how state-capital reform, mixed ownership and factor distribution are justified in Marxist terms.
quoteEn: Property-rights theory is an extension of ownership theory.
quoteZh: 产权理论是所有制理论的拓展。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula: unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector, and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official characterisation of China's current historical stage, in which less-developed productive forces justify a mix of ownership forms.
The policy course launched in 1978 that introduced market mechanisms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

Enterprises in which state, collective and private capital hold shares together. The Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) named it an important realisation form of the basic economic system.

t: The human-centred meaning of China's cultural modernization and paths to building it
zh: 我国文化现代化的人学意蕴及其建设路径
paras: Most scholars study cultural modernization by looking at how the economy and politics shape culture. Zhang Zhonghua and Feng Yanli accept this but argue that culture is a product of human practice, so its modernization is at core the modernization of people. The article contends that advancing China's cultural modernization in the new era therefore requires an anthropological (renxue) perspective, one centred on the human subject.

The article has four parts. It first defines cultural modernization as part of modernization as a whole, using a three-layer model of culture (material, institutional, spiritual) and three features of modernization (transformative, developmental, comprehensive). It then argues that the modernization of people is the core of cultural modernization, and explains why China's version is marked by the primacy of the people. Finally it sets out three practical requirements: adequate understanding, effective measures and joint effort.

The central move is that people's modernization, meaning knowledge, skills, social relations, psychology, values and ways of thinking, is both what produces culture and what culture shapes. The authors hold that imported educational models or cultural management methods will remain nominal if the public's mindset does not match them. They cite Alex Inkeles on psychological barriers to development. In the authors' account, Western cultural modernization is capital-centred and polarised, leaving workers with vulgar commodities and spiritual poverty. China's, they say, rests on four features: leadership by the Communist Party, a socialist character, service to the people and to socialism, and social benefits ranked above economic ones.

In practice, the authors call for stronger awareness that cultural modernization advances people's modernization, self-liberation and civilisation. They urge adherence to the socialist path of cultural development with Chinese characteristics, coordinated material and spiritual progress, and skills support for disadvantaged groups. They also assign roles to government (policy and ideological security), society (cultural organisations and enterprises) and individuals (modern consciousness and practical ability). Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Party-affiliated scholars link cultural modernization to a theory of the human subject and to the idea of the primacy of the people.
quoteEn: Culture is a product of human practice, and the core of cultural modernization is the modernization of people; advancing cultural modernization ultimately depends on people's active participation.
quoteZh: 文化是人类实践活动的产物，文化现代化的核心是人的现代化，推进文化现代化，归根到底要通过人的积极参与才能实现。

glossary.explanation: The transformation of the cultural sphere from traditional to modern forms, treated in Party discourse as one component of socialist modernization alongside the economic, political, social and ecological ones.

The idea that modernization depends on people acquiring modern skills, values and ways of thinking. The article draws on Alex Inkeles and on Xi Jinping's statement that the essence of modernization is the modernization of people.
A principle in Party discourse that the people's interests come first. The article treats it as the defining feature of China's cultural modernization.

t: Drawing wisdom for theoretical innovation from the creations of the people
zh: 从人民群众的创造中汲取理论创新智慧
paras: Ai Silin takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at a Politburo study session of the 20th Central Committee, to "pay attention to drawing wisdom for theoretical innovation from the creations of the people". The article reads this as an application of the Marxist theory of knowledge and the view of history centred on the masses, and as a summary of the Party's historical experience. Ai's thesis is that the people's creative practice is the inexhaustible source of Marxist theoretical innovation, so the Party must follow the mass line in developing theory.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical basis: the primacy of practice in Marxist epistemology and the people's role as the makers of history. The second reviews the Party's history, from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist construction and reform and opening up to the new era. The third turns to practical requirements for theoretical innovation.

In Ai's argument, practice is the basis and test of knowledge, and the masses are the main force transforming the world. The people's practice therefore decides which problems theory must address, supplies its content, and supplies a standard for judging results. Ai presents the results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times as the distilled experience and collective wisdom of the Party and the people. Examples include rural investigations behind Mao Zedong's strategy of encircling cities from the countryside, and household contract responsibility, township enterprises and ownership reform in the reform era. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is described as rooted in the people's practice.

Ai proposes that the mass line be followed in theoretical work through three measures. The first is large-scale investigation and research, in which officials act as the people's pupils and go down to grassroots level. The second is to condense investigation findings into new theory, so that investigation does not become a "broken bridge" to research. The third is a lasting mechanism: education in the mass viewpoint, better evaluation of research, open channels for suggestions and criticism, and theorists who write their papers "on the land of the motherland". Read the original if you want to see how a Red Flag Manuscripts article links Party theory-making to the mass line and to investigation and research as methods.
quoteEn: The practice of the people is the raw material of theoretical innovation, and our Party bears the responsibility of integrating, systematising, refining and elevating it.
quoteZh: 人民群众的实践是理论创新的原材料，我们党承担着将其整合起来、系统起来、完善起来、升华起来的责任。

glossary.explanation: A Party method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of ordinary people, turning them into policy and returning to the people to test it. It is presented as the Party's basic work style.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era. Its results are treated as successive theoretical innovations.
A Party working method, stressed by Mao Zedong and revived under Xi Jinping, in which officials gather first-hand information at the grassroots before making policy or theory.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978.

t: Firmly holding the bottom line of economic security
zh: 牢牢守住经济安全底线
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in December 2023, after the Central Economic Work Conference, Ding Jinqing asks how China can keep economic security secure while pursuing growth. The commentary argues that high-quality development and a high level of security must reinforce each other, and that economic security is the foundation of national security and part of the holistic approach to national security. Ding holds that this requires Party leadership across economic work and a firm grasp of four basic characteristics of economic security.

The piece is organised around those four characteristics: stability, strategic nature, dynamism and interconnectedness. Each section gives three or four practical requirements, supported by statements from Xi Jinping and the Central Economic Work Conference. The dynamism section covers four priority fields: food, energy, key technologies and finance.

On stability, Ding calls for seeking progress while keeping stability, handling reform, development and stability as an organic whole, and pursuing quality and quantity together without judging success by growth rates alone. On strategy, Ding stresses economic development as the central task, upholding and improving the basic socialist economic system, with the Two Unwaverings, and a people-centred approach. Ding says doubts about the basic economic system or about the role of private business should be clearly rebutted. On dynamism, Ding says food, energy, core technology and finance must each be secured, including through the 1.8 billion mu farmland red line, a new energy security strategy, self-reliance in science and technology, and comprehensive financial regulation to avoid systemic risk.

On interconnectedness, Ding argues that economic security is a whole-system matter, so risks must be stopped from chaining together or escalating, for instance from economic risk into social and political risk, or from international risk into domestic risk. Ding concludes that development and security should be planned together, with a new security pattern matching the new development pattern, so that development builds security and security protects development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official commentary frames economic security in the language of the Central Economic Work Conference and Xi Jinping's statements.
quoteEn: Coordinating development and security is a major principle of our Party in governing the country.
quoteZh: 统筹发展和安全，是我们党治国理政的一个重大原则。

glossary.explanation: A formula calling for unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A security concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats security as covering political, economic, military, cultural, technological and other fields together.
The official goal of the current stage of China's economy, stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.
An official strategy, put forward in 2020, centred on the domestic economic cycle with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The official term for China's system of public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the main form, and a socialist market economy.

t: The threefold significance of building the new development pattern
zh: 构建新发展格局的三重意蕴
paras: Why did the Party Central Committee decide to accelerate the building of a new development pattern? Chen Yanbin argues that the decision answers two pressures: insufficient domestic demand within the domestic cycle, and weakening momentum in the international cycle amid de-globalisation and uncertainty. The article sets out three aspects of the pattern's significance: it clears the domestic circulation and supports high-quality development; it promotes interaction between domestic and international circulations and builds new advantages in cooperation and competition; and it brings supply and demand into a higher-level dynamic balance while raising the efficiency of macroeconomic regulation.

The piece is an explanatory essay in the Party journal Qianxian, written after the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the 14th Five-Year Plan had both called for a pattern with the domestic cycle as the mainstay. It draws on World Bank and National Bureau of Statistics figures and on Xi Jinping's statements. Its three sections move from consumption and investment, to industrial chains and the super-large market, to macroeconomic policy.

On the domestic cycle, Chen notes that household consumption was only 38.4 per cent of GDP in 2022, well below the global average and the middle- and high-income averages. Chen also reports that capital formation contributed 50.1 per cent of GDP but drove only 1.5 percentage points of growth, and that private investment's share fell to 52.9 per cent in the first half of 2023. The proposed remedies are fairer income distribution, a sounder social security system, a larger middle-income group and more productive investment. On the international side, Chen argues that the old low-end embedding in global value chains is no longer sustainable. China's complete industrial system and its super-large market could instead raise supply-chain resilience, help overcome 'chokepoint' technologies, and create a new 'gravitational field' for global resources. On regulation, Chen holds that traditional demand-side stabilisation cannot cope with interacting short- and long-term, supply and demand problems. Chen advocates the 'three-in-one' framework, which unifies stabilisation, growth and structural policies.

Chen concludes that the new pattern is a systematic project and the strategic basis for high-quality development. For current conditions, the author calls for a growth target slightly above potential growth, moderately stronger monetary and fiscal policy, and combined use of structural and growth policies to remove bottlenecks. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official economic rationale for the new development pattern, together with the policy-framework proposals of a CASS macroeconomist.
quoteEn: The essential meaning of building the new development pattern is to clear the leading domestic circulation: by taking expanding domestic demand as the strategic basis, it breaks through the key bottlenecks restricting the national economic cycle and effectively resolves weak household consumption and imbalanced investment structure.
quoteZh: 构建新发展格局的题中之义是畅通起主导作用的国内大循环，通过以扩大内需为战略基点，打通制约国民经济循环的关键瓶颈，有效解决居民消费乏力和投资结构失衡的问题。

glossary.explanation: A strategy put forward by Xi Jinping in 2020 with the domestic cycle as the mainstay and domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It was written into the 14th Five-Year Plan.
The flow of production, distribution, exchange and consumption within China's economy. Official policy treats it as the main body of the new development pattern.
The official goal for China's economy since the late 2010s. It stresses quality, efficiency and balance rather than speed alone.
A macroeconomic framework that combines stabilisation, growth and structural policies. The article presents it as an alternative to purely demand-side countercyclical regulation.

t: Adhering to the general principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability
zh: 坚持稳中求进工作总基调
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 27 September 2023, presents the "general principle of making progress while maintaining stability" as a guiding principle of Party governance and a methodology for economic work. Han Baojiang argues that, with the economy recovering but facing new difficulties, officials should study, grasp and apply this methodology so as to meet the year's economic and social targets with high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the meaning of the principle, drawing on Chinese reform experience since reform and opening up and on a series of statements by Xi Jinping. It then discusses how to handle the dialectical unity of "stability" and "progress". Finally, it lists three areas for effort: high-quality development, deepening reform and opening up, and coordinating development with security.

Han's central claim is that stability and progress must be understood as a whole. Stability is the premise, meaning steady growth, employment and prices, no systemic financial risk, and consistent policy direction. Progress means restructuring the economy and deepening reform, and stability does not mean inaction. Two relationships follow. Reform, development and stability must be balanced, so that the pace of reform and development stays within what society can bear, under the Party's leadership. Groping for stones to cross the river must also be combined with top-level design, as reform enters what Han calls its deep-water stage. Han's recommended measures include the new development philosophy, a unified national market, the Two Unwaverings, institutional opening up and the Belt and Road Initiative. They also include a holistic approach to national security, which Han describes as ensuring that security and development advance together.

Han concludes that the Party should build on a secure foundation while working harder on "progress", aiming at an effective improvement in quality and a reasonable growth in quantity. The commentary also calls on leading cadres to master the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and use it to analyse economic questions. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how official commentary framed the "stability with progress" principle in economic policy in autumn 2023.
quoteEn: Seeking progress while maintaining stability does not mean doing nothing; it means achieving something within proper limits, doing just the right thing, keeping balance and seizing the right moment.
quoteZh: 稳中求进不是无所作为，而是要在把握好度的前提下有所作为，恰到好处，把握好平衡，把握好时机。

glossary.pinyin: wěn zhōng qiú jìn gōngzuò zǒng jīdiào
glossary.en: general principle of making progress while maintaining stability
glossary.literal: general keynote of seeking progress within stability
glossary.explanation: A guideline for economic and social work that the Party leadership has stressed since the early 2010s. It asks officials to put stability first while advancing reform and restructuring.

An official formulation, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over pure growth speed. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
A set of five concepts, namely innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015 as the guide to economic policy.
The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: From the "first integration" to the "Two Integrations": an important development and innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 从“一个结合”到“两个结合”：马克思主义中国化的重要发展和创新
source: Studies on the History of the Communist Party of China (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2024 no. 2
paras: Ren Guixiang asks how the "Two Integrations" put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 relate to the earlier Party principle of combining Marxism with China's concrete realities. The article argues that the Two Integrations inherit, enrich and develop that "first integration". It presents the addition of a "second integration", with China's fine traditional culture, as a further innovation and leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has four parts. It first traces the first integration from Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. It then examines how Xi enriched the first integration after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third part reviews the Party's earlier attitudes to traditional culture and the stages by which Xi proposed the Two Integrations. The last part sets out the significance of the second integration.

Ren argues that Xi's treatment of the first integration is macro-level and holistic, linking a century of Party history to five hundred years of world socialism. It is also dynamic and open to the times, and it extends to concrete cases such as the Zunyi Conference and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. The Two Integrations took shape gradually in Xi's speeches from 2014 to early 2021. They were formally proposed on 1 July 2021, written into the Party's third historical resolution (2021) and elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Ren holds that Mao and later leaders handled the relation to traditional culture correctly but never framed it as an explicit proposition. In this reading, the first integration is the premise of the second and the second is its development.

Ren draws four conclusions about the second integration. It is a new leap in adapting Marxism and creates a "new cultural life form". It is a further ideological emancipation, comparable to the New Culture Movement and the 1978 truth-criterion debate. It widens the cultural foundations of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It supplies the cultural soft power for Chinese modernization, national rejuvenation and building a strong cultural nation. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history account of how the Two Integrations were developed and justified, with extensive citation of Xi's speeches.
quoteEn: The "first integration" is the premise and foundation of the "second integration", and the "second integration" is the development and outcome of the "first integration".
quoteZh: “第一个结合”是“第二个结合”的前提和基础，“第二个结合”是“第一个结合”的发展和结果。

t: The laws of truth embedded in advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 推进马克思主义中国化时代化蕴含的真理规律
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 5
paras: Yan Xiaofeng takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the 20th Party Congress (2022) that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is a process of pursuing, revealing and putting into practice truth. The article argues that the process works because it follows the practical principle and the laws of truth. On that basis, theoretical innovation guides creative practice.

The article has four parts. It first presents pursuing, revealing and practising truth as an essential requirement of Marxism, using Marx's and Engels's own careers as illustration. It then treats the adaptation of Marxism as such a process, and identifies the Two Integrations as its fundamental route. Finally it turns to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the tasks of the new journey after the 20th Party Congress.

Yan holds that Marxism's truth rests on its advanced class character, on the historical law of human emancipation, and on a scientific spirit that rejects "ultimate truth" and dogma. Adaptation is described as the unity of the universal and the particular, so that adapting Marxism to China also means adapting it to the times. In this account the Party's ideological line, the Two Integrations and the successive theoretical results (Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, Xi Jinping Thought) each embody this truth-seeking. The "second integration", with fine traditional Chinese culture, is presented as a further liberation of thought that broadens the cultural base of socialism with Chinese characteristics and expresses cultural subjectivity.

Yan concludes that Xi Jinping Thought carries a "truth character" shown in the "six musts" and a "truth force" of conviction, responsibility, creativity and practice. The article calls for further theoretical thinking on the questions of the new journey. These include the question "where is the world heading", Chinese modernization, and the problems peculiar to a large governing party, to which the article says the Party's self-reform is the second answer to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party theorist ties epistemology and the theory of truth to official doctrine on the adaptation of Marxism.
quoteEn: Upholding the unity of the universal and the particular is the path and the law of the development of truth.
quoteZh: 坚持普遍性和特殊性的统一，是真理发展的途径和规律。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxist principles to China's concrete conditions and to each era. It was extended from "sinification of Marxism" to include "adapting to the times" in recent Party documents.
Xi Jinping's formula: integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second was stressed from 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.

An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, presented as its answer to the problem of long-term rule. Xi Jinping has called it the second answer to the "historical cycle".
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept, adopted in 2007. It stresses people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

t: Several hot issues in current domestic research on new quality productive forces
zh: 当前国内新质生产力研究的几个热点问题
paras: This review, published in 2024, surveys how Chinese scholars have responded to the concept of new quality productive forces, which Xi Jinping first put forward during inspection tours from July 2023 and elaborated further in 2024. Dong and Li note that the concept drew wide attention, and they summarise the main debates in the field. They report that scholars from economics, science and technology and theory differ in sources and methods but largely converge in their basic conclusions.

The review is organised around three questions: why the concept was proposed, what it contains, and what practical steps its development requires. On background, it lists five rationales: advancing Chinese modernization, high-quality development, higher-quality living for the people, seizing the new round of technological and industrial change, and offsetting profound shifts in the world political and economic order. A short concluding section assesses the research as a whole.

On content, the review follows Xi's definition and reports scholars' discussion of the three elements (labourers, means of labour, objects of labour), technological innovation as the core factor, and a large rise in total factor productivity as the core marker. It also covers the role of traditional, emerging and future industries and the three keywords "innovation", "superior quality" and "advanced productive forces". On practice, it records scholarly proposals on high-level scientific and technological self-reliance, a modern industrial system, green transformation, deeper reform to build matching new relations of production, a virtuous cycle of education, science and talent, and development adapted to local conditions. Some scholars warn that the concept should not be over-extended or applied indiscriminately.

Dong and Li characterise the literature as strongly oriented to real-world problems, solid in tracing theoretical sources, and rigorous in generalising practice. They acknowledge that research is sometimes insufficiently focused. Two open problems stand out: how to avoid both the over-broad labelling of everything as "new quality productive forces" and a narrow reading limited to technology and industry, and how to treat the relation among emerging, future and traditional industries. Read the original if you want a map of mainstream Chinese scholarly positions on the concept in its first year, with the Party-line framing intact.
quoteEn: How to avoid both the \"over-extension\" and \"idling\" of the concept (labelling everything as \"new quality productive forces\") and the \"narrowing\" of its strategic meaning (pointing it solely at certain technology and industrial sectors).
quoteZh: 如何既避免新质生产力的“概念泛化”“概念空转”的问题（把什么都贴上“新质生产力”的标签），又避免将新质生产力的战略内涵“狭义化”（将其只单纯指向一些技术和产业部门）

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading. It has since become a central theme in Chinese economic policy and scholarship.
The official name for the Party's path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which it presents as distinct from Western models.
An official policy goal that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to efficiency, innovation, green development and sharing of results.

t: The generative logic and meaning of the concept of "new quality productive forces"
st: An understanding based on historical materialism
zh: “新质生产力”的概念生发逻辑与内涵探析
zhSub: 基于唯物史观的理解
source: Journal of Guizhou University (Social Sciences Edition), 2024 no. 3
paras: Since Xi Jinping first used the term in September 2023, "new quality productive forces" has become a national development priority. Zhang argues that much of the existing commentary blurs the concept: it equates new quality productive forces with "new economy", "new business forms" or "new industries", or treats their causes, conditions and functions as their meaning. The article's thesis is that the concept must be returned to Marx's definition of productive forces and traced through the practice of China's economic development. On that basis Zhang defines the essence of new quality productive forces as advanced labour productive force.

The article has four parts. The first reviews Marx's concept of productive forces, including Chinese scholarship's departure from the Soviet-textbook "element theory" and its recovery of the concept's origins in The German Ideology and Marx's technology notebooks. The second explains why the concept arises necessarily from historical materialism and from the demands of high-quality development. The third gives a multidimensional account of the concept's meaning, with examples from agriculture, industry, the digital economy and daily life. A short conclusion follows.

Zhang's central move is to read Marx's "productive force" as the capacity of useful, concrete labour to create use-value, which cannot be separated from the relations of production. Productive forces are formed within given relations, and the old quality dissolves as a new one forms. On this reading, "new quality" is not a break with earlier industrial productive forces: digital technology amplifies them through a "multiplier effect". The author cites figures from a 2023 China Academy of Information and Communications Technology report: a digital economy of 50.2 trillion yuan in 2022, 41.5 per cent of GDP. Zhang also argues that self-reliance in core technology, with chips as the example, is a necessary condition. New quality productive forces then appear in four forms: a leap in the means of production, high-quality development of natural forces, innovative use of collective force, and the broad distribution of "general intellect". Zhang's examples include public ownership of natural resources, the "East Data, West Computing" project and ride-hailing platforms.

Zhang concludes that Marx's productive-forces theory is a living methodology, not a dogma. It is the theoretical root of the concept, and it keeps the people-centred character of socialism with Chinese characteristics in view. The author holds that "new quality" is not an isolated quality: it is the product of China's successive revolutionary, construction and reform stages. Developing it requires attention to labour, means of production, natural force, collective force and general intellect together. Read the original if you want a Marxist-theoretical account of how Chinese scholars ground the concept in Marx's texts, and a view of how the concept is being defined and defended in academic debate.
quoteEn: "New quality" is not an isolated quality: it is the trait by which modern science and technology, through a distinctive multiplier effect, amplify the productive forces of traditional, emerging and future industries.
quoteZh: “新质”非孤立之质，而是现代科技以独特的乘数效应放大传统产业、新兴产业、未来产业生产力的特质

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in September 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading. It was elaborated at a Politburo study session in January 2024.

The official goal of shifting China's growth from scale and speed towards efficiency, innovation and quality. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it the first task of building a modern socialist country.
The Marxist theory that material production and the relations of production shape the development of society and its institutions.
A concept from Marx's 1857–58 manuscripts (the Grundrisse) for the general social knowledge that becomes a direct productive force.

t: The "Second Integration" and the space for innovation
zh: “第二个结合”与创新空间
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Liu Tongfang asks how the "Second Integration", the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, opens a space for innovation for the modern civilization of the Chinese nation. The article argues that it is a civilizational methodology and not merely a theoretical abstraction of specific cases. In Liu's view it breaks through the spatial pattern framed by Western modern civilization and shows the theoretical wisdom of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three parts. The first explains how the Second Integration opens the innovation space. The second sets out its "overall perspective" and the value positioning of that space. The third examines its inclusive mechanism and the continuing construction of the space. Liu draws on Marx's account of world history and capitalist modernity, and on categories such as cultural space, spatial justice and the production of space.

Liu's central move is to read the Second Integration as combining a diachronic totality (a historical process from past to future, from tradition to modernity) with a synchronic totality (a structure of social relations). Together these give the innovation space its coordinates and locate it as a cultural space, produced through cultural production and exchange across public and individual, urban and rural, real and virtual spaces. A second move contrasts Western modernity with the Chinese case. Liu says Western modernity rests on the logic of capital, which turns time into space, uses the world market to create spatial barriers, and reduces "inclusiveness" to homogenisation. By contrast, Liu argues, the Second Integration draws on the inclusiveness, continuity, innovativeness and unity of Chinese civilization. It therefore offers a mechanism for different civilizations to coexist, grounded in rational consensus and in the unity of conformity to laws and purposiveness, and of endogenous development and external extension.

Liu concludes that the Second Integration is the necessary path to cultural identity and to a modern Chinese civilization with its own style. Liu presents it as a cultural strategy of the Party in the new era that takes up the problems of modernity within Marx's world-history framework, expresses the originality of Chinese modernization, and supplies civilizational strength useful to human society. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar draws on spatial theory and the critique of capitalist modernity to interpret the Second Integration.
quoteEn: The "Second Integration" is not a theoretical abstraction of specific practices of integration, but a vibrant methodology of civilization.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”不是对具体结合实践的理论抽象,而是充满活力的文明方法论

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2023 formulation of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It follows the first integration, with China's concrete realities, and is part of the Two Integrations.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing localisation and updating of Marxism in China.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept used in Party discourse for the new civilizational form said to emerge from the Second Integration and Chinese modernization.

t: The concept of democracy: Mao Zedong's construction of democracy and its multidimensional reflections
st: With a discussion of Mao Zedong's foundational contribution to the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 民主的概念：毛泽东的民主构境与多维镜像的阐释
zhSub: 兼论毛泽东对中华民族现代文明的奠基性贡献
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2024 no. 3
paras: Li Panqiang asks what Mao Zedong's concept of democracy actually was, arguing that although Mao's democratic thought has been widely studied, it has rarely been treated as a conceptual whole. The article contends that people's democracy is the core concept of Mao Zedong Thought and that Mao built an independent Chinese body of knowledge about democracy. On this basis Li claims that Mao laid the foundations of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces how Mao's concept formed through the combined influence of Chinese tradition, modern Western thought and Marxism-Leninism, and presents it at two levels: the "idea" (people's democracy as the people being masters of the country) and its concrete "existence" in practice. The second examines four dimensions of Mao's democratic framework, drawing on his speeches and writings from the 1920s to the 1960s. The third sets out Mao's contribution to Chinese modern civilization.

In Li's reading, Mao defined democracy plainly as ordinary people being able to speak and act, and as a means rather than an abstract end. The four dimensions are democracy as rights (freedoms of speech, assembly and association, and workers' right to manage the state and enterprises); as a method of realising Party leadership (the mass line, gathering popular opinion, opposing bureaucracy); as an institutional system (from the people's republic to the people's congress system, the people's political consultative conference and consultative democracy); and as a democratic spirit (mutual respect, the search for truth through discussion, and shared ideals). Li presents Mao's 1945 answer to Huang Yanpei, that democracy is the way to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall, as a key moment.

Li concludes that Mao contributed to the democratic ideal, path, institutions and form of Chinese modern civilization. In the article's account, Mao avoided copying Western liberal democracy, broke the presumed uniqueness of the Western path, and created a new form that combines consultative and electoral democracy and goes beyond Western voting democracy. Li presents this as the root of whole-process people's democracy in the new era. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-theoretical reconstruction of Mao's democratic thought, with dense citations of his texts, as one strand of current Chinese discourse on democracy.
quoteEn: The democracy Mao Zedong pursued was people's democracy, that is, the people being masters of their own affairs.
quoteZh: 毛泽东追求的民主，就是人民民主，即人民当家作主。

glossary.explanation: Mao's term for a democracy led by the proletariat and based on the worker-peasant alliance, in which the people are said to be the masters of the state. It is the core concept of the article.
A concept advanced by Xi Jinping in 2019 and promoted as the form of democracy in China's socialist system, said to cover every stage of democratic life rather than only elections.
A Party working method associated with Mao: leaders gather views from the masses ("from the masses, to the masses") and turn them into policy.
China's fundamental political institution, a hierarchy of people's congresses from local level to the National People's Congress, established in 1954.
Democratic practice based on consultation, institutionalised mainly through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and Party–non-Party cooperation.

t: The value essence, value composition and value orientation of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的价值本质、价值构成与价值指向
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2024 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2024, Yao Chong asks what Chinese modernization looks like when read through the theory of value rather than through economic or institutional description. The article argues that Chinese modernization is the Chinese Communist Party's value practice of understanding and changing the world. Its essence, content and orientation are all organised around meeting the needs of the human subject, in contrast with Western modernization, which Yao says serves capital.

The article has three parts. The first sets out three aspects of the value essence of Chinese modernization. The second breaks its value composition into five elements: value fact, value goal, value principle, value driving force and value choice. The third identifies four value orientations, ranging from national rejuvenation to a new form of human civilization. Throughout, Yao draws on Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, Capital, The German Ideology and Engels's Anti-Dühring, together with speeches by Xi Jinping.

In the first move, Yao holds that Chinese modernization is essentially the satisfaction of people's needs, the affirmation of the objectification of human essential powers, and a Chinese interpretation of free and all-round human development. Western modernization, by contrast, is said to satisfy the needs of capital and to turn labour into forced, repetitive activity. In the second move, each value element is tied to a Chinese policy theme. The huge population is the value fact, common prosperity the goal, coordinated material and spiritual civilization the principle, harmony between humanity and nature the driving force, and the path of peaceful development the choice. Yao presents these as expressions of Marx's view of humanity, nature and society.

Yao concludes that Chinese modernization points towards four ends: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a modernized socialist country; the development of twenty-first-century Marxism and a new picture of modernization theory; a model for developing countries that respects their cultural agency; and a new form of human civilization built on a community with a shared future for mankind. The article claims that it breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and enriches common human values. Read the original if you want a value-theory reading of Chinese modernization that ties the official slogans to Marx's concepts of need, objectification and free development.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is itself the value practice through which Chinese Communists continually understand and transform the world.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化就是中国共产党人不断认识世界、改造世界的价值实践本身。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization under Communist Party leadership. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, aimed at reducing poverty and gaps between groups. Xi Jinping has given it new prominence since 2021.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity. It is linked to the second centenary goal of 2049.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing common interests, peace and cooperation among countries.

glossary.literal: harmonious coexistence of humans and nature
glossary.explanation: An official formulation of ecological civilization. It treats humans and nature as a life community in which nature is to be respected, accommodated and protected.

t: Making vigorous efforts to cultivate and practise the core socialist values
zh: 着力培育和践行社会主义核心价值观
paras: Following the national work conference on propaganda, ideological and cultural work held shortly before publication, and Xi Jinping's instruction listing 'seven efforts', Zhang Chuanhe takes up the task of cultivating and practising the core socialist values. The article argues that this task is a spiritual force for advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Zhang's account it bears on social harmony and long-term national stability, and is a major task of the new era.

The piece, a commentary in a Party theoretical journal, has three parts. The first explains why the core values matter; the second sets out guiding principles for cultivating them; the third proposes concrete channels of implementation. It draws throughout on the 20th Party Congress (2022) report and on Xi Jinping's statements.

In the first part, Zhang argues that a country of over 1.4 billion people and 56 ethnic groups without shared core values could easily become 'a sheet of loose sand'. The core values are presented as the soul of cultural soft power and an element of state governance capacity. The second part holds that the work must be guided by Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, with ideals and convictions at its centre. Its focus is shaping 'new-era people' able to shoulder national rejuvenation, described as self-confident, ethical, dedicated, practical and enterprising, and fostered through patriotism and Party, national and reform-era history education. The third part proposes four channels: law and policy, as expressed in combining rule of law with rule by virtue; excellent literary and artistic works; families, schools, workplaces and online space; and practical activities such as Martyrs' Day commemorations, model selections and volunteer service.

Zhang concludes that the core values must be built into legal construction, social governance, national education and cultural production so that society identifies with and consciously acts on them. Education alone is insufficient without institutional norms and policy backing. Online space needs close attention to value orientation, with content contrary to the core values to be firmly kept out. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Party press frames the practical routes for implementing the core socialist values in law, culture, education and daily activity.
