The author also links the approach to the change in the principal contradiction, now between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

Cui concludes that development must be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by them. The author ties this to the 20th Party Congress (2022) goals of a modern socialist country by mid-century and to common prosperity achieved through high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary presents the people-centred development idea and its Marxist lineage.
quoteEn: Development for the people is the fundamental stance of Marxist political economy.
quoteZh: 发展为了人民，是马克思主义政治经济学的根本立场。

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thinking with the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding idea promoted by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress. It holds that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by them.
The economic component of Xi Jinping Thought, presented officially as applying Marxist political economy to China's development in the new era.
The official framework, announced in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of the masses and serving them.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised under Xi Jinping.
The official term for a growth model stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed.

t: Shouldering the new cultural mission
zh: 担负起新的文化使命
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 13 October 2023, responds to Xi Jinping's recent instruction on propaganda, ideological and cultural work. Dong Zhenhua argues that this work bears on the Party's future, national stability and national cohesion. In Dong's reading, it can be carried out properly only by taking up the "new cultural mission" of promoting cultural prosperity, building a culturally strong country and building a modern Chinese civilization, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The piece has three numbered sections. The first explains why propaganda, ideological and cultural work is of extreme importance, drawing on Party history and on lessons from the world socialist movement. The second sets out the principles of the new mission: firm cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and upholding fundamental principles while innovating. The third turns to the guiding role of Xi Jinping's cultural thought and to practical tasks for Party committees at all levels.

Dong holds that a shared ideological foundation is the precondition for a party, a state and a nation to exist. The article cites the collapse of the Soviet Communist Party as the result of giving up Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, and calls for leadership, management and discourse power over ideological work to be kept firmly in Party hands. On the three principles, Dong argues that Marxism is the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture the "root" of the new civilization, and that the two must be linked together. Openness means mutual learning among civilizations. Because social thinking is increasingly diverse, the article contends, a single guiding ideology must lead varied social consciousness, with core socialist values as the leading force.

Dong concludes that Party committees must treat this work as a major political responsibility. The proposed measures include studying and implementing Xi Jinping's cultural thought, strengthening positive publicity and public-opinion guidance, practising core socialist values, developing cultural undertakings and industries, improving international communication, and guarding against ideological risks. The stated aim is to bring the thinking and action of more than 1.4 billion people into line with central decisions in support of Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party commentators framed the "new cultural mission" in autumn 2023.
quoteEn: The collapse of a regime often begins in the realm of ideas: political turmoil and regime change may happen overnight, but the evolution of ideas is a long process.
quoteZh: 一个政权的瓦解往往是从思想领域开始的，政治动荡、政权更迭可能在一夜之间发生，但思想演化是个长期过程。

glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping in 2023. It combines promoting cultural prosperity, building a culturally strong country and building a modern Chinese civilization.
An official term for the new form of civilization the Party says it is building. It is presented as combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It was formally put forward in October 2023 as guidance for ideological and cultural work.
An official concept that stresses confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It is counted among the Four-sphere Confidence.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official term for the Party's path of national development, held to differ from Western models of modernization.

t: Grasping the inner connection between economy and culture
zh: 深刻把握经济与文化的内在联系
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 27 November 2023, asks how economists should relate Xi Jinping's economic thought to his thought on culture. Qiu Haiping argues that the two are mutually connected and together reveal how economy and culture interact and merge. The commentary proposes that economists study them jointly.

The piece begins with the National Conference on Publicity, Ideology and Culture, which presented Xi Jinping Thought on Culture as the cultural part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It then sets out two directions of research: the cultural foundations of Xi's economic thought, and the economic foundations of his cultural thought.

Qiu holds that the key task is to study the internal logic linking high-quality development, cultural construction and the building of a self-reliant Chinese system of economic knowledge. In Qiu's account, economists have mostly read Xi's economic thought through political economy. Qiu urges them to examine how it carries forward traditional Chinese economic thought and the Marxist theory of culture found in Marxist political economy. In the other direction, Qiu says understanding of Xi's cultural thought lacks social-science perspectives, including economics. Philosophy and social sciences, economics among them, are themselves part of social culture, which Qiu says accords with basic Marxist views. Literature and art have relative independence but cannot be discussed apart from economic development.

Qiu concludes that economists, political economists especially, should unify the two bodies of thought and draw out the cultural substance and humanistic spirit in Xi's economic thought. This work should then inform the construction of a self-reliant Chinese system of economic knowledge. Qiu presents this as a remedy for treating culture and economy in isolation. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Chinese economists are being urged to link economic and cultural theory.
quoteEn: We need to understand Xi Jinping's economic thought from the angle of culture, and also to understand Xi Jinping's thought on culture from the angle of economics.
quoteZh: 我们既需要从文化角度出发理解习近平经济思想，也需要从经济角度出发理解习近平文化思想。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally articulated at the national conference on publicity, ideology and culture in October 2023. It is presented as the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for Xi Jinping's ideas on economic work, treated as part of the Party's guiding ideology and a basis for a Chinese political economy.
An official development goal emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over growth speed. It has been prominent in Party economic policy since 2017.

t: Unwaveringly following the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚定不移走中国特色金融发展之路
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in November 2023, Ding Xiaoqin and Yan Xinqi comment on the Central Financial Work Conference held on 30–31 October 2023. They argue that Xi Jinping's speech there gives fundamental guidance for high-quality development of finance and for unwaveringly following a path of financial development with Chinese characteristics.

The short commentary has five parts. It covers the Marxist theory of finance, the Party's centralised and unified leadership over financial work, financial supervision and risk prevention, high-standard opening up of the financial sector, and financial innovation.

The authors present the Party's recent financial theory and practice as a continuation and renewal of Marxist financial theory, which deals with money, credit and financial crises. In their account, since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has combined that theory with China's conditions and traditional culture, producing results that form part of Xi Jinping's economic thought. As evidence of leadership, they cite the 2023 creation of the Central Financial Commission and the Central Financial Work Commission. They describe supervision moving from "one bank, two commissions" to "one commission, one bank, one bureau, one commission", and report that the renminbi's SDR weight rose from 10.92% to 12.28% in 2022.

The authors conclude that China must guide finance to serve the real economy, strengthen supervision, defuse risks and build skilled financial cadres in order to become a financial powerhouse. They call for wider institutional opening up and more work on technology, green, inclusive, pension and digital finance. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned summary of how Chinese scholars presented the October 2023 financial work conference.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's centralised and unified leadership over financial work is the concentrated expression, in the financial field, of upholding the Party's centralised and unified leadership over economic work.
quoteZh: 坚持党对金融工作的集中统一领导是坚持党对经济工作集中统一领导在金融工作上的集中体现。

glossary.explanation: A high-level Party meeting on financial policy. The one held in October 2023 stressed building a financial powerhouse and strengthening Party leadership over finance.
The official name for the body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought.
A decision-making and coordinating body of the Party Central Committee, set up in 2023 to handle top-level design of financial stability and development.
A body dispatched by the Party Central Committee, also set up in 2023, to lead Party work in the financial system.

t: Advancing green development under the Belt and Road Initiative to inject strong momentum into global sustainable development
zh: 推进共建“一带一路”绿色发展 为全球可持续发展注入强劲动能
paras: Marking ten years of the Belt and Road Initiative, this commentary (first published in Guangming Daily, 24 October 2023) takes up Xi Jinping's announcement at the third Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation that "promoting green development" is one of eight actions to support high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. Hu Sai and Sun Juhong argue that China, as a participant, contributor and leader in global ecological civilization, has made green development the defining colour of the Initiative and a strong driver of global sustainable development.

The article has three parts. The first explains why green is the "base colour" of the Initiative and how the concept has been built into its top-level design. The second reviews progress in five areas of cooperation: policy coordination, infrastructure connectivity, trade, financial integration and people-to-people bonds. The third sets out how to continue, under four headings: practising green development concepts, strengthening green technological innovation, deepening green finance cooperation and improving green development institutions.

The authors present green development as a way for partner countries to escape the path of "pollute first, clean up later". They cite the end of new overseas coal-power projects, the promotion of wind and solar, environmental technology transfer centres and the Green Silk Road Envoys Programme. As evidence of results, they report more than 50 ecological and environmental cooperation documents, a green development partnership initiative with 31 countries, and more than 40 major institutions signing the Green Investment Principles by the end of 2022. They also say cumulative green and low-carbon energy investment in partner countries now exceeds traditional energy projects, and that China became the world's largest green trade economy in 2021, supplying nearly 70 per cent of global photovoltaic capacity.

For the future, the authors call for cross-border circular-economy cooperation mechanisms, a green institutional convention, green loans, bonds and funds, project classification systems, ecological risk early warning and protected areas for key ecological spaces. They also call for centralised, unified leadership of the Initiative's green work, along with assessment of its tasks. They conclude that these steps would make the Initiative a more competitive and influential platform and add to the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise official-style overview of how Chinese commentators describe the Belt and Road's green agenda, with the figures and programmes they cite.
quoteEn: Green development in jointly building the Belt and Road is the engine driving global sustainable development.
quoteZh: 共建“一带一路”绿色发展是全球可持续发展的动力引擎。

glossary.explanation: A China-led international cooperation framework proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, covering infrastructure, trade, finance and cultural exchange across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
A Chinese Party-state concept that makes harmony between humans and nature a goal of development. It has been part of official policy since the early 2010s.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing common interests and joint development.
The label for the environmental and low-carbon dimension of the Belt and Road Initiative, promoted in official documents since the mid-2010s.

t: Common prosperity from the perspective of fairness and justice
zh: 公平正义视阈下的共同富裕
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily, asks how common prosperity relates to fairness and justice. Wang Li argues that common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a defining feature of Chinese modernization. In the author's view, it is also the core category through which Chinese thought explains its own conception of fairness and justice. Steadily advancing common prosperity for all the people is presented as both a concentrated institutional realisation of social justice and a practical basis for a socialist discourse on fairness and justice.

The article has three parts. The first compares capitalism and socialism, arguing that whether common prosperity can be realised is an important measure of justice. The second considers what common prosperity means when seen through fairness and justice. The third sets out three ways in which Chinese practice offers a "Chinese approach" to justice: eliminating absolute poverty, uniting fairness with efficiency, and pursuing the free and all-round development of the human being.

Drawing on Marx, Wang argues that under capitalism fairness and justice are separated from common prosperity. Liberty, equality and fraternity are described as the ideological expression of bourgeois material relations, and class opposition and private ownership of the means of production are said to rule out common prosperity. Under socialism, by contrast, public ownership unites owners with labourers and producers with beneficiaries, so that common prosperity and justice coincide in form and content. Wang adds that justice is not abstract: given the primary stage of socialism and the principal contradiction identified since the new era, it requires a system guaranteeing fair rights, opportunities and rules. Common prosperity is described as covering material and spiritual life, democratic participation, rights and a healthy environment, not only economic growth.

Wang points to the victory over absolute poverty since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as the foundation for justice. The article also cites the socialist market economy, the coordination of three distribution tiers and the provision of basic livelihood guarantees as ways of combining efficiency with fairness. It concludes that the Party keeps productive forces and the people's interests, and the measure of things and of people, in unity, with the free and all-round development of the human being as the highest value. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary links common prosperity to a Marxist critique of bourgeois justice.
quoteEn: There is no abstract fairness and justice, and no common prosperity detached from reality.
quoteZh: 没有抽象的公平正义，也没有脱离实际的共同富裕。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis in Party policy since the 2010s. It is presented officially as covering both material and cultural-spiritual wellbeing.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The Party's official name for its model of socialism since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, public ownership and a socialist market economy.
The official judgement, formalised in the 1980s, that China is in an early and long historical stage of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces.

t: Understanding the significance of advancing high-standard opening up
zh: 深刻理解推进高水平对外开放重要意义
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in September 2023, asks why China should keep expanding high-standard opening up to the outside world. Yang Lu argues that it is an objective requirement of the new development stage and a necessary base for high-quality development and Chinese modernization. The piece presents Xi Jinping's statements on opening up as part of Xi Jinping economic thought.

The commentary is organised around four reasons. Opening up is tied to the change in China's principal contradiction, to high-quality development and the new development pattern, to balancing development and security, and to steering economic globalization. It closes with a call to follow Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Yang argues that the principal contradiction is now between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. In Yang's account, imports, foreign investment, trade and regional opening help meet that need and create jobs. The new development pattern, Yang stresses, is not a closed domestic cycle but an open dual circulation of domestic and international flows, and China's past achievements came under open conditions. On security, Yang holds that openness brings the capital, technology, markets and talent that support a higher level of security. Yang also contends that cutting economic flows between countries is impossible and against historical trends.

Yang proposes mutually beneficial opening, better top-level design of the open economy, institutional opening in rules and standards, wider market access, a better business environment, and high-quality Belt and Road Initiative cooperation. Yang concludes that China should unwaveringly expand opening up at every level. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official press justifies high-standard opening up in the framework of Xi Jinping's economic thinking.
quoteEn: In the past, China's economic achievements were made under conditions of openness; in the future, China's high-quality economic development must be advanced under still more open conditions.
quoteZh: 过去，中国经济发展成就是在开放条件下取得的；未来，中国经济高质量发展必须在更加开放的条件下推进。

glossary.literal: high-level opening to the outside world
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party documents since the 2010s for a deeper stage of opening, stressing alignment with international trade and investment rules and institutional opening.
A strategy put forward in 2020 that treats the domestic market as the mainstay while linking it with international circulation, known as dual circulation.
Official goal since 2017 of shifting from rapid growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and balance.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A Chinese-led infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Understanding the connotation of new quality productive forces
zh: 理解新质生产力的内涵
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 22 December 2023, asks what new quality productive forces are and how to cultivate them. Yang Huixin and Jiao Yong argue that accelerating their formation is a key step for seizing the opportunities of a new round of technological revolution, building a modernized industrial system and shaping new development advantages.

The authors first define the concept through its two components, "new" and "quality", and then set out four roles: supporting strategic emerging and future industries, building a modern industrial system, driving the shift from old to new growth drivers, and serving as a decisive factor in great-power competition.

On definition, Yang and Jiao hold that "new" means innovation in technology, business models, management and institutions. "Quality" means that these forces are not a partial optimisation or simple iteration of traditional productive forces, but advanced forces born of revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial transformation. Intelligent, numerically controlled, precise production tools, such as lithography machines and high-end machine tools, are named as important markers. The authors list priority sectors, including new-generation information technology, new energy and civil aviation, and future industries such as the metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, humanoid robots and quantum information. They also call for upgrading traditional industries and for digital transformation. They describe Western "small yard, high fence" technology restrictions as harmful to China, and call for self-reliance and a new-type whole-nation system.

The authors conclude that China should use its complete industrial system and very large market to foster these forces. They propose tackling "chokepoint" technologies through open competitive selection of research teams, greater autonomy for researchers, support for young talent and a role for leading and specialised enterprises. Read the original if you want a concise early official-media statement of how new quality productive forces were defined and what industrial priorities were attached to them.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are not a partial optimisation or simple iteration of traditional productive forces, but contemporary advanced productive forces born of revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial transformation and upgrading.
quoteZh: 新质生产力不是传统生产力的局部优化与简单迭代，而是由技术革命性突破、生产要素创新性配置、产业深度转型升级而催生的当代先进生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in place of reliance on traditional growth models.

A model that mobilises state, market and institutional resources nationally for major scientific and technological goals. It builds on the earlier whole-nation system of concentrating resources on key projects.

glossary.en: open competitive selection of research teams
glossary.explanation: A research-funding mechanism in which major problems are publicly posted and capable teams compete to take them on, regardless of rank or affiliation.

t: Questioning and seeking the ethical foundation of Chinese modernization
zh: 追问和追寻中国式现代化的伦理基础
paras: Yan Hui asks what ethical foundation Chinese modernization rests on and how it can be secured. The article argues that this inquiry contains two tasks: an ethical-foundation argument, which identifies the ultimate good and the holistic 'good life' at stake, and a moral grounding, which supplies both a subjective basis (virtue) and objective conditions (norms and institutions). Yan's thesis is that Chinese modernization is the practical movement that turns what 'is' in reason into what 'ought to be' and then into reality.

The article has three parts. The first sets out a philosophical method drawn from Hegel's account of reason and actuality and from a sequence of sensibility, understanding and reason. The second defines the 'ethical world' as the ultimate good and examines its economic, political and personal dimensions, discussing Adam Smith, Kant and Marx along the way. The third turns to how Chinese modernization is a new path and how it can be grounded morally through a revolution in ideas, institutional innovation and practice.

Yan defines the ultimate good in three statements: an economic organisation that creates and fairly distributes wealth continuously; institutions through which everyone can voluntarily and rationally express a political will; and the capacity and conditions for everyone to live a holistic good life. Economy and politics are only means, and the good life is the end. Yan argues that the capitalist market economy, driven by the logic of capital, produces alienation and polarisation, and that Smith's 'invisible hand' ignores the difference between private and public ownership. The market therefore cannot distribute fairly by itself, and political power must be limited and used through institutions, which Yan presents as the fundamental advantage of the socialist system. Chinese modernization is said to differ from Western modernization in its origins (equal and mutually beneficial rather than colonial), its path and its goal of common prosperity. Yan calls for reconstructing the concepts of politics, wealth (material, social and spiritual) and happiness, and for institutions that combine incentive with coordination and include self-restraint for those who hold power.

Yan concludes that inquiry into the ethical foundation of Chinese modernization must respect holism, complexity and conflict, since values and costs, opportunities and risks coexist, and difficulties can only be resolved through repeated practice. The article presents the Party's century of practice as having built a political system embodying common prosperity, democracy, equality and justice. Read the original if you want a philosophically dense, Hegelian and Kantian account of how Chinese modernization is given ethical justification in current Chinese theory.
quoteEn: Building the new path of Chinese modernization is the 'ought to be' that realises the 'what is', and it is an element, a moment and a road towards realising the ultimate good.
quoteZh: 构建中国式现代化新道路就是实现“所是”的“应是”,是实现终极之善的要素、环节和道路。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

A goal of shared affluence for all, which official discourse places at the centre of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is stressed under Xi Jinping and is not understood as equal distribution.
Yan's term for a life in which material, social and spiritual needs are met together. Yan treats it as the ultimate good that economy and politics serve.
A concept from ethical philosophy for the final end that gives other goods, called 'goods of means', their value. Yan uses it to separate ends from means in modernization.

t: Practical requirements for advancing common prosperity in the new era
zh: 新时代推进共同富裕的实践要求
paras: This commentary, originally published in the Economic Daily in November 2023, asks what practical conditions are needed to move common prosperity forward in the new era. Ai Silin and Li Hanke present common prosperity as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a defining feature of Chinese modernization. Drawing on Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), they argue that it must be pursued through four requirements: strategic resolve, internal motivation, developmental strength and institutional potential.

The piece is organised under four short headings matching these requirements. It sets out the staged goals announced by the Party Central Committee: solid steps by the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, more marked substantive progress by 2035, and basic realisation by the middle of the century. It then turns to the role of the people, to high-quality development, and to the income distribution system.

On strategic resolve, the authors stress that common prosperity is a long-term goal and a political question bearing on the Party's governing base, not only an economic one. They cite the scale of China's population and regional disparities as reasons to expect a long, arduous process, and they argue that the Party's overall leadership and top-level design are decisive. On motivation and strength, they say prosperity must be created through the hard work of the people, who should share in reform and development outcomes, and that it must come through high-quality development guided by the new development philosophy, with innovation as the first driving force. On institutions, they call distribution the foundational system and propose coordinated primary distribution, redistribution and third distribution. Primary distribution should raise labour's share. Redistribution should "raise the low, expand the middle and regulate the high" to build an olive-shaped income structure. Charity should supplement both under stronger legal oversight.

The authors conclude that, with the Party's leadership, consistent goals and a single blueprint carried through, China can make steady progress towards common prosperity and achieve more marked substantive progress. They urge making the economic pie bigger while dividing it more fairly, and they warn against polarisation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists frame the policy agenda for common prosperity, especially the sequencing of distribution mechanisms.
quoteEn: While promoting high-quality development and making the "cake" bigger and better, we must go further in dividing the "cake" well.
quoteZh: 要在推动高质量发展、做好做大“蛋糕”的同时，进一步分好“蛋糕”。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping. It refers to prosperity shared by all, with narrower gaps in income and public services.
The official term for China's path to modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. Common prosperity is listed as one of its features.
An official economic goal stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it the first task of building a modern socialist country.
A framework of five principles (innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing) introduced in 2015 to guide economic policy.
Income distribution through voluntary charity and donations, added to market-based primary distribution and state-led redistribution via taxes and transfers.

t: Practical requirements for advancing common prosperity in the new era
zh: 新时代推进共同富裕的实践要求
paras: This newspaper commentary asks what practical demands follow from the Party's current approach to common prosperity. Ai and Li treat common prosperity as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a defining feature of Chinese modernization. They argue that, guided by Xi Jinping's ideas since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the task is to understand these demands fully and accurately so that "more notable substantive progress" can be made.

The article is organised under four headings: maintaining strategic resolve, stimulating endogenous motivation, strengthening development capacity, and tapping institutional potential. It opens with the political significance of common prosperity and the staged targets set for the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, for 2035 and for the middle of the century. It then moves from the role of the people and of economic growth to the income distribution system.

The authors first present common prosperity as a political issue bearing on the Party's governing base, not only an economic one. They describe it as a long-term goal that needs the Party's overall leadership, top-level design and a single blueprint pursued consistently. They contrast this with developed countries, where, in their account, the social system has left wealth gaps widening. They then tie common prosperity to people's own effort and to a people-centred idea of development, with shared fruits of reform and open channels of upward mobility. They also argue that development, specifically high-quality development guided by the new development philosophy, remains the basis, given the primary stage of socialism. Finally, they set out a three-tier distribution system: primary distribution through the market and distribution according to work, redistribution through taxes, social security and transfers, and charity as a third distribution. Redistribution aims to "raise the low, expand the middle, regulate the high" so as to form an olive-shaped income structure.

Ai and Li conclude that firm Party leadership, mobilised popular effort, sustained high-quality growth and a coordinated distribution system together make steady progress possible. They also call for regulating excessive and illegal income, and for better legal oversight of charity. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy framework for common prosperity as it stood in late 2023, including its staged targets and the three-tier distribution scheme.
quoteEn: While promoting high-quality development and making the "cake" bigger and better, we must also divide the "cake" more fairly.
quoteZh: 要在推动高质量发展、做好做大“蛋糕”的同时，进一步分好“蛋糕”。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared affluence for all, described in Party discourse as an essential requirement of socialism. It has been given greater prominence since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, with features such as a huge population and common prosperity for all.
An official formulation stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
Five principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015.
The official assessment that China is in an early, long-lasting phase of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces.
Voluntary redistribution through charity and donations, treated in official texts as a supplement to market-based primary distribution and state redistribution.

t: Shouldering the new cultural mission at a new historical starting point
zh: 在新的历史起点担负起新的文化使命
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 25 October 2023, this commentary responds to Xi Jinping's recent instruction on propaganda, ideological and cultural work. Huang and Qiu take up the "new cultural mission" of continuing to promote cultural prosperity, building a culturally strong country and building a modern Chinese civilization. They argue that the mission follows from history, the times and practice, and that it supplies a roadmap and a set of tasks for cultural work in the new era.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the mission is necessary, under three headings: continuing the Chinese cultural lineage, meeting the demands of developing socialist culture, and driving the building of a modern Chinese civilization. The second sets out what the mission requires. The third offers five practical directions for carrying it out.

The authors' central move is to link three goals in sequence. Cultural prosperity is the foundation of a culturally strong country. Building a socialist cultural power is included in, and lays the groundwork for, the longer-term and larger aim of a modern Chinese civilization. That civilization is in turn said to grow out of Chinese modernization, which the authors describe as a new form of human civilization different from the Western model. The two are presented as mutually reinforcing: Chinese modernization gives Chinese civilization modern strength, and the civilization gives modernization its depth. Throughout, the authors rely on the Two Integrations, the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, and cultural confidence.

For action, Huang and Qiu call for strengthening Party leadership over ideological work and its responsibility system, and for thorough study of Xi Jinping's cultural thought. They also call for protecting and passing on traditional culture through heritage protection, databases and education. Further proposals are to use modern technology to renew traditional culture, and to improve international communication so as to "tell China's story well". Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in late 2023 framed the new cultural mission and its practical tasks.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization gives Chinese civilization modern strength, and Chinese civilization gives Chinese modernization deep foundations; the two interconnect and make each other possible.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化赋予中华文明以现代力量,中华文明赋予中国式现代化以深厚底蕴,二者相互融通、彼此成就。

glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on cultural work: to promote cultural prosperity, build a culturally strong country and build a modern Chinese civilization at a new historical starting point.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and rooted in Chinese conditions and traditions.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
An official concept stressing confidence in China's own cultural traditions, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture.
The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on culture, formally put forward at the national conference on propaganda, ideological and cultural work in October 2023.
A goal stated by Xi Jinping in 2023: a modern civilization of the Chinese nation, presented as growing out of Chinese modernization.

t: Creating a new culture that belongs to our era
zh: 创造属于我们这个时代的新文化
paras: Writing in Qiushi (2023, no. 24), Gao Xiang presents Xi Jinping Thought on Culture as the defining achievement of cultural work since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Gao argues that it enriches and develops Marxist cultural theory and serves as the banner and soul of cultural prosperity in the new era. The piece is an official-style exposition rather than an empirical study.

The article has three parts. It first explains the "milestone significance" of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture for the history of Chinese civilisation and of Marxist cultural theory. It then sets out the thought's scientific content as a system of theoretical "substance" (ti) and, finally, its practical "application" (yong), meaning the tasks it sets for cultural work.

On the theoretical side, Gao identifies several distinctive features. These include placing culture at the centre of the Party's and state's overall work, stressing the Party's cultural leadership, and giving cultural confidence a core place. The thought also advances the Two Integrations, above all the "second integration" of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, which Gao says gives cultural subjectivity to building a modern Chinese civilisation. Gao calls the new cultural mission, and the concept of a "modern civilisation of the Chinese nation", its major innovations. That civilisation is described as socialist, balanced across five dimensions, oriented to common prosperity and to a community with a shared future for mankind, and different from the Western model of modernization.

On the practical side, Gao calls for arming the whole Party with its innovative theory, upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds in propaganda and ideological work, and strengthening the Party's leadership over that work. Gao also calls for fostering core socialist values, improving the reach and credibility of the media in the information age, protecting cultural heritage, and developing cultural undertakings and industries. Further tasks are building international communication capacity, analysing how the Western ideological apparatus operates, and constructing China's autonomous knowledge system. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences leadership frames Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and its practical agenda.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Culture is a system that combines both theoretical substance and practical application.
quoteZh: 习近平文化思想是一个体用兼备的体系。

glossary.explanation: The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, formally articulated in 2023. It covers Party leadership of ideology, cultural confidence and the building of a strong socialist culture.

The formula of integrating Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second integration was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.
A formulation from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised leadership.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the leadership presents as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, based on shared interests and cooperation.

t: Strengthening digital technology innovation and application to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 加强数字技术创新与应用 加快发展新质生产力
paras: Qi Yudong and Xu Kaige ask how new quality productive forces can be formed and developed, and answer that digital technology innovation and application are the core driver. Starting from Xi Jinping's remarks on revitalising Northeast China, they present the concept as a Marxist innovation in productive-force theory. In their account it captures a leap in productive forces caused by the digital technology revolution, and it helps the country seize the current round of technological and industrial change, build a modern industrial system and gain new competitive advantages.

The piece, which first appeared in Guangming Daily in October 2023, has two parts. The first explains why new quality productive forces are a leap brought about by digital technology. The second sets out how digital innovation and application supply the core impetus, and names four priority directions: technological self-reliance, industrial upgrading, changes in the mode of production, and digital talent. Along the way the authors compare strategies in the United States, Germany, the EU and Japan.

The central argument starts from the two basic elements of productive forces, labourers and means of production. Citing Marx's view that the means of labour mark out economic epochs, the authors contend that digital technology gives the means of labour a digital character, with strong connectivity and penetration, acting on data as a new object of labour. They place the resulting leap after the steam and electrical eras. On this basis they argue that key core digital technologies must be mastered, through concentrated efforts under the new whole-nation system or through 'changing lanes' to leapfrog on disruptive innovation. They also argue that digital technology should be fused with the real economy, especially manufacturing, so that intelligent, customised production on industrial internet platforms, with data as a production factor, replaces mass standardised output.

The authors conclude that self-reliance in digital technology is the most urgent task and industrial upgrading the key focus. They hold that changing production methods is the critical link, since intelligent customised production is still far from widespread in China. Talent is the foundation: they call for complementary types of personnel and a more tolerant research management system and innovation culture. Read the original if you want a concise Party-press statement of how digital technology is linked to new quality productive forces and of the policy priorities that follow.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are a leap in productive forces that corresponds to digitalised means of production.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是与数字化的生产资料相适应的生产力跃迁。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and officially promoted as a basis for high-quality development.
An official term for mobilising state, market and institutional resources nationwide to achieve breakthroughs in key science and technology fields.

t: Shouldering the new cultural mission with a high degree of cultural consciousness
zh: 以高度文化自觉担负起新的文化使命
paras: This commentary, first published in the Economic Daily in October 2023, sets out how Party members should understand and carry out the "new cultural mission" announced by Xi Jinping. The mission is defined as continuing to promote cultural prosperity, building a culturally strong country and building a modern Chinese civilization. Jin Minqing argues that taking up this mission requires a high degree of cultural consciousness and a sense of responsibility, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The article has three parts. The first explains the historical grounds for the mission: the tasks of the new era, the changing principal contradiction in society, and the international and national situation. The second turns to the goal of building a modern Chinese civilization and the principles it must follow. The third discusses methods and paths, drawing on Xi's "seven focuses" for propaganda, ideological and cultural work and on his remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development.

Jin contends that the mission follows from objective conditions. The principal contradiction is now between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, which Jin says is still visible in public cultural provision and in the coordination of material and spiritual civilization. Jin adds that the "great changes unseen in a century" bring ideological and cultural-security risks, and that Chinese modernization requires spiritual as well as material prosperity. A modern Chinese civilization must rest on three things: Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as its guiding "soul"; fine traditional Chinese culture as its "root"; and absorption of the achievements of other civilizations. Jin presents the Second of the Two Integrations, joining Marxism with fine traditional culture, as the key method. It is meant to make Marxism Chinese and traditional culture modern, and to strengthen China's cultural subjectivity.

Jin concludes that the mission calls for firm cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and adherence to fundamental principles alongside innovation. The practical tasks Jin lists include strengthening Party leadership of ideological work, upholding Marxism's guiding position, promoting core socialist values, building Chinese philosophy and social science, improving international communication and encouraging exchange among civilizations. Jin holds that this provides ideological assurance and spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how the new cultural mission and the Second of the Two Integrations are framed in Party discourse.
quoteEn: In building a modern Chinese civilization, we must carry forward fine traditional Chinese culture, which is its root.
quoteZh: 建设中华民族现代文明，必须传承赓续中华优秀传统文化这个根脉。

glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping used in June 2023: to continue promoting cultural prosperity, build a culturally strong country and build a modern Chinese civilization on a new historical starting point.

glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept in official discourse for a civilization that combines Chinese tradition, Marxism and the achievements of other civilizations. It is presented as a product of Chinese modernization.

The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The second was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023.
The body of Xi's statements on cultural work, formally named in October 2023, as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
Confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture, including traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It is counted among the Four-sphere Confidence.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, described by the Party as combining material and spiritual prosperity, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping since 2017 to describe the shifts in the global political and economic order that Chinese leaders see under way.

t: A review of Mao Zedong Thought research in Chinese academia in 2022
zh: 2022年度国内学界毛泽东思想研究述论
source: Mao Zedong Studies (《毛泽东研究》), 2023 no. 2
paras: This is a literature review of how Chinese scholars studied Mao Zedong Thought in 2022. Che Zongkai treats it as an important result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and as a continuing focus of attention. By the author's count, 2022 produced four substantial academic monographs, 1,094 journal articles with "Mao Zedong" as a keyword (297 in CSSCI or core journals), and 105 master's and doctoral theses.

The review is arranged by theme: the overall formation and development of the Thought; Mao's writings and their textual versions; political thought; philosophy; economic thought; cultural and educational thought; Mao's life and experiences; and studies of Zhou Enlai, Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yun and other first-generation leaders. It notes that research on Zhu De produced few high-quality results that year. A final section sets out priorities for further work.

Among the highlights, scholars read the three Party historical resolutions as texts that interpret Mao Zedong Thought, and link Mao's thought to Xi Jinping's writings on Mao. Work on the Yan'an Talks, in their 80th anniversary year, examines textual versions and Mao's literary and aesthetic ideas. Textual study of the revisions to Mao's essays and poems, and of his reading notes, is described as opening new materials. In economics, Meng Jie is reported as presenting Mao as a forerunner of institutional economics of socialism in contemporary China. Other scholars trace Mao's ideas on modernization and industrialization. Wu Xuan's survey of competing views on when the young Mao became a Marxist is summarised as arguing that this was a gradual process, not a single point.

Che proposes four directions: Mao Zedong Thought and the Party's theoretical innovation; its relation to Chinese modernization; study of Mao's writings and versions, including text-criticism methods and links to current problems; and the contributions of other leaders and Party theorists such as Hu Qiaomu, Ai Siqi and Zhang Ruxin. With the 130th anniversary of Mao's birth in 2023 approaching, Che calls for a comprehensive, historical and dialectical approach. Read the original if you want a bibliographic map of 2022 Chinese scholarship on Mao, with named authors and topics, or a sense of the research agenda officially encouraged for it.
quoteEn: Deepening research on the writings and versions of Mao Zedong Thought requires holistic thinking.
quoteZh: 深化毛泽东思想的著作及版本研究，需要具有整体性的思维

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, defined as the first major adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions. It was written into the Party constitution at the 7th Party Congress in 1945 and is treated as the collective achievement of the Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxism to China's conditions and to each era. Mao Zedong Thought is presented as its first major result.
Three Central Committee resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021) that give the Party's official assessment of its history, including Mao Zedong and his thought.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Accelerating the building of a leading education country with Chinese characteristics
zh: 加快建设中国特色社会主义教育强国
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2023, Zhang Donggang, identified as Party secretary of Renmin University of China, takes up Xi Jinping's formulation of what a 'leading education country' (jiaoyu qiangguo) with Chinese characteristics must be. Zhang argues that universities, as the 'leading edge' of this project, should grasp and apply each element of Xi's definition, and should treat building world-class universities and strong disciplines with Chinese characteristics as the top priority.

The article is organised around the components of Xi's statement, delivered at a Political Bureau study session: the fundamental guarantee, fundamental task, fundamental goal, important mission, basic path and core function, ending with the aim of education that satisfies the people. Each of the seven sections first explains why the element matters, citing Xi and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and then lists measures for universities.

Zhang's core claim is that the Party's overall leadership over education is the 'fixed anchor' of the whole undertaking, and that the other elements follow from it. Moral education (lide shuren) is presented as the basic task because every society trains people to meet its own political requirements. Talent cultivation serves the Party and the country and the second centenary goal. Education is also said to support Chinese modernization, which the article defines as the modernization of the whole population.

The measures proposed include the presidential responsibility system under Party committee leadership, ideological and political courses, a self-reliant Chinese system of knowledge in philosophy and social sciences, and cultivation of top innovative talent. They also include modernization of educational concepts, institutions and governance through digital transformation, international exchange, and fairer, higher-quality provision. Zhang concludes that the ultimate purpose is education 'satisfying to the people', which is meant to lay the foundation of national strength and popular well-being. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how a senior university Party official translates Xi Jinping's education directives into concrete institutional tasks.
quoteEn: Building a leading education country with Chinese characteristics must in the end be carried out in the teaching and educating process in schools, and moral education must be internalised in every sphere, aspect and link of school construction and management, with cultivating people at the core and building virtue as the foundation.
quoteZh: 建设中国特色社会主义教育强国，归根结底要落实到学校的教书育人过程中，必须把立德树人内化到学校建设和管理的各领域、各方面、各环节，做到以树人为核心，以立德为根本。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of making China a world leader in education, elaborated by Xi Jinping in 2023 and tied to national rejuvenation and modernization.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: building moral character and political commitment alongside knowledge, in line with the Party's educational guideline.
The official description of China's path to modernization, put forward by the Party at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Four preconditions for contemporary Marxist studies in China
zh: 当代中国马克思主义研究的四个前提性问题
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxist Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2023 no. 1
paras: Chen Xueming asks what must be settled before contemporary Marxist research in China can proceed on firm ground. The article argues that such research continues the history of Marxism and of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, so it must first reach a reasonably shared view of four major questions. Chen holds that vagueness on these questions would seriously impair further study.

The four preconditions are: how to understand the stages of Marx's own intellectual development; how to understand the development of Marxism after Marx and Engels died; how to understand the fierce struggles that accompanied Marxism's spread in China; and how to assess the competing interpretations of Marxism produced by Chinese scholars since reform and opening up. Each section sets out a typology of positions, then states what contemporary research should take from it.

Chen identifies three turning points in Marx's thought: from social democrat to communist in the mid-1840s; from historical idealism to historical materialism around 1850; and, in the late 1850s and early 1860s, the move to the critique of political economy, which gave the "two inevitables" a scientific basis beyond what the Communist Manifesto could offer. Only the Marx of this third stage, Chen argues, is the real founder of Marxism, so Capital should be read mainly as political economy and not as an ontological philosophy. Chen also distinguishes three post-Marx currents (Second International, Third International and so-called Western Marxism), three directions in China since the May Fourth Movement (cultural conservatism, wholesale Westernisation, socialism), and three readings since reform and opening up (Enlightenment-style, postmodern, and one centred on Marx's "two great discoveries"). Chen presents the first two readings as one-sided or mistaken, because their standpoints were superseded within Marx's own development.

Chen concludes that Chinese research should build theoretical innovation on the post-turning-point Marx, treat the Third International tradition as the main line to inherit while learning from the other two currents, prepare to debate the conservative and Westernising tendencies that persist, and adopt the third interpretive path as the mainstream. Chen also calls for continued study of how the three paths relate and where their limits lie. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how a Fudan Marxist philosopher defines orthodoxy, and what he rejects, in Chinese Marxist scholarship around 2023.
quoteEn: The critique of political economy is the core of Marx's thought; this is the most important theoretical legacy that Marx and Engels left us.
quoteZh: 政治经济学批判是马克思思想的核心，这是马克思、恩格斯留给我们最重要的理论遗产。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary issues. It is the framework within which Chen situates contemporary Marxist studies.
The tradition associated with Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School. Chen describes it as stressing philosophy, humanism and alienated labour.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in China from 1978. Chen uses it to periodise Chinese scholarly interpretations of Marxism.

The conclusion of Marx and Engels that capitalism will inevitably perish and socialism inevitably triumph. Chen says the Manifesto could treat it only as a scientific hypothesis until Capital supplied its economic basis.

t: Grasping the formation and development of the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics through the "big history" perspective
st: Analysis of key and difficult points in Chapter 5 of the 2023 edition of the textbook "Introduction to Mao Zedong Thought and the Theoretical System of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics"
zh: 以大历史观把握中国特色社会主义理论体系的形成发展
zhSub: 《毛泽东思想和中国特色社会主义理论体系概论（2023年版）》第五章重点难点问题解析
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 5
paras: This is a teaching-oriented guide to a newly added chapter of the 2023 revised university textbook on Mao Zedong Thought and the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Chapter 5 gives an overall account of the social and historical conditions in which that theoretical system formed and of its developmental stages. Wang argues that instructors should use a \"big history\" perspective, showing the unity of theoretical, historical and practical logic, so that students understand the system as a coherent whole.

The chapter links the earlier chapters on Mao Zedong Thought with the later chapters on Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. Wang organises the teaching points under four headings: the international background, the historical conditions, the practical basis, and the stages of development together with the system's historical standing. Each heading lists specific questions teachers should make clear.

On the international background, Wang stresses that peace and development became the theme of the age partly through Mao Zedong's opening of Sino-American normalisation and his \"three worlds\" strategy. Wang warns against the simplistic idea that changes in the world automatically produce theoretical innovation, and ties each leader's contribution to a particular international challenge. On historical conditions, Wang says the theory drew on lessons from the periods before and after 1978, which the author holds are not to be set against each other. It also rested on judgements about the primary stage of socialism and on a succession of \"questions of the times\". On the practical basis, Wang points to household contract responsibility, special economic zones and the socialist market economy. Wang also stresses continuity across generations and the claim that the masses' creativity is the source of theoretical innovation.

Wang concludes that the four component theories are \"of one lineage\" (yimai xiangcheng) and \"advance with the times\". In the author's account they share the same guiding sources, themes, qualities, basis in the primary stage of socialism, and goal of serving the people's fundamental interests. Teachers should also mark the key dates when propositions emerged and the theory matured. Wang presents the system as continuing and developing Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought, and as the guiding ideology the Party and state must uphold over the long term. Read the original if you teach or study the official framing of this textbook chapter and want to see how its key themes are meant to be taught.
quoteEn: One should avoid the simplistic misconception that changes in the international situation naturally bring about theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 要避免“国际形势变化自然带来理论创新”的简单化认识误区

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has promoted, urging that events be understood across long historical spans and in their world context. Here it serves as the organising approach for teaching the chapter.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义理论体系
glossary.en: theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official name for the body of Party theory comprising Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought. The Party treats it as its guiding ideology.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept emphasising people-centred, comprehensive, balanced and sustainable development.
The official judgement that China is in a long early phase of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces. It is used as the basis of Party lines and policies since 1978.

keywords: theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics

t: A historical examination of the mutual fit between Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture
zh: 马克思主义同中华优秀传统文化相互契合的历史考察
paras: Bu Xianqun takes up a formulation from Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development: that Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture have different origins but are highly compatible, and that only mutual fit allows organic integration. Writing in the Guangming Daily in June 2023, Bu argues that the Marxist encounter with Chinese tradition, and the opening of socialism with Chinese characteristics, were no accident. In the article's account they rest on historical, philosophical, cultural and social foundations.

The short commentary has three parts. The first presents "mutual fit" as a historical insight, in three respects: it explains why the two could be combined, it affirms traditional culture, and it deepens the historical roots of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second part treats the fit as a grasp of historical regularity. The third considers its value as a resource for theoretical and institutional innovation.

Bu's central argument is that the acceptance of Marxism in China was historically necessary and culturally prepared. Changes since the Ming and Qing dynasties are cited as background: sprouts of capitalism, a rising urban stratum, critiques of autocracy and the transformations after the Opium War. Bu holds that among the paths tried in modern China only socialism suited the people's aspirations and conditions. Bu also points to the openness of Chinese culture, which absorbed Confucianism, Buddhism and Neo-Confucianism, and lists elements said to echo historical materialism: the Five Phases and yin-yang as early dialectics, the unity of knowing and doing, the ideal of "all under heaven is public", and the people-based (minben) tradition.

Bu concludes with three requirements. Scholars should recognise the continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness of Chinese civilization. They should draw critically on historical governance experience, including unitary centralised rule, the bureaucracy, supervisory and remonstrance systems, merit-based selection and law combining virtue with punishment. They should also ground theory in the practice of the Chinese nation and turn Chinese experience into Chinese theory, in order to build a modern Chinese civilization and strengthen cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated historians present the Two Integrations and the continuity of Chinese civilization with Marxism.
quoteEn: Socialism with Chinese characteristics did not "fall from the sky"; it has "an incomparably deep historical heritage".
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义不是“从天上掉下来的”，而是“具有无比深厚的历史底蕴”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path, theory and system since reform and opening up, combining socialism with Chinese conditions.
Official formula: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021–23.
A slogan for confidence in China's cultural tradition, revolutionary culture and socialist culture, elevated in official discourse after 2012.
A strand of classical Chinese political thought holding that the people are the foundation of the state, often cited as echoing Marxist views on the masses.

t: Deeply understanding the value implications of the new form of human civilization
zh: 深刻认识人类文明新形态的价值意蕴
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2023, asks what theoretical value lies in the "new form of human civilization" that Xi Jinping links to Chinese modernization. Wang argues that it sums up the Party's century of struggle, carries forward the Marxist view of civilization, goes beyond Western civilizational theory and practice, and opens a new realm of scientific socialism.

The piece follows Xi's remarks at a study session on the 20th Party Congress (2022) and has three sections. The first traces how Party thinking on civilization developed from the reform era to the present. The second places the new form within Marx and Engels's critique of capitalist civilization. The third treats it as an advance for scientific socialism.

Wang says Chinese modernization promotes the coordinated development of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization. This is said to build on earlier formulas, from the "three civilizations" to the "five-sphere integrated plan". Wang reads Marx and Engels as showing that capitalist civilization is brilliant yet contradictory, driven by surplus-value and by a Western-centred, hegemonic logic of the "law of the jungle" and zero-sum games. Against this, Xi's call for mutual respect and learning among civilizations is presented as a basis for world peace. Under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, rural revitalization, poverty alleviation and ecological governance are cited as evidence of socialism's advantages.

Wang concludes that, facing great changes in the world, the era and history, China must firmly uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics and keep creating the new form of human civilization through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a short, official-style statement of how Chinese modernization is tied to the Marxist theory of civilization.
quoteEn: This shows that the coordinated advancement of the "five civilizations" is a very distinctive feature of the path of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 这表明，“五个文明”协调推进是中国式现代化道路一个非常鲜明的特点。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping, notably in 2021, to describe the civilization he says Chinese modernization creates, distinct from the Western model.
The official name for China's path to modernization, presented in Party documents as distinct from Western models; it was stressed at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The overall layout adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012), which advances economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development together.

t: Understanding the Chinese revolution from the standpoint of "Chinese modernization"
zh: 立足“中国式现代化”理解中国革命
source: Studies on the History of the Communist Party of China (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Following the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which put forward Chinese modernization, Qu Jun asks how the Chinese revolution should be understood from that standpoint. The author takes Xi Jinping's 2018 remark that the Party does not treat revolution and governing as two entirely different things as the starting point. Qu argues that modernization and revolution are interfused rather than opposed, and that the revolution is still continuing in a new-era form.

The article has three parts. The first criticises the older opposition between a "modernization view of history" and a "revolution view of history". The second describes the hopes and practice of the revolution led by the Communist Party. The third turns to how the "Chinese revolution" of the new era should be advanced, drawing on the 20th Party Congress report and Xi's speeches.

Qu first contends that separating modernization from revolution narrows the meaning of revolution. In the author's reading, a social revolution has a violent, overturning side and also a constructive and creative side. Reforms and popular enlightenment over the past century belong to it, so the revolution is part of Chinese modernization and a pivot of its key stages. Second, Qu says the Party's revolution combined three historical tasks: changing the state of the country, of the people and of Chinese civilization. It did so by taking the people as the centre, judging Chinese conditions independently, and combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Qu sets this against rival socialisms that remained bookish, imitative or confined to small circles. Third, the author says the new-era revolution is carried forward through the Party's self-reform, which "leads the social revolution". Qu names four requirements: continued adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, stronger basic institutions, a "great struggle" with many new historical features, and a firm belief that the Party remains a revolutionary party.

Qu concludes that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is "always on the road". Understanding the revolution through Chinese modernization is meant to sustain socialism with Chinese characteristics under Party leadership. The author warns against complacency over achievements. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Party historians now link revolutionary history to the Chinese modernization framework and to current Party-building.
quoteEn: Modernization and revolution are not in a dichotomous relation, still less in an oppositional one, but in a relation of mutual interfusion and convergence.
quoteZh: 现代化与革命不是二分关系，更不是对立关系，而是交融互汇的关系。

glossary.explanation: A concept highlighted in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It presents China's modernization as following a path distinct from Western models.
A Party formulation for continuous internal purification and improvement. Official texts present it as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official name for China's system and path since reform and opening up, described as Marxism applied to China's conditions.

t: The logic of a new type of international relations in the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路的新型国际关系逻辑
paras: Writing in 2023, as what official discourse calls changes unseen in a century accelerate, Ouyang Xiangying asks what logic underlies the new type of international relations that China advocates and how it serves Chinese modernization. The author argues that this new type of relations, whose core Xi Jinping first described in 2013 as win-win cooperation, ultimately points towards a community with a shared future for mankind. Since building such a community is, in Ouyang's account, an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, the new international relations must serve both.

The commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper, is organised around the three components named in the 19th Party Congress (2017) formula: mutual respect, fairness and justice, and win-win cooperation. Each section sets the Chinese approach against what the author presents as the outdated logic of some Western powers, especially the United States: bullying the weak, zero-sum games and plunder. The text draws on reports of the 19th and 20th Party Congresses, speeches by Xi Jinping, political philosophers such as Rawls and Habermas, and aid figures from a government white paper.

On mutual respect, Ouyang contends that equality among states, rooted in the Chinese idea of harmony in diversity, suits an era of networked, multipolar power better than hierarchy derived from Machiavellianism and social Darwinism. The author lists four channels for building the new relations: great-power ties, neighbourhood ties, ties with developing countries, and exchanges between political parties. On fairness and justice, Ouyang charges that US trade disputes, export controls, unilateral sanctions and rule-manipulation violate basic justice, while China, in the author's description, pursues peaceful development, pledges never to seek hegemony and promotes the Global Security Initiative. On cooperation, the author blames dollar hegemony and US interest-rate policy for instability in developing countries, and contrasts this with the Belt and Road Initiative and Chinese aid. The author cites 270.2 billion yuan of foreign aid in 2013–2018, 47.3 per cent of it grants, given without political conditions.

Ouyang concludes that China, as a builder of peace, contributor to global development, defender of the international order and provider of public goods, will advance under Party leadership and win new victories on the path of Chinese modernization. The Global Development Initiative is presented as a call to build a community of shared development. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a CASS researcher frames China's diplomatic principles and sets them against US conduct.
quoteEn: Mutual respect accords better with modern civilizational thinking than bullying the weak.
quoteZh: 相互尊重比恃强凌弱更符合现代文明思维

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first presented in a March 2013 speech in Moscow, centred on win-win cooperation. The 19th Party Congress formulated it as mutual respect, fairness and justice, and win-win cooperation.
