t: A Marxist text offering a preliminary systematic exposition of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 对新时代坚持和发展中国特色社会主义初步系统阐述的马克思主义文献
paras: Writing ten years after Xi Jinping's speech of 5 January 2013 (the "1.5 speech"), delivered to newly elected Central Committee members after the 18th Party Congress (2012), Zhu Jiamu asks what place the speech holds in the new era. Zhu argues that it is an important Marxist document, the opening work of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era and the foundation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In Zhu's reading, it is the first written answer the Party leadership gave "to history and to the people".

The article sets the speech against the background of problems the 20th Party Congress (2022) report said existed a decade earlier, including wavering faith, formalism and historical nihilism. It then works through seven themes: that socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism and not another "ism"; that modernization must start from China's conditions; the unity of the periods before and after reform and opening up; the aim of historical nihilism; the deepening of understanding of socialism; communist ideals; and long-term cooperation and struggle between socialism and capitalism. For each, Zhu traces how Xi's later statements and policies developed the speech's points.

Zhu's central moves are, first, to read the speech as a response to a "bourgeois liberalization" current since the 1980s. The speech's insistence that the basic principles of scientific socialism cannot be abandoned is taken to mean that reform has a fixed direction and that some things must not be changed. Second, Zhu holds that the two historical periods are essentially one exploration of socialist construction. Third, Zhu argues that historical nihilism is a political project to incite the overthrow of Party leadership, citing the Soviet collapse as a warning. Zhu also draws the speech's later lineage: Chinese modernization, the Four-sphere Confidence, and the division of the primary stage of socialism into sub-stages such as the new development stage.

Zhu concludes that the speech is the upstream source of Xi Jinping Thought. Zhu presents ideological and political security, firm communist ideals, and long-term cooperation and struggle with capitalist states as continuing tasks. Zhu also calls on historians of the PRC to take up a "defend the country" function and to resist historical nihilism. Read the original if you want a Party-aligned account of how the 2013 speech is retrospectively framed as the origin of core themes in Xi-era ideology.
quoteEn: When Xi Jinping stressed in the \"1.5 speech\" that socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism and that the basic principles of scientific socialism must not be lost, this was the background he faced.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记在“1·5”讲话中强调中国特色社会主义是社会主义、科学社会主义的基本原则不能丢，面对的就是这个背景。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path of socialism since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a market economy and public ownership as the mainstay.
The official judgement, formalised in 1981 and 1987, that China will remain for a long historical period in an underdeveloped initial phase of socialism.
The official concept of China's own modernization path, set against Western capitalist modernization and elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, formulated by Xi Jinping between 2012 and 2016.
In official discourse, a label for views that negate the Party's revolutionary and socialist history, which the Party treats as a political danger.

t: The common values of all humanity embedded in the new form of human civilization, and their contemporary significance
zh: 人类文明新形态内蕴的全人类共同价值及其当代意义
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 4
paras: Wang Yuchen and Peng Yiwei ask how the new form of human civilization created by Chinese modernization relates to the common values of all humanity. They argue that this civilization unites the core socialist values, which are specific to China, with the common values of all humanity, which they treat as a universal ideal. The article, published in 2023, frames the relationship through two dialectical pairs: universality and particularity, and the reality of civilizational development versus its ideal aims.

The article has three sections. The first presents the new form of human civilization as a unity of the core socialist values and the common values of all humanity, drawing on a typology of 'early-developing endogenous' and 'late-developing exogenous' modernization and on Marx and Engels's account of capitalist civilization. The second treats the common values themselves, and sets them against the core socialist values and against the actual civilization. The third sets out their historical significance. It traces the core socialist values through successive Party leaders, from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping.

The authors contend that so-called 'universal values' rest on theories of civilizational superiority, clash and end, and absolutise the Western model as the only one. Their account is that the common values (peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom) rest instead on civilizational equality and mutual learning, and take different forms in each country according to its history and interests. The core socialist values apply only to China and are described as the 'greatest common divisor' of its people. The common values are the minimum requirement of the socialist ones and are the greatest common divisor among nations. The new civilization is already real, while the common values are still mainly an aspiration. Wang and Peng say that building a community with a shared future for mankind is what can bridge the two.

Wang and Peng conclude that the common values express the Party's people-centred orientation and its sense of responsibility for humanity. They say the 'Chinese approach' answers the questions of the world, the people and the times raised by the great changes unseen in a century. They also say it resolves the relationship between diversity and unity in civilization, and guides the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. They add that China does not export its model, and that its appeal depends on further enriching the new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese account of how the common values of all humanity are distinguished from 'universal values' and tied to the core socialist values.
quoteEn: The core socialist values are the concrete embodiment and means of realisation of the common values of all humanity under contemporary China's historical conditions and cultural traditions, and the two stand in a dialectical unity of advancedness and breadth, of universality and particularity.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观是全人类共同价值在当代中国历史条件与文化传统下的具体体现和实现途径，二者的关系是先进性与广泛性、普遍性与特殊性的辩证统一关系。

glossary.explanation: An official formulation, used by Xi Jinping from 2021, for the socialist civilization said to be created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as surpassing both capitalist civilization and the Soviet model.

A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2015 and developed later, naming peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Chinese officials present it as an alternative to Western 'universal values'.

A 24-character set of values announced at the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels: prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony; freedom, equality, justice, rule of law; patriotism, dedication, integrity, friendship.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since 2012–13, stressing cooperation, multilateralism and shared interests among states.
The official term for China's path to modernity under Party leadership. It is said to be distinguished by features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping uses for the current global shifts in power and the international order, often cited as the context for Chinese foreign policy.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The formation of the path of Chinese modernization: historical review and practical expansion
zh: 中国式现代化道路的成型：历史审视和现实拓展
paras: Qi Weiping takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's account of Chinese modernization as the product of long exploration since 1949, and argues that the Congress's full exposition of the theory marks the path's maturation and formation. Qi holds that this path emerged through setbacks, costs and trials, and is presented as the only correct road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Looking at its history, the article says, shows how hard-won the result is and strengthens the resolve to broaden and deepen it.

The article follows the three time markers in the Congress report: the founding of the People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). After a brief look at modernization as a goal since the Opium War, it moves through four sections: laying the foundation with the "four modernizations"; opening the path with the "moderately prosperous society" concept; the theoretical and practical breakthroughs of the new era; and six requirements for the next stage.

Qi's central argument is that each stage built on the last. The pre-1978 period is credited with setting a socialist direction distinct from Western modernization, building an industrial base and producing theoretical groundwork, despite detours caused by copying the Soviet model and the Cultural Revolution. Deng Xiaoping's idea of a moderately prosperous society, which he distinguished from Western models and pitched at a realistic level, became the programme that carried modernization forward until it was declared achieved in 2021. Since 2012, Qi says, the Party has summed up the features, essential requirements and major principles of Chinese modernization, so that a preliminary theoretical system now exists. Qi claims this offers a new option for other countries and breaks Western discursive dominance over modernization theory.

For the future, Qi calls for adherence to Party leadership, full application of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, political clarity, use of the Party's historical experience to build unity, a fighting spirit against external risks, and the Party's self-reform. Qi concludes that cherishing and extending the achievement is the Party's sacred mission. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account that periodises the path of Chinese modernization from the four modernizations to the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The strategic conception of building a moderately prosperous society became the programme of action for advancing Chinese-style modernization since reform and opening up.
quoteZh: 建设小康社会的战略构想成为改革开放以来推进中国式现代化的行动纲领。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for China's own path to modernization, which it contrasts with Western models. Deng Xiaoping used a similar phrase in 1979, and the 20th Party Congress set out the theory in full in 2022.
A Confucian-derived term for a modestly well-off society. Deng Xiaoping adopted it in 1979 as a realistic modernization goal, and Xi Jinping declared it fully achieved in 2021.
The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology. It was set out in the 1960s and revived by Deng Xiaoping after 1976.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation' that began with the Opium War.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The Party's term for its efforts to discipline and renew itself, including anti-corruption work.

t: Understanding the threefold logic of common prosperity
zh: 深刻理解和领悟共同富裕的三重逻辑
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which called for steadily advancing common prosperity and described Chinese modernization as a modernization of common prosperity for all the people, Zhou Wen and Tang Jiaocheng ask what laws and logic govern common prosperity. They argue that it should be examined along three dimensions: theory, history and practice. Their thesis is that common prosperity is the organic unity of a theoretical, a historical and a practical logic.

The article is divided into four parts: three analytical sections, one for each logic, and a short conclusion. The theoretical section draws on Marx's Capital and Critique of the Gotha Programme. The historical section runs from the founding of the People's Republic through reform and opening up to the new era after 2012. The practical section covers Party leadership, the market system, the public and non-public sectors, and the distribution system.

The theoretical logic, in the authors' account, is a "labour logic". Labour is the source of wealth, and distribution according to labour, which they argue fits the primary stage of socialism with public ownership as the main body, motivates workers and promotes fairness and shared wealth. They treat common prosperity as the counterpart of the liberation of labour, with capital logic replaced by labour logic. Historically, they trace a sequence: socialist political and economic institutions as the institutional base, the path of "some getting rich first" as the productive-forces base, and poverty alleviation and a moderately prosperous society as an improvement in relations of production. In practice they call for centralised, unified Party leadership of economic work, a high-standard socialist market economy combining an "effective market" with an "effective government", and the Two Unwaverings to "make the cake bigger". They also call for coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution to "divide the cake well", and note remaining gaps between urban and rural areas, regions and industries.

The authors conclude that common prosperity must run through the whole process of Chinese modernization. This means coordinating productive forces and relations of production, advancing high-quality development, and refining the theory through the cycle of practice and understanding. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese political-economy account of common prosperity, with its framing in labour theory, Party history and policy measures, and its use of the 20th Congress language.
quoteEn: The logic of common prosperity unfolds through labour, not capital. Socialist society is governed by the logic of labour, which is essentially a human logic: everything that is a thing under capital logic becomes human under labour logic.
quoteZh: 共同富裕的逻辑展开是劳动而非资本，社会主义社会由劳动逻辑主导，本质上就是人的逻辑，即资本逻辑下一切物的东西，在劳动逻辑下都变为人的东西。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing goal of Chinese socialism, stressed again under Xi Jinping since 2021. It means prosperity shared by all, as opposed to wealth concentrated in a few hands.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.
The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

A principle drawn from Marx's account of the first phase of communist society, in which individuals receive consumer goods in proportion to the labour they contribute. In China it is the main body of income distribution alongside other methods.

glossary.pinyin: xiān fù – hòu fù – gòng fù
glossary.literal: first rich – later rich – common prosperity
glossary.explanation: Deng Xiaoping's reform-era formula that some people and regions may prosper first and then help others, leading to common prosperity.

A formula for the relationship between market and state in China's socialist market economy. The market is meant to allocate resources efficiently and the government to intervene constructively where needed.

t: How Chinese modernization has successfully avoided the "modernization traps"
zh: 论中国式现代化对“现代化陷阱”的成功规避
paras: Wu Zhongmin asks why Chinese modernization has succeeded since reform and opening up, and answers that a major reason is its success in avoiding "modernization traps". Wu defines these as relatively hard problems or predicaments that any country meets in modernizing, and argues that a country's success depends largely on whether it can avoid sinking into them.

The article lists several traps, including dependency, capital supremacy, economic transition, growth, de-industrialization, the "Tacitus trap" and excessive wealth gaps. It then examines five that Wu regards as most important, each tied to one dimension of modernization: dependency (national autonomy), de-industrialization (material economic base), capital supremacy (economic institutions), excessive welfare (social protection) and social turmoil (safe social functioning). For each, Wu cites cases such as Latin America, Africa, Japan after the Plaza Accord, Brazil and the Philippines, then sets out China's practice.

Wu's central contrast is between countries that lost autonomy, hollowed out their industry, let capital or welfare logic run unchecked, or tolerated corrupt public power, and China. Wu credits China with combining self-reliance with openness through the "dual circulation" pattern, keeping a complete industrial system and curbing financial and property bubbles. Wu also credits China with improving livelihoods and regulating the market against capital supremacy, and with tying social spending to economic capacity. For stability, Wu points to prioritising economic growth, livelihood improvement and an anti-corruption campaign backed by Party rules and laws. Xi Jinping, Deng Xiaoping and Mao Zedong are cited throughout as guidance.

Wu concludes that the five traps can interlock and compound if left unchecked, and that Chinese modernization has so far avoided them only in a staged, not permanent, way. Risks of old traps returning and of new kinds of traps remain, and the second centenary goal depends on continued avoidance. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's systematic account of how mainstream Chinese theory frames development pitfalls, with comparative cases and policy data.
quoteEn: In a sense, the success of a country's modernization lies in its success in avoiding these modernization traps, especially the important ones.
quoteZh: 从一定意义上讲，一个国家现代化建设的成功就在于该国对于这些现代化陷阱特别是重要的现代化陷阱的成功规避。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A development pattern promoted from 2020 with the domestic cycle as the mainstay and domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A term for the loss of public trust in authorities: once a government loses credibility, whatever it says or does is distrusted. It is named after the Roman historian Tacitus.
The official aim of building a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Striving to write a new chapter of high-quality development in the old revolutionary areas
zh: 奋力谱写革命老区高质量发展新篇章
paras: Writing in 2023 in Red Flag Manuscripts, Cai Songtao, the Party secretary of Xinyang in Henan, takes up how the Dabie Mountains, an old revolutionary area, can achieve high-quality development. Citing the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and Xi Jinping's remarks during his inspection of Jiangxi, Cai argues that the area should set an example in accelerating such development and compete for the lead in the rise of the central region. The article holds that this is a requirement for improving the lives of people in old revolutionary areas.

The piece is a policy-oriented commentary in three parts. The first concerns upholding a people-centred approach to development. The second concerns raising the quality and efficiency of growth. The third concerns seizing opportunities and making full use of national policy. It is linked throughout to the Party's thematic education campaign and to the Dabie Mountains' revolutionary history.

On the people-centred approach, Cai presents the aim of making old revolutionary areas "better" and the lives of their people "better" as the starting and end point of revitalisation. Cai calls for stronger public services and social security, and for consolidating poverty-alleviation gains through "precise" identification, assistance and management to prevent a return to poverty. On growth quality, Cai argues for ecology-first green development, the faster replacement of old growth drivers with new ones through technological innovation, talent and green finance, and a better business environment through streamlined administrative services and "clean and amicable" government–business relations.

In the third part, Cai calls on the area to use the 2021 State Council opinions on supporting the revitalisation of old revolutionary areas, together with special bonds and major projects. Cai also urges it to play to local strengths, including red culture and ecological assets, and to turn its status as a latecomer region into an advantage, since it has fewer burdens from legacy industries and more room for emerging ones. The author concludes that the area must carry forward its revolutionary heritage and strive to be first in regional competition. Read the original if you want an example of how a local Party leader translates national high-quality development and common prosperity language into a programme for a former revolutionary base.
quoteEn: The ecological environment is the greatest wealth, the greatest advantage and the greatest brand of the old revolutionary areas.
quoteZh: 生态环境是革命老区的最大财富、最大优势、最大品牌。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, stressed since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that favours quality, efficiency, innovation and green growth over speed of expansion alone.

Regions that served as bases of the Communist-led revolution before 1949, such as the Dabie Mountains. They receive special policy support, and their history is part of the Party's legitimating narrative.
A stated goal of socialism in China, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by a few. It has been given heightened emphasis in policy since 2021.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A principle in Xi Jinping's thought holding that development should be aimed at improving the people's wellbeing and should be shared by them.

t: Chinese modernization in the light of modern Chinese history
zh: 从近代历史进程看中国式现代化
paras: Guo Ruoping asks how Chinese modernization, set by the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the Party's mission for the new era, should be understood against more than a century of modern Chinese history. The article argues that every modernization plan since the mid-nineteenth century was conditioned by the principal contradiction of Chinese society at the time. Only by tracing those contradictions, Guo holds, can one grasp what is distinctive and epoch-making about Chinese modernization.

The article moves through three periods. The first covers the late Qing quest for "self-strengthening", in its Westernisation-movement, reform-movement and constitutional phases. The second covers modernization thinking in the revolutionary years under the Communist Party, from 1921 to the eve of 1949. The third covers the People's Republic: the Four Modernizations, reform and opening up, and the formulation of Chinese modernization after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Guo's central move is to read each period through Mao Zedong's analysis of principal contradictions. The late Qing efforts are described as limited reforms led by the court and some elites, meant to preserve dynastic rule, and so unable to resolve the conflict between imperialism and the Chinese nation. The Communist Party is presented as changing the political subject that could resolve that conflict. Its early programmes on industrialization, its debates with agrarian conservatives, and Mao's vision of a New China in 1945 are treated as the first conceptions of socialist modernization. After 1949, Guo traces how redefinitions of the principal contradiction (1956, 1981, 2017) tied the goals of modernization to the Eighth Party Congress, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the 19th Party Congress (2017). Deng Xiaoping's 1979 phrase "Chinese-style modernization" is cited as the origin of the concept, which Guo says the 20th Party Congress expanded into five features and an integrated, system-wide strategy.

Guo concludes that Chinese modernization rejects "Westernization" and one-way "integration with international norms", and pursues an autonomous socialist path. It is described as comprehensive, covering the economy, national governance, ecology, people's livelihoods and national security. Guo also presents it as a new option for countries that want development while keeping their independence, and as creating a "new form of human civilization". Read the original if you want a historian's account that places Chinese modernization in a long line of modern Chinese modernization projects, organised by the changing principal contradiction.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization discards the \"Westernization\" model long fixed in people's minds, goes beyond one-directional \"docking\" thinking, and consciously upholds the autonomy of the socialist path of modernization.
quoteZh: “中国式现代化”摈弃了长久以来人们观念中凝固的“西化”模式，超越了单向度的“接轨”思维，高度自觉地坚持社会主义现代化道路的自主性

glossary.explanation: A Party concept that Deng Xiaoping used in 1979 and Xi Jinping elevated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as a socialist path to modernization that differs from the Western model.

A concept from Mao Zedong's analysis of contradictions. It names the central social conflict that shapes a period and guides Party policy. The Party has redefined it several times, most recently in 2017.

The goal of modernizing industry, agriculture, national defence, and science and technology. Zhou Enlai announced it in 1954 and elaborated it in 1964, and it became a core aim of the Party and state.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Several questions on comprehensively advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization
zh: 以中国式现代化全面推进中华民族伟大复兴的几个问题
source: Research on Marxist Theory Education in Colleges and Universities, 2023 no. 2
paras: Sun Tanghou takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) formula that the Party's central task is to "comprehensively advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization". Sun argues that the formula gives Chinese modernization a distinct strategic position and a direct causal link to national rejuvenation. Understanding its "reasoning, theory and philosophy" is said to be essential for grasping the Congress's strategic plans. The article, published in 2023, is a study-oriented exposition of that formula.

The article has four parts. The first sets out four "logics" behind the formula: political, historical, theoretical and practical. The second traces the origins of Chinese modernization from Mao Zedong's 1945 remarks and the "four modernizations" through Deng Xiaoping's "Chinese-style modernization" to Xi Jinping's 2020 formulation, then lists its five features and nine essential requirements. The third covers the overall goals for 2035 and the mid-century, and the "two-step" strategic arrangement. The fourth examines the new strategic situation, the major principles and nine practical routes.

Sun argues that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Party, and that this defines its nature and direction. Drawing on the Two Establishes, Sun treats the Party's leadership as the decisive guarantee. Sun distinguishes Chinese modernization from what the article calls Western modernization, which it describes as driven by capital, materialist, human-centred in its ecology and tied to colonial plunder. At the same time Sun holds that it shares common features and general laws of modernization, such as industrialization, urbanization and market allocation. Methodologically, Sun draws four lessons: autonomy, innovation, diversity and inclusiveness. Sun also describes a hostile external environment, attributing it to the United States and the West, and calls for a spirit of struggle.

Sun concludes that Chinese modernization is the only correct path to national rejuvenation. Success is said to depend on five principles: the Party's overall leadership, the socialist path, a people-centred approach, deepening reform and opening up, and the spirit of struggle. Sun lists nine practical tasks, including high-quality development, whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity, green development, national security, a community with a shared future for mankind and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned survey of how Chinese academics systematise the 20th Congress's modernization theory.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is the only correct path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and a major achievement the Party and people won through immense hardship and at great cost.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，是实现中华民族伟大复兴唯一正确的道路，是党和人民历经千辛万苦、付出巨大代价取得的重大成果。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of socialist modernization under Party leadership. Xi Jinping first presented it as a standalone concept in 2020, and the 20th Party Congress elaborated it.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China to a leading place in the world after the decline of the modern era.
A 2021 Party formula affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Official term, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, for China's democratic model, said to cover every stage of political and social decision-making.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared interests and joint global governance.
Official economic goal that emphasises quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Xi-era slogan for strict Party discipline, anti-corruption work and organisational reform.

t: Upholding fundamentals and breaking new ground: the internal logic and basic guideline of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 守正创新：马克思主义中国化时代化的内在逻辑和根本遵循
source: Journal of Anhui Normal University (Humanities and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 3
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhang Zhengguang asks why Marxism keeps its vitality and how the Communist Party of China has advanced the process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The answer, in the article, is the paired principle of "upholding fundamentals and breaking new ground" (shouzheng chuangxin): holding to Marxism's basic principles, stance and method while innovating in step with practice. Zhang presents this as both Marxism's "secret code" of renewal and the internal logic of its Sinicization.

The article has three sections. The first traces the principle through the history of Marxism, from Marx's early development and the revisions to the Communist Manifesto to Engels and Lenin. The second reads the Party's century as a history of the same principle, moving through the new-democratic revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to the Two Integrations as the present path, and to how the two integrations relate to each other.

Zhang argues that social-science theory is a dialectical unity of absolute and relative truth and must stay open to practice. On this reading, Marx and Engels never treated their theory as final, and they developed it through involvement in working-class struggle and through polemics against rival currents. Zhang rejects Bernstein's view, echoed by some Western Marxist scholars, that such development amounts to "revisionism", and says it confuses theoretical innovation with abandoning fundamentals. In the Chinese case, Zhang names successive theoretical results: Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Each, the article says, held to basic principles while responding to new conditions.

Zhang concludes that integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture is the fundamental route by which Marxism stays vital. The two integrations are said to be equally important: without the first, theory becomes rigid and rootless, and without the second it loses its "roots and soul". The article also holds that the present era is still the historical epoch Marxism identified, so Marxism is not outdated. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese academic account of how the Party's theory frames Sinicization as continuity plus innovation, with its historical narrative and its response to the "revisionism" charge.
quoteEn: \"Upholding fundamentals\" means always holding unwaveringly to the basic principles of Marxism and to its stance, viewpoint and method.
quoteZh: 所谓“守正”，就是始终坚持马克思主义基本原理不动摇，坚持马克思主义立场观点方法不动摇。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the older formula of integration with Chinese realities and is associated with Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxist theory in response to Chinese conditions and contemporary issues. "Sinicization of Marxism" was first put forward by Mao Zedong in 1938; "of our times" was added in recent Party documents.

glossary.en: upholding fundamentals and breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keep to the correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A slogan of continuity and innovation: hold to Marxism's basic principles while developing theory in response to new practice.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the latest stage in the Sinicization of Marxism.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义理论体系
glossary.explanation: Listed here as one of the Party's theoretical results after Deng Xiaoping Theory and the Three Represents. It was put forward under Hu Jintao and stresses people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.

keywords: upholding fundamentals and breaking new ground

t: The theoretical system of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的理论体系
paras: Xiang Jiuyu takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the 20th Party Congress (2022) that Chinese modernization has become a preliminary, relatively stable theoretical form, and asks what that theoretical system consists of. The article argues that Chinese modernization is a new body of theory: it rests on a distinct philosophical foundation, breaks with existing modernization narratives and has a definite core and distinctive features. Xiang presents grasping it as a key to understanding the changes of the new era and to building China's independent knowledge system.

The article is organised in four parts. The first sets out the conceptual foundations, the second the historical change the theory represents, the third its theoretical "hard core", and the fourth its distinctive traits. Along the way Xiang engages Francis Fukuyama's "end of history" thesis and Western-centrism, and cites Marx, Engels, Deng Xiaoping and Xi.

On foundations, Xiang argues that the theory goes beyond Fukuyama's thesis through historical materialism, combining the general necessity of modernization with China's particularity. It rejects the equation of modernization with Westernization and takes a people-centred stance as its value core. The change it brings is described as a "revolution in terminology" (concepts such as high-quality development, whole-process people's democracy and a community with a shared future for mankind), a shift of research paradigm, and an original theoretical narrative. The hard core has five parts: leadership by the Communist Party, socialist institutional character, Chinese characteristics, the nine essential requirements and distinctive advantages in material production, state governance and social development. Xiang ranks the advantage in material production as fundamental.

Xiang concludes that the system is shaped by three unities. These are the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, the fine traditional Chinese culture, and socialist modernization. In this reading it enriches socialist modernization theory, applies scientific socialism to China's conditions, and is still developing. Xiang also claims that it breaks the West's monopoly on modernization theory and offers guidance to other developing countries. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars map the structure and sources of the theory of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization" and shown another picture of modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，打破了‘现代化=西方化’的迷思，展现了现代化的另一幅图景

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, aimed at national rejuvenation, and as an alternative to Western models.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from around 2019. It describes China's democracy as covering every stage of decision-making, not just elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing cooperation, peaceful development and shared security.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours innovation, efficiency and balance over growth in speed or volume alone.

t: Winning the cyber ideological struggle of the new era with a spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以历史主动精神打赢新时代网络意识形态斗争
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2023, Wang Yonggui asks how the Party can win the ideological struggle in cyberspace, which the article treats as a main arena for clashing ideas and a key area of political and ideological security. The answer is to apply the "spirit of historical initiative" that Xi Jinping has stressed since the new era began. Wang argues that this spirit combines respect for objective laws, readiness to seize opportunities and a talent for summing up experience. It operates at three levels: cognitive, practical and methodological.

The article follows these three levels in three parts. The first part analyses the risks of the online environment, to build "cognitive consciousness". The second part sets out opportunities and supports for action, to build "practical consciousness". The third part draws on the experience of the new era to supply methods, for "methodological consciousness". Wang supports the argument throughout with quotations from Xi Jinping's speeches, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and a small number of scholarly sources.

Wang identifies four features that make the online struggle harder. Open, free cyberspace weakens the old propaganda-based model and makes anonymous attacks hard to trace. A multiplicity of online actors blurs the line between ordinary users and hostile forces. Entertainment content can carry historical nihilism and other "erroneous trends", and can feed capital's collusion with technology. Algorithmic "information cocoons" and closed communities undermine a common value base. Wang then proposes five supports: a new view of cybersecurity that is scientific, holistic, dynamic and coordinated; cultural supports, including the guiding position of Marxism; talent; infrastructure; and rule by law. The article's methods are fought as four campaigns: positional, public opinion, hearts-and-minds, and technology.

Wang concludes that experience of the new era should be turned into method so that the Party keeps the initiative in cyberspace. Concrete proposals include promoting "positive energy" and expanding the "red zone" against "grey" and "black" zones. Officials are to take the mass line online and answer public opinion crises quickly while resolving the real-world problems behind them. Wang also calls for breakthroughs in core technologies and for China to gain a voice in international rule-making. Read the original if you want a systematic example of how Chinese Party-theory scholarship frames online ideological security and the policy measures it ties to it.
quoteEn: To win the cyber ideological struggle, we should fully seize and make effective use of this strategic opportunity, plan the ideological struggle systematically on the basis of the strategy of building a cyber power, use the building of a cyber power to innovate governance methods, and build a firm barrier for cyber ideological security.
quoteZh: 打赢网络意识形态斗争，应当充分捕捉和有效利用这一战略机遇，依托网络强国战略系统谋划意识形态斗争，以建设网络强国为契机推进治理方式的创新，筑牢网络意识形态安全屏障。

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has used since the new era began to urge the Party to act proactively, seize opportunities and follow historical laws rather than react to events.
The idea that a state's dominant ideology must be protected from hostile ideas as part of national security. It is a prominent theme in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
In Party usage, a label for views that question or reject the official account of Chinese revolutionary and socialist history.
A term for the narrowing of users' information exposure by personalised algorithmic recommendation. It is borrowed from the 'echo chamber' and 'filter bubble' debate.
A long-standing Party method of work that stresses going among the people, listening to them and then acting on their demands.

t: Chinese modernization and common prosperity
zh: 中国式现代化与共同富裕
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 4
paras: Han Xiping and Wang Siran ask how common prosperity relates to Chinese modernization and how it can be achieved. They argue that, unlike capitalist modernization, which they say produces polarisation between rich and poor, Chinese modernization takes common prosperity as its essential requirement and basic feature. The article draws on the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and on Xi Jinping's statements on the subject.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why common prosperity is a defining feature of Chinese modernization, in four respects: socialism's essence, China's cultural heritage, the Communist Party's historical goals, and a claimed new form of human civilisation. The second lays out strategic steps by stage: the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, 2020 to 2035, and 2035 to the middle of the century. The third proposes three sets of measures: high-quality development, a better distribution system, and a fuller social security system.

On theory, the authors cite Marx, Engels and Deng Xiaoping to place common prosperity at the heart of socialism. They also trace it through Chinese ideals such as "great harmony" and a moderately prosperous society, and through the Party's record from land reform to poverty alleviation. They hold that Chinese modernization breaks with "Western centrism" and the "end of history" thesis, because it rests on public ownership as the mainstay with several forms of ownership developing together. On policy, they stress that common prosperity does not mean equal or simultaneous wealth. They call for innovation-driven growth, rural revitalisation and coordinated regional development, and for coordinating primary distribution, redistribution and the "third distribution" (charity). They also warn against "welfarism", which they say only adjusts capitalist relations and cannot alter the basic divide between bourgeoisie and proletariat.

The authors conclude that common prosperity is a long-term, gradual process that cannot be rushed. They propose milestones such as an olive-shaped income distribution, equalised basic public services and a Gini coefficient below 0.3. They present Chinese modernization as offering developing countries a new option for balancing efficiency and fairness. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how official discourse links common prosperity to Chinese modernization, with the staged targets and policy tools it cites.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization with common prosperity has broken the \"Western-centric theory\", ended the \"end of history thesis\" and overcome the inherent defects of capitalist modernization.
quoteZh: 共同富裕的中国式现代化打破了“西方中心论”，终结了“历史终结论”，克服了资本主义现代化的固有弊端

glossary.explanation: A Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path to modernization. Official texts say it features common prosperity, a huge population and material and cultural-ethical advancement.
A goal of shared affluence for all, which official texts call an essential requirement of socialism. It was stressed by Deng Xiaoping and given new prominence under Xi Jinping.
The official economic orientation that puts quality and efficiency ahead of growth speed. It was formally adopted as a priority in 2017.
Income redistribution through voluntary charity and donations, in addition to market-based primary distribution and state-led redistribution via tax and transfers.
The goal of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, declared achieved by the Party in 2021. The word xiaokang also appears in classical Chinese texts.

t: Mao Zedong's historical contribution to China's modernization drive
zh: 毛泽东对中国现代化事业的历史贡献
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 4
paras: Marking the 130th anniversary of Mao Zedong's birth in 2023, Zhu Siyuan asks what Mao contributed to China's modernization and why it matters for Chinese modernization today. The article argues that Mao made pioneering and decisive contributions: he created the social conditions, the political and institutional premise, the material base and the theoretical foundation on which later modernization rests.

The article is organised in four parts that follow Mao's career. They cover the victory of the new-democratic revolution, the socialist transformation and the founding of the basic socialist system, socialist construction from 1953 to 1978, and Mao's strategic thinking on modernization. Throughout, Zhu argues against what the author calls historical nihilism, including the view that Mao understood only revolution and class struggle and neglected construction.

In the first two parts, Zhu argues that independence, unification and liberation were preconditions for a modernization that is neither Western nor dependent on the West. The author uses historical materialism, and Engels's critique of economic determinism, to reject the idea that revolution delayed modernization. Zhu also rejects the view, which the author labels a 'productive forces first' position, that China should have consolidated new democracy for a long period. In Zhu's account Mao, Liu Shaoqi and Zhou Enlai held that new democracy was a transitional form that had to move toward socialism, so the socialist transformation completed in 1956 secured the political premise for modernization. The third part cites GDP and industrial output growth figures for 1949–1978, a quotation from the historian Maurice Meisner, and the creation of an independent and relatively complete industrial system. Zhu concedes setbacks and errors but says they cannot erase these achievements. The fourth part credits Mao with drawing lessons from the Soviet model and calling for the 'Second Integration' of Marxism with Chinese realities. Zhu also credits him with the 'Four Modernizations', the 'two-step' strategy, the principle of overall balance, and the theory of contradictions among the people.

Zhu concludes that reform-era achievements were built on the basic system and the material foundation of the Mao period. The author presents Deng Xiaoping's 'three-step' strategy and Xi Jinping's new 'two-step' strategy as continuations of Mao's staged approach. Mao's ideas are said to remain a guide for building a modern socialist country and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a representative statement of the official Chinese case for continuity between the Mao era and later modernization, set against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: The new-democratic revolution was not a delay to China's modernization; on the contrary, it set China's modernization on the fastest and most reliable path.
quoteZh: 新民主主义革命不仅不是对中国现代化事业的拖延，相反，它使中国的现代化沿着最快速最可靠的道路前进。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a socialist modernization path with Chinese characteristics, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article presents Mao's work as one of its foundations.
In official Chinese usage, a label for interpretations that downplay or negate the Party's revolutionary history and leaders. Here it is applied to critics of Mao and of the revolution.

Mao's theory of the stage of the Chinese revolution led by the Communist Party before socialism, directed against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism. It is dated 1919–1949 in official historiography.
The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology. The article traces its development from 1954 to 1975.
Mao's call in the 1950s to combine Marxism-Leninism's basic principles with Chinese realities in socialist construction, after drawing lessons from the Soviet model.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and tied to the second centenary goal of 2049.

t: The historical logic of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
st: "New judgements, new interpretations" written discussion, part 1
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化的历史逻辑
zhSub: “新论断·新阐释”笔谈（一）
paras: Taking its cue from the 20th Party Congress report (2022), which says that what works is Marxism "adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times", Sun Daiyao asks what historical and theoretical logic underlies this process. The article argues that localisation and contemporisation are inherent requirements of Marxism as an open, developing theory. In Sun's account, the Chinese Communist Party's repeated theoretical innovation around China's practical problems forms the historical basis of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is organised in three parts. The first examines the theoretical character and development of Marxism, drawing on Marx, Engels and Lenin. The second traces the laying of foundations and deepening of Sinicisation from Li Dazhao and Yun Daiying through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. The third treats the "new leap" since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the formation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Sun's central claim is that Marxism is a method, not a ready-made dogma, so it must change with time and place; Lenin's "concrete analysis of concrete conditions" and Mao's "seeking truth from facts" express this. The article presents each stage as a response to new problems: Mao Thought as the first historic leap, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the second, and Xi Jinping Thought as a new leap. For the latest leap, Sun identifies its practical basis as the three "major questions of the times" and its theoretical mark as original ideas such as the "Ten Affirmations". Its philosophical basis is the view that truth is pursued through practice, together with the Two Integrations, which Sun reads as including a "penetrating" fusion of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture.

Sun concludes that, because theory that stands still falls behind real life, continued innovation depends on grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought and applying its stance, viewpoint and method. The article calls for historical initiative and theoretical confidence in writing new chapters of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-historical genealogy of Sinicisation, from Mao to Xi, as presented in an official-academic account.
quoteEn: Scientific theory must keep developing as the times and practice change.
quoteZh: 科学的理论必定随时代和实践变化而不断发展。

t: The logical relationship and value convergence between fine traditional Chinese culture and the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 中华优秀传统文化与人类命运共同体理念的逻辑关系与价值融通
paras: Shi Si asks how the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind relates to fine traditional Chinese culture, and how the two connect in value terms. The article argues that traditional culture is the concept's cultural foundation and source of values, and that the concept is in turn a creative transformation and innovative development of that culture, carried out under Marxist guidance. Without this cultural root, Shi contends, the concept would lose its "root and soul".

The article opens with the "great changes unseen in a century" and the questions of where the world and humanity are heading. It then reads the concept's proposals on politics, security, the economy, culture and ecology as expressions of traditional philosophy. Next it traces four lines of development, from "harmony and integration", benevolence, people-as-the-root thinking and the righteousness–profit debate. The final part sets out five "convergences" of values, citing classical sources such as Mencius, the Book of Rites, Zhuangzi and Zhang Zai.

In Shi's account, the concept develops each tradition rather than simply repeating it. Benevolence is carried from the "small self" to the "greater self" and from family-state to humanity, removing the hierarchical limits of Confucian feudal ethics. The people-as-root idea expands from the Chinese people to the peoples of the world. Under the Marxist theory of contradiction, the opposition between righteousness and profit becomes a dialectical unity in which states build economies together. The five convergences pair traditional ideas with goals: harmony with a lasting peaceful world; "all under heaven as one family" with a universally secure world; mutual aid with common prosperity; harmony in diversity with an open and inclusive world; and the unity of heaven and humanity with a clean and beautiful world.

Shi concludes that the concept is a theoretical crystallisation of the convergence between contemporary Chinese Marxism and fine traditional culture. In this reading it marks a new height of theoretical confidence and practical consciousness in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article presents it as a Chinese solution to global problems, drawing on remarks by Xi Jinping throughout. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links classical sources to current foreign-policy language, and which traditional concepts are used to ground the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: The concept of a community with a shared future for mankind is the theoretical crystallisation of our era, in which contemporary Chinese Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture converge in values.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体理念就是当代中国马克思主义与中华优秀传统文化价值融通的时代理论结晶

glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for shared responsibility among states in security, development, civilisation and ecology.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化

A traditional Chinese idea of harmony, coexistence, fusion and cooperation. The author treats it as the core of Chinese culture and the main source of the concept.
A traditional cosmology that sees humans and nature as an inseparable whole. The author uses it to ground the idea of a life community of humanity and nature.

t: The distinctive "six outlooks" contained in Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化蕴含的独特“六观”
paras: This short commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today takes up a statement by Xi Jinping of 7 February 2023. Xi said that the distinctive world outlook, values, view of history, view of civilization, view of democracy and view of ecology contained in Chinese modernization are a major innovation in the theory and practice of world modernization. Xin Xiangyang argues that unpacking these "six outlooks" helps explain the global influence of Chinese modernization.

The article takes the six outlooks in turn, giving each a short section: world outlook, values, view of history, view of civilization, view of democracy and view of ecology. Each section lists a few defining propositions rather than developing a sustained case.

On the world outlook, Xin contends that Chinese modernization is part of world modernization and follows its general laws. In the author's account it also breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and the idea that only capitalism makes a country strong. The values are said to have four sources: traditional Chinese culture, scientific socialism, the core socialist values and common values of all mankind. The view of history exposes the violence behind Western modernization, citing Marx on primitive accumulation, and stresses China's independent exploration. The view of democracy holds that without whole-process people's democracy there is no Chinese modernization, and that Western modernization achieved only a democracy of capital. The ecological view criticises capital's plunder of nature and calls for harmony between humanity and nature.

Xin concludes that these outlooks make Chinese modernization an alternative picture of modernization and offer developing countries another path and a "Chinese solution". Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned summary of how Party theorists present the worldview behind Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization" and dispelled the fog that Western modernization is the only choice for humanity's destiny.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，打破了西方现代化就是人类命运唯一选择的迷雾

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official term, promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, for China's claimed form of socialist democracy, which stresses popular participation at every stage and not only at elections.
A set of twelve values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) at national, social and individual levels, including prosperity, democracy, harmony, freedom and patriotism.
Xi Jinping's formulation, from 2015, of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared by all humanity.

t: Safeguarding the foundation and source, the root and soul of Chinese modernization
zh: 守好中国式现代化的本和源、根和魂
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2023, Wang Mingyi comments on Xi Jinping's address at the study session on the 20th Party Congress (2022) spirit. Xi called on the Party to "safeguard the foundation and source, the root and soul" of Chinese modernization by holding firmly to its Chinese characteristics, essential requirements and major principles. Wang argues that doing so ensures the correct direction of Chinese modernization and keeps this unprecedented undertaking moving forward.

The piece is organised in three parts, each taking one of the three elements Xi named. It moves from Chinese characteristics, to the essential requirements, to the major principles, and quotes Xi throughout. Wang presents these as the answer to a set of major theoretical and practical questions and as a guide to action for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

On Chinese characteristics, Wang argues that no single or universal model of modernization exists. Wang presents the five features of Chinese modernization, namely a huge population, common prosperity, coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development, as growing out of China's national conditions and traditional culture. On the essential requirements, Wang stresses that Party leadership is the greatest strength and fundamental guarantee of Chinese modernization. Wang treats advancing modernization as the Party's central task from now on, and reviews the 20th Party Congress goals for 2035 and for the next five years. On the major principles, Wang lists five commitments: Party leadership, the socialist path, a people-centred approach, deepening reform and opening up, and a fighting spirit. Wang says these answer the risks and challenges the undertaking will meet.

Wang concludes that the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has summarised these three elements and begun to build a theoretical system of Chinese modernization, making it clearer, more scientific and more workable. Holding to them, the author argues, will widen the path to a modern socialist country and increase the significance of Chinese modernization in the history of human civilization. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a Party-school-style commentary presents Xi's three-part formula on Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the greatest strength and fundamental guarantee of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是中国式现代化的最大优势和根本保证

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
The policy line launched in 1978 combining domestic economic reform with opening to the outside world.

t: How Chinese modernization was successfully advanced and expanded in the new era
zh: 新时代何以成功推进和拓展中国式现代化
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in May 2023, Chen Li asks how the Communist Party has succeeded since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in advancing and expanding Chinese modernization. The piece is a study session commentary built on Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of a seminar on studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022). Chen argues that Chinese modernization is the major result of long exploration under Party leadership, and that the new era produced theoretical and practical breakthroughs in understanding, strategy and practice.

The article opens with a historical survey. It runs from the failed attempts after the Opium War (the Self-Strengthening Movement, the 1898 reforms, the 1911 Revolution) through the New Democratic Revolution, the socialist revolution and construction after 1949, and the reform and opening up period. It then devotes three sections to the new era, covering deepening understanding, improved strategy and enriched practice.

Chen's central claim is that earlier reformers failed for lack of advanced scientific theory, and that the Party succeeded by integrating Marxism with Chinese realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. On understanding, Chen holds that the creation of Xi Jinping Thought is the greatest achievement of the decade. The 20th Party Congress report, in Chen's account, set out the features, essential requirements and principles of Chinese modernization and began to build its theoretical system. On strategy, Chen cites the five-sphere integrated plan, the Four Comprehensives and the two-step plan towards a modern socialist country by mid-century, and says the 20th Congress set higher targets for 2035. On practice, Chen cites institutional maturation, GDP growth from 54 to 114 trillion yuan, and the elimination of absolute poverty. Chen also lists gains in Party discipline, ecology, the military, Hong Kong, cross-Strait relations and diplomacy.

Chen concludes that the decade's achievements gave Chinese modernization a more complete institutional guarantee, a firmer material base and greater spiritual initiative. Chen asserts that practice has shown it to be the only correct path to national rejuvenation, and calls for stronger confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, avoiding both a closed, rigid old path and an "evil path" of abandoning socialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official narrative links its history to the new-era claims about Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that Chinese modernization works and is stable, and that it is the only correct path to building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 实践证明，中国式现代化走得通、行得稳，是强国建设、民族复兴的唯一正确道路。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīnshídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and opening the economy to the outside world.

t: Enriching the people's spiritual world is an essential requirement of Chinese modernization
zh: 丰富人民精神世界是中国式现代化的本质要求
paras: Wang Xinsheng, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2023, comments on a formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The report listed enriching the people's spiritual world among the essential requirements of Chinese modernization, alongside the claim that it is a modernization of material and cultural-ethical advancement in coordination. Wang argues that this places spiritual civilization and spiritual strength at the centre of the national project, and that material and spiritual civilization are like a bird's two wings or a cart's two wheels.

The article has three parts. The first explains why enriching the people's spiritual world matters, in theoretical and practical terms. The second reviews cultural work in the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012), presented as the foundation for this goal. The third turns to the 20th Party Congress agenda of building a socialist cultural power and sets out what it requires.

Wang's core argument is that Chinese modernization is socialist and must therefore create a new form of human civilization that meets both material and spiritual-cultural needs. In this account, spiritual enrichment is a measure of social development, of all-round human development and of socialism's superiority. Wang credits the past decade's achievements to several measures: establishing Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, promoting core socialist values, creatively transforming traditional Chinese culture, and a people-centred orientation in cultural production and public cultural services. The article also treats cyberspace as a shared spiritual home. It cites Xi Jinping's remarks that regulation must cover all media and cites the Cybersecurity Law, and it calls for the Party to hold the initiative in online ideological work.

Wang concludes that cultural construction is a long-term systemic project, covering content, talent, institutions, the cultural industry and the dissemination of Chinese civilization, to be carried out as the Congress specified. Success would, in this view, supply a powerful spiritual impetus to national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior academic restates the 20th Party Congress's cultural and ideological priorities and links them to the concept of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Cultural prosperity is the spiritual hallmark of a strong nation, and a rich spiritual world is the cultural expression of the people's affluence.
quoteZh: 文化繁荣是国家强盛的精神标识，精神世界丰富是人民富足的文化呈现。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of development, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 through five features, including coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement.
An official goal of building a country with strong cultural influence and cohesion under Party leadership, to be reached by 2035 according to Party documents.
A twelve-word set of values promoted officially since 2012, at national, social and individual levels.

t: Further strengthening research on basic theoretical questions of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 进一步加强马克思主义中国化时代化基础理论问题的研究
source: Thought and Political Education Theory (思想教育理论), 2023 no. 5
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which called for opening up new realms for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, Tian Keqin asks which basic theoretical questions in this field need deeper study. The article argues that research should be strengthened in five areas: core concepts, the historical standing of theoretical achievements, themes, the system of theoretical achievements, and the fundamental path and method. Tian presents this as necessary for grasping the Party's internal laws of adaptation and for serving the scholarly mission of building arguments for the Party and the people.

The article is organised in five sections, each tied to a guiding reference point: the relationship between the two processes ("sinicization" and "contemporization" of Marxism); the "three leaps"; the overall theme of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; the three Party "historical resolutions" (1945, 1981, 2021) as documentary basis; and the Two Integrations. It draws on Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation, the 13th, 14th, 15th and 17th Party Congresses, and the 2021 resolution. It closes by linking the research agenda to Xi Jinping's call to let the world know "China in academia" and to build an autonomous knowledge system with Chinese characteristics.

Tian makes three main moves. First, the two processes are distinct but inseparable: Mao did not stress contemporization in 1938 because China's situation still fell within Lenin's imperialist era and the pressing task was to correct dogmatism, whereas from the 1980s changed world conditions led the 14th Party Congress (1992) to add the "features of the times". Second, on the "three leaps", the 2021 resolution speaks of one "first historic leap" (Mao Zedong Thought) and two "new leaps" (the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era). Tian says the latter two need more study, including Deng Xiaoping Theory's foundational role and the logical relation between those two achievements. Third, Tian identifies four theme shifts culminating in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and holds that "the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation" is the overarching theme. Tian also reads the 20th Congress's selective restatement of earlier summaries as showing that the content system of Xi Jinping Thought is still being developed.

On the Two Integrations, Tian argues that the second (with fine traditional Chinese culture) was already implicit in Mao's call to inherit China's historical heritage, rests on the first, and answers present needs of cultural confidence. Tian concludes that advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization requires both integrations and thorough study of Xi Jinping Thought. Theorists are urged to speak both accurately and freshly. Read the original if you want a Party-theory scholar's map of the research agenda on adapting Marxism in China, including how the official periodisation and terminology have shifted since 1938.
quoteEn: The vitality of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context lies in combining the basic principles of Marxism with current realities and the features of the times.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化的生命力就在于使马克思主义基本原理与当前实际和时代特征相结合

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化

glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for the continuing process of combining Marxism with China's conditions and with the characteristics of each era. "Sinicization" dates from Mao Zedong in 1938; "contemporization" was added to the formula in recent official usage.

The principle that Marxism's basic tenets must be combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–22.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, which official texts treat as the unifying theme of its century of struggle.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the 20th Party Congress presented as the way to advance national rejuvenation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想

t: The cultural dimension of the "Two Integrations" and the development of Sinicized Marxism
zh: “两个结合”的文化维度与中国化马克思主义的发展
source: Social Science Journal (Shehui kexue jikan), 2023 no. 3
paras: Hong Jun asks why integrating Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, alongside its integration with China's concrete realities, has come to be stated as a principle only now. The article takes up Xi Jinping's formulation of the Two Integrations, made in the 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary and repeated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). Hong argues that the cultural dimension emerged gradually through a century of debate and struggle, and that its explicit affirmation moves Sinicized Marxism to a new and higher stage.

The article is a historical-theoretical survey in four parts. It begins with Engels's and Lenin's thoughts on adapting Marxism to local conditions and with Stalin's formula of proletarian content in national form. It then turns to Mao Zedong's writings of the late 1930s and 1940s, followed by wrong views of the Marxism–tradition relationship, both inside and outside the Marxist camp. The final part sets out the grounds on which the two can be integrated.

Hong makes three main moves. First, Mao's idea of Marxism's adaptation to Chinese conditions already had a realistic dimension and a historical-cultural one. Mao studied Mohist and Confucian philosophy with Chen Boda and Zhang Wentian, yet in formal statements he stressed integration with China's realities, so recognition stayed at a single integration for decades. Second, Hong traces obstacles: Comintern and Soviet hostility, cultural conservatives from Zhang Zhidong to the Kuomintang, and nihilist attitudes among early Communist intellectuals and later scholars who treated tradition as feudal or unscientific. Third, Hong argues that Marxism and traditional culture share an "affinity". The evidence offered includes the Confucian ideals of Great Harmony and the moderately prosperous society, the people-as-basis tradition, and early Chinese Marxists' use of Datong language, as well as Li Zehou's and Jacques Gernet's observations.

Hong concludes that influence ran both ways: Chinese tradition was transformed by Marxism, while foreign Marxism took national form and was nourished by fine traditional culture. In Hong's view, the 20th Congress formulation clears away a century of confusion, shows cultural self-awareness and self-confidence, and supports the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a Chinese path to modern civilization. Read the original if you want a detailed intellectual history of how the Marxism–traditional culture question was fought over in China, with citations from Mao, Chen Duxiu, the Kuomintang and conservative thinkers.
quoteEn: One important reason Marxism was able to take root and flower in China, and to show such vitality, is a certain "affinity" between Marxism and traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 马克思主义之所以能够顺利地在中国生根开花，并显示出了强大的生命力，其中的一个重要原因，就在于马克思主义与中国传统文化之间具有某种“亲和性”。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping stated it in 2021 and repeated it at the 20th Party Congress.
Term for adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. Mao Zedong put it forward in 1938, and it also names the resulting body of Chinese Marxist theory.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, central to Party discourse since the early 2010s.
A Confucian-derived idea of modest well-being, which Deng Xiaoping adopted as a development goal in the reform era.
The Confucian ideal of a world in which "all under heaven is shared", described in the Book of Rites. Some Chinese thinkers have linked it to communism.

t: Marking a new height in understanding Chinese modernization
zh: 标注中国式现代化认识的新高度
