source: Party and Government Cadres Forum (Zhongguo dangzheng ganbu luntan), 2023 no. 4
paras: Tian Pengying takes up the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and its account of Chinese modernization. Tian argues that the report gave a comprehensive, systematic theoretical summary of its Chinese characteristics, essential requirements and major principles, and so formed a complete theoretical system. In Tian's reading, this marks a new height in the Party's understanding, building on a line of work running from the First Five-Year Plan to the Fourteenth.

The article is a commentary in three parts. The first sets out the Chinese characteristics of Chinese modernization against a reflection on world modernization theory. The second turns to the major principles to be upheld in what Tian calls a great and arduous undertaking. The third discusses the basic dimensions of modernization through several major relationships that Xi Jinping has said must be handled correctly.

In the first part, Tian contrasts Chinese modernization with Western paths. Tian says neoliberal theories hold that modernization means following the West, and that countries copying Western models have developed slowly and with difficulty. By contrast, Chinese modernization is said to proceed from national conditions, pursue common prosperity and avoid polarisation, balance material and cultural-ethical progress, and pursue harmony between humanity and nature. It also follows a path of peaceful development, which Tian presents as dissolving the historical logic that a rising power must seek hegemony. The second part lists principles: upholding the Party's overall leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, the people-centred approach, deepening reform and opening up, and a fighting spirit. The third part pairs top-level design with practical exploration, strategy with tactics, fundamental principles with innovation, efficiency with fairness, vitality with order, and self-reliance with opening up. Tian presents these as applications of materialist dialectics.

Tian concludes that Chinese modernization is the fundamental route to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Tian calls on the whole Party to strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, hold firm the Four-sphere Confidence and carry out the Two Upholds, while staying alert to new contradictions in a complex international environment. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how the 20th Party Congress report's framework on Chinese modernization is presented to Party cadres and academic readers.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a modernization that fits China's realities, reflects the people's wishes and embodies the general laws of human social development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是符合中国实际、反映人民意愿、体现人类社会发展一般规律的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for China's own path to modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A goal of prosperity shared by all the people, not only some groups. Official usage stresses that it is to be achieved gradually and does not mean egalitarianism.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The overarching official national goal of restoring China to a leading global position, tied to the two centenary goals.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The Party requirement to uphold the authority of General Secretary Xi Jinping as the core of the Party and the Central Committee's centralised, unified leadership.
The official name for China's current system and path, associated with reform and opening up since 1978.

t: Chinese modernization and the construction of China's independent knowledge system
zh: 中国式现代化与中国自主知识体系构建
paras: Writing in 2023, Sun Leqiang asks how Chinese philosophy and social science can build what Xi Jinping in 2022 called an independent knowledge system, and how this relates to the theory of Chinese modernization. The article takes up Xi's 2016 call for discipline, academic and discourse systems with Chinese characteristics. Sun judges that, seven years on, scholarly work still falls well short of what the Party and state expect. The thesis is that such a system must start from the autonomy of Chinese practice, be measured against world history, and rest on theorising that practice.

The piece is organised in three parts: starting from "China", taking "all under heaven" as the yardstick, and grounding the work in practice. The first part sets out three ways of understanding China. The second compares Chinese and Western paths, and the third turns to the tasks of scholars. Sun draws on Marx on civil society and the Germanic form of property, on Engels's warning to Germany's "young ones", and on extensive quotation from Xi.

Sun argues that the narrative "modernization equals Westernization" is a product of capital-led world history. Seen through Western yardsticks, China appears as a distorted "mirror image". Sun treats China as a generative process, as a totality of history and structure, and as an autonomous practical totality that never passed through an independent Western-style civil society. Against both "universalism" and "particularism", Sun contrasts the two paths. Capitalism is described as centred on private property, individuals and nation-states. Chinese modernization is described as public-ownership-based, people-centred, ecologically harmonious and oriented to a pluralistic civilisation and to a community with a shared future for mankind. Sun adds that it transcends capitalist modernity and represents a new form of human civilisation.

Sun calls for concrete research that turns Marxist principles into the specific universality of Chinese society, for example by contrasting the Asiatic mode of production and public ownership with Germanic and capitalist forms. Such work should theorise China's particular experience as Smith, Ricardo, Hegel and Marx did for the British, German and Western paths, with the aim of producing a Chinese counterpart to The Wealth of Nations and Capital. Sun also urges enriching the "three laws" and rejecting a linear reading of the five social formations. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist philosopher links Xi's calls for a self-reliant knowledge system to world-historical claims about Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has already overflowed the framework of Western capitalist modernity and is a sublation of the entire capitalist world system, and therefore represents a new form of human civilisation different from the West.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化已经溢出了西方资本主义现代性的框架，是对整个资本主义世界体系的扬弃，因而代表了一种不同于西方的人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party after the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and civilisational concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for common development and cooperation among states.
The official umbrella term for the humanities and social sciences in China. Xi Jinping's 2016 symposium set the goal of building such scholarship with Chinese characteristics.

A phrase used by Xi Jinping in 2022 for scholarship that rests on Chinese practice rather than Western frameworks. It is presented as the ultimate aim of building the three systems (discipline, academic, discourse).

t: The spread of "isms" in the May Fourth period and the opening of the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 五四时期“主义”传播与中国式现代化道路的开启
paras: Sun Shan asks how the historical process now called Chinese modernization began, and answers that it was opened by the spread of Marxism as an "ism" during the May Fourth period. Starting from the 20th Party Congress (2022) formulation that Chinese modernization advances the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the author argues that the early dissemination of Marxism formed the essential link between China's modernization and scientific socialism.

Combining intellectual history with social history under a "grand historical view", the article examines how Marxism spread after the October Revolution and the May Fourth Movement. It is organised in four parts, each tied to a core element of Chinese modernization: socialist direction, the path, the leading force, and the driving force. Evidence comes mainly from writings, letters and periodicals of Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Cai Hesen, Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Li Da and others, plus societies such as the Awakening Society and the New People's Study Society.

Sun's central claim is that Marxism's propagation shaped each element in turn. Through debates with reformism, anarchism and Guild Socialism, Marxism gained discursive authority and fixed a socialist orientation, after the First World War had, in the author's account, shown capitalist modernization to be necessary but impossible for China. The turn to "learning from Russia" produced a "revolution–modernization" path, replacing reform with social revolution and moving Chinese modernization, in Sun's phrase, from passive to active. Early Marxist societies trained a core of cadres, and the Marxist theory of the proletarian party prepared the founding of the Communist Party as modernization's leading core. Finally, mobilisation of workers and peasants ("going to the people"), stress on popular agency and adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions formed its driving force.

Sun concludes that the May Fourth spread of Marxism gave modernization in China its direction, path, leadership and driving force. It also sidestepped the capital-centred logic of Western modernization and gave China theoretical self-awareness and historical initiative. The author presents this as the value and historical starting point of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-rich account of how Chinese scholarship links early Marxist propagation to the origins of the current official modernization narrative.
quoteEn: That is, the spread of the "ism" led Chinese society to establish a modernization direction with socialism as its future.
quoteZh: 即“主义”传播引领中国社会确立以社会主义为前途的现代化方向。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as socialist modernization led by the Communist Party. It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping, of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
A phrase for the early twentieth-century turn of Chinese radicals from imitating Western Europe and the United States to taking the Russian Revolution as a model.
The author's term, citing Luo Rongqu, for a path in which China reaches modernity through social revolution rather than gradual reform.

t: Guiding and regulating the healthy development of capital under the socialist market economy
zh: 社会主义市场经济条件下引导和规范资本健康发展
source: Studies on Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2023 no. 4
paras: Cai Wanhuan takes up a question that Xi Jinping has described as a major theoretical and practical problem for Marxist political economy in the new era: how capital, which must exist in a socialist market economy, can be used for productive purposes while its negative effects are held to a minimum. The article argues that this requires a Marxist understanding of capital's nature and laws of behaviour, a clear definition of capital's place under socialism, and concrete rules for guiding and regulating it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the general attributes of capital under market conditions and its specific character under capitalist private ownership. The second examines capital under the socialist market economy, covering its historical positioning and the institutional advantages of socialism. The third proposes principles for regulation, including the Two Unwaverings, rules governing capital's conduct, and "red and green lights" for capital's entry into different sectors.

Drawing on Marx's Capital, Cai holds that capital is not a thing or a real factor of production but a social relation of production embodied in a thing. Its profit-seeking drives cooperation, technical innovation and resource allocation, yet it also produces exploitation, monopoly, financialisation, a gap between expanding production and narrow worker consumption, and ideological influence. Under the socialist market economy, Cai says, capital is a tool and not an end, and the state should "master" it, rejecting both liberal opposition and Keynesian supplementation. Three institutional safeguards are named: a public sector as the mainstay, Communist Party leadership, and the balancing of long-term and short-term, whole and part. Cai argues that public enterprises are more efficient when measured by new value (v + s) created for society, not by profit alone.

Cai concludes that public and non-public capital must be distinguished in nature and positioned clearly, with the Two Unwaverings applied only on the basis of public ownership as the mainstay. Regulation should cover labour's share of distribution, anti-monopoly enforcement (especially against platform and digital capital), enforcement of labour contract law, and restricted private capital in housing, healthcare and other livelihood areas. Capital must not be allowed to turn from servant into master. Read the original if you want a Marxist-economics account, from a Tsinghua scholar, of how Party theory justifies regulating private capital after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: Capital is one of the tools driving the development of China's productive forces at the present stage; it is a means, not an end.
quoteZh: 资本是现阶段推动我国生产力发展的工具之一，是手段而不是目的。

glossary.explanation: A Party principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership as the mainstay and Party leadership.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization through informatization and contributing to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 以信息化推进中国式现代化为中华民族伟大复兴贡献力量
paras: Writing in 2023, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhuang Rongwen, a senior official in China's cyberspace administration, argues that informatization should be pursued deliberately as a route to Chinese modernization. The article says the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the "great changes unseen in a century" and the information revolution are converging historically. In Zhuang's account, informatization enriches the setting, path, driving forces and goals of Chinese modernization and offers a rare opportunity.

The piece is organised in six sections. It begins with Xi Jinping's statements on informatization, such as "without informatization there can be no modernization". It then covers the Party's achievements in cyberspace work since 2012, the major principles of Chinese modernization, and the five features of Chinese modernization set out in the 20th Party Congress report. It also covers the key relationships to be handled and the strategic arrangements for building a cyber power. Each section ends with tasks for the cyberspace and informatization field.

Zhuang's central move is to read the principles and features of Chinese modernization as direct guidance for internet work. Informatization is said to be an accelerator of the "four modernizations" (new-type industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization), which the article says must develop in parallel rather than in sequence as in the West. The author cites digital economy growth from 11 trillion yuan in 2012 to 45.5 trillion yuan in 2021 and 1.051 billion internet users by June 2022. Party leadership is treated as decisive. The principle that the Party manages the internet is said to have ended the earlier fragmented "nine dragons controlling the water" arrangement. Zhuang also pairs each feature of Chinese modernization with a task. These include using the world's largest user base, spreading the gains of the internet to all, developing the digital economy alongside online culture, promoting green digital transformation, and building a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

Zhuang concludes with a list of priorities. They are digital infrastructure, breakthroughs in core technologies through the new whole-nation system, a stronger digital economy, digital government and society, digital culture, digital ecological civilization, cybersecurity, and international cooperation including a "Digital Silk Road". The author calls for building a cyber power in step with the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want to see how a senior Chinese official presents the cyberspace and digital agenda within the official framework of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Unswervingly advance Chinese modernization through informatization.
quoteZh: 坚定不移以信息化推进中国式现代化

glossary.explanation: The official term, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to modernization. It lists five features: a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China to a position of national strength and prosperity.
A strategic goal announced after 2012 of making China a leader in internet technology, infrastructure, security and governance.
A principle that Party leadership must direct all internet governance. It was institutionalised through the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission, which was previously a leading group.

t: Chinese modernization broadens the paths to modernization open to developing countries
zh: 中国式现代化拓展发展中国家走向现代化的路径选择
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2023, no. 6), Chai Shangjin asks what Chinese modernization offers developing countries. The article opens from Xi Jinping's remark that each country's people are best placed to judge which modernization suits them. Chai argues that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of "modernization = Westernization" and gives developing countries a new model for independent modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first treats Chinese modernization as an innovation in world modernization theory and practice, tracing the Communist Party's role through the new-democratic revolution, the founding of the People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second contrasts Chinese modernization with the Western pattern. The third sets out its significance for humanity's common problems and for developing countries.

Chai's central claim is that Chinese modernization differs from Western modernization in kind. In the article's account, Western modernization began with enclosures and colonial plunder and has always been bound by the "logic of capital", which produces polarisation between rich and poor. Chinese modernization is described as people-centred and aimed at common prosperity, balancing material and cultural-ethical progress and harmony between humanity and nature. Chai also holds that Party leadership determines its fundamental direction and success. Chai adds that it follows the path of peaceful development rather than hegemony or resource plunder, and that the West-led model has brought widening North–South gaps, crises and conflict.

Chai concludes that no country has succeeded by copying developed countries' models, that no fixed model of modernization exists, and that each country should explore a path suited to its own conditions. Chinese modernization, in this reading, shows the Western road is not the only one and will keep widening developing countries' options, while China seeks shared development with them. Read the original if you want a concise statement, in the official register of 2023, of how Chinese modernization is presented as a model and a contrast to Western modernization for the Global South.
quoteEn: The successful practice of Chinese modernization shows that the Western road is not the only road to modernization for humanity, and that the Chinese road will continue to widen the options open to developing countries.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的成功实践表明，西方现代化道路并非人类通向现代化的唯一道路，中国式现代化道路将不断拓展发展中国家走向现代化的途径选择。

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Communist Party's account of China's path to modernization. It was elaborated in Xi Jinping's speeches and at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in official discourse as a defining feature of socialism. It has been given greater weight in Party policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Serving Chinese modernization through high-quality educational modernization
zh: 以高质量教育现代化服务支撑中国式现代化
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in 2023, after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhang Jun asks how universities should carry out the Congress's guidance on Chinese modernization. The author argues that educational modernization and Chinese modernization are dialectically united, and that universities must place themselves within the larger picture of national development and serve what the article calls the "matters of greatest national importance".

The commentary is organised around four perspectives: the political, the systemic, the long-term, and digitalisation. It draws on the experience of Beijing Institute of Technology, where the author is Party Secretary, as an illustration.

Zhang contends that Chinese modernization requires educational modernization to come first, and that Party leadership is its political guarantee. Universities are to cultivate talent through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and red cultural resources. Zhang then reads the Congress report's joint planning of education, science and technology, and talent as a "trinity" and calls for a "big education view". Disciplines are treated as the core unit of this trinity, with talent training, technological self-reliance and talent-team building all tied to national strategic needs, including "bottleneck" technologies.

Zhang calls for a high-quality education system, with the Double First-Class initiative shifting from "catching up in quantity" to "surpassing in quality". Zhang also urges an education digitalisation strategy and a modernised system of school governance, and says this could offer a Chinese approach to global education governance. Read the original if you want a short example of how a senior university Party leader links Party leadership, discipline building and digital education to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Disciplines are the most central basic unit of the "trinity" and its point of convergence.
quoteZh: 学科是“三位一体”最核心的基础单元，是“三位一体”的汇聚点。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
A national programme launched in 2015 to build world-class universities and disciplines in China.

t: Independent innovation in the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路的自主创新
paras: Luo Yuting asks what makes the path of Chinese modernization distinctive and answers that its defining feature is independent innovation (zizhu chuangxin). Independence and self-reliance, in Luo's account, are the soul of the national spirit, and innovative development is the essence of the spirit of the times. The article presents the path as one the Communist Party opened by proceeding from China's concrete realities and the fundamental interests of the people.

The article is organised around four 'combinations' that Luo treats as innovations of the path: national independence with independent exploration; universal truth with concrete conditions; socialism with the market economy; and primary reliance on indigenous innovation with learning from others as a supplement. Each section sets out the historical, theoretical and policy grounds for the claim. Evidence ranges from modern Chinese history and the 'two bombs, one satellite' programme to industrial statistics and the experience of Japan and South Korea.

Luo first contrasts independent modernization with modernization permitted within the bounds of imperialism, which the author describes as dependent on international monopoly capital. In this reading, the failures of the Self-Strengthening Movement, the 1898 reforms and the 1911 Revolution show that dependent modernization cannot succeed. Luo argues that Japan and South Korea became 'vassal-type' modernizers, constrained by the United States. By contrast, the author stresses China's complete industrial system, which the article says includes every category in the UN industrial classification. Luo then argues that the path rests on Marxist principles, including socialized large-scale production and science and technology as a productive force, applied to China's national conditions, culture and the goal of common prosperity. The central 'combination' of socialism and the market, in Luo's view, produces a 'two-way coupling' of state macro-regulation with market vitality, of regulating capital with preventing its disorderly expansion, and of efficiency with fairness.

Luo concludes that China must rely mainly on its own innovation, especially in science and technology, because core technologies cannot be bought, particularly amid what the author calls a technology war waged by the United States and its allies. Learning from other countries remains a necessary supplement, so that self-reliance does not become self-isolation. Luo contends that adhering to this path is essential to building a modern socialist country and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative Party-theory account of how Chinese modernization is justified as independent, Marxist and innovation-led.
quoteEn: Independence and self-reliance are the soul of the national spirit, innovative development is the essence of the spirit of the times, and independent innovation is the distinctive hallmark and essential characteristic of the path of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 独立自主是民族精神之魂，创新发展是时代精神之髓，自主创新是中国式现代化道路的鲜明底色和本质特征。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Communist Party's model of modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as led by the Party, with a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all people, stressed in official discourse as opposed to polarisation between rich and poor.

t: Opening up a new realm of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 29 March 2023, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's statement that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is a process of seeking, revealing and acting on truth. Lin Zhenyi, a secretary-general at the Central Party School's research centre on Xi Jinping Thought, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era achieves a new leap in this process and opens a new realm for it. It is presented as the latest in a line running from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development.

The article is organised in four sections. The first deals with how the thought answers the major questions of the era. The second considers its original theoretical contributions. The third turns to its guiding role in practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The fourth discusses its contribution to the world through Chinese wisdom and Chinese solutions.

Lin's core claim is that the thought answers the questions of the new era: what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold, how to build a modern socialist country, and how to build a Marxist party that stays long in power. In Lin's account it offers an answer on Party building through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform, which is said to be a way of escaping the historical cycle of rise and decline. Theoretically, Lin says it combines Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture, and has become a coherent system summarised in the 'ten affirmations', the 'fourteen commitments', the 'thirteen areas of achievement' and the 'six stances' of the 20th Party Congress report. Lin credits the thought and the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core with the achievements of the past decade, and calls the Two Establishes the most important political outcome of the new era.

Lin concludes that a great theory is necessarily global in reach. The article lists the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind, the Belt and Road Initiative, the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives and common values of humanity as contributions to peace and development. It presents these as evidence of the world significance of twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily framing of Xi Jinping Thought as a new stage in the adaptation of Marxism.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has developed into a systematic, comprehensive, logically rigorous, rich and internally unified scientific theoretical system.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想发展成为一个系统全面、逻辑严密、内涵丰富、内在统一的科学理论体系。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to changing historical periods. The 20th Party Congress report (2022) added 'times' to the older 'sinicization of Marxism'.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage of Marxism adapted to China.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding status of his thought.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official policy of strict Party discipline and anti-corruption, promoted since 2012.
The official idea that the Party can correct its own problems through internal rectification and supervision. It is promoted as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's guiding idea for China's foreign policy, referring to shared interests and joint responsibility among countries.
A Chinese-led infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries in Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: How to keep up an enterprising spirit at all times
st: Maintaining the drive to get things done and start new undertakings
zh: 如何始终保持干事创业精神状态
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily and posted in May 2023, asks how the Communist Party can always keep the mental state needed to get things done and start new undertakings (ganshi chuangye). Huang Jian calls this a problem peculiar to the Party that it must solve. The author argues that only by keeping this spirit can the Party lead the people in advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization.

The piece first explains why the question matters, pointing to historical cases in which rulers grew complacent after long peace and their governments collapsed. It then recalls the Party's long awareness of the danger, citing Mao Zedong's call before national victory to keep up a modest, prudent and hard-working style, and Xi Jinping's warnings. It lists measures taken since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and ends with practical requirements for Party members and cadres.

Huang contends that the Party's rise and the nation's revival came from struggle, and that complacency or love of comfort would endanger the Party's vanguard character and vitality. The author describes cadres' mental state as the combined expression of ambition, responsibility, drive and work style, which decides whether the Party's blueprint becomes reality. Three problems must be solved: willingness, through study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and firm ideals; ability, through learning from books, practice and the masses; and courage, through combining strict management with care, and through a mechanism that tolerates and corrects errors.

Huang concludes that cadres should take on heavy responsibilities in economic development, grassroots work and service to the people. Those who dare to struggle and take responsibility should be backed and boldly promoted. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary frames cadre morale and incentives in 2023.
quoteEn: Any thought of seeking comfort and being unwilling to keep struggling hard is unacceptable, and any thought of complacency and unwillingness to keep forging ahead is unacceptable.
quoteZh: 一切贪图安逸、不愿继续艰苦奋斗的想法都是要不得的，一切骄傲自满、不愿继续开拓前进的想法都是要不得的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: mechanism that tolerates and corrects errors
glossary.explanation: A policy allowing leniency for cadres' mistakes made in good faith while reform and innovation are pursued, so as to encourage initiative.

t: Advancing theoretical and practical innovation in Chinese modernization through a systems perspective
zh: 以系统观念推进中国式现代化理论和实践创新
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2023, Zang Fengyu takes up the theory of Chinese modernization set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and asks how a systems perspective can guide its theoretical and practical development. The article argues that Chinese modernization is a "systematic project" that must be understood through universal connection, comprehensiveness and development, and managed through forward-looking thinking, overall planning and integrated advancement.

The piece has two main parts. The first applies the systems perspective to the content and essence of Chinese modernization, covering its institutional guarantees, material foundation and spiritual strength, its five distinctive features and the nine essential requirements listed in the Congress report. The second turns to six pairs of relationships that Xi Jinping named as needing correct handling, and ends with a note on the habits of thought required.

Zang's central claim is that the features, essential requirements and major principles of Chinese modernization are themselves systematic, so the theory is "clear, scientific" and workable in practice. In the account given, Party leadership determines its basic character, and it is said to have discarded the antagonistic contradictions produced by the logic of capital and to offer a new form of human civilisation. The second part treats top-level design and practical exploration, strategy and tactics, upholding fundamental principles and innovation, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and self-reliance and opening up. Each is presented as a dialectical pair whose two sides define and condition each other. Zang gives, for example, innovation as the key and "upholding principles" as the foundation, and describes China's rapid growth and long-term social stability as two "miracles".

Zang concludes that these relationships will keep generating new contradictions, and calls for stronger strategic, historical, dialectical, systems, innovative, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking. The aim is development that is higher in quality, efficiency, fairness, sustainability and security, and further practical creation of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Xi Jinping's "major relationships" framework is applied to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The systems perspective is a basic way of thinking and working for advancing Chinese modernization, and an effective intellectual tool for analysing the intricate contradictions in economic and social development.
quoteZh: 系统观念是推进中国式现代化的基础性的思想和工作方法，是解析经济社会发展中错综复杂矛盾的有效思维工具。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official account of China's path to modernity, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It lists five features and nine essential requirements and is presented as distinct from Western models.
A method of thinking stressing overall planning, interconnection and coordination among parts. Xi Jinping has promoted it as a basic approach to governance.

t: The evolution of Party Congress themes since the 15th Party Congress and adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 党的十五大以来党代会主题演进与马克思主义中国化时代化
paras: Duan Yan asks what the themes of the six Party Congress reports since the 15th Party Congress (1997) reveal about the process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article argues that this process runs through the whole sequence. In Duan's account, the Party has repeatedly judged the era, the national conditions and the Party's own situation, and has used these judgements to advance theoretical innovation. Duan notes that the 15th Congress was the first to condense its content into a stated theme, and that later reports have opened with one.

The article is built in four parts, followed by lessons for the present. It first traces how the themes reflect the Party's reading of the era (peace and development), of the basic national condition (the primary stage of socialism) and of the historical position (the new era). It then follows the phased goals named in the themes, from building a moderately prosperous society to a modern socialist country. Third, it reviews the guiding ideology each theme proclaims, from Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Duan's central claim is that each theme joins a judgement of the times to a concrete task and a theoretical banner. The goals are said to apply Marx's and Lenin's idea of socialism and communism as developing in stages, linking long-term and near-term aims. The ideological sequence is presented as continuous innovation: Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and finally Xi Jinping Thought, which the 20th Party Congress (2022) described as a new leap. Duan credits the Two Integrations with giving Marxism Chinese features and with drawing on traditional culture.

Duan draws six lessons for further adaptation: put the people first, maintain self-confidence and self-reliance, uphold fundamental principles while innovating, remain problem-oriented, use systematic thinking, and keep the whole world in view. The author insists that holding to fundamental principles means rejecting dogmatism and ossification as well as distortions of Marxism, and that self-reliance does not mean closing the door to other civilisations. Read the original if you want a close reading of how Party Congress themes since 1997 are officially tied to the theory of adapting Marxism.
quoteEn: The theme is the soul and core of a Party Congress; it is all-encompassing and of its time, and aims to proclaim the Chinese path and indicate the direction of future development.
quoteZh: 主题是党代会的灵魂与核心，具有统摄性与时代性，旨在宣示中国道路、指明未来发展方向。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to the demands of the contemporary period, giving the Party's theoretical innovation a continuous lineage.
The Party's assessment, first stated at the 13th Party Congress (1987), that China remains at an early stage of socialism and will do so for a long time. It is used as the basis for policy.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture.

The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development that is people-centred. It was written into the Party's guiding ideology at the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Jiang Zemin's thought holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, the advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority.
A Party goal of comfortable but not yet affluent living standards, pursued in stages from the 1980s and declared achieved in 2021.

t: Where it lies and what to do: new thinking on the creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture
zh: 何在与何为：中华优秀传统文化创造性转化的新思考
source: Journal of Liaoning University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 1
paras: Starting from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls for combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, Zuo Yuhe asks which traditional resources are truly "fine" and how they can be creatively transformed. The article argues that such resources exist in China's ideas of governance, morality and the conduct of life. It holds that they must be sifted with a Marxist standpoint, method and viewpoint, and renewed so as to serve contemporary socialist culture.

The article is organised in five parts and draws heavily on Xi Jinping's remarks on traditional culture. It first treats the ideological core and "cultural genes" of Chinese civilisation. It then surveys political resources, namely the people-as-foundation idea (minben) and the Confucian ideal of the Great Harmony (datong), and moral and life-philosophy teachings from Confucius, Mencius, Mozi, Xunzi, Fan Zhongyan, Zhang Zai and others. The last two parts discuss the method of transformation and warn against two wrong tendencies.

Zuo's central argument is that the tradition falls into three kinds: elements that are progressive and democratic in character and should be inherited, elements serving the ruling class that should be criticised and removed, and a large mixed category that is hardest to judge. Confucian ren (benevolence) is the example: it is bound to hierarchical ritual, yet also expresses universal love with humanist and popular content. Even apparent dross such as ritual, loyalty and filial piety may be reinterpreted in an egalitarian sense once their patriarchal content is stripped away. Zuo reads the Great Harmony ideal and minben thought as sources that helped Chinese thinkers move towards modern democracy and socialism.

Zuo identifies two errors to guard against. Cultural and historical nihilism, rooted in cultural inferiority, is said to lead to Westernisation and to denial of the revolution, reform and opening up, and socialism with Chinese characteristics. Cultural restorationism, rooted in complacency, is said to include attempts to "Confucianise" Marxism. Zuo insists that the Party's guiding ideology is Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought and the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, not Confucian culture. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated historian's account of how Chinese scholars are expected to sort the "essence" of tradition from its "dross" in the Marxist-Chinese culture agenda.
quoteEn: Inheriting and promoting traditional Chinese culture does not mean clinging to old rules or being rigidly fixated on the ancient, and it certainly does not mean replacing Marxism with Confucian culture.
quoteZh: 继承与弘扬中国传统文化不等于墨守成规、食古不化，更不是以儒家文化取代马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: A traditional political idea, traced to the phrase "the people are the root of the state", that rulers' legitimacy and stability depend on the people's welfare.
A Confucian vision of an ideal society, set out in the Liji chapter "Liyun", in which "the world is shared by all". Modern thinkers such as Kang Youwei and Sun Yat-sen reinterpreted it.
A term the author uses for an excessive affirmation of tradition and a wish to revive Confucian culture in place of other ideas, including Marxism.
The Communist Party's official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era.

t: How the proposition of "adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times" inherits and develops "the Sinification of Marxism"
zh: “马克思主义中国化时代化”命题对“马克思主义的中国化”的继承和发展
paras: Chen Xixi and Wang Jicheng ask how Xi Jinping's call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to open up new realms for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times relates to Mao Zedong's 1938 proposition of the "Sinification of Marxism". They argue that the relation cannot be read literally, as if "times" were simply added to "China". In their view the new proposition both continues the old one and deepens it.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Mao's proposition through its theoretical basis, its practical logic and its scope. The second identifies three points of continuity with the later formulation. The third identifies three ways in which the later formulation deepens the earlier one.

On the theoretical basis, the authors argue that Marxism is "concrete" because it applies the universal materialist conception of history to the particular contradictions of European capitalism. Applying it in China therefore needs a dialectical movement between universal and particular, not a formal-logic addition of Chinese "specific differences" to a general whole. Mao's 1925 class analysis and his 1956 call for a "second integration" are presented as examples. Continuity lies in making Chinese experience Marxist, combining Marxism with traditional culture, and placing it in a world frame. The deepening lies in three moves. First, combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture is made the historical foundation of the new formulation. Second, creating Chinese modernization gives Marxism worldwide significance, since the authors say its five Chinese features address problems capitalist modernization could not solve. Third, developing twenty-first-century Marxism takes Sinification further towards "worldization". This requires studying contemporary capitalism, exchanges with Marxism outside China, and a community with a shared future for mankind grounded in common values of humanity.

The authors conclude that because Marxism is concrete it needs and can undergo Sinification, and that continuing this process must enrich its adaptation to the times. They hold that the two formulations are therefore continuous and also deepened. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese theorists derive the logic of Sinification from universal–particular dialectics and use it to frame current Party theory.
quoteEn: In sum, precisely because Marxism is concrete, it needs to be Sinified and can be Sinified, and in continuing to advance Sinification it must enrich the content of adaptation to the times.
quoteZh: 总之，正因为马克思主义是具体的，因而它需要中国化，也可能中国化，而在持续推进中国化的进程中，必然需要丰富时代化的内涵

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era. It was highlighted in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
Formula Mao Zedong put forward at the Sixth Plenum of the 6th Central Committee in 1938. It calls for applying Marxism according to Chinese particularities and against dogmatism.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. Official texts describe it as having distinctive features such as a huge population and common prosperity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing interdependence, shared values and non-interference. It is presented officially as a path towards a more just world order.

t: Chinese modernization and promoting the all-round development of the human being
zh: 中国式现代化与促进人的全面发展
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 4
paras: Hao Lixin asks how Chinese modernization relates to the all-round development of the human being, a question raised by the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which describes Chinese modernization as unifying material abundance with people's all-round development. Hao argues that promoting all-round human development is the fundamental value goal of Chinese modernization, and that the practice and theory of the new era have in turn enriched Marxist thinking on the subject.

The article has two main parts. The first grounds the value goal in three sources: the founders of Marxism on the nature of socialist society, the Chinese Communists' exploration of modernization from Mao Zedong to the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second part examines how new-era practice has extended the idea, through the people-centred approach, the thesis that the essence of modernization is the modernization of the human being, and the stages by which all-round development is realised.

Hao draws on Marx's account of human essence, alienation and the division of labour, and on his sequence from relations of personal dependence to dependence on things to free individuality. Capital-driven modernization, in Hao's view, cannot deliver all-round development, and the author cites Ellen Meiksins Wood's account of rising inequality in the United States as evidence. Chinese modernization is instead said to rest on common prosperity. Hao reads Xi's 2013 thesis that modernization is the modernization of the human being as meaning that people are its subject and its purpose. Hao also distinguishes this from Alex Inkeles's Western notion, which is said to neglect social systems and historical difference.

Hao concludes that all-round development is realised gradually, through common prosperity, high-quality development, a richer spiritual life, harmony between humans and nature, world peace and a community with a shared future for mankind. Hao adds practical demands: more free time for workers and an education system that combines moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour training. Chinese modernization and human development are described as dialectically unified, offering what the author calls Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to other countries. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-theoretical account of how the Marxist idea of the free and all-round development of the individual is placed within Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization takes the promotion of all-round human development as its value goal, and in turn creates or provides the economic, political, cultural, social and ecological foundations and conditions for that development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化以促进人的全面发展为价值目标，又为人的全面发展创造或提供经济、政治、文化、社会和生态等方面的基础或条件。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, foregrounded in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Deng Xiaoping used the phrase 'Chinese-style modernization' in 1979.

glossary.en: all-round development of the human being
glossary.explanation: A Marxist idea of the free development of individuals' abilities, relations and character, treated in Chinese official discourse as a goal of socialism. It is commonly linked to moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, covering material and cultural life and aimed at reducing polarisation. Xi Jinping has stressed it since the early 2020s.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A principle of Xi Jinping's thought that development should serve the people's interests and wellbeing. It was prominent from the 18th Party Congress (2012) onward.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao in the 2000s. It called for people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations based on shared interests and common values.

t: Festival commemorations and youth mobilisation in the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Border Region
zh: 节日纪念活动与晋察冀边区的青年动员
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2023, asks how the Chinese Communist Party used commemorations of revolutionary festivals to mobilise young people during the War of Resistance against Japan. Fan and Liu argue that after the full-scale outbreak of war the Party turned such commemorations into a key arena for awakening youth, building a sense of national identity and drawing them into the resistance. They treat the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Border Region, described as a model anti-Japanese base area, as the place where this practice was most extensive.

The article is organised in three parts, drawing mainly on reports in the Jin-Cha-Ji Daily (Jin-Cha-Ji is the Chinese name of the region) and on archival documents. The first part covers the Party's recognition of youth and its protection of their rights; the second describes the content of festival activities and their results up to 1942; the third turns to the rectification campaign and its integration into youth commemorations.

In the authors' account, festival speeches affirmed the May Fourth and December Ninth movements as symbols of justice and progress and presented youth as a driving force of history. The Border Region government backed this with guarantees in politics (voting rights from age 18), culture (the 'four great educations' in the Ten-Ten Programme), marriage and labour. Youth Day, May Fourth and related campaign weeks combined military, political, sporting and entertainment events, and slogans and contests pushed enlistment and wartime production. The authors cite 1942 figures of 470,000 organised young people and children in the Northern Yue district, 430,000 of them in the Youth Vanguard, and four-year totals for operations, land reclamation and school enrolment.

Fan and Liu note that subjectivism, rigid leadership and detachment from reality also affected youth work, so rectification study was built into festival activities through inspections, self-criticism and renewed education. In their reading, this made mobilisation more effective, deepened young people's national consciousness and political identification with the Party and revolutionary government, and made them a backbone of the resistance. Read the original if you want a concise, source-based account of how commemorative events served political mobilisation in a wartime base area, as presented from the Party's perspective.
quoteEn: Our Party used commemorative days as time markers for mobilisation, which brought about profound changes in the thinking of the broad mass of young people and gradually strengthened their national consciousness.
quoteZh: 我们党以纪念日为时间节点开展动员活动，使广大青年的思想发生深刻变化，民族意识逐步增强

glossary.explanation: A Party-wide education and discipline movement launched in 1942 in Yan'an, aimed at combating subjectivism, sectarianism and formulaic 'Party eight-legged essays'.
An anti-Japanese base area behind enemy lines in North China, established in 1937–38 under Communist leadership.
The 1940 policy programme of the Border Region, formally issued by the North China Bureau of the Party, setting out ten tasks in government and ten in other fields.
A youth paramilitary organisation in Communist-led base areas that trained young people for resistance work and often served as a pool for army recruitment.

t: The new form of human civilization in the perspective of the Marxist view of civilization
zh: 马克思主义文明观视域中的人类文明新形态
paras: Tang Aijun takes up the concept of the "new form of human civilization", which Xi Jinping linked to Chinese modernization in his 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary and which the 20th Party Congress (2022) called an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. Tang argues that the concept can be explained through a Marxist view of civilization built from Marx's and Engels's historical materialism. Read this way, the new form is a civilization that moves towards an information-age civilization, is integrated across five domains, and takes human all-round development as its value goal.

The article first defines the Marxist view of civilization as a system covering the nature, origin, structure, driving forces and forms of civilization. It then uses three lenses as its framework: a theory of civilizational forms, a theory of civilizational structure, and a theory of the civilizational subject. Each lens gets a section, and each is tied to a practical orientation for Chinese modernization.

On forms, Tang draws on Marx's "technological social formations", classified by tools and industrial structure, to distinguish agricultural, industrial and information civilizations. Tang holds that the new form's direction of evolution is information-age civilization, which is not the same as the new form itself. Because China's industrialization is unfinished, Tang describes a "parallel" path in which industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization advance together, unlike the "serial" Western sequence. On structure, Tang reads Marx and Engels as implying material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization, and presents the new form as a coordinated whole whose political core is a new institutional civilization. On the subject, Tang uses Marx's three stages of human development to argue that the new form criticizes the reification produced by modern capital-centred civilization and takes people, not capital or things, as the measure.

Tang concludes that Chinese modernization should move beyond traditional industrial civilization, beyond a single material-civilization model, and beyond capital-led modernization. The article says this means pursuing a new type of industrialization with the four modernizations in step, and promoting all five civilizations together. It also means harnessing capital to serve socialism and human all-round development, since capital remains usable in the primary stage of socialism. Read the original if you want a systematic Marxist-theoretical grounding of the Party's concept of a new form of human civilization, as presented by a Central Party School scholar.
quoteEn: What is capital-based is modern capitalist civilization; what is people-centred is the new form of human civilization.
quoteZh: 以资本为本的是现代资本文明，以人为本的是人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, prominent since Xi Jinping's 2021 centenary speech, for the civilizational form said to be created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as going beyond Western modernity.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The official judgement that China, though socialist, remains at an early stage of development. It is used to justify market mechanisms and the use of capital.

Xi Jinping's description of China's modernization as running industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization simultaneously, in contrast to the Western "serial" sequence.

t: The succession of early Chinese Marxists' theories on the evolution of social formations
zh: 我国早期马克思主义者关于社会形态演变理论的递嬗研究
source: Journal of Hunan University of Science and Technology (Social Science Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Wang Xiangqing and Liang Yanli ask how the first generation of Chinese Marxists understood the evolution of social formations, a core category of historical materialism, and what their work contributed. Before Marxism arrived, they note, Chinese scholars largely held an idealist view of history. The authors argue that thinkers from Cai Hesen to Mao Zedong moved step by step towards a scientific account that spread Marxist social-formation theory in China and served the cause of national salvation.

The article first sets out the background and intellectual sources. The background is the debates over "ancient and modern, China and the West" and over "problems versus isms"; the sources are the Marxist classics, Soviet and Japanese Marxism, and traditional Chinese philosophy. It then follows five stages: Cai Hesen's foundation-laying, Zhang Bojian's advance, Fan Shoukang's innovation, Li Da's deepening and Mao Zedong's refinement. A final section draws out three general features of the early Marxists' work.

In the authors' reading, each thinker added something and left gaps. Cai's Social Evolution History (1924) used Morgan's three-stage scheme but said little about feudal, bourgeois and socialist formations. Zhang's eight-stage scheme was more concrete but unorthodox. Fan and Li used five-stage schemes, and Li stressed the special features of each formation and of the transitional period. Mao analysed China's semi-colonial, semi-feudal formation and emphasised class struggle as the driving force.

The authors identify three features. The early Marxists used historical materialism to sublate evolutionism, shifting from the vocabulary of evolution to class struggle and the unity of evolution and revolution. They moved from general theory to the realities of China. They also moved from a plurality of views towards acceptance of the five-formation theory, which the authors say became orthodox after the 1938 Short Course of the Soviet Communist Party. They conclude that this work shifted Chinese historical outlooks, strengthened the Communist Party's leadership and was confirmed in revolutionary practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, Chinese-language account of how Cai, Zhang, Fan, Li and Mao each periodised history and how the five-stage scheme became dominant in China.
quoteEn: In studying the development and evolution of social formations through historical materialism, China's early Marxists achieved a shift from the spontaneous to the conscious, from individuals to a collective, and from theory to practice.
quoteZh: 我国早期马克思主义者在以唯物史观研究社会形态的发展与演变时，实现了从自发到自觉、由个体到群体、从理论到实践的转变

t: Chinese modernization and the question of capital: theoretical framework and practical wisdom
zh: 中国式现代化与资本问题：理论架构及其实践智慧
source: Journal of Northeast Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2023 no. 3
paras: Xia Ying and Cui Juran ask how Chinese modernization differs from Western modernization, and how capital can be regulated in practice. They argue that Marx's critique of political economy, centred on the logic of capital, offers the key. On this basis, they hold that Chinese modernization sublates that logic: it keeps capital as a factor of production while removing it as a relation of production, producing development with "capital" but without "capitalism".

The article moves from theory to practice in four sections. It first traces how modern society, civil society and classical political economy emerged in the West, through Habermas, Hegel, Marx's reversal of Hegel and Adam Smith. It then examines the dual character of the logic of capital in modernization, and the limits Marx identified for it, with a side-look at Sismondi. The last section sets out the practical wisdom of Chinese modernization.

The authors' central move is Marx's distinction between capital as a factor of production and capital as a relation of production. As a factor, capital in the Grundrisse drives market expansion, productivity, innovation, scientific discovery and new needs, and may create free time for human development. As a relation, it forces workers into wage labour and alienation, and meets internal limits: a falling rate of profit and overproduction crises. Sismondi saw the demand-side contradiction but sought only government correction, which Marx judged superficial. The authors then argue that three features of Party leadership contain capital. The Party's proletarian character gives modernization a socialist orientation. Marxism guides its grasp of capital's nature. Its people-centred approach prevents polarization of wealth. In practice they point to a socialist market economy with public ownership as the mainstay, checks on the disorderly expansion of capital, and an "effective market" joined with an "enabling government".

The authors conclude that, as the Party deepens its understanding of capital, its capacity to harness it will grow. Capital's drive to expand and the technical progress that follows can then serve prosperity and give people free time, and capital's operation can become a ladder to common prosperity. Read the original if you want a Marx-based, philosophically framed account of how Chinese scholars justify using capital under socialism, set against Hegel and classical political economy.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is building a development process that has \"capital\" but not \"capitalism\".
quoteZh: 中国式现代化正在构筑一种有“资本”而无“资本主义”的发展进程。

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path of modernization, presented as socialist and distinct from the Western capitalist model. It is stressed in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, with narrower wealth gaps. It has been given prominence in Party policy under Xi Jinping.
The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s, which combines market allocation of resources with public ownership as the mainstay and Party leadership.

t: The new path of Chinese modernization and new developments in the modernization of the human being
st: An analysis based on Marx's theory of world history
zh: 中国式现代化新道路与人的现代化新发展
zhSub: 基于马克思世界历史理论的分析
paras: Qiao Yuqiang asks what Chinese modernization contributes to global modernization when read through Marx's theory of world history, which traces how national and regional histories become world history and how individuals move from one-sided to all-round development. The article argues that Chinese modernization is a new type of modernization. By critically reconstructing and going beyond modernization led by the logic of capital, it widens the paths open to other states and advances the modern attributes of the human being.

The article has three main parts. The first describes how capital and Enlightenment reason together opened the modern era in the West, and where their combined role reaches its limits. The second sets out four contributions of Chinese modernization to global modernization: its subject, its driving force, its values and its goal. The third examines how three attributes of the human being (sociality, historicity and practicality) develop further on this path. A short conclusion closes the piece.

Qiao holds that capital, with Enlightenment reason as its legitimating partner, drove productive forces, markets and political revolutions, but then reduced people to instruments of profit and left the world in global risk. Against this, the article says Chinese modernization makes the people, not capital, its subject and "sublates" capital critically, so that capital serves human development. Its "endogenous" driving force, built on the state, the market and the people, is contrasted with the "outward-oriented" force of commercial, industrial and finance capital. Its "common values" replace Western "universal values", which the author describes as a metaphysical expression of Western centrism. Its goal is cooperative interaction, sustainable development and the liberation of humanity as a "species" being, in place of a centre–periphery hierarchy. On the attributes of the human being, the author points to common prosperity (sociality), the shift of the people from onlookers to masters of the country (historicity), and the people's practice at home and a community with a shared future for mankind abroad (practicality).

Qiao concludes that the essential task of modernization is the modernization of the human being as a species being. In this account Chinese modernization, led by the Communist Party and using Marxist methodology, makes up for the theoretical and practical shortcomings of Western capitalist modernization and ends its monopoly. It offers an original contribution and useful experience to states that want to modernize while staying independent. Read the original if you want a worked example of how Marx's world-history theory is used to place Chinese modernization within a philosophy of history and of human development.
quoteEn: The fundamental task of modernization is to realise the modernization of the human being as a "species" being.
quoteZh: 现代化的根本任务就是要实现作为“类”存在的人的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in Party policy since the 2010s and especially from 2021. It aims to narrow gaps in income and development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for cooperation among countries on shared global challenges.

Values such as liberal democracy and freedom presented by the West as applying to all humanity. Official Chinese discourse often criticises them as Western-specific and contrasts them with "common values".
In Marx's historical materialism, the process by which isolated national histories become an interconnected global history through capitalism and world markets.

t: Further strengthening research on basic theoretical questions of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 进一步加强马克思主义中国化时代化基础理论问题的研究
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2023 no. 5
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which called for opening up "new horizons" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, Tian Keqin and Zhang Zeqiang ask which basic theoretical questions research in this field must now deepen. They argue that studying the Congress report's new formulations, and the core concepts, historical course, theoretical results, themes and methods they touch on, is necessary to grasp the inner laws of the Party's project and to fulfil scholars' task of serving the Party and the people.

The article is organised around five areas of research. These are the core concepts and the relation between "Sinicization" (zhongguohua) and "contemporization" (shidaihua); the historical status of the "three leaps"; the theme of the process; the system of theoretical results as set out in the Party's three historical resolutions; and the method of the Two Integrations. Each section combines a historical account with a list of questions the authors regard as still open.

The authors argue that the two "hua" are distinct yet inseparable. In their account, Mao Zedong stressed Sinicization in 1938 because Leninist-era conditions and the fight against dogmatism demanded it, while the Party's turn to "the features of the times" came with the changes of the 1980s and was written into the 14th Party Congress (1992). On themes, they identify four major shifts and conclude that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is the overarching theme, above "socialism with Chinese characteristics". They also maintain that the Two Integrations rest on one another: the first, combining Marxism with China's concrete realities, was the groundwork for the second, combining it with fine traditional Chinese culture, and Mao's own idea of Sinicization already contained the second. They hold that the 2021 resolution's wording of one "historic leap" and two "new leaps" requires clearer study of Deng Xiaoping Theory's foundational role and of how Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era relates to the earlier theoretical system. The system of Xi's thought is, they say, still being summarised and not finished.

The authors conclude that such work fits Xi Jinping's call to let the world know "academia in China" and "theory in China", and that it strengthens the discipline and a self-reliant Chinese knowledge system. Scholars should "speak accurately and speak anew" on the basis of the third historical resolution and the 20th Congress. Read the original if you want a detailed map of the research agenda that Party-theory scholars set for the "two hua" after the 20th Congress, and of how they periodise the Party's theoretical results.
quoteEn: The vitality of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context lies in combining the basic tenets of Marxism with present realities and the features of the times.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化的生命力就在于使马克思主义基本原理与当前实际和时代特征相结合

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for combining Marxism with China's conditions and with the features of the current era. Adding "时代化" to the older "中国化" became prominent in recent Party documents.
Combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was emphasised by Xi Jinping from 2021.
Resolutions on Party history adopted by the Central Committee in 1945, 1981 and 2021. They set the Party's official assessment of its past and of Mao Zedong and Mao Zedong Thought.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing. The article treats it as the overarching theme of the Party's century of struggle.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: A brief discussion of state capital in the socialist market economy
zh: 略论社会主义市场经济中的国有资本
paras: Meng Jie asks in what sense state capital is the form that socialist ownership by the whole people takes under market conditions, and what this implies for reform of state-owned enterprises since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article argues that state capital is a transformed form of that ownership relation. Its decisive dimension is the relation between state and enterprise, which sets it apart from private capital analysed in Marx's Capital.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theory of state capital and its goals. The second turns to the reforms after the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013): classified reform of state-owned enterprises, the shift to "managing capital", and the overall governance structure of the state economy. The third addresses how to judge the dominant position and efficiency of the state sector and the role of Party leadership. Meng draws on asset and ranking data, including Fortune Global 500 figures, to support the argument.

Meng holds that ownership by the whole people has two internal moments, the state and the enterprise. Reform therefore changes how the state acts, replacing administrative orders with economic and legal means, but cannot fully separate ownership from management. State capital has three dimensions: state–enterprise, capital–labour and capital–capital. Its goals are plural, combining profit with use-value goals set by national strategy. In Meng's reading, the capital–labour relation shifts from zero-sum antagonism toward distribution according to labour. Meng classifies enterprises by function rather than by market structure or profit motive, and presents state enterprises as tools of national economic governance. Meng also warns that "managing capital" through state financial capital risks subordinating industrial capital to short-term returns, which would call for guiding and regulating state financial capital.

Meng concludes that the state sector remains dominant, citing 2018 data on state-controlled enterprises' share of assets, especially in finance, and its weight among the largest firms. Claims that state firms are inefficient are described as one-sided, because they ignore reform lag, long-run recovery and the wider economic functions of state capital. Meng calls for Party leadership to be built into corporate governance in order to make the state economy stronger, better and larger. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy account of state capital in China, linked to current state-owned enterprise reform.
quoteEn: Under socialist market-economy conditions, the state acts not outside the market but within it, exercising its regulatory role through state capital as the medium.
quoteZh: 在社会主义市场经济条件下，国家不是在市场之外而是在市场之内，即以国有资本为媒介发挥其调节作用。

glossary.explanation: A reform approach proposed in 2013 in which state asset regulators supervise state capital as value-form assets, for example through investment and operating companies, instead of directly managing enterprises.
The constitutional name for state ownership, one of the two forms of socialist public ownership alongside collective ownership by the working masses.

t: The historical setting of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化的历史场景
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 12
paras: Cao Yongxin starts from Marx's point that people make history under inherited conditions.
