It first examines how the theory understands "historical change" dialectically; it then treats the theory as opening a turn in the epoch of world history; third, it considers how the theory helps build a pattern of common development in the contemporary world; and finally it places the theory within scientific socialism. Throughout, Liu draws on Marx and Engels's theory of world history, the unity of the historical and the logical, and the totality of social relations.

Liu's central claim is that the theory rests on three sets of historical relations: humanity and nature, China and the world, and material and spiritual civilization. Against the Western-dominated idea of modernity, which Liu describes as equating modernization with Westernization or capitalization, Chinese modernization is presented as a "part" of world history that advances the whole. Liu says it does so through a community with a shared future for mankind, common values of humanity and reform of global governance. On this account it sublates the capitalist form of civilization and creates a new form of human civilization. The theory is also said to apply historical materialism's totalising method to the Party's leadership and its people-centred approach.

Liu concludes that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era guides the practice of Chinese modernization. This practice, in Liu's account, answers "the people's question", "the world's question" and "the question of the times", and gives scientific socialism a contemporary Chinese form with a global character. Liu urges Marxist researchers to grasp contemporary Chinese Marxism through the "Chinese logic" of historical materialism and to strengthen the reach of Chinese governance experience abroad. Read the original if you want a philosophical, world-history-centred account of how official Chinese modernization theory is justified through historical materialism.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a "part" of a particular world history, and the new historical mission it undertakes at this stage is to promote an essential connection, for different nations and countries, between their own modernization and the progress of human society as a whole.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是特定世界历史的“部分”,其在新的历史阶段所担当的全新历史使命就是推动不同民族和国家在自身现代化建设与人类社会整体进步之间建立本质联系。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012. It calls for shared security, development and values among nations.
An official formulation naming peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as shared values, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2015.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The Lei Feng spirit as a spiritual coordinate for the new social ethos of our times
zh: 时代新风新貌的精神坐标
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in 2023, on the 60th anniversary of Mao Zedong and other veteran revolutionaries' inscriptions for Lei Feng, Chen Peng takes up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to foster a new social ethos. Chen argues that the Lei Feng spirit matches five spirits named in that report and is a 'spiritual coordinate' for the new ethos.

This short commentary links each of the five spirits to episodes from Lei Feng's life: labour, striving, dedication, creativity, and thrift and frugality. Each section pairs an anecdote or quotation with a statement from Xi Jinping or a claim about the Party and nation.

Chen presents Lei Feng as a model labourer, honoured at work in Wangcheng, on the Weishui project and at Anshan Iron and Steel. His seven-day flood-control effort at a reservoir in 1960 is offered as an example of striving. His maxim of 'benefiting others without thought of self' and his help to strangers on a train illustrate dedication. His fuel-saving truck modification and a mud-hauling device illustrate creativity, and his refusal of a second uniform and his donations from a small allowance illustrate thrift. Chen contends that the Chinese people and the Party have advanced through these qualities, and that Lei Feng has become a common name for selfless contributors.

Chen concludes that Lei Feng, a 'people's hero', embodies the spirit of the age, and that his example has lit people's hearts for 60 years. Chen calls for deeper study of Xi Jinping's statements on promoting the Lei Feng spirit, so that it is passed on and builds strength for the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an example of how Party publicity officials link the Lei Feng model to the 20th Party Congress's language on spiritual civilization.
quoteEn: The Lei Feng spirit is a vivid expression of the spirit of creativity; Lei Feng was always surging with passion and vitality for innovation.
quoteZh: 雷锋精神是创造精神的生动表达，雷锋身上始终澎湃着创新的激情与活力

glossary.explanation: The set of virtues associated with Lei Feng (1940–1962), a soldier held up since 1963 as a model of selflessness, hard work and service to the people. Official campaigns to 'learn from Lei Feng' have recurred for decades.
A slogan Xi Jinping popularised from 2012, equating the Dream with national rejuvenation and the people's well-being.

t: Whole-process people's democracy as a transcendence of Western democratic politics
st: An analysis based on the system of people's congresses
zh: 全过程人民民主对西方民主政治的超越
zhSub: 基于人民代表大会制度的分析
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 10
paras: Cheng Enfu and Sun Shaoyong ask what institutional vehicle makes whole-process people's democracy real, and argue that it is the system of people's congresses. Published in 2022, shortly before and in the light of the 20th Party Congress, the article presents this system as a wholly new political institution that goes beyond Western democratic politics.

The article has three parts. The first describes the nature and features of the people's congress system and compares it with earlier Chinese options (constitutional monarchy, the Kuomintang presidential system) and with Western models, namely the separation of powers in the United States and cabinet government in Britain. The second argues that the system embodies a democracy that is the most extensive, the most genuine and the most effective. The third sets out Xi Jinping's eight \"whether" tests and four \"look at, but look more at\" criteria for judging whether a political system is democratic and effective, and applies each to China and the United States.

The authors hold that the form of state follows its content: the people's congress system is the form of government that corresponds to the people's democratic dictatorship. They argue that it is extensive because Party leadership and democratic centralism cover a huge population. In their account it is genuine because it joins electoral and consultative democracy at the \"input end\" with decision-making, management and supervision at the \"output end\", all under the rule of law. They argue that it is effective because it keeps the people as masters of the country. By contrast, the authors describe American democracy as elite or oligarchic. In their reading it is dominated by money, lobbying and a politics of vetoes, and it reduces popular participation to periodic voting, with unfulfilled promises. Chinese practice, they say, offers orderly leadership succession, collective decision-making, merit-based recruitment and layered supervision.

The authors conclude that the people's congress system unifies Party leadership, the people as masters of the country and law-based governance. They call for upholding and improving it, strengthening its lead role in legislation and the effectiveness of its supervision, and rejecting what they call superstitious faith in Western-style democracy. They expect this to raise governance capacity and contribute to human political civilisation. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese scholars use the people's congress system to contrast whole-process people's democracy with the American model, and to see how the official criteria for judging democracy are applied point by point.
quoteEn: Without a people's congress system matching it, China's whole-process people's democracy would become water without a source and a tree without roots, an empty and untrue slogan that could not express its authenticity.
quoteZh: 没有与我国全过程人民民主相配套的人民代表大会制度，我国全过程人民民主就成为无源之水、无本之木，成为一句空洞不真实的口号，无法表达其真实性。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019 and promoted since 2021. It holds that democracy covers the whole chain of election, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision, not only voting.
China's fundamental political system. It consists of the National People's Congress and local people's congresses, formally the organs through which the people exercise state power.
The official definition of the Chinese state's class nature. It means democracy for the people alongside coercive power over those defined as hostile to them, under working-class leadership.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party and the state. Decisions are made through discussion and then binding on all members and lower organs.

t: Continuously raising the level of urban safety governance
zh: 不断提升城市安全治理水平
paras: This short commentary, originally published in the People's Daily in 2023, asks how cities can improve their safety governance as part of public safety governance. Wu Aiqun argues that, guided by Xi Jinping's statements on urban work and the strategic plans of the 20th Party Congress (2022), cities should pursue reform and innovation in three areas: evaluation standards, safety safeguards and governance effectiveness.

The piece is organised under three headings that follow these areas. It draws heavily on quotations from Xi Jinping and on central Party and State Council documents on work safety and urban safety development. It closes the opening framing with the aim of weaving an all-round, multi-layered public safety net.

On evaluation, Wu holds that the city is a complex system, so assessment must use a systems perspective. Accident counts are an outcome measure, while hazard checks, supervision and enforcement, and rescue capacity are process measures that should also be included, moving governance towards prevention. On safeguards, Wu calls for strengthening grassroots foundations and responsibility systems, improving laws and local regulations under Xi Jinping's thought on rule of law, and expanding technology such as data sharing and urban lifeline projects.

On effectiveness, Wu stresses a people-centred approach, the principle that development must not come at the expense of safety, governance innovation, and systemic governance that breaks down departmental and regional fragmentation. Wu concludes that urban safety should be treated as comprehensive and holistic, with "whole-chain" supervision and "all-hazard" rescue capacity, and with Party committees, governments, departments and enterprises each bearing their responsibilities. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames urban safety governance in the terms of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: We must adhere to systemic governance, observing and grasping urban safety governance issues in a developing rather than static way, comprehensively rather than one-sidedly, and systematically rather than piecemeal.
quoteZh: 要坚持系统治理，做到发展地而不是静止地、全面地而不是片面地、系统地而不是零散地观察和把握城市安全治理问题。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on rule of law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on law and governance, formalised as official guidance for legal work in 2020.

t: On historical confidence, cultural confidence and civilizational confidence
zh: 论历史自信、文化自信和文明自信
source: Journal of Sun Yat-sen University (Social Science Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Chen Jinlong takes up three concepts that appear in recent Party discourse: historical confidence, cultural confidence and civilizational confidence. The 20th Party Congress report (2022) called for firm historical and cultural confidence, and Xi Jinping had earlier put forward civilizational confidence. Chen argues that the three are distinct in content yet closely linked, and that clarifying their meanings, features and relations is the basis for strengthening them.

The article has four sections. The first three deal with each concept in turn, tracing when Xi Jinping first used it, defining it and listing its characteristics. The fourth examines how the three relate. Chen draws mainly on Xi's speeches and on the Party's third historical resolution (2021).

Chen holds that historical confidence, as Xi uses the term, refers specifically to confidence in the history of the Communist Party. It covers the Party's major achievements over a century and the spirit of its struggle. Cultural confidence means confidence in socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, meaning fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture. Civilizational confidence covers confidence in Chinese civilization and in the "new form of human civilization" that Chinese modernization is said to have created. The author describes this new form as people-centred, aimed at all-round human development, and as having moved beyond the defects of Western capitalist civilization and corrected the deviations of traditional socialist models. On their relations, Chen argues that history comes first, so historical confidence underlies the other two. Culture precedes civilization, which Chen treats as the refined, progressive part of culture. Cultural confidence therefore rests on historical confidence and prepares the ground for civilizational confidence.

Chen concludes that civilizational confidence grows out of, and sublimates, the other two. It is the higher and more lasting form, and it shows more fully the world significance of Chinese civilization and the new form of human civilization. Listing the three together follows both a temporal logic, the order in which history, culture and civilization form, and a spatial logic of decreasing scope. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Party theorists define and rank these three "confidences" and of the Xi Jinping speeches they cite.
quoteEn: Historical confidence is the foundation of cultural confidence and civilizational confidence; without historical confidence, cultural confidence and civilizational confidence cannot arise.
quoteZh: 历史自信是文化自信、文明自信的基础，缺乏历史自信，就无法生成文化自信、文明自信。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in 2021, referring to the Party's confidence in its own century of struggle and achievements. The 20th Party Congress report presents it as a precondition for "strengthening historical initiative".

Confidence in socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, including fine traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture. Xi Jinping presented it in 2016 as the deepest of the "four-sphere confidence".
Confidence in Chinese civilization and in the new form of human civilization. Xi Jinping first used the term in 2019 at the Dialogue of Asian Civilizations.
A term Xi Jinping introduced in 2021. It describes the civilization said to arise from Chinese modernization.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, which Party documents present as an alternative to the Western model.

t: Accelerating the building of a strong agricultural country
zh: 加快建设农业强国
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in spring 2023, Han Yang takes up the Party Central Committee's call, restated in the 2023 No. 1 Central Document, to speed up the building of a strong agricultural country. Han's thesis is that agricultural strength is the foundation of a modern socialist country, so that agriculture must move from being a large sector to being a strong one. The piece presents itself as a study of Xi Jinping's remarks at the Central Rural Work Conference of December 2022 and of the Document.

The article has two parts. The first sets out why the task matters, in five points. The second sets out routes to achieving it, in five more: stable output and supply, international competitiveness, technological self-reliance, a green and low-carbon rural environment, and rising farmers' incomes. Han frames the whole as guidance for work on agriculture, rural areas and farmers (the "three rural issues") in the coming period.

On significance, Han argues that without agricultural modernization national modernization would be "incomplete, unbalanced and unsound". The author notes that goals for building a strong country rose from four at the 18th Party Congress (2012) to twelve at the 19th (2017) and thirteen at the 20th (2022), the last including agriculture. Han adds that China's agriculture is still "large but not strong", lagging behind industrialization, informatization and urbanization. Food demand has also shifted from eating enough to eating well and safely, widening food security into a broader notion of food supply. On the routes, Han calls for grain security based on domestic supply, a greater say in global agri-food rules, pricing power and diversified imports, and breakthroughs in seeds and machinery. Han also calls for resource-saving green development and raising farmers' incomes through integrated rural industries, urban–rural integration, land-market reform and fairer distribution.

Han concludes that this is a long-term historic task that will run through the whole process of building a modern socialist country. Agriculture is cast as the "ballast stone" for coping with a changing world. The author ties it to common prosperity, saying the hardest part of achieving it lies with farmers and rural areas. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the policy logic and priorities behind the agricultural-power goal as it stood in 2023.
quoteEn: Agriculture is the foundation of the nation and the base of national strength.
quoteZh: 农业是立国之本，强国之基。

glossary.explanation: A standard shorthand for agriculture, rural areas and farmers, used in Chinese policy documents to cover rural development as a whole.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, which Party documents describe as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The first policy document the Party Central Committee and State Council issue each year. Since the 2000s it has been devoted to rural and agricultural issues.

A goal that the 20th Party Congress report (2022) added to the aims of building a modern socialist country. It means a country strong in agricultural supply, technology, competitiveness and rural development.

t: How to deepen research on Chinese modernization
zh: 如何深化对中国式现代化的研究
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which made Chinese modernization the Party's central task, Wu Zhongmin asks how scholarship can supply the theoretical support the project needs. The article argues that research should be deepened in two main directions: study of Chinese modernization itself, and study of modernization 'meta-theory', meaning the general theory and laws of modernization. A closing section adds three methodological recommendations.

The first part takes up five topics: why China places such weight on modernization, its gradualist way of advancing, the advantages and disadvantages of being a very large country, how to inherit valuable elements of traditional civilisation, and the leadership role of the Communist Party. The second part covers reflection on existing modernization theories, new trends in modernization worldwide, the 'welfare excess trap', and win-win cooperation among states. The final section concerns Marx and Engels, interdisciplinary work and comparative country studies.

Wu contends that Chinese modernization combines features common to all modernization with features rooted in China's conditions, so general theory underpins the study of the specific case. The author describes China's approach as gradual: easy tasks first, balanced development, and a 'security first' principle. Wu judges that size brings strategic depth, a large market and global influence, but also uncertainty, path dependence on quantitative expansion and complacency, since per capita indicators lag. The author criticises Western-centric theory, postmodern theory, dependency theory and world-system theory, each credited with contributions but faulted for specific flaws. Wu also holds that post-war modernization has entered an 'intermediate stage' in which market competition and social protection must be balanced, and that many states are caught in a welfare-excess trap. The author attributes the stability of China's modernization to the Party's leadership, and attributes recent international turbulence mainly to US hegemonism.

Wu concludes that research should take Marx and Engels's ideas on modernization as its theoretical starting point and develop them in light of the necessity of the market economy and China's conditions. It should be interdisciplinary without becoming an all-inclusive 'pan-modernization' field, and should draw on comparative studies of other countries to avoid insularity. Read the original if you want a systematic agenda of research topics on Chinese modernization, and an example of how a Central Party School scholar frames modernization theory, welfare and international order.
quoteEn: In a certain sense, the standard of research on modernization meta-theory determines the depth and breadth of research on Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 从一定意义上讲，现代化元理论研究的水准决定着中国式现代化研究的深度和广度。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. It was given central place in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

t: The place of the theory of human development within Marxism
zh: 人的发展理论在马克思主义中的地位
source: Research on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2023 no. 3
paras: Chen Xinxia asks what position the theory of human development holds within Marxism. The article argues that the complete liberation of humanity and the free and all-round development of the individual form the core value of Marxist theory. The theory of human development, in Chen's account, is the theoretical expression of that value orientation: it rests on Marxism, and the value it carries runs through all of Marxism's component parts.

The article has three sections. The first shows that the theory is grounded in Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. The second argues that human development is the core value running through those same three parts. The third explains why it matters to clarify this position, both theoretically and for contemporary China.

On the first point, Chen draws on the Marxist view of practice and historical materialism to define the 'real human being engaged in practical activity', the meaning of human development and its social conditions, including the role of productive forces and social systems. Chen reads Marx's theory of surplus value as showing that, under capitalism, workers lose free time and cannot develop, so that abolishing private ownership becomes the precondition of liberation. On the second point, Chen argues that human development is the highest-level, most inclusive value orientation in Marxism and the shared value dimension of its three parts. Liberation is its logical and historical precondition, associated with revolution, while development is its goal, associated with construction. Chen holds that this value orientation took scientific socialism beyond modern humanism and utopian socialism.

Chen concludes that clarifying this position confirms the unity of Marxism as 'a single block of steel'. In Chen's view, scholars have affirmed the consistency of its scientific cognition but neglected the consistency of its value orientation. Chen also argues that it strengthens Marxism's capacity to guide social progress. In contemporary China, where the principal contradiction has shifted, Chen proposes human development as the higher value yardstick for handling the relation between unbalanced and inadequate development. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language argument that human development is the core value linking Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism, and its application to current policy.
quoteEn: The value orientation of human development is the core value of Marxism, its ultimate value aim; like a red thread it runs through every component of Marxist theory and becomes their shared value dimension.
quoteZh: 人的发展价值取向是马克思主义的核心价值即价值旨归，它像一根红线贯穿于马克思主义理论各个组成部分中，成为它们共同的价值维度。

glossary.explanation: A strand of Chinese Marxist scholarship centred on Marx's idea of the free and all-round development of the individual. Chen treats it as the theoretical expression of Marxism's core value.

glossary.en: free and all-round development of the individual
glossary.explanation: A formula drawn from Marx and Engels describing the goal of communist society, in which each person can fully develop their abilities and relationships. Chinese official and academic writing often treats it as the ultimate aim of socialism.
The evaluative stance or normative direction of a theory, as opposed to its scientific account of reality. Chen distinguishes it from 'scientific cognition' within Marxism.

The Marxist theory of the conditions of proletarian liberation and the path to socialism and communism, as distinguished from utopian socialism. It is conventionally counted as one of the three component parts of Marxism.

In official Chinese formulations, the central contradiction shaping the stage of development. Since 2017 it has been defined as that between unbalanced and inadequate development and the people's growing need for a better life.

t: The philosophical contribution of the new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
st: Review of the 2022 annual meeting of the Chinese Society for Historical Materialism and academic symposium
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化新飞跃的哲学贡献
zhSub: “中国历史唯物主义学会2022年年会暨‘马克思主义中国化时代化新飞跃的哲学贡献’学术研讨会”综述
paras: This is a report on the 2022 annual meeting of the Chinese Society for Historical Materialism, held online on 10 December 2022 with a symposium on the philosophical contribution of the new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The Society and Sun Yat-sen University co-hosted it in Guangzhou, with the journal Studies on Marxism and the university's Institute of Marxism among the co-organisers. According to Fang, more than 300 scholars from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Peking University, Tsinghua, Renmin University, Wuhan University and other institutions took part.

Fang organises the proceedings under four themes. These are the original contribution of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to Marxism; dialectical and historical materialism as the worldview and methodology of Chinese communists; building a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power; and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Speakers were mostly vice-presidents or standing council members of the Society, including Hou Huiqin (president), Zhao Jianying, Jin Minqing, Yang Haifeng, Xin Xiangyang, Yan Xiaofeng, Feng Yanli and Ai Silin.

Participants agreed that Xi Jinping Thought represents a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that adherence to historical materialism guarantees it. Hou argued that only by studying historical materialism can one grasp the significance of the Two Establishes and the Two Integrations, and he located the thought's philosophical contribution in a new leap in dialectical thinking, including community thinking behind a community with a shared future for mankind. Others treated "six musts" as its philosophical summation, innovation within fundamentals as its logic, and Marxist philosophy as open and historical. Xin Xiangyang used the two methods to interpret changes in the principal contradiction of Chinese society, and Lin Jinping examined how to uphold them within the Two Integrations.

On ideology and modernization, speakers drew on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Feng Yanli described it as a programme for fairness and justice; Yang Shengping gave philosophical definitions of a new form of human civilization; Wang Yan set out the value claims of whole-process people's democracy. Ai Silin, Yuan Yinchuan, Hou Yanshe and Dong Hui each analysed Chinese modernization's methodology, common features and Chinese characteristics, essential requirements and historical-materialist meaning. Read the original if you want a quick map of who in China's Marxist philosophy circles presented which positions on Xi Jinping Thought and Chinese modernization at the end of 2022.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has achieved a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and is contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想实现了马克思主义中国化时代化新的飞跃，是当代中国马克思主义、21世纪马克思主义。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and contemporary developments. It was extended with "of our times" in recent Party documents.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's status as the Party's core and the decisive role of his thought.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, foregrounded in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official description of China's democratic system, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, which stresses popular participation at every stage and not only in elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and joint development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, stressed since Xi Jinping took office in 2012.

t: The international environment of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era, seen through new changes in contemporary capitalism
zh: 从当代资本主义的新变化看新时代中国特色社会主义面临的国际环境
source: Contemporary World Socialism Issues (Dangdai shijie shehuizhuyi wenti), 2022 no. 4
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which speaks of changes in the world, the era and history unfolding in unprecedented ways, this article asks how new changes in contemporary capitalism shape the external environment of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Lin and Sun argue that capitalism is undergoing a new 'change of the century'. In their reading, this change both alters the conditions of the world socialist movement and makes China's international environment more complex and more competitive.

The article has three parts. The first describes capitalism's economic transformation through globalisation, financialisation and digitalisation, and its systemic crisis after 2008. The second assesses what these changes mean for the world socialist movement, setting out new opportunities and new problems. The third turns to their effects on the international setting in which China operates.

On the crisis, the authors point to social tearing between 'winners' and 'losers', political polarisation and the spread of populism, which they say cast doubt on representative democracy itself. Rising inequality, they argue, opens space for radical and progressive politics: 'red-green' politics, direct democracy, digital socialism, and a younger base around figures such as Sanders and Mélenchon. At the same time, the shrinking industrial working class, the erosion of collectivism and state-centred politics, the challenge that digital capitalism poses to classical critiques, and disputes over left populism all trouble traditional socialism. For China, the authors identify three effects. Uneven development intensifies competition over the international economic order, and restraining China's rise has become a consensus among developed capitalist states. Domestic political changes in the West, including populist right parties and a generational split between conservatism and radical liberalism, spill over into China policy. Competition between the two systems over development paths becomes a lasting factor.

Lin and Sun conclude that China's international environment will be more complex and that competition will run through its relations with developed capitalist countries. They hold that its form and limits depend on both sides' strategic choices. They end by affirming China's commitment to peaceful development, in line with the 20th Party Congress report. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account, from the CPC's theoretical perspective, of how Western political and economic change is read as shaping China's external conditions and the prospects of world socialism.
quoteEn: New changes in contemporary capitalism mean that the international environment of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era will be more complex, and competition will be the theme running through relations between China and the developed capitalist countries.
quoteZh: 当代资本主义的新变化意味着新时代中国特色社会主义的国际环境将更为复杂，竞争也将是贯穿中国与发达资本主义国家间关系的主题。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's development path since the reform era, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and market-oriented reform.
The Communist Party of China's national congress held in October 2022, whose report set the Party's agenda for the following five years.
Chinese scholarly term for socialist states, parties and currents worldwide, including left movements in capitalist countries.
A crisis seen as affecting the economic, social and political structure of capitalism as a whole, not only its financial sector.

t: The history of Chinese philosophy as a coordinate system for studying the sinicization of Marxist philosophy
zh: 马克思主义哲学中国化研究的中国哲学史坐标系
paras: Li Weiwu takes up a question raised by Xi Jinping's call to combine the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture (the Two Integrations). How can research on the sinicization of Marxist philosophy show that Chinese Marxist philosophy has moved from being a 'philosophy in China' to being a 'philosophy of China'? Li argues that this requires a neglected framework: the history of Chinese philosophy, rather than only the history of Marxist philosophy.

The piece, printed in Guangming Daily in April 2023, first sets out two complementary coordinate systems for this research. It then explains what the Chinese philosophy coordinate system contains, with attention to the 'ancient-to-modern change' (gu-jin zhi bian) after the Opium War. Finally it reads the sinicization of Marxist philosophy within that change, drawing on Mao Zedong's philosophical writings and on concepts such as 'seeking truth from facts'.

Li holds that the Marxist-philosophy-history framework places sinicization within the worldwide spread of Marxism and shows its universality. The Chinese-philosophy-history framework instead links it to the sources and traditions of Chinese philosophy and shows its particularity. Earlier studies, Li says, mostly used the first. In Li's account, Chinese philosophy changed form after the Opium War, from an ancient to a modern form and from an ancient to a modern tradition, through two movements: the sinicization of Western philosophy and the modernization of Chinese philosophy. Li insists this was not a rupture or mere 'Westernization'. Marxist philosophy, in this reading, took part in the change by answering questions that other currents could not: a materialist conception of history replacing cyclical and evolutionary views, New Democracy as an answer to 'where is China going', and a Chinese form of dialectical materialism built on practice.

Li concludes that Chinese Marxist philosophy did not grow directly out of ancient Chinese philosophy. Yet by shaping and settling into the modern tradition, and by reactivating ideas such as 'seeking truth from facts', 'the ideal of great harmony' and 'a moderately prosperous society', it has entered the Chinese philosophical tradition. Li calls for future research on combining Marxist philosophy with that tradition to start from the Chinese philosophy coordinate system. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese philosophers frame Marxism's place in the history of Chinese thought.
quoteEn: Although Chinese Marxist philosophy did not arise directly from the ancient forms and traditions of Chinese philosophy, in the course of sinicization it took part in, and came to lead, the shaping of Chinese philosophy's modern form and modern tradition.
quoteZh: 中国马克思主义哲学尽管不是从中国哲学的古代形态和古代传统中直接产生出来的，但在中国化的过程中，参与和主导了中国哲学的现代形态和现代传统的塑造

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second 'integration' was added in official discourse around 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义哲学中国化
glossary.explanation: The process by which Marxist philosophy is adapted to Chinese conditions, culture and philosophical traditions. It belongs to the wider official programme of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.
A phrase from Chinese historiography used here for the transformation of Chinese philosophy after the Opium War, under the impact of Western thought.
A classical Chinese phrase that Mao Zedong reinterpreted as a Marxist principle of basing policy on actual conditions. It later became a core slogan of the Party.
Mao Zedong's theory that China should pass through a stage of anti-imperialist, anti-feudal revolution led by the proletariat before moving to socialism.

t: Four suggestions for raising the level of research on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
zh: 努力提高习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想研究水平的四点建议
source: Journal of Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications (Social Science Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Wang Chuanli takes up a practical question: how scholars can raise the quality of research on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang acknowledges that the field has grown rapidly, with dedicated institutes, large projects and many publications, but argues that research must still go deeper. The article offers four suggestions: cultivate a good scholarly and writing style, strengthen intellectual content and linguistic appeal, bring out historical depth through comparison, and adopt a lofty outlook grounded in a 'people first' and national sentiment.

The article is a normative essay in four numbered sections. It draws on the history of the Communist Party of China, especially Mao Zedong's Yan'an rectification campaign and his attack on 'Party stereotyped writing', and on the collapse of the Soviet Union as Wang reads it. It cites Russian authors Lisichkin and Shelepin on Soviet textbooks, praises particular articles in Chinese journals, and refers to Xi Jinping's own comparative history and personal experience at Liangjiahe. It also quotes Marx's school essay on choosing a profession.

Wang's central claim is that style is not a minor matter: in Wang's account, a party's creative theoretical capacity and vitality show in its scholarly and writing style. Dogmatic, empty writing is linked to the Party's early setbacks and to the Soviet decline. Wang therefore criticises research that lacks 'problem awareness', is written from the study rather than from practice, and rearranges leaders' phrases. Wang also criticises papers that list points in numbered sequences and that overuse 'logic' in titles (historical logic, practical logic and so on) while merely listing facts. Wang asks instead for comparison with the history of Marxism, world socialism, past regimes and anti-corruption experience, and for scholars whose motives are service to the people rather than careers, bonuses or publication prominence.

Wang concludes that researchers should combine love of country and people with their work, so that study of the new thought becomes work with warmth and high purpose. Wang argues that without a people-first outlook scholars cannot understand Xi Jinping's thinking and will produce only empty results. Read the original if you want to see how a Tsinghua Marxism scholar frames scholarly style, language and motivation as questions of political and intellectual standards for research on Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Research without problem awareness often turns into hollow, groundless lamentation, into generalities that make something out of nothing.
quoteZh: 没有问题意识的研究，往往成为空对空的无病呻吟，成为无事生非的泛泛之谈。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts present it as the latest form of Marxism adapted to China.

t: Understanding and advancing Chinese modernization from the height of Marxist philosophy
zh: 从马克思主义哲学高度理解和推进中国式现代化
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in April 2023, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhao Jianying and Zhu Huabin argue that Chinese modernization should be understood through Marxist philosophy. They contend that doing so gives the theory sound scholarly grounding and guides practice. Their starting point is Xi Jinping's elaboration of Chinese modernization at the Congress and in later speeches, which they say has produced an initial theoretical system.

The commentary has three parts. The first treats the goal of Chinese modernization through the Marxist view of history and values. The second applies the dialectic of universality and particularity to the features Chinese modernization shares with other countries and those specific to China. The third turns to the dialectics of advancing it: coordination, and the systems approach to major relationships.

On goals, the authors hold that the people are both the makers and the value-bearers of history. From this they derive Xi's claim that the essence of modernization is the modernization of the human being, with the free and all-round development of the person as its final aim. They contrast this with Western modernization, which they say freed people from religious and royal authority but left them under the rule of capital and money fetishism. On commonality and particularity, they list shared features such as industrialization, urbanization and modernized governance. They set against these the five features named at the Congress: a huge population, common prosperity, coordinated material and cultural-ethical advance, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development. On method, they cite Xi's list of relationships to be balanced, including top-level design and practical exploration, efficiency and fairness, and vitality and order. They stress finding the right measure and a dynamic balance.

The authors conclude that the theory of Chinese modernization is an integrated whole, the latest major achievement of scientific socialism. They say it opens a new stage in adapting Marxist philosophy to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They also say it breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers developing countries a model. They call for deeper study of the theory. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2023 framed Chinese modernization in Marxist-philosophical terms.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization", offering developing countries a new path to modernization and setting an example.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，为发展中国家走向现代化提供了新的路径选择，树立了典范。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, set out systematically in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping. Official texts distinguish it from egalitarianism and say it is to be achieved in stages.

t: Theoretical features and historical evolution of the contemporary adaptation of Marxism to the times
zh: 马克思主义时代化的理论特征和历史演进
paras: He Haigen and Sun Daiyao take up the idea of Marxism's "adaptation to the times" (shidaihua), which the 20th Party Congress (2022) report names, together with adaptation to the Chinese context, as a historic responsibility of Chinese communists. They argue that adapting Marxism to the times is an internal requirement of Marxist development. In their account it runs through the history from the birth of scientific socialism to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and it must always stay within the direction of the "big era" of transition from capitalism to socialism.

The article first sets out a framework. It distinguishes "big eras" (social formations such as feudalism or capitalism) from "small eras" (stages defined by technology and shifting themes). It then lists two preconditions for adaptation: real needs, and objective conditions in which the character of the age changes substantially. The second part traces three historical stages: scientific socialism after the first technological revolution, a "Russian stage" after the second, and a "Chinese stage" after the third. The third part identifies four features of Xi Jinping Thought.

The authors link each stage to a technological and economic shift. In their reading, the first revolution gave socialism a real basis, so it could move from utopia to science. Monopoly capitalism and imperialism, with Russia as a weak link under heavy foreign capital, led Lenin to a new stage of theory. After 1945 the third revolution and the turn to "peace and development" exposed the Soviet model. The authors cite East–West German comparisons of productivity and incomes, and say that socialism with Chinese characteristics arose from Deng Xiaoping's reassessment of the age. For Xi's thought they list four features: grasping what changes and what does not in the age; the "two-in-one" unity of Sinicisation and adaptation to the times; continuing to answer basic questions of socialism from within the big era; and answering the "question of the world" through a community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors conclude that Marxism remains the guide for an era still marked by capitalism's basic contradictions, and that Xi's thought is both Chinese and of world significance. They present Chinese modernization as an answer to questions that are at once China's and the world's. Read the original if you want a detailed periodisation of Marxism's development by technological revolution, or an account of how Party theorists justify the link between Sinicisation and adaptation to the times.
quoteEn: The nationalisation and the adaptation to the times of Marxism are an inseparable "two-in-one", and adaptation to the times is the precondition of nationalisation.
quoteZh: 马克思主义的民族化和时代化是不可分割的“二元一体”，时代化是民族化的前提条件

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's path to a modern socialist country, emphasised in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, based on cooperation and shared development.

keywords: adaptation of Marxism to the times

t: On socialism with Chinese characteristics creating a new form of human civilization
zh: 论中国特色社会主义创造了人类文明新形态
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2023 no. 3
paras: Liu Jianjun examines the claim, made by Xi Jinping in 2021 and repeated in the Party's 2021 historical resolution and at the 20th Party Congress (2022), that socialism with Chinese characteristics has created a new form of human civilization. The article asks why the Party advanced this claim, what it means and what theoretical and practical significance it has. Liu answers that the claim is a coherent and scientifically grounded proposition, and argues that it will be borne out by future development.

The article has five parts. It first sets out the background: the maturing and success of socialism with Chinese characteristics, rising assessments of it, the growth of a Party discourse on civilization, and the Party's historical, practical and future confidence. It then analyses the phrase semantically, treats socialism with Chinese characteristics as a civilization form, and explains why it is a new one. It closes with the world-historical significance of this form.

Liu draws on the historical-materialist notion of social formations rather than the comparative approach of Spengler, Toynbee and Kishimoto Takuro, which treats civilizations as separate cycles. Liu argues that the new form is a composite, "atypical" one, produced by the interaction of three civilizations. It is a contemporary form of Chinese civilization, a Chinese form of socialist civilization, and a form of modernization civilization that transcends industrial, Western-centred and capitalist modernity. Liu reads the perfect tense of "has created" as meaning "has taken shape" rather than "has been completed", with the decisive period running to 2035 and 2050. On the world stage, Liu says this civilization enriches civilizational diversity, promotes exchange and mutual learning, advances civilization through innovations such as whole-process people's democracy, and offers guidance for the future, partly through its communist elements.

Liu concludes that the new civilization form is a major creation of the Chinese nation and a landmark in the history of human civilization, with its scientific validity to be confirmed by later development. Throughout, the author presents the Chinese path as a peaceful alternative to colonial and Western-centred modernization, and as one that coexists with other civilizations without replacing them. Read the original if you want a detailed, theoretically structured account of how Chinese scholarship justifies the Party's "new form of human civilization" thesis, including its use of Marxist social-formation theory and civilizational discourse.
quoteEn: The civilization form of socialism with Chinese characteristics is a new form of Chinese civilization, a new form of modernization civilization and a new form of socialist civilization, and a new form created through the combined innovation of these three civilizations.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义文明形态是中华文明的新形态，是现代化文明的新形态，是社会主义文明的新形态，是这三种文明综合创新而成的新形态。

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation used by Xi Jinping in July 2021 and repeated in the Party's 2021 historical resolution and at the 20th Party Congress. It presents China's socialist modernization as a new civilizational type with significance beyond China.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up, combining a socialist political system with market mechanisms and China-specific practices.
An official concept for China's democratic system, which stresses participation across the whole cycle of governance and combines electoral and consultative forms.

t: Strategic blueprint and theoretical-system elevation of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的战略擘画和理论体系升华
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (Marxist Theory Discipline Research), 2023 no. 3
paras: On 7 February 2023, at a study session on the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022), Xi Jinping stated that a theoretical system of Chinese modernization had been "initially constructed". Gu Hailiang reads this judgement as a summary of the Party's century of struggle and of the practical and historical logic of Chinese modernization. The article argues that the judgement rests on historical initiative and theoretical confidence, and that it deepens Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has four sections. The first traces the exploration of modernization through the New Democratic Revolution, the Mao-era building of socialism and the period of reform and opening up, then sets out the theoretical innovations since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second lists the components of the theoretical system, from Xi's 2020 account of five features to the 20th Party Congress report. The third relates the theory to the three major questions of the new era. The fourth examines the worldview and methodology behind it.

Gu's central move is to treat Chinese modernization as a system with defined parts. These include its Chinese characteristics, five main features, nine essential requirements, eight goals for 2035, five major principles and its roots in traditional Chinese culture. Gu further reads it as the answer to three questions: what socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold, what kind of modern socialist country to build, and what kind of long-governing Marxist party to build. Gu holds that Party leadership determines the fundamental nature of Chinese modernization. The article also draws out six "views" in Xi's account (on the world, values, history, civilization, democracy and ecology). It links them to dialectical and historical materialism and to six relationships to be handled in a "systematic process", such as top-level design and practice, or efficiency and fairness.

Gu concludes that Xi's judgement shows the historical basis of Chinese modernization as an innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In Gu's account it also shows the integrated innovation in the content of the theory and its answers to the three major questions. It further brings out the scholarly and philosophical reasoning of the system, which Gu says raises contemporary Chinese Marxism to a new level. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Party theorists organise Chinese modernization into a theoretical system, including the historical debates of the 1920s–30s.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization took shape as a \"theoretical system\" in the course of exploring the major question of the era: what kind of modern socialist country to build and how to build it.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是在对建设什么样的社会主义现代化强国、怎样建设社会主义现代化强国这一重大时代课题探索中成型为“理论体系”的

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Deng Xiaoping had earlier used the phrase "Chinese-style" modernization in 1979.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of combining Marxism with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.

t: Understanding several theoretical questions
zh: 谈谈对几个理论问题的理解
source: Journal of Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications (Social Science Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Ren Dakui takes up four questions in Party theory on which, in the author's view, some scholars' formulations are imprecise or mistaken. The article argues that the Party's century-long struggle has one theme, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, with modernization as the path; that the market economy can be a basic economic institution only in a limited sense; that the community with a shared future for mankind must not be confused with communism; and that Party leadership is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article has four numbered sections. The first treats the Party's historical theme and socialist modernization, including how Chinese modernization differs from capitalist modernization, and it criticises historical nihilism and some assessments of the Self-Strengthening Movement, the 1898 reforms and the 1911 Revolution. The second examines the "three basic economic systems" set out by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). The third discusses the community with a shared future for mankind. The fourth explains why Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Ren holds that treating modernization and rejuvenation as twin themes blurs the line between goal and path. Modernization is neutral in the abstract, and since the October Revolution it has split into capitalist and socialist forms. On the economy, Ren reads the three systems as basic in three separate domains: public ownership as main body in ownership, distribution according to work in distribution, and the socialist market economy in resource allocation. Only the ownership system determines the nature and direction of society. On the community with a shared future, Ren rejects readings that call it a "green channel" to the "association of free individuals", a driver of change in the mode of production, or something grounded in human nature, arguing these ignore class and risk convergence theory.

Ren concludes that Party leadership underpins every other feature of socialism. The Party can reform itself because of its nature and purpose and its acceptance of supervision by the people, which Ren links to Mao Zedong's answer to Huang Yanpei on the historical cycle. Ren defends the Two Upholds against charges of a personality cult and warns of lessons from the Soviet and East European collapse. The article ends by urging students to study Marxism and follow the Party. Read the original if you want a worked example of how a senior Party-school theorist polices orthodox formulations on modernization, the economic system and the community with a shared future.
quoteEn: National rejuvenation is the theme of the Party's century of struggle; how to achieve it is a matter of exploring the correct path.
quoteZh: 民族复兴是党百年奋斗的主题，如何实现民族复兴是探索正确道路的问题。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". Xi Jinping has described it as the single theme of the Party's century of struggle.

The official description of China's path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization, led by the Party and aimed at common prosperity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted since about 2013 and now the stated overall goal of China's diplomacy. It stresses interdependence, cooperation and mutual benefit.
The Party's call to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and its centralised, unified leadership.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The new-era "theory of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation"
zh: 新时代“中华民族伟大复兴论”
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Wang Huxue takes up Xi Jinping's statements on the Chinese Dream and treats them as a coherent body of thought, which the author calls the new-era "theory of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation". The article argues that these statements answer, at the level of "where is the Chinese nation heading", what kind of rejuvenation is to be achieved and how. In Wang's account, the theory defines the concept's scientific content, identifies the path, names the leading force and draws up the blueprint.

The article is organised in four parts that follow those four claims. It draws on speeches by Xi, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and passages from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. It also gives a historical outline of the Party's century of struggle in four periods and the two-step timetable to 2035 and mid-century.

Wang first reads the Chinese Dream through "one core, two levels, three dimensions": rejuvenation as the core, national and individual dreams as the two levels, and national prosperity, national rejuvenation and people's happiness as the three dimensions. Rejuvenation is said not to mean reviving past imperial glories or seeking hegemony, but peaceful development and a community with a shared future for mankind. The path requires Chinese modernization, described as socialist rather than capitalist, together with the "Chinese spirit" of patriotism and reform and innovation, and the unity of the people as "Chinese strength". The leading force is the Communist Party, which Wang calls the only party able to lead the nation to rejuvenation, and rejuvenation is presented as the single theme of its hundred years of struggle.

Wang concludes that the Chinese nation has moved from "standing up" and "growing rich" to "becoming strong", and that rejuvenation is now an irreversible historical process. The author cites the strategic arrangement of a basically modernized country by 2035 and a great modern socialist country by the middle of the century, and calls for continued fighting spirit under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-theoretical exposition of how the Chinese Dream and national rejuvenation are defined and tied to Chinese modernization and Party leadership.
quoteEn: If development cannot be called successful without the people's prosperity, then rejuvenation cannot be called complete without the people's happiness.
quoteZh: 如果说没有人民富裕,发展就不算成功,那么,没有人民幸福,复兴就不算完成。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often described as restoring China's strength and standing after the modern era of decline. It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream and to the two centenary goals.
Slogan first put forward by Xi Jinping in November 2012, equating national rejuvenation with a shared aspiration for national prosperity, rejuvenation and people's happiness.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as socialist and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing common interests and cooperation among states.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions from 2017–2018.

t: Organising and mobilising the masses: the logic of Mao Zedong's "rise up" revolutionary discourse (1921–1949)
zh: 组织动员群众：毛泽东“起来”革命话语的逻辑建构（1921-1949）
paras: This research article asks how Mao Zedong built the word "qilai" (rise up, stand up, get organised) into a revolutionary discourse that mobilised the masses between 1921 and 1949. Xia and Kang argue that Mao's use of the term formed a systematic discourse within the Chinese Communist Party's organisational language, and that it helped the Party win popular trust and the victory of the New Democratic revolution.

The authors begin with the word's meanings and historical setting. They trace the stages from which Mao's discourse emerged: the failures of reformism, the Party's alliance with the Kuomintang, the period of Soviet-influenced revolutionary language, and the wartime construction of a New Democracy discourse. They then analyse the first to fourth volumes of the Selected Works of Mao Zedong and the first to fifth volumes of the Collected Writings of Mao Zedong, sorting uses of "qilai" into three semantic types and drawing conclusions about the discourse's features.

The core of the argument is the three meanings. The first, "to rise up, stand forward, take up arms", is the discourse's core: Mao applied it to peasants, workers, students, women, Party members and oppressed peoples abroad, and, in the authors' account, adapted it to each moment, from the anti-imperialist struggle to the war against Japan and the civil war. The second, auxiliary sense appears in compounds such as "unite", "organise" and "mobilise" with "qilai"; the authors say Mao deliberately preferred "unite the masses" in this form, giving colloquial speech revolutionary force. The third, "stand up", expresses the goal and result, culminating in the 1949 declaration that the Chinese people had stood up. According to the authors' count, the two collections contain 1,138 instances of the word, and about 66 per cent of the roughly 958 uses of the second type have revolutionary significance.

Xia and Kang conclude that the discourse was mass-oriented, easy to spread, firm in conviction, and marked by class identity and exclusivity that separated "revolution" from "counter-revolution". They see the three meanings as mutually reinforcing: the first supplies the content, the second its vivid forms, and the third confirms its success, building a bond of trust between Party and people. Read the original if you study Mao-era political language, Party mobilisation methods or quantitative discourse analysis of Mao's texts.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong consistently held to the revolutionary discourse of "rising up" as his lever for mobilising the masses.
quoteZh: 毛泽东始终坚持以革命话语“起来”作为动员群众的抓手。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's theory, developed around 1940, of a transitional stage of revolution in China led by the proletariat and the Communist Party, aimed against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism before the move to socialism.

t: China's ecological civilization construction and its contribution to the development of human civilization
zh: 我国生态文明建设对人类文明发展的贡献
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in 2023, Cao Mengqin asks what China's ecological civilization construction offers to human civilization as a whole. Cao argues that its achievements belong to the world as well as to China, and that it supplies experience for a new form of civilization beyond the predicament of industrialisation. Cao presents the topic as important for breaking what the article calls the West's discursive monopoly and ideological hegemony over green development.

The short commentary opens from the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, which describes historic changes in environmental protection, and then sets out three kinds of contribution: theoretical, practical and institutional.

On theory, Cao presents Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization as a complete scientific system summed up in the "ten adherences". Its original contributions, in this account, include the principle that when ecology thrives civilization thrives, the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets, and a green vision linked to a community with a shared future for mankind. On practice, Cao points to ecological red lines, a development path said to differ from the Western model of "pollute first, clean up later", international recognition of projects such as the Three-North Shelterbelt and Saihanba, and carbon peaking and neutrality efforts. On institutions, Cao lists systems such as ecological compensation, river and forest chief systems, the "same responsibility for Party and government" principle, and carbon-market mechanisms.

Cao concludes that this theory, practice and institutional system offer Chinese wisdom, a Chinese approach and Chinese strength for global green development and the progress of civilization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official scholarship frames China's ecological policy as a model for the world.
quoteEn: The great achievements of China's ecological civilization construction belong not only to China but also to the world.
quoteZh: 我国生态文明建设所取得的伟大成就不仅是中国的，也是世界的

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on environment and development, formalised after the 18th Party Congress (2012) and summarised in the "ten adherences".

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山

glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan attributed to Xi Jinping (2005) holding that environmental protection and economic prosperity are mutually reinforcing.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and joint responses to global problems, including ecological ones.
China's declared goals of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Telling the story of Chinese modernization in the capital of a major country in the new era
st: Beijing as material for ideological and political theory courses
zh: 讲好新时代中国式现代化的大国首都故事
paras: Ding Yun asks how university ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke) can tell the story of Chinese modernization through the example of Beijing. Taking up Xi Jinping's call to tell good stories about the new era, the article argues that the capital's development over the past decade offers vivid teaching material. Telling it well, Ding contends, is an important route to reforming these courses and raising them to a new level.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical basis, namely the distinctive features of Chinese modernization as presented in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The second reviews what Ding calls the Beijing chapter of Chinese modernization, drawing on five areas of Beijing's development. The third turns to teaching practice and the idea of the "big ideological and political course" (da sizhengke). It was published in Ideological and Educational Research, 2023, no. 3.

In Ding's account, Chinese modernization combines features common to all modernizations with Chinese ones: an enormous population, common prosperity, coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development. Ding presents these as going beyond Western modernization. Beijing's story is then told through five themes: reduced-scale development and the relocation of non-capital functions within Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei coordination; innovation backed by education, science and talent; green development and air-pollution control; people-centred urban governance, including the "respond to complaints" mechanism, which the article links to whole-process people's democracy; and opening up, including hosting the Belt and Road Forum and the Winter Olympics.

Ding proposes three steps for teaching. Courses should link the classroom to society by using Beijing's museums and mass activities. They should assemble a "big teaching corps" that includes model workers, heroes, scientists and officials, together with guides from memorial sites. They should also carry a "big mission": teaching students the national standpoint, innovation, green practice and a sense of responsibility for a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxism-school scholar links official accounts of Beijing's development to the design of ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Telling well the story of Chinese modernization in the capital of a major country is an important way to advance new reforms in ideological and political theory courses (hereafter "sizhengke") and to lift them to a new level in the new era.
quoteZh: 讲好中国式现代化的大国首都故事，是新时代推进思想政治理论课（以下简称“思政课”）新改革、升华思政课新境界的重要途径。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, set out prominently in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as having five main features, which the article lists.
Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities, commonly abbreviated as sizhengke.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's call to extend political education beyond the classroom into society and real-life practice, using wider resources and teachers.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented officially as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
An official term for China's democratic model, which stresses popular participation at every stage of governance, not only in elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations based on cooperation and shared interests, presented as China's contribution to global governance.

t: Mao Zedong's historical contribution to exploring the correct path of resolving ethnic issues with Chinese characteristics
zh: 毛泽东对探索中国特色解决民族问题正确道路的历史贡献
source: Journal of Xiangtan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2023 no. 1
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement at the Fifth Central Conference on Ethnic Work that the Party's greatest achievement in ethnic work is the "correct path of resolving ethnic issues with Chinese characteristics", Li Taojun asks what role Mao Zedong played in opening that path. The article argues that Mao and the Communists around him began the exploration, supplying the basic policies, the institutional foundation and the value principles of socialist ethnic relations in China.

The article is organised in three parts, which Li describes as moving along a historical axis and a thematic one. The first follows Mao's thinking and the Party's minority policy from the early 1920s through the Long March and the War of Resistance. The second covers the shift from federalism to regional ethnic autonomy and how that system was refined. The third sets out the values behind the system, which Li presents through the traditional contrast between "instrument" and "way".

Li's central claim is that the Party began with Soviet-influenced ideas of national self-determination and federation, which were never put into practice and were gradually abandoned. Mao's route to the Common Programme of 1949 ran through a class analysis of ethnic oppression, cautious and non-coercive work on the Long March, and the Inner Mongolian autonomous government of 1947 as a model. Li cites Mao's remarks of 1958 that China's demographic make-up, with Han people at 94 per cent, ruled out a Soviet-style union of republics. The article presents regional autonomy as socialist in character, dependent on training minority cadres, written into the 1954 constitution with flexibility for Tibet, and bound to central directives. It then identifies the guiding values as a multi-ethnic view grounded in the Chinese nation, ethnic equality and unity, opposition to both Han chauvinism and local nationalism, and religious harmony with freedom of belief.

In the conclusion Li traces the successful experience summed up in the 1992 formulation of the correct path back to Mao's theory and practice. The article states that Mao's approach accords with the laws governing the rise and decline of nations and with dialectical and historical materialism. It holds that the basic framework and good traditions of China's ethnic work follow from Mao's aim of great unity of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of how Mao's ethnic policy is presented in current Chinese Party scholarship, including his statements on autonomy, cadres and religion.
quoteEn: Ethnic equality is the most central and most fundamental element in Mao Zedong's view of nationalities.
quoteZh: 民族平等是毛泽东民族观中最为核心也是最根本的一条。

glossary.explanation: The system by which areas where minorities live in compact communities set up organs of self-government within the unitary state. It was set out in the 1949 Common Programme and written into the 1954 constitution.
The Party's term for attitudes and practices that privilege the Han majority over minorities. It is paired with 'local nationalism' as the 'two isms' to be opposed.
The Party's term for narrow nationalism among minority groups, treated as the counterpart of Han chauvinism.
The provisional governing programme adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in September 1949, which served as a temporary constitution before 1954.

t: Mao Zedong's strategic thinking on major questions of the Chinese revolution from a global perspective during the New Democratic Revolution
zh: 新民主主义革命时期毛泽东以世界眼光对中国革命重大问题的战略思考
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2023 no. 1
paras: Liu Huiqiang and Lian Tong ask how Mao Zedong, during the New Democratic Revolution, placed the Chinese revolution within world history. They argue that from his earliest explorations, with the 1920 aim of 'remaking China and the world', Mao treated Chinese questions as world questions. In their account, this global perspective ran through his judgements on the revolution's stages, position, nature, path and significance, and helped the Party find a path suited to China.

The article is organised in three parts followed by a conclusion. The first covers the new epoch opened by the October Revolution and Mao's division of the revolution into two steps.
