Li calls for work on three questions: what counts as "fine" in tradition, why integrate (rejecting wholesale Westernisation, "Chinese learning as substance" and cultural conservatism), and how, through practice rather than mere interpretation. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-school account of how the "second integration" is justified historically and theoretically within official discourse.
quoteEn: "Integration" is both a result and a process.
quoteZh: “相结合”既是结果，也是过程。

t: The formation, sources and logic of the narrative discourse of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 中国化时代化马克思主义叙事话语的形成、来源与逻辑
source: Research on Marxist Theory Education in Colleges and Universities, 2023 no. 1
paras: Responding to the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to build a Chinese discourse and narrative system and tell China's story well, Jia asks how the theoretical narrative discourse of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times took shape. The article treats this discourse as a core part of Chinese discourse and of the wider narrative system. It argues that it can be understood through three basic questions: its formation, its sources and its internal logic.

The article is built in three parts. The first periodises the discourse into four stages: from the founding of the Party to 1949; from 1949 to reform and opening up; from reform and opening up to the 18th Party Congress (2012); and the period since 2012. The second identifies six sources of discourse. The third sets out six principles that Jia presents as the discourse's internal logic.

In the historical part, Jia traces how each generation of Party leaders produced its own vocabulary: Mao Zedong's revolutionary and socialist-construction terms, the reform-era terms of Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, and, since 2012, Xi Jinping's terms such as Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind. The six sources are Marxist discourse (the basic source), the discourse of Chinese practice, traditional Chinese culture, the language of ordinary people, Western and other foreign discourse, and domestic and international scholarship. Jia ranks them: Marxist discourse supplies the foundation and method, while practice and tradition carry the Chinese context, and the rest are supplements. The logic is summarised as being based on practice, grounded in national conditions, problem-oriented, people-centred, referenced to the times and oriented to popularisation.

Jia concludes that this discourse grows out of Marxism and is continually refined from the experience of Chinese practice, drawing on traditional culture, popular speech and other resources. The author sees the three questions as the basis for developing the discourse further and explaining why Marxism works in China. Jia adds that further research should cover textual carriers, political standpoint, modes of thinking and discursive techniques. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-theoretical account of how Chinese leaders' signature phrases are classified by period, source and logic.
quoteEn: The narrative discourse of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is not an arbitrary pile or disordered arrangement of terms, but an "artistic whole" in which concepts, categories and propositions prove one another according to a definite logic, following Marxist materialism and dialectics.
quoteZh: 中国化时代化马克思主义叙事话语不是话语的任意堆积和无序摆放，而是遵循马克思主义唯物论和辩证法，按照一定的逻辑组成的概念、范畴和命题之间相互论证的“艺术整体”。

glossary.explanation: The language, concepts and modes of expression through which a theory or national story is told. In current Chinese usage it is linked to the effort to build China's own 'discourse power' abroad.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted under Xi Jinping and prominent in the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and governance concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2013, presented as a vision of cooperative international relations.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Core socialist values: the unity of "what" and "how to build" socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 社会主义核心价值观：中国特色社会主义“是什么”与“怎么建”的统一
paras: Sun Weiping and Yin Bangwen ask how the core socialist values relate to socialism with Chinese characteristics. They argue that the values express what that socialism is and also show how it should be built. In their account, the values are a concrete form of the communist values of Marx and Engels in contemporary China, and an organic part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has four sections. It first traces how the core socialist values emerged as a product of the Party's "value consciousness", from Marx and Lenin through Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then maps the three levels and twelve concepts onto the essence of socialism, and examines the relation between these values and "common human values". The last section sets out how the values bear on building socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The authors argue that each value matches a feature of socialism's essence as Deng Xiaoping defined it. Prosperity and common prosperity answer the liberation of the productive forces; democracy and the rule of law answer people's mastery of the country; civilisation and harmony follow from public ownership. They hold that the values absorb common human values such as peace, democracy and freedom, while the socialist values should in turn guide those common values. They contrast this with Western "universal values", which they say rest on private ownership and the "logic of capital".

On practice, Sun and Yin call for three things. The values should serve as the shared ideological basis for uniting a plural and fragmented society. They should guide institutional reform and top-level design, in a two-way interaction between values and institutions. They should direct national education so as to train "new people of the era". They conclude that the values give socialism with Chinese characteristics its direction and its spiritual core. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-theory account that links the core socialist values to the essence of socialism, to common human values and to institution-building.
quoteEn: The core socialist values answer the question of the positioning and direction of development of socialist China; they are the "soul of life" of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the "beacon" guiding socialist China forward in the new era.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观回答了社会主义中国的定位和发展方向问题，是中国特色社会主义的“生命之魂”，是新时代社会主义中国奋勇前进的“航标灯”。

glossary.explanation: A twelve-word set of values in three tiers (national, social, individual), set out in the report to the 18th Party Congress in 2012. They are promoted through education and public campaigns.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology under Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

Xi Jinping's formulation, first stated at the UN in 2015, of peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as shared human values. Official texts present it as distinct from Western "universal values".
The goal of shared wealth for all, which Deng Xiaoping included in his definition of socialism's essence. Xi Jinping has made it a major policy theme.

t: Commemorating International Women's Day means fighting for women's freedom and equality
st: Mao Zedong's 1939 Yan'an speech and a Party chronology of the women's movement
zh: 纪念三八妇女节，就是要争取妇女的自由与平等
paras: This compilation, posted on International Women's Day 2023, is not a research article. It combines excerpts from Mao Zedong's speech of 8 March 1939 in Yan'an with a Party-centred chronology of the Chinese women's movement. Its message is that women's liberation depends on organisation and on joining the wider struggle for national and social liberation.

The first part reproduces Mao's speech and his 1939 inscription poem for the magazine Chinese Women. The second part is a chronology from 1921 to 2023, drawn from sources such as Xinhua and CCTV. It covers the Soviet areas, the War of Resistance against Japan, the first national women's congress of 1949, the 1954 Constitution, the reform era and the Party congresses since 2012.

In the speech, Mao says the Chinese nation and people lack freedom and equality under imperialism and feudal forces. He argues that no great task, whether resisting Japan or increasing production, can succeed without women. He adds that women's strength is scattered unless they form organisations. He also holds that social liberation requires mobilising women, and that women's own liberation requires joining that struggle, with rights to manage affairs, to hold meetings and to speak. The chronology presents equality policy as continuous under Party leadership. It cites the Party's gender-equality commitments in the 18th Party Congress (2012) report, repeated in the 19th and 20th, and a greeting from Xi Jinping on 6 March 2023.

The compilation presents women's emancipation as a project realised under Party leadership, from Mao's call for organisation to current policy. Read the original if you want Mao's 1939 wording on women and the national struggle, or a short official chronology of the women's movement and its legal milestones.
quoteEn: To achieve true social liberation, the broad masses of women must be mobilised to take part; likewise, to achieve women's own liberation, women must take part in the struggle for social liberation.
quoteZh: 要真正求得社会解放，就必须发动广大的妇女参加；同样，要真正求得妇女自身的解放，妇女们就一定要参加社会解放的斗争。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese name for International Women's Day on 8 March. Communist-led women's groups observed it in China from the 1920s, and it is marked in Yan'an in this speech.

t: Chinese modernization: a great creation in "skipping the Caudine Forks"
zh: 中国式现代化：“跨越卡夫丁峡谷”的伟大创造
paras: How can an economically and culturally backward country modernize? Wang Gonglong takes up this question through Marx's late hypothesis that Russia might "skip the Caudine Forks" of capitalism. Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Wang argues that Chinese modernization is a socialist path taken by a non-Western country without passing through the capitalist system. In this reading it both verifies Marx's hypothesis in practice and develops it creatively.

The article has four sections. The first traces the origins of the hypothesis against Marx's critique of Western capitalist modernization. The second presents Chinese modernization as the successful "answer" to a problem that Marx only "posed" and that the Soviet Union, in Wang's account, failed to solve. The third sets out three ways in which China's experience confirms the hypothesis. The fourth lists five creative developments of it.

Wang reconstructs the hypothesis in three logical steps: skipping is necessary, possible and conditional. The conditions are economic (absorbing capitalism's positive achievements, including advanced productive forces and the market), historical (socialist victory in the West) and revolutionary (a mutually reinforcing revolution in East and West). Wang observes that the last two conditions never materialised, which left the question open. The author's answer is that China built socialist institutions that in turn drove productive forces forward, combined rapid growth with long-term stability, and set out to avoid capitalism's "chain of problems". The article lists these problems as polarisation, alienation, crisis, plunder abroad and ecological strain.

Wang names five creative developments: the socialist market economy; a "parallel" strategy that integrates industrialisation, urbanisation, agricultural modernization and informatisation, in contrast to the Western "serial" sequence; a path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; a framework for coexistence between two systems through a community with a shared future for mankind; and inspiration for other developing countries. The author concludes that the path answers a major question in the history of socialism and will shape world socialism and human modernization in the twenty-first century. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese scholarship links Marx's late writings on Russia to the official narrative of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a new path of socialist modernization that a non-Western country has successfully explored in human history without going through the capitalist system.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是人类历史上非西方国家不通过资本主义制度而成功探索出的社会主义现代化新道路

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of socialist modernization under Communist Party leadership, elaborated especially in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations based on joint development and peaceful coexistence.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse: restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity by the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: Major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics in the new era: strategy and practical requirements
zh: 新时代中国特色大国外交战略及其实践要求
paras: Gao Zugui, director of the Institute of International Strategy at the Central Party School, asks what strategy and practical requirements the 20th Party Congress (2022) set for major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics. The article argues that as the world faces profound change, Chinese diplomacy should be built on a single overall goal, a community with a shared future for mankind, pursued through a peaceful development path, an independent foreign policy of peace, opening up and reform of global governance. It also holds that China must be ready to struggle when its core interests are threatened.

The article begins with Gao's reading of the international situation, then moves through eight areas of practice. These cover the aim and overall goal of foreign work; the peaceful development path; the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence and a new type of international relations; opening up as a basic national policy; global governance; the Global Development Initiative and Global Security Initiative; and common values of humanity. A final section calls for daring and skilful struggle. Gao draws throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches and the 20th Party Congress report.

Gao describes the "great changes unseen in a century" as a change in the world, in the era and in history. In his account, developed countries' share of world GDP fell from 78.85 per cent in 2001 to 59.08 per cent in 2021, while emerging and developing economies rose to 40.92 per cent. He also points to rising unilateralism and protectionism, and to a renewed coexistence of capitalism and socialism. Against this background, the article presents the community with a shared future for mankind as a Chinese contribution that does not replace one system or civilisation with another. It treats China's development as peaceful by character and rejects the claim that a strong country must seek hegemony. It sets "extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits" against hegemonic and bloc politics. It presents the "common values of humanity" as going beyond Western "universal values" and the clash-of-civilisations thesis.

Gao concludes that China must keep the initiative over its own development and security by relying chiefly on its own strength. He expects external containment to intensify, with the United States named as the main source of pressure. He says China must keep its strategic resolve, hold to bottom-line thinking and be prepared for severe tests, while working for peace and common development. Read the original if you want a systematic Party School account of how the 20th Party Congress's foreign policy line is framed and justified.
quoteEn: The most fundamental thing is to base the nation's development on its own strength, to run our own affairs well, and to hold the destiny of China's development and progress firmly in our own hands.
quoteZh: 最根本的是坚持把国家和民族发展放在自己力量的基点上，把我们自己的事情做好，把中国发展进步的命运牢牢掌握在自己手中。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward from 2013 as the overarching aim of Chinese foreign policy. Official texts describe it as a world of common security and prosperity that does not replace one system with another.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
glossary.explanation: Mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. They were jointly advanced by China, India and Myanmar in 1954.

glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.explanation: The official formula (共商共建共享) for Xi Jinping's approach to global governance: decisions made through wide consultation, institutions built jointly, and benefits shared by all.
A proposal Xi Jinping put forward in 2021. It stresses putting development first and aligns with the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
A proposal Xi Jinping put forward in 2022. It promotes a concept of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security and the principle that security is indivisible.

Xi Jinping's formulation, first given in 2015, of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared by all. Official texts present it as an alternative to Western "universal values".

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The political-civilisation implications of the Chinese modernization path
st: Centred on the new type of state system
zh: 中国式现代化道路的政治文明意蕴探析
zhSub: 以新型国家制度为中心
paras: Li Yingrui asks what the political-civilisation content of Chinese modernization is, and answers by looking at China's "new type of state system" (xinxing guojia zhidu). The article argues that the path's political-civilisation meaning is concentrated in this system, which it presents as both distinctively Chinese and as enriching the forms of human political civilisation. Li treats the topic as relevant to developing socialism with Chinese characteristics, modernising national governance and telling China's story abroad.

The article has three parts. The first traces the system's century-long evolution in five "historic developments": early Soviet-republic experiments, the New Democratic republic, the establishment of the socialist state system in the 1950s, the formation of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics after reform and opening up, and the more mature and defined system of the new era. The second part sets out the system's threefold meaning and six defining features. The third assesses its contributions to human political civilisation.

Li defines the system as socialist, as a system with Chinese characteristics, and as a new kind of modern state system. On the last point, Li says it has not fully escaped the logic of capital, yet it criticises and goes beyond the capitalist modern state through what the article calls "new modernity". Its six features are a economic base with public ownership as the mainstay, Communist Party leadership, the political value of putting the people first, democratic centralism, whole-process people's democracy, and a united-front "base colour". Li then claims three contributions: a "people's logic" that breaks capital's domination of state-building, a Chinese democratic discourse that criticises and goes beyond Western democratic discourse, and a demonstration of institutional diversity that guides developing countries. In Li's account, Western liberal democracy faces crises and the "end of history" thesis has been refuted.

Li concludes that the system, as a product of the Party's creative development of the Marxist theory of the state, can promote China's development and has world-historical significance. Li calls for building a theoretical, discourse and academic system for China's institutional construction, rebutting distortions of the Chinese path, and turning institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. Read the original if you want a systematic example of how Chinese Party theorists narrate the state system's history and present its comparison with Western political models.
quoteEn: The successful practice of China's new type of state system shows that, although countries' institutional civilisations differ, civilisations are not higher or lower, and no single identical institutional form exists that suits every country.
quoteZh: 中国新型国家制度的成功实践表明，虽然各个国家的制度文明存在着差异，但文明没有高低贵贱之分，世界上也不存在一种完全相同的、能够适用一切国家的制度形式。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernity, prominent in Party discourse since the 2021 centenary and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as combining material, political, cultural-ethical, social and ecological advancement.
A term for China's socialist state institutions, described as guaranteeing that the people are masters of the country and as distinct from both capitalist and traditional Soviet-style systems.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019 to describe Chinese socialist democracy as covering all stages and fields of political life, not only elections.
An organisational principle, formulated in Leninist parties, combining democratic discussion with centralised, binding decisions; in China it also guides the organisation of state organs.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 守正创新推进马克思主义中国化时代化
paras: Deng Chundong takes up a principle from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), 'We must stay committed to the principle of upholding fundamental truths and breaking new ground' (守正创新). The article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2023, argues that this principle is the key to continuing to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In Deng's account, abandoning fundamentals leads to betrayal of Marxism, while abandoning innovation leads to dogmatism and stagnation.

The piece is a three-part commentary in the style of Party theory writing. It first sets out why the principle matters, drawing on the history of Marxism, world socialism and the Party's century of struggle. It then explains the 'three unwaverings' that make up fidelity to fundamentals, and finally the requirements of innovation. Deng relies heavily on Xi Jinping's statements and the 20th Party Congress report.

On fidelity, Deng calls for unwavering commitment to the basic principles of Marxism, to the Party's overall leadership, and to socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author calls Party leadership the 'core code' of past achievements. On innovation, Deng presents the two as dialectically unified: both rest on respect for objective laws, namely the laws governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development. Deng warns against treating rigid dogmatism or repeated past errors as fidelity. Deng also warns against treating policies that depart from Marxist fundamentals, or the copying of Western capitalist governance, as innovation.

Deng proposes that theoretical innovation start from China's actual conditions and combine Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It should also answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. This means studying contemporary capitalism and the 'great changes unseen in a century', and engaging with Marxism outside China selectively, neither rejecting it wholesale nor copying it. The article ends by calling for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to guide practice and for new openings under the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists frame the balance between orthodoxy and innovation after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: At bottom, both upholding fundamentals and innovating are a steadfast adherence to Marxism, which reveals objective laws, and through innovation new laws are continually revealed.
quoteZh: 守正与创新，本质上都是对揭示客观规律的马克思主义的坚守，并通过创新不断揭示新的规律。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental truths and breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keep to the correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A principle listed among the 'six musts' in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It pairs fidelity to Marxist fundamentals and the Party's line with theoretical and practical innovation.
The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Advancing the Two Integrations to write a new chapter in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 推进“两个结合”谱写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章
authors: Party School of the CPC Central Committee (National Academy of Governance) Council
paras: Published in Qiushi after the 20th Party Congress (2022) and signed by the Party School's governing council, this commentary asks how theoretical innovation should continue on the new journey. Its answer is that the Two Integrations must be upheld consistently. These are combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The article presents this as the fundamental route for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The text has three parts. The first reviews the integration of Marxism with China's concrete conditions since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second covers integration with fine traditional Chinese culture. The third sets out tasks for the future. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches and the 20th Party Congress report, and gives examples of what it calls original contributions.

The article argues that the Party has tied theory to the changing national situation. Examples are the judgement at the 19th Party Congress (2017) that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era and that the principal contradiction in society had changed. It says this is not a break with orthodoxy: Marx's and Engels's analysis of capitalism's basic contradictions has not become outdated, and "keeping to the fundamental" does not mean conservatism. It lists new ideas it considers original, including the Party's leadership as the defining feature of the system, a people-centred approach, the new development philosophy, and the Party's self-reform. On culture, it says Xi has joined the essence of Marxism with traditional ideas. Examples are harmony between humanity and nature behind ecological civilization thought, and the 'all under heaven' worldview behind a community with a shared future for mankind. It also links people-as-the-foundation thought to whole-process people's democracy.

For the future, the article proposes holding to the worldview and methods summed up in the "six musts" of the 20th Party Congress report. It also calls for organising theory around the Party's central task of building a modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. A third call is for firm historical and cultural confidence, so that theoretical innovation becomes what it calls comprehensive innovation in a civilizational sense. The article closes by urging the Party to arm itself with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how Party institutions present the Two Integrations and the link between Marxism and traditional culture.
quoteEn: Keeping to the fundamental is not the same as being conservative; only by upholding it can we develop better.
quoteZh: 守正不等于守旧，坚持才能更好发展。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to official formulations in 2021–2022.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official term, prominent since the 20th Party Congress, for China's own path to building a modern socialist country.
The official description of China's democratic system as involving popular participation at every stage of governance.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared global interests and joint development.
The official idea that the Party must continually purify and renew itself, presented as a way to avoid the historical cycle of rise and decline.

t: The scientific connotations and major significance of the "five paths that must be followed"
zh: “五个必由之路”的科学内涵与重大意义
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily interprets a formulation from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): the "five paths that must be followed" (wu ge biyou zhi lu). These hold that the Party's overall leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, unity and struggle, the new development philosophy, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party are each the indispensable route to, respectively, developing socialism, national rejuvenation, historic achievements, national growth and the Party's lasting vitality. Xin Xiangyang argues that the formulation is at once a summary of history, a conclusion about the present and a roadmap for the future, and that its principles, theory and philosophy should be grasped in depth.

The article has two parts. The first sets out four aspects of the formulation's meaning. The second sets out three aspects of its significance, and a closing paragraph ties the formulation to the Party's century of struggle, more than seventy years of the People's Republic, over forty years of reform and opening up, and the ten years of the new era.

On meaning, Xin reads "biyou" as implying that there is no other way, and treats the formulation as the core code of the Party's achievements. It is presented as a law-like conclusion drawn from the Party's century of experience, as an answer to the questions of which banner to raise, which road to take and which goal to pursue, and as an organic whole rather than five separate items. Party leadership is described as the skeleton running through all five, and Xin urges that they be studied together with the "ten adherences" and the "nine musts". On significance, Xin presents the formulation as a methodological principle to be cherished and upheld, as the basis for meeting the people's expectations on the "new road to the examination" (the Party's new test of governing), and as the path for going beyond Western modernization and creating a new form of human civilization.

Xin concludes that the formulation bears on the Party's future, the nation's destiny, the people's wellbeing and human progress, and so must be cherished and upheld consistently. He also states that it offers a reference for other developing countries and "Chinese wisdom" for human problems. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 20th Party Congress formulation was interpreted in official Party-theory commentary soon after the Congress.
quoteEn: The "five paths that must be followed" are at once a summary of history, a conclusion about reality, and above all a path for the future.
quoteZh: “五个必由之路”既是历史的总结，也是现实的结论，更是未来的路径。

glossary.en: five paths that must be followed
glossary.explanation: A formulation in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) listing five essentials: Party leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, unity and struggle, the new development philosophy, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s, combining Marxism with China's conditions and the reform-era market economy.
A guideline put forward in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's disciplinary and organisational tightening, including anti-corruption work, since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: How is the creation of a "Chinese original Marxist philosophy" possible?
zh: 创建“中国原创性马克思主义哲学”何以可能
paras: Liu Tongfang and Liu Tian ask whether and how a "Chinese original Marxist philosophy" can be created, taking their cue from the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to keep writing new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They argue that such a philosophy is necessary, faces two real difficulties, and is now feasible. In their view it should function as a scientific community that drives theoretical innovation and as a platform on which Chinese and Western thought can coexist and reinforce each other.

The article is organised in three parts: why creation is necessary, why it is difficult, and why it is feasible. It draws on hermeneutics, Thomas Kuhn's notion of paradigm and scientific community, and Ferdinand Tönnies' distinction between community and society. It also uses the Frankfurt School, as analysed by Rolf Wiggershaus, as a reference case for how a school coheres. Domestic examples include the textbook-system debates of the reform era and Chinese Marxist archaeology.

On necessity, the authors say Western-centred social science holds a discursive hegemony that treats its own perspective as universal, while Chinese Marxist philosophy suffers a paradigm crisis, scattered individual research and theory that lags behind practice. On difficulty, they identify a relative lack of autonomous, original concepts, though they list examples such as \"Chinese modernization\", and a lack of shared recognition among scholarly communities divided by lineage, region and method. On feasibility, they hold that the Frankfurt School's real \"inner principle\" was a problem-consciousness oriented to its own era. For Chinese scholars they derive three requirements: shared research questions centred on Chinese modernization; resource sharing and integration that produces internationally influential work, in a \"harmony without uniformity\" polyphony and without isolation from Western scholarship; and a critical and self-critical character aimed at construction, not nihilism.

The authors conclude that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the necessary conditions, including a large research workforce and funding, are in place. They present clarifying necessity, difficulties and community principles as only a starting point, with further theoretical and practical work left to the scholarly community. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Marxist philosophers frame the project of a self-reliant knowledge system and use the Frankfurt School as a model for school-building.
quoteEn: A system of autonomous, original categories whose content is Chinese practical experience is the substance of China's autonomous knowledge system.
quoteZh: 以中国实践经验为内容的自主性、原创性范畴体系，是构成中国自主知识体系的实质。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of adjusting Marxism to Chinese conditions and contemporary developments. The 20th Party Congress report presented it as an ongoing historical responsibility.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The milestone significance of the great transformation of the past decade in the new era
zh: 新时代十年伟大变革的里程碑意义
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily and posted on the Academy of Marxism site in February 2023, asks what the changes of the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012) mean in historical terms. Gong Yun argues that the "great transformation" of the new era is a milestone in the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, of socialism worldwide and of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised as a series of five claims about what the decade achieved. These concern the Party's strengthened leadership, the renewed historical initiative of the Chinese people, the irreversible progress of national rejuvenation, the revitalisation of scientific socialism in twenty-first-century China, and the decisive role of the Two Establishes. It closes with a call to unity, citing Mao Zedong's 1957 remarks on the path to an ideal society.

On the Party, Gong says that under the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the Eight-point Regulations and an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign produced an "overwhelming victory". The author presents this as finding a "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and decline through the Party's self-reform. On development, Gong cites GDP growth from 54 trillion to 114 trillion yuan, a world share of 18.5 per cent, urbanisation of 64.7 per cent, the eradication of extreme poverty and a moderately prosperous society as evidence that national rejuvenation is now irreversible. Gong also contends that Chinese modernization surpasses capitalist modernization, has revived the standing of socialism after the Cold War, and offers humanity a new option, citing the Italian Communist Party leader Mauro Alboresi.

Gong concludes that these achievements were won by struggle and that the Two Establishes are their decisive factor and the Party's greatest source of certainty. The author calls on the whole Party and people to rally around the Central Committee, uphold the banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and continue the drive toward a modern socialist country and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative of the new era's first decade is framed for a mass readership in the People's Daily.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization, successfully advanced and expanded in the new era, has surpassed capitalist modernization.
quoteZh: 新时代成功推进和拓展的中国式现代化，超越了资本主义现代化。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Party leadership since 2012 covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
Official term for the Party's claimed ability to purify and renew itself without external checks, presented as its answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A formulation adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's core status in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Official concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path to a modern socialist country as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party rhetoric under Xi Jinping: restoring China to a strong, prosperous position after the 'century of humiliation'.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucracy and formalism among officials.

t: Advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through Chinese modernization
zh: 《求是》杂志评论员：以中国式现代化全面推进中华民族伟大复兴
paras: This commentary by a Qiushi journal commentator, republished from Hongqi Wengao in February 2023, is a study guide to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Its starting point is Xi Jinping's statement that the Party's central task is to lead the people in building a modern socialist country and to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. The commentator argues that this path is the bright road to national rejuvenation, and that it must be grasped in its distinctive features, essential requirements and guiding principles.

The text has four sections. The first traces the history of modernization goals from Sun Yat-sen's Plans for National Reconstruction through the periods of revolution, reform and opening up, and the 19th Party Congress's two-stage plan to 2035 and mid-century. The second sets out the five features and nine essential requirements of Chinese modernization set by the congress report. The third presents five major principles for the road ahead. The fourth turns to the opening phase of the new journey and to economic work in 2023.

The commentator contends that, before the Communist Party was founded, every attempt at a modernizing path to national revival failed. Under Party leadership, in this account, China completed in decades an industrialization that took Western countries centuries, and achieved rapid growth together with long-term stability. Chinese modernization is described as socialist modernization led by the Party and serving the majority, set against Western modernization characterised as capital-centred, polarising, materialist and based on expansion and plunder. The five principles are upholding the Party's leadership, the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a people-centred approach, deepening reform and opening up, and fighting spirit. The text also calls for vigilance and bottom-line thinking in the face of severe tests.

For the near term, the commentator names high-quality development as the primary task and says 2023 is the first year of implementing the congress's decisions. The article acknowledges weak demand, supply shocks and weakening expectations, but maintains that China's economy is resilient and that the long-term fundamentals are sound. It calls for steady progress, a new development pattern and greater market confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party press summarised and promoted the 20th Congress's modernization agenda in early 2023.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization transcends the old Western road of capital-centred, polarising, materialistic and expansionist modernization, and enriches and develops world theory and practice of modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，是对西方以资本为中心的现代化、两极分化的现代化、物质主义膨胀的现代化、对外扩张掠夺的现代化老路的超越，是对世界现代化理论和实践的丰富和发展。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official concept of a socialist modernization path suited to China's conditions. It was formalised at the 20th Party Congress (2022) with five features and nine essential requirements.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse, linked to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.
The official economic paradigm that emphasises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. The 20th Congress named it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
The official name for China's governing ideology and system since the reform era, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and market-oriented reform.

t: Chinese modernization seen through the coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement
zh: 从物质文明和精神文明相协调看中国式现代化
authors: Xi Jinping Economic Thought Research Center
paras: Taking up the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this article from the Xi Jinping Economic Thought Research Center examines one of the five features of Chinese modernization: the coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement (wuzhi wenming and jingshen wenming). The authors argue that material abundance and spiritual richness together are the fundamental requirement of socialist modernization, and that this coordination must run through the whole modernization drive.

The piece, published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2023, has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical and historical logic of the principle, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin and the Party's own record. The second describes the vision for 2035 and the mid-century goal in both material and cultural-ethical terms. The third lists practical requirements.

In the authors' reading, Marxism treats the two civilizations as a dialectical unity: material production conditions cultural life, while ideas react back on material conditions. They hold that the Party has long pursued both, from Mao Zedong's early statements through Deng Xiaoping's strategy of 'grasping with both hands' to the efforts since the 18th Party Congress (2012) on ideology and values. They contend that development of material wealth alone, without cultural-ethical progress, would not be genuine socialist modernization. The vision joins a prosperous China (economic strength, innovation, national security, better livelihoods) with a culturally flourishing one (core socialist values, common prosperity, strength in education and culture). The practical section calls for promoting 'all-round abundance of material things' through high-quality development and the new development philosophy, widely practising core socialist values, promoting fine traditional Chinese culture through creative transformation, and advancing 'all-round human development' under a people-centred approach.

The authors conclude that economic development must remain central while cultural-ethical work is pursued with equal persistence, so that the nation gains both material strength and spiritual force. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists in 2023 explained this feature of Chinese modernization and the policy tasks they attached to it.
quoteEn: It requires not only a higher material standard of living, with every household well provisioned and clothed, but also a rich cultural and spiritual life in which everyone knows propriety and can tell honour from disgrace.
quoteZh: 不仅要求物质生活水平提高、家家仓廪实衣食足，而且还要求精神文化生活丰富、人人知礼节明荣辱。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is said to have five features, including common prosperity and coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement.
A paired formula for economic and material progress on one side and cultural, ideological and moral progress on the other. It has been a staple of Party discourse since the Deng Xiaoping era.
A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels, such as prosperity, democracy, harmony and patriotism.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, which the Party presents as a basic requirement of socialism and an aim of Chinese modernization.
The official economic goal that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. The 20th Party Congress called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
A guiding framework of five concepts: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It was put forward in 2015.

t: Firmly grasping the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the history of New China
zh: 牢牢把握新中国史的主题主线、主流本质
paras: This newspaper commentary responds to Xi Jinping's congratulatory letter on the 30th anniversary of the Chinese Society for the History of the People's Republic of China. Song Yuehong takes up the letter's call to firmly grasp the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the history of New China. The author argues that studying the letter requires an objective, comprehensive and accurate understanding of New China's development, achievements and experience, so that research, publicity and education on that history can advance with high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the theme and main threads of New China's history, tracing how the Party's goals and its reading of the principal social contradiction changed from the socialist revolution and construction period through reform and opening up to the new era. The second defines the mainstream and essence of that history. The third draws out what this means for research, with proposals on topics and on building the discipline.

On the theme, Song states that New China's history is a history of entrepreneurship, exploration and struggle, and that its theme is to keep adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, to found and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics, and to build a modern socialist country and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Citing Engels' image of history as a resultant of many forces, Song lists four main threads: safeguarding sovereignty and world peace and building a community with a shared future for mankind; upholding Marxism and the Party's self-reform; advancing Chinese modernization and common prosperity; and achieving complete national reunification. The mainstream is described as building and strengthening the country, taking its own path and benefiting the people. Song acknowledges mistakes and a serious setback in the socialist construction period, but presents them as part of exploration whose theoretical results and material base prepared the ground for later reform.

Song concludes that research should clarify the historical necessity of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, study Chinese modernization as running through New China's history, and build the discipline, academic and discourse systems of New China history. The author also calls for combining source collection with theory and for openly opposing historical nihilism. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party historians are told to frame the history of the People's Republic and set research priorities.
quoteEn: The mainstream of New China's history can be expressed as founding, rejuvenating and strengthening the country, taking its own path, bringing benefit to the people and helping build a better world, with brilliant achievements and broad prospects.
quoteZh: 新中国史的主流可表述为，立国兴国强国，走自己的路，为民造福，推动建设美好世界，成就辉煌、前景广阔。

glossary.explanation: The history of the People's Republic of China since 1949, treated as a distinct field of research, publicity and education alongside Party history.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that negate or distort the Party's and the revolution's history; the term is used polemically against such interpretations.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each era.
The Party's official description of China's path to modernization, said to share features with other countries while having distinct Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and cooperation.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, emphasised under Xi Jinping.
The official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself.

t: Chinese modernization: inheriting and innovating Marx's thought on modernization
zh: 中国式现代化：马克思现代化思想的传承与创新
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Dou Yongchao takes up Chinese modernization, set out systematically in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and asks how it relates to Marx's own thinking. The article's thesis is that Chinese modernization is essentially an inheritance and creative development of Marx's thought on modernization, and that it should therefore be examined at the level of Marxist theory rather than only through its historical, comparative or world-significance dimensions, which Dou says dominate current scholarship.

The article has two main parts. The first reconstructs the theoretical logic of Marx's thought on modernization, although Marx never used the term itself. The second sets out how Chinese modernization carries forward and innovates on this thought in four respects: value standpoint, development path, civilizational structure and ideal goal. A short conclusion follows.

In Dou's reconstruction, Marx understood modernization through the "economic formation of society", as the transition to the modern bourgeois mode of production, and criticised its capitalist form dialectically. Capital produced vast productive forces, cities, modern states and a world market, but also economic crisis, ecological crisis and alienation between people, nature and things. Marx therefore pointed to a new type of modernization, aimed at the free and all-round development of the individual and, in his late reflections on Russia, possibly reachable without passing through capitalism. Dou argues that Chinese modernization carries this forward. Its people-centred standpoint develops Marx's "interests of the immense majority" and draws on Chinese minben (people-as-foundation) ideas. Under Party leadership it seeks to steer capital rather than be ruled by it, pursues harmony between humanity and nature, and treats material modernization as serving the modernization of people. The five-sphere layout and the goals of high-quality development, whole-process people's democracy and common prosperity extend Marx's account of future civilization, while the community with a shared future for mankind is presented as the present-day expression of communist ideals fused with the traditional Datong (Great Harmony) ideal.

Dou concludes that Marx's thought supplies the theoretical guidance for Chinese modernization, while Chinese practice provides the ground for developing that thought further. Chinese modernization is described as an important result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It is said to move socialism with Chinese characteristics towards communism, and Dou calls for continued theoretical and practical innovation, guided by Marx's thought, Chinese conditions and traditional culture, in a world where capitalism and socialism coexist. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar derives the official concept of Chinese modernization from Marx's critique of capital and from his late writings on non-Western paths.
quoteEn: Marx's thought on modernization provides theoretical guidance for the path of Chinese modernization, and Chinese modernization lays the practical foundation for the innovative development of Marx's thought on modernization.
quoteZh: 马克思现代化思想为中国式现代化道路提供了理论遵循，中国式现代化为马克思现代化思想的创新发展奠定了实践基础。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path under Party leadership, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 and set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western capitalist modernization.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping's development thinking, holding that development should start from, rely on and benefit the people.
An official term for China's socialist democracy, which the Party says involves the people in every stage of governance, not only in elections.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the Party has emphasised in the new era as a defining feature of socialism.
The official term for a development model that stresses quality, innovation and balance rather than speed of growth alone.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, which stresses shared interests and joint responses to global problems.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the demands of each era.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: A programmatic document for advancing the rule of law in China in the new era and on the new journey
zh: 新时代新征程推进法治中国建设的纲领性文件
paras: Writing shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhou Youyong presents the Congress report's chapter on "upholding law-based governance in all respects and advancing the building of a rule-of-law China" as a programmatic document for the new era. The article argues that the chapter, the first in a Congress report to treat the topic in a dedicated section, sets out the direction and tasks of legal construction under Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law. Zhou takes it as showing the Party's determination to pursue the rule of law, and as the guide for the new journey.

The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscripts, has three parts. The first reviews the achievements of the decade since 2012 and credits them to Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law. The second links Chinese modernization to law-based governance. The third summarises the report's general requirements and four priority tasks: the legal system centred on the Constitution, law-based administration, fair justice, and a law-based society.

Zhou's central claim is that modernization and the rule of law are internally bound together. Law is both a basic guarantee of national modernization and part of its content, so a country that modernizes must also move to the rule of law. The article cites Xi Jinping's view that this must proceed through top-down and bottom-up interaction. It reads the report's call to "advance law-based governance in all areas of work" as meaning that law should run through economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development, as well as national security, the military, "one country, two systems" and international relations. Zhou also lists the guiding requirements: keep to the socialist rule-of-law path with Chinese characteristics, keep Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee, and keep a people-centred stance.

Zhou concludes that the Party must stay guided by Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law, hold to the goals set for a rule-of-law China, and provide long-term legal safeguards for building a modern socialist country and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The text is an authoritative-style exposition of the report rather than an independent analysis. Read the original if you want a concise, Party School-style account of how the 20th Party Congress framed the rule of law and its link to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: As the basic mode of governing the country, the rule of law is both a basic guarantee for achieving national modernization and an important part of it; a country that is to modernize must move towards the rule of law.
quoteZh: 法治作为治国理政的基本方式，既是实现国家现代化的基本保障，也是国家现代化的重要内容，国家要走向现代化必须走向法治化。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law
glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on law-based governance attributed to Xi Jinping, presented as a component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It was formally made the guiding ideology of law-based governance at a central work conference in November 2020.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for comprehensively governing the country according to law, under Party leadership. It became one of the "Four Comprehensives" strategic layout after 2014.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, often linked to the Chinese Dream.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law

t: Integrating the essence of Marxist thought with the shared values people live by without noticing
zh: 把马克思主义思想精髓同人民群众日用而不觉的共同价值观念融通起来
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily and posted on 27 February 2023, asks how Marxism can take firm root in China. Jiang Chang argues that the Two Integrations require the essence of Marxist thought to be fused with the common values that people hold and act on daily without being aware of them. Doing so, the author says, strengthens the historical and popular foundations for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece has three parts. The first describes how Marxism has already entered Chinese people's values. The second concerns consolidating a shared value system led by Marxist values. The third sets out how the fusion can be achieved gradually and almost imperceptibly.

Jiang holds that fine traditional Chinese culture contains distinctive values, such as the unity of heaven and humanity, the unity of knowing and doing, and governing by virtue, and that many of them are compatible with Marxism. This, in the author's account, helped Chinese people accept Marxism, and basic principles such as the primacy of matter and the people as makers of history are now widely held. The author presents the socialist core values as continuous with Marxist values, citing improved livelihoods, fairness and justice, and free and all-round human development. Both Marxist theory and core values, Jiang says, come from the people's practice and must work through it.

Jiang calls for two measures. The first is to make the Party's innovative theory, above all Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, take hold among the people, moving them from recognising Marxism to truly understanding and using it. The second is to promote the unity of knowing and doing, through Party-wide study and a learning society and through individual moral cultivation and practice. Read the original if you want a short example of how official commentary links Marxism, traditional culture and the socialist core values.
quoteEn: Turn the essence of Marxist thought and the requirements of the socialist core values into everyday rules of conduct, so that Marxism deeply shapes people's thoughts, words and actions and becomes the idea guiding their behaviour.
quoteZh: 把马克思主义思想精髓和社会主义核心价值观要求变成日常的行为准则，让马克思主义深刻影响人们的思想、言论、行动，成为指引人们行为的理念。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing the combination of Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to official discourse in 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the continuing effort to adapt Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the contemporary era.
A set of twelve values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at the national, social and individual levels, including prosperity, democracy, justice, patriotism and integrity.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the unity of knowing and doing
glossary.explanation: A concept from Chinese philosophical tradition, associated with Wang Yangming, that knowledge and practice are inseparable. The author uses it for turning Marxist understanding into conduct.

t: Linking up the essence of Marxism with the best of traditional Chinese culture
zh: 同中华优秀传统文化精华贯通起来
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily in early 2023, takes up a formula from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): linking up the essence of Marxist thought with the best of traditional Chinese culture. Shang argues that doing so requires understanding the essence of Marxism, drawing out the best of that culture, and studying the inner logic that connects the two.

The piece has three parts. The first presents Marxism as open to the achievements of human civilization and as a method rather than a dogma. The second traces how the Party has drawn on traditional culture since Marxism reached China. The third sets out what must be done next.

Shang notes that Marxism's three components built on German classical philosophy, British classical political economy and French utopian socialism. On this basis Shang holds that Marxism must be combined with each country's actual conditions, and that in China this is the work of the Two Integrations. Shang's examples include Mao Zedong's "seeking truth from facts", Deng Xiaoping's "moderately prosperous society" and Hu Jintao's "harmonious society". Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Shang says, Xi has linked the Marxist view of the masses to the idea of the people as the foundation of the state. He has also drawn on classical sayings on reform and patriotism, and on the ideal of "all under heaven as one family" to explain a community with a shared future for mankind. In Shang's account, Marxist dialectics in turn revitalise traditional culture.

Shang calls on Party members to grasp the essence of Marxism, in its worldview and methodology. They should also use that standpoint and method to mine the classic values of traditional culture, which Xi's report describes as highly compatible with scientific socialism. The aim is connection in content, fit in method and convergence in values. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Chinese commentators justify combining Marxism with traditional culture.
quoteEn: Marxism is not a dogma but a scientific method.
quoteZh: 马克思主义不是教条，而是科学方法。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to the formula in 2021–22.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states. It is used in official foreign-policy discourse.
A term from classical Chinese texts that Deng Xiaoping adopted as a development target for China.
A social goal promoted under Hu Jintao in the 2000s, stressing social balance and cohesion.
A classical phrase that Mao Zedong made the core of the Party's ideological line, meaning that policy should start from actual conditions.

t: Advancing economic theoretical innovation grounded in practice: making original contributions to developing Marxist political economy
zh: 不断推进实践基础上的经济理论创新 为发展马克思主义政治经济学作出原创性贡献
source: People's Daily (Renmin Ribao), reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 27 February 2023
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily, argues that Xi Jinping's economic thought, formed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), makes important original contributions to Marxist political economy. Zhou Wen presents it as upholding the basic principles and methods of Marxist political economy while summarising the Party's understanding of economic laws, especially those of socialist economic construction, and opening a "new realm" for the discipline.

The article is organised around three areas of contribution: deepening understanding of the laws of socialist economic construction, answering major questions of economic development in the new era, and resolving the relationship between government and market.

On the first area, Zhou argues that the stress on the Party's overall leadership of economic work enriches Marxist theory on the relation between economics and politics. The people-centred approach and the pursuit of common prosperity are said to clarify the nature and purpose of socialist production. Treating public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work alongside other methods, and the socialist market economy as the basic economic system is said to enrich theory on the market economy. On the second, Zhou describes the new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing as a systematic framework that answers questions about development's purpose, driving force, method and path. On the third, Zhou holds that combining the market's "invisible hand" with the government's "visible hand" overcomes the drawbacks of capitalist market economies and goes beyond Western mainstream economics in theory and practice.

Zhou concludes that this approach offers a fundamental guide for building a Chinese-style disciplinary, academic and discourse system in economics. In the new stage of development, Zhou calls for further research and practice on combining socialism with the market economy, so as to bring together an efficient market and a capable government. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style statement of how Chinese scholars frame Xi Jinping's economic thought as a contribution to Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: How to handle the relationship between government and market is the core question of a market economy, and also a worldwide puzzle in economics.
quoteZh: 如何处理好政府和市场的关系，是市场经济的核心问题，也是一个经济学世界性难题。

glossary.explanation: A framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 that centres development on five principles: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It is presented as the guiding principle of China's economic policy.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping as an objective of development and a corrective to inequality.
The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping since 2012, formally named in 2017 and treated as a component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, which combines market mechanisms with public ownership as the mainstay and Party leadership.

t: Supporting high-quality development: strengthening the building of the industrial workforce in the new period
zh: 为推动高质量发展提供支撑 加强新时期产业工人队伍建设
paras: This short commentary, originally published in the People's Daily in February 2023, asks how China should build up its industrial workforce to support high-quality development. Zhou argues that industrial workers are the main supporting force within the working class, and that stable industrial and supply chains, smarter, more digital and greener manufacturing, and more world-class firms all depend on a high-calibre workforce.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's call for a large army of knowledge-based, skilled and innovative industrial workers, and links it to the Reform Plan for Building the Industrial Workforce in the New Period. It then sets out three areas of work: skills improvement, diverse incentives and the protection of workers' rights.

On skills, Zhou calls for enterprises to draw up training plans, for large leading firms to host demonstration training bases for highly skilled personnel, and for skills competitions tied to major national projects and key industries. On incentives, the author proposes distribution that favours front-line workers, portable social insurance across ownership types, sectors and regions, and ending the dual-track system separating personnel management from worker management. The author also proposes allowances for highly skilled staff and distribution according to skills and innovation as factors of production.

On rights, Zhou urges strengthening democratic management through workers' congresses, open factory affairs, and worker directors and supervisors, with trade unions fulfilling their rights-protection duties and collective consultation institutionalised. The aim, in the author's words, is to build harmonious labour relations with Chinese characteristics and a social climate that respects labour and prizes skill. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style statement of the policy measures for industrial workers promoted in China in early 2023.
quoteEn: Create a social atmosphere that respects labour, values skills and encourages creativity, and strengthen the sense of honour and responsibility of the broad mass of industrial workers.
quoteZh: 营造尊重劳动、崇尚技能、鼓励创造的社会氛围，增强广大产业工人的荣誉感、责任感。

glossary.explanation: An official economic goal, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.
The basic form of democratic management in Chinese enterprises and public institutions, in which elected employee representatives review and discuss major workplace matters.
An official aim of cooperative relations between employers and employees, pursued through collective consultation, unions and legal protections; it derives from the 'harmonious society' idea.

t: Scientifically understanding and grasping the Party's innovative theory of the new era
zh: 科学理解和把握新时代党的创新理论
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 21 December 2022, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Liu Dehai takes up how the Party's innovative theory of the new era should be understood. Liu argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is the major theoretical achievement of the Party's exploration, and that it marks a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The commentary is organised in three parts. It first describes the content and structure of the Thought, then explains the Two Integrations, and finally turns to the Thought's worldview and methodology as summarised in the Congress report's "six musts".

Liu presents the "ten affirmations", the "fourteen commitments" and the "thirteen areas of achievement" as mutually reinforcing parts of one scientific theoretical system. On the Two Integrations, Liu says integration with China's specific realities means looking at the primary stage of socialism, the changed principal contradiction, and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation alongside global change. It means applying Marxism's worldview and method, not reciting its conclusions or treating it as dogma. Integration with fine traditional Chinese culture rests, in Liu's view, on the compatibility of ideas such as "the world belongs to all" and "the people as the foundation of the state" with the values of scientific socialism, and calls for creative transformation of that culture.

Liu reads the "six musts" (putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and a global vision) as an organic whole. In Liu's account, they answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. Liu calls on readers to use Marxism as the arrow aimed at the target of China in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style overview of how the Thought is framed after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The Two Integrations point out the fundamental path for advancing the Party's theoretical innovation, and reveal the secret of why the tree of Sinicized, contemporary Marxist theory stays evergreen.
quoteZh: “两个结合”深刻指明了推进党的理论创新的根本途径，揭示了中国化时代化马克思主义理论之树常青的奥妙所在。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added to official formulations in 2021–22.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the current era.
The official judgement that China is at an early stage of socialist development, which is expected to last a long time. It underlies the Party's policy line since the 1980s.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream.

t: Green development reflects the responsibility of a major country
zh: 绿色发展体现大国担当
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 30 October 2022, argues that green development, one element of the new development philosophy, both benefits China and shows China acting as a responsible major country. Men presents it as a guiding principle and a method of modernization.

The piece has two parts. The first, on how green development benefits China, links it to the report of the 20th Party Congress (2022) and to Chinese modernization, one of whose features is harmony between humanity and nature. The second, on how it benefits the world, reviews China's part in global climate, biodiversity and development governance.

In the first part Men quotes Xi Jinping's formula that protecting the ecological environment protects productive forces. Men then cites figures for the past decade: 960 million mu of afforestation, forest coverage of 24.02%, a 34.4% fall in carbon intensity, and coal's share of primary energy consumption falling from 68.5% to 56%. In the second part Men lists China's pledges and initiatives: peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060, the Global Development Initiative, South–South cooperation, the Kunming Declaration, and a green Belt and Road Initiative with partner agreements and an international coalition.

Men concludes that China has both positions and commitments, offers successful experience and public goods, and has won broad international recognition. The article holds that China's continued development and opening up will energise the global green economic recovery. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary in 2022 presented environmental achievements and global climate diplomacy as proof of major-country responsibility.
