quoteEn: China is showing the responsibility of a responsible major country, promoting reform of the global governance system and becoming an active participant, builder and leader of the international order.
quoteZh: 中国展现负责任大国的担当，推动全球治理体系变革，成为国际秩序的积极参与者、建设者、引领者。

glossary.explanation: Five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) set out by Xi Jinping at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in October 2015. They serve as an official guide to economic and social policy.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. Its listed features include harmony between humanity and nature.
A Chinese-led international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
An initiative Xi Jinping announced at the UN General Assembly in September 2021. It stresses development cooperation and the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

t: Xi Jinping Thought on Economy has enriched and developed Marxist political economy
zh: 习近平经济思想丰富发展了马克思主义政治经济学
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily in January 2023, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Economy has enriched and developed Marxist political economy. Yan presents it as an important component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In Yan's account, it grew out of practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and opens a new horizon for contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy.

The article is organised around three sets of "original contributions", each pairing a policy idea with the questions it answers and the Marxist theory it is said to extend. These cover the Party's leadership of economic work, the shift to high-quality development, and the reform of the market economy and opening up.

First, Yan holds that centralised, unified Party leadership of economic work and the people-centred approach to development answer the questions of the fundamental guarantee and standpoint of economic development. Yan links this to the Marxist relationship between economic base and superstructure. Second, the judgement that China has moved from high-speed growth to high-quality development, together with the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern, is said to answer questions of historical position, guiding principles and path. Yan presents this as continuing and innovating Marx and Engels's ideas on development principles, stages and social reproduction. Third, improving the socialist market economy, supply-side structural reform and the healthy development of economic globalization are said to address institutional foundations, the main line of work and opening up.

Yan concludes that these ideas deepen the Party's understanding of the laws of socialist construction, the socialist market economy and economic globalization, and extend Marxist theory on the economy and politics, on market economy and on the world economy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames Xi Jinping's economic thought as an innovation within Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Economy upholds a practice-oriented approach, looks at objective reality, and focuses on the problems of unbalanced and inadequate development in China's economy.
quoteZh: 习近平经济思想坚持实践导向，着眼客观实际，聚焦我国经济发展中的不平衡不充分问题

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, formally presented in the Party's official discourse as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official formulation, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and sustainability of economic development.
The Party's five-part guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
A strategy, launched in 2020, centred on the domestic economic cycle with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.
An economic policy line introduced in 2015 aimed at improving the structure of supply, such as cutting overcapacity, rather than relying mainly on stimulating demand.

t: On the global significance of Xi Jinping's economic thought
zh: 论习近平经济思想的世界意义
paras: Writing in the Party-run Economic Daily in October 2022, Zhou Wen asks what Xi Jinping's economic thought offers beyond China. The author argues that, formed in practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012), it answers questions such as "what is wrong with the world and what should we do" and gives "the key of wisdom" for resolving global development problems under today's complex conditions.

The commentary is organised in four parts: an introduction and three thematic sections. These present the thought's significance through high-quality development and the sharing of Chinese experience, the path of Chinese modernization as a Chinese approach to world development, the combination of an efficient market with an enterprising government, and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind in global governance. Zhou supports the argument with economic figures, quotations from Xi, and the Belt and Road Initiative.

Zhou's central claims are that modernization is not Westernization and that Chinese modernization is not a copy of Western models. According to the author, many developing countries that copied the West lost their autonomy and fell into stagnation and instability, whereas China industrialised in decades and rose peacefully, without colonial expansion. The author adds that China's socialist market economy, which combines public ownership with the market, has dispelled the "myth" of neoliberal economics and offers a model for handling the state–market relationship. Zhou cites GDP growth from 53.9 trillion yuan in 2012 to 114.4 trillion in 2021, and a World Bank assessment that the Belt and Road Initiative would lift millions out of poverty.

Zhou concludes that Xi Jinping's economic thought extends Marxist political economy, including its theory of the world economy, and that it points to a path for countries seeking both faster development and independence. The author presents China's initiatives, including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the New Development Bank and South–South cooperation funds, as steps towards narrowing the global development gap and reforming the global economic order. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Chinese commentary presents the international relevance of Xi Jinping's economic thought.
quoteEn: Modernization is not a single-choice question with the Western model as the answer but an open question that all countries explore together; nor is it a one-way street of the capitalist model, but a garden in which human civilizations compete to bloom.
quoteZh: 现代化不是西方模式的单选题，而是世界各国共同探索的开放题；现代化也不是资本主义模式的单行道，而是人类文明争相绽放的百花园。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping and developed since 2012. It is officially presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official policy goal that shifts emphasis from the speed of growth to its quality, efficiency and sustainability. It has been central to economic policy since 2017.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, introduced in 2012–13, which holds that countries' interests are interlinked and calls for joint governance and shared development.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s. It combines market mechanisms with public ownership and state macro-control.

t: The decisive significance and inner logic of the "Two Establishes"
zh: “两个确立”的决定性意义及内在逻辑
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 9 October 2022, explains why the Two Establishes are of decisive significance. Han Qingxiang argues that the Party's establishing of Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and of the guiding position of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is both necessary and decisive for the Party and the country.

Han opens with the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, which describes Xi as the main creator of this body of thought. The article then reads the Two Establishes through three "logics": theoretical, historical and practical (or realistic). It ends with a call to strengthen political, intellectual, theoretical and emotional identification with the Two Establishes.

On the theoretical side, Han grounds the Two Establishes in the historical-materialist unity of objective laws and subjective initiative. The objective tasks of the new era are building a modern socialist country, common prosperity and national rejuvenation. Han holds that achieving them depends on the masses and on the guiding role of leaders. On the historical side, Han points to the Zunyi Conference of 1935 and the achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as showing that the Party succeeds when it has a strong leadership core and correct guiding thought. On the practical side, Han argues that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is now irreversible and that no fundamental mistakes can be allowed. Han says that standing on the right side of history and keeping the initiative requires centralised Party leadership, continued adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and the two core establishments themselves.

Han concludes that, under Xi's leadership and guided by his thought, China has achieved the first centenary goal and is moving towards the second. The Two Establishes are presented as the fundamental guarantee of national rejuvenation. Han calls on Party members to turn identification with them into conscious action in carrying out the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official case for the Two Establishes was framed in the weeks before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The "Two Establishes" is a major judgement put forward around the aim of standing on the right side of history and taking the historical initiative.
quoteZh: “两个确立”是围绕站在历史正确一边并掌握历史主动而提出的重大论断。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's status as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party slogan requiring members to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The Party presents it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping since 2012. It refers to restoring China's national strength and international standing by mid-century.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all of the people, stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

t: Making willingness, courage and skill in taking responsibility a prevailing norm
zh: 让愿担当、敢担当、善担当蔚然成风
source: Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao); posted on marxism.cass.cn 24 February 2023
paras: Writing in early 2023, Yin Yuping takes up how the Communist Party can make its cadres willing, bold and skilled in taking responsibility (dandang zuowei). The commentary starts from Xi Jinping's speeches of December 2022 and January 2023, which list keeping up a drive to get things done among the unique problems the Party must solve. Yin argues that building incentive, protection and care mechanisms will make such conduct the prevailing norm. This, the author says, provides organisational support for building a modern socialist country and for national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization.

The piece has four parts. The first sets out why taking responsibility is required by the new journey of the new era. The second covers incentive and accountability mechanisms that build willingness to take responsibility. The third turns to mechanisms for tolerating and correcting errors, which aim to make cadres bold enough to act. The fourth deals with care for cadres, which Yin presents as the basis for building their skill. Each part draws heavily on Xi Jinping's remarks.

Yin first presents responsibility-taking as a political quality of the Party, a hallmark of the "good cadre" standard of loyalty, integrity and responsibility, and a practical route to the goals of the 20th Party Congress (2022). Yin sets these goals against warnings of "black swan" and "grey rhino" risks. The core institutional proposals follow. Evaluation should put political standards first, define specific cases of inaction, and reward those who take on difficult tasks. Accountability should be precise, since Yin says that over-broad or crude accountability produces the perverse result that those who act make more mistakes and those who do nothing make none. The error-tolerance mechanism should rest on Xi's "three distinctions", which separate inexperienced or exploratory mistakes from knowing violations of discipline and law, and it should follow clear procedures that guarantee cadres' right to appeal. Yin adds that tolerance is not an end in itself and must be paired with correction.

Yin concludes that rewards, tolerance and care must work together: strict management combined with warm concern, with particular support for grassroots cadres. Care is to take the form of trust and guidance at work, attention to daily and family difficulties, and moral support through honours and protection of reputation. The commentary offers no new theory but sets out how current Party policy on cadre management is meant to operate. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the Party's official reasoning on cadre incentives, accountability and error tolerance after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: To motivate cadres to get things done and start new ventures, there must be positive incentive and guidance mechanisms, negative disciplinary mechanisms, and also protection mechanisms.
quoteZh: 激励干部干事创业，既要有正面激励引导机制，也要有负向惩戒机制，还要有保护机制。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 and presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to a leading place among nations, linked to the 'second centenary goal' of a modern socialist country by 2049.

glossary.literal: to shoulder responsibility and take action
glossary.explanation: A cadre-management term for readiness to shoulder responsibility and act proactively, including in the face of risk and difficulty. Xi Jinping has made it a key criterion for assessing officials.
Xi Jinping's guideline for separating mistakes made through inexperience, in untested exploration, or without self-interest from deliberate violations of discipline and law.
The criteria for cadres set out under Xi Jinping: loyalty, integrity and a willingness to take responsibility.

t: Advancing and expanding Chinese modernization under the leadership of the Party
zh: 在党领导下推进和拓展中国式现代化
paras: This short commentary, written after the 20th Party Congress (2022), argues that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China. Yue Kui notes that the Congress report lists "upholding the leadership of the Communist Party of China" first among the essential requirements of Chinese modernization. In Yue's view, building a modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation require that Party leadership be applied in every field and link of the process.

The article has three parts. The first reviews how the Party has advanced and expanded Chinese modernization over more than a century. The second covers the blueprint set out by the 20th Party Congress. The third addresses how to gather the strength needed to carry it out.

Yue traces the Party's modernization goals from the revolutionary and construction period, through the reform and opening up era's concept of "Chinese-style modernization" and the three-step strategy, to the innovations since the 18th Party Congress (2012). On this account, history and reality show that Chinese modernization is led by the Party and suited to China's conditions. The author presents the Congress's two-stage plan, which calls for basic modernization by 2035 and a modern socialist country by the middle of the century, as consistent with China's reality and the people's wishes. Yue also contends that the Party, as the core of leadership, has united the whole nation, and that this unity produced the achievements of socialist modernization.

Yue concludes that the Party's overall leadership must be upheld and strengthened. The author calls for mobilising all positive factors, consolidating unity among the peoples of China and strengthening unity with Chinese people overseas. The article is a brief, official-style exposition of the Party-leadership theme in the Congress report. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars presented the link between Party leadership and Chinese modernization soon after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: History and reality fully show that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China, a modernization with Chinese characteristics that suits China's actual conditions.
quoteZh: 历史和现实充分表明，中国式现代化是中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化，是具有中国特色、符合中国实际的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. Official texts describe it as led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, meaning the restoration of China's national strength and international standing. It is tied to the two centenary goals.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: China's responsibility in promoting fairer development of the global governance system
zh: 促进全球治理体系公平发展的中国担当
paras: Writing in early 2023 in the wake of the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhao Zhongxiu asks how China has taken part in global governance and what further role it should play. The commentary, first published on Guangming Online, argues that under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era China has pursued high-level opening up and offered Chinese solutions to the world's "great changes unseen in a century". Zhao presents this as the conduct of a responsible major power.

The piece has two halves. The first surveys five fields in which China is said to have contributed: economic governance, health governance, poverty governance, security governance and climate governance. The second turns to the future, setting out five matching tasks. A short passage between them warns of obstacles in the international environment.

In the first half Zhao cites concrete evidence. It includes a fall in China's average import tariff from 15.3% to 7.4%, the negative-list system for foreign investment, and the declared completion of poverty eradication in 2020, ten years ahead of the UN 2030 Agenda target. It also includes a 48.4% cut in carbon intensity against 2005 and agreements on climate cooperation with 38 developing countries. Zhao contrasts this with protectionism, unilateralism, localism and pragmatism in the economic policies of developed countries, which in Zhao's view harm global development cooperation. China is cast as a "constant" amid a changing world economy.

For the future Zhao calls for several steps. These are multilateralism through the WTO, APEC and the G20 and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation; a global public health system and a Chinese global health strategy; and poverty reduction tied to the Belt and Road Initiative and to Chinese firms going abroad. Zhao also proposes opposing hegemonism, double standards and unilateral sanctions while giving developing countries a larger voice on security, and leading South-South climate cooperation while meeting the dual carbon goals. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese university leader presents China's global governance role, in official language, across economy, health, poverty, security and climate.
quoteEn: China will keep raising the quality and level of its opening up, show its consistent responsibility as a major power in promoting an open world economy, contribute to improving global governance, play the role of a \"constant\" amid changes in the world economy, and push global governance in a just and reasonable direction.
quoteZh: 中国将不断提高对外开放质量和水平，在促进开放型世界经济过程中展现负责任大国的一贯担当，为完善全球治理贡献力量，在世界经济变局中扮演“常量”，推动全球治理朝着公正合理的方向发展。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions.
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the current shift in the international order, often linked to the relative rise of emerging economies.
China's pledge to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and reach carbon neutrality before 2060.

t: Continuously shaping new drivers and new advantages for development
zh: 不断塑造发展新动能新优势
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in February 2023, reads the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) on education, science and technology, and talent. Pan notes that the report for the first time gave "implementing the strategy of invigorating China through science and education and strengthening talent support for modernization" its own section. In Pan's view, this shows a strategic outlook that treats the three fields as one whole in building China into a leading country in each.

The piece first sets out the three fields' place in building a modern socialist country, then cites achievements of the past decade. It then turns to three headings: giving education priority, self-reliance in science and technology, and talent as a leading and driving force.

Pan holds that education is the foundation, science and technology the key, and talent the fundamental factor of Chinese modernization. Pan cites the claim that science and technology are the primary productive force, talent the primary resource and innovation the primary driving force. As evidence, Pan gives figures: national R&D spending rose from 1 trillion to 2.8 trillion yuan over the decade, ranking second in the world, and China has the largest number of researchers. For each field Pan lists tasks, including a high-quality education system, a new system for mobilizing national resources, a national laboratory system, work on "bottleneck" technologies, and the principle of the Party managing talent.

Pan concludes that the strategies for invigorating China through science and education, for strengthening the country through talent, and for innovation-driven development should be implemented in depth, so as to open new fields and keep shaping new drivers and advantages for development. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how the 20th Party Congress linked education, science and technology, and talent.
quoteEn: In comprehensively building a modern socialist country, education is the foundation, science and technology the key, and talent the fundamental factor.
quoteZh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家，教育是基础，科技是关键，人才是根本。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.en: strategy of invigorating China through science and education
glossary.literal: strategy of reviving the country through science and education
glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced in the mid-1990s that makes science, technology and education central to national development.

glossary.en: new system for mobilizing national resources
glossary.explanation: A model in which the state coordinates resources across sectors to achieve major scientific and technological goals.
The principle that the Communist Party leads the selection, training and use of talent.

t: Better playing the role of trade unions around the Party's central task
zh: 围绕党的中心任务更好发挥工会作用
authors: Leading Party Group of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions
paras: Published in the People's Daily and reposted in February 2023, this commentary by the Party group of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions takes up how trade unions should act after the 20th Party Congress (2022). It starts from the Congress report's statement that the Party's central task is building a modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. The authors argue that trade unions, in keeping with their tradition, must centre their work on this task and serve the overall agenda under Party leadership, so as to gather the strength of the working class.

The text is organised in five sections, each opening with a part of the Congress report and ending with what unions should do. The sections cover Party leadership and the Two Establishes; study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; the skills of the workforce and high-quality development; a people-centred approach and workers' status as masters; and trade union reform and building.

The core argument is that each element of the Party's central task gives unions a concrete duty. In the authors' account, Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of Chinese modernization, so unions must make it their political principle and uphold the Two Upholds. Unions are to spread Party theory "into enterprises, workshops and teams" and consolidate the Party's class and mass base. For high-quality development they are to build a knowledgeable, skilled and innovative industrial workforce through skills competitions, mass innovation activities and the promotion of the model worker, labour and craftsman spirit. On the people-centred approach, the authors call for protecting workers' legitimate rights, applying whole-process people's democracy through workers' congresses, raising labour's share in primary distribution, strengthening protection for flexible and new-form employment workers, and enriching cultural life in support of common prosperity.

The authors conclude that unions should keep and strengthen their political, advanced and mass character as a bridge between the Party and workers. They propose strengthening grassroots organisations, building a high-calibre professional cadre of union officials, improving online union work and using high-quality Party building to guide innovation. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the national union leadership framed the unions' tasks after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Centring on the central task and serving the overall situation is the tradition and strength of trade union organisations.
quoteZh: 围绕中心、服务大局是工会组织的传统和优势。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses Party leadership, a socialist orientation and common prosperity.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the authority of Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the Party Central Committee's centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
An official economic goal that replaces speed of growth with quality, innovation and efficiency. The 20th Party Congress called it the first task of building a modern socialist country.
The official description of China's democracy, which the Party says covers every stage of governance and not just elections.
A stated goal of socialism in which prosperity is shared by all. It has been given new prominence in Party policy since 2021.

t: The generative logic, mechanism and contemporary cultivation of the cultural gene of common prosperity
zh: 共同富裕文化基因的生成逻辑、作用机理及时代涵育
paras: Cui Haiying asks what cultural resources sustain the pursuit of common prosperity, beyond its economic conditions and institutional guarantees. The article argues that there is a "cultural gene" of common prosperity: a stable, inheritable and evolving spiritual structure that Cui describes as the "genetic code" of how the Chinese people think and act in pursuing a better life. It is presented as the cultural root of the Party's effort to seek happiness for the people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts: how the gene was formed, how it operates, and how it should be cultivated in the present. The first part traces its formation through historical, theoretical and practical logics. The second examines its effect through the Party's nature and purpose, its original aspiration and mission, and its spiritual lineage. The third sets out measures drawn from the gene's stability, inheritance and evolution.

In Cui's account, the historical logic runs from early notions of equitable distribution and the pre-Qin thinkers (Confucius's "not worrying about poverty but about inequality") to Sun Yat-sen. The theoretical logic draws on three features of Marxism: its people-centredness, openness and progressiveness. The practical logic follows the Party from land reform through the first use of the term common prosperity, Deng Xiaoping's formulations, and Xi Jinping's statements in the new era. Cui argues that the gene shapes the Party's direction, for example in distribution policy, anchors its values across generations of leaders, and sustains its drive through spirits such as the Daqing spirit and the poverty-alleviation spirit. For cultivation, Cui proposes upholding Party leadership, the socialist system and the people's principal position. Cui also proposes drawing on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, and balancing preserving fundamentals with innovation, openness with confidence, and understanding with practice.

Cui concludes that cultivating this gene gives common prosperity a value foundation and a source of strength. The article also warns against what it calls egalitarianism, "lying flat", Western-style welfarism and ideas of "robbing the rich to help the poor", and calls for building a Chinese discourse on common prosperity. Read the original if you want a culturalist, Party-centred account of how Chinese scholars link the Party's history, Marxism and traditional thought to the common prosperity agenda.
quoteEn: The cultural gene of common prosperity accompanies all the practice of carrying out the Party's purpose, and through value expression and meaning-construction that meet the people's interests it acts as a "stabilising anchor" in guiding the direction of advance.
quoteZh: 共同富裕文化基因与贯彻党的宗旨的全部实践活动相伴相生，以满足人民利益要求的价值表达和意义建构，在引领前进方向上发挥“定海神针”之效。

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism that the Party has stressed since the 1950s and, under Xi Jinping, made a central policy aim. It stands for prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority, and is not egalitarianism.

A biological metaphor for deep, stable and inheritable cultural patterns of thought and value that shape a people's behaviour. Chinese official and academic discourse uses it often in discussing traditional culture.
The Party's stated founding purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It was emphasised from the 19th Party Congress (2017).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream and Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: Putting health first and building a Healthy China
zh: 坚持健康优先 建设健康中国
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yao Jianhong asks what it means to give priority to people's health and how this principle should drive the building of a Healthy China. The author argues that health-first development is both an important principle and a key mechanism of Healthy China, and that it requires changes in government priorities, in the health system and in individual attitudes.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the meaning of health-first development from three angles: health's place in economic and social development, a fundamental change in how the health sector operates, and citizens' own sense of responsibility. The second gives four reasons for its significance, and the third lists the priority tasks, from high-quality development and public health to medical science, talent and local experimentation.

Yao's central reasoning is that health is a basis of development as well as its goal. The author sums up the first angle as 'three priorities and one continuing effort': prioritising health spending, medical science and technology breakthroughs and the training of health workers, while keeping health integrated into all policies. The health system is to shift from a treatment-centred to a people's-health-centred model, with prevention first. Yao also stresses that individuals are the 'first persons responsible' for their own health. As reasons for health priority, the article cites the people-centred development philosophy, the fragmentation of services and weak coordination of medical care, medical insurance and medicines, the risks of epidemics and chronic disease in an ageing society, and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The proposals include a government-led non-profit health service system, a stronger four-tier public health network, early warning and biosecurity law, and public health spending that grows faster than overall health spending. Yao also suggests health-risk taxes and labels on tobacco and high-salt, high-sugar foods, and insurance incentives for healthy behaviour. They further call for more funding for medical research and for local authorities to treat health as a major livelihood project and to share good practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Healthy China policy priorities were framed after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Health is a right, but even more it is a responsibility.
quoteZh: 健康既是一种权利，更是一种责任。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy launched in 2016 to improve public health through prevention, health services and healthier environments and lifestyles. The 20th Party Congress report called for 'advancing the building of a Healthy China'.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展理念
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn lǐniàn
glossary.literal: development concept centred on the people
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping that presents the people's wellbeing as the starting point and aim of development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of making China prosperous, strong and influential, often linked to the Chinese Dream.
A principle that sectors such as industry, transport and education should assess the health effects of their policies, similar to the international 'Health in All Policies' approach.

t: Improving the comprehensive governance system and building a healthy online ecosystem
zh: 健全综合治理体系 营造良好网络生态
paras: Writing in early 2023, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yang Liqun, a Jiangsu provincial propaganda and cyberspace official, takes up how China should carry out the Congress's call to "improve the comprehensive governance system for cyberspace and foster a good online ecosystem". The commentary argues that this system is a political necessity and a core part of Xi Jinping's thinking on building China into a cyber power. Yang holds that it needs a systematic, whole-of-society approach under Party leadership.

The piece has three parts. It first explains why the system matters, then reviews recent achievements and the challenges that remain, and finally sets out six areas of work for applying the 20th Party Congress's guidance. It traces the policy line from the 19th Party Congress (2017) through the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) to the 20th Congress, and refers to the national meeting of cyberspace administration heads held on 4–5 January 2023.

Yang's core argument is that the internet has become the main arena of ideological struggle, so governing it is tied directly to political and national security and to the Party's long-term rule. Comprehensive governance is also presented as part of modernizing the system and capacity of national governance, and as a condition for high-quality development of the cyber sector. On results, Yang cites ideological-responsibility inspections, the "Qinglang" (clear and bright) campaigns, online legal education and cadre training. The stated problems are fast-changing technologies such as the metaverse and AI, weak influence of mainstream new-media platforms and internet firms, and a few platforms that neglect their responsibilities. The remedies are organised under image-laden headings: clarified lines of responsibility, a stronger multimedia opinion landscape, cleaner online content, online civility work aimed at young people, law enforcement, and cybersecurity and data-security checks.

Yang concludes that governance should move from after-the-fact management to process-based governance, and from fragmented to coordinated control, with integrated online and offline governance. The guiding formula is that positive energy is the overall requirement, control is the hard principle and good use is the real skill. Read the original if you want to see how a provincial Party cyberspace official translates central internet-governance doctrine into operational tasks and slogans.
quoteEn: Improving the comprehensive cyberspace governance system is a comprehensive, systematic and foundational undertaking; it should uphold that positive energy is the overall requirement, being able to control is the hard principle, and using well is the real skill.
quoteZh: 健全网络综合治理体系是一项综合性、系统性、基础性工程，应坚持正能量是总要求、管得住是硬道理、用得好是真本事

glossary.explanation: A policy concept first put forward at the 19th Party Congress (2017) for managing cyberspace through coordinated Party, government, platform, industry and public participation, combining legal, technical and ideological tools.
The name of a series of annual special campaigns run by China's cyberspace authorities to clean up online content and behaviour deemed harmful.
A goal and body of thought associated with Xi Jinping, aiming to make China strong in internet technology, content, infrastructure and governance.

t: New changes in the world landscape and new features of great-power competition
zh: 世界格局新变化与大国博弈新特点
paras: Writing in early 2023, the tenth anniversary of the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind and of the Belt and Road Initiative, Wang Wen asks how China should read the world situation and great-power rivalry in the third decade of the century. The author argues that the 'great changes unseen in a century' are continuing to unfold and that great-power competition is intensifying. China therefore needs strategic resolve and policy patience, and should view its problems as a 'protracted war' in the long term. The piece was published in the Party journal Qianxian.

The article has three parts. The first sets out three dimensions of the continuing transformation: world politics, the international economy and global ideas, drawing mainly on events of 2022. The second warns that the change will be uneven and that China must prepare for severe tests in political security, economic and financial affairs, and ideology. The third lists three guidelines for 2023, namely focusing on development, daring to struggle, and expanding opening up and cooperation.

Wang's central claim is that non-Western countries are rising collectively and independently, citing Russia, Latin America's leftward turn, ASEAN, India, Central Asia, the Arab world, Africa and RCEP. The author describes a 'de-Westernisation' of economic development, pointing to falling shares of the US dollar in reserves and Europe in world output, and a 'demythologising' of Western democracy, with development replacing it as the dominant global discourse. At the same time Wang cautions that Western strengths persist and that the trend will not be linear. The author portrays the United States as pursuing an Indo-Pacific strategy, provoking possible conflict in the western Pacific and over Taiwan, imposing chip embargoes and other economic measures, and using cultural influence to shape ideas, all in the author's account aimed at delaying the decline of Western hegemony.

Wang concludes that China should keep its independent, peaceful foreign policy and win-win opening, restore the economy through high-quality development, resist hostile forces while distinguishing politicians from ordinary people, and push for a community with a shared future for mankind. The author also calls for stronger ideological security. Read the original if you want an example of how a Chinese international-relations scholar close to Party discourse framed the post-2022 world order and the rivalry with the United States for a Party-journal audience.
quoteEn: The West is no longer the prime mover of economic growth and social development in other countries, still less the sole centre of world development.
quoteZh: 西方不再是各国经济增长与社会发展的原动力，更不再是世界发展的唯一中心区。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping, first put forward in 2013, calling for shared security, development and governance among states.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since about 2017 to describe a shift in the global balance of power, including the relative rise of non-Western states.
An official goal of the economy since the late 2010s, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

keywords: great changes unseen in a century

t: Only unity brings victory, only struggle brings success
zh: 团结才能胜利 奋斗才会成功
source: Guangming Daily (originally published); posted on marxism.cass.cn 23 February 2023
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily, takes up Xi Jinping's formulations at the 20th Party Congress (2022) that "unity is strength" and that "only unity brings victory, only struggle brings success". Sun Xiuling argues that unity and struggle are the key to the Party's past achievements and a requirement for building a modern socialist country in all respects. The author presents the slogan as a rule drawn from long practice.

The piece is organised in three numbered sections. The first treats unity and struggle as a lesson of the Party's hundred-year history. The second presents them as the most distinctive spiritual hallmark of the Communist Party and the Chinese people. The third explains why they are indispensable for the new journey towards a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Sun first gives the slogan a philosophical grounding in the Marxist law of the unity of opposites: possibility and reality depend on each other and convert into one another under certain conditions. In this reading unity and struggle are the basis and path of victory, and victory is their result, linked through human subjective initiative. Historically, the author holds that unity within the Party, and the centralised and unified leadership of the Central Committee, have been decisive, from the Zunyi Meeting under Mao Zedong to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping as core. Sun then traces the spirit of unity and struggle to five thousand years of Chinese civilisation, which the Party is said to have inherited. Finally, the author calls for resolutely upholding the Two Establishes, strengthening the Two Upholds, forging a sense of community of the Chinese nation as the main thread, and consolidating the broadest patriotic united front.

Sun concludes that the project of national rejuvenation is a relay race that requires even greater unity, together with a fighting spirit embedded in the effort to unite, given what the author calls the long-term, complex and arduous nature of the great struggle. The author calls on readers to align thinking and action with the 20th Party Congress and to unite all forces that can be united. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school commentary links the 20th Congress slogan on unity and struggle to Party history, national spirit and loyalty to the Central Committee.
quoteEn: Only through unity and struggle can victory and success be achieved, and no victory or success can do without unity and struggle.
quoteZh: 只有团结奋斗才会胜利成功，任何胜利成功都离不开团结奋斗。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted by the Party in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the early 2010s.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly forge the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official policy line on ethnic affairs that stresses a shared national identity among all ethnic groups in China.

t: Clarifying the direction of Chinese modernization: a deep grasp of its Chinese characteristics
zh: 明确中国式现代化建设的方向 深刻把握中国式现代化的中国特色
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily, interprets a passage from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The report describes Chinese modernization as socialist modernization led by the Communist Party, with features common to all countries and Chinese characteristics rooted in national conditions. Shao argues that these characteristics set the direction of modernization and reflect the Party's mission and the essential features of socialism.

The article takes the five characteristics in turn: a huge population, common prosperity for all, coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and a path of peaceful development. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi and then sets out practical requirements.

For Shao, the huge population of over 1.4 billion brings unprecedented difficulty and potential, and calls for steady, step-by-step progress, a people-centred approach and a shift from a large to a strong country in human resources. Common prosperity is described as a long historical process that combines market and government and enlarges and then fairly divides the "cake". On material and cultural-ethical progress, the author puts high-quality development first and calls for advancing socialist culture. Shao says the ecological path rejects pollution first and clean-up later, and that the peaceful path rejects war, colonialism and plunder.

Shao concludes that these characteristics should be applied in every field and link of socialist modernization. The article ends by calling for a community with a shared future for mankind, the Global Development Initiative and the Global Security Initiative. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style summary of how the five Chinese characteristics of modernization were presented to a wide readership in early 2023.
quoteEn: Modernization is not only the accumulation of material wealth but also the development of cultural-ethical progress.
quoteZh: 现代化不仅是物质财富的积累，也是精神文明的发展。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official description of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is defined by five features: huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical coordination, harmony with nature, and peaceful development.
A goal of shared affluence for all citizens, presented by the Party as an essential requirement of socialism. It has been emphasised in official policy, especially since 2021.
An official economic goal, formally stated in 2017, that emphasises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.
A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 that calls for international cooperation on development, with a focus on the Global South.
A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2022 that sets out China's principles for international security cooperation.

t: The "ideational", "material" and "real" content of the ideology of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 论中国特色社会主义意识形态的“观念”“物质”和“现实”内容
paras: Kou Qingjie and Li Pingping ask what the ideology of socialism with Chinese characteristics actually consists of. They argue that existing scholarship has studied how to strengthen its discourse power and summarised the Party's experience of ideological work, but has not examined its content in a broad sense. Their thesis is that this ideology should be understood as having three components: an "ideational" one, a "material" one and a "real" one.

The article is organised in three sections, one for each component. It draws on Marx and Engels's The German Ideology, on Louis Althusser's notion of ideological state apparatuses, on Lenin's What Is to Be Done? and on speeches by Xi Jinping. The authors treat Marxism, Sinicised Marxism and traditional Chinese culture as ideas; institutions, Party organisation and state apparatuses as material form; and people and their practice as the lived dimension.

The authors hold that ideas depend on a material base and that both ideas and material structures stay "dead" without human subjects. For the ideational content they list Marxism as truth and method, Sinicised Marxism (from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, in three stages: revolutionary, constructive, and both since the 18th Party Congress of 2012) and fine traditional culture such as people-centred thought. The material content is the socialist system, the Party's organisational system, and education, communication and propaganda bodies, which the authors treat as ideological state apparatuses following Althusser. The real content is Party members, Marxist researchers and communicators, and ordinary people, together with practices such as propaganda work, poverty alleviation and ideological and political theory courses. In the authors' account, exemplary figures are "walking" ideology.

The authors conclude that a full account of the ideology must cover all three dimensions, because each is necessary for it to operate. In practice they call for stronger education of young people, better ideological and political discipline among Party members, and more training of Marxist researchers. Read the original if you want a systematic account, from within Chinese academia, of how ideology is conceptualised as ideas, institutions and practice, including its use of Althusser.
quoteEn: For the ideology of socialism with Chinese characteristics to come "alive" and take real effect, it must rely on subjects such as Communist Party members, Marxist researchers and communicators, and the people.
quoteZh: 要使中国特色社会主义意识形态“活”起来、真正地发挥效用，那就必须依靠中国共产党人、马克思主义研究者和传播者，以及人民群众等主体。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path, system and theory since the reform era, associated with Deng Xiaoping. It is the framework within which the Party presents its ideology.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of Sinicised Marxism.

A concept from Louis Althusser for institutions such as schools, media, churches and families that reproduce ideology, as distinct from repressive apparatuses such as the army and police. The authors apply it to China's education, communication and propaganda systems.
The official term for the body of theory produced by combining Marxism with Chinese conditions, running from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought.
Compulsory courses on Marxism and Party theory taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.

t: Continuously improving the effectiveness of cyberspace governance
zh: 不断提升网络空间治理效能
source: People's Daily (Renmin Ribao); posted on marxism.cass.cn 21 February 2023
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily, takes up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to improve the system of comprehensive internet governance and foster a healthy online ecosystem. Lin argues that cyberspace governance must be strengthened so that China can move from being a large internet country to a strong one.

The piece opens by noting that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party Central Committee has pursued the strategy of building China into a cyber power, which Lin says has brought historic achievements. It then sets out three directions for further work: a people-centred approach, governance by law, and multi-party participation.

On the first, Lin cites Xi Jinping's call for internet development to serve the people and urges stronger online content building, with a positive, healthy online culture nourished by core socialist values. On the second, Lin lists laws such as the Cybersecurity Law, the Data Security Law and the Personal Information Protection Law, plus more than 300 national standards. Lin calls for faster supporting legislation, tougher enforcement, cross-departmental coordination, platform accountability and a mix of campaign-style and routine governance. On the third, Lin describes a pattern led by Party committees, with government management, corporate responsibility, social oversight and netizen self-discipline. A 2019 opinion on this system, Lin says, shifted governance from after-the-fact management to process governance.

Lin concludes that the Party's overall leadership, better coordination among agencies, platform responsibility, industry self-regulation and netizens' ability to recognise false information together create a good online ecosystem. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line on internet governance was presented to a general readership in early 2023.
quoteEn: We must uphold the Party's overall leadership over comprehensive internet governance, strengthen cooperation among the departments that govern the internet, further improve coordination mechanisms, and form a combined governance force.
quoteZh: 要坚持党对网络综合治理工作的全面领导，强化治网管网各部门相互配合，进一步完善协调机制，形成治理合力

glossary.explanation: A strategic goal in Party discourse of making China strong in internet technology, content and security. It has been promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

An official framework that involves Party committees, government, enterprises, society and individual internet users in governing online space. It was formalised in a 2019 opinion of the Central Committee for Comprehensively Deepening Reform.
A set of 12 official values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including prosperity, democracy, patriotism and the rule of law.

t: Contributing the strength of veterans' work to building a modern socialist great power
zh: 为社会主义现代化强国建设贡献退役军人工作力量
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily and written by the Party secretary and minister of the Ministry of Veterans Affairs, sets out how veterans' work should serve the goals laid down at the 20th Party Congress (2022). Pei Jinji argues that, because the Party's central task is now to build a modern socialist great power and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, the veterans' affairs system must make studying and implementing the Congress's spirit its first political task.

The article takes Xi Jinping's report to the Congress as its framework and organises the discussion into five areas of work. These are modernizing the governance system and capacity of veterans' affairs; contributing to economic and social development; serving the modernization of national defence and the armed forces; supporting the modernization of the national security system; and rallying unity and morale for the national goal. Each section opens with a passage from the report and then lists practical tasks.

Pei's central claim is that veterans' work is an integral part of the work of the Party and state and must be organised around its central tasks. On governance, Pei calls for stronger Party leadership, standardised service centres and stations, tighter accountability mechanisms, information platforms and a fuller legal and policy framework, including the Veterans Protection Law and revised regulations on resettlement and pensions. On development, Pei presents veterans as a talent pool and proposes training, job fairs, placement in grassroots Party and village committees, and individualised, file-based services. On defence and security, Pei describes the system as an extension of military modernization: aligning policy with military reform, supporting combat readiness and wartime response, easing soldiers' family concerns, resolving grievances through the 'Fengqiao experience', and organising veterans for emergency rescue.

In its final section Pei calls for keeping veterans closely united around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, through campaigns such as 'Veterans Always Follow the Party' and 'Most Beautiful Veterans'. Pei also urges consolidating unity between the military, government and people through the 'double support' work, and using red resources and martyr commemoration to promote the national spirit. Read the original if you want to see how the Ministry of Veterans Affairs translated the 20th Party Congress report into concrete policy priorities for veterans' services in early 2023.
quoteEn: Veterans' work is an extension of, and an important support for, the modernization of national defence and the armed forces, and it must be considered and advanced within the cause of building a strong military.
quoteZh: 退役军人工作是国防和军队现代化建设的延伸和重要支撑，必须放在强军事业中来思考和推动。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, given a systematic formulation at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 as the Party's route to national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party slogan for restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.

glossary.literal: dual support (supporting the army and the people)
glossary.explanation: A long-running campaign in which the army and government/people are to support each other: society honours soldiers and their families, and the military supports local communities.
A grassroots conflict-resolution model originating in Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s, promoted as a way to settle disputes locally without escalation.

t: Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国式现代化是中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily and posted in February 2023, takes up a formulation from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China. Qi Yingyan argues that this statement sets out the fundamental character of Chinese modernization and is the core marker distinguishing it from, and in the author's view making it superior to, Western modernization.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first treats the Party as the leading force of Chinese modernization and traces its role from the 7th Party Congress (1945) through the industrialisation goals of the 1950s and reform and opening up to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second treats socialism with Chinese characteristics as the source of the basic nature and direction of modernization. The third derives the principle of the people's principal position from the Party's leadership and from the scale of China's population.

Qi's core argument is that the Party's leadership and the socialist system together fix what kind of modernization China pursues. Drawing on Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, the author says this is socialist modernization and nothing else, marked by common prosperity, the coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humans and nature, and peaceful development. Western modernization is contrasted as driven by the logic of capital, aimed at extracting surplus value, treating people as reified factors of production, and, in the author's account, bringing ecological damage, colonialism and plunder. Because a population of over 1.4 billion is larger than that of all existing developed countries combined, Qi holds that China has no ready model to follow and must rely on itself, proceed patiently and share the fruits of development among all the people.

Qi concludes that upholding Party leadership is the highest principle and the greatest political advantage of Chinese modernization. Development must be for the people and rely on the people, and the Party's leadership must be carried into every sphere of work in order to mobilise popular initiative. The author also presents the Chinese path as widening the options for developing countries that want to modernise while keeping their independence. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line exposition of how the 20th Party Congress report links Party leadership, socialism and the people-centred approach to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Upholding the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the supreme principle that must be followed in advancing Chinese modernization, and it is also its greatest political advantage.
quoteZh: 坚持中国共产党的领导，是推进中国式现代化必须坚持的最高原则，也是中国式现代化的最大政治优势。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models, with features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory, path and system since reform and opening up, introduced by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s.
An official goal of shared wealth for all the people, described by the Party as an essential requirement of socialism and given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping.
A Party principle that the people are the main body of development and that the Party puts their interests first. The article links it to the people-centred approach to development.

t: Promoting a community with a shared future for mankind is an essential requirement and unremitting pursuit of Chinese modernization
zh: 推动构建人类命运共同体是中国式现代化的本质要求和不懈追求
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary asks how Chinese modernization relates to the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Fu Xiaoqiang argues that promoting such a community is an essential requirement of Chinese modernization and one of its unremitting pursuits. In Fu's account, Chinese modernization points the way and opens a path for both the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the building of that community.

The article, first published on Guangming Online in February 2023, has three parts. The first sets out the international responsibility and global contribution of Chinese modernization. The second draws lessons that Chinese modernization offers for building the community, under the headings of common prosperity, openness and inclusiveness, harmony between humanity and nature, and universal security. The third describes four paths Chinese modernization opens: shared development through cooperation, peaceful development through mutual learning among civilizations, comprehensive and coordinated development, and independent development that draws on others.

Fu presents the idea as a theoretical innovation that draws on the Marxist theory of world history and of the community, and on traditional Chinese views of "all under heaven". Chinese modernization is portrayed as surpassing Western modernization, which Fu describes as driven by capital and marked by war, colonialism, plunder, wealth polarization and ecological damage. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is said to centre on the people, seek peaceful development, and ease the "security dilemma" through dialogue and partnership without alliances. Fu argues that it breaks the monopoly of "Western-centrism" and encourages developing countries to find their own paths, since no single model of modernization exists.

Fu concludes that Chinese modernization offers humanity a new choice and an inexhaustible impetus for the community with a shared future for mankind. The article states that the Communist Party and the Chinese people will offer more Chinese wisdom, solutions and strength, and will advance the Global Development Initiative and the Global Security Initiative. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese official discourse after the 20th Party Congress links domestic modernization to its vision of global order.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization abandons the capital-centred logic of Western modernization. It upholds a people-centred approach to development and takes the free and all-round development of the individual and the liberation of all humanity as its fundamental value, thereby giving it a distinct "people's hue".
quoteZh: 中国式现代化摒弃了西方现代化以资本为中心的逻辑，坚持以人民为中心的发展思想，以人的自由全面发展和全人类解放为根本价值追求，从而铸就了鲜明的“人民底色”。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts describe it as marked by a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for shared security, prosperity and governance among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often tied to the Chinese Dream. It is generally set against the period of national weakness since the nineteenth century.
A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed under Xi Jinping, in which all the people share in affluence. It is presented as a remedy for wealth polarization.
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2021 that puts development at the centre of international cooperation, including progress on the UN 2030 Agenda.
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2022 that advocates common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The deep meaning and contemporary value of the new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化新的飞跃的深刻意涵与当代价值
paras: Zhang Zhongmin takes up the claim, made in the Party's third historical resolution (2021) and the 20th Party Congress report (2022), that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has achieved a "new leap" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article asks what this judgement means and what value it has. Zhang argues that the leap is a real historical process that is still under way. In Zhang's account it grows out of the interplay between theory and practice, and between "using Marxism to transform China" and "using China to transform Marxism".

The article has four parts. The first reads the leap through historical materialism, looking at its strategic meaning, its concrete referents and its causes. The second sets out the theoretical form and essential content of the leap. The third discusses its historical significance. The fourth turns to its contemporary value, set against the history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of world socialism, and ends with practical proposals.

Zhang ties the three leaps to the Chinese nation's progress from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong". The third leap is said to answer three major questions and to move the Party's formulation from "eight clarifications" to "ten clarifications". Zhang also credits it with finding the Party's self-reform as a second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. The causes are analysed under four logics: historical, practical, political and internal. The political logic rests on the Two Establishes, and the internal logic on the tension between the goals of the "two centenaries" and real conditions. Zhang holds that the leap fuses Marxism with the cultural genes of Chinese civilization through the Two Integrations. It is presented as proof that Marxism remains vital and as a challenge to the "end of history" thesis.

Zhang concludes that the leap closes the first century of adapting Marxism to China and opens a new starting point. It is also presented as a scientific programme for world socialism and a source of reference for developing countries. The article proposes studying the whole history of this adaptation with a "big history" outlook and balancing "upholding fundamental principles" with "innovation". It also proposes turning the leap into practical results for Chinese modernization, covering Party building, military modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how the official narrative of the "new leap" is justified through historical materialism and the Party's three historical resolutions.
quoteEn: Achieving the new leap is not only an expansion of theoretical content and practical experience, but above all a qualitative leap in the adaptation of Marxism to China, from the "one integration" to the "Two Integrations".
quoteZh: 实现新的飞跃不仅是理论内容与实践经验层面上的扩充，更是马克思主义中国化由“一个结合”到“两个结合”的质变飞跃

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second element was added to the earlier formula in the Party's 2021 resolution and the 2022 Party Congress.

A formula from the 2022 Party Congress affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is presented officially as a decisive political outcome of the new era.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party presents as an alternative to Western models. It was prominently elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping. It calls for cooperative global governance and shared development.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxism to Chinese conditions and the demands of each era. The phrase "and of our times" was added at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The Party's official term for rigorous internal discipline and anti-corruption work. It is presented as a way of avoiding the historical cycle of rise and decline.

t: Striving to the fore on the track of national rejuvenation
zh: 在实现民族复兴的赛道上奋勇争先
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily and posted on the Academy of Marxism site in February 2023, takes up Xi Jinping's 2023 New Year address. Guan Jian, a professor at Nankai University, argues that realising the Chinese Dream is a historical relay race and that each generation of young people must strive to the fore on the track of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised under three headings: merging personal ideals with the cause of the Party and the state; contributing wisdom and strength in the broad arena of the new era; and keeping youthful vitality and an uplifting spirit. It draws on Xi Jinping's remarks on youth, a historical sketch from the May Fourth period to the present, and a line attributed to Marx on the spirit of youth.

Guan reads modern Chinese history as one in which young people were a vanguard force. The author cites the May Fourth generation's choice of Marxism-Leninism and the 13 delegates, averaging 28 years old, at the Party's first congress in 1921. Today's youth, in this account, live in the best and most critical era for national rejuvenation, and the Party Central Committee supports them through the principle that the Party manages youth affairs and a policy of youth-priority development. Guan notes that young people face competing social currents and doubts, for example between ideals and reality or the individual and the collective.

Guan concludes that firm ideals and convictions are the remedy: faith in Marxism, belief in socialism and communism, and confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author calls for arming youth with Party theory so that they join Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary frames youth, ideals and Party leadership around the Chinese Dream.
quoteEn: Realising the Chinese Dream is a historical relay race, and it requires generation after generation of young people to strive to the fore on the track of national rejuvenation, turning the Chinese Dream continually into reality.
quoteZh: 实现中国梦是一场历史接力赛，需要一代又一代青年在实现民族复兴的赛道上奋勇争先，将中国梦不断变为现实。

glossary.explanation: A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the prosperity of the country and its people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation' beginning with the Opium War.

glossary.en: the principle that the Party manages youth affairs
glossary.literal: principle of the Party managing youth
glossary.explanation: A principle stressed under Xi Jinping that Party organisations hold leadership over youth work and the cultivation of young people.
The official name for China's path of socialism since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market economy.
The official concept of China's own path to modernity, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

t: Comprehensively raising the capacity to train legal professionals, to provide solid personnel support for law-based governance
zh: 全面提升法治人才培养能力 为全面依法治国提供坚实人才保障
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), which gave law-based governance its own chapter in the work report for the first time, Hu argues that training legal professionals is a basic, supporting part of comprehensively governing the country by law. The article is a short commentary by the Party secretary of China University of Political Science and Law. It contends that law schools, as the main place of such training, must follow Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law and turn out large numbers of legal professionals loyal to the Party, the country, the people and the law.

The piece sets out four lines of work for law schools: value guidance, curriculum, textbooks, and collaborative and practical teaching. Each is presented as a requirement drawn from Xi Jinping's remarks, including his 2017 visit to the university.

Hu first calls for combining moral and legal education. Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law should enter textbooks, classrooms and students' minds, ideological-political content should be built into law courses, and professional ethics should be taught alongside skills. On curriculum, Hu proposes cross-disciplinary study, a full course system for foreign-related legal work, and possible new fields such as Party regulations, national security law and data law, together with digital teaching platforms. On textbooks, they should start from China's conditions and absorb foreign experience selectively, not copy Western theory. They should also draw creatively on traditional Chinese legal culture.

Hu closes by urging joint training between institutions, citing the university's law-and-English joint degree with Beijing Foreign Studies University.
