Law schools should also build internship bases with courts, procuratorates, law firms and government bodies, and appoint practitioners as part-time professors and practice mentors. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a leading law-school leader translates Party legal-education policy into concrete measures.
quoteEn: In writing law textbooks, we should actively absorb the successful experience and advanced achievements of world legal civilisation, but must never copy or mechanically imitate Western theory; we should screen it carefully and sublate it boldly.
quoteZh: 法学教材编写要积极吸收借鉴世界法治文明的成功经验和先进成果，但绝不能照搬照抄、机械临摹西方的理论，而是要仔细甄别、大胆扬弃。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on law-based governance, formally set out at the 2020 Central Conference on Law-based Governance. It is now the guiding doctrine for legal education and legal work in China.

glossary.en: comprehensively governing the country by law
glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: A Party policy line, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the 2014 Fourth Plenum, that places law-based governance within Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

China University of Political Science and Law

t: Chinese modernization displays a new form of human civilization
zh: 中国式现代化展现人类文明新形态
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Hu Changshuan asks what distinguishes Chinese modernization from the modernization of the Western developed countries, and what responsibility follows from that difference. The author argues that Chinese modernization is socialist in essence, goes beyond capitalist modernization, and carries a solemn duty to create a new form of human civilization.

The commentary has three parts. The first contrasts capitalist and socialist modernization. The second traces how the pursuit of modernization has been tied to national rejuvenation, from the late Qing reform efforts through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and the two-stage plan for the second centenary goal. The third sets out the contributions Hu attributes to Chinese modernization.

In Hu's account, Western modernization is driven by the logic of capital, the limitless drive to accumulate, and rests on plunder, aggression and the exploitation of the majority, as Marx's Capital is cited to show. Chinese modernization is described as comprehensive, covering the economy, politics, culture, society and ecology, and as aiming at common prosperity, coordination of material and spiritual civilization, harmony between humans and nature, and peaceful development. Hu argues that Western-style paths failed in modern China, and that the Communist Party chose its own route. On this basis the author names three contributions: a reference point for developing countries, a way of overcoming the ills of capitalist modernization (ecological damage, world wars), and a new form of civilization. Hu describes that form as the coordinated development of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization, people-centred and committed to all-round human development. It is said to combine a Marxist view of civilization with traditional Chinese views.

Hu concludes that, with capitalist modernity in what the author calls an unprecedented crisis, Chinese modernization offers developing countries a new option and carries the task of promoting a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative presents the link between Chinese modernization, national rejuvenation and a new form of human civilization shortly after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is, in essence, socialist modernization. Guided by Marxism, it goes beyond capitalist modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化就其本质来说是社会主义的现代化。它以马克思主义为指导，是对资本主义现代化的超越。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, given a full formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, people-centred and distinct from the Western path.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all the people rather than a few. It is presented as a defining requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping. It stresses the shared interests of all countries and cooperation over confrontation.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formula used by Xi Jinping and in Party documents to describe the civilizational significance of Chinese modernization. It is presented as an alternative to the Western model.
Two goals set by the Party: building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021), and building a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

t: Comprehensively advancing rural revitalisation is an important task of building a strong agricultural country in the new era
zh: 全面推进乡村振兴是新时代建设农业强国的重要任务
paras: Huang Chengwei, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in early 2023, takes up the question of how rural revitalisation should be advanced as part of building a strong agricultural country. The article is an exposition of Xi Jinping's speech at the Central Rural Work Conference and of the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022). Huang's answer is that two bottom lines must be held, three aspects of the countryside must be handled together, new sources of momentum must be generated, and Party leadership must be strengthened.

The piece is organised in four parts. It begins with the two bottom lines: national food security and preventing large-scale return to poverty. It then turns to the coordinated promotion of rural development, rural construction and rural governance. The third part covers four sources of new momentum: deepening rural reform, pooling assistance forces, digital villages, and county-township-village coordination of infrastructure and public services. The last part concerns Party leadership over agriculture, rural areas and farmers (the "three rural issues").

On the bottom lines, Huang argues that feeding more than 1.4 billion people is always the top priority. The article calls for holding the 18-billion-mu farmland red line, building high-standard farmland, achieving self-reliance in seed technology, and strengthening incentives for grain farmers and major grain-producing regions. It also calls for better monitoring and assistance mechanisms and stronger minimum-guarantee social assistance. On the three aspects, Huang proposes industrial integration and local employment for development, planning-led and quality-first construction, and a governance system combining self-governance, rule of law and moral governance under Party leadership. Reform is to centre on the farmer–land relationship, including land requisition, homestead and contracted-land reforms.

Huang concludes that the Party's leadership is the key to rural work. The article calls for the five-level Party secretary mechanism, with county Party secretaries as "frontline commanders", and for a responsibility system running from the centre through provinces to cities, counties and townships, with differentiated targets and tolerance for error. It also urges more resident first secretaries and work teams, and wider mobilisation of private enterprises and social organisations. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented summary of the official agenda for rural revitalisation and agricultural modernisation after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Reform and innovation are the fundamental driving force of rural development; we should start from resolving the deep-seated contradictions in agricultural and rural development, press ahead unremittingly with rural reform and institutional innovation, and take the handling of the relationship between farmers and land as the main thread.
quoteZh: 改革创新是农村发展的根本动力，应从解决农业农村发展的深层次矛盾出发，坚持不懈地推进农村改革和制度创新，以处理好农民和土地的关系为主线

glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress in 2017 to modernise agriculture, villages and farmers' livelihoods. After the 2020 end of extreme-poverty eradication it became the main framework for rural policy.
Shorthand for agriculture, rural areas and farmers, used in Chinese policy to refer to rural affairs as a whole.
A goal stressed in the 20th Party Congress report and the 2022 Central Rural Work Conference, aiming at a high-capacity, modern agricultural sector as part of building a modern socialist country.

t: Effectively preventing and defusing major economic and financial risks
zh: 有效防范化解重大经济金融风险
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in early 2023, Li Jianjun interprets the fifth of the policy priorities set by the Central Economic Work Conference of 15–16 December 2022: effectively preventing and defusing major economic and financial risks. Li argues that this task is the key to coordinating development and security, and that it must be pursued under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The commentary has three parts. The first deals with the property sector, the second with financial risk and local government debt, and the third with the policy measures needed to keep the economy stable. Li sets the discussion against what the article calls triple pressure: shrinking demand, supply shocks and weakening expectations.

On property, Li reads the Conference's line of guaranteeing completed housing, people's livelihoods and stability as a way to avoid unfinished projects, stop debt risk from spreading to finance and hold the bottom line of no systemic risk. Li treats the principle that housing is for living in, not for speculation, as the fundamental remedy. It would de-financialise real estate and move the sector away from high debt, high leverage and high turnover, towards a new model combining market and affordable housing, rental and purchase together, and urban renewal. On finance, Li points to external shocks, such as central-bank tightening abroad, and to weak small banks, rural banks and trust companies at home. Li calls for stronger centralised Party leadership over financial work, rigorous Party self-governance and anti-corruption campaigns in the sector. For local debt, Li proposes halting new hidden debt, resolving existing stock through market-based and law-based default mechanisms, and holding to the principle that the central government does not bail out localities.

Li concludes that economic and financial risks ultimately stem from obstructed circulation in the real economy. Li therefore urges stable growth, employment and prices, support for innovation, fuller use of domestic demand and steadier foreign trade and investment. Citing the 20th Party Congress report on "black swan" and "grey rhino" events, Li calls for greater awareness of danger and bottom-line thinking. Read the original if you want a Party-school-style reading of the 2022 Central Economic Work Conference on property, financial supervision and local debt.
quoteEn: At root, economic and financial risks come from poor functioning of the real economy and blockage in the circulation process.
quoteZh: 从根源上讲，经济金融风险来自实体经济运行不畅，循环过程阻滞。

glossary.explanation: An annual closed-door meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually held in December, that sets the main economic tasks and policy direction for the coming year.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 as the Party's guiding ideology.

glossary.en: housing is for living in, not for speculation
glossary.literal: houses are for living, not for speculating
glossary.explanation: A slogan first used by Xi Jinping in 2016 and adopted as the guiding principle of housing policy. It aims to curb speculative property investment.

glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption within its ranks.

t: Law-based governance in all fields is an inherent requirement and an important safeguard of Chinese modernization
zh: 全面依法治国是中国式现代化的内在要求和重要保障
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2023, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's call to run the country in all respects according to law. Zhai Guoqiang argues that law-based governance is both an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization and an important safeguard for it, since a modern country must be one governed by law.

The article is organised around five features of Chinese modernization named in the report: a huge population, common prosperity for all, coordinated material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and a path of peaceful development. For each, Zhai explains why comprehensive law-based governance is needed.

Zhai holds that the rule of law is the most reliable and stable form of governance, and that modernizing a country of over 1.4 billion people in the primary stage of socialism, amid mounting risks, requires law to consolidate foundations, stabilise expectations and secure long-term stability. On common prosperity, social fairness and justice must be turned into legal institutions covering distribution, public services, taxation and property rights. On civilisational balance, the author reads the principal contradiction as now also appearing in law, and calls for combining rule by law with rule by virtue. On ecology, Zhai attributes environmental problems to weak and poorly enforced rules, and urges strict, enforceable ecological legislation. On peaceful development, the author links China's constitutional principles to upholding international law and building a foreign-related legal system.

Zhai concludes that law-based governance will carry growing responsibilities as Chinese modernization advances. Domestic and foreign-related rule of law should be advanced together, so that China helps shape international rules and supports a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the 20th Party Congress linked rule of law to each feature of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: When the rule of law flourishes, the nation flourishes; when the rule of law is strong, the country is strong; a modern country is necessarily a country under the rule of law.
quoteZh: 法治兴则民族兴，法治强则国家强，一个现代化国家必然是法治国家。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is defined by features such as a huge population, common prosperity, and peaceful development.
A goal of shared affluence for all, described in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism and a feature of Chinese modernization.
The official assessment that China remains in an early, long-lasting stage of socialist development, used to justify current policies.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of China's vision for international relations, based on cooperation and shared interests.

t: Promoting the unity of material abundance and spiritual richness
zh: 促进物质富足和精神富有相统一
paras: Writing in early 2023, after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Chen Juan asks how common prosperity should be understood and pursued. The commentary, originally published on Guangming Online, argues that common prosperity means abundance in both material and spiritual life, and that the two must be advanced together as a unity.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out why prosperity in both spheres belongs to the socialist view of common prosperity. It then presents material abundance and spiritual richness as the basic requirement of socialist modernization. Finally it offers practical directions for making the two integrate and reinforce each other.

Chen describes the material and spiritual as dialectically unified: material needs come first, citing Engels, but spiritual life, once formed, gains relative independence and in turn sustains material prosperity. In Chen's account, Western modernization is capital-centred, sees things rather than people and produces exploitation, polarisation and materialism. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is people-centred and pursues human all-round development. Chen also links this to the change in the principal contradiction of Chinese society in the new era, where people's needs for a better life now extend to spiritual and cultural demands.

Chen calls for improving the socialist market economy, narrowing urban–rural, regional and income gaps, applying the new development philosophy, advancing rural revitalisation, and developing advanced socialist culture guided by core socialist values. Chen also urges stronger public cultural services and guidance of public opinion. Material and cultural construction are to reinforce each other, with cultural undertakings and industries opening new sources of material growth. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary on the 20th Party Congress frames common prosperity as both material and spiritual.
quoteEn: Material poverty is not socialism, and spiritual poverty is not socialism either; socialist modernization pursues common prosperity in which material abundance and spiritual richness go together.
quoteZh: 物质贫困不是社会主义，精神贫乏也不是社会主义，社会主义现代化追求的是物质富足和精神富有的共同富裕。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Party leaders have stressed since the early 2020s. It denotes prosperity shared by all people rather than a few, and is here extended to cultural and spiritual life.
A set of five concepts (innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing) announced in 2015 to guide economic and social development.
A twelve-word official value formulation promoted since 2012, covering national, social and individual levels.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from the Western model.

t: Science and technology innovation for building a great modern socialist country
zh: 面向社会主义现代化强国的科技创新
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this short commentary asks how science and technology innovation can serve the goal of building a great modern socialist country. The authors argue that science and technology, as the primary productive force, should underpin all five dimensions of modernization: economic, political, cultural, social and ecological.

The article is organised as six sections, each linking innovation to one strategic task: a modernized economic system, common prosperity, peaceful development, advanced culture, ecological civilization and the modernization of national governance.

On the economy, the authors call for breakthroughs in key core technologies, secure and controllable industrial and supply chains, and a stronger national innovation system integrated with rural revitalization and regional strategies. On common prosperity, they say innovation should combine wealth creation with wealth sharing, widen participation beyond firms, and supply solutions for health, ageing, disaster prevention and green development. On security, they hold that control of core technologies is the basis of economic and defence security, and propose a new whole-nation system to overcome "stranglehold" problems and achieve "de-dependence". On culture, they stress the scientist spirit, model-worker spirit and craftsman spirit; on ecology, technical work on carbon peaking and neutrality.

For governance, the authors propose organised research on frontier technologies, reformed management, evaluation and talent systems, and use of big data, cloud computing, blockchain and AI to make public decisions more scientific. They conclude that innovation must be systematically aligned with every part of the modernization agenda. Read the original if you want a compact view of how Chinese scholars link technology policy to the 20th Congress agenda.
quoteEn: A modernized economic system urgently needs strategic support from science and technology innovation.
quoteZh: 现代化经济体系迫切需要来自科技创新的战略支撑

glossary.explanation: A Party goal of shared affluence for all, stressed under Xi Jinping, involving both growing the economy and distributing its gains more evenly.
An approach that mobilises state, market and research resources nationwide to achieve breakthroughs in strategic technologies.
A common expression for China's dependence on foreign suppliers for critical technologies, which could be used to constrain it.
An official concept that puts environmental protection and green development at the centre of national development goals.

t: Understanding the new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times from three dimensions
zh: 从三重维度深入理解马克思主义中国化时代化新的飞跃
paras: Li Youxin takes up an official judgement found in the Resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) and in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). That judgement holds that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has achieved a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Li argues that the claim can be understood along three dimensions: the development of practice, the combination with culture, and theoretical innovation.

The article, published in Mao Zedong Studies in late 2022, is built as three sections, one for each dimension. The first places the Thought within the sequence of historical periods and their leading theories, from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. The second looks at Xi Jinping's treatment of traditional Chinese culture since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third lists the main original contributions that Li attributes to the Thought.

On practice, Li argues that a theoretical leap is measured first by whether real practice has entered a new era. Each earlier leap answered the practical themes of its own period, and the new era is a distinct historical period with new tasks, which the Thought is said to answer. On culture, Li says Marxism can take deep root in China only if combined with its excellent traditional culture. Li reports that Xi set out principles for treating tradition, defended cultural confidence, and put forward the Second Integration. Li also lists creative transformations, such as a community with a shared future for mankind drawing on the idea of "great harmony under heaven", and the Belt and Road Initiative drawing on the ancient Silk Road. On theory, Li names eight areas, including Party leadership as the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, Chinese modernization, and common prosperity.

Li concludes that the Thought is the theoretical crystallisation of the historic achievements and changes since 2012. It is also the contemporary essence of Chinese culture and the Chinese spirit, and it is Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century. These three aspects together are presented as the grounds for the new leap. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars justify the claim of a "new leap" in the Sinicisation of Marxism, and of how the Second Integration is presented.
quoteEn: The primary basis for judging whether the adaptation of Marxism to China has achieved a leap is whether the development of real practice has entered a new era.
quoteZh: 衡量马克思主义中国化是否实现了飞跃，首要的依据是现实实践的发展是否进入了一个新的时代。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. Official texts treat it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and to each new historical period. The 20th Party Congress (2022) added "of our times" to the older phrase "Sinicisation of Marxism".

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-building and anti-corruption strategy pursued since 2012. It stresses discipline and supervision within the Party.
The official name for China's path to modernisation, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.
A goal of shared wealth for all people, given prominence in official policy under Xi Jinping. It is presented as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted since 2012–13. It stresses shared interests and cooperation among states.

t: An action guide for advancing Chinese modernization
zh: 推进中国式现代化的行动指南
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 16 February 2023, p. 6
paras: This commentary, published in the Party discipline newspaper China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News in February 2023, studies Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of a seminar for newly elected Central Committee members and provincial and ministerial leaders. Qu Qingshan calls the speech a brilliant Marxist document, the culminating work of the Party's innovative theory of Chinese modernization and an authoritative elaboration of the 20th Party Congress (2022). In Qu's account, it gives direction and fundamental guidance for building a modern socialist country and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Qu first sets the background: the "three-step" strategy, the Two Centenary Goals, the completion of the first goal, and the 20th Party Congress report's summary of Chinese modernization. That summary comprises five Chinese features, nine essential requirements and five major principles. The article then goes through the six questions Xi addresses in the speech, one section for each.

Qu argues that the six questions form one coherent theoretical system. They cover how Chinese modernization came about, through long exploration by the Party and the people. They cover its fundamental character, which Qu describes as socialist modernization under Party leadership, "the first and most important question". They cover its Chinese features, understood as a unity of general laws and national particularity, and its creation of a "new form of human civilization". In Qu's reading, this form breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers developing countries a new option. The last two questions are methodological. One is the six relationships to be handled correctly, including top-level design and practical exploration, efficiency and fairness, and vitality and order. The other is the need for "great struggle", which requires strategic clarity, confidence and initiative.

Qu concludes that Xi's speech raises the Party's understanding of Chinese modernization to a new level and should guide efforts to implement the 20th Party Congress. He calls for steadfastness on this path and says struggle must be undertaken without hesitation against forces seeking to contain or obstruct national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of Xi's 2023 seminar speech and how the Party's leading historian presents its six themes.
quoteEn: By expounding Chinese modernization through history, General Secretary Xi Jinping has reached a convincing conclusion.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记从历史中阐述中国式现代化，得出了令人信服的结论。

glossary.explanation: The Party's formulation of China's path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models and as having five Chinese features and nine essential requirements.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan describing the restoration of China's national strength and international standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream.
A Party claim that Chinese modernization creates a civilizational form distinct from the Western model, rooted in Chinese tradition and scientific socialism.
A term in Xi Jinping's speeches for the need to confront major risks, challenges and hostile pressure during the drive for national rejuvenation.

t: On the requirements of the new era for upholding historical confidence and strengthening historical initiative
zh: 论坚持历史自信、增强历史主动的新时代要求
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2022 no. 10
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Wang Tingyou and Pei Yanan take up the Congress report's call on the whole Party to "uphold historical confidence and strengthen historical initiative", alongside the newly formulated "three musts". The authors argue that this twofold requirement rests on three things: grasping historical laws and trends, seizing opportunities through innovation, and treating history, including its errors, correctly.

The article has three numbered sections, each opening with a statement of one condition for historical confidence and initiative and closing with practical requirements for studying the Congress's spirit. It moves from the Party's century of struggle and the Marxist view of historical laws, through innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture, to the Party's three historical resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021) and the fight against historical nihilism. It was published in a journal on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping theory.

In the first section the authors hold that history is objective and governed by laws, so a Marxist party must align itself with its direction. They read the Party's path from the founding goal of socialism and communism through reform and opening up to the two centenary goals and Chinese modernization as a record of following those laws. In the second, they argue that necessity makes its way through the practice of the people. The Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, together with the Two Integrations, is presented as the source of its vitality, and the authors list historic shifts in economy, opening up, development philosophy and Party building. In the third, they say that mistakes, including the Cultural Revolution, were unavoidable in exploring a new path, and that what counts is the attitude toward them. Historical nihilism is described as an attempt to deny Party leadership by distorting history. The authors call for viewing history in its concrete conditions and with a long-term perspective.

Wang and Pei conclude that Party members must systematically study Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, keep a spirit of struggle, continue innovation, and learn Party history and the history of the People's Republic, reform and socialism. They present this as the way to ensure that socialism with Chinese characteristics keeps widening its path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a close, officially aligned account of how Party theorists linked historical confidence, historical nihilism and the 20th Congress agenda in late 2022.
quoteEn: The crux is not whether slips and errors occur, but whether the stance and attitude toward them are correct and whether the methods and measures for correcting them are appropriate.
quoteZh: 问题的关键不在于会不会发生失误、出现错误，而是对待失误和错误的立场、态度是否端正，纠正失误和错误的方法、措施是否得当。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in the 20th Party Congress report (2022), meaning confidence in the Party's historical path and achievements, grounded in its reading of historical laws.
The idea that the Party and people actively shape history by grasping its trends and seizing opportunities, rather than passively following events.
A formulation in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) calling on all Party members to remain true to the original aspiration, to be modest and hard-working, and to dare and know how to struggle.
In Party discourse, a label for views seen as denigrating or distorting the Party's history and achievements in order to undermine its leadership and the socialist system.
The official name for China's path to modernization, characterised in the 20th Congress report by features such as huge population scale, common prosperity and peaceful development.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

t: Major innovations of Chinese modernization seen from history
zh: 从历史看中国式现代化的重大创新
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 14 February 2023
paras: Writing in early 2023, Yu Heping asks in what sense Chinese modernization is a major innovation in world modernization theory and practice. Taking up Xi Jinping's claim that it breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization, Yu argues that it contains four innovations: a new summing-up of the course of human civilization, a new direction and form of civilization, a new picture of world modernization, and a new creation in modernization theory. Yu holds that these are concentrated in its stated connotations and fit the historical facts.

This short commentary approaches the question through the changing meaning of "modernization". It moves from the early modernizers, who imitated Britain or the West, to the spread of the concept and Western theory, and then to Chinese ideas of socialist modernization after 1921. It ends with the five connotations set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Yu distinguishes an early stage of intuitive, "perceptual" modernization, largely imitation without a theory of modernization, from later rational understanding. Western modernization theory, in Yu's account, grew from Western experience and mainly meant capitalist industrialization and democratization, so it amounted to a theory of Westernization. Chinese modernization, Yu says, contains these general elements, especially industrialization and democratization, and adds five distinctive features, including a huge population, common prosperity and the harmonious coexistence of humanity and nature. Its decisive difference is a people-centred ultimate purpose. Capitalist modernization, Yu argues, centres on capital accumulation and shares benefits only passively and unevenly.

Yu concludes that Chinese modernization theory is the newest, most comprehensive and highest understanding of modernization so far, and an epoch-making innovation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a CASS historian uses the history of the modernization concept to support the official claim of Chinese modernization's originality.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization explicitly aims at "common prosperity for all the people" and "harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature", and thus makes raising and improving people's lives the fundamental purpose of modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化则明确要实现“全体人民共同富裕”“人与自然和谐共生”，从而把提高和改善人民生活作为现代化的根本目的。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctively Chinese path to modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, one of the five connotations of Chinese modernization named at the 20th Party Congress.

t: Rethinking the relationship between the Sinicization, modernization (keeping pace with the times) and popularization of Marxism
zh: 关于马克思主义中国化、时代化与大众化关系的再思考
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2023 no. 2
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Chen Peiyong asks how three long-discussed categories relate to one another: the Sinicization of Marxism (zhongguohua), its adaptation to the times (shidaihua) and its popularization among the masses (dazhonghua). The article's thesis is that the first two are inseparable yet distinct, and that the third has a different focus. It holds that the Congress's emphasis on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, with popularization no longer named alongside it, does not make popularization less important.

The article first traces the history of the formulations. It covers Mao Zedong's 1938 proposal of Sinicization, the pause in its use after 1952, Deng Xiaoping's formulations about combining universal truth with Chinese realities, and the post-2001 revival. It also covers the 2009 Fourth Plenum document that first listed all three terms together. Chen then analyses each term's meaning, and ends by comparing the Congress reports' wording with the earlier triple formula.

Chen defines Sinicization as the unity of transforming Marxism and transforming China, and adaptation to the times as the unity of transforming Marxism and transforming the age. Both oppose dogmatism, and since China's concrete reality is changing and set within the world, Sinicization already contains adaptation to the times. The difference is that Sinicization stresses space and the times stress time. For a country that lags behind the world's front rank, Chen argues, localization may run against 'keeping up with the times', as in the revolutionary period, when pursuing urban proletarian revolution would have failed. As China's standing has risen, the two requirements are said to be converging, so that Sinicized Marxism now also aims to lead the era.

Popularization is defined as the unity of transforming Marxism and reaching the masses. It concerns the form of expression, whereas the other two concern theoretical content. Chen sees possible tension: popularization can slide into vulgarization or trivialization and misread new theoretical results. Chen nonetheless insists that the task is far from finished and that its success should be a standard for judging whether Sinicization and adaptation to the times succeed. Read the original if you want a conceptual and textual history of how the Party's official triple formula developed, and a Party-theorist's reading of why popularization dropped out of the 20th Congress wording.
quoteEn: The Sinicization of Marxism stresses the dimension of space, whereas the adaptation of Marxism to the times stresses the dimension of time.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化强调的是空间的维度，马克思主义时代化强调的则是时间的维度。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's realities and to contemporary conditions, and developing theory in the process. The 20th Party Congress (2022) used it prominently.

t: Opening up a new realm for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in February 2023, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Tao contends that the Party's success and the strengths of socialism with Chinese characteristics ultimately rest on Marxism in this adapted form. In Tao's account, the thought answers major questions of the new era and opens a new realm of that adaptation.

The piece is organised around six headings: answering the major questions of the new era; revealing the innovative mechanism of the Two Integrations; its original content; its scientific worldview and methodology; and its guidance of the great changes of the new era. It draws on Marx's remark that true philosophy is the essence of its own age's spirit, and it sets the thought against the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and what Tao calls changes unseen in a century.

Tao argues that the thought arose from the practice of the new era and addresses what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics, socialist modernised power and long-governing Marxist party should be built, and how. Combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture is presented as the fundamental path of Marxism's innovative development in China. Tao says the thought, summarised in the “Ten Clarifications”, “Fourteen Commitments” and “Thirteen Areas of Achievement”, has made original contributions to Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. It also embodies a worldview and method: people-centredness, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, problem orientation, systematic thinking and a global outlook.

Tao concludes that the great changes since the 18th Party Congress (2012) were achieved under the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and under the guidance of this thought, and that the Two Establishes are the decisive political achievement behind them. In this reading, the changes strengthened the Party, advanced the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and gave Chinese modernization as a new option for other countries. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line in early 2023 presented Xi Jinping Thought as a theoretical innovation within the Sinification of Marxism.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era upholds combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture, and thereby profoundly reveals the fundamental path of Marxism's innovative development in China.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，坚持把马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合、同中华优秀传统文化相结合，深刻揭示了马克思主义在中国创新发展的根本途径

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's effort to fit Marxism to Chinese conditions and to contemporary developments. The phrase “of our times” was added to the older “Sinification of Marxism”.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was stressed in Xi Jinping's 2021 and 2023 statements.
A formula adopted in the Party's 2021 historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central national goal in Party discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Why high-quality and full employment should be emphasised
zh: 为什么要强调高质量充分就业
paras: This short newspaper commentary takes up a line from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls for strengthening the employment-first policy and promoting high-quality and full employment. Zhang asks what the term means, why it deserves emphasis and how it can be achieved. The answer is that employment of this kind meets the needs of employers and workers alike and supports wider economic upgrading.

The article first defines high-quality and full employment through four features, then sets out four policy directions. It is a compact policy explainer rather than a theoretical study, and it closes by calling the task a systematic project.

On definition, Zhang describes such employment as meeting enterprises' demand for human resources, as decent work for employees, as supporting a unified, competitive and flexible national labour market, and as promoting technological change and industrial restructuring. Decent work is understood as adequate pay, good working conditions, harmonious labour relations and secured rights. Zhang notes that labour supply has fallen short of demand in recent years and that structural mismatches persist. The four policy directions are keeping the economy within a reasonable range, strengthening firms' capacity to absorb workers, matching workers' skills to market needs, and improving supporting labour-market institutions.

Zhang's proposals include relief for firms, a better environment for private enterprise, lifelong vocational training, reform of the household registration and social security systems, and better protection for flexible and platform workers. The author concludes that labour-market institution building and related reforms must go further, with social policy providing a safety net. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line account of how Chinese policy commentary framed employment goals after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: High-quality and full employment is a systematic project.
quoteZh: 高质量充分就业是一项系统工程。

glossary.explanation: A policy stance, reaffirmed in the 20th Party Congress report, that treats employment as a priority in macroeconomic and social policy.
A goal stated in the 20th Party Congress report that combines the quantity of jobs (full employment) with their quality, including pay, conditions and rights.
A concept, also used by the International Labour Organization, covering adequate pay, good working conditions, social protection and sound labour relations.

t: How Chinese modernization resolves the problems of China's modernization, and why it matters
zh: 中国式现代化对中国现代化难题的解决及其意义
source: Journal of Guizhou University (Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 1
paras: Wang Yuchen asks how Chinese modernization differs from earlier attempts to modernize China, and what it offers the world. The article argues that Chinese modernization is modernization led by the Communist Party, and that it solved four problems that China's modernization faced: forming a political leadership force, combining efficiency with common prosperity, overcoming ecological constraints, and pursuing peaceful development through exchange and mutual learning among civilizations.

After defining modernization in broad and narrow senses, Wang classes China's case as "late-developing, externally stimulated" modernization, a challenge-and-response type, in contrast to the "early-developing, endogenous" Western type. Four sections treat the four problems in turn, drawing on the Party's historical record from Mao Zedong through Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. A final section sets out the significance for late-developing countries and for human civilization.

On leadership, Wang holds that the late-Qing reform efforts and the 1911 Revolution failed for lack of a mature political leader, whereas the Party's founding mission and its Marxist, people-centred character made it that force. On common prosperity, the article contrasts capitalist modernization, which it says produces polarization and alienation, with the Party's explorations from Mao's socialism through Deng's "some get rich first" approach to Xi's staged targets for 2035 and the middle of the century. On ecology, Wang traces a shift from industrial-era environmental protection to ecological civilization, and presents Xi's "lucid waters and lush mountains" approach, legal institutions and "community of life" ideas as a path distinct from the West. On peace, Wang says Chinese modernization rejects colonial plunder, the "clash of civilizations" thesis (Huntington) and the "end of history" thesis (Fukuyama).

Wang concludes that Chinese modernization offers late-developing countries a model of building mature political leadership while developing independently rather than copying others. It also overcomes what Wang calls the one-sided, distorted character of Western modernization, and so creates a new form of human civilization. In this reading it deepens understanding of the laws of human and socialist development and is a new development of contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-line account of how Chinese modernization is positioned against Western modernization and dependency-type development paths.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is modernization led by the Party, and is different from the modernization of China.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是党领导的现代化，不同于中国的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's own path to modernization, first used by Deng Xiaoping in 1979 and elaborated by Xi Jinping, especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all rather than a few. It has been emphasised again under Xi Jinping, with targets set for 2035 and mid-century.
A Party concept that places environmental protection at the centre of development. It entered Party documents at the 17th Party Congress (2007) and was elevated at the 18th (2012).

t: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army: an enduring monument between the White Mountains and Black Waters
zh: 东北抗联精神：白山黑水间永立的不朽丰碑
paras: This commentary, published in the Party journal Dangjian in 2023, takes up the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, the Communist-led guerrilla force that fought Japanese occupation in north-east China. He argues that this spirit, forged in blood in the mountains and forests of the north-east, is a lasting part of the Party's spiritual heritage. It remains, in his account, a resource for the Party and the country in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how the spirit formed and where it stands historically. The second analyses its content under three headings. The third lists its present-day value. He draws on statements by Mao Zedong (1949) and Xi Jinping (2015 and 2016) to support the spirit's standing.

In the first part, He identifies four features of the Northeast struggle: it lasted 14 years, it was cut off behind enemy lines without Nationalist aid, its hardship reached the limits of human endurance, and it was marked by setbacks, including the influence of "Left" errors in the Party. He names five conditions behind the spirit: Party leadership, firm ideals and convictions, strong political and ideological work, the example of Communist commanders such as Zhao Shangzhi, Li Zhaolin and Zhao Yiman, and the harsh environment. Its core content, he argues, is loyalty to the Party, the national righteousness of answering the call of national crisis, and a heroic determination to fight to the end. The last includes mountain guerrilla warfare and cooperation with Korean and Soviet anti-Japanese forces, which he calls internationalism.

For the present, He calls for five tasks. These are to strengthen Party members' ideals and convictions through regular, institutionalised education, and to promote patriotism in pursuit of the Chinese Dream. He also calls for a fighting spirit to meet the "great struggle" with many new historical features, and for the Party's absolute leadership over the armed forces. Finally he calls for a global outlook that advances a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want an example of how Party publications present a regional anti-Japanese war history as part of the Party's spiritual lineage and link it to current political tasks.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army is a precious spiritual asset created by the Party leading the people through a century of struggle, an immortal monument of the spirit that transcends time and space, grows ever fresher, and inspires later generations for ever.
quoteZh: 东北抗联精神是党领导人民在百年奋斗中创造的宝贵精神财富，是超越时空、历久弥新、永激后人的不朽精神丰碑。

glossary.explanation: Communist-led guerrilla forces that fought the Japanese occupation of Manchuria from the 1930s to 1945. Often abbreviated in Chinese as 东北抗联.
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing cooperation and shared interests.
The official term for the series of named 'spirits' (such as the Jinggangshan spirit or the Daqing spirit) that the Party presents as its inherited moral and political tradition.

t: The spiritual force for realizing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation: connotation, relationships and paths
zh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴的精神力量：内涵、关系与路径
paras: Zhang Zhiyong takes up a theme highlighted in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): strengthening the "spiritual force" (jingshen liliang) for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article argues that national rejuvenation needs spiritual as well as material strength. It defines this force as the confident, self-reliant, innovative and proactive energy the Chinese people show under Party leadership, and proposes ways to strengthen it.

The article opens with a literature review. It covers the Marxist theoretical basis of spiritual force, how scholars explain its content and origins, and the paths they propose for promoting it, such as the great founding spirit of the Party, the spiritual lineage built on it, and core socialist values. Zhang finds the field short on historical-process studies, interdisciplinary work and innovative findings. The body then has three parts: the connotation and distinctive features of this force, four relationships to be handled, and a set of practical paths.

On connotation, Zhang draws on Marx to say that spirit is a reflection of social being, and that rejuvenation is a practical and historical undertaking, not a purely spiritual one. Theory guided by Marxism turns into material force when it grips the masses. Zhang identifies three features: autonomous initiative, selection and creativity, and mature self-confidence. The four relationships are material and spiritual needs in a good life, material and spiritual civilization in Chinese modernization, material and spiritual prosperity in common prosperity, and positive and negative mentalities in the pursuit of happiness. Zhang says material gains do not automatically bring spiritual ones, and cites problems such as money worship, "lying flat" (tangping) and "involution" (neijuan).

For the paths, Zhang calls for five efforts. The first is to study Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era so as to take spiritual initiative. The second is to teach the Party's centenary achievements and the changes of the past decade, to build confidence. The third is to produce literary and artistic works built around patriotism and core values. The fourth is to promote a fighting spirit. The fifth is to celebrate striving, with officials, model workers and youth as examples. Zhang concludes that a theoretical system of Chinese spiritual force remains an important research task. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-scholar account of how the spiritual dimension of national rejuvenation is conceptualised and how it is to be cultivated in policy.
quoteEn: Realizing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is in essence a practical and historical activity, and cannot be understood simply as an activity of pure spiritual force.
quoteZh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴本质上是一种实践的历史的活动，不能单纯理解为纯粹的精神力量的活动。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central long-term goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity. It is closely associated with Xi Jinping's slogan of the Chinese Dream.
The article's key term for the subjective drive, confidence and initiative of a people and a Party. It is stressed in the 20th Party Congress report as a complement to material strength.
The official description of China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It is said to coordinate material and spiritual civilization and to pursue common prosperity.
A socialist goal of shared wealth, which official discourse since 2021 has stressed. Here it is read as covering spiritual as well as material wellbeing.

glossary.en: the great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation introduced by Xi Jinping in 2021 for the values of the Party's founding period. It is treated as the source of the Party's "spiritual lineage" (jingshen pupu).

keywords: great founding spirit of the Party

t: The evolution of the Socialist International's conception of democracy
zh: 社会党国际民主观的演进研究
paras: Wang Zhao asks how the Socialist International (SI) has understood democracy since its refounding in 1951 and what its shifts reveal about world social democracy. The article argues that democracy has been the core of SI theory throughout, and that its conception of democracy has passed through three successive "third ways". The first lay between capitalism and communism, the second between traditional social democracy and neoliberalism, and the third, now emerging, between traditional social democracy and social liberalism.

The article is organised chronologically in three parts. The first traces the historical starting point, from the 1848 revolutions and Bernstein's revisionism to the 1951 Frankfurt Declaration, and the later broadening of its "four democracies" (political, economic, social and international). The second covers the post-Cold War period: the shift from "democratic socialism" to "social democracy", the promotion of democracy abroad, the rightward turn of the Blair-style "third way", and a democratic conception of global governance. The third examines the period since the financial crisis, the split of 2013 and the SI's recent adjustments.

Wang's central claim is that the SI's democracy has moved along the ideological spectrum from left to centre-left to "centrist", then back left. Before the Cold War ended, the SI treated democracy as a reform tool within capitalist parliamentary systems, while still retaining a European-centred standard. After 1991 it dropped the "socialism" label and converged with bourgeois liberal democracy, which Wang says cost social-democratic parties their distinct identity. After the 2008 crisis, a dispute between a Western European "reformist" camp and a "traditionalist" camp of southern European and developing-world parties over political, social and organisational democracy led to the 2013 founding of the Progressive Alliance. Wang presents this as the ideological cause of the split.

Since the split, Wang reports, the SI has shifted left and added "progressivism" to its democratic vision. This takes in political democracy, economic democracy opposed to neoliberalism, a revived welfare state, and democratisation of the UN and of globalisation, with attention to weaker groups and developing countries. Wang judges that this brings no theoretical breakthrough, and that a fourth theoretical transformation of social democracy remains at an exploratory stage. Read the original if you want a detailed, document-based account of Socialist International congress resolutions and declarations as seen from a Chinese contemporary-socialism research perspective.
quoteEn: On the whole, although the Socialist International has adjusted its conception of democracy since the financial crisis and moved towards \"progressivism\", there has been no great breakthrough at the theoretical level.
quoteZh: 总体来看，金融危机以来社会党国际的民主观虽然进行了调整，推动了向“进步主义”的转变，但在理论层面并没有太大的突破

glossary.explanation: The worldwide association of social-democratic, socialist and labour parties, refounded in Frankfurt in 1951. Chinese scholarship studies it as the main organisational form of world social democracy.
The label adopted in the 1951 Frankfurt Declaration for the SI's doctrine, set against Soviet-style socialism. Chinese scholarship treats it as a reformist current distinct from scientific socialism.
A position between two opposed systems or doctrines. The author uses it for three phases of SI thought and also for the Blair-era centrism of the 1990s.
A network of social-democratic parties founded in 2013, led by the German SPD and other Western European parties, as an alternative to the Socialist International.
The author's term for the framework set out in the 1951 Frankfurt Declaration: political, economic, social and international democracy.

t: Strengthening the spiritual force for realizing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 增强实现中华民族伟大复兴的精神力量
paras: Shen Zhuanghai takes up a strategic requirement set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022): strengthening the spiritual force needed to realize the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Shen argues that a nation without spirit cannot stand, and that the achievements of Chinese civilisation, of the Party and people over the past century, and of the decade since 2012 all depended on such spirit. On this basis the article holds that the new journey toward a modern socialist country requires an even more buoyant spiritual state.

This is a short commentary published in Qiushi in early 2023. It is organised around six conditions, each introduced with the same formula: spiritual force cannot be strengthened without scientific theory, a conscious and firm development strategy, the inheritance and renewal of spiritual traditions, a flourishing culture, advanced institutions, and, finally, concrete practice. Each section ends with what Shen says must be done on the new journey.

Shen's central claim is that spiritual force becomes deeper and more lasting only when scientific theory is fused with it. Theory, in this account, gives spirit direction, cohesion, purity and firmness. Marxism, and now Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is to be the guiding ideology that turns conviction into practice. Shen also stresses that spirit and institutions shape each other. The 20th Party Congress report's emphasis on Chinese modernization, on coordinating material and spiritual civilisation, and on a more complete institutional guarantee is read as showing that institutional strength must be converted into governance capacity and into united spiritual force among the people.

Shen further calls for passing on traditional Chinese virtues and the Party's spiritual lineage, which begins with the spirit of the founding of the Party. This is to be done through education in Party history and the history of the People's Republic. Shen also calls for building a socialist cultural power under Marxist ideological leadership and the core socialist values. The article ends by arguing that spiritual force becomes real only through practice, and that the new era is both a time of struggle and a time to build a new spiritual highland for the nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists in 2023 linked ideology, culture, tradition and institutions to the national rejuvenation agenda.
quoteEn: A society's institutional system and its spiritual system, its institutional force and spiritual force, its institutional advantages and spiritual advantages, shape one another.
quoteZh: 一个社会的制度体系与精神体系、制度力量与精神力量、制度优势与精神优势是互塑的。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, usually tied to making China prosperous and strong by the mid-twenty-first century. It was given prominence under Xi Jinping through the idea of the Chinese Dream.

The official name for China's path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It lists distinctive features such as a huge population, common prosperity, and coordination of material and spiritual civilisation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

An official term for the ethical, cultural and ideological side of social development, paired with material civilisation. Since the reform era the Party has treated its construction as a task alongside economic growth.
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since 2012 as the basis for cultural and moral education.

t: Three errors in the theory of "wholesale Westernization"
zh: “全盘西化”论的三个错误
paras: Zuo Yuhe takes up the theory of "wholesale Westernization" (quanpan xihua), a cultural current that was influential in modern China, and argues that it is flawed in theory. Zuo holds that although Hu Shi was the first to use the slogan, its genuine advocates were Chen Xujing of Lingnan University and a group of like-minded scholars. The article identifies three core errors.

The piece is a short commentary. It first sets out Chen Xujing's position, developed in his 1930 essay and his 1932 book on the future of Chinese culture, then examines the premises on which it rests: the claim that Western culture is superior, the denial that Chinese civilisation can modernise itself, and a doctrine of cultural wholeness and indivisibility.

Zuo concedes that the West was more advanced in Chen's time and that the advocates' aims of democracy, science, individual liberation and attacks on feudal hierarchy were progressive. Against them, Zuo argues first that civilisation has both a temporal and a national character, so backwardness in era does not prove national inferiority, and that the fine traditions of Chinese culture can be creatively transformed. Second, civilisation has material, institutional and spiritual levels that are connected but relatively independent, so wholesale acceptance does not follow. Third, the equation of modernization with Westernization is false: Zuo points to new factors in Ming–Qing China and treats Westernization as only one model among several.

Zuo concludes that the advocates neglected national character, absolutised the unity of culture and equated Western civilisation with world civilisation, which Zuo calls Eurocentric. Zuo adds that China has opened a distinctive path of Chinese modernization that points to a new form of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese historian's critique of the 1930s Westernization debate, framed in terms of present-day official discourse on modernization.
quoteEn: Modernization is the trend of development of world civilisation; "Westernization" is merely one of the models of world modernization.
quoteZh: 现代化是世界文明发展趋势，“西化”仅仅是世界现代化发展模式中的一种而已。

glossary.explanation: A cultural position of the 1920s–30s holding that China should adopt Western culture entirely. Hu Shi used the slogan, and Chen Xujing developed it theoretically.
An official Party term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from the Western model.

t: Comprehensively advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization
zh: 以中国式现代化全面推进中华民族伟大复兴
paras: This article is a study of the 20th Party Congress (2022) thesis that Chinese modernization should be the means of comprehensively advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Zhang argues that this path is rooted in China's own conditions, is shaped by distinctive Chinese features and advantages, and offers a new option for other countries. The text follows Xi Jinping's report to the Congress closely and quotes it often.

The article is organised in three parts. The first presents Chinese modernization as the necessary road to national rejuvenation and traces how Party leaders set modernization goals in different periods. The second sets out the features, essential requirements and principles that the report attributes to Chinese modernization, and stresses two defining elements. The third considers its significance for the world and for the Global South.

In the first part, Zhang reads Xi's remark that China's modernization is both "the most difficult" and "the greatest" as reflecting a late-developing, populous Eastern country that lost the chance of the Industrial Revolution and had to find its own way. The article lists Mao Zedong's goal of the four modernizations, Deng Xiaoping's use of a moderately prosperous society (xiaokang) to define Chinese-style modernization with a three-step strategy, and Xi's formulation since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second part argues that Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics are the two features that matter most in the long run. Zhang presents them as the basis of two achievements, rapid economic growth and long-term social stability, and of the coordinated development of five forms of civilization. In the third part, Zhang says the path rejects modernization through war, colonialism and plunder, and cites Xi's statements that no single modernization model exists and that diverse paths should be respected.

Zhang concludes that Chinese modernization has driven national rejuvenation into an irreversible historical process and has brought the goal into the lives of ordinary people. The article presents the path as a "new form of human civilization" that gives developing countries seeking both growth and independence a new choice. It also promises Chinese wisdom, proposals and strength for humanity's shared problems. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how Party scholars summarised the 20th Party Congress line on Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation shortly after the Congress.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization fits China's realities, and it reflects both the laws of socialist construction and the laws of human social development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化既切合中国实际，体现了社会主义建设规律，也体现了人类社会发展规律。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for its own path of modernization, elaborated in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as led by the Party and combining features common to all countries with features specific to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in official discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the 'century of humiliation'.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership and a socialist system with market mechanisms and China-specific conditions.

A term Deng Xiaoping used from the late 1970s for a modest level of prosperity as the first target of China's modernization. It has remained a staple of official goals, including the building of a moderately prosperous society in all respects.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in official texts to describe the outcome of Chinese modernization, presented as an alternative to Western modernization models.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse often presents as the main audience for China's development experience.

t: Five dimensions of the critique of historical nihilism
zh: 历史虚无主义思潮批判的五重论域
source: Research on Ideological and Political Education (思想教育研究), 2022 no. 12
paras: Jing Hui takes up historical nihilism, which the article treats as a foreign import and an ongoing threat to China's ideological security. The article argues that it should be criticised systematically from five angles: its existence, essence, harms, duration and methodology. Its stated aim is to clear away the value confusions the trend creates and so strengthen the ideological defences of the Party and the country.

The article opens by citing Xi Jinping's calls since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to oppose historical nihilism openly, in the context of the goal of the Two Consolidations. It then proceeds through five sections. The first maps where historical nihilism now appears: academic research, literary and artistic work, and cyberspace. The second identifies its essence. The third sets out its harms. The fourth explains why the struggle against it will be long. The fifth proposes a method of critique.

Jing's central claim is that historical nihilism is, at root, a denial of Marxism's guiding role, of the Communist Party's leadership and of the historical necessity of China's path to socialism. The author describes its tactics as selective deconstruction, fragmentation and subjective arrangement of history, and in online settings the use of big data, algorithms and recycled old content. The author holds that it fragments historical understanding, dissolves national spirit and erodes cultural confidence, and points to Xi's remarks on the collapse of the Soviet Union and the Soviet Communist Party. Its persistence is attributed to the coexistence of several forms of ownership, lingering cultural inferiority, anxiety about reform, and what the article calls ideological infiltration by hostile forces at home and abroad.

Jing calls for a methodological response grounded in historical materialism, which is meant to expose the idealist basis of historical nihilism. It also calls for class analysis, which is meant to reveal its bourgeois standpoint, and for a rigorous, fact-based approach to historical scholarship. That approach would treat the mainstream and tributaries of history dialectically and refuse to let isolated errors cancel out achievements. The author also urges preparing for a long struggle rather than expecting quick results. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist education journal frames historical nihilism as an ideological-security problem and what counter-method it proposes.
quoteEn: Historical nihilists often collect, organise and analyse historical sources with a pragmatic or utilitarian bent, being "nihilistic about some things and not about others" according to usefulness, and so end up with conclusions that contradict historical fact.
quoteZh: 历史虚无主义者往往带着一种实用主义或功利色彩搜集整理、分析论证史料，根据有用与否对之“有所虚无，有所不虚无”，最终得出违背历史事实的结论。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese official discourse, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history, the history of the People's Republic or the revolutionary tradition. It is treated as an ideological threat, and critics of the label see it as covering a wide range of historical debate.
An official formula about consolidating the Communist Party's ruling position and consolidating the socialist system. It is used to frame ideological work as a matter of political security.
An official term for confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It is presented as underpinning confidence in the path, theory and system.

t: The value orientation and generative logic of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的价值旨归和生成逻辑
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhao Chaofeng asks what Chinese modernization is for and how it came about. The article argues that Chinese modernization is the necessary path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, that it was created through the Party-led socialist practice of the People's Republic, and that it fits Chinese realities while also embodying scientific laws. The 20th Congress slogan of comprehensively advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Zhao says, gives modernization a clearer value orientation.

The article has three parts. The first treats modernization as the fundamental route to rejuvenation and as the shaper of a new form of human civilization. The second traces the historical formation of the path: the New Democratic Revolution, industrialization under the Five-Year Plans, the Four Modernizations, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third explains why the path suits China's conditions and reflects three sets of laws. Zhao draws on Marx, Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, and on Party congress documents from the 13th (1987) to the 20th.

Zhao's central move is to identify modernization with rejuvenation in both logic and timing. Both goals, the article says, were placed in the same period by the theory of the primary stage of socialism and the later two-centenary targets, so rejuvenation is the arrival of a modern socialist country that leads its age and is not a return to the past. Zhao then equates socialism with Chinese characteristics with the Chinese modernization path, as two expressions of one thing. Modernization fits Chinese conditions through staged strategies and a 'parallel' catch-up model that combines industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization. It embodies socialist laws through Party leadership, the liberation and development of the productive forces, and common prosperity. It also embodies general laws of social development: the movement of contradictions, human liberation and all-round development, and a rejection of the Western capital-centred route and of Western-centrism.

Zhao concludes that Chinese modernization has taken China from 'catching up with the times' to 'leading the times', and that it will continue after the building of a modern socialist country, lifting the primary stage of socialism to a higher level. The path is said to have created a new form of human civilization, to give the Party a concrete route towards the Second Centenary Goal, and to offer developing countries a Chinese option. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Chinese modernization is tied to rejuvenation, socialism with Chinese characteristics and the primary stage of socialism, with references to Party congress documents.
quoteEn: "Socialism with Chinese characteristics" and "Chinese-style modernization" are different expressions of one and the same thing, in terms of social nature and state condition; in this sense, the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics is the path of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: “中国特色的社会主义”和“中国式的现代化”是同一事物在社会性质和国家状态方面的不同表达，从这个意义上说，中国特色社会主义道路就是中国式现代化道路。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
