glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for restoring China to national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It is associated with the Chinese Dream and the two centenary goals.
A thesis set out at the 13th Party Congress in 1987. It holds that China is in a long initial period of socialism in which it must complete industrialization and develop a commodity economy.
The Party's name for its overall theory, path and system since reform and opening up. It is presented as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.
A stated goal of socialism in Party discourse, meaning prosperity shared by all people. It has been emphasised heavily under Xi Jinping.

t: The internal mechanism and implementation path of state-owned enterprises in promoting common prosperity
zh: 国有企业促进共同富裕的内在机理及其实现路径
paras: Di Minxue asks how common prosperity can be advanced in practice and why state-owned enterprises should take the lead. The article argues that the main obstacle is distribution, that distribution is at root a question of ownership, and that state-owned enterprises, because of their ownership character and strength, should act as pilots by raising workers' pay.

The text has three parts. The first sets out the problems facing common prosperity and the theoretical analysis behind them, drawing on Marx, Deng Xiaoping, Xi Jinping and the economist Liu Guoguang. The second explains the mechanism by which state-owned enterprises contribute. The third proposes a micro-level pilot scheme with four steps: creating a favourable environment, enterprise applications, approval and supervision, and guiding policies.

Di frames the issue as "making the cake" and "dividing the cake", and holds that after four decades of rapid growth, division is the main problem. The article cites a Gini coefficient of 0.465 in 2019 and an urban–rural income ratio of nearly 2.6 in 2020. Following Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme, Di maintains that production conditions determine consumption distribution, so widening gaps reflect the shift from public to private ownership and the growth of private employment, and that public ownership must stay dominant. State-owned enterprises are said to be specially suited because they are owned by the whole people and under Party leadership, and because they are strong in technology and capital. Di credits them with supplying cultural products, paying higher wages than private firms (using wage tables for 2011–2020), remitting profits for transfer payments, investing in the western regions and Xinjiang, and serving as a "universal light" that steadies markets and strengthens private-sector wage bargaining.

Di proposes that the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission set up a working group on raising labour remuneration. It would select pilot firms that are large, technology-based, and have good labour relations. These firms would put into practice the shared development philosophy through joint consultation, joint construction of mechanisms, joint creation of benefits and shared results. Incentives would include honours, priority in national projects and legislation treating wage increases as profit remitted to the state, preferably at a lower credited rate. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist-economics case for assigning state firms the lead in common prosperity, including a concrete institutional design.
quoteEn: The distribution problem is in essence an ownership problem; this is the economic position of Marx, the founder of Marxism, and one that Chinese Communists have consistently upheld throughout reform and opening up and the new stage of development.
quoteZh: 分配问题本质上是所有制问题，是马克思主义创始人马克思的经济学主张，也是中国共产党人在改革开放和新发展阶段始终坚守的主张。

glossary.explanation: A goal first raised by Mao Zedong in the 1950s and restated by Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. It refers to prosperity for all the people, material and cultural, as distinct from egalitarian levelling.
One of the five development concepts adopted at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2015), holding that the fruits of development should be shared by all.

t: Belt and Road research seen through the global value chain of ideas
zh: 从全球思想价值链角度看“一带一路”研究情况
paras: Wang Wen gives this keynote speech at a Zhejiang seminar on area studies and the Belt and Road Initiative, held with the opening ceremony of Zhejiang Normal University's African area-studies institute. He argues that the Initiative is reshaping the global value chain of ideas, and that research on it has cooled at home while being distorted abroad.

The speech first sets out the decline in publication, then explains why research has cooled, and ends with proposals for rebuilding the chain of ideas and organising future work. Wang also lists gaps the Initiative fills in global public goods, trust, governance and multilateralism.

Wang cites falling numbers: Chinese-language journal articles peaked at over 30,000 in 2017 and fell by 2021 to a third of that, and books fell to 447 in 2021. Foreign-language books fell from 37 in 2019 to 3 in 2021. Meanwhile, according to Wang, over 1,400 international think tanks issued 674 reports in the first nine months of 2021, twice the previous year's figure, mostly negative, citing debt traps, opacity and vaccine diplomacy. Wang attributes the domestic cooling partly to a clearing-out of superficial, trend-chasing work, and partly to a lack of new topics and an underestimate of how long and contested the Initiative will be. In Wang's view, it faces a short-term contest over public opinion and a long-term contest over quality.

Wang calls for firm rebuttal of what are described as US distortions, and for more in-depth, innovative work by Chinese think tanks and scholars. Proposals include a dedicated research fund, a transnational research association, and combining strategic firmness with tactical flexibility. Read the original if you want a Chinese think-tank leader's account of how the Initiative's research and international image are framed as a contest of ideas.
quoteEn: Belt and Road research has met the negative phenomenon of cooling at home and distortion abroad, which is a very important new change.
quoteZh: “一带一路”研究遇到了国内转冷、国际扭曲的消极现象，这是非常重要的一个新变化。

glossary.explanation: China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, announced by Xi Jinping in 2013, covering many countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.
A Chinese academic field devoted to the study of particular regions and countries, promoted in recent years as a discipline of its own.

t: Opening up new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界
source: China Higher Education Social Sciences (Zhongguo gaoxiao shehui kexue), 2023 no. 1
paras: Guo Jianning and Wei Yueyan take up a central theme of the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): opening up new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Writing in early 2023, they argue that this task is the theme, general outline and guiding thread of the Party's theoretical innovation in the new era, and that it expresses a high degree of theoretical consciousness. In their account, theoretical innovation, like practice, has no end point.

The article is organised in four parts. It sets out the theoretical form of the new horizon, centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It then examines the practical achievements, above all Chinese modernization and a "new form of human civilization". Next it discusses the cultural foundations, and finally the features of the era that shape the theory.

The authors' core claim is that the Party's strength rests on Marxism that has been adapted to China and the times. They present the Two Integrations (of Marxist principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture) and the "six persistences" as the essence of the Thought. They see Chinese modernization as the main practical result: they describe its five distinctive features, nine essential requirements and five major principles, and argue that it is not a copy of foreign models. They contrast it with a Western modernization that, in their characterisation, is capital-centred, polarising and expansionist. On culture, they argue that traditional ideas such as people-based governance and harmony are activated by Marxist truth, so that Marxism takes root in China. They add that the "two overall situations" (national rejuvenation and global change unseen in a century), a community with a shared future for mankind, a fighting spirit and "taking the historical initiative" define the era.

The authors conclude that the Party must keep a vigorous spirit and take the historical initiative in advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They also link this task to the Party's central mission of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned reading of the 20th Party Congress theoretical framework, with the major slogans of the Two Integrations, Chinese modernization and cultural confidence laid out in one place.
quoteEn: Marxism can take root only when it is adapted to China, win people's hearts only when it is localised, and be full of vitality only when it keeps pace with the times.
quoteZh: 马克思主义只有中国化才能落地生根、本土化才能深入人心、时代化才能充满生机。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's concrete conditions and updating it for each era. The 20th Party Congress report added "times" (shídàihuà) to the older "sinicization" formula.

Xi Jinping's formula for integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in 2021–2023 official discourse.

The Party's official concept of China's own path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is characterised by a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017. Official texts describe it as "contemporary Chinese Marxism" and "twenty-first-century Marxism".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since 2012–2013, stressing cooperation and shared interests among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China to strength and prosperity by the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: Continuously writing new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 不断谱写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Shen Chuanliang asks how the Party should keep adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The author's answer is that this requires treating Marxism scientifically, treating Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as its latest achievement, and holding to the Two Integrations as the fundamental route. Shen also calls for mastering the stance, viewpoint and method that run through that body of thought.

The article is a study-and-interpretation piece in five sections. It begins with why Marxism must be localised and how the Party has done so over a century. It then sets out the content of Xi Jinping Thought: the "ten affirmations", the "fourteen commitments" and the "thirteen areas of achievement". The third section treats the Two Integrations, the fourth the "six musts" of the Congress report, and the fifth the role of the Thought in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Shen argues that any scientific theory has to be localised to work, citing Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao on applying theory according to concrete conditions. Integrating Marxism with China's concrete realities means grasping both what stays constant and what changes: the primary stage of socialism, the principal social contradiction and popular expectations. The author says integration with fine traditional Chinese culture is possible because the two share values, such as "all under heaven for the public good" and the people as the foundation of the state, and the ideal of a great harmony. Shen presents the "six musts" (putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, problem orientation, systematic thinking, a global vision) as a logically connected system. The article also stresses that the Thought is open and still developing, and that the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds are decisive for the Party.

Shen concludes that the Thought gives the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation its basic direction (socialism with Chinese characteristics), spiritual support and scientific method. The author calls on the whole Party to study the Thought's worldview and methodology and apply them to risks and challenges. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's systematic, officially aligned reading of the 20th Congress report's theoretical formulations, including the "ten affirmations" and the "six musts".
quoteEn: Problems, as the concrete manifestation of reality, are not only the voice of the times but also the \"midwife\" of theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 问题作为实际的具体表现，不仅是时代的声音，也是理论创新的“助产婆”。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party Constitution in 2017. Official texts call it the latest achievement of adapting Marxism to China.
The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–22.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's project of developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and the demands of each era.
A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, with 2049 as the target for a modern socialist country.
The official characterisation of China's current development stage, in use since the 1980s. It underlies the Party's judgement of national conditions.

t: Striving to promote common prosperity for all the people on the new road of the "examination"
zh: 在新的赶考路上着力促进全体人民共同富裕
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Jiang Shuping takes up a new formulation in Xi Jinping's report: for the first time, "achieving common prosperity for all the people" is named an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, beyond being one of its important features. Jiang argues that this reflects the Party Central Committee's conscious commitment to its original aspiration and founding mission, and that it places common prosperity at the centre of the new journey of building a modern socialist country.

The piece is a short interpretive commentary built in three parts. The first reviews how the Party has pursued common prosperity, from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping through to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second traces how the issue has been raised in priority, from the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) to the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission meeting of August 2021 and the 20th Congress report. The third sets out how substantive progress is to be made.

Jiang presents the pursuit of common prosperity as a basic Marxist position and as a continuous line of Party exploration, citing Mao's "common wealth, common strength" and Deng's definition of the essence of socialism. For the recent period, the author points to the elimination of absolute poverty, the building of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, and the large education, social security and health systems. Jiang notes the three-stage goals set in 2021 (narrowing gaps by the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan, equal access to basic public services by 2035, basic realization by mid-century). The author concedes that unbalanced and inadequate development and urban–rural, regional and income gaps remain large, and argues that progress requires doing one's best within one's means, improving the distribution system and social security, and pursuing high-quality development under the new development philosophy.

Jiang concludes that, on the new "examination" road, the Party must uphold its overall leadership, keep economic development as the central task, rely on the people and persevere to produce a better answer for history and the people. Common prosperity is described as a long-term yet practical task for more than 1.4 billion people, one that can be neither rushed nor delayed. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the 20th Congress report positions common prosperity within Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Achieving common prosperity for over 1.4 billion people is both a long-term task and a practical one; it can be neither rushed nor delayed, and requires doing one's best while acting within one's means, working steadily and persistently.
quoteZh: 实现14亿多人的共同富裕是一项长期任务，也是一项现实任务，推动共同富裕急不得，也等不得，要尽力而为，又要量力而行，脚踏实地、久久为功。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, restated by Xi Jinping's leadership since 2021 as a central aim, with targets for 2035 and mid-century.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) with defining features and essential requirements.
Official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015 to guide economic policy.
The official policy goal, declared the first task of building a modern socialist country at the 20th Congress, of shifting from rapid growth to better-quality, more balanced growth.
A metaphor of taking an examination, associated with Mao Zedong's remark in 1949 and used by Xi Jinping for the Party's ongoing tests of governance.

t: Marxism of China in the new era and twenty-first-century Marxism
zh: 新时代的中国马克思主义与21世纪马克思主义
paras: The Italian Marxist Vladimiro Giacché, vice-president of the Association Marx XXI (Italy), asks how Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should be understood by readers used to discussing Marx in a Western political culture. The text is a Chinese translation of his article, published in World Socialism Studies in 2022. Giacché argues that this body of thought is non-static, non-dogmatic Marxism and a developing twenty-first-century Marxism.

He begins by naming three obstacles for Western readers: the habit of splitting Marx's and Engels's thought into isolated aspects, the weakening of the link between Marxism and political practice in the West, and the differing background of Chinese Marxism, which serves to build socialism rather than mainly to critique capitalist relations. The article then proceeds through Xi's speeches and writings. It covers the development of theory through practice, the role of traditional Chinese culture, dialectical materialist method, trends in the contemporary world, and the competitive advantages of China's socialist system.

Giacché's central claim is that the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics develops Marxism rather than merely recording policy. He notes that Marx and Engels had no experience of governing a socialist state and that Lenin made a similar point about state capitalism, so Chinese communists had to find their own solutions. He identifies contradiction, relations, institutions and systematic thinking as the core categories of Xi's method. He reads the community with a shared future for mankind as a universalism that rejects imperialism and a single model of civilisation. He also reads the Chinese system's advantage as lying in public ownership as the mainstay, a socialist market economy and Party leadership, which he says allow long-term strategy not dominated by bourgeois interests.

In six concluding points, Giacché stresses that practice runs through the evolution of the thought, that traditional culture provides fertile soil, and that China's stance is rooted in independence rather than any inferiority complex towards the West. He observes that the features Xi stresses, the role of the state and Party leadership, are the same ones Western critics target, and says this is no coincidence. Read the original if you want a Western Marxist's systematic, sympathetic reading of Xi Jinping Thought, and of how it frames institutional competition with capitalism.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is non-static, non-dogmatic Marxism, a developing twenty-first-century Marxism.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想是非静态的、非教条的马克思主义，是发展中的21世纪马克思主义。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012–13. It calls for shared security, cooperation and mutual respect between civilisations.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines a socialist system with a market economy under Communist Party leadership.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The development and prospects of Chinese political science in the new era
zh: 新时代中国政治学的发展与前瞻
source: Social Science Research (Shehui kexue yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Writing just after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Wang Bingquan takes stock of a decade of Chinese political science since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article argues that the discipline, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, has entered a stage of self-reliance and self-direction. Wang holds that its central task is to build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system and to advance the "three systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse) of Chinese political science.

The article proceeds in six parts. It sets out the new demands on the discipline: the "great changes unseen in a century", the modernization of national governance, social transformation and a growing native awareness. It then surveys research themes, from the Party's leadership system, institutional reform and grassroots governance to whole-process people's democracy and common prosperity. Next it reviews ten sub-fields (historical, rural, ethnic, comparative, technology, spatial, environmental, political communication, political psychology and the history of political thought) and new methods such as big data, experiments and cross-disciplinary work.

Wang's core argument is that the discipline's growth is explained by a set of internal and external drivers: the guidance of Party theory, practical demands of reform, a turn from imitating Western concepts to local ones, international competition, new technology and openness. In Wang's account, earlier reliance on Western frameworks could not capture China's experience, and the contrast between "China's order" and "Western disorder" strengthened the case for indigenous theory. The article also presents the Party's leadership, the new type of party system and Chinese governance theory as innovations that go beyond Western theories. It says Marxism and a creatively transformed traditional political culture should remain the foundations.

Wang concludes that the discipline should strengthen four forms of awareness: self-awareness, strategic awareness, community awareness among scholars and integration across disciplines. Political scientists are urged to build new concepts and analytical frameworks from Chinese practice and to raise them to general theory. They are also urged to centre research on Chinese modernization and to place political reform research within the modernization of national governance. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned overview of how Chinese political science describes its own sub-fields, themes and methods since 2012.
quoteEn: Chinese political science can have vitality only if it starts from China's national conditions, takes root in its foundations, combines with Chinese reality, and uses Chinese theory to explain China's political phenomena and guide its political processes.
quoteZh: 中国政治学只有从本国国情出发，扎根基底，与中国实际相结合，运用中国的理论解释中国的政治现象，引领中国的政治过程，才能具有生命力。

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping and the Party leadership to describe a period of deep shifts in the global order, including changes in the balance of power and technology.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set by the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and elaborated by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th (2019). It refers to improving the country's institutions and its capacity to run them.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2019 to describe China's democratic model as covering every stage of decision-making, not only elections.

The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership. It is contrasted by official sources with Western competitive party systems.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Marxism adapted to China and our times works
zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义行
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报)
paras: This short commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement, repeated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), that the Party succeeds and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good because Marxism works, and specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Wang Shuyin argues that the formulation expresses Marxism's theoretical character and gives a basic guide for opening up new horizons in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece has three parts: the Party's innovative theory guiding new practice; the continual opening of new horizons for Marxism; and the Party's role in writing what Wang calls the grandest epic in the history of the Chinese nation.

Wang argues that Marxism is a method and guide to action, not a dogma, and that it is a developing theory. It works because the Party keeps combining its basic principles with China's realities and the features of the era, and solves practical problems in revolution, construction and reform. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is presented as the latest leap in this process, and Wang lists six stances and methods for further theoretical innovation, including putting the people first and keeping a problem-oriented approach.

Wang concludes that the Party's guidance by Marxism underlies its historical initiative and the achievements of the past decade, which he describes as setting the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on an irreversible course. He calls for grasping the decisive significance of the Two Establishes and fully applying Xi's thought in building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars explain the 20th Party Congress formula on Marxism.
quoteEn: Whether Marxism can play a role in practice depends on whether its basic principles can be combined with China's realities and the features of the era, and whether it can solve practical problems in China's revolution, construction and reform.
quoteZh: 马克思主义能不能在实践中发挥作用，关键在于能否把马克思主义基本原理同中国实际和时代特征结合起来，能否解决中国革命、建设、改革进程中的实际问题。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with Chinese conditions and with current historical features. The 'times' element was added in the 2021 Party history resolution and the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
