glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and described by the Party as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the 21st century.
A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution, affirming Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream, of restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity by the mid-21st century.

t: On common prosperity and value guidance
zh: 论共同富裕与价值引领
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 12
paras: Luo Yuting and Liu Shuhao, writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), treat common prosperity not only as an economic and political question but as a question of values. Their thesis is that Chinese modernization, which the Congress report defines as the modernization of common prosperity for all the people, requires deliberate value guidance to build a social consensus on what common prosperity means and how to reach it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why such guidance is needed now: China has entered a historical stage of making solid progress towards common prosperity, common prosperity is described as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and creating a better life for the people requires shared values. The second identifies four value tendencies to correct. The third proposes five ways of advancing value guidance: policy orientation, public opinion, cultural cultivation, behavioural norms and model demonstration.

In the authors' account, each of the four value questions is a pairing of a principle to uphold and a deviation to resist. "Prosperity for all" must guard against polarisation, but also against absolute egalitarianism, which the authors say contradicts the law of value and distribution according to labour. "Comprehensive prosperity" means material and cultural-ethical wealth together, against a one-dimensional "materialism". "Gradual prosperity" rejects "simultaneous prosperity", which the authors link to the influence of Nordic welfarism and call unrealistic for the largest developing country. "Prosperity through joint building" rejects getting something for nothing, which they call parasitic and tied to exploiting classes' values.

On implementation, the authors call for policies that embody the idea that labour is honourable and prosperity comes through struggle. They also call for positive publicity that answers mistaken views at home and abroad, and for drawing on traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. Legal and institutional norms should help hard-working, honest and innovative workers become prosperous, and exemplary cases, such as the Zhejiang common prosperity demonstration zone, should be promoted for emulation. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party-oriented theory frames common prosperity as an ideological and moral task as well as an economic one.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is not only a major economic and political question, but also a major question of values.
quoteZh: 共同富裕不仅是一个重大的经济问题、政治问题，也是一个重大的价值问题。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Its features include a huge population, common prosperity for all and coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress.

A long-standing socialist goal, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping, of shared affluence for all the people. Official usage stresses narrowing regional, urban-rural and income gaps while rejecting both polarisation and egalitarianism.
The official name for the Party's theory and system of socialism since the reform era, presented as Marxism applied to China's conditions.

t: The primary stage of socialism and socialism in the primary stage (part 2)
st: Keynote report to the 8th Forum on Marxist Theory and Contemporary Chinese History, 12 August 2022
zh: 社会主义初级阶段与初级阶段社会主义（下）
paras: This is the second half of a keynote report that Zhu Jiamu, president of the Chinese Society for the History of the People's Republic of China and former vice-president of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, gave at the 8th Forum on Marxist Theory and Contemporary Chinese History on 12 August 2022. Zhu asks how to tell whether practice in the primary stage of socialism is guided by the theory of socialism as practised in that stage, rather than departing from scientific socialism. Zhu's answer is that policies suited to the primary stage must be combined with fidelity to the basic principles of socialism.

This part sets out three further tests, continuing from the first half: holding to the communist ideal alongside the Party's basic programme; upholding the Four Cardinal Principles alongside the policies of socialism with Chinese characteristics; and resisting Western "peaceful evolution". The argument draws on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Chen Yun and Xi Jinping, on the Soviet collapse, and on the 2021 Party resolution on history.

On the first test, Zhu argues that the Party's "minimum" programmes in each period have differed but that its "maximum" programme of communism has kept it from losing direction and slackening its will to struggle. On the second, Zhu holds that combining reform and opening up with the Four Cardinal Principles is the main reason for China's success, that hostile forces attack precisely this combination, and that Gorbachev's abandonment of those principles caused Soviet failure. Zhu goes through each principle. Public ownership must remain dominant, judged by control of the economy's lifelines rather than by the private sector's share of output or employment. The "dictatorship of the proletariat", in Zhu's account, still has a target in subversion and bourgeois liberalization. Party leadership and the guiding role of Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought must continue, while theory keeps developing.

On the third test, Zhu presents peaceful evolution as concentrated in the political and ideological spheres. Zhu treats corruption, especially collusion between officials and private capital, as a product of it and as a route for "colour revolutions". Zhu concludes that China must neither attempt what is beyond the primary stage nor violate socialist principles, so that it can advance to a higher stage and eventually to communism. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how a senior Party historian justifies the limits of marketization and the case for strict ideological vigilance.)
quoteEn: In the final analysis, it lies in China's combining adherence to the Four Cardinal Principles with adherence to reform and opening up.
quoteZh: 说到底，在于中国把坚持四项基本原则与坚持改革开放结合在了一起。

glossary.explanation: The official characterisation of China's present stage, adopted in the 1980s, in which socialism is established but productive forces remain relatively underdeveloped. It is meant to last a long time.
Formulated by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, Communist Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
A term in Chinese Party discourse for alleged Western efforts to transform socialist states from within through ideological, cultural and economic means rather than force.

t: The primary stage of socialism and socialism in its primary stage (Part 1)
zh: 社会主义的初级阶段与初级阶段的社会主义（上）
paras: This is the first part of a keynote report that Zhu Jiamu gave on 12 August 2022 at the Eighth Forum on Marxist Theory of Contemporary Chinese History. Zhu argues that, just as understanding the nature of Chinese society was decisive for the revolution, understanding the nature of the present stage explains the achievements of reform and opening up. In Zhu's account, that stage is the primary stage of socialism, and socialism with Chinese characteristics is the theory and policy suited to it. Zhu asks readers to grasp how the two ideas in the title relate.

The speech has two main sections. The first traces how Marx, Engels, Lenin, Stalin, Khrushchev, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping understood the length and internal divisions of socialist society. The second asks whether China's rise since the late 1990s means it has left the primary stage. Zhu draws on Party Congress reports and the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020).

Zhu holds that Marx and Engels treated socialism as the first phase of communism but did not say how long it would last. Lenin, Stalin, Khrushchev and the Great Leap Forward in China, Zhu says, all tended to underestimate the time required. Mao later stressed a long period, and Deng tied socialism's task to developing the productive forces. Zhu presents distinguishing a primary stage within socialism as a major theoretical innovation, and treats socialism with Chinese characteristics as the system of theory and policy for that stage. The Party's judgement that the new era is a higher phase within the primary stage rests, Zhu says, on a changed principal contradiction and on advances in GDP, poverty reduction, social security and international standing. Zhu nonetheless lists reasons why China has not reached an advanced stage. Per capita indicators are still low, growth is resource-intensive and uneven, and core technologies remain foreign-held. Demographic and external pressures persist, and the standards for industrialization and modernization keep rising.

Zhu concludes that after more than 70 years of effort China has entered a new stage of development in the new era. That stage is still insufficiently developed and remains far from the advanced world level. It can therefore only be a higher level within the primary stage of socialism, not the advanced stage of socialist society. The text ends with "to be continued". Read the original if you want to see how a senior Party historian justifies, historically and statistically, the claim that China remains in the primary stage of socialism.
quoteEn: Therefore, this new stage of development can only be a higher level within the primary stage of socialism, not the advanced stage of socialist society.
quoteZh: 所以，这个新的发展阶段只能是社会主义初级阶段中的更高一级阶段，而不是社会主义社会的高级阶段。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official judgement that China is already socialist but still underdeveloped, and will remain so for a long time. It was elaborated at the 13th Party Congress in 1987.

The official name for the theory, path and system of socialism pursued in China since reform and opening up. The term first appeared in Deng Xiaoping's opening speech at the 12th Party Congress in 1982.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.

t: Sinicized and modernized Marxism works
zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义行
paras: Taking its title from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary asks why the Communist Party of China has succeeded and why socialism with Chinese characteristics is judged good. Dong Zhenhua answers that, in the end, it is Marxism that works, specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The piece appeared in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2022 and presents continued theoretical innovation as a solemn historical responsibility of today's Communists.

The article has three parts. The first reviews more than a century of the Party's history as a process of seeking, revealing and putting truth into practice. The second explains why writing new chapters of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is a duty. The third sets out the stances, viewpoints and methods that Dong says theoretical innovation must rely on, drawing on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

In the historical section, Dong presents three leaps for the Chinese nation: from being weak to standing up under Mao Zedong, from standing up to growing rich under Deng Xiaoping and reform and opening up, and from growing rich to becoming strong in the new era. Each is attributed to combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and, more recently, with fine traditional Chinese culture, which the article calls the Two Integrations. Dong argues that success has come whenever the Party kept Marxism open and used a developing Marxism to guide practice, and setbacks followed when it did not. Looking forward, the author lists six commitments: put the people first, be self-confident and self-reliant, uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground, be problem-oriented, apply systems thinking, and keep the whole world in view.

Dong concludes that the 20th Party Congress report is the Party's political declaration and action programme for the new journey. The author calls on readers to improve their ability to analyse and solve practical problems with Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and to arm themselves with Xi Jinping Thought. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party School scholars present the official narrative of Marxism's adaptation in the months after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Practice has fully proved that Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times works.
quoteZh: 实践充分证明，中国化时代化的马克思主义行。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's effort to fit Marxist theory to China's conditions and to current times. The addition of "needs of our times" was prominent from the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was stressed in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 speeches.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name of China's political and economic system and path since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.en: uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: hold to what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for keeping to core principles while innovating in theory and practice.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Inquiry into several questions on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 关于马克思主义中国化时代化的若干问题探赜
source: Nankai Journal (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 1
paras: Writing in early 2023, after the 20th Party Congress (2022) made advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times a Party duty, Li Sicong asks how this formula arose, what it means, how it relates to a century of Party theory, and how it should be pursued. Li argues that existing scholarship leans towards grand theoretical narrative and has not examined these points closely. The article's answer is that the formula is a systematic summation of the Party's century of theoretical innovation and a dynamic process of applying Marxism to China's realities and the features of the era.

The article has four parts. It first traces how the formula was proposed, then defines its "scientific connotation". It then reads the Party's century as three leaps (Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era). Finally it sets out how Xi Jinping Thought opens up a "new realm" of this adaptation.

On origins, Li adds two conditions to earlier scholarly explanations: the "spatial extension" (local modes of production, culture, religion) and the "temporal continuity" (era, stage, tasks) that bound any theory's development. Li divides the formula's emergence into three phases: a period from the 18th Party Congress (2012) when its meaning was carried by older phrases; a preparatory period after the 19th Congress (2017), when Xi first used it as an independent concept in 2018; and a period of establishment from the Party's centenary in 2021, via the third historical resolution and the 20th Congress. Li holds that the new formula does not merely add to the earlier "sinification, adaptation to the times, popularisation" formulations but sublimates them, uniting their theoretical, era-related and popular dimensions.

Li then treats the "Six Musts" as the worldview and methodology for the Party's pursuit, revelation and practice of truth: putting the people first, global vision, self-confidence and self-reliance, innovation while upholding fundamental principles, problem orientation and systems thinking. Li stresses that the political stance in "upholding fundamental principles" matters because judging what counts as "science" and "truth" requires a position. The article concludes that Party members should grasp Xi Jinping Thought's worldview and methods to shoulder the duty of continued theoretical innovation. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how the formula was periodised and defined, and of how it is tied to the Six Musts.
quoteEn: Adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is a dynamic process of theoretical innovation, a picture of how a body of thought from abroad spreads and develops in China.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化时代化是一个理论创新的动态过程，是一个来自国外的思想体系在中国传播发展的图景呈现

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles named at the 20th Party Congress as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought: people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systems thinking, and a global vision.

t: Chinese advanced intellectuals and the integration of Marxism-Leninism with the Chinese workers' movement
st: An important perspective on research into the founding of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国先进知识分子与马克思列宁主义同中国工人运动的结合
zhSub: 中国共产党创建史研究的一个重要视角
paras: Official Party documents repeatedly present the founding of the Communist Party of China as the product of the integration of Marxism-Leninism with the Chinese workers' movement. Huang Guangqiu asks how this integration should be understood and how it came about. The article argues that placing China's advanced intellectuals inside this process is an important angle for studying the Party's creation, and that they played a major role in bringing the two together.

The article is organised in four parts. It first sets out why intellectuals were needed, given the character and weaknesses of the Chinese working class. It then traces how intellectuals such as Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Mao Zedong, Cai Hesen, Dong Biwu and Qu Qiubai came to Marxism through comparison and reflection. The third part examines how the May Fourth Movement showed them the strength of the workers, and how they then went among workers in Shanghai and Beijing. A short conclusion links these steps to the First National Congress in July 1921.

Huang's central argument is that the working class, despite its revolutionary qualities, could not by itself reach class consciousness. The author describes workers as marked by feudal habits, low education and peasant small-producer outlooks, so Marxism had to be brought to them by intellectuals. Intellectuals, in this account, turned to Marxism because other Western doctrines and the capitalist road had failed in China, because the First World War and the Paris Peace Conference disillusioned them, and because the October Revolution showed a workable alternative. The author cites Li Dazhao's and Chen Duxiu's shift away from bourgeois democracy as evidence that this was a reasoned choice. After the May Fourth strikes they surveyed workers, organised May Day events and founded journals, and in the process their own outlook shifted towards the proletariat.

Huang concludes that because intellectuals chose Marxism after repeated comparison, recognised the workers' strength and propagated Marxism among them, the integration of Marxism-Leninism with the workers' movement occurred and the Party could be founded. The article presents this as the basis for the Party's later achievements. Read the original if you want a Party-history account of how early Marxist intellectuals are said to have linked theory and the labour movement, with many quotations from Li, Chen, Mao and their contemporaries.
quoteEn: Chinese advanced intellectuals chose Marxism, regarding it as scientific truth and as the only thing that could save China; this was the result of doubt, comparison and selection, a conclusion reached through rational reflection.
quoteZh: 中国先进知识分子选择马克思主义，认为马克思主义是科学真理，只有马克思主义才能救中国，这是经过怀疑、比较、选择的结果，是经过理性思考而得出的结论。

glossary.explanation: Party-historiographical term for the educated radicals of the New Culture and May Fourth period who adopted Marxism and helped found the Communist Party.

The 1919 patriotic protests that began on 4 May in Beijing against the Paris Peace Conference decisions, followed by strikes in other cities. Party historiography treats it as a turning point for Marxism's spread and the working class's entry into politics.

t: Some reflections on building an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese historiography
zh: 关于建构中国历史学自主知识体系的几点思考
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2023, Zhu Hu asks how Chinese historical scholarship can build its own autonomous knowledge system, in response to Xi Jinping's call to construct an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences. Zhu argues that this task is necessary both for the internal development of the discipline and as part of criticising the cultural hegemony of Western knowledge systems. The piece is a short commentary rather than a full research article.

The article opens with Xi's statements that history underpins all social sciences and with his hope, expressed in a letter to the Chinese Academy of History, for a discipline, academic and discourse system with Chinese characteristics. It then sketches Chinese historiography from its long premodern tradition through the shock of Western academic influence, to Marxist historiography in the revolutionary, construction and reform periods. Zhu next diagnoses current problems and closes with four proposed directions for construction.

Zhu identifies several problems. Marxist guidance has weakened since the late twentieth century, which Zhu attributes partly to unresolved dogmatism and partly to imported Western schools, some of which are said to have encouraged historical nihilism. Zhu also points to fragmentation, with ancient and modern history, world history, archaeology and the auxiliary fields each retreating into their own walls. The discipline's scope is said to be narrowed and its practical function weakened, because specialised histories within economics, law or politics lack proper historical training. The four proposals are: adhere to Marxist guidance and practical application; honour traditional foundations such as the 'four keys' of official posts, geography, bibliography and chronology, together with the Marxist theory of social formations; broaden vision and answer the questions of the era, including those of Chinese modernization; and integrate fields and interdisciplinary work in a professional way.

Zhu concludes that philosophy and the social sciences, history included, reflect a nation's intellectual capacity and comprehensive national strength. Zhu calls for accelerating the discipline, academic and discourse systems of Chinese historiography under historical materialism, while engaging in international exchange. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese historian, writing in an official newspaper, links Xi Jinping's guidance on autonomous knowledge systems to concrete diagnoses of the history discipline.
quoteEn: Historical research is not a discipline of the ivory tower, detached from worldly affairs, but a field of learning with a strong awareness and function of practical application.
quoteZh: 历史研究也不是象牙塔里的不问世事之学，而是有强烈致用意识和功能的学问。

glossary.explanation: A phrase stressed by Xi Jinping in 2022 for philosophy and the social sciences, meaning knowledge and theory grounded in Chinese realities rather than derived from Western frameworks.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's and the revolution's history and the mainstream historical narrative.

t: Upholding and developing Marxism through the Two Integrations
zh: 在“两个结合”中坚持和发展马克思主义
paras: This short commentary, published in Economic Daily in December 2022 shortly after the 20th Party Congress, asks why and how Marxism should be upheld and developed through the Two Integrations. Wang argues that combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture is both an inner requirement of theoretical development and an objective need of China's present development.

The piece opens by tracing the formulation of the Two Integrations from Xi Jinping's speech marking the Party's centenary (2021) through the Sixth Plenum's historical resolution to the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is then organised in two sections, one for each integration, and draws mainly on Xi's remarks and the Congress report.

On the first integration, Wang holds that Marxism is a guide to action rather than dogma, and that it takes root only when Sinicized. Upholding it therefore means using its worldview and methodology to solve China's problems, not reciting phrases or conclusions. On the second, Wang describes a two-way relationship. Marxism activates Chinese civilization, citing parallels between Marx's view of humans as natural beings and the ideal of harmony between heaven and humanity, between the law of unity of opposites and "harmony without uniformity", and between dialectics and the reformist spirit of the Zhou. In turn, traditional culture nourishes Marxism, giving it Chinese features and a stronger historical and popular foundation.

Wang concludes that only a Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times can take root in the hearts of hundreds of millions of Chinese people. The Two Integrations are presented as a summation of the Party's experience of theoretical innovation and as an expression of cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Two Integrations were explained to a general readership just after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Only a Marxism that has been adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times can truly take root in the hearts of hundreds of millions of Chinese people, flourishing with deep roots and luxuriant, evergreen foliage.
quoteZh: 只有中国化时代化的马克思主义才能真正扎根于亿万中国人民的心中，根深叶茂、枝叶长青。

glossary.explanation: Formula stating that the basic tenets of Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping stated it in 2021, and it was written into the Party's historical resolution that year.
Official term for confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture, including its revolutionary and traditional heritage. It is part of the Party's wider "confidence" discourse.

t: On the basic foundations of Chinese modernization
zh: 论中国式现代化的基本立足点
source: Studies on National Modernization (国家现代化建设研究), vol. 1 no. 5, November 2022
paras: Written shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), this article asks what Chinese modernization rests on. Wang Junwei answers that it has three basic footholds: China's basic national conditions, its fine traditional culture, and the Chinese Communist Party's founding mission. The author presents this as the reason China had to take its own path, since neither Western models nor the Soviet one, in Wang's account, solved China's problems.

The article opens with a historical sketch. It covers the failed attempts to learn from the West after 1840, the Party's pre-1949 struggle, the pursuit of the "four modernizations", Deng Xiaoping's concept of a Chinese-style modernization, and developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then devotes one section to each of the three footholds. It ends by placing Chinese modernization in a changing world, and it draws on statistics, classical Chinese sources and foreign commentators such as Arnold Toynbee and Jean-Paul Sartre.

On national conditions, Wang argues that the basic condition remains the primary stage of socialism, summed up as a large population, a weak foundation and uneven development. Wang says the specifics have shifted: the birth rate and working-age population are falling, GDP and wealth have grown, yet per capita indicators, technological self-reliance and inequality still lag. The article therefore links common prosperity and high-quality development to these conditions, and quotes Xi Jinping that the Party's leadership is China's greatest national condition. On culture, Wang contends that the Party inherits and renews traditional culture. In this reading, communism echoes the ancient ideal of a harmonious society, and "serving the people" echoes "the people as the foundation of the state". The Two Integrations are presented as the route for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

On mission, Wang holds that the Party's outlook extends to human progress, so that Chinese modernization offers developing countries an alternative to capital-centred, polarising and expansionist Western modernization. The article describes China as never imposing its model on others and as playing a stabilising role in past crises. It criticises some developed countries for shifting burdens onto others and suppressing latecomers. It concludes that a modernization built on these three foundations will create new achievements for China and the world. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party theorists ground Chinese modernization in national conditions, tradition and Party mission.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is grounded in China's basic national conditions.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化立足于中国的基本国情。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization. The 20th Party Congress (2022) defined its features and essential requirements.
The official judgement, formulated in the 1980s, that China is still in an early and long phase of socialist development. It is used to explain the country's basic national conditions and policies.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which Xi Jinping has emphasised in recent years. It is tied to distribution policy and to narrowing inequality.
The official term for a growth model that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed. It has been a central theme since the 19th Party Congress (2017).
The formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is presented as the way to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context.

t: Striving to write a new chapter in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 奋力谱写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in December 2022, responds to the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The report calls writing ever new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times a solemn historical responsibility of today's Communists. Duan Hong argues that Marxism is a scientific system that keeps developing with the times, and that this task is both a theoretical necessity and a practical one.

The piece has two parts. The first reviews the Party's history of more than a century as a history of theoretical innovation, running from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist revolution and construction and reform and opening up to the new era. The second sets out what the author says is required to write the new chapter: the Two Integrations, the "six musts", and theoretical innovation grounded in practice.

Duan reads each historical stage as a theoretical achievement, from Mao Zedong's "second integration" to Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On the Two Integrations, the author holds that Marxism must keep answering the questions of China, the world, the people and the times, and must take root in fine traditional Chinese culture. For each of the six commitments (putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, staying true while innovating, a problem-oriented approach, systematic thinking, and a global vision), Duan argues that neglecting it would cost Marxism its essential character, direction or capacity to grow.

Duan concludes that theory and practice must interact productively, so that innovation does not become "closed-door" work. Innovation should be rooted in contemporary Chinese practice and guided by Xi Jinping Thought, so that new theory guides new practice. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars presented the 20th Party Congress's line on the adaptation of Marxism.
quoteEn: The Party's more than a century of struggle and development is a history of theoretical innovation that has continually written new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 党的一百多年奋斗发展史就是一部不断谱写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章的理论创新发展史。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing effort to fit Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. The addition of "shídàihuà" (of the times) was made prominent in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao's leadership, stressing people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory, introduced around 2000, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

t: Re-examining the course of the young Mao Zedong's worldview transformation
st: With comments on the 1920 "summer", "winter" and "process" theses
zh: 青年毛泽东世界观转变历程再考察
zhSub: 兼评1920年“夏天说”“冬天说”和“过程说”
paras: When did Mao Zedong become a Marxist? Wu Xuan takes up a long-running debate in Chinese scholarship over the date and the criteria of the young Mao's worldview transformation, including the "summer" thesis (1920), the "winter" thesis and the "process" thesis. Wu argues that the change was a complex, gradual process in which Marxist elements came to dominate Mao's thinking, and that it cannot be pinned to a single season or to the reading of particular books.

The article has four parts. It first treats Mao's second stay in Beijing (1919–20) and his own account to Edgar Snow that by summer 1920 he was a Marxist "in theory, and to some extent in action". It then follows his practice after returning to Hunan in 1920: the Cultural Book Society, the Russian Studies Society, contacts with Chen Duxiu, and the founding of the Changsha communist group and Socialist Youth League. The third part assesses the Hunan self-government movement and the method for judging worldview change, and a short conclusion follows.

Wu concedes that the three books Mao named (the Communist Manifesto, Class Struggle, History of Socialism) were published after August 1920. The author denies that this undermines Mao's claim, since what matters is whether he had broken with reformism and anarchism and accepted class struggle and the dictatorship of the proletariat. Wu reads Mao's Hunan activities as evidence of this shift, and reads the self-government movement's reformist and anarchist traces as a secondary current, not the main one. A transformation, Wu holds, means that Marxist elements became dominant, not that non-Marxist ones vanished; the same was true of Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu. Wu cites Mao's letters and the 1921 New People's Study Society meeting as marking completion by early 1921, when he was a Marxist in both theory and action.

Wu concludes that Mao's transformation followed a path of knowing, practice, re-knowing and re-practice, moving from idealism to materialism and from radical democrat to communist. The author presents this path as typical of early Chinese communist intellectuals and as the basis of the Party's later achievements. Read the original if you want a detailed account of the Chinese historiographical debate over the dating of Mao's turn to Marxism and the evidence marshalled on each side.
quoteEn: Therefore, in understanding the dynamic process of Mao Zedong's worldview transformation, we cannot simply define it by specific markers such as "summer" or "winter", nor should we mechanically and dogmatically equate it with which Marxist-Leninist works he had read.
quoteZh: 因此，我们在理解毛泽东世界观转变这一动态过程时，不能简单用“夏天”或“冬天”等具体尺度来界定，也不应当机械地、教条地同读过哪些马列著作等同起来。

glossary.explanation: The view, based on Mao's 1936 account to Edgar Snow, that Mao became a Marxist in summer 1920.
The view that Mao's turn to Marxism was completed only in winter 1920 or around early 1921, after the failure of the Hunan self-government movement.
The view that Mao's turn was a gradual process that cannot be tied to one date; Wu's own position is closest to it.
A 1920–21 movement for provincial autonomy in Hunan, in which Mao took part and which sought to build a Hunan republic.
A bookshop and organisation founded by Mao in Changsha in 1920 to circulate new periodicals and books, including Marxist and Russian revolutionary writings.

t: Why Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times works
zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义为什么行
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in December 2022, takes up the line from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) that the Party succeeds and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good because Marxism works, specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Chen Jinlong argues that this adapted Marxism works because it suits China's conditions, answers the questions of the age and speaks to the people's concerns.

The piece is organised in three parts after a short introduction, one for each reason. It draws on Marx and Engels, on the stages of China's revolution and construction, and on concepts from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It closes by restating the author's call for a continuing effort to renew Marxism in China.

First, Chen holds that Marxism rests mainly on European history, so applying it mechanically elsewhere would be dogmatism. In the author's account, it has been fitted to China through the Two Integrations: with China's concrete realities, including the nature of society and its principal contradiction, and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Examples given are the unity of heaven and humanity feeding ecological ideas, and the idea of the people as the foundation of the state feeding the people-centred approach. Second, Chen says each era sets its own questions. The author presents Xi Jinping Thought as the response to the questions raised by great changes unseen in a century (globalisation and deglobalisation, great-power rivalry, AI and big data). Third, because the people are the main body of practice, theory must come from and serve them, and their practice tests its truth. Chen lists the principal contradiction, whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature as questions the theory addresses.

Chen concludes that this Marxism is close to national conditions, the times and the people, and that this is why it works. Practice and theoretical innovation have no end, and the author calls it the historic responsibility of today's Communists to keep writing new chapters. They call for using Marxism to observe, grasp and lead the times, for drawing on China's practice, and for absorbing the achievements of other civilisations. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register statement of the standard rationale for the adaptation of Marxism in China after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times stays close to national conditions, the times and the people, and answers the questions of China, the world, the people and the age; this is why it works.
quoteZh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义贴近国情、贴近时代、贴近人民，回答了中国之问、世界之问、人民之问、时代之问，这是中国化时代化的马克思主义行的缘由所在。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added in Xi Jinping's formulation in 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented officially as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century.
Xi Jinping's term for China's democratic model, which official sources say covers every stage of governance and not only elections.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, stressed in Party policy since 2021 as an essential requirement of socialism.

t: Deeply grasping the core meaning of the "six musts"
zh: 深刻领悟“六个必须坚持”的核心要义
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in December 2022, explains the "six musts" set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Han Qingxiang argues that they form a tightly linked organic whole. In the author's reading, they are the worldview, methodology, standpoint, viewpoint and method that must be followed in opening up new realms of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article first places the "six musts" within the Congress report's call to advance theoretical innovation grounded in practice. It then takes each in turn: putting the people first, being self-confident and self-reliant, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, adopting a problem-oriented approach, applying systems thinking, and taking the whole world into account.

Han assigns each "must" a distinct function. The people-first principle is the fundamental standpoint, and self-confidence and self-reliance the foothold. Upholding fundamental principles while innovating is the scientific attitude, and the problem orientation is theory's central task. Systems thinking is the method of thought, and a global outlook is the worldview. Han presents these as an expression of materialist dialectics, in which continuity and change, principle and creativity are unified. The author also calls for advancing the Two Integrations and addressing problems at home and abroad together.

Han concludes that the "six musts" are the basic points for understanding Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and for continuing theoretical innovation. The author calls for applying them so that the Thought is carried through every area of Party and state work. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how the 20th Congress "six musts" are explained and organised.
quoteEn: Problems are the voice of the times, and answering them and guiding their solution is the fundamental task of theory.
quoteZh: 问题是时代的声音，回答并指导解决问题是理论的根本任务。

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles listed in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought: the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systems thinking, and a global perspective.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the Marxism of contemporary China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxism to Chinese conditions and to current times. The 'of our times' element was added in the 2021 historical resolution and the 20th Congress report.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It has been stressed in Party documents since 2021–2022.

t: The theoretical implications of the maturation and consolidation of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义制度成熟定型的理论意涵
paras: Ren Peng takes up a formulation from the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the socialist system with Chinese characteristics has become "more mature and more定型" (more fully formed). The article asks why this became possible in the new era, what marks a system as mature and consolidated, and how it should be developed once it is. Ren argues that the maturation rests on advanced productive forces and on the system's own self-improvement, that it can be recognised by identifiable criteria, and that it carries significant theoretical and practical weight.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the theoretical necessity of maturation, then the signs of it, then its contributions, and finally its theoretical value, meaning the tasks that follow. Ren draws mainly on historical materialism, on speeches by Xi Jinping, and on the Party's documents from the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019).

Ren's central move is to define a mature system by three marks. The outward mark is a system that is scientific, complete and stable. The inward mark is institutional confidence, value identification and compliance among the people. The third is orderly creation and revision of rules, smooth operation and good performance. On this account the system's performance shows in efficiency, in effectiveness against risks such as poverty alleviation and the Covid-19 epidemic, and in wider benefits. Ren then argues that maturation shows the Party has deepened its grasp of three laws: those governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development. It also means a new stage for the modernization of national governance and, in Ren's reading, supports entry into the "new development stage" of the primary stage of socialism. The article describes the system's advantages in comparison with Western systems and as a model for developing countries.

Ren stresses that maturity is both absolute and relative, because it holds only under given productive forces and conditions. The article proposes three tasks. These are to persist in institutional reform and innovation, including measures for common prosperity; to strengthen institutional awareness and enforcement, especially among leading cadres as the "key minority"; and to balance stability with development so that institutional advantages become governance effectiveness. Ren holds that the Party's leadership system must remain unshaken. Read the original if you want a systematic statement, in the Party-theoretical idiom, of how Chinese scholars define institutional maturity and tie it to national governance modernization.
quoteEn: A mature and consolidated system is one whose institutional framework is scientific, complete and stable, whose subjects are confident in it, identify with it and abide by it, and whose institutional effectiveness is markedly good.
quoteZh: 成熟定型的制度就是制度体系科学完备稳定、制度主体自信认同遵循、制度效能显著优良的制度体系。

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.explanation: A goal set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), sometimes called the 'fifth modernization'. It covers both the institutional system of governing and the capacity to carry out governance.

Official shorthand for the laws governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and the development of human society. The Party presents deepening understanding of them as a basis of its theory.
Official term for the period beginning with the drive to build a modern socialist country after 2020. It is described as a new phase within the primary stage of socialism.
A policy goal of shared wealth for all, promoted strongly by Xi Jinping since around 2021. It is presented as an essential requirement of socialism.
Official phrase for Party members in leading positions, who are expected to set an example in following rules and institutions.

t: On the characteristics and behavioural laws of capital in the socialist market economy
zh: 论社会主义市场经济中资本的特性和行为规律
paras: Following the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2021 and Xi Jinping's speech at the Politburo study session of April 2022, Liu Fengyi takes up the task of correctly understanding the characteristics and behavioural laws of capital under a socialist market economy. Liu argues that Marx's analysis of capital remains the basis, but that Marx did not foresee the combination of socialism and the market, so Marxist political economy must work out how capital's laws are modified in that setting. The article holds that the aim is to use capital well and to rein it in, with regulation as the main aspect.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the starting points for studying capital theory, then derives capital's behavioural laws from its essence, then from its forms, and finally proposes ways to use institutional strengths to make good use of capital and to govern it. Liu separates public from private capital, and organises capital's forms by production, circulation and distribution, drawing on Marx's Capital throughout.

Liu first defines capital in Marx's terms as a social relation that seeks self-expansion of value, not a thing, a sum of money or a production factor. Liu rejects the idea that capital has a natural attribute alongside a social one. Under capitalism, competition and money's limitlessness drive endless accumulation, which promotes productive forces but also produces exploitation, polarisation and crises. In the socialist market economy, Liu contends, public capital has a dual character: it follows market rules in form, while internally it embodies socialist production relations. Private capital keeps its wage-labour relation, but its laws are 'deformed' because production aims at meeting people's needs and public capital serves as the 'universal light'. Liu also stresses that capital prefers to 'divide the cake' in the virtual economy rather than 'make the cake' in the real economy.

Liu concludes that capital's profit-seeking nature must be harnessed through the strengths of the socialist system, using six measures. These are the Two Unwaverings, using capital to serve the people, improving economic governance under Party leadership, supervising capital in direct production, setting 'traffic lights' for green development, and ideological and political work with private entrepreneurs. Liu says red lights for a few kinds of capital are meant to create green lights for most, and that the new development pattern follows the laws of capital circulation and turnover. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how a Chinese Marxist economist links Capital's categories to current policy on regulating capital.
quoteEn: Capital not only pursues the expansion of value, but pursues it endlessly.
quoteZh: 资本不仅追求价值增殖，而且还无休止地去追求价值增殖。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula calling for unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A strategy put forward in 2020 that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.
The official name of China's economic system, which combines public ownership as the mainstay with market allocation of resources under Party leadership.

t: The historical necessity of building an independent knowledge system in Chinese philosophy and social sciences, and paths towards it
zh: 中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系建构的历史必然与路径探索
paras: Han Xiping takes up Xi Jinping's statement that building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics comes down to constructing China's own independent knowledge system. Writing in 2022, after the April release of the national 14th Five-Year Plan for philosophy and social sciences, Han argues that such a system is a call of the times and a historical necessity. In Han's view it also accords with the general laws of how the discipline develops.

The article first defines knowledge, knowledge systems and "independent" knowledge, drawing on Aristotle, Russell, Polanyi and the OECD. It then traces how Western liberalism, with its "rational economic man" assumption, came to dominate the world's philosophy and social sciences and produced "Western centrism". Four sections follow on why the system is needed: by the era, by China, by the world, and then a section on practical routes.

Han contends that Chinese scholarship remains in an "apprenticeship" to Western paradigms. The author says Chinese practice, such as poverty alleviation, the socialist market economy and ecological civilization, has not been distilled into its own theory, and that concepts like the "China model" are often defined by Western scholars. Liberal theory, in Han's account, can explain neither the current global turbulence nor the question of where humanity is heading. Chinese modernization is presented as transcending capitalist modernization and sublating its oppositions between humans and nature, capital and labour, and states. The author presents a community with a shared future for mankind and a new form of human civilization as Chinese answers to these questions.

For the path forward, Han calls for Marxism as the guiding theory, a real break from imitation rather than the addition of some Chinese terms, and creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture combined with Marxism. The author also calls for theory that addresses both Chinese and global problems, supported by think tanks, and a new explanatory paradigm for Chinese experience built on Marxist standpoint and method. The aim is to end the "absence" of Chinese discourse in disciplines, textbooks and forums. Read the original if you want a representative statement of the 2022 official case for an independent Chinese knowledge system and its justification.
quoteEn: The fundamental requirement for building China's independent knowledge system in philosophy and social sciences is to uphold Marxism as the guiding theory.
quoteZh: 构建中国自主的哲学社会科学知识体系，根本要求是要坚持马克思主义的理论领航。

glossary.explanation: A phrase stressed by Xi Jinping in 2022 for scholarship grounded in China's own experience and concepts rather than Western paradigms.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from the Western capitalist model.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward from 2012 as the guiding idea of China's vision for international relations.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official formulation, prominent around the Party's centenary in 2021, describing Chinese modernization as a civilization type beyond the capitalist one.
The official term for the parts of China's cultural heritage deemed worth carrying forward, to be creatively transformed and combined with Marxism.

t: Chinese modernization makes new and greater contributions to mankind
zh: 中国式现代化为人类作出新的更大贡献
paras: Published in Guangming Daily shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary asks what Chinese modernization offers the wider world. Chai Shangjin argues that it breaks the claim that Western modernization is the only model, promotes global sustainable development, and both develops China and benefits other countries. The piece leans heavily on Xi Jinping's statements to frame these claims.

The article opens by summarising the Party's account of Chinese modernization: a modernization of a huge population, of common prosperity for all, of material and cultural-ethical progress, of harmony between humanity and nature, and of peaceful development. Three sections follow. The first contrasts Chinese and Western paths, the second deals with ecological civilization and green development, and the third covers peaceful development and China's international initiatives. Chai supports the last section with a quotation from the British scholar Martin Jacques.

Chai's central move is a contrast. In the author's account, Western modernization is essentially capitalist, centred on capital, expansionist and predatory, and it widens wealth gaps and political division at home and abroad. Chinese modernization, led by the Communist Party, is described as people-centred and aimed at common prosperity, and as having overcome the materialism and alienation from nature that accompany the Western path. Chai then argues that harmony between humanity and nature is intrinsic to this path. As evidence, the article cites figures for the past decade: average annual energy consumption growth of 3% supporting average economic growth of 6.6%, and a cumulative 26.2% fall in energy intensity. It adds that China pursues the new development philosophy and the carbon peak and carbon neutrality pledges. On peace, Chai states that China has never sought hegemony and will not, and links modernization to a community with a shared future for mankind and the Global Development and Global Security Initiatives.

Chai concludes that the Chinese path has solved China's practical problems and, in a certain sense, answers the common question of how less developed countries can modernize. It is presented as both the proper road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a correct choice for leading global modernization trends. The text is an official-line commentary rather than a detailed analysis. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated writers presented the international significance of Chinese modernization right after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: There is neither a single, supreme model of modernization in the world, nor a standard of modernization that holds good everywhere.
quoteZh: 世界上既不存在定于一尊的现代化模式，也不存在放之四海而皆准的现代化标准。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated especially at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is defined by five features, including a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has stressed since 2021. It means prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
A policy framework set out in 2015 that stresses innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of interdependent states pursuing shared development and security. Chinese official texts present it as an alternative to bloc politics.

An official concept that puts environmental protection and green development at the centre of national development. It was added to the Party's overall plan for socialism with Chinese characteristics.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind
